The Dharma-Eye School, under Mount Heng, Eighth Generation.
Chan Master Wenyi of Qingliang Monastery in Jinling was a dharma successor of Chan Master Luohan Chen. He was the son of the Ru family of Yuhang.

At the age of seven, he received the tonsure under Chan Master Quanwei of Zhitong Monastery in Xinding. In his youth, he received full ordination at Kaiyuan Monastery in Yuezhou, specializing in the Vinaya.
Master Jiaoxi was flourishing in his propagation of the Dharma at Yuwang Temple on Mount Mao in Mingzhou. The Master went there to attend his lectures and master his subtle teachings;
he further explored the Confucian classics and frequented the circles of literary refinement. Master Jiao regarded him as a "Yu" or "Xia" of our school.
Once the profound mechanism of the Way had been awakened within him, he cast aside all miscellaneous affairs and, shaking his monk’s staff, traveled south until he reached Fuzhou.
He visited Changqing, but did not achieve great realization. Later, together with Shaoxiu, Fafa, and Jin, the three of them intended to cross the mountain ridges.

Passing through Dizang Monastery, they were delayed by snow and rested for a short while. As they sat by the brazier, Dizang asked, "Where are you going on this journey? The Master replied, "I am traveling as a wandering monk."

Zang asked, "What is the matter of traveling on pilgrimage? The Master said, "I do not know. Zang said, "Not knowing is most intimate. They then discussed the *Zhao Lun* together with three others; when they reached the passage, "Heaven and earth share the same root as I," Zang asked, "Are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth the same as your own self, Venerable Sir, or are they different? The Master said, "They are different. Zang held up two fingers. The Master said, [They are the same]. Zang said, "If you say they are different, you will fall into the error of dualism. The Master said, "If you say they are the same, you will fall into the error of monism. Zang said, "If you can avoid both errors, I shall grant you the robe and bowl. The Master remained silent. Zang said, "The robe and bowl have been granted. The Master still did not speak. Zang said, "Do not be stingy with your words. The Master said, "I am not stingy with my words; it is just that there are no words. Zang said, "If there are no words, how can you avoid falling into the error of monism? The Master said, "It is precisely because there are no words that I avoid falling into the error of monism. Zang said, "If there are no words, how can you avoid falling into the error of dualism? The Master said, "It is precisely because there are no words that I avoid falling into the error of dualism. Zang said, "Excellent! Excellent! He then presented the robe and bowl to him. Later, when the Master was about to depart for the South, he visited Zang again. Zang asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "To the South. Zang said, "If you go to the South, you must first visit me. The Master said, "I have already visited you. Zang said, "How did you visit me? The Master said, "When I first came here, I did not yet know anything. Zang said, "Now you know. The Master said, "I still do not know. Zang said, "If you truly do not know, you are most intimate. The Master said, "I am not intimate. Zang said, "If you are not intimate, you are most intimate. The Master said, "I am neither intimate nor not intimate. Zang said, "Neither intimate nor not intimate—this is the ultimate intimacy. The Master said, "Ultimate intimacy is not intimacy. Zang said, "If it is not intimacy, what is it? Dazang did the same. Then he held up two fingers and immediately departed. When Xueji was taking his leave, Dazang saw him off at the gate and asked, "Upādhyāya, you usually say that the three realms are mind-only and all phenomena are consciousness-only.
He then pointed to a stone slab in the courtyard and said: [The text here implies a challenge regarding the consistency of this teaching with the perceived reality of the physical world.]

"Tell me," said Mazu, "is this stone inside the mind or outside the mind? The Master replied, "It is inside the mind. Mazu said, "A wandering monk, for what reason do you place a piece of stone upon your head?
The Master was at a loss for a reply. He immediately set down his pack, sat below the master's seat, and requested a definitive resolution.
For nearly a month, he presented his insights and explained his principles. Mazu then spoke to him, saying: [The text continues with Mazu’s instruction.]
"The Buddha-dharma is not like that," [Nanquan] said. The Master replied, "I am at a loss for words; my reasoning has reached its limit.
Zang said, "As for the Buddha-dharma, everything is already fully present. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Consequently, they discussed having him remain.

However, as the Master and his companions intended to tour the monastic centers (*conglin*) throughout the region south of the Yangtze River, they were ordered to travel together. Upon arriving in Linchuan, the Prefect invited the Master to reside at Chongshou Monastery.

On the day of opening the hall, while the tea ceremony was still in progress and before the central seat had risen, the Sangha Rectifier (Sōjō) addressed the Master, saying, "The fourfold assembly has already surrounded the Venerable’s Dharma seat.
The Master replied, "Let the people go and consult the true Good Spiritual Friend. After a short while, he ascended the seat.
A monk asked, "The great assembly has gathered like clouds; we request the Master to raise the cry.
The Master said, "The assembly has stood for a long time," and then added, "Since everyone is here, this mountain monk cannot remain silent. For your sake, I shall cite a device of an ancient worthy.
Take care! He then descended from his seat. At that time, the monk Zifang had come from Changqing. The Master cited a verse by Changqing and asked, "What [is it]?"
"What is this body that stands alone amidst the myriad phenomena? The student just raised his whisk when the Master said, "How can you understand it in such a way?
The student asked, "What is your honorable intention, Master? The Master said, "What do you call 'the myriad phenomena'?
The student said, "The ancients did not negate the myriad phenomena. The Master said, "'The body stands alone amidst the myriad phenomena'—what does it matter whether one negates them or not?"

The disciple suddenly attained a clear and expansive realization and offered a verse in sincere devotion. From that time on, those from various quarters who possessed intellectual understanding flocked there in great numbers.
At first, they were all rigidly conventional; the Master subtly stimulated them, and they gradually came to accept his teachings.
The assembly, like a gathering at the sea, never numbered fewer than a thousand. One day, after the great assembly had stood for a long time, he addressed them, saying:
If they simply disperse like that, is there any principle of the Buddha-dharma? Try to explain it. If there is none, why have you come here?
If there is, it is also found in the midst of crowds in a great marketplace; why must you come to this place?
Everyone has once read the *Returning to the Source Contemplation*, the *Ocean of Meaning in a Hundred Gates*, the *Avataṃsaka Treatise*, the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*, and many other commentaries.
In which of these teachings is there such a moment? If there is, try to cite it and see.
Is it perhaps because such words exist within such a sūtra that this is the moment? What connection could there possibly be? Therefore, it is said:
Subtle words remain stagnant within the mind, often becoming the field for discursive thought. Ultimate reality dwells right before one’s eyes, yet it instead becomes the realm of names and forms.
How can these be overturned? And if they are overturned, how can one then attain correctness?
Do you understand? Do not merely recite such notes; what use are they? A monk asked: "As for..."
[The student] asked, "When is it revealed? Is it when one attains correspondence with the Way? The Master said, "When do you reveal it? It is precisely when there is no correspondence with the Way.
[The student] asked, "What is it like when the six sense bases do not know their own sounds? The Master said, "They are your family members, a whole brood of children."
The Master said again: "How do you understand this? Do not say that because you have come to ask such a question, it is already incorrect.
You should say: 'In the six sense bases there is no sound; in the locus of the eye there is no sound; in the locus of the ear there is no sound. If the fundamental were existent..."

There is no attainment through striving for liberation. An ancient said: "To leave behind sound and form yet remain attached to sound and form; to leave behind names and words yet remain attached to names and words.

This is why those who cultivate the Realm of No-Thought (Āsaṃjñika-sattva) may attain it after eighty thousand great kalpas, yet fall back in a single morning, with all their former states remaining as they were.
This is because they do not know the fundamental ground. True cultivation proceeds stage by stage: in three lifetimes one completes sixty kalpas, and in four lifetimes one completes one hundred.
Kalpas. In this manner, one proceeds until the fruit of the three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* is fulfilled. An ancient master still said:

"It is not as good as the single thought-moment of dependent origination without arising, which transcends the provisional views of those who study the Three Vehicles. He also said: "In the snap of a finger, the eighty thousand gates are perfectly accomplished;
in a single instant, the three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* are extinguished. One must investigate this deeply. If used in such a way, how much effort would it require? A monk asked:
[The monk] said, "I do not ask about the finger; what is the moon? The Master said, "Which is that finger of yours which you do not ask about?
Another monk asked, "I do not ask about the moon; what is the finger? The Master said, "The moon. The monk said, "I am asking about the finger; why does the Master answer with the moon?
The Master said, "Because you are asking about the finger. The Prince of Jiangnan, who revered the Master’s Way, went out to welcome him.
He resided at Baon Temple Chan Monastery and was titled Chan Master Jinghui. A monk asked, "The great bell has just been struck and the assembly has gathered like clouds;

we request the Master to speak thus. The Master said, "How does the assembly understand compared to how you understand? A monk asked, "What is the ancestral style of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, "Where do you see anything that is insufficient?

Regarding the "person who has gone beyond," the Master said, "It is expediently called 'Buddha. He was asked, "What is the student’s single volume of scripture?
The Master said, "The title is very clear. He was asked, "Who can penetrate the two characters 'sound' and 'form'?
The Master then said to the assembly, "Venerable seniors, tell me: has this monk penetrated them yet? If you understand where this monk was asking, [you will know]."
"Penetrating sounds and forms is not difficult. Question: "In seeking the Buddha’s knowledge and vision, what path is most direct?
The Master said: "None surpasses this. Question: "What is it like when auspicious grass does not wither? The Master said: "Idle talk. Question: "The great assembly has gathered;

we pray that the Master will decisively resolve our web of doubts. The Master said: "Discuss it within the quarters; discuss it in the tea hall. Question: "When the clouds part and the sun is revealed..."
"How is it at that time? The Master said, "It is truly mere idle talk. "Question: What is the place most esteemed by a śramaṇa?

The Master said, "If there were even a hair’s breadth of something esteemed, one would not be called a śramaṇa. "Question: Among the thousand billion transformation bodies, which one is the pure Dharma-body?
The Master said, "They are all [the Dharma-body]. "Question: When they come forward in such a dense throng, what is your intention, Master? The Master—
[The student] said: "This eye is not the eye. He asked about the meaning of "the whole body," requesting the Master to resolve it definitively.
The Master said: "Your own meaning is already destroyed. He asked: "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said: "It flows forth as kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity. He asked:
"A dark room of a hundred years can be dispelled by a single lamp. What is this one lamp? The Master said: "Why discuss 'a hundred years'? He asked: "How... [The text here ends.]
"This is the path of true correctness. The Master said, "The first vow is to teach you how to practice;
the second vow is to teach you how to practice. He asked, "What is the ground of the one true reality? The Master said, "As for the ground, there is no 'one true' thing.

He asked, "How does it stand forth? The Master said, "It turns away from all points of contact. He asked, "What is the ancient Buddha? The Master said, "Even now, there is no suspicion or doubt. He asked again.

"How should one conduct oneself throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said, "Step by step, tread firmly. "Before the ancient mirror has been opened, how does it manifest its illumination?
The Master said, "Why ask more than once? "What is the profound purport of all Buddhas? The Master said, "It is yours as well. "I have heard the teaching that says:
'From the root of non-abiding, all dharmas are established. What is this 'non-abiding'? The Master said, [it is]... (text fragmentary).

[The Master] was dwelling at Ben. A student asked, "Form arises before substance; names arise before names. Regarding the question on the robes of a deceased monk, when the assembly chanted, "The robe of the Patriarch," [the Master] asked, "Who is it that chants?
The student replied, "What kind of robe of a deceased monk can you chant? A student asked, "When a wanderer returns home, what is the case?
The Master said, "With what will you make an offering? The student said, "I have nothing at all. The Master said, "Daily provisions."
"How is it? Later, when the Master was residing at Qingliang, he ascended the hall and said: "For those who have left the household life, it is sufficient simply to accord with the times and seasons.
When it is cold, it is cold; when it is hot, it is hot. If you wish to know the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should contemplate the causes and conditions of time and season.
The skillful means of past and present are not few. Have you not seen how the Venerable Shitou, while reading the *Zhaolun*, remarked: 'To realize all things as oneself'?"
Is it not only the Sage? Other teachers say that the Sage has no self, yet there is nothing he does not take as himself.
He has a certain saying called the *Cantong qi* (The Merging of Difference and Unity), which concludes by stating: "The mind of the Great Immortal of India does not exceed these words.
Throughout the middle sections, he merely speaks according to the occasion. Now, you, Venerable One, wish to realize that the myriad things are for your own sake.
This is because throughout the great earth, not a single dharma can be seen. He further instructed him, saying: "Do not let time pass in vain.

What I just said to you, Venerable One, was simply that one must act according to the season and the occasion. If one acts at the wrong time or misses the proper moment, that is to let time pass in vain.
To perceive form within that which is not form—Venerable One, to perceive form within that which is not form is [to err]."
"This is to shift the time and lose the occasion. Now tell me, is it appropriate or not to interpret form as non-form?
Venerable sir, if you understand it in this way, there is no connection at all. This is precisely 'the madman running between two ends'; what use is there in that?
Venerable sir, simply maintain your station and pass the time according to the season. Take care. A monk asked, "What is the house style of Qingliang? The Master said:
[The Master] said, "When you arrive at another place, simply say that you have come from Qingliang. [The monk] asked, "How can one attain the state where all dharmas are without obstruction?
The Master said, "What dharma is there for you, Venerable Sir, to be obstructed by? [The monk] said, "What about day and night? The Master said, "Idle talk."
Question: "When one contemplates the body as being like an illusion or a magical transformation, and likewise contemplates the internal in the same way, how is that?
The Master said: "Have you attained suchness yet? Question: "To seek immediate resonance, it is said that 'only non-duality' applies. What is this word of non-duality? The Master said:
"Could you add a little more? [The Master] asked. [The student] asked, "What is the Dharma-body? The Master said, "This is the response-body (*nirmāṇakāya*).
[The student] asked, "What is the primary meaning (*paramārtha*)? The Master said, "If I were to tell you, it would be the secondary meaning.

Master Liri served at Jinling, where he presided over three great monasteries and expounded the essential teachings morning and evening. At that time, the monastic communities throughout all regions followed his influence and transformation.
Those from distant lands who admired his Dharma traveled great distances to reach him. Thus, the orthodox lineage of Xuansha was revived within the Jiangbiao region.

As for the phrase "the place of movement," what is it? Some say: "The mind is clarified by means of objects; there is no need to recognize the objects themselves.
Others say: "Form is itself emptiness. Still others say: "It is not the wind or the banner that moves; one must have a subtle realization.

If you understand it in such ways, how does this relate to the intent of the Patriarchs? Since such interpretations are not permitted, you venerable seniors should surely know this. If, regarding this—
When one has thoroughly awakened within, what dharma-gate would not be clear? The skillful means of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are all at once and completely understood.
What further grounds for doubt could there be? Therefore, the ancients said: "With one awakening, a thousand things are clear; with one delusion, ten thousand confusions arise."
"Elder, how could it be that you understand one principle today and yet do not understand it tomorrow?
Is it that there is a portion of the 'upward' matter that is difficult to understand, while another portion is something that inferior ordinary people cannot understand?

Such a view—even if maintained for kalpas as numerous as dust motes—will only exhaust your own spirit and weary your thoughts; it is simply not possible. A monk asked: "The mark of the quiescence of all dharmas..."
"It cannot be proclaimed in words. How does the Master act for the sake of others? The Master said, "When you reach other places, ask this once more.

[The monk] said, "If that is so, then it is beyond words and phrases. The Master said, "To be clearly awake even in a dream. [The monk] asked, "When both oars and rudders have been set aside, how can one reach the other shore?
The Master said, "It is a blessing for your entire life. [The monk] asked, "What are the three kinds? The Master said, "..."
The patient asked: "Master, you have hit the mark. [The patient] asked: "What is the mind of the ancient Buddha?
The Master said: "This question is not weak. [The patient] asked: "What are the six characteristics? The Master said: "It is you yourself. [The patient] asked:

"What is skillful means? The Master said: "This question is most appropriate. [The patient] asked: "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? The Master said: "I certainly will not tell you."
[The student] asked, “Why do you not speak to me? The Master said, “I fear you would not understand. [The student] asked, “One flower opens into five petals;
the fruiting occurs naturally. What is ‘one flower opening into five petals’? The Master said, “The sun rises and the moon is bright.
[The student] asked, “What is ‘the fruiting occurring naturally’? The Master said, “Heaven and earth are luminous. [The student] asked, “What is...? (The question was left unfinished.)
Regarding the Buddha Aśoka, the Master said, "He brings such grief that he kills people. Question: From what do all the mountains, rivers, and the great earth arise?
The Master said: "From what does this question itself arise? Question: What is the mind that repeatedly arises? The Master said: "How can you avoid it?"
Question: "What is the eye of a śramaṇa? The Master said: "Black as lacquer. Question: "How is it when all news is cut off? The Master said: "Thank you for pointing it out. Question:
"What is it to transform things such that one is identical to the Tathāgata? The Master said: "What do you call 'things'? [The questioner] said:
"If that is so, then one is identical to the Tathāgata. The Master said: "Do not let out the howl of a jackal. Question: [Regarding] Nanda... (text ends)
"The Prince cut his flesh to give to his mother and his bones to give to his father; only then did he preach the Dharma for his parents upon a lotus flower.
"Unsure of what constitutes the Prince’s body," the Master said, "Everyone sees the Elder. The questioner asked, "In that case, the great trichiliocosm is of one true nature?
The Master said, "It is vaguely like a tune just fit to be heard, yet it is again disturbed by the wind."
While playing a different tune, he asked, "The six sense organs have all been extinguished; why then are principle and phenomena not clear? The Master said, "Where are they not clear?
The monk said, "If that is so, then principle and phenomena are both as they are. The Master said, "Where was my previous statement?
He ascended the hall and said, "Generally speaking, words and phrases must be free of leakage before they are acceptable. At that time, a monk asked, "What is being free of leakage?"
The Master said, "Your mouth is like your nostrils. A monk asked, "What is not realizing a single dharma?
The Master said, "Wait for my words. The monk asked, "What is realizing all dharmas? The Master said, "Why are you drunk?
Then he said, "As for this mountain monk answering you in such a way, how do you, venerable seniors, understand it? Is it perhaps a case of providing genuine assistance?"
Is it not that at this very moment there is not a single dharma to be realized? Is it not that you recognize its place of origin?
Is it not that the whole body is fully manifest? Do not misunderstand! Such an understanding is called "clinging to grass and leaning on wood."
This is worlds apart from the Buddha-dharma. Even if one’s ability to respond and discern were like a cascading river, it would only result in a perverted view.
If you merely value responding and discerning, what difficulty could there be? I only fear that it will be of no benefit to others and, on the contrary, lead to deception and error.
As for the discernment, questioning and answering, memorization, and discourse that you, Venerable One, have studied in the past—
The principles are extremely numerous. Why does your doubt not cease? You hear the expedient means of the ancient sages, yet you specifically fail to understand them;
this is simply because there is much that is empty and little that is real. It would be better for you, Senior, to see through it all at once from the very root of your feet:
what kind of principle is this? How many Dharma gates are there to provide you with doubts and seek a solution? Only then will you know that what you have held before...
The matter of study is nothing other than the root-source of birth and death; it is the livelihood within the realms of the aggregates. Therefore, the ancients said:
"If seeing and hearing are not liberated, one is like the moon in the water. "Be careful with this non-action. The Master had a verse which says:

"At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, it is not of the human world. Outside the mind there is no dharma; before one's eyes are green mountains. Fayan heard of this and said: "This single verse alone is sufficient."
He established my school. Later, the Master opened the hall at Prajñā Monastery and preached the Dharma in twelve assemblies.
Entering the hall, he said: "A hair swallows the vast ocean, yet the nature of the ocean remains unimpaired; a tiny speck is cast upon a sharp blade, yet the keen edge remains unmoved.

Whether one sees or does not see, whether one understands or does not understand—only I know it. He then uttered this verse: "Having briefly descended from the high peak, the Prajñā [Perfection of Wisdom] is fully proclaimed."
Pervading throughout the ten directions, the vast expanse of humans and devas is without distinction; the Dharma-realm manifests everywhere, both vertically and horizontally.
Take care! [The Master] ascends the hall. A monk asks: "I have heard an ancient saying: 'If a person sees Prajñā, they are bound by Prajñā;
if a person does not see Prajñā, they are also bound by Prajñā. Now, having seen Prajñā, why are they instead bound? The Master—
[The Master] said, "Tell me, what does Prajñā see? [The student] said, "It does not see Prajñā. "Why, then, is it also bound?
The Master said, "Tell me, where does Prajñā not see? He then said, "If one sees Prajñā, it is no longer named Prajñā."
One does not see Prajñā, nor is it called Prajñā. But how can one speak of seeing or not seeing? Therefore, the ancients said:
"If there is even one dharma lacking, it is not the Dharmakāya; if there is even one dharma in excess, it is not the Dharmakāya;
if there is even one dharma present, it is not the Dharmakāya; if there is not even one dharma present, it is not the Dharmakāya. This is the true nature of Prajñā.
This is the essential point. A monk asked, "Having just left the master’s chamber on Mount Ningfeng, you have now come to sit in this Prajñā assembly hall.
Regarding today’s family style, I ask the Master for a single phrase. The Master said, "In what way do you fall short?

The monk said, "If that is so, then the thunderous sound shakes the realm of heaven and earth, and there is no one who does not receive its grace. The Master said, "Fortunately, you have not yet understood; do not stick out your head just yet. The monk— [remained silent].
[The assembly] prostrated. The Master said: "To poke one's head out [of the crowd] is not the way.

May all you venerable elders join me in bearing witness, so that the Dharma may endure for a long time and the land may remain peaceful. Be careful. Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "I have heard it said in the teachings:
'The source of returning is non-dual, yet the gates of expedient means are many. What is the source of returning? The Master said: "You ask, and I answer. The monk asked: "What is..."
[The student] asks about the gate of skillful means (*upāya-mukha*). The Master says, "Answer my question. [The student] asks, "How does one proceed? The Master says, "Why do you act so invertedly?
[The student] asks, "One body is the infinite body; the infinite body is one body. What is the infinite body? The Master says, "One body.

[The student] says, "If that is so, then what was seen at Vulture Peak in the past is now being witnessed directly. The Master says, "If the principle is correct," [the student] says, "Then it is so. The Master says, "Indeed."
As he was walking, he said: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time all bear witness to the Elder at this very moment.
How, then, do you understand this, Elder? If you understand it, there shall be no shifting; not even a single thread of a hair can be moved or altered. Why is this?

Because the past, future, and present—these three limits—are the Elder himself. Elder, for your part, let the three limits be like rain falling upon the great ocean, where every drop is [one with the whole]."

Fullness. A single speck of dust contains the emptiness of nature; the entire Dharma-realm is fully encompassed. Take heed! Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "The fourfold assembly has gathered like clouds; devas and humans pay respectful homage.
With our eyes beholding your honored countenance, we pray that you will proclaim the Prajñā. The Master said: "Take this clearly to heart. The monk said:

"As the Master proclaims the wondrous Dharma, may the King live ten thousand years, and may the people enjoy peace and happiness. The Master said: "Who told you that? The monk said: "It is the very nature of things (dharmatā)."
However, the Master said, "You are indeed quick-witted. You ask: 'The Buddhas of the three periods do not know that there is; the cat and the white ox, however, do know that there is.
Since they are the Buddhas of the three periods, why do they not know that there is? The Master said, "It is actually you who know that there is.
[The student] asked, "Why do the cat and the white ox, however, know that there is? The Master said, "Where have you seen them?"
"The Buddhas of the three periods of time have asked: according to the teachings we receive, it is said that 'the eye does not see form-objects' and 'the mind does not know dharmas.
What does it mean for the eye not to see form-objects? The Master said, "It is actually the ear that sees.

"What does it mean for the mind not to know dharmas? The Master said, "The eye knows. "If that is so, then the paths of seeing and hearing are cut off, yet sounds and forms are clamorous. The Master said:
"Who told you that? He replied: "As for all questions and answers, they are like the meeting of needle points;
there is not the slightest discrepancy. There is no matter that is not penetrated, and no principle that is not complete.

This is truly because all speech, all samādhis—whether horizontal or vertical, deep or shallow, hidden or manifest, coming or going—are the gate of the true mark (*dharmatā*) of all Buddhas, which is verified right now, at this very moment."
Take this up. Be careful. [The Master] ascends the hall and says: An ancient said, "What is Chan? The three realms are continuous.
What is the Way? The ten directions are vast. Why does he say the three realms are continuous? Where is the principle that the ten directions are vast?
Do you wish to understand? Block the eyes; block the ears; block the tongue, body, and mind. Leave no opening whatsoever.
There is no place for movement. Elder, how do you understand this? It cannot be grasped horizontally; it cannot be grasped vertically;

it cannot be grasped lengthwise; it cannot be seized away. There is no place for the application of mind, nor is there any place for its establishment. If you can understand it in this way, [you have understood].
From the very beginning, the Dharma-gate of assembly is free from selection; all speech is free from leakage.
Once there was a monk who asked, "What is speech that is free from leakage? I told him, "The mouth is like the nostrils—how excellent!
If you, Venerable One, understand it in this way, naturally no wind will pass through. If you can recognize that the entirety of the ten directions is the diamond eye, [you have understood].
"Take care, and bid you farewell. He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The world is at peace; may Your Majesty live long. What is the King?
The Master said, "The sun blazes and the moon is bright. The monk asked, "How should one understand this? The Master said, "Who is the student?
He then said, "The world is at peace; may the Great King live long; the land is abundant and joyful, free from all calamities and hardships. These are the words of the Buddha, as spoken of old."
"Unchanging. Now, not shifting. A single word can settle both antiquity and the present; grasp this well.
Furthermore, a monk asked, "I have heard an ancient saying: 'There is a thing prior to heaven and earth; formless, it is fundamentally silent and desolate.

How is it that there is a thing prior to heaven and earth? The Master said, "Neither identical nor joined. The monk asked, "How is it that it is formless and fundamentally silent and desolate? The Master said... [text ends]
[The monk] asked, "Who asks about that which precedes heaven and earth? [Dongshan] said, "If so, then you shall go alone to roam in the quiet, still forest.

The Master said, "Why do you speak such nonsense? He then continued, "The Buddha-dharma is not this kind of principle. Do you wish to understand? When words are uttered, they are not sound; before form, there is no object.
Only then will you understand that all under heaven is at peace and the Great King enjoys long life. [He stood for a long time. "Take care."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Buddha-dharma is already manifest; all things are fully complete. Have you not heard it said: 'Perfectly identical to the great void, there is neither deficiency nor excess'?
If this is so, then who is lacking and who has a surplus? Who is right and who is wrong? Who is the one who understands and who is the one who does not understand?
Therefore it is said: 'If you go east, you are still the Venerable One; if you go west, you are still the Venerable One. South..."
Going west is also the Elder; going north is also the Elder. For what reason do east, west, south, and north come to be established?
If you can understand this, the paths of seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing will naturally be cut off, and all dharmas will manifest before you. Why is this so?
Because the Dharmakāya is without marks, yet forms appear before every eye; Prajñā is without cognition, yet it illuminates in response to conditions—all at once.
"Understand this thoroughly, all you elders. For one who has left the household life, what else is there to do? This is the principle inherent within; it is not something extraordinary.
To recognize the mind and reach the source—therefore, one is called a śramaṇa. If you recognize the mind as brilliantly clear, there is truly not a hair’s breadth of obstruction, O Elders.
[He stood for a long time. "Take care. He ascended the hall. A monk asked: "I wish to enter the state of non-..."

[The Master] said: "It is the ocean. First, one must board the boat of *prajñā*. What is the boat of *prajñā*? The Master said: "Always abiding nowhere. [The student] asked: "What is the ocean of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*)?
The Master said: "First, understand the boat of *prajñā*. [The student] asked: "An ancient worthy said:

'To ascend to heaven, one does not borrow a ladder; across the earth, there is no path to walk. What is 'to ascend to heaven without borrowing a ladder'? The Master said: "Not leaving behind even a single thread."
Fadi asked, "What is meant by 'the entire ground has no path to walk upon'? The Master said, "What did I just tell you?

He then continued, "The hundreds of thousands of gates of samādhi, the hundreds of thousands of gates of supernatural powers, and the hundreds of thousands of gates of wondrous function—all do not transcend the ocean of prajñā.
Why is this? Because all dharmas are established upon the foundation of non-abiding. Therefore it is said:"
Arising and ceasing, going and coming, the heterodox and the orthodox, movement and stillness—these myriad transformations are the gate of the great samādhi of all Buddhas;
there is nothing that surpasses this. All you venerable elders, investigate this thoroughly to increase the life-span of the Buddha-dharma. Be careful. Ascending the hall, a monk asked:
"The World-Honored One entrusted the Eye of the True Dharma to Mahākāśyapa. But as for Kāśyapa being at Piṇḍava..."
[Luohan] asked, "I do not know to whom you have entrusted [the Dharma]. The Master said, "Who would I teach it to?
[Luohan] said, "If that is so, then the entrustment at Vulture Peak is no different from today. The Master said, "Where did you see Vulture Peak?
[Luohan] asked Fayan Wenyi, "The Patriarch personally transmitted the 'Precious Seal. I wonder, to whom should it be entrusted today? The Master said, "The drum beats: dong, dong. One end..."
[The Master] struck [the gong]. It rang out from both ends. He said, "If that is so, then the thousand sages are of one kindred, and the ancient and the modern are no different.
The Master said, "The waves of the Zen river are stilled; you seek the water but lose the source. The monk Qingyu asked, "When an Emperor requests your presence, you respond to the King’s grace.

Within this Prajñā assembly, we request that you proclaim the Dharma. The Master said, "Take this clearly to heart. [Qingyu] said, "If that is so, then it is like the jeweled nets of the Cloud Terrace."
They performed the wondrous sound together. The Master asked, "Where is Qingyu? He replied, "The Dharma King’s Dharma is thus. The Master asked, "Who can testify to this?
He then said, "The entrustment at Vulture Peak was clear; let all you venerable elders verify it at once. If you can verify it..."

There is no other principle; it is simply as it is now, like the vast void. Whether the sun is bright or the clouds are dark, the mountains, rivers, the great earth, and all conditioned worlds are clearly manifest; even the unconditioned is likewise so.
From the time the World-Honored One entrusted [the Dharma] until the present, there has not been the slightest difference. To whom else could it be entrusted? Therefore, the Patriarch—
The Way: The mind is the original mind from the beginning; this original mind is not a dharma that exists. If there were a dharma that existed, there would be an original mind;
but since it is neither mind nor fundamental dharma, this is the model for the entrustment at Vulture Peak. All you venerable seniors, grasp this thoroughly!

Do not let your time pass in vain. The kindness of the king is difficult to repay; the kindness of the Buddhas is difficult to repay; the kindness of parents and teachers is difficult to repay. Ten...
The kindness of the donor is already difficult to repay; how much more so when one establishes such a sequence for the flourishing of the Buddha-Dharma.
If it were not for the power of the King’s grace, how could this have been achieved? If you wish to repay his kindness, you must clarify the eye of the Way and enter the ocean-nature of Prajñā;
only then will it be attained. [I] take my leave and bid you farewell. Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "An ancient worthy said: 'The person is empty, and the dharmas are also empty.'"
"The two marks are fundamentally identical. The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. The student said, "I do not understand. I beg the Master for a skillful means.

The Master said, "Where is it that this is not a skillful means? [The student] asked about the provisional nature of names and phenomena, the emptiness of persons and phenomena, and how to turn away from all conditions;

he requested the Master to point directly. The Master said, "Thank you for this question. [The student] said, "If one does not behold the magnificence of the royal palace, how can one know [its splendor]?"
The Son of Heaven was honored. The Master said, "In your greed to gaze at the moon in the heavens, you have lost the oar in your hand.
He asked about the Middle Way in the Teachings: "Because the mind is pure, the Dharma-realm is pure. What is this pure mind? The Master said, "The kalaviṅka bird and the saṃjīva bird.
[The student] asked, "Are these one with the Dharma-realm, or are they two? The Master said, "You should ask someone else yourself," and then he spoke further.
The Great Way is vast and open; how could it be confined by past or present? Nameless and formless, this is the Dharma and this is cultivation.

This is truly because the Dharma-realm is boundless and the mind is likewise limitless. There is no phenomenon that does not manifest, and no word that does not reveal it. To realize this is what is called *prajñā*.

When the principle is manifest before one, it is identical to the True Limit (*bhūtakoṭi*). All mountains, rivers, and the great earth, the myriad phenomena of the forested universe, and even walls—[are all thus].
There is not even a speck of rubble; nothing whatsoever can be lacking. There is no need to stand for long; take care. Ascending the hall, a monk asked:
"I have heard the Master say, 'The nine heavens uphold the jade seal; the seven Buddhas manifest the prior mind. What is this seal? The Master said:
He did not reveal the text. [The student] asked, "What is the mind? The Master said, "Your name is An-si.
He then said, "The nature-sea of the Dharma-realm is like a box and its lid, like a hook and its lock, like gold and gold;

in every position they are all equal, without the slightest discrepancy, without being mixed or confused, neither one nor different, neither the same nor distinct. If you return to the ground of reality, every dharma..."
All reach the bottom. It is not that it is "so" simply because one comes forward and asks "how" or "what"; nor is it "not so" when one does not ask.

When sitting on the long benches, it exists; when not sitting, it does not exist. Yet, as for the teachings of the venerable masters throughout all quarters, they are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
the entire Great Canon of the Tathāgata, volume after volume, speaks entirely of the Buddha’s principle.
Every word speaks exhaustively of the Buddha-mind. Why, then, do you fail to understand?

If you continue to weave together the teachings and seek understanding through the conscious intellect, even if you were to spend eons as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, you still could not attain penetration.

This is called inverted knowledge and views; it is the calculating mind’s livelihood, and there is no place in it where true power is found. This is because the foundation of your very roots is not clear.

If one exhaustively investigates the source of all Buddhas' teachings, the great treasuries as numerous as the sands of the Ganges will manifest all at once—neither lacking even a hair’s breadth, nor exceeding it by a hair’s breadth.
The Buddhas appear in the world constantly and preach the Dharma constantly; their saving of sentient beings never ceases.

Even down to the cries of monkeys and the calls of birds, and the grasses, trees, and forests, they always assist this Elder in triggering his realization; there has not been a single moment when this was not so.
As the Elder, there is such a marvelous state as this. It is truly to be cherished.
May all you Elders investigate it thoroughly, so that the Dharma may long abide in the world, increasing the lifespan of humans and devas, and bringing peace and security to the king and his realm.
Be careful. Entering the hall, he cited the ancients who said: "I have a single word; whether in the heavens or among men, if people do not understand it, [it is like] green water and blue..."
"Shan! Furthermore, what is the principle of this 'one word'? The words of the ancients must be understood thoroughly before they can be grasped.
If one merely uses words to name words, there will be no point of realization. It is only by investigating the very root of all phenomena that one finally understands the 'one word.
This 'one word' is not something to be conceptualized or understood through mere intellectual calculation; it is called the 'one word' [only in this sense]."
When the path of language is cut off and the sphere of mental activity ceases, one finally reaches the realm of the ancients. Yet even this is not it;

do not mistakenly understand it as closing one's eyes and hiding the pupils, seeing nothing in the dark, and calling that "the cutting off of the path of language. The Buddha-dharma is not such a principle.
Do you wish to understand? Even if one were to speak for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there would never have been even half [of it].
The phrase is complete. For aeons as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, the various elders have not spoken it, nor has there ever been even half a phrase lacking.
You must understand it thoroughly from the very depths before you may attain it. If you deliberate upon names and words in such a manner, you will merely exhaust your mind and strength to no avail.
I ask the elders to bear witness together: those who are beginners in their later studies must quickly investigate and grasp this. I shall remain standing for a long time; cherish it.
[The Master] ascended the hall. A monk asked, "A skull constantly dries the world; the nostrils touch the family style. What is 'a skull constantly drying the world'?
The Master said, "Wait for my answer. [The monk] asked, "What is 'the nostrils touching the family style'?
The Master said, "From time to time, I raise it once more. [The monk] asked, "One person holds a torch and burns his own body; another..."

"A man is carrying ice. A corpse lies across the road. Which of these two can distinguish the Way? The Master said, "The one who does not leave it behind. [The monk] said, "I do not understand. I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master said, "Your name is Jingxin (Respectful New). [The monk] said, "I wonder if there is anyone else who can testify to this?
The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "Who is the witness? The Master said, "Jingxin. [The monk] asked about Niu-tou before he had seen the First Patriarch.
"How was it during the time of the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "A sacred trace in a strange realm; all who behold it admire it. [The monk] asked, "What is it like after one has seen it?
The Master said, "What did I just tell you? [The monk] asked, "An ancient said: 'Striking at empty space, the *gǔgǔ* resounds.'"
The stone man and the wooden man respond in unison. In the sixth month, snow falls in profusion. This is the Tathāgata’s Great Perfect Enlightenment.
What is it that strikes at empty space? The Master said: "A servant from Mount Kunlun wears iron trousers;
with each blow of the staff, he takes a step. [The student] said: "If that is so, then the stone man and the wooden man respond in unison. The Master said: "Do you hear?"

Mo then said: "The Dharma-gates of all Buddhas are always thus. They are like the great ocean, with its thousands of waves and myriad ripples, which never for a moment abide, never for a moment exist, and never for a moment do not exist.
In this vast expanse, there is luminous sovereignty: the three periods of time are contained within the tip of a hair, and past and present are perfected in a single thought-moment.
You must attain thorough and fundamental penetration before you can realize this; it is not otherwise."

I ask a single word and respond with a turning phrase; skillfully constructing principles like wind, clouds, water, and moon, or matching rhymes in four- and six-character couplets—do not mistake these for the Buddha-dharma and deceive yourselves.
O venerable elders, in the end, this is of no benefit. If you understand it thoroughly to the bottom, there is truly nothing to hide.
There is not a single land where it is not manifest, nor a single speck of dust where it does not appear. Right here and now, the ordinary person stands on the same level as all Buddhas.
"Do not exert even a hair’s breadth of effort; grasp this all at once. Be careful, for there is nothing more to do.
The Master was then asked by Master Ming of Xingjiao: "Kāśyapa held Śākyamuni’s six-foot robe at Mount Kukkuṭapāda, awaiting Maitreya’s descent.
When he shall don that six-foot robe upon his thousand-foot body, it will fit perfectly. But as for Śākya..."
“Kāśyapa’s body was sixteen feet tall; Maitreya’s body is one thousand feet tall. Is it that his body understands shortness, or is it that his robes understand length?
The Master said, “You have understood it backwards. Ming brushed out his sleeves and went out.

The Master said, “Little fellow, if I had answered you as being wrong, there would have been cause and effect. If you were not wrong, I would have seen it for myself. Ming returned home. Seven days later—
One day, he spat up blood. Master Fuguang urged him, saying, "You must go quickly to repent.

Ming went to the master’s quarters and wept bitterly, saying, "I pray that the Master will show compassion and grant me permission to repent. The Master said, "It is like a person who has fallen to the ground;
they rise from the ground. I have never taught you how to rise from a fall. Ming spoke again, saying, "If you grant me permission to repent, I shall serve you for the rest of my life."

The attendant asked, "Master, please provide a verse for this. The Master spoke: "The Way of Buddha after Buddha is equal; yet it appears as high or low. Śākyamuni and Maitreya are like a seal impressing clay.
In the fourth year of the Kaibao era, the year of Xinwei, the western peak of Mount Kōfuku suddenly collapsed, its sound shaking the entire mountain. The Master said:
"It will not be long. In the sixth month of next year, a great star shall fall upon the peak, and the forest trees shall turn white.

Thereupon, the Master manifested illness at Lotus Peak; his inquiries and instructions remained as usual until the twenty-eighth day, when he gathered the assembly to bid them farewell and passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture.
Chan Master Taichin Fading of Qingliang in Jinling was a native of Weifu. From birth, he knew the Way; his eloquence was unimpeded.
Having entered the chamber of Fayen, the assembly of disciples gathered around him, all of whom declared him a master of exceptional skill. He first resided at Shuanglin Monastery in Hongzhou.
On the day he ascended the Dharma seat, he pointed to it and said: "In former times, venerable patriarchs of this mountain have preached the Dharma here."
The seat is high and vast; how can one of no talent ascend it? There is an ancient saying:
"One must pay homage to the Tathāgata Sumerudīparāja before one may take a seat. But tell me, where is the Tathāgata Sumerudīparāja now? Does the assembly wish to see him?
After a single prostration, he ascended the seat and remained silent for a long while, then said, "The assembly is exactly like this.
Is there anyone who understands? A monk asked, "What is the realm of the Twin Trees? The Master said, "It cannot even be painted.
The monk asked, "What about the person within the realm? The Master said, "Go away! You do not even recognize the realm; first find that realm! Another monk asked, "When one Buddha appears..."
[The Master said: "The world shakes heaven and earth. When the Abbot appears in the world, in which direction does he cause the shaking? The Master said: "Where do you see the shaking?
[The monk] said: "What can be done about this very moment? The Master said: "What business is there today? A monk came forward and prostrated.
The Master said, "As for the Way, I thanked you for your request earlier; what good thing could I possibly give you?

As the monk was about to ask further, the Master said, "I thought we were on the same wavelength, yet it turns out you do not understand. A monk asked, "What is the profound, secret meaning of the West? The Master said, "Suffering.

A monk asked, "When one Buddha appears in the world, he universally moistens all living beings. When you, Master, appear in the world, for whom are you acting? The Master said: [The text here ends abruptly].
[The questioner] said, "It is not for nothing. [The Master] said, "If that is so, then the great assembly has someone to rely upon.
The Master said, "Why bother? He then continued, "Stay a while. Your Excellency and the entire assembly have been most diligent and earnest in inviting me today.
How can this extraordinary merit be adequately described? Therefore it is said: 'Let those who have not yet realized listen to one word. Who is it right now?"
He opened his mouth and immediately descended from the seat. Standing leaning on his staff, he addressed the assembly, saying:

"Do you understand? The devas and nāgas listen in silence as flowers rain down; do not take this as a painted image of Subhūti to carry away. For now, simply believe, accept, and practice accordingly."
He questioned a newly arrived monk, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "Mount Lu. The Master picked up the incense box and said, "Is there also this thing at Mount Lu?
The monk was speechless. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "I have come seeking the fragrance to pay my respects to the Master.
A monk asked, "When the hundred skeletal parts all decay and scatter, that one thing remains eternally conscious. I wonder, how far apart are the hundred skeletal parts and that one thing?"
The Master said, "The hundred limbs are one thing; the one thing is the hundred limbs. He subsequently resided at the Huguo Cloister of Shanglan.
A monk asked, "When drums are struck in all ten directions, they are heard simultaneously in ten places. What is this 'hearing'? The Master said, "From which direction have you come?"

Question: "One practices the Bodhisattva path without being stained by the characteristics of phenomena (*dharmalakṣaṇa*). What is this Bodhisattva path? The Master said: "The characteristics of all phenomena. [The student] asked:
"How can one avoid being stained? The Master said: "In what place would you be stained? Question: "Before long, the examination hall will open.
Will you allow students to take their selection there as well? The Master said: "You are a person who has already been marked on the forehead [as a failure]. He added: "You are..."
"What subject matter? [The questioner asked. "How is it that one expounds the great Dharma? The Master said, "My exposition is like yours.

Later, while residing at Longguang Monastery in Jinling, he ascended the hall. The Rector struck the gavel and said, "O assembly of dragons and elephants at this Dharma feast, you should contemplate the primary meaning.
The Master said, "The Rector has already reached the secondary meaning; Elder, as for you now, what rank does it occupy?"
Yi then raised his sleeve and said, "Do you understand? O assembly, this is dancing with hands and feet.
Do not say that he was once a master of music five hundred lifetimes ago. If there are any lingering doubts, please request an instruction.
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the orthodox lineage of all Buddhas? The Master said, "What lineage are you? The monk asked, "How so? The Master said, "How?"
[The monk] did not understand. He asked, "Master Shanglan once personally sang a verse; what is the matter with Longguang today? The Master said, "When did you ever come to Shanglan?
[The monk] asked, "What about 'attending to things as they truly are'? The Master said, "If it is not attending to things as they truly are, then seek it elsewhere.
He asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "First ask about the small meaning, and then come back and I will tell you."
"Great Intention," the Master later resided at the Great Site of Qingliang. He ascended the hall, and as a monk came forward to prostrate, the Master said, "This monk comes first;
he shall answer on behalf of the assembly for the profound kindness of the National Preceptor. The monk then asked, "The National Preceptor has issued an invitation."

The patriarchal seat was opened once more. A student came forward and requested, "I pray that the Master will directly point out the source of the mind. The Master said, "Having come up, go back down.
The student asked, "Fayan’s single lamp divided its light to illuminate the world; whose light does the Master’s single lamp divide to illuminate? The Master said:
"From where does the Dharma-eye shine forth? The Master replied, "I originally intended to dwell in the mountains to hide my ineptitude and pass my time nursing my illness;
however, because the late Master has a case that remains unresolved, I have come out to settle it for him.
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the unresolved case of the late Master? The Master struck him and said, "The Patriarch did not..."

[The Master] said, "It is finished. The calamity will extend to your descendants. [The King] asked, "Where does the fault lie? The Master replied, "The fault lies with me; the calamity falls upon you.
When the Prince of Jiangnan was still the Duke of Zheng, he received the Dharma of the Mind from the chamber of Fayen. Subsequently, when Fayen entered nirvana...
He once asked the Master, "Does the former master have any unresolved case? The Master replied, "I see you analyzing it.
On another day, he asked again, "I have heard that the Elder has some extraordinary insights regarding the former master.
The Master made a gesture as if rising. The Ruler said, "Please sit down. The Master addressed the assembly, saying, "The former master’s Dharma seat had five hundred followers; now..."
There are only a dozen or so people who act as leaders and guides in various regions. Do you think there might be anyone among them who points out the wrong path?
If they were to point one astray, it would lead to entering water or fire, falling into pits or ditches. Yet the ancients also said:

"If I head toward the mountain of blades, the mountain of blades shall collapse of its own accord; if I head toward the cauldron of boiling oil, the cauldron of boiling oil shall extinguish itself. Now then—
"How do you deliberate on this? Your words are fluent, yet when questioned, you become hesitant.
Why is that? It is simply because we have been apart for a long time. Elder, you should understand: where could I possibly go that I cannot reach? There is nowhere I cannot go."
"For the sake of the various faculties such as the eye, and for the various phenomena such as form—setting those phenomena aside for a moment, Elder, open your eyes and see what!
Therefore it is said: 'Not seeing a single dharma is the Tathāgata; only then can one be named Avalokiteśvara. Take care!

In the sixth month of the seventh year of the Kaibao era, the Master manifested illness and addressed the assembly, saying: "This old monk lies ill; I have forcibly dragged myself here to give this to you."

We meet face to face; wherever one may be now is a site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). It is just like a conjured city (*nirmāṇapurī*). But tell me, what is this conjured city? Have you not seen the ancient Guide say:
"The jewel-studded destination is not far away; you must continue forward"? Yet, upon arriving at the city, he further said: [It is merely a conjured city].
"I have manifested this through transformation. Now, you people, try and state a principle for me to see:
Is this the Tathāgata-dhyāna or the Patriarchal-dhyāna? Can you still determine it? Although you are all late-born, you must know that you have been granted a great honor by our National Master.
In every superior location, he has established a Dharma-hall, and whatever is required there is provided without lack; he only desires that you open your mouths. Now, you do not know."

Which of these is your mouth? How can you hope to repay the four debts of gratitude and respond to the three realms of existence? Do you wish to understand this? Simply recognize the mouth and there will surely be no fault.
Even if there were faults, they would exist because of you. Now, as fire and wind press upon me, going or staying is the eternal Way.

I, this old monk, have served as abbot for nearly twelve years. Throughout this time, I have constantly received the support and encouragement of the sovereign, as well as from donors, fellow practitioners from the ten directions, administrative officials, and junior disciples;
all have served me with sincere hearts. This is something difficult to express in words, yet it is evident in their conduct—some even wear hempen robes and carry cloth sashes.

This is merely to conform to worldly convention; my Way contradicts the conventional truth. Now, tell me, is it better to conform or to contradict? However, if one simply conforms to my Way, there will be no delusion.

As for my remains, I must request a burial plot from the side of the Venerable Master Dazhizang of the South Mountain, so that my ascent and descent may remain distinct and clear, without sinking into oblivion.
Strive with diligence and cherish this well. On the twenty-fourth day, I sat in meditation.
He passed away there.

Chan Master Qingsong of Lingyin Temple in Hangzhou was a native of Fuzhou. When he first visited Fayen, Fayen pointed to the falling rain and said to him, "Every drop falls right into the eyes of the Venerable.
At first, the Master did not understand the meaning. Later, while reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, he finally realized it.
He attained profound realization and received the seal of approval from [Zhaozhou]. He returned to Mount Siming in Mingzhou, where he established a hermitage.
Qian Yi, the Regional Commander, treated him with the etiquette due to a master. King Zhongyi ordered him to propagate the Dharma at two locations in Lin’an.
Later, he resided at Lingyin Upper Monastery and was granted the title Chan Master Liaowu. Entering the hall, he said: "The Buddhas of the ten directions are always before you; do you see them?"
If one says that there is seeing, is it seen with the mind or is it seen with the eyes? Therefore it is said: "All dharmas are neither born nor extinguished;
if one can understand them in this way, the Buddhas are ever present before one. It is also said: "To see form is to see the mind."
Furthermore, what do you call "mind"? Are the mountains, rivers, the great earth, the myriad phenomena, the colors blue, yellow, red, and white, and the characteristics of male and female the mind?
Or are they not the mind? If they are the mind, why do they instead become material objects?
If they are not the mind, yet it is also said that "upon seeing form, one sees the mind. Do you understand? It is simply because of delusion regarding this that one falls into perversion.
There are various differences, yet within that which is neither identical nor different, one forcibly creates identity and difference.
If you can now directly accept this at once, your fundamental mind will suddenly open up; it will be luminously clear, with not a single thing to be seen or heard.

If you seek liberation apart from the mind, the ancients called this "searching for the source in the waves"; it is ultimately difficult to awaken to. A monk asked: "When both the faculties and their objects have vanished..."

"What principle or phenomenon is not yet understood? The Master said, "Set aside the matter of phenomena and principles for a moment; what do you call the sense bases and objects when they are both utterly extinguished?
Question: "What is the primary meaning of Avalokiteśvara? The Master said, "Wrong. Question: "The true nature of ignorance is itself Buddha-nature.
What is Buddha-nature? The Master said, "What do you call ignorance? Question: "What is the Master? The Master said, "What do you call 'Master'?"
Regarding family style: The Master said, "From antiquity to the present, when there is neither question nor answer—how is it then?

The Master said, "Why speak in your sleep? Question: "How was it before Niu-tou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "Green mountains and blue waters. Question: "How was it after he saw him?
The Master said, "Blue waters and green mountains. The Master asked a monk, "Do you understand the Buddha-dharma? The monk replied, "I do not understand."
The Master said, "Are you truly not understanding? The monk replied, "Yes. The Master said, "Go for now; come back at another time. The monk said, "I take my leave.
The Master said, "That is not the principle. [The monk] asked, "What is Mahāprajñā? The Master said, "The snow falls vast and boundless.
The monk was speechless. The Master asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master showed him this verse: Mahāprajñā...

"O assembly of dragons and elephants at this Dharma feast, you should contemplate the primary principle. The Master says: "If it is the primary principle, then how do you contemplate it? In this way..."

"When the Buddhas appear in the world, they preach the Dharma to deliver beings, moving heaven and earth. When the Master appears in the world..."

"Of old there was Jinfeng; today there is Guizong. I do not know whether they are one or two. The Master said, "Thank you for providing this testimony.
Question: "Fayan’s single arrow shot straight at Guizong; as for Guizong’s single arrow, whom should it shoot? The Master said, "Do not slander my Dharma-eye. Question:
"Today the Military Commissioner has personally realized the Dharma; where does the Master repay his profound kindness? The Master said, [silence].
He said, "What should I teach you so that you may attain it? He then replied, "A question and an answer have no end. The Buddha-dharma is not such a principle.
"O Great Assembly, the events of this day were certainly not my original intention. As for dwelling in the mountains, I had no ulterior motive;
as for attaining Buddhahood in the past, I likewise had no heart for it. It was simply because I accepted the request of the military commander."
The assembly of this temple has come here with sincere hearts; what, then, can be said? Do you understand? If you cannot believe it, the ancients said:
"We meet and wish to call out to one another, yet we remain silent, unable to speak. How do you understand this?
If you understand, you will be worthy to repay the unrequited kindness and sufficiently assist the transformation of non-action. If you do not understand, do not...
When the Venerable Master ascends the hall, he merely cites the words of an ancient. This great event is as vast as the heavens and as deep as the sea; no metaphor can reach it.
Furthermore, I dare not venture to praise the imperial wind or dedicate merit to the ranks of the court. Why is this? An ancient said, "I have long been praying.
How much more so for the sagely and enlightened ruler of the present day! Take care. A monk asked: "What is the King of Emptiness?"
[The Master] was at the Temple. A student said, "Do not slight the deity. [The student] asked, "What is it like to be among those within the temple? The Master said, "I did not deceive you just now.

[The student] asked, "When the numinous tortoise has not yet produced its omens, what is it like? The Master said, "Is it auspicious? Is it ominous? [The student] asked, "Before one has reached the source, I beg the Master for a skillful means.

The Master said, "One has already reached it. [The student] said, "After reaching it, what is it like? The Master said, "In the end, one would not ask in such a manner. [The student] asked. The Master said, "... (The text here ends abruptly).
A monk asked, "What sutra are you reading? He replied, "The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra*. The Master said, "Since you are a śramaṇa, why are you reading the *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra*?
The monk was speechless. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying: "Its application throughout past and present is inexhaustible."
Chan Master Daoheng of Baizhang in Hongzhou went to study under Fayan. He requested instruction regarding the story of the outsider asking the Buddha:

"I do not ask about words; I do not ask about wordlessness. Before he had finished recounting these words, Fayan said, "Stop! Stop! Do you intend to understand this by looking toward the World-Honored One’s long silence?
From this, the Master attained awakening. Later, when he ascended the hall, he said: "Ride this precious vehicle straight to the Way."
[The Master was] at the site. Every day many senior monks came to visit him, but there was no one to receive them.

As the weather was cold, he did not wish for them to stand for long and instead invited them to turn their carriages back, saying, "Take care. A monk asked, "What is the matter of a student traveling on foot?
The Master said, "Have you even managed to break your staff yet? Another asked, "An ancient said, 'Śākyamuni and I studied together. I do not know what it means to have studied together with him."
The man said, "Only those of the same rank can know. The Master said, "If that is so, then you do not understand how to practice Zen.

The man asked, "How should one approach this person? The Master said, "In that case, you do not understand how to practice. The man asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

The Master said, "Usually, people do not ask the right question. The man asked, "How should one sing the song of returning home? The Master said, "Even if you were to sing it, it would fall short of your expectations."
Later, [a monk] asked, "What is the realm of Baizhang? The Master said, "How is it different from Yunju? [Another monk] asked, "What is the single phrase by which Baizhang saves people?
The Master said, "If you go to other places, you must ask about this thoroughly. He then added, "In truth, there is nothing at all."
Each and every person here is a Buddha. What further doubt could there be to have reached this place? An ancient said: "The ten directions gather together;
each and every one studies non-action. This is the field for selecting Buddhas; with an empty mind, they return as the valedictorian. But what is this "empty mind"?
It is not merely sitting there with eyes closed and a cold composure—that is precisely the functioning of the conscious intellect.
Consider this: does the Elder wish to realize that the mind is empty? Simply recognize the mind, and you will see that the mind is empty.
Thus it is said: "The past has already passed; do not calculate the future. Sit upright and without concern; who has ever called out to you?"
If someone calls out to you, Elder, you should respond; it is not right not to respond. If you respond, who would call out to the Elder?
If you do not respond, yet you are not afflicted by deafness, [you must realize that] the essence of the three periods of time is empty, and you are certainly not a block of wood.
Therefore, the ancients said: "When the mind is empty, one may see the Dharma King. Do you see the Dharma King? It is simply this old, sick monk.
Furthermore, do not say that he is merely boasting of his own excellence. Take care! A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?

The Master said, "How many things do you have that you do not ask about? The monk cited an instance: Someone asked Xuansha, "I am not asking about the Three Vehicles or the twelve divisions of the teachings..."
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Sha said, "The Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings are unnecessary.
I do not understand; I beg the Master to explain them for me. The Master said, "You truly do not understand. Sha replied, "I truly do not understand. The Master then showed him this verse:
"Do not seek the Three Vehicles; seek the Ancestor. The Three Vehicles are not what I share with you.

If you now wish to comprehend the fundamental principle, listen to the cry of the ape in the chaotic peaks at the end of the night. He ascended the hall and said: "Venerable elders, you have just come out from the Sangha Hall.
Before your feet have even crossed the threshold, you should have turned back; that would have already been a repetition of the verse. Why then do you come here again?"
One must not repeatedly apply the "cutting foot" (the final character) to the back [of the verse]. An ancient said: "Studying others is not as good as studying oneself.
Therefore it is said: "The myriad phenomena of the universe are the master of Sudhana; karmic delusions and worldly toil are the realm of Samantabhadra.
If you can study in this way, you are studying alongside Sudhana. If you are unwilling to study in this manner, then return to the hall.
Facing the fire. Take this from the Brahmin Jñānagupta (Shengre). Be careful. [The Master] ascends the hall; as soon as the assembly has gathered, he says, "Go drink tea.
At other times when the assembly gathers, he simply says, "Be careful" (*zhēnzhòng*). At yet other times when the assembly gathers, he simply says, "Rest. Later, there is a verse that says:
