Do you understand? If there were anyone today who gave rise to a view of the Buddha-dharma, I would simply brew two cups of tea with them.
But tell me: is this a reward for him or a punishment? Is it the same as the intent of the teachings or different from the intent of the teachings?

In the fourth year of the Kaibao era, the general Ling Chao founded a monastery at Wuyun Mountain to serve as the master’s place for his final years. The master would often carry a large fan while begging for money.

He purchased meat to feed the tiger, and the tiger would always come to meet him; he would carry it back to the mountain with him. In the second year of the Yongxi era, he manifested parinirvāṇa and was interred in a stupa at this very monastery.
On the occasion of the Dharma Master Fadu Huìyuè of Bào'ēn Monastery in Hangzhou ascending the hall, he spoke for several nights with the various senior monks.
This Western talk has not yet exhausted its source. Today, for the sake of you venerable elders, I shall open wide the skillful means and speak it all at once.
Do you still wish to hear it? Long standing, take care. A monk asked, "As this student has come up here in this manner, I ask the Master to receive me.
The Master said, "I do not receive you. The monk asked, "Why do you not receive me? The Master said, "Because you are too clever."
Chan Master Shaoyuan Tongbian Mingda of Bao’en Temple in Hangzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, “The great assembly is listening intently;
we pray that the Master will not be sparing of his words. The Master said, “How extraordinary! The monk said, “In that case, today I have met the Master. The Master said, “What words are these?
He then continued, “A single phrase can permeate the spirit and remain indestructible for ten thousand kalpas. Today, for the sake of you all—”
He uttered a single phrase, then after a long silence, said, "Keep this clearly in mind," and immediately descended from his seat.

He ascended the hall and said, "Fortunately, there are pavilions reaching to the ground that constantly uphold the ancestral seal; do not fail, venerable monks, to investigate them. I have stood for a long time; take care. A monk asked, "What is the master’s house style?
The Master said, "It is already accomplished in every place. The monk said, "If that is so, then it transcends antiquity..."
Now, the Master said: "Do not engage in idle talk.
Chan Master Shouwei Zongyi of Guangping Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of that province.

He studied under National Teacher Tiantai, attained his realization, and was subsequently entrusted with the robe and Dharma. At that time, a monk asked: "At the head of Dayu Ridge, it could not be lifted; how is it now?"
He presented this to his teacher. The teacher held it up and said, "Is there anyone who dares to say that Tiantai attained [this]?

He ascended the hall and said, "The Great Master Bodhidharma said, 'My Dharma shall not shift by even a hair’s breadth three thousand years hence. Today, I, this mountain monk, do not shift a hair’s breadth from Bodhidharma.
Those who have already reached this state, may you all bear witness together. As for those who have not yet reached it, [the Dharma] does not shift by even a hair’s breadth. A monk [asked].
Question: "The resonance of the great bell has ceased; the assembly is gathered before the dais. The Patriarchal intent has come from the West—please, Master, proclaim it!
The Master said: "The resonance of the great bell has ceased; the assembly is gathered before the dais. [The questioner] asked: "An ancient said, 'Let a thousand sages see you as they will;
I have the Buddha of True Nature. What is the Buddha of True Nature? The Master said: "The thousand sages are but disciples. [The questioner] asked: "What is the family of Guangping?"
"Wind. The Master said, "Who does not enjoy it? Ascending the hall, he said: "There is no need to open the sutras or chant the Sanskrit;

there is no need to spread out the commentaries or arrange the sections. Is there any place for theoretical discussion? Even if there were a place for theoretical discussion, that too would be merely a skillful means.
As for the matter of the *zong* (the fundamental school), how should one act? A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "No one has ever answered it."
[The student] said, "I have attained it. [The Master] said, "Please ask the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, "Why do you not ask further?
Chan Master Yong’an of Bào’ēn in Hangzhou was the son of the Wēng family of Wēnzhōu. In his youth, he relied upon Dàshī Huìzhēng of his native commandery to leave the household life.
During the Tiānchéng era of the Later Táng dynasty, he followed his preceptor into the capital. King Zhōngyì commanded Huìzhēng to serve as a monk-official.

Zheng was particularly disinclined toward worldly affairs. He intended to travel incognito to Min River to seek out Chan masters, but as the roads were difficult and obstructed, he returned to Mount Tiantai to build a thatched hut.
There he encountered National Teacher Shao, who gave him instructions, leading to his sudden awakening to his original mind.

He then took his leave and went into the mountains to report this to the King. The King ordered him to reside at Qingtai Temple in Yuezhou; subsequently, he summoned him to dwell at Shangsi Temple, where he was appointed [to the position of Abbot].
Chan Master Chengjue Konghui ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas of the ten directions have all gathered like clouds at once to bear witness with you, venerable elders.
You, venerable elders, and the Buddhas bear witness together at this very moment. Do you believe this? Be most careful not to engage in intellectual speculation. A monk asked:
The fourfold assembly gathered like clouds. [A monk] asked, "How should one raise and proclaim [the Dharma]? The Master said, "If you go to various places, do not fail to raise it correctly.

[The monk] said, "It is not only for students; the great assembly relies on you. The Master said, "Pay your respects. [Another] asked, "There are many who are thoroughly versed in the Five Vehicles and the Three Baskets.

As for the Patriarchal intent that came from the West, I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "The Five Vehicles and the Three Baskets. [The monk] asked, "Is there anything further above these?"
[The monk] said, “There is no such thing. The Master said, “You are indeed sharp-witted. [The monk] asked, “How does one perform great Buddha-activities? The Master said, “What is there to dislike?
[The monk] said, “In that case, I have personally received the Master’s touch upon my head. The Master said, “Where did you see the World-Honored One?
[The monk] asked, “What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, “Stand over here. As soon as the monk took a step, the Master called out, “Do you understand?”
[The monk] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Listen to this verse: 'You ask about the meaning of the Westward Transmission; for now, stand over here.
Last night at the third watch, the rain soaked the void. A flash of lightning suddenly shone; it was no more hurried than a centipede.
In the seventh year of the Kaibao era, he manifested illness. Addressing the assembly to take his leave, a monk asked, "Regarding the Tathāgata’s Right Dharma Eye of old..."
"Kāśyapa transmitted it personally; I do not yet know the profound style of the Master. How shall I realize it after a hundred years? The Master said, "Where did you see Kāśyapa come from?
He replied, "If that is so, then I shall accept it in faith and practice accordingly, never forgetting this intent.
The Master said, "The Buddha-dharma is not a matter such as this. Having finished speaking, he sat in the full lotus posture and passed away. Upon cremation, his tongue remained intact.
His faculties were unimpaired; he was as supple and soft as a red lotus, dwelling within the *bodhimaṇḍa* of Samantabhadra.

Master Huo Chanshi of Guangsheng Monastery in Guangzhou was a native of Min. Having received the Dharma from Tiantai, his transformative influence spread throughout the regions south of the Ling Mountains.
The local ruler, the Liu clan, established a great monastery and invited the Master to reside there, bestowing upon him the title of Chan Master Dayi. A monk asked:
"In the past, the Brahma King invited the Buddha; today, the sovereign of this land presides over the assembly. The Patriarch’s intent came from the West—how can it be proclaimed?
The Master said, "There is no need for it to come from the West; I, this mountain monk, have already proclaimed it. [The Emperor] asked, "Is there not some skillful means? The Master said, "..."
"Was it not a skillful means just now? A student who has newly entered the monastery asks for the teacher’s instruction regarding the wondrous secret of the West.
The Master said, "Before you had even entered the monastery, I had already shown it to you. The student asked, "How am I to understand this?"
The Master said: "Do not seek to understand through intellectualization.
Chan Master Qingyu of Fengxian Temple in Hangzhou was a native of Yongjia. King Zhongyi summoned him to enter the palace to inquire about the Way.
Chuangfeng first took up residence there and was appointed as the Chan Master Yuantong Miaojue. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?
The Master said, "Speak it out loud for the assembly."
Chan Master Zhiquan of Zining Pumen Temple in Taizhou was asked by a monk, "What is it to hold a hoe with empty hands?
The Master said, "Simply believe with such earnestness. The monk asked, "What is it to walk while riding a water buffalo?
The Master said, "From where have you come? He then presented a verse to the assembly, saying: "This year I am fifty-five, Yet my feet have not yet trodden an inch of soil. Mountains and rivers..."
"This is my eye; the great ocean is my belly. In the fourth year of the Taiping Xingguo era, an imperial decree was issued to test the monastic mastery of the scriptures.
The veteran elders of the mountain gate each wrote down their Dharma names, but the Master alone was unskilled in calligraphy. At that time, Li Xian, the Vice Governor, asked him:

The World-Honored One asked, "Do you still understand how to read this letter? The Master replied, "All people in the world know. At the beginning of the Chūn-hua era, when he was not yet ill, he ordered his attendant monk to prepare the bath.

Having finished bathing, he offered final instructions to the assembly of disciples, sat upright, and passed away. His stupa was erected at the mountain monastery. Three years later, his disciples moved the stupa and opened the coffin;
they beheld the Master’s countenance and deportment as solemn as ever, with his beard and hair having grown long again. They subsequently brought him back and enshrined him in a new [stupa].
Stupa. Chan Master Yuanqi of Yandang Mountain in Wenzhou was the son of the Jia family of Qiantang. He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The night moon spreads its light;
why is there no reflection in the azure depths? The Master said, "There is a fellow who dandles his shadow at home. The monk followed from the east.
He passed by and stood to the west. The Master said, "Not only do you play with shadows, but you are also terrified of your own head.
Chan Master Xibian of Pumen Temple in Hangzhou was a native of Suzhou. King Zhongyi appointed him to preside over Qingtai Temple in Yuezhou, bestowing upon him the title Huizhi.
Later, he moved to Shangsi. Ascending the hall, he said: "This mountain monk has always lacked insight and knowledge, and furthermore, my learning is meager."
"Hold on. Although you have been standing in attendance upon the National Teacher for some time, you have not received a single word of instruction.
This has led to the situation where today, gathered here with you virtuous ones, there is not a single Dharma by which I can assist or inspire you.

How much less could I possibly distinguish between the ordained and the laity for you, or deliberate upon matters of past and present? Do you still find fault with this mountain monk? If there are those who do find fault, tell me this:"
People may possess the eye [of wisdom] or lack it; they may hold to the principle of a host and guest, or lack the principle of a host and guest.
Those who are late learners and beginners must examine these matters with great care. A monk asked, "What is the manifestation of spiritual powers through the Universal Gate?

The Master said, "If that were so, you would be resentful toward this old monk. The monk asked, "How is it when there is no resentment? The Master said, "For now, go down to the hall and reflect upon it."
He departed for Tàipíng Xīngguó in the third year of that reign. When the King of Wúyuè came to the imperial court, the Master followed the precious stupa there and was received at Zífú Hall.
He was granted purple robes and the title Chan Master Huìmíng. During the Duānɡǒng era, he requested leave to return to his native village, and the Emperor granted his request.
The Emperor bestowed a poem composed by himself. King Zhōngyì provided gold for the construction of a brick pagoda at the original monastery in Cháshū.

It had seven tiers and was two hundred feet high. Once the work was completed, in the eighth month of the third year of the Zhidao era, he passed away. His stupa was erected in the northwest corner of the monastery.
Chan Master Yu’an of Guangqing Temple in Hangzhou was the son of the Shen family of Qiantang. He ascended the hall. A monk asked, “The priceless jewel—please, Master, bestow it upon us.
The Master said, “You are well able to express it. The monk said, “If that is so, then everyone is already fully endowed with it.
The Master said, “Where is the jewel? The monk bowed. The Master said, “That too is but empty talk. [Question: “What about when one brings it forth?”...
When the main line is raised, the collar is secured; all stand as host and guest. What is the host? The Master said, "I thoroughly understand this question.

[The monk] asked, "What is the guest? The Master said, "What did I just say to you? [The monk] asked, "When host and guest are in accord, what then? The Master said, "His commands will not be carried out.
[A monk] asked, "The mind-moon is solitary and full, its light swallowing the ten thousand phenomena. What is 'swallowing the ten thousand phenomena'?"
"Dibao Guang. The Master said, "The entire assembly has seen you ask such a question. Guang replied, "Light swallows the ten thousand phenomena;
following the Master's Way, what is the meaning of 'the solitary fullness of the moon-mind'? The Master said, "Exert your spirit and apply yourself!

Guang said, "A heron perched in a snow nest may still be distinguished, but the matter of light swallowing the ten thousand phenomena is difficult to clarify. The Master said, "Be careful to withdraw. [Guang] asked, "Regarding green mountains and blue waters, everywhere..."
"Clearly! This is the家风 (household style) of our Master. Please grant us a single word. The Master said, "It has all been spoken by you.

The monk said, "Not necessarily so; I ask the Master to answer the question. The Master said, "There is no need for idle talk. Another monk was just about to prostrate when the Master said, "Question and answer are both complete.
As the monk prepared to ask a question, the Master rebuked him. He then ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to know the purport of Caoxi, look at the clouds..."
Flying ahead to the mountain before us—this is clearly and truly it; there is no need for further pursuit.
A monk asked, "The ancient masters said, 'Red dust arises from the bottom of the well; waves surge upon the mountain peak. I do not understand the meaning of this.
The Master said, "If you go to other places, simply ask in this way. The monk asked, "What is your own intention, Reverend? The Master said, "I have already told you."
"What is it? he asked. "The tradition passed down through the ages says: 'Dust is born at the bottom of the well; waves rise upon the mountain peak. Fruit is formed from empty flowers;
a child is born to a barren woman. How do you understand this? Is it that you send forth affairs with harmonious sounds and manifest the mind by means of objects?
Is it that the sharp edge is hidden within the phrase, while the whole is revealed before the sound? Or is it that there is the name but no substance, a wondrous discourse of divergent singing?"
"Ma! If you, Elder, can understand for yourself, that would be fine; however, the meaning of the ancients was not like that.
Since you cannot understand it in this way, how then should you understand it? Elder, do you wish to understand? Just look: where the earthen ox walks, mirages surge into waves;
when the wooden horse neighs, empty flowers cast their shadows. When the holy and the ordinary are thus, the principle is clear—why need one linger?"
Recorded with care.
Chan Master Youchan of Bānruò Monastery in Tàizhōu was a native of Qiántáng. He first resided at Yúnjū Púxián, where the Prince Zhōngyì appointed him as Chan Master Cíwù.
He later moved to the Upper Monastery, where his assembly numbered over five hundred. A monk asked: "As soon as the drum sounds—"
[The assembly] dispersed. The great multitude gathered like clouds, requesting the Master to proclaim the supreme vehicle of the ancestral lineage. The Master said, "What is lacking in you?
[A monk] said, "If that is so, then everyone will surely receive your grace. The Master said, "Do not speak recklessly."
When Chan Master Quanken of Zhiye Temple in Wuzhou first visited National Teacher Huairang, the National Teacher asked, "What is your name?
The Master replied, "Quanken. The National Teacher asked, "What do you approve of? At these words, the Master had an awakening and prostrated himself.
While [Dongshan] was staying there, a monk asked, "If someone is unwilling to accept this, would they still have to acquiesce? The Master said, "If anyone asks me, I will simply tell them:

'Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are all within the eyes of everyone. Zen Master Yiqing Yilong of Yushan in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are entirely within the eyes of you all."

[The Master] said, "Inside. [The monk asked,] "For what reason do you speak of 'understanding' and 'not understanding'? At that time, there was a monk who asked, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are within the eye;
to whom does the Master now wish to point as the ultimate destination? The Master said, "It is precisely because your destination, Venerable One, is clear.

[The monk] said, "If I had not come forward to pose this question, how would I have known that these skillful means were not applied in vain? The Master said, "Vaguely resembling a melody, it is just barely fit..."
Listen. Furthermore, it was blown by the wind into another tune.
Chan Master Xiaorong of Longce Monastery in Hangzhou, a native of the Deng family of Wenzhou, was asked by a monk: "The patriarchs have transmitted [the Dharma] to one another in succession."
"I do not know to whom the Master has transmitted [the Dharma]," [the monk] asked. The Master said, "Do you recognize the Patriarch yet?
The monk Huìwén asked, "What is a true śramaṇa? The Master said, "You are Huìwén. He asked, "What is the great divine pearl of Prajñā?
The Master said, "The great divine pearl of Prajñā manifests ten billion bodies; in every atom it reveals its wondrous essence, and in every world-system..."
[The Master] filled the lands of Vairocana. A monk asked, "What is the matter of daily life? The Master said, "A single thought pervades the sands of the world;

ten thousand modes of daily activity are all penetrating. Serenely and eternally quiescent, one constantly unfolds one's own house style. Following the small assembly lecture, a monk asked, "I do not ask about matters above this;
what is the direct meaning of the 'Exquisite Goodness Terrace'? The Master said, "If you go to other places..."

[The monk] clearly recounted [the previous exchange]. [The Master] said, "If that is so, then the clouds have the appearance of emerging from the mountains, yet the waters lack the sound of plunging into the ravine.
The Master then rebuked him. A monk asked Chan Master Qingxiao of Gongchen in Hangzhou, "What is the家风 (household style) of Gongchen? The Master said, "Clear."
"Darkness, color, and emptiness. The monk said, "If that is so, then all dharmas are non-arising. The Master said, "What do you call 'all dharmas'?
The monk bowed. The Master said, "Listen to this verse: The house style of the Accomplished One: Brightness, darkness, color, and emptiness.
Dharma after dharma is not different; Mind after mind naturally penetrates. If you understand it thus, you have grasped the true source of all Buddhas."
A monk asked Chan Master Jingjin of Cheshen in Yuezhou, "I have packed my bags; please entrust me to you.
The Master said, "Do not try to evade it. The monk asked, "In what way have I failed the Master? The Master said, "It is you, rather, who has failed me."
Chan Master Shishu of Yanfeng in Fuzhou ascended the seat for his inaugural address. Master Jile asked, “The great assembly looks up with eager expectation;
please thunder forth the Dharma drum. The Master said, “Does the assembly understand? Can you discern it?
Today is no different from Vulture Peak, nor even from the lands of all Buddhas; whether in heaven or among men, it is everywhere thus, pervading through eternity.”
Now, there shall be no change. How do you understand the principle of being without change? If you can understand it, that is why it is said:
"The realms of boundless lands are not separated by a hair’s breadth between self and other; ten ages of past and present, from beginning to end, do not depart from this very moment.
A monk asked: "At the assembly on Vulture Peak, Kāśyapa heard it personally. At the assembly on Mount Yanfeng, who is it that hears?"
The Master said, "The questioner is no weakling. A monk asked, "What is Mañjuśrī? The Master said, "His place of origin is perfectly clear.
A monk asked Chan Master Huairun of Huayan in Lufu, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth.
He asked, "What is the realm of Huayan? The Master said, "Everywhere before one’s eyes, there is no form or shadow."
A monk asked Chan Master Daoyuan of Qingtai Monastery in Yuezhou, "Where has the deceased monk gone after passing away?
The Master said, "He passed away this very day. The Abbot Lingzhong asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The Master said: "I cannot tell you that it is the cypress tree in front of the courtyard.
Changqing Guanyuan Yuanxiang Chanshi was a native of Yuhang.

His eloquence surpassed all others, and his vast learning and powerful memory were such that he was regarded by the disciples of Tiantai as preeminent. A monk asked: "The profound, perfect luminosity—please, Master..."
[The monk] asked, "A single decision. The Master said, "A vast lake ten li wide; a single orb of autumn moon. [The monk] asked, "In a perilous and evil path, what serves as the ferry and the bridge?
The Master said, "This very thing serves as the ferry and the bridge. [The monk] asked, "What is this? The Master said, "It strikes right at your nostrils.
[The monk] asked, "Where does one plant the rootless tree? The Master said, "From where did you get that?"
Chan Master Xingming of Kaishua Temple in Hangzhou was the son of the Yu family of that same prefecture. He took Zen Master Zhijue of Xuedou as his teacher.
When Zhijue moved to Yongming, Xingming subsequently entered the quarters of National Teacher Zhiyi of Tiantai and received his transmission and prediction of enlightenment.
He then returned to Yongming to assist and support his own teacher, becoming an object of veneration for the assembly gathered like the sea. King Zhongyi established six... [temples].
Wa-ji (originally granted the name Kāihua by the Imperial Court of this land). He was invited to serve as abbot; he gathered disciples and preached the Dharma.
A monk asked, "What is the skillful means flowing forth from within the gate of Kāihua? The Master said, "The sound of the tide is heard twice every day.
The monk asked, "What is the inexhaustible lamp? The Master said, "Thank you, Dharma brother, for your illumination."
A monk asked Chan Master Yiyuan of Kaishan Temple at Yupu in Yuezhou: "One year departs, another year arrives;
within the gate of expedient means, we pray that the Master will open it for us. The Master said, "Take this clearly to heart.
The monk said, "If so, then the lion’s roar of former times is today the elephant king’s return. The Master said, "For now, let us say there is no connection."
Chan Master Yuan’an of the Upper Hall at Ruiluo Monastery in Wenzhou was a native of Fuzhou. He received the Dharma from Tiantai and frequently studied the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.
Upon reaching the passage, "When knowledge and vision establish knowledge, that is the root of ignorance; when knowledge and vision are without seeing... [he attained realization].
"This, then, is *nirvāṇa*. The Master then broke the phrasing and read it as: "When knowledge and vision are established, that is the root of ignorance;
when knowledge and vision are absent, that is *nirvāṇa*. At this, he attained a realization. Someone said to the Master, "You have broken the phrasing!
The Master replied, "This is where I have attained awakening; I shall not change it for the rest of my life. At that time, he was called "An Lèng'ān" (An of the Śūraṃgama). When [the text] reached...

In the first year of the Daoyuan era, as he was about to manifest his passing, his heir Yuren stood in attendance. The Master then spoke a verse to him: "It is not a matter brought from the mountain peaks;
How could it have been transmitted from Mount Kukkuṭapāda? From antiquity, all sages and worthies were like this;

It is not I alone who provides this measure for you today. Having completed his final instructions, he bathed himself, changed his robes, and sat upright. He then ordered that the coffin be carried forth.

Upon reaching the chamber, he entered the coffin of his own accord after a long while. After three days had passed, the disciples opened the coffin and beheld the Master lying in the auspicious posture on his right side.
The fourfold assembly was moved to profound grief. The Master then rose once more, ascended the hall, and preached the Dharma, reprimanding them and offering admonitions:
"Whoever opens my coffin again in this lifetime shall not be my true child. Having spoken these words, he entered the coffin once more and departed forever.
Chan Master Huiju of Longhua Monastery in Hangzhou was a native of Min. Having received the essential instructions from Tiantai, King Zhongyi ordered him to reside at the aforementioned monastery.
When he ascended the hall to address the assembly, he said: "As for the ancestral vehicle of the Buddhas and patriarchs, how can it be proclaimed upon reaching this point?
Even regarding the teachings of a lifetime delivered by Śākyamuni Buddha—like pouring water from one vessel into another—an ancient worthy once remarked that it is still..."
It is like a dream or the muttering of sleep-talking. But tell me, by what principle do you speak thus?
Do you understand? The Great Gate of Generosity is ever open; when has it ever been obstructed? Producing ordinary beings and nurturing sages, not even a speck of dust is leaked.

To speak of the ordinary, they are entirely ordinary; to cite the sage, they are entirely sage. Ordinary and sage do not wait for one another; each and every one is uniquely honored. Therefore it is said:

The mountains, rivers, and the great earth have long been preaching the Dharma and long have been emitting light; the same is true for each of the elements of earth, water, fire, and wind. At that time, a monk came forth and prostrated. The Master said, "What an excellent question! Ask it according to the Dharma. As the monk was about to step forward, the Master struck him. The monk remained silent. The Master said, "I have answered you; why do you not speak? The monk still did not respond. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "You have already bowed; why do you not speak? The monk again did not respond. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed once more. The Master said, "You have bowed three times; why do you not speak? The monk remained silent. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "You have bowed four times; why do you not speak? The monk again did not respond. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "You have bowed five times; why do you not speak? The monk remained silent. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "You have bowed six times; why do you not speak? The monk again did not respond. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "You have bowed seven times; why do you not speak? The monk remained silent. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "You have bowed eight times; why do you not speak? The monk again did not respond. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "You have bowed nine times; why do you not speak? The monk remained silent. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "You have bowed ten times; why do you not speak? The monk again did not respond. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "You have bowed eleven times; why do you not speak? The monk remained silent. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "You have bowed twelve times; why do you not speak? The monk again did not respond. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "You have bowed thirteen times; why do you not speak? The monk remained silent. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "You have bowed fourteen times; why do you not speak? The monk again did not respond. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "You have bowed fifteen times; why do you not speak? The monk remained silent. The Master said, "If you had spoken, you would have attained the Way. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, "Why do you find the old monk strange?
The monk said, "I do not understand; I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, "Was it not just now that you asked about the meaning of the West?"
A monk asked Chan Master Daodu of Guangxiao Monastery in Hangzhou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Ask with a loud voice.
The monk said, "Is it not that very thing? The Master said, "There is no connection. Later, while residing at Lingyin, he passed away.
Chan Master Nying of Baiching Yuan on Mount Xishan in Hangzhou ascended the seat for the opening of the hall. Two monks prostrated at the same time.
The Master said, "Both of you are mistaken. As the monks were about to offer words in response, the Master immediately descended from the seat.
Chan Master Bianlong of Zhiti Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of Mingzhou. He ascended the hall and said:
"The majestic true reality (dharmatā) fills the void; its adamantine essence is indestructible. Does the assembly see it or not?
If you say you see it, yet the essence of true reality is fundamentally neither blue, yellow, red, nor white, neither long, short, square, nor round—it is also not seeing."
Regarding the dharmas of hearing, awakening, and knowing, how can one speak of the principle of seeing?
If you say one does not see, yet it is also said that the sublime reality (*dharmatā*) fills all of space; why then is it not seen? A monk asked:
"What is the path that leads upward? The Master said: "That which is beneath your feet. The monk said: "In that case, we are constantly treading upon it. The Master said: "Do not err."
[The Master] acknowledged. [The student] asked, "What is the firm and dense body? The Master said, "Nakedly. [The student] said, "If that is so, then it is not dense.
The Master said, "What do you see?"
A monk asked Chan Master Xiyuan of Ruelong Monastery in Hangzhou, “What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, “I thank you specifically for asking. The monk said, “There is no doubt that I have asked; what then is the house style? The Master said, “You sleepyhead!”
A monk asked Zen Master Xinglin Zuyin of Nan-kang County, successor to Zen Master Rou of Guizong: "The heavens shed sweet dew and the earth wells up the seven treasures—whose domain is this?
The Master said, "Thank you for informing me. The monk said, "If that is so, then it is the Buddha's son."

"Abiding in this ground is precisely the Buddha’s enjoyment of going. The Master said, "You must still be more meticulous. Upon ascending the hall, as soon as he sat down, a cat suddenly leaped onto his body.
The Master picked it up and showed it to the assembly, saying, "In the past, Nanquan personally slew one such as this."
"Early this morning, Yaśas showed it to his disciples of the profound; now he sells it to these guests of meditation. Is the contract clear and explicit?
Or not? After a long silence, he threw down a cat and descended from the seat.
A monk asked Master Xinzhen of Tiantong in Mingzhou, “What is the secret functioning? The Master said, “When has it ever been secret?
The monk asked, “How is it when the path of the mind has not yet been traversed? The Master said, “What thing is obstructing you? The monk asked, “How is it when one seeks but cannot find?
The Master said, “Why seek? The monk asked, “What then is it? The Master said, “When has it ever been lost?”

Question: "What is the realm of Tiantong? The Master said: "When the clouds have no one to plant them, how can they reach their limit? When the water has no one to teach it, why does it flow away and never return?
A monk asked Zen Master Jueke Xinyin of Gōngshèn in Hangzhou: "The Patriarch is not on the mountains of the East or the West. [The Master said: "... (The text here is incomplete).
"Examine it thoroughly; where is it? The Master said, "Go and seek it. He asked, "What is the true-born Buddha? The Master said, "How would one dare to embellish it?
Chan Master Qingjian of Tiantong in Mingzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Qiantang. The Master’s conduct was solitary and pure; at that time, people said of him:
This is the record from Zhejiang. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

The Master said, "I do not wish to tell you. The monk said, "Please, Reverend, tell me. The Master said, "Bodhidharma cannot come again. The Master lived at Xuedou in his later years and passed away there;
his stupa was erected in the southeast corner of the monastery.
A monk asked Chan Master Chengzhi of Xiqian on Mount Lu, a dharma successor of Chan Master Heng of Baizhang: "Zhaozhou’s stone bridge ferries donkeys and horses across;
as for the stone bridges of the Three Gorges, whom do they ferry? The Master said, "Shrimp and earthworms. The monk said, "If that is so, then every single thing receives its share."
[The monk] said, "Thank you. The Master said, "You have not stepped upon it. [The monk] asked, "Yesterday the Master finished his chanting at Xian-dong;

today Qixian invites the Master to proclaim the Dharma. The Master said, "What will you do tomorrow? [The monk] said, "I do not yet know how to comprehend this. The Master said, "The arrow has already passed beyond Silla.
[The monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Zhang San and Li Si. [The monk] asked, "What was the intent behind the ancients' slaying of the snake? The Master said, "Zhang San and Li Si."
"How is it? The Master said, "You still do not know pain or itch. The student asked, "This is the field for selecting Buddhas; one returns having attained the 'first place' with an empty mind.
How can a student attain that first-place rank and return? The Master said, "Lacking talent, I respectfully withdraw. In the evening assembly, when the multitude had gathered, the Master said:
"I did not meet with anyone this morning; tonight I must not remain silent.
He then descended from his seat, took the hand of the Seer Vimala, and said, "When you saw the myriad Buddhas as fine as motes of dust, what was it that you saw before you had taken my hand?
The Master replied, "What do you see now? Ascending the hall, he remained silent for a long while and then said, "How fortunate to have a single bowl of rice!"
"One must not sprinkle pepper and ginger [into it]. Nevertheless, try taking a bite. He then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Dexing of Wanshou Monastery in Suzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The assembly gazes upon him all at once.
He was further asked, "What is the single phrase for the Master’s benefit of others? The Master said, "You should first benefit yourself. He then said:
Question and answer are both complete; who among you has grasped the meaning? If you seek it from another, you will merely end up acting in vain.
This old monk has long dwelt in the deep mountains, intending to hide his ineptitude. Who would have expected that today, having entered the gate of Wanshou, he could no longer conceal it?
Since it cannot be concealed, it is clearly revealed. I do not know which of you perceives it first. If there is anyone...
"Regarding this point of view, come forth and reveal your message to the assembly. After a long silence, he said, "I have stood for a long time; take care.
Chan Master Yongxi Yong of Yunmen in Yuezhou was asked by a monk, "What is it like before a lion has emerged from its cave?
The Master said, "Do not roar yet. The monk asked, "What is it like after it has emerged from the cave? The Master said, "Step back. [The monk] asked, "What is..."

[The student asked about] the path of the ancient Buddhas. The Master said, "Who does not tread upon it? [The student] asked, "What is the place where a student lets the mind rest and ceases its intentions?
The Master said, "Have you even broken your staff yet? [The student] asked, "How is it when the Mind-King issues an imperial edict? The Master said:
Please proclaim it once more for me to see. Question: What is the definitive meaning? Master: It is not to be clung to. Question:
What is the great purport of the Buddha-dharma? Master: This purport is no small matter.
Chan Master Kuangsheng of Qianguangwang Monastery in Hangzhou was a dharma heir of Chan Master Yongming Quan. He was the son of the Zheng family of Wenzhou.

Having left home at a young age, he thoroughly studied the Vinaya-piṭaka and listened to the *Wenju* (Commentary on the Lotus Sūtra) of Tiantai. He settled his mind in the Perfect and Sudden *Zhiguan*. Later, he read the *Lengyan jing wen* (Commentary on the Śūraṅgama Sūtra).
The principles were vast and profound; he was unable to penetrate them fully. One night, after reciting the sutras for a long time, he dozed off at his desk.

In a dream, he saw the sun’s orb descend from the sky and opened his mouth to swallow it. From that moment on, he suddenly attained awakening; the various categories of doctrine became clear and free of obstruction.
Later, he visited Yongming, who merely confirmed his prior understanding and offered no further instructions or metaphors, as [Yongming] recognized his sincerity.
King Yi bestowed upon him a patchwork robe as a token of his faith. After taking up residence, he ascended the hall and said: "Venerable Elders, the Buddha-dharma is a matter of no concern.
The sun and moon of the past are the sun and moon of today; the wind and rain of the past are the wind and rain of today;
the elders of the past are the elders of today. To raise it is complete; to explain it is complete. Everything is manifest before you. Be careful and cherish this, O Kaimao!"
In the seventh month of the fifth year, a jeweled tree and bathing pool suddenly appeared before him. The Master said, "All phenomena that possess marks are entirely illusory.
Three days later, he manifested illness; he gathered the assembly to bid them farewell, sat upright, and passed away. His body was cremated, and his relics were collected to build a stupa.
In the *Qingzhou Zhenjing Zhishi*, a monk asked Zen Master Cheng, "What is the sword that settles heaven and earth?
The Master said, "It does not leak so much as a hair’s breadth. The monk asked, "How is it used? The Master said, "One does not know.
Once, during a communal work session (*pùqǐng*), a monk asked, "When the hoe damages toads and earthworms, is there still sin? The Master said, "Who laid hands upon them? The monk said, "If so..."
"If that were so, there would be no fault. The Master said, "Cause and effect are clearly manifest.
Chan Master Qingxiang of Chongfu Monastery in Mingzhou ascended the hall and said, "O Zen practitioners! The nature of seeing is all-pervasive; the nature of hearing is likewise.
It penetrates the ten directions, being neither internal nor external. Therefore, the ancients said: 'Acting in accordance with conditions without fabrication, moving...'"
"Quiescent, eternal, and true. Such acts as these are entirely the functioning of true wisdom. A monk asked, "What is the person of original nature?
The Master said, "Tall and dignified at six chi, he is most clearly manifest. The monk asked, "Does the person of original nature still rely upon such a physical appearance?
The Master said, "What do you call 'the person of original nature'? The monk said, "I beg the Master for an expedient means. The Master said, "Teach [him]..."
Whose expedient means?
Master Daocheng Tongfa of Baoming Monastery in Fuzhou, a successor of Chan Master Bao'en Ming, ascended the hall and said: "As it is for one person, so it is for many."

"Indeed. Take care. A monk asked, "The perfect sound vibrates everywhere; those of the three vehicles hear it equally. The immortal mind of India—please grant us its secret transmission. The Master remained silent for a long time.
The monk said, "If that is so, then the wild horse of the will has become a precious steed, and the ox of the mind has suddenly turned into a white ox.
The Master said, "Seven topsy-turvy, eight upside-down. The monk said, "If that were the case, you would surely invite much laughter. The Master [remained silent].
[The monk] said, "After performing prostrations, I withdrew. He asked, "What is the meaning of the Master’s coming from the West? The Master said, "I have never been to the Western Heaven.
[The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of this student’s coming from the West? The Master said, "How long have you been in this Eastern Land?"
Baoci said: "The Dharma heir of Master Yunju Yinen of Nankang Commandery, the Guiding Teacher, ascends the hall.

Without coming up into the hall, Elder Kauṇḍinya shall, for the sake of all you elders, turn the wheel of the primary truth (*paramārtha*). Can this still be accomplished? If you can believe it, each of you..."
He went to the hall to take his turn in attendance, then descended from the seat.

Later, he asked a monk, "Just as I instructed you, Venerable, to take your turn in attendance upon the Holy Monk (Śānta), what did the Holy Monk say? The monk replied, "I specifically thank the Master for raising this matter again."
A questioner asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The very mind is the Buddha. The questioner said, "I do not understand; I beg the Master for an expedient means.
The Master said, "To call it 'the Buddha' is merely an expedient. Turn the light back upon yourself and reflect: what are this body and mind?"
Chan Master Lingcen of Mount Yuntai in Quanzhou was a successor of Chan Master Chou of Chongshou. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Mount Yuntai?
The Master said, "The mountain in front and the mountain behind. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "A sleepyhead."
The Abbot of Ziguang Monastery, Master Yuanjin, asked: "What is the meaning of Danxia burning the wooden Buddha?

The Master said: "Inviting the cause while carrying the fruit. He asked: "What is the meaning of 'the cypress tree in front of the hall'? The Master said: "The blue-eyed barbarian monk smiles and nods his head. He asked:
"An ancient said, 'At the eastern house he becomes a donkey; at the western house he becomes a horse. What is the meaning of this? The Master said: [as above].
The Master said: "One's acquaintances fill the world.

This refers to Chan Master Daojian of Qixian on Mount Lu, a successor of Chan Master Baoen. An official asked him: "I have gathered my troops at Jinling and am about to deploy them for battle. I shall kill—"
"A person has no fixed measure. Does he still have offenses or not? The Master said, "I simply keep watching.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The Yanglan and Zuoli rivers: waves arise even without wind."
Chan Master Huicheng of Guizong on Mount Lu was a native of Yangzhou. On the day he ascended the hall, he stood before the Dharma Hall and addressed the assembly, saying:
"When devas and humans attain the Way, they take this as proof. To disperse now would already be redundant;

yet since you do not yet understand, I shall explain it once more. He then ascended the seat. A monk asked: "The Prefectural Governor has arrived at the assembly; we pray that the Master will expound the Dharma."
The Master said, "I am not your equal. [The student] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "How could it not be so?
[The student] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "I do not know. He then said, "Stop your questioning for a moment.

Even if you were to question until the end of kalpas, you would still not reach it; even if one were to answer until the end of kalpas, one would still not suffice. Why is this? It is simply because of all [sentient beings]..."
Each person has their own fundamental duty. It is complete throughout the ten directions, spanning from antiquity to the present;
even the Buddhas dare not err in it. People call this the "Crown Clan," yet it merely serves to assist and inspire the Elder. Therefore it is said:
"All sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm of the ten directions realize the fruit of the Sugata in every thought-moment. Since they are great men, so am I."
How can you disparage yourselves and retreat in defeat? You elders, do not be discouraged; simply believe and accept this, and let it rest.
When the Patriarch came from the West, he spoke only of seeing one's nature to become a Buddha; all other teachings fall short of this.
Furthermore, there is a most extraordinary expedient means which I shall present to you all. After a long silence, he said: "Take this clearly to heart. If you go to various places, you must not..."
A brief mention. [The Master] stood for a long time; take care. A monk asked, "How can one pass through where there is no passage for the wind? The Master said, "From where have you come?
The monk related that Nanquan asked Deng Yinfeng, "This bronze pitcher is an object. There is water in the pitcher. Without touching the object, bring me some water.

Yinfeng then picked up the pitcher and poured out the water. I do not know—[what was his meaning?]— *Note: This is a partial translation of a Zen dialogue (mondo) excerpted from a classical Chinese text.*
"What do you think of this? The Master said, "Deng Yinfeng was truly extraordinary; however, he was merely pouring things out in disorder.
Chan Master Bianshi of Chang’an Monastery in Luzhou, a successor of Chan Master Chang’an Gui, was asked by a monk: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master—
It is said: Lingfeng of Shaoshi dwells in the nine heavens.
Chan Master Yongqing of Tanzhou Yungai was the son of the Zhao family of Hezhou. A monk asked, "If there is a person at the bottom of a ten-thousand-fathom well, how can they get out?
The Master said, "I am glad to have met you. The monk said, "In that case, they must pierce through the clouds..."
[The monk] passed through the moon and departed. The Master asked, "What about the matter of the Thirty-three Heavens?
The monk had no reply. The Master said, "Why do you speak such deceptive words? A monk asked, "What is the realm of Yungai? The Master said, "Three spring wells outside the gate.
[The monk] asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "The young novice. He presented a verse to the assembly, saying: "The secret oral instructions of Yungai."
Any attempt to deliberate upon this would split one’s brain; clap your hands and pursue the void. The clouds reveal the moon over the western mountains.

A monk asked, “What is the secret instruction for locking the mouth? The Master said, “Pervading heaven and pervading earth. The monk said, “If that is so, then the stone man nods his head and the pillar claps its hands.
The Master said, “A single pitcher of pure water and a single burner of incense. The monk said, “This is still just a shrimp at the bottom of a well.”
The Master said, "I trouble the great assembly. He regularly moderated his food and drink; he would simply spread out his bowl twice daily in accordance with the community.

Even when months or years passed, he did not practice physical conditioning or take medicinal tonics, yet this did not hinder his work. Whenever there was an invitation, he would certainly attend and eat his fill, remaining free from attachment or constraint.
On the second day of the fourth month in the second year of the Zhìdào era, he manifested illness and passed away.
A monk asked Chan Master Congjin of Puzhao at Bore Monastery in Taizhou, a successor of Chan Master Yunju Xi: "What is it like when the cold spring flows in the ancient ravine?
The Master said, "By all means, avoid drinking from it. The monk asked, "And if one drinks from it? The Master said, "You will lose your very life."
A monk asked Chan Master Zhi-chao of Qinghua in Yuezhou, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Who are you?
The monk said, “Is it not you yourself? The Master said, “If it were, there would be no connection.”
Chan Master Fazhi of Changshou Monastery in Suzhou,
a native of Wuzhou and the dharma heir of Chan Master Changshou Yan,
the eleventh-generation successor of Nanyue, initially lectured on the *Mingmen lun* and the *Inming lun*. Subsequently...
Setting aside his travels, he received the mind-seal from Chan Master Guangfa. When the regional inspector Qian Ren invited him to serve as the abbot, he succeeded Guangfa in holding the position.
On the day of the opening of the hall, the Dharma Master Bafa asked a question; at the request of the Duke, the fourfold assembly gathered like clouds.

[The student] requested, "Please, Master, proclaim the upward-tending vehicle of the patriarchal lineage. The Master said, "The *Śata-dharma-prakāśamukha-śāstra* (Treatise on the Gate of Illumination of the Hundred Dharmas).
[The student] asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, "All dharmas are without self. [The student] asked, "The old woman of the eastern city was born at the same time as the Buddha;
why did she not see the Buddha? The Master said, "If you do not see, then speak! [The student] said, "In that case, then I see. The Master said, "The city..."
The Eastern Old Mother was born at the same time as the Buddha.
A monk asked Chan Master Qi Gui of Yunju in Nankang, a successor of Chan Master Qiji of Yunju: "When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it; [place it] in a bottomless basket."
Zi Sheng was about to depart to return home. He did not know whether the Master would accept his departure or not.
The Master asked, "Where did you get this? Zi Sheng said, "In that case, it has not been bestowed in vain. The Master said, "For now, take it with you.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Beyond praise. The monk asked, "Is this it right here? The Master said, "It does not cause people to praise it."
A monk asked Zen Master Wensheng Ciji of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou, "What is it like when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished?

The Master said, "The ancient mirror. The monk asked, "What is it like after it has been polished? The Master said, "The ancient mirror. The monk asked, "I do not know whether there is distinction or not. The Master said: [He remained silent.]
[The Master] looked after him further. [A monk] asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Do not be surprised by its rusticity.
[The monk] asked, "What do you do when a guest suddenly arrives? The Master said, "Go drink tea."
Chan Master Yihai of Ruiyan in Mingzhou was a native of Xichuan. He went to the Dharma seat of Yunju, where Yunju asked him, "What thing comes like this?
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and subsequently composed a verse, which says: "Yunju, what thing?"

Question: When confronted with a head-on challenge, one is dazed; to simply accept it as it comes is still to be buried alive. To transcend the world and abide in the fundamental source—this is the way.

A monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "If you go to other places, just say that I have returned to the source and do not know how to answer questions.
Question: "What is the style of your monastery, Master? The Master said: "There is no prohibition. [The monk] said: "But what if one suddenly encounters..."
"How can one resolve this contradiction? The Master said, "If you do not know how to be a guest, you only trouble the host. Question:
"Śākyamuni kept silent in Magadha, and Vimalakīrti remained speechless in Vaiśālī. I wonder, how did they instruct the assembly? The Master said, "You do not wish for me to speak.
[The questioner] said, "I have not yet grasped the Master's intent. The Master said, "Withdraw for now. Question: "What is the state that has no rank?"
The Real Man. The Master said, "There is no place here for you to arrange yourself.
Chan Master Guanghui Zhiquan of Mingzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the fundamental matter of a patch-robed monk?"

The Master said, "Do not treat me with such dull indifference. The monk bowed. The Master said, "In fact, it is the assembly that treats you, Venerable Sir, with dull indifference," and then descended from his seat.
A monk asked, "What is it like when a thief does not strike the house of a poor man? The Master said, "Even if I were to tell people, they would not believe me.
The monk said, "In that case, I shall bow and withdraw. The Master said, "What have you gained?"
A monk asked Chan Master Juxu of Baofu at Damei in Mingzhou, "What was the intent behind the ancients facing the wall?
The Master said, "Just understand it in this way. The monk asked, "I do not know how to comprehend it; how should I receive and understand it? The Master said, "Prostrate yourself."
A monk asked Chan Master Wuishu of Chuzhou Nanming: "The dharmas do not conceal themselves; they have always been manifest throughout past and present.
What is this manifest dharma? The Master said, "I am showing it to the assembly. The monk said, "If that is so, I shall respectfully withdraw.
The Master said, "One who recognizes their error must surely correct it."
A monk asked Chan Master Qingxi Qing of Jingmen Commandery, "The ancient path is level and smooth; how does one tread upon it?
He replied, "Are you a wandering monk?
[He was] a successor of Chan Master Zhiti Long.
A monk asked Zen Master Xuánběn of Línghyìn in Hangzhou, “When the oyster has not yet opened, how is it? The Master said, “From where does the light come?
[The monk] raised Linji’s practice of shouting upon entering the gate and Deshan’s practice of striking with the staff upon entering the gate; he asked, “What is the meaning of this?”
The Master said, "The sky is clear, yet you refuse to go. Seeing a monk reading a sutra, the Master asked, "What sutra are you reading?
The monk was speechless. Thereupon, the Master presented this verse: "Reading a sutra without understanding the sutra, One merely exhausts one's eyes in vain. If you wish not to damage your eyes,"
Clearly recognize the scripture.
A monk asked Chan Master Shaolin of Huili Temple in Linjiang Commandery, successor to Chan Master Luohanlin: "What is it like before the golden cock has crowed? The Master said:

[The monk] asked, "What season is this? [The Master] said, "After the cry, what then? The Master said, "I do not know the time. [The monk] asked, "How is it when the lion has not yet emerged from its cave?
The Master said, "It is right there. [The monk] asked, "How is it after it has emerged from the cave? The Master said, "Just run!"
A monk asked Zen Master Qingcong of Danning Monastery in Hongzhou, "When the Way prevails, the imperial decree is not transmitted;
all people sing songs of Great Peace. I wonder, what is the meaning of your teaching now, Master? The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, am at fault.
The monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Mount Sumeru. He ascended the hall and said, "Birth and death, as well as nirvana, are like a dream from yesterday. Moreover..."
"The Way. What excellence do the Buddhas of the three periods, or even Old Śākyamuni, possess? Even so, do not misunderstand! [The Master] claps his hands once and descends from the seat.
A monk asked, "I have heard an ancient saying: 'The eastern mountain and the western ridge are green. I do not know what the meaning of this is.
The Master said, "The eastern mountain and the western ridge are green; it rains, and then the sky clears. Ask one more question."
This was acceptable. A dove gave birth to a hawk.

Regarding the Dharma successor of the meritorious master Ke Chan, Zen Master Hao Xian of Yao Feng in Suzhou, a monk asked: "I am a student who has newly entered the monastic community; I beg the Master for a reception."
The Master said, "Go. [The monk] asked, "I have heard it said in the teachings: 'This Dharma is equal; there is no high or low. What is this equal Dharma?
The Master said, "Mount Yao is high; Treasure Flower is low. [The monk] said, "In that case, does this not result in there being high and low?"
The Master said, "I knew you would understand it this way. Addressing the assembly upon hearing the sound of thunder, he asked, "Do you hear the sound of thunder?
Do you know its place of origin? If you know its place of origin, you will know where body and life fall.
If you do not even know this, as the ancients said: 'Those who do not know heaven and earth yet insist there are the heavens and earth—better to go drink tea. [Question: As for this...
"What is the Way? The Master said, "To die at evening would suffice. "Who is the Vajrapāṇi? The Master said, "He is of no use here.
"Where does a deceased monk go after his transformation? The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven!
Then he said, "As for that monk who finally asked, 'Where does a deceased monk go after his transformation? Shan..."
The monk said to him, "Heaven! Heaven! But tell me, where does the meaning lie?
Is it perhaps a sorrowful lament for his passing, or a piteous remembrance of the Master? If you evaluate it in such a way, you truly know nothing of his destination.
Do you wish to know his destination? There is no need to stand here long; go and rest. [Later,] he ascended the hall and said: "Winter departs and spring arrives; the gates of the pavilions..."
[The Master] said: "Open! If you can enter, there is no need to linger. Venerable Elders, have you yet been able to enter here?
If you can enter, then as the ancients said: 'Every place is Maitreya; there is no gate and no Sudhana.
If you have not yet entered, it is simply because you, venerable elders, are wandering aimlessly. I shall say no more. You have stood for long; take care."
Chan Master Zhisheng of Shengshou Monastery in Wujang, Suzhou, ascended the hall and said: "If one speaks of the Buddha-dharma, what further matter is there?
Therefore it is said: the mountains and rivers of past and present; the sun and moon of past and present; the human relations of past and present; the cities and towers of past and present."
This is called the Dharma-gate of Equality, which transcends the limits of past and future. Can you all believe it?
If you can believe it, practice in accordance with it. I shall take my leave; farewell.
Chan Master Shouru of Kaishua, a meritorious official of Hangzhou, ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "Do you know that the Holy Monk has arrived here together with all of you?
Since you have condescended to come from afar, how could I dare detain you? I shall take my leave; please remain long and be well."
