"If you are not from Henan, then you must be from Hebei. Baizhang Baizhuang struck him. The Master (Huangbo) held him back and gave him a slap.
Baizhang laughed heartily and called to his attendant, "Bring the meditation board and desk of our late master Baizhang here. The Master said, "Attendant, bring some fire.
Baizhang said, "Not so. You simply take it away; in the future, you shall sit and cut off the tongues of all people under heaven."
The Master arrived at the head of the Dharma-Body Stūpa. The stūpa master asked, "Which do you pay homage to first: the Buddha or the Patriarch?
The Master said, "I pay homage to neither the Patriarch nor the Buddha. The master said, "What grievance could there possibly be between the Patriarch, the Buddha, and you, Elder?

The Master shook his sleeves and departed. While the Master was delivering a letter for Huangbo to Mt. Wei, he was conversing with Yangshan. Yangshan said, "Elder brother, you will travel north in the future."
"There is a place where one may dwell. The Master said, "How could such a thing be? Yang said, "Just go;
later there will be one person who will assist you. This person will have only a head but no tail; he will have a beginning but no end. (This was a prediction concerning Puhua.
Later, the Master resided at Linji in Zhenzhou, where disciples gathered like clouds. One day, he said to the two senior monks Puhua and Kefu: "I..."
"I wish to establish the fundamental tenets of Huangbo here; you two go ahead and dismantle them for me. The two men bowed respectfully and departed.
Three days later, Puhua came back up and asked, "What did you say three days ago, Master? The Master struck him immediately.
Three days later, when Ke Fu came up and asked, "Why did the Master strike Puhua the other day? the Master struck him as well.
That evening, during the *xiaochan* (informal sermon), he said: "Sometimes one takes away the person but not the environment; sometimes one takes away the environment but not the person."
Sometimes both the person and the object are negated; sometimes neither the person nor the object is negated. (The dialogue and responses are fully contained within this chapter.
A monk asked: "What is the true Buddha? The true Dharma? The true Way? I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said:
"The Buddha is the purity of the mind. The Dharma is the luminosity of the mind. The Way is the pure light that is unimpeded everywhere. These three are one and all—"
This emptiness is a mere name and lacks substantial reality.

Just as a true practitioner of the Way maintains an uninterrupted state of mind from moment to moment—ever since Master Bodhidharma came from the Western Land, he sought only one who would not be deluded by others—and later encountered the Second Patriarch’s single word and attained realization, finally realizing that all his previous efforts had been in vain. This is the insight I have today.
This is no different from the Patriarchs and Buddhas. If you can realize it within the first phrase, you are fit to be a teacher to the Patriarchs and Buddhas.
If you can realize it within the second phrase, you are fit to be a teacher to gods and humans. If you can realize it within the third phrase, you will not even be able to save yourself.
A monk then asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "The seal of the three essentials opens; the vermilion dot is narrow."

Before there is even room for deliberation, the distinction between host and guest is already established. [The student] asked, "What is the second phrase? The Master said, "How could one with wondrous understanding fail to ask Wuzhuo?
How could Upagupta fail to match the mechanism that cuts the current? [The student] asked, "What is the third phrase? The Master said, "Just look at the puppets performing on the stage;
their every movement depends entirely upon the person inside pulling the strings. He then said, "In general, when expounding the essence of our school..."
"Vehicle. Within a single phrase, one must possess the three mysterious gates (*san xuanmen*). Each mysterious gate must possess the three essentials (*san yaoyao*):

there is the provisional (*quan*) and the real (*shi*); there is illumination (*zhao*) and function (*yong*). How do you all understand this? The Master said to the monks, "Sometimes a single verse..."
Sometimes a single verse is like a precious sword of the Vajra King; sometimes a single shout is like a lion crouching on its haunches;
and sometimes a single shout is like a probing pole with a blade of grass—it does not function as a mere shout.

How do you understand this? When the monk hesitated, the Master shouted. He addressed the assembly: "Those who study the Way must be extremely careful, like guests and hosts meeting one another. Then he shouted.
There was an exchange of discourse. At times he manifested forms in response to objects; at other times he functioned with his entire being.
Sometimes he wielded skillful means through displays of joy or anger; sometimes he appeared as half a body, or mounted a lion, or rode an elephant king.

When there was a genuine seeker of the Way, he would suddenly shout and first produce a lacquer basin. The good teacher failed to discern it as an external object and thus entered into that other’s realm.
The former person acted with pretension and affectation, whereupon the student again shouted. The former person refused to let go; this is a terminal illness that cannot be cured.
This is called "the guest looking at the host. Or, if it is a true spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), they do not bring forth any object;
they simply seize [the student] right at the point of their questioning. When the student is seized, they resist to the death and refuse to let go. This is...
The host looks at the guest. There may be a student who presents a single pure object before a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*).
When the spiritual friend discerns that this is an object and seizes it to hurl it into a pit, the student says, "Excellent, O spiritual friend!
The spiritual friend then says, "Alas! You do not distinguish between good and evil. The student then prostrates; this is called "the host looking at the host. Or...
A student of the Way comes before a spiritual friend wearing his shackles and fetters; the friend further places another layer of shackles and fetters upon him, and the student rejoices.
Neither can discern the other; this is called "the guest looking at the guest. This is what I, an old mountain monk, have brought up, O Virtuous Ones.
These were all instances of the Master using skillful means to distinguish between them, so that they might know the false from the correct.

The Master asked Lopu, "Since time immemorial, one person has used the staff and another has used the shout; which of these is more intimate? Lopu replied, "Neither is intimate. The Master asked, "What is the point of intimacy?"
Pufu let out a shout, and the Master struck him. Ascending the hall, the Master said: "There is one person who, for kalpas, remains on the road yet never leaves home.
There is another person who leaves home yet is not on the road. Which of these two is worthy of receiving the offerings of devas and humans? The Master asked the temple steward, "Where have you been?
The steward replied, "I have been to the prefectural city to sell yellow rice. The Master said, "Did you sell it all? The steward... [replied].
[The Master] said, "I have sold it all. The Master drew a line with his staff and asked, "Can you sell this? The host gave a shout, and the Master struck him.
When the head cook arrived, the Master recounted the previous conversation. The cook said, "The abbot did not understand the Master's meaning."
The Master said, "And how about you? The monk bowed, and the Master struck him as well. He ascended the hall and said:
"One person is atop a solitary peak with no way out; another person is at the crossroads with no front or back.
Tell me, which one is in front and which one is behind? Not acting as Vimalakīrti, not acting as Dharma Master Fu—take care! There was a pause.
An old veteran monk went to visit [the Master]. He immediately asked, “Is it right to prostrate, or is it right not to prostrate?
The Master gave a shout. The veteran bowed. The Master said, “What a fine ‘grass bandit’! The veteran said, “Thief! Thief! and then went out. The Master said, “Do not say that there is nothing to it.
At that time, the Head Seat was standing in attendance. The Master said, “Is there any fault here? The Seat said, “There is. The Master said, “The guest.”
“There is a fault. “The master’s house has a fault. “Both have faults. The Master asked, “Where does the fault lie?
The monk then went out. The Master said, “Do not say it is ‘no matter. (Nanquan heard this and said, “Official horses trampling one another. Later, the Master went to the capital to solicit alms.

Arriving at the door of a certain household, he said, “I am here to receive a portion of the family’s meal. An old woman said, “You are truly insatiable! The Master said, “Have you even had your rice yet?”
“I have already attained it. Why do you say I am so insatiable? Ba then closed the door. When the Master ascended the hall, a monk stepped forward;

the Master gave a shout, and the monk also shouted. The monk then prostrated, and the Master struck him. When Zhaozhou was traveling and arrived at the monastery, he was washing his feet in the rear quarters when the Master asked him, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou replied, “I happen to meet the mountain monk right now.”
[The Master] was washing his feet. The Master stepped forward and made a gesture as if listening. Yizhou said, "If you understand, then you understand;
why do you keep picking at it? The Master then returned to his quarters. Yizhou said, "After thirty years of traveling as a monk, today I have mistakenly provided a commentary for others.
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Dingzhou. The Master raised his staff. The monk hesitated, and the Master struck him. The monk did not accept this.
The Master said, "In the future, you will encounter those with clear eyes. Later, this monk went to visit Sansheng; as soon as he brought up the previous conversation, Sansheng struck him.
When the monk hesitated, Sansheng struck him again. The Master frequently used the shout (*he*) in response to stimuli, and the disciples under his guidance also learned to shout like their teacher.
The Master said, "If you all simply imitate my shouting, I shall now question you: suppose there were a person coming from the east..."
The Master emerged from the hall. One person came out from the West Hall; two people shouted in unison.
"Can you distinguish guest and host here? How would you go about making that distinction? "If you cannot distinguish them," he said, "you must not imitate this old monk’s shouting in the future.

He addressed the assembly: "Sometimes I first manifest illumination and then function; sometimes I first function and then manifest illumination; sometimes illumination and function occur simultaneously."

Sometimes illumination and function do not occur simultaneously; first there is illumination, then function—this occurs when there is a person present. First there is function, then illumination—this occurs when there is a dharma present.

Illumination and function are simultaneous—this is like driving away the ox of the plowman, seizing the food of the starving man, breaking the bone to extract the marrow, and applying needles and awls with piercing pain.
When illumination and function are not simultaneous, there is questioning and answering, the establishment of guest and host, and the mixing of water and mud.

He responded to others according to their capacity. If one were a person of superior caliber, they would have "lifted up and departed" even before he had raised his staff—this would still leave something to be desired.

When the Master was traveling on pilgrimage, he arrived at Longguang Temple just as the abbot was ascending the hall for the discourse. The Master stepped forward and asked, "Without deploying any sharp edge, how can one achieve victory?
Longguang remained seated. The Master said, "Great Teacher of Virtue, surely you have some skillful means? Longguang stared at him with wide-open eyes.
"Ha! The Master pointed his finger and said, "This old fellow has been defeated today. Next, he went to the place of Master Sanfeng Ping.
Ping asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Huangbo. Ping asked, "What words or phrases did Huangbo say?"
The Master said: "Last night, the Golden Ox met with calamity; even until now, no trace of him is seen. Ping said:

"The golden wind blows through the jade flute; who is the one who knows the music? The Master said: "He passes straight through ten thousand layers of barriers, never dwelling within the azure heavens."
Fengxue Ping said, "This question of yours is far too lofty. The Master said, "A golden phoenix born from a dragon breaks through the azure lapis lazuli.
Ping said, "Sit for a moment and drink some tea. He asked again, "Where have you recently come from? The Master said, "Longguang.
Ping asked, "How is it at Longguang these days? The Master then went out. Later, he went to Fenglin and encountered a woman on the road. The woman asked:
“Where has she gone? The Master said, “She has gone to Fenglin. The old woman said, “It happens that Fenglin is not there at the moment.

The Master asked, “Where has she gone? The old woman then departed. The Master called out, “Old woman! She turned her head back; the Master then departed. (An alternative version reads: The Master said, “Who says she is not there? He arrived at Fenglin.
Lin said, "May I ask you about something? The Master said, "Why do you gouge out flesh to create a sore?
Lin said, "The sea moon is clear and without shadow; the roaming fish alone is deluded. The Master said, "Since the sea moon has no shadow, how can the roaming fish be deluded?
Lin said, "By observing the wind one knows the waves arise; by gazing at the water, the wild sail drifts. The Master said, "The solitary moon shines alone upon the river."
The mountain was still. With a single long cry, heaven and earth turned autumnal. Lin said, "Let Zhang wield his three inches at will; try to speak a phrase on the spot.
The Master said, "When meeting a swordsman on the road, one must present a sword; if one is not a poet, one does not offer a poem.
Lin then desisted. The Master then offered this verse: "The Great Way is beyond sameness; Go west or east as you please. Like a spark from flint, do not—"

Furthermore: "The flash of lightning has no passage" (Miaoshan asked Yangshan: "The spark of fire cannot reach it; the flash of lightning has no passage. By what means do the sages of old define a person?"). Yangshan said: "What is your intention, Master? Miaoshan said:

"As long as there is verbal expression, there is no real meaning. Yangshan said: "Not so. Miaoshan said: "How about you, my son? Yangshan said: "In public, even a needle is not admitted; in private, a carriage and horse may pass. Magu asked:
"Of the twelve-faced Avalokiteśvara, which one is the front face? The Master descended from his meditation seat, seized him, and said: "Twelve-faced Avalokiteśvara!"
"Where have you gone? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! As Gu turned his body to prepare to sit, the Master struck him.
Gu caught the staff and they grappled each other back to the abbot’s quarters. The Master asked a nun, "A good arrival? A bad arrival? The nun shouted. The Master raised his staff and said:

"Speak further! Speak further! The nun shouted again, and the Master struck her. One day, the Master held up a steamed bun and showed it to Luopo, saying, "The myriad kinds and thousand variations do not depart from this;
their principle is non-dual. Luopo asked, "What is this principle of non-duality?
The Master again held up the bun and showed it to him. Luopo said, "In that case, there are the myriad kinds and thousand variations. The Master said, "..."
Regarding the "excrement" (poo) case: Master Puhui said, "Luo Gong looks in a mirror. When a monk approached, the Master raised his whisk; the monk bowed, and the Master struck him.

Another monk came, and the Master again raised his whisk; the monk paid no heed, and the Master struck him as well. Yet another monk came to visit; the Master raised his whisk, and the monk said, "Thank you for the Master’s instruction," whereupon the Master struck him again.

(Yunmen spoke on his behalf: "Master, do not hit me twice!"* *Note: Yunmen’s substitute response implies that the Master’s repeated striking was redundant and unnecessary. The "excrement" case refers to the fact that when one sees through the nature of reality, there is nothing left to grasp—like seeing one's own reflection in a mirror, or like the natural process of excretion, which leaves no trace.*

Yilao Zhihan asked, “The Great Awakened One said, ‘To attain it is to attain it,’ yet one has still not seen the pivot of Linji’s teaching. Magu asked, “Of the Great Compassionate One’s thousand hands and eyes, which is the true eye?
The Master grabbed him and said, “Of the Great Compassionate One’s thousand hands and eyes, what is the true eye? Speak quickly! Speak quickly!
Magu dragged the Master down from the meditation seat and sat back down. The Master made a formal inquiry, saying, “How do you do? As Magu hesitated, the Master struck him.
"Ho! [The Master] pulled down the meditation seat and sat back down. Gu stepped out. Later, he ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master held up his whisk. The monk gave a shout; the Master struck him. Another monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master again held up his whisk. The monk gave a shout; the Master also shouted. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him.
He then said, "O Great Assembly! Those who seek the Dharma do not shrink from the loss of body or life.

At the place of my late teacher Huangbo, I asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma three times, and on each occasion I was struck with a blow that felt like being brushed by a bundle of mugwort."
"Now I am thinking of another meal; who will take the first step? At that time, a monk came forward and said, "I, so-and-so, shall take the first step.
The Master handed him his staff. As the monk was about to receive it, the Master struck him. Later, while accompanying Puhua to a donor's banquet, the Master asked:
A hair swallows the vast ocean; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. Is this the wondrous function of supernatural powers, or is it simply the nature of things as they are?
[When the Master] transformed and kicked over the rice table, he said, "Too coarse, you fellow. [The monk] asked, "What kind of place is this?"
He spoke of the coarse and the subtle. On the following day, they went to the meal together again. The Master asked once more, "How does today’s offering compare to yesterday’s?
Yunhua kicked over the rice table again. The Master said, "You have succeeded, indeed, but you are far too crude. Yunhua gave a shout and said, "Blind fellow!"
"What do the Buddha-dharma teachings say about coarse and subtle? The Master then stuck out his tongue. The Master and the King’s attendant went to the Sangha Hall.
The King asked, "Do the monks in this hall study the sutras? The Master said, "They do not study the sutras. [The King] asked, "Then do they practice meditation?
The Master said, "They do not practice meditation. [The King] asked, "Since they neither study the sutras nor practice meditation, what exactly are they doing? The Master—
[The Master] said, "I am teaching him generally to become a Buddha and a Patriarch. [A monk] asked, "It is said that 'though gold dust is precious, if it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract.

What does this mean? The Master said, "I took you for a mere worldly fellow. Later, while the Master was ascending the hall, the two head seats from the two halls met and simultaneously let out a shout.
A monk asked the Master, "Is there still a distinction between guest and host? The Master said, "Guest and host are clearly distinct. The Master then called to the assembly.
He said: "To truly grasp the 'Guest and Host' phrase of Linji, go and ask the two head monks in the hall. Later, the Master resided in the Eastern Hall of Xinghua Temple in Daming Prefecture.
On the tenth day of the fourth month of the eighth year of the Xiandong era (the Dinghai year), as he was about to pass away, he spoke this verse of transmitting the Dharma:
"Following the current without ceasing—ask how it is? True illumination is boundless—explain it to him. Free from all marks..."
“One who lacks the name does not receive it. When the 'Blow-Off' blade has been used, one must quickly polish it.

He further addressed the assembly, saying, “After my passing, you must not let my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye be extinguished. Sansheng stepped forward and said, “How would we dare extinguish the Master’s Treasury of the True Dharma Eye?
The Master said, “In the future, if someone asks you, what will you say to them? Sansheng gave a shout. The Master said:
"Who would have known that my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye would be extinguished before this blind donkey? Having said this, he sat upright and passed away.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the northwest corner of the prefecture. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Huizhao, and his stupa was named Chengling.
Chan Master Xinghua Cunjiao of Weifu was a dharma heir of Chan Master Linji Xuanshi of the fifth generation under Nanyue.
While serving as the head seat in the assembly of Sansheng, he would often say: "I, when I..."
"I traveled once through the south, yet with my staff I never once struck upon a single person who truly understood the Buddha-dharma.
Upon hearing this, Sansheng asked, "What kind of eye do you possess to speak in such a manner? The Master then gave a shout. Sansheng said, "It must be you who can do so.
Later, when Daqiao heard this account being cited, he remarked, "How could the wind have ever blown it here?"
[The Master] came from within the gate of Dajue. Later, he went to Dajue and served as the head of the monastery (yuanzhu).

One day, Dajue called out, "Head of the Monastery, I have heard you say that after traveling throughout the South on pilgrimage, you have never once struck upon a single person who understands the Buddha-dharma.
On what basis do you speak in such a manner? The Master then gave a shout; Dajue then struck him. The Master—

Again Mazu shouted; Xuedou struck him. The next day, as Mazu was passing by the Dharma Hall, Xuedou summoned the head of the monastery and said, "I have a direct doubt regarding those two shouts you gave yesterday.
Mazu shouted again; Xuedou struck him again. Mazu shouted once more; Xuedou struck him yet again. Mazu said:
"Venerable Elder Brother, I have learned a phrase regarding guest and host from you three holy masters, yet I have been completely defeated by you all.
I pray that you will grant me a dharma-gate of peace and bliss. Jue said, "You blind fellow! You come here to surrender your defeat;
take off your patched robe and I shall give you a thorough beating! At these words, the master realized the teaching of his late master Linji.
Regarding the principle of receiving the staff at Huangbo’s place, when the Master later opened the hall, he held up the incense and said:

"This one stick of incense was originally intended for my elder brother Sansheng; Sansheng was too distant from me. It was originally intended for my elder brother Dajue; Dajue was too remote from me.
It is better that I offer it to my late teacher Linji. A monk asked: "Before the Many-Sons Stupa, together..."

"What is it you are discussing? The Master said, "One person transmits what is false; ten thousand people transmit what is true. On another occasion, the Master called to a monk. The monk responded, "Yes.
The Master said, "The pointing was there, but he did not arrive. He then called to another monk. The monk responded, "Yes. The Master said, "He arrived, but the pointing was not there."
A monk asked, "What is it like when [the host] comes from the four directions and eight sides? The Master said, "Strike the one in the middle. The monk then bowed.
The Master said, "Yesterday I went to a village feast. On the way, I encountered a sudden storm of wind and rain, but I managed to take shelter inside an old temple and get through.
He then asked the monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the place of Cui Chan. The Master said, "Did you bring anything back?"
Cui Chan shouted, "Have you brought it? The monk replied, "I have not brought it. The Master said, "If that is so, then it did not come from Cui Chan.
The monk then shouted. The Master struck him. Addressing the assembly, he said: "I hear shouting in the front corridor and shouting in the back quarters as well.
My sons, do not shout blindly or recklessly. Even if you were to shout yourself into existence, you would still be left in empty space."
He struck him down; there was not a breath of life left in him. When I had recovered and risen, I said to you, "It is not yet. Why?
Because I have never scattered genuine pearls within a purple silk curtain for you all to go after. Why do you shout and clamor so wildly?
When Yunju was living at Sanfeng Hermitage, the Master asked: "I shall temporarily borrow a question to serve as a shadow."
When Jū was serving as an attendant, how did it go? Jū had no reply. The Master said, "I suspect you, Preceptor, would have been unable to answer this question;
it would have been better to simply pay your respects and withdraw. Twenty years later, Jū said, "Reflecting on it now, at that time I need not have said, 'Why bother?
Later, when the Master sent a messenger for alms to the Teacher's location, the Master asked, "When you were staying at Sanpō-an, I, the old monk, asked—"
"That story cannot be answered," [the Master] said. "Even now, can you answer it? The Master brought up the previous story again.
The Teacher said, "For twenty years at Yunju, I have only been able to say, 'What need is there? Xinghua is not like this; how could he compare to saying, 'There is no need'?
The Master said to the rector Kebin, "Before long, you will become a master who leads the assembly. Kebin said, "I will not enter this protection."
The Master said, "If you have understood, you do not enter; if you have not understood, you do not enter. [Kebin] replied, "In neither case is it so.
The Master then struck him and said, "Venerable Kebin, having failed in the Dharma-battle, you shall be fined five strings of cash and provide a meal for the assembly.
The following day, the Master himself struck the gavel and said, "Venerable Kebin, having failed in the Dharma-battle, he is not permitted to eat," and he was immediately expelled.
At the Monastery, a monk asked, "What was the meaning of the National Teacher calling for his attendant? The Master said, "One blind man leading a crowd of blind men.
When the Master was serving as an attendant under Linji, Luopu came to visit him. Linji asked, "Where have you come from? Luopu replied, "From Luancheng."
Ji said, "May I ask you something? Pu replied, "A newly ordained monk does not understand.
Ji said, "Even if one were to shatter the Great Tang Empire, there would be no one to be found who does not understand. Go to the meditation hall.
The Master followed him and asked, "Just now, regarding that newcomer, did you intend to humble him, or not? Ji replied, "Who am I to concern myself with whether you are humbled or not?"
[Zhaozhou] was about to bestow [the robe). The Master said, "The Abbot only knows how to pick up a dead sparrow and pelt it on the ground;
he does not know how to use a turning phrase to cover it over. Jue said, "And what about you? The Master said, "I ask the Abbot to act as the newly arrived monk.
Jue then said, "A new precept-holder does not understand. The Master said, "That is rather my own fault. Jue said, "Your words conceal the sharp edge. The Master—

[The Master] was about to deliberate [on the matter]. Linji struck him. When evening came, Linji said again, "Today when I questioned the newly arrived one, it was like hitting a dying sparrow on the ground;
I hit him right where he was in his nest. But when you produced your words, I shouted and raised him up, hitting him toward the blue clouds.

The Master said, "The grass-thief has been utterly defeated. Linji then struck him. Seeing that a fellow practitioner had arrived, the Master had just stepped onto the Dharma seat— [Note: The provided text ends abruptly.]
The Master gave a shout. The monk also shouted. The Master shouted again. The monk also shouted. The Master stepped forward and raised his staff. The monk shouted once more. The Master said, "Look!
This blind fellow still dares to act as the host. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him down directly from the Dharma hall.
An attendant asked, "What did that monk just do to offend you, Master? The Master replied, "Just now..."
It has power; it has substance; it has illumination; it has function. Yet when I stretch my hand across his face two times, he cannot proceed here.
For a blind fellow such as this, when shall we wait to strike him?
The monk bowed and asked: "I know you have long hidden your precious sword; today, I beg to borrow it briefly upon the stage."
The Master said, "It is not borrowed. The monk asked, "Why is it not borrowed? The Master said, "If one does not possess the eyes of Zhang Hua, one merely gazes at the light piercing the Dipper.
The monk asked, "What of the one who employs it? The Master said, "Lying across the body to confront the universe—who is the person who emerges with their head above?

The monk then made a gesture of stretching out his neck. The Master said, "Ha! The monk said, "Yes," and then returned to the assembly. Later, the imperial carriage of Emperor Zhuangzong of the Later Tang [arrived].

He traveled north to Hebei. Upon returning to the imperial palace at Weifu, the Emperor summoned the Master and asked, "Since I recovered the Central Plains, I have obtained a treasure for which no one has yet offered a price.
The Master said, "I beg Your Majesty to let me see this treasure. The Emperor extended the ends of his *faku tou* (a head-dress) with both hands.
The Master said, "Who would dare to offer a price for the treasure of a sovereign? [Xuanjue’s Probe]: Now tell me, did Xinghua approve of Zhuangzong, or did he not? If [you can say],...

"If you accept [the Emperor's] honor, where is the eye of the Flourishing Dharma? If you do not accept it, where lies the fault of the Emperor? The Emperor’s countenance was greatly pleased, and he bestowed upon the Master purple robes and a title.

The Master declined both. The Emperor then presented a horse for the Master to ride; the horse suddenly bolted, and the Master fell, injuring his foot. The Emperor again bestowed medicine for treatment.
The Master called for the head monk and said, "Make me a wooden crutch. When the head monk had finished it and brought it to him, the Master—
Upon receiving him, [the Master] walked around the monastery and asked the monks, "Do you recognize this old monk? They replied, "How could we not recognize the Master?

The Master said, "A 'leaping-leg' Dharma teacher—one who can speak but cannot practice. He then went to the Dharma Hall and ordered the *vinaya-dhara* (Venerable One) to strike the bell to assemble the community.

Ji asked, "What is the Way? The Master struck him. He asked, "What is one who is on the Way? The Master said, "This old monk has long resided in the Chéngxīn Monastery.
He asked, "What is one who is among those on the Way? The Master said, "Wearing a tattered robe for many years.

He asked, "What is it like when the open ground does not allow a breeze to pass? The Master said, "Lacquer. He asked, "Since this is the 'Chéngxīn' (Transparency of Mind), why do you come out and go in? The Master said:
The Master applied moxibustion to the bridge of his nose. The monk bowed, and the Master struck him.
A monk asked the Abbot of Zhuyuan Mountain in Jingnan Prefecture, "I have long heard that you, Master, are proficient in Chan; is this true? The Master said:
The monk said, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master stepped forward, covered the monk's mouth with his hand, and said, "Lower your voice.
Lower your voice. The monk gave him a slap and pushed him away. The Master said, "I brought this upon myself. The monk shook out his sleeves and left.
The Master laughed and said, "Had I known it would turn out like this, I would regret not having done so. He then asked, "Since it is a bamboo grove, will there be any shoots? The Master [replied].
[The Master] said, "A thousand trees, ten thousand trees. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then the student has a share. The Master asked, "How do you understand this?
As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him.
A monk asked the Master of Fahua Monastery in Songzhou, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Sitting alone before the five peaks.
The monk asked, “What is the newly risen moon? The Master said, “Neither high nor low. The monk asked, “Does this allow a student to gaze upon it with reverence?
The Master said, “Look after three days. The monk asked, “What is the家风 (monastic style) of the Lotus School? The Master said, “When it is cold...”
"Killed by cold; killed by heat when it is hot. A monk asked, "What is 'killed by cold when it is cold'?

The Master said, "In threes and twos, they walk with their heads embraced. He asked, "What is 'killed by heat when it is hot'? The Master said, "Those who see them from east, west, south, or north laugh at them.
A student asked, "When a practitioner holds a white blade in hand and advances directly into the gate, what then? The Master said, "Try it yourself and see."
The monk gave a shout. The Master seized him; the monk struck him with a palm as soon as he was caught. The Master pushed him away and said, "Today I have suffered a loss.
The monk performed a dance and departed. The Master said, "A thief who has committed the primary offense."
A monk asked Chan Master Jiao of Luzu Mountain in Pizhou, a successor of Chan Master Xian of Guankui, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said:

Today I will not answer your questions. [The monk] said, "How wonderful that you do not answer! The Master then struck him. [The monk] asked, "What is the tree at the Twin Groves? The Master said, "The formless body within the body with form.
[The monk] asked, "What is the formless body within the body with form? The Master said, "An iron barbarian beneath a golden incense burner.

[The monk] asked, "What is it like for one who dwells alone on a solitary peak? The Master said, "The formless body within the body with form. [The monk] asked, "What is the formless body within the body with form? The Master said, "An iron barbarian beneath a golden incense burner."
The Master said, "At midnight the sun is bright; at noon it strikes the third watch. A questioner asked, "What is the matter beyond the norm?
The Master said, "After the karmic conditions of transformation have ended, what lies beyond empty space? A questioner asked, "When there is no door through which to advance, what then?
The Master said, "Too dull-witted! The questioner said, "It is not a matter of being dull-witted. When there is truly no door through which to advance, what then? The Master said, "..."

The spiritual mechanism has never been discussed in terms of boundaries; adhering to the Dharma without a gate, one remains within the darkness. A student asked, "What is the place where a student exerts effort?
The Master said, "When spring comes, the grass turns green of its own accord; once the moon rises, it is already bright. He asked, "What is the place where there is no exertion of effort?
The Master said, "Mountains crumble and stones fall; wild fires spread across the level plains."

The monk who was the Dharma heir of Master Zhīyī asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master replied, “Wrapped in hemp and bound in paper. A monk asked, “When the hundred matters are resolved and the thousand instances are clear, what then?
The Master struck him with his staff as he spoke. A monk asked, “I pray that the Master will proclaim a discourse that transcends the conventional.”
The Master said, "A narrow path does not allow the wind to pass. [Zhijian] asked, "Is it not simply this very thing? The Master then sighed repeatedly.
When Upāsaka Ji arrived at Nanchan in Luojiang while traveling on pilgrimage, the military commander Zhu hosted a vegetarian feast.

Entering the Sangha hall, he looked around and said, "Right here! He then proceeded to distribute the incense, his mouth never ceasing its discourse. Upon reaching the Master’s presence, the Master immediately questioned him.
"Right here it is. What is this? Xingjun then gave a shout. The Master said, "Xingjun is fortunately one who understands the Buddha-dharma;
why do you flare up in anger? Xingjun said, "It would not do to call it 'flaring up in anger. The Master then gave a shout.
Xingjun said, "The hook was in a place beyond doubt. The Master then shouted again, whereupon Xingjun ceased.

After the midday meal, he ordered the Guest Office to invite the monk who had just shouted to come before him. When the monk arrived, the Master engaged in conversation with Xingjun alone, paying no heed to anyone else.
The Record Keeper said, "Just now, how could Xingjun tolerate this monk’s impertinence? Xingjun replied, "If it were anyone else..."
"You all drink! This official has a sword. The Monastic Registrar said, "We certainly do not understand;
it must be Elder Huī who can. The General said, "Even if it were Elder Nanchan, you would not have even dreamed of him yet.
A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The dragon soars over the vast ocean; the fish leap in the deep pool."
[The monk] asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, "At night one hears the drums for the sacrificial spirits; at dawn one listens to the songs of those crossing the rapids.
[The monk] asked, "What is the house style of the Venerable One? The Master said, "A three-legged toad carries a great elephant on its back."
Chan Master Yanzhao of Fengxue in Ruizhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Nanyuan Yong of the seventh generation under Nanyue.
He was a native of the Liu clan from Yuhang. From childhood, he abstained from meat and pungent vegetables and studied the Confucian classics.

He was to have entered the civil service examination, but failing to succeed on his first attempt, he left home to become a monk. He relied upon Master Zhigong at Kaiyuan Temple in his native prefecture to shave his head and receive full ordination.
There he studied the Tiantai system of *śamatha-vipaśyanā*. At the age of twenty-five, he visited Jingqing. Jingqing asked him, "Where have you recently departed from?"
The Master said, "Since leaving the East, I have come here. Qing asked, "Did you cross the Xiao River? The Master said, "A great vessel sails alone through the void; there is no Xiao River to cross.
Qing said, "At Mirror Water and Qin Mountain, even birds cannot fly across. Do not speak of hearsay.
The Master said, "Even the vast ocean fears the power of the *meng-lun* warship; with sails flying across the Milky Way, one crosses the Five Lakes. Qing stood upright.
Fuzi said, "What can be done about this? The Master asked, "What is this? Qing said, "Indeed, I do not recognize it.

The Master said, "Appearing and disappearing, rolling up and unfolding, you act in the same way as the Master. Qing said, "Using a ladle to divine by listening to empty sounds; sleeping soundly while indulging in idle chatter.
The Master said, "A vast marsh conceals mountains; principle can subdue a leopard. Qing said, "Forgiving sins and releasing transgressions—hurry!"

"You must go out. The Master said, "If you go out, you will lose it. He then went out to the Dharma Hall and said, "For a traveler on foot, if one's karmic conditions have not yet exhausted their goodness, one must not simply stop and leave.
He returned and said, "I, this humble monk, have just now rashly presented my small ignorance and presumed to trouble your venerable countenance.
I humbly receive your compassion and have not been granted punishment. Qing said, "What you said just now was correct."
"Coming from the east—is that not coming from Cuiyan? The Master said, "Xuedou personally dwells to the east of Bao’ai.

Qing said, "Not following the mad interpretations of the 'lost sheep,' you have instead come here to recite verses. The Master said, "When meeting a sword-wielder on the road, one must present a sword;
if you are no poet, do not offer a poem. Qing said, "Hide the poem quickly for now; let me borrow the sword for a moment. The Master [held out his hand].
Wushou said, "The person from Shouzeng took his sword and left. Xuefeng Qing said, "Not only did he offend public morality, but he also revealed his own coarseness.
Wushou said, "If one does not offend public morality, how can one manifest the mind of the ancient Buddhas? Qing asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas?"
The Master said, "If you grant me another permission to enter, what do you have now? Qing said, "A monk coming from the East cannot distinguish beans from wheat;
he has only heard 'never ceasing,' so how can he suppress himself with 'only ceasing'? The Master said, "A great wave surges a thousand fathoms, yet the clear waves do not depart from the water.
Qing said, "One phrase cuts off the flow; ten thousand functions are stilled and pared away. The Master then bowed. Qing said:
"Excellent, this patch-robed monk! Excellent, this patch-robed monk! When the Master arrived at Huayan, Huayan asked him, "I have a 'Song of Herding Cattle';

I request that you, O Kalyāṇamitra, provide a verse in response. The Master said: "The *gegu* drum beats and the whip cracks as the ox leaps like a leopard; by the plum trees of the distant village, its muzzle is a blur of movement."
The Master visited Nanyuan. Upon entering the gate, he did not prostrate. Nanyuan said, "Upon entering the gate, one must discern the host.
The Master said, "If you are being earnest, please distinguish it for me, Master. Nanyuan patted his left knee once; the Master then let out a shout. Nanyuan patted his right knee once.
The Master shouted again. The Abbot said, "Setting aside the single blow on the left, what about the single blow on the right?
The Master said, "Blind! The Abbot then raised his staff. The Master said, "Do not apply blind fetters or strike blindly; seize and beat the Old Buddha! Do not say I did not warn you."
The Abbot threw down his staff and said, "Today you have been thoroughly outwitted by this yellow-faced monk from Zhejiang.
The Master said, "The Abbot seems much like one who, unable to obtain alms, falsely claims he is not hungry. The Abbot said, "Have you ever been to this place before, Dharma-heir?
The Master said, "What kind of question is that? The Abbot said, "I am simply asking you a straightforward question. The Master said, "In that case, you cannot let me go."

[The Master] passed through [the hall], then descended to join the assembly. Upon finishing, he ascended to the head of the hall to offer his thanks. The Abbot asked, "Disciple, whom have you encountered?
The Master replied, "I was at Huayan in Xiangzhou, where I spent the summer retreat with Attendant Kuang. The Abbot said, "You have personally met a master.

The Abbot then asked, "Regarding the single blow of the staff in the South, how do they deliberate upon it? The Master replied, "They deliberate upon it as something extraordinary. The Master [then departed].
He then asked, "How do you, Master, deliberate upon this single blow here? Yuan took up his staff and said, "In the blow of the staff, there is no patience with birth;
when facing the situation, the teacher is not seen. At these words, the Master attained a great realization of the profound principle and remained in attendance for six years.

The fourfold assembly invited Fengxue to serve as their presiding master for another eight years. Then, Magistrate Li, together with the officials and commoners of the entire city, invited him once more to open the hall and expound the Dharma.
Ascending the hall, [Fengxue] said: "For those who possess the eye of study, when facing a critical moment, you must have the great function manifest before you;
do not constrain yourselves by minor details. Even if you were to gain realization prior to words, it would still be a lingering shell and a deluded enclosure. Though one may transcend phrases..."

Those below have attained proficiency, yet they cannot avoid encountering wild views wherever they go; these must stem from their previous reliance on others to form interpretations, resulting in two divergent paths—clarity and obscurity.
I shall now sweep them away all at once, so that each one becomes like a lion cub, letting out a roar with a "tsha-ya" sound, standing upright as if carved from a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
Who would dare look upon such a one with a direct eye? To look is to blind one's own eyes. At that time—
A monk asked, "What is the Eye of the True Dharma? The Master said, "It is already blind. The monk asked, "After it has become blind, what then?

The Master said, "Reaching for the sky and groping on the ground. Later, because military rebels were causing havoc in his native district, the Master went with the assembly to seek refuge in Yingzhou.

He visited the former host, Governor Li, who invited him to stay in the government office to spend the summer retreat. There, he presided over a great assembly where offerings were universally distributed.
He requested the Master to ascend the hall. As soon as he had taken his seat, he said: "The mind-ground of the Patriarchs is like the mechanism of an iron ox:
if it moves, it is sealed; if it stays, it is broken. But what of neither moving nor staying—is it sealed, or is it not sealed?"
"Is there anyone who can speak to this? At that time, the Elder Lupi came forward and asked, "This student possesses the mechanism of the Iron Ox;

I pray that the Master will not affix his seal upon me. The Master said, "I am accustomed to fishing for whales and leviathans in vast depths; yet you sigh over the frog’s strides as it wallows in the mud and sand.
Lupi stood there lost in thought. The Master shouted, "Elder, why do you not offer a word? As Lupi hesitated, the Master struck him.
The Master struck him once with his whisk and said, "Do you still remember the *huatou*? Try to bring it up. As Bo was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him again with the whisk.
The Herdsman said, "I know now that the Buddha-dharma and the royal law are one and the same. The Master asked, "What principle have you seen?
The Herdsman replied, "To hesitate when one ought to act decisively brings disorder in its wake. The Master then descended from his seat. This occurred in the ninth month.
The Grand Master Song of Ruizhou donated his residence to establish a monastery and subsequently came to Yingzhou to invite the Master to reside as its abbot.

In the first year of the Guangshun era of the Zhou dynasty, the monastery was granted the name Guanghui. The Master resided there for twenty-two years, with a community of over a hundred followers at all times.
One day, while presiding over the assembly, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "How is it that he is not the Buddha? The monk said, "I do not yet understand this mystery."
The student said, "I request that the Master point directly. The Master said, "My home is on the Isle of the Sea Gate; the sun of Fusang is the first to shine upon it.
The student asked, "What is it like when the bright moon is suspended in the sky? The Master said, "It does not roll down from the heavens; let it lie buried in the earth as it pleases.
The student asked, "The ancient melody has no rhyme or meter; how can one harmonize with it? The Master said, "A wooden cock crows at midnight; a straw dog barks until dawn."
Ascending the hall, he cited a poem by Hanshan: “The Brahmin has passed away and come back; His soul and consciousness meet Lord Yama.
Though he has read all the books of a hundred kings, He cannot yet escape being flogged and interrogated. If he but once utters ‘Namo Buddha,’ He shall thereby attain the Way of Buddhahood.
A monk asked, “What is this ‘once uttering Namo Buddha’? The Master said, “The lamp connects with the phoenix wings, illuminating the hall; the moon reflects upon the lady’s蛾眉 (yumei) brows.”
[The Master] looked at him with a stern face. He asked, "What is Buddha? The Master said, "A wooden horse whinnies in the wind because it has no tether;
a clay ox with horns on its back suffers under the lash. He asked, "What is the sword of vast wisdom? The Master said, "I do not slay the dead.

He asked, "How was it before the ancient mirror had been polished? The Master said, "The celestial demons’ hearts burst. He asked, "How is it after it has been polished? The Master said, "Xuan-yuan [the Yellow Emperor]."
[The Master] said: "There is no Way. [The student] asked: "The question of the spear and shield fundamentally constitutes a dual obscuration;

what of the matter of the bright pearls in the celestial net? The Master said: "To build a mountain, one climbs nine *ren*; to weigh a thousand *jin*, one must grasp the soil. [The student] asked: "When Gan Mu received the Duke Wen, how many people knew his mind?"
The Master said: "In my youth, I once resolved the array of dragons and snakes; now grown old and decrepit, I listen to the songs of children.
A monk asked: "What is the Lord of Mount Qingliang? The Master said: "A single phrase was not sufficient for Wuzhuo’s question; even until now, he remains a wandering monk in the wilds.
A monk asked: "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: "The crane has nine layers of mists, yet its wings find it hard to soar; the horse lacks—"
"Trailing the wind for a thousand *li* is but a vain pursuit. [The questioner] asked: "Please speak words that have never been uttered before.

The Master said: "Entering the market, one can let out a long whistle; returning home, one wears short trousers. [The questioner] asked: "At the end of summer, today, what is the Master’s intent? The Master said: "I do not pity the goose protecting the snow;
I am merely glad for the wax figure on the ice. [The questioner] asked: "When there is no road back to one's hometown, what then? The Master said: "Plainly looking down upon the red [sun/sky]."

[The Master] said, "A place of rot. It exhausts the life-long efforts of one who kills his own son. [Question: "The green of the desolate wilds fills the eyes; yet auspicious grasses flourish there. What is the situation at such a time?
[The Master] said, "A golden ball freshly cast from a red furnace; it shatters the iron-skin face of the *jiaoluo* (monk). [Question: "What is the pivot of mutual exchange?
[The Master] said, "Blindly shouting and crying out in total blindness. [Question: "If the true nature does not follow conditions, how [is this so]?"

[The student] attained realization. The Master said: "Incense smoke drips onto the pork stall. [The student] asked: "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said: "The horse-herder’s wife at the sands of Jinshe. [The student] asked:

"When a single color is difficult to distinguish, I request the Master to reveal it. The Master said: *Note: This passage consists of Zen kōans (public cases) featuring exchanges between masters and students regarding the nature of reality and the ineffable state of enlightenment.*
The brazier is filled with added coals, yet one still laments the cold; travelers on the road merely endure the chill. [A student] asked, "What is the place where a student establishes themselves?
The Master said, "The mud ox bellows from the bottom of the well; the jade hare is startled in the forest. [Another] asked, "What is the Way?"
The Master said, “In front of the Five-Phoenix Pavilion. [The monk] asked, “What is it like for one on the Way? The Master said, “Ask the Imperial City Prefect.

[The monk] asked, “Regarding the principle of not harming things, please, Master, speak directly. The Master said, “Even ripping open the belly and exposing the heart would still not satisfy your impatience.

[The monk] asked, “Before things have settled into turbidity, how can one attain illumination? The Master said, “Running downhill, one does not stop; such a swift opportunity is difficult to encounter. [The monk] asked, “As for suchness...”
"What is the place where a patch-robed monk practices? The Master said, "Receiving blows upon the head while muttering in one's mouth.

[The student] asked, "Regarding the talk of the moon at Vulture Peak and the pointing to the moon at Caoxi—setting aside these two paths, I ask the Master to point directly. The Master said, "To remain silent would be improper for one who is not mute.

[The student] said, "I ask the Master to provide a definitive judgment. The Master said, "First, cross the Muli River. [The student] asked, "When floating or sinking according to nature, it is like..."
"What? the Master said. "Leading an ox that will not enter the pen. "Question: When one attains realization upon hearing [the Master] remain silent, what then?
The Master said, "With ears cut off, lying in the street. "Question: When the smoke of war has forever ceased, what then? The Master said, "Both feet kicking at the empty air. "Question:

When the Patriarchal Command is being put into practice, what then? The Master said, "A dot. "Question: When one ascends to the Nine-and-Five Throne without wielding so much as an inch of blade, what then? The Master—
[The Master] said: "To whip a corpse and force it to bow its neck, and to ascend the hall. He raised [the following] saying: An ancient said, "I have an arrow that has long been tempered and refined;
when shot, it reaches throughout the ten directions, yet where it falls, no one sees it. The Master said: "I, this mountain monk, am not like that.
I have an arrow that has never been tempered or refined; it does not reach throughout the ten directions when shot, yet nonetheless, no one sees it. A monk then asked:
"What is the Master’s arrow? The Master drew a bow. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Drag out this dead man!
A monk asked, "How was it before Niu-t'ou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "Spreading the mat and holding the bowl. The monk asked, "How was it after he saw him?
The Master said, "Spreading the mat and holding the bowl. A monk asked, "How was it when one has not yet reached the source? The Master said, "The crane is cold."
Moving the nest is easy; for a dragon to emerge from its cave in the cold is difficult. Regarding the phrase that does not reveal its sharp edge, how does one distinguish host from guest?

The Master said: "Mouth holding a ram's horn, glued with glue. Question: "When putting one’s body to face danger, what then? The Master said: "A long letter laid bare, writing out the source of transgression.
Question: "The student understands how to ask about enigmatic phrases; I request the Master to bring forth a mechanism that startles people. The Master said: [Silence].
The Master said, "It is clear within the mind, yet the eyes are dark. A questioner asked, "When the time of birth and death arrives, what then?
The Master said, "A shirt cut from blue cloth invites the barking of dogs. The questioner asked, "How can one ensure they do not bark? The Master said, "It is best to withdraw and avoid them;

then there will be silence and no sound. A questioner asked, "What is a true man of the Way? The Master said, "Prostrating toward the West atop the tip of a bamboo pole. A questioner asked about fish... [text ends]
[Question: "What is it like when one is hidden in a deep pool? [Master: "Washed away by boiling water and scorched by fire. [Question:
"What is the place where all Buddhas walk? [Master: "Beneath the green pines and lush bamboos. [Question: "What is a great spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*)?
[Master: "One who kills people without blinking. [Question: "Since he is a great spiritual friend, why does he kill people without blinking? [Master: "..."
In the midst of dust and shadows, one does not brush away the sleeves; before the painted halberd gate, one grinds an inch of gold.
"One is six, and six is one. When both one and six have vanished, what then? The Master said, "A single arrow brings down two vultures. [The student] asked, "What is the meaning?"
The Master said: "The body perishes and the traces fade away. [The student] asked: "I do not ask about picking leaves or seeking branches;

as for the matter of directly reaching the source, what is it like? The Master said: "Leaving at dawn to attend the offering; returning with the rain while opening the pond. [The student] asked: "Question, question, question—all of this is merely fabricating the strange."

"Please, Master, point directly to the root source. The Master said, "Rare is the guest who pierces their own ears; many are those who mark the boat after the jade has been lost. The student asked, "At this very moment, how is it?
The Master said, "Though the blind tortoise finds the floating wood—how secure and steady! When flowers bloom upon withered wood, it is spring beyond all things.
The student asked, "The jeweled stupa is originally without seams; the golden gate opens this very day. At such a time, what is it like? The Master said, "Zhizhi. (Jizhi Bodhisattva).
Zao came forward and joined his palms. The Heavenly King held him out, but no one recognized him. [Someone] asked, "What is it like for one within the stupa?

The Master said, "Withered flowers are swept away by the wind; fragrant water rains down. [Someone] asked, "When one who remains unchanging amidst changing conditions suddenly meets a true知音 (zhīyīn—'one who understands'), what then?
The Master said, "Clad in *shā* grass, standing askew beyond a thousand peaks; leading water to irrigate vegetables before the Five Elders."
Question: "It is like carving a mark on a boat to find what fell into the water; how is this applied to everyday affairs? The Master said: "Great merit goes unrewarded;

the thatched gate is overgrown with weeds. Question: "Since the ancients of old, seal after seal has been matched in accord. What is the eye of this mutual accord? The Master said: "The frivolous and garrulous practitioner knows the shifts of opportunity;
cast away the handkerchief for wiping tears and summoning the soul. Question: "Regarding the rewards for labor during the nine months of summer retreat..."

"Please, Master, grant me a word of recommendation. The Master said: "The whisk emerges from the sleeve, clearing away the rain from the dragon’s cave; the cup floats upon the waves, and the flower overflows from the alms-bag. He asked:

"Regarding the original freedom of self-indulgence (*svairacarya*), with whom should one respond? The Master said: "A handful of fragrant kusha grass has not yet been picked up, when the six-ringed golden staff resounds through the distant void.
He asked: "The West Patriarch transmitted [the Dharma]; I pray the Master provide the definitive point. The Master said: "One dog barks at the empty sky."
A thousand monkeys gnawed at the fruit. [A monk] asked, "How far apart are the Way of the King and the Way of the Buddha?

The Master said, "When the straw dog barks, heaven and earth merge; after the wooden cock crows, the ancestral lamp shines. [Another] asked about the Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs, requesting the Master to polish it for him.

The Master said, "The Patriarch’s moon soars into the void, perfecting sacred wisdom; on what mountain would the pines and cypresses not be lush green? He ascended the hall and said, "If you establish even one..."

When there is a single speck of dust, the state and its people flourish, yet the village elders frown. When not a single speck of dust is established, the state and its people perish, yet the village elders remain at peace.
In this matter, it is clear that the *śrāmaṇera* has no share; it is entirely the old monk’s. If one does not understand this, the old monk is actually the *śrāmaṇera*.
Both the *śrāmaṇera* and the old monk can cause all people in the world to awaken, and they can also cause all people in the world to go blind.
[The Master] addressed the assembly: "Do you wish to recognize the *kalyāṇamitra*? [He] snapped his fingers once to the right and said, 'It is here.

Do you wish to recognize this old monk? [He] snapped his fingers once to the left and said, 'It is here. A monk asked, "The great assembly has gathered like clouds; we pray that the Master will preach the Dharma. The Master replied:

The barefoot man chases the rabbit; the one wearing boots eats the meat. Question: "I have never extensively studied the teachings of the Empty King. May I briefly borrow your wondrous mechanism to try and speak?
The Master said: "Jade is flawless; yet the foot is cut off by the decree below. Question: "What is the phrase of non-action? The Master said:
"The precious candle stands in the courtyard, its red light piercing the Great Void. Question: "What is it like when facing [death]?"

A single phrase of the pivot. The Master said: "Using the wind to fan the fire requires little effort. Question: "When the plain face is presented, what then? The Master said: "Remove the veil covering the face. Question: "Purple chrysanthemums half-bloom as autumn grows old; when the full moon faces the door, what is the meaning? The Master said: "The moon rises over Mount Penglai and all people see it; last night it was struck by frost, yet you did not know.
