Ji asked, "Ordinarily you do not hold anything in your hands; how do you provide offerings for the monks of the Five Lakes? The Master said, "I eat heavenly *sūdhā* rice, not precious delicacies;
with a single flavor of fine soup, one is satisfied and stops. He asked, "What was it like before Oxhead saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "A new deity still requires a shamaness to perform the sacrifice. He asked, "And what was it like after he saw him? The Master said, "The old deity has been replaced by a new one."

The Master said: "An ancient temple has once again been inscribed by a scholar. He ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "Now, one who expounds the Dharma must possess the Ten Wisdoms Identical with Reality.
If one does not possess these Ten Wisdoms Identical with Reality, one cannot distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox, nor differentiate the monastic from the lay;
thus, one cannot serve as eyes for gods and humans to determine right from wrong. It would be like a bird flying through the sky with broken wings, or like an arrow..."
When the arrow is shot, the string snaps. Because the string snaps, the arrow does not hit its mark. Because the wing is broken, it cannot fly through the air.
When the string is strong and the wing is firm, the arrow pierces both the air and the target. What is this "Ten Wisdoms Identical with Reality"? Point them out for all you venerable seniors:
first, identical substance; second, identical great matter; third, collectively identical companionship; fourth, identical true resolve; fifth, identical pervasiveness.

1. Universal; 2. Identical in being fully endowed; 3. Identical in gain and loss; 4. Identical in birth and death; 5. Identical in the roar of the voice; 6. Identical in attaining entry. It is further asked:
With what kind of person is one identical in attaining entry? With whom is one identical in the roar of the voice? What is it that is identical in birth and death?
What thing is identical in gain and loss? Which one is identical in being fully endowed? And what is it that is identical in pervading all?
Universally! Who shares the true resolve? Who can be said to be a fellow practitioner? Which one shares in the Great Matter? What thing shares the same substance?
Is there anyone who can point it out? Those who can point it out do not begrudge their compassion; those who cannot point it out have not yet attained the eye of study.
You must discern this with urgency; you must recognize right from wrong. The face is present before you—it must not be delayed.

[The Master] stood up. "Be careful. Li Hou, the Governor of Longde Prefecture, had long been acquainted with the Master. He sent an invitation to the Master at Chengtian Monastery, but though he went three times, the Master did not go.
The messenger was punished for this. When the messenger arrived again, he said, "I must have you come with me; otherwise, I shall simply die.
The Master laughed and said, "I am old and ill, and have already resolved not to leave the mountain. If I were to go, it would be a matter of who goes first and who follows; why [bother]?"

The master said, "We must go together. The messenger replied, "If you grant me leave, I shall follow whether before or after; it is for you to choose. The master ordered that the meal be prepared and his traveling gear readied, saying, "I shall depart first.
He set down his chopsticks and passed away. His body was cremated, the *śarīra* were collected, and a stupa was erected.
Chan Master Guisheng of Guangjiao Monastery in Ye County, Ruizhou, was the son of the Jia family of Jizhou.
In his early twenties, he left home for ordination at Baoshou Monastery in Yizhou and received full precepts there. Later, he traveled to various regions to study under Shoushan.

One day, Shoushan held up a bamboo stick and asked him, "If you call it a bamboo stick, you contradict [the ultimate]; if you do not call it a bamboo stick, you turn your back [on the conventional]. What do you call it? The Master—
He snatched it up, threw it onto the ground, and asked, "What is this? Shanshan replied, "Blind! At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.

When he opened the hall for formal teaching, a monk asked, "The patriarchs have transmitted one to another the seal of the patriarchate; of whom do you now receive the Dharma as a successor? The Master said:
The Son of Heaven within the realm; the General beyond the passes. [The student] said: "I have heard that you are a single drop from the ocean;

I have received your instruction, but what is the matter of the supreme ancestral wind? The Master said: "Fan Kuai’s wrath before the Hall of the High Ancestor—know that ten thousand miles away, smoke and dust are utterly extinguished.
[The student] asked: "In Vimalakīrti’s chamber, the sun and moon do not serve as illumination. In your Reverence’s chamber, what serves as illumination? The Master said:
His eyebrows were parted in the shape of the character "八" (eight). [The monk] asked, "I do not yet understand the meaning of this. The Master said, "Both ears hang down to his shoulders.
[The monk] asked, "What is the act that transcends the teacher? The Master said, "How long are the old monk’s eyebrows? [The monk] asked, "What is the body revealed alone amidst the dust?
The Master said, "A thousand tents in the north; ten-thousand-hu ships in the south. [The monk] said, "If it is so, then it is not..."

[The student] said, "It is but dust. The Master said, "This is the talk of those who merely parrot words. [The student] asked, "How are the myriad practices? The Master said, "A single letter contains them all.

[The student] asked, "What is the Master’s profound depth? The Master said, "The cat has the merit of drinking blood; the tiger has the virtue of raising the dead. [The student] asked, "Is it not this very thing?
The Master said, "The mortar pounds toward the southeast; the millstone grinds toward the northwest. [The student] asked, "What is the indestructible diamond body? The Master said, [as before].
The Master said, "A hundred fragments. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning? The Master said, "In the end, it is but a heap of ashes.
[The monk] asked, "Without falling into any conditions, please, Master, speak directly. The Master said, "It falls. [The monk] asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body?

The Master said, "The tally-stick at the head of a latrine pit. [The monk] asked, "What are precept, concentration, and wisdom? The Master said, "Broken household utensils. One day, the Master ascended [the Dharma seat].

[The Master] was seated. A monk asked, "What is it like when one has just ascended into the Dharma Hall? The Master struck the meditation seat once. The monk said, "I do not yet understand the meaning of this.

The Master said, "No one has bid more than this price; I strike for three hundred coins. A monk asked, "If a person of great *icchantika* nature should suddenly come, would you still act on his behalf?
The Master said, "After the Dharma has long been established, it becomes corrupt. The monk asked, "Where, then, is compassion? The Master— [replied].
He said: "Old age becomes the demon. Ascending the hall, [he declared: "The lifeblood of the ancestral masters—whether ordinary or sagely; Nāgārjuna and Aśvaghoṣa; heaven and hell;
the boiling cauldrons and glowing coals; the Ox-Headed Hell-Warden; the myriad phenomena of the forest-like universe; the sun, moon, and stars; other lands and this land;
sentient beings and insentient things—all enter this school. With his hand, he drew a line and said: "All enter this school. This is the School Gate."
The Middle Way can kill a person, and it can also bring a person to life. To kill a person, one must have the sword that kills;
to bring a person to life, one must have the phrase that brings to life. What is this sword that kills? What is this phrase that brings to life?
Come forward and speak! Speak before the assembly! If you cannot speak, you will have brought your entire life to naught. Take care. [The monk] asked: "What is the Master’s fourth [teaching]?"
[The monk asked about] the immeasurable mind (*apramāṇacitta*). The Master said, "Setting fire to [a house] and killing people. [The monk] asked, "Wherein lies compassion?
The Master said, "Present it to one who possesses the clear eye. [The monk] asked, "It is not within, not without, and not in between.

In what place does it reside? The Master said, "Six in the Southern Dipper; seven in the Northern Dipper. [The monk] asked, "What is the Dharmakāya Lord, the Vairocana Teacher? The Master said, "Monk."

When the monastic seniority was being arranged according to secular age, [a monk] asked, "Is there anything further above this? The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What is this matter that lies above?
The Master said, "You go yourself to Yuzhou, ten thousand miles away; as you depart, who can you blame for your sorrowful resentment? He ascended the hall.
After a long silence, he said, "As for those wandering monks who practice Chan, you must truly reflect upon it. To study through inquiry, one must possess the capacity for inquiry."

The eye of study: when seeing the ground, one must attain the phrase of seeing the ground; only then will there be a mutual affinity, so that one is no longer deluded by various objects and does not fall into the evil realms.
Ultimately, how can this be fully understood? Sometimes the phrase reaches the ear while the meaning does not reach the mind.

Delusively taking external objects as conditions, one discriminates among reflected phenomena. Sometimes the meaning reaches the mind while the words do not; it is like the blind touching an elephant, each proclaiming a different version.
Sometimes both meaning and words reach the mind, shattering the realm of empty space so that light illuminates the ten directions.
Sometimes neither meaning nor words reach the mind; like a sightless person wandering aimlessly, they suddenly and unconsciously fall into a deep pit.
Question: "What is the path that has been no different from ancient times to the present? The Master said: "Worldly people all wear their heads wrapped.
Question: "What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "The *ācārya* has no scholar’s cap. Question: "When one's own matter is not yet clear, what serves as the proof?

The Master said: "Striking the gong for silence in the midst of a bustling market. Question: "What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "Lighting a golden lamp at midday. Question: "Regarding the 'cloth drum'..."
[The Master] struck the screen with his staff and said, "Who here is a connoisseur? The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "There is a rusted nail in your eye.
The monk asked, "I do not yet understand what you mean by this. The Master said, "Old Qiao competing with the Southern God. The monk requested further instruction on the story of the "Pine Tree.

The Master said, "I do not refuse to explain it to you, but will you believe it? The monk replied, "Since the Master speaks with such gravity, how would I dare not believe? The Master said, "Do you still..."
"Do you hear the sound of water dripping from the eaves? The monk was suddenly enlightened; unconsciously, he let out a cry of "Ye!
The Master asked, "What principle have you seen? The monk then replied with a verse: "The water dripping from the eaves is clear and distinct."
He shattered heaven and earth; in that very moment, his mind was stilled. The Master was delighted and asked the monk, "At sunset you cast yourself into the forest;
where did you depart from this morning? The monk replied, "I am a newly ordained monk who has never studied Chan. The Master said, "You have entered hell in your living body! He then sent him away.
Later, another monk brought this up at the place of Master Zhimen Kuan. Kuan said, "Why did you not say, 'The key is in the hands of the Master'?"
In the inner quarters, the Master went to the infirmary to visit a sick monk. The monk asked, "The Four Elements are fundamentally empty; from where does illness come?
The Master replied, "It comes from the place where you, Venerable, ask. The monk, gasping for breath, asked again, "What is it like when one does not ask?
The Master said, "Let go and lie in the vast sky. The monk said, "Yes," and then passed away.
Chan Master Hongyin of Shending in Tanzhou was the son of the Hu family of Xiangshui. Since he began his travels, he had passed through the vicissitudes of cold and heat clad in but a single robe.
Once, while traveling with several senior monks through the region of Xiangmian, a monk raised a discussion on the lineage of the Dharma (zongcheng), displaying considerable agility of mind.

While a vegetarian meal was being prepared at the Yeban Mountain Inn, the monks were engaged in endless debate. The Master said, "The three realms are mind-only; the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only.
'Consciousness-only' and 'mind-only'—who is it that speaks of eyes and sounds, ears and forms? A monk replied, "That is the teaching of Fayan. The Master asked, "What is its meaning?
The monk said, "Because it is mind-only, the sense organs and their objects do not reach one another. Because it is consciousness-only..."

The sounds and colors were vivid and clear. The Master asked, "Are the tongue and flavors not the sense organ and its object? The monk replied, "They are. The Master then used his chopsticks to place a vegetable in his mouth;
while holding it there, he spoke, "What do you mean by 'mutual entry'? Those sitting there were startled, and the monk was unable to answer.
The Master said, "The joy of the journey does not mean one has finally reached home; to penetrate the subtleties of intellectual understanding is not called 'seeing the Way.
One must practice with true practice; one must awaken with true awakening. King Yama does not fear much talk. The monk bowed and withdrew.
Later, he returned to Changsha and lived in seclusion at Sengsheng Zang on Mount Heng. A wealthy and nobleman from Xiangyin came to visit Foyan, who was [at that time] the Master.
He entered the master’s quarters and saw that his countenance was serene and composed. A single alms bowl hung upon the wall, and he possessed no belongings beyond his daily meal.

The master felt a deep affinity for him and, bowing and kneeling, requested: "This divine hall is the place where my family has planted roots of merit; it has long lacked a patriarchal master. I pray that you, Master, will come with me.

What do you think? The master smiled and consented. He immediately loaded the master onto his own horse and brought him there. It was only after ten years that the monastic community was finally established.
His seat was a single dilapidated wooden bed used as a Dharma throne; his contentment with such austerity was beyond compare.
Furthermore, because both his virtue and seniority were eminent, he was revered by all quarters like the ancient Zhaozhou. A monk asked, "What is it like before one has heard of all dharmas?

The Master said, "The wind whistles; the rain falls. The monk asked, "What is it like after one has heard them? The Master said, "It is good to understand the words. Another asked, "Before the fish-drum has sounded..."
"How is it at that time? The Master said, "Look at the sky; look at the earth. "How is it after the cry? The Master said, "Holding the bowl, he ascends the hall.
"Regarding 'the cold spring of the ancient ravine,' how is it? The Master said, "This is not where a patch-robed monk walks. "What is the place where a patch-robed monk walks?
The Master said, "Not seeing the cold spring of the ancient ravine. "A pair of hands offering a vessel—how is this? The Master said, "It is not something that can be grasped."
“How is it when one enters the hall? The Master said, “What is this? A student asked, “When a scholar reaches a mountain of treasures but returns empty-handed, what then?

The Master said, “The thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month. A student asked, “What is the patriarchal style of the Master’s house? The Master said, “When hungry, one does not choose among the food. A student asked, “What is the Master’s phrase for benefiting others?
The Master said, “Picking up firewood and selecting vegetables. The student said, “Is that all there is to it? The Master said, “Do not merely... [The text here ends abruptly].
"This is also 'not having. The Master said, "You must be even more thorough. [A monk] asked, "When one brushes away dust and sees the Buddha, what then?
The Master said, "The Buddha is also dust. [A monk] asked, "What is the livelihood of a man of the Way? The Master said, "This mountain monk has never entered a schoolhouse since childhood.
An official pointed to a wooden fish and asked, "What is this? The Master said, "It startles many back to their senses."
The man was slightly drowsy. The official said, "Have you not come to this place? The Master said, "Striking the mindless with the mindless.
He asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said, "A head of ash and a face of dust. He asked, "Why is it like this? The Master said:
"How can one not find the mountain monk strange? [The student] asked, "I do not know for certain: is there anything beyond the Dharma-body (dharmakāya) or not? The Master said, "There is.
[The student] asked, "What is this matter that transcends it? The Master said, "The golden crown atop Vairocana’s head. [The student] asked, "Bodhi originally has no tree;
from where could the fruit come? The Master said, "Do you call it 'no attainment'? [The student] asked, "When the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta practiced..."
[The Master] asked, "When did you repair the bridge? The Master said, "Not long ago. [The monk] asked, "What was it like before you had met the former masters?
The Master said, "Walking east, walking west. [The monk] asked, "What is it like after you have met them? The Master said, "Carrying my staff slung across my shoulder.
He ascended the hall and cited Dongshan, who said: "Greed, anger, and ignorance are utterly ignorant; fortunately, this morning I have come to recognize them."
When he walks, he strikes; when he sits, he beats. Entrust this to Prince Xinzai for detailed investigation;

for immeasurable kalpas, one has not been liberated. "I ask you three: do you know or not? The Master said, "The ancients spoke thus, but Shending is not like that. Greed, anger, and ignorance are truly without knowledge;
throughout the twelve hours of the day, let them be as they will. When he walks, go; when he sits, follow. Entrust this."

The Way of Nan-yuan is as steep as a cliff rising ten thousand fathoms; the Way of Linji is dull as a spark from flint or a flash of lightning.
Yang-shan possesses the phrase that settles heaven and earth. Everyone, raise your eyes high! Raise your eyes high! [He] planted his staff and descended from the seat.
As soon as Chan Master Shouzhi of Mount Dayu in Ruizhou ascended the seat, a monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Once a word leaves the mouth, even four horses cannot overtake it. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha within the city? The Master said:
At a stone pillar at the crossroads, [a monk] asked, "What is it like when one does not fall into the 'three inches'? The Master said, "The Qian trigram has three long lines;
the Kun trigram has six short lines. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Above all, avoid filling or emptying the ground.

[Another monk] asked, "Regarding the event of the two masters meeting when the former Buddha divided his seat in half at Vulture Peak in the past—what was that? The Master said, "Do you remember? After the monk had remained silent for a long while, the Master struck him.
As he stepped down from his meditation seat, he said, "I have forgotten this for many years. He then continued, "Stop, stop!

If you seek the principle within words or clarify the function within phrases, it is like losing one's head and recognizing only its reflection. If you were to proclaim the essential teaching of our school, it would be much like a dreamer’s talk.
Nevertheless, though this is so, official channels do not admit even a needle, yet private paths allow for carriages and horses. I shall grant you a single thread of a path."
"There is a point of entanglement. He then struck the meditation seat once and said, "All Buddhas of the three periods of time suffer from headaches.
Now tell me, does anyone among the assembly have a way to avoid this? If even one person could avoid it, such a thing would not exist.
If no one can avoid it, then the Sea-Seal radiates light. The Master then held up his whisk and said, "This is the seal. Which is that?"
"This is light. This here is light. That there is the seal. A mechanism as swift as a flash of lightning—vain is it to stand and ponder.

Do you understand? This old monk is speaking of a dream. But tell me, what did he see in the dream? Ten watches of the "South Branch" (the dream of King Liang). If you do not understand, listen to this verse:
The Northern Dipper hangs from Mount Sumeru; A staff-tip carries the sun and moon. In the forests and springs, let us deliberate: At the end of summer, autumn arrives.

Fengqie. Take care. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The weather is cold and the days are short. The monk asked, "The Dharma of the mind has no form;
how can it be carved and polished? The Master said, "One notch, two notches. The monk asked, "How does one who does not yet understand come to a realization?
The Master said, "Penetrating the seven, penetrating the eight. He ascended the hall and said: "A single strike rings out with crystalline clarity; its resonance thunders through the universe."

As soon as those who know the sound tilt their ears, Xiang Yu has already crossed the river to the east. To understand it in such a way is just like mistaking the bridge on a donkey’s back for one’s father’s chin.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Daguy received the Great Hero’s grandson; the clouds and waters of the Five Lakes rush forward in competition."
They vie with one another in their headlong rush. What gate is there for striking the arrow? How could one know that withered wood endures? Withered wood endures;
in one year it has experienced spring twice. Spring comes twice; within the curtains, pearls are scattered to others. Pearls scattered to others—considering this, they too long for the Western Qin.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Vertically it exhausts the three periods of time; horizontally it pervades the ten directions. When picked up, even Śakra is struck with alarm."
When set down, even the earth spirits tremble with fear. Not grasping, not letting go—what is it called? He himself replied, "A frog. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The Buddhas of the three periods do not know its existence; the cat and the white ox, however, do know it exists. He then picked up his whisk and said:
"The cat and the white ox are both here, emitting light and shaking the earth. Why is this so? (He paused) "Two segments of non-..."

The same. [A monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Sawing apart a weight-stone. Ascending the hall, when the assembly had gathered and settled, he said, "This ready-made case is also a matter of failing to settle the accounts.
He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall again, he said, "Standing in ranks at the bottom of the great ocean, the second hair on the head is already streaked with gray.
Why do you not say that the first hair on the head is streaked with gray? He then descended from his seat.
"Do you understand? Golden stamens and silver filaments form the jade dew; the eminent monk does not sit upon the phoenix terrace. He ascended the hall.

When the assembly had gathered, he said, "To exert one's utmost for the sake of the multitude brings calamity to one’s own private gate. He then descended from his seat. He ascended the hall again. "The path at Cuiyan is perilous and treacherous."
Taking a step, he traverses a thousand streams; yet there is still the water of the great source, surging and flowing to the west of the ridge.

Striking the meditation seat, he descends and addresses the assembly. Holding up an incense box, he says: "If you can say, 'It fits at the bright end,' it fits at the dark end as well; then you may roam freely throughout the world.
If you cannot say it, then close it up. He descends from the seat. A monk asks: "What is the one phrase for benefiting others? The Master says: "Four corners."
Six sheets. [A monk] asked, "What is the essential meaning? The Master said, "Eight concavities and nine convexities. Ascending the hall, he said: "To find no oil in the sand is a pitiable matter;
Cuiyan is chewing his food and feeding it to an infant. When you understand the truth of good and evil at that time, you will realize for the first time that your face was once covered in dust.
He struck the meditation seat and descended from the seat.
A monk asked Chan Master Faying of Shishuang in Tanzhou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The sleeves are short while the arms are long.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The knees are worn through the trousers."
When Chan Master Quanju of Fahua Monastery in Shuzhou went to the place of Master Yuan of Gong’an, Yuan asked, “What is the monastery?
The Master replied, “In deep mountains, solitary tigers hide; in shallow grass, swarms of snakes are exposed. Yuan asked, “Who are the people within the monastery?
The Master replied, “Green pines cannot cover them; how could yellow leaves conceal them? Yuan said, “Tell me more!”
[The monk] said, "Ma! The Master said, "In youth, one plays with the moon at the edge of the sky; in old age, the sun sinks behind the rising forest.

[The monk] asked, "Regarding 'one phrase, two phrases,' when the clouds part, the moon and dew appear—what is that? The Master said, "It illuminates Buddhas and patriarchs. He then went to the place of Master Zhi of Dayu.
Zhi asked, "When the ancients saw peach blossoms, what was their meaning? The Master said, "A curve does not conceal a straight line. Zhi said, "..."
"Let us set that aside for a moment. As for this one, how is it? The Master said, "One picks up gold on the main street;

if one is not a poet, one does not offer a poem. [The monk] said, "A master poet! The Master said, "A single red thread is pulled by two people. [The monk] said, "Xuansha..."
"Way! It is true, most truly true. I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the end. "How so? the Master said. "The sea may dry up, yet its bottom will eventually be seen;

the peaks and ridges are layered with emerald green. He arrived at the place of Master Jue of Langye. Langye asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master said, "From the two [realms]."
Zhe asked, "Did you come by boat or by land? The Master said, "By boat. Zhe asked, "Where is the boat? The Master said, "Underfoot.
Zhe asked, "How do you express that which does not involve the journey? The Master struck him once with his sitting cloth and said, "Fabricated elders are as numerous as hemp and millet.

The Master then gave a shout and asked again, "Elder, when did you arrive at Fenyang? Xie said, "I arrived at such-and-such a time. The Master said, "I was..."

The Master raised a verse, saying: "Upon the western peak above the summit, Who dares to face such a formidable faculty?

Transcending both the mundane and the sacred, A double radiance flashes forth. The Master asked, "What is this 'double radiance'? The Abbot replied, "The moon rises in the east; the sun sets in the west.
The Master asked, "Before you met Mingzhao, what was it like? The Abbot replied, "A full cup of oil is difficult to exhaust."

The Master said, "What is it like after you have seen? The host replied, "A mind with many thoughts is easily dried up. Later, a monk asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'?
The Master said, "White chrysanthemums just now blooming under the warmth of the double sun; a young gentleman of a hundred years has not yet encountered spring.
The monk asked, "What is 'taking away the environment but not taking away the person'? The Master said, "Throughout the great earth there is no news; one remains solitary and carefree."

Ren-zhen asked, "What is meant by 'both the person and the realm being simultaneously negated'? The Master said, "The weeds overgrow and the man’s complexion changes; both ordinary and sage are equally empty.
Ren-zhen asked, "What is meant by 'neither the person nor the realm being negated'? The Master said, "The clear breeze and the bright moon;

[The monk] presents a flower. The Master says, "When the forest is sparse, the birds do not pass through. [The monk] asks, "The seven stars shine with radiance as dawn approaches;
without violating the Imperial Wind, try to speak of it. The Master says, "The general’s horse hooves are red. [The monk] says, "Wrong. The Master then strikes him.
The monk bows, spreads his sitting cloth, and begins to fold it. The Master says, "One spreading, one folding—every dharma is complete. If you wish to ask further, what will you do?"
The Master then asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master struck him.
Chan Master Gudai Guquan of Bajiao Hermitage on Mount Nanyue was a native of Quanzhou. He received the Dharma from Fenyang and roamed freely through Lake Xiang.
Later, he went to visit his fellow practitioner, Chan Master Ciming. Ciming asked, "White clouds hang across the valley mouth; where does the man of the Way go?"
"Where have you come from? the Master asked, looking to his left and right. Baoming said, "Last night, where was there a fire that burned out the ancient tombs?

The Master said, "Not yet; speak further. Baoming made the sound of a tiger. The Master struck him with his sitting cloth (*zuoju*), caught hold of it, and pushed Baoming onto the meditation seat (*chánchuáng*).
Baoming then made the sound of a tiger again. The Master laughed loudly and said, "I have seen more than seventy virtuous..."
Zhisheng: "Today I have finally met a true master. The Master leaned back as Layman Yu arrived to pay his respects (Yu later resided at Fachang).

He asked, "Is the Hermitage Master here? The Master said, "Who is it? He replied, "A traveling monk. The Master asked, "What are you doing here? He said, "I am coming to pay my respects to the Hermitage Master.

The Master said, "It happens that the Hermitage Master is not here. He asked, "And what about you? The Master said, "I told you he was not here; why do you ask? He said, "What then? The Master said, "I told you he was not here; why speak further?"
"Ma ni-wo! [The Master] seized his staff and chased him out. When he came again the next day, the Master chased him out once more.
On another day, he came again and asked, "Is the hermitage master here? The Master said, "Who is it? He replied, "A wandering monk. Upon pulling back the curtain, he entered;
the Master grabbed him by the chest and held him fast, saying, "Tigers and wolves roam here! You bed-wetting little devil has come to seek me three or two times already!"

"What is it? he asked. The Master replied, "People say that the Hermitage Master personally met Fenyang. The Master stripped off his robe and shook it out, saying, "Tell me, what extraordinary thing did you see in my meeting with Fenyang?
He asked, "Who is the master of this hermitage? The Master said, "You must discern him as soon as you enter.
He asked, "Is it not simply this very thing? The Master said, "How many people have been deceived! He asked, "What about your previous words?"
[The monk] asked, "Where is it? The Master said, "Hearing things not clearly, you call a bell a water jar. [The monk] said, "When the myriad dharmas are extinguished, the whole body is manifest;
where the ruler and minister meet, the right departs from the center. The Master said, "You blockhead! If you do not understand, then stop. Why do you talk such nonsense?

[The monk] asked, "I wonder, when a guest arrives, with what will you receive them? The Master said, "Yunmen’s rice cake; Zhaozhou’s tea. [The monk] said: *Note: This dialogue is from the *Wumenguan* (Gateless Barrier), Case 21.*

"If it is so, then I shall depart to thank the Master for his offerings. The Master rebuked him, saying, "In my place, the very seeds of fire have not yet appeared, and you already speak of thanking me for offerings.
Because of the heavy snow, the Master composed a verse, saying: "Today’s snow is most excellent, Falling thickly like the moon in autumn.
Mañjuśrī does not show his head; Samantabhadra displays his ugliness and clumsiness. When Ciming moved to reside at Fuyan, the Master [again]...
He went to visit him, stayed for a short while, and then returned. He composed a verse to send him, saying: "It has been half a year since we parted;
I know not with whom you have been discussing Chan. Amidst the same exquisite scenery within Mount Xiang, you yourself guide your followers while I sleep."
Ming-lan merely smiled.
Chan Master Xiao-yu of Longhua Monastery in Huangmei, Qizhou, went to the place of Wuzu Heshang Jie.

The Master asked, "How do you express that single phrase which does not fall within the range of lips and tongue? The Master replied, "Even for one as old and venerable as you, this is still just a 'talking head' (a mere conceptual crutch)."
[The Master] did not attend to him. The Patriarch then shouted; the Master also shouted. The Patriarch raised his staff; the Master clapped his hands and went out.
The Patriarch called out, "Dharma-heir! Stay a moment—the matter remains. The Master placed his sitting cloth over his shoulder and, without looking back, ascended the hall.
Kāśyapa Mātanga’s entry into Han territory already involved excessive elaboration; Bodhidharma’s coming from the West failed to maintain his own proper measure.
When I, this mountain monk, speak thus today, it is likewise to increase delusion through involvement in idle affairs for their sake.
When Chan Master Tiansheng Haotai of Anjī Prefecture arrived at Langye, Langye asked him, "Amassing troops and engaging in battle is not yet the mark of a master;
with a single horse and a lone spear, I request that you meet me. The Master pointed at Langye and said, "If the general does not lead with courage, he brings ruin upon his three armies.
Langye struck the Master once with his sitting cloth (*zuoju*), and the Master likewise struck Langye once with his sitting cloth. Langye caught hold of it and said, "Just now..."
When [Xuedou] came, he spread out his sitting mat; this was the mountain monk’s command for practice. "Where does the Venerable One's sitting mat fall?
The Master said, "I humbly pray that you will partake. Xuedou spread out his mat and opened it wide, saying, "At the fifth watch, rising even earlier, there are still those traveling at night.
The Master said, "Drawing the bow after the thief has fled. Xuedou said, "Sit and drink tea. Later, when he resided [at a monastery], a monk asked, "What is the Buddha?"
The Master said, "A black-lacquered holy monk. [The monk] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Look at the wall; it is the color of earth.
Chan Master Longtan Zhiyuan of Tangzhou took his leave of Fenyang. Fenyang said, "There is no other road for seeing you off; I give you this one [verse]."
[The Master] held a staff and a hand-towel. The Master said, "The hand-towel you may use, but you do not need this staff.
Yang said, "Just take it with you; there will be a time for its use. The Master then put it away. Yang said, "And yet you say it is not needed."

The Master then gave a shout. Yang said, "In the future, you will not yield to Linji. The Master said, "The true command has already been issued. On the following day, as Yang was being escorted out through the three gates, the Master asked him, "When you encounter Weichi at Mount Jie, what will you do? Yang said, "One stroke, two pieces. Yang asked, "If he manifests as Nezha, what then? Yang then shouted, "This! and the Master pulled his staff toward him. Yang shouted again, "This! and the Master struck him. Yang said, "Master, this is too much! The Master said, "You have just received the seal of approval; why do you speak of 'too much'? Yang bowed. The Master said, "From now on, you must not let anyone surpass you. Yang then departed. Later, when Yang returned to the capital, he told people that the Chan Master of Mount Huangbo was truly a man of great capacity. He also said, "When I first met him, I thought he was just a fellow from the marketplace; I never imagined he would be so extraordinary. Yang later went to see Mazu, who asked him, "Where have you come from? Yang said, "From Mount Huangbo. Mazu asked, "What kind of Dharma does Huangbo teach? Yang said, "He says that if you raise your hand, he strikes you; if you open your mouth, he strikes you. Mazu laughed and said, "That fellow is indeed a man of great capacity. Yang then bowed. The Master said, "Once returned to the green peaks, he does not emerge from the white clouds. [The monk] asked, "What is one who returns?
The Master said, "Since wandering the purple thoroughfares, who would be willing to hide in the green mountains? [The monk] asked, "What is 'seizing the person'?"
"Not robbing the object. The Master said: "At home there is no longer news of a return; by the roadside stands empty the signpost for longing for one's hometown.

the green mountains are ground down until they become dust. [The student] asked: "What is 'robbing both person and object'? The Master said: "Heaven and earth are already empty; the state of Qin..."

Chan Master Ciren Shouzhen of Chuzhou was asked by a monk: "I know that you have already attained the essential meaning within Chan;

Sweeping with the mountain boy, pine needles fill the paths as we please. Entering the hall: It is clearly so—there is no awakening; where there is a dharma, there is delusion.
When the sun rises without clouds, it shines radiantly across the heavens; when the eyes are free of cataracts, space is fundamentally without flowers.
Do not speak erroneously before those who lack wisdom. *Chan.*
Chan Master Xianqin of Yunmen in Yuezhou ascended the hall. After a long silence, he said, "What an excellent koan!
If you go to other places, do not misrepresent it. He then descended from his seat.

"When the sun rises, sit in the shade; when it is cold, do not raise your head. Later, as the Master entered the room, Guyin asked:

[The Master] used [the whisk]. When [the monk] did not understand, [the Master] said, "This is merely the circulation of conventional truth (*saṃvṛti-satya*). [The monk] said, "Not yet; speak further. The Master shook his sleeves and departed.

The Layman Li Zunxū, Prince of Huaiyin, visited Gūyǐn and asked about the matter of leaving the household life.
Gūyǐn answered him with the public case concerning the Duke of Cui and Zhao asking Jìngshān. Upon hearing these words, the Duke attained great enlightenment and composed a verse, saying:
"To study the Way, one must be an iron man; When the hand touches the heart, judgment is immediate. Directly proceeding toward unsurpassed Bodhi, All matters of right and wrong are left behind."

One day, Guǎn Gōng saw off the Venerable Jiān. Gōng asked, "Having recently departed from Shàngdǎng and arrived at Zhōngdū, we have just engaged in this refined conversation when you suddenly turn your tiger-staff back toward the verdant peaks of Yúnpíng to visit the clear streams of Xuělǐng."
The Master asked, "I do not understand: what is the matter with this place and that place? The Seat-holder said, "A sharp sword sweeps through, and heaven and earth are stilled;
a frosty blade is just raised, and the Ox and Cow constellations grow cold. The Master said, "It happens that today my ears are deaf. The Seat-holder said, "One arrow brings down two vultures.
The Master said, "Why, Seat-holder, are you sleeping in straw sandals? The Seat-holder gave a single sweep with his sleeve.
The Duke lowered his head and said, "Today may truly be called a moment of subjugation. The Master said, "Puhua has come out of the Sangha Hall.

When the Duke was at the point of death and his stomach and chest were burning with fever, the nun Daojian said to him, "When sentient beings see the end of the kalpa and are scorched by the great fire, you, Excellency, must carefully look after the Host. The Duke said, "Master, please brew me a dose of medicine."
The physician arrived. Jian remained silent. The official said, "This nun does not even know how to decoct medicine.
After the official finished his exchange with Ciming, he passed away peacefully. This account is found in the *Biography of Ciming*.
The Duke of Ying, Xia Song, a lay practitioner whose courtesy name was Ziqiao, had long since attained awakening at Guyin and spent his days in the company of aged monks.
Once, when Chan Master Lanpu of Shanglan arrived, the Duke asked, "When the hundred members of the body disintegrate, which one is the Elder’s own self?
Lan replied, "I left Qiyang on the twentieth day of last month. The Duke ceased questioning. Lan, however, asked in turn, "When the hundred members of the body disintegrate..."
At the time of dispersal, [Master] Lan asked, "Which one is yours, sir? The Master then shouted. Lan said, "The shout is certainly not lacking, but after all, which one is yours, sir?
The Master replied with a verse: "Do not mistake the foremost pivot before the wind;
Where in the vast void can thought be placed? If this mountain monk wishes to convey the message, Ten thousand miles of cloudless sky and the moon."
At that time, Lan said, "This too is merely playing with one's spirit.
Chan Master Guanghui Lian was the successor of Chan Master Daolung of Huayan in Dongjing. When he first visited Master Shimen Che, he asked: "The ancients said..."
"One need only find peace and ease wherever one is, and naturally one will follow the ancient tracks. Although these words exist, what is it like when the mind of doubt has not yet ceased?
The Master said: "Only by knowing that there is [the Way] can one find peace and ease wherever one is.

It is like a person living in a prefecture or county who, upon hearing or seeing all manner of strange and wondrous things, treats them all as ordinary. To find peace and ease without knowing that there is [the Way] is like..."
The Master lived in a village; whenever there was even a slight sound or sight, he would be startled and speak of it as strange.
Upon hearing these words, [his teacher] attained realization. The teacher then bestowed upon him the entire essence of the Dongshan school.

Later, he became a successor of Guanghui. One day, Master Fuyan asked him, "Chan Master, you personally met Shimen; why then did you become a successor of Guanghui? The Master replied, "I saw Guanghui."
He wished to shave his hair and told me to bring a stool. Huì said, "Dharma Master, I have a poem about the stool;
please listen. He then said: "Set it down and you will find stability. At that moment, I immediately accepted this. I then recounted what I had attained while at Shimen.
Guanghuì said, "What Shimen showed you is like a hundred flavors of exquisite delicacies—it simply cannot satisfy one's hunger. The Master [laughed].
In the early years of the Zhihe era, he traveled to the capital and stayed at Jingde Temple. Every day he would wander through the city markets, returning home regularly at the second watch.
One night, unable to enter, he lay down beneath the gate. Emperor Renzong dreamed that he arrived at the temple gate and saw a dragon coiled upon the ground;

startled awake, he dispatched a palace attendant in the middle of the night to investigate. Seeing the Master fast asleep with a loud snoring, the attendant shook him, causing him to startle awake. The attendant then questioned him.

His name was Guizou. When the Emperor heard that his Way was flourishing, he said with joy, "This is an auspicious omen. The following day, he summoned him to the private audience hall and inquired about the essential tenets of his school.
The Master’s responses were detailed and appropriate, and the Emperor was greatly pleased. Thereafter, they exchanged verses and couplets, which circulated incessantly along the roads.

On occasion, the Master would enter the palace for an audience and stay overnight within the imperial precincts; the honors accorded to him were exceptionally generous. He was bestowed the title Chan Master Mingwu (Illuminated Enlightenment) by Imperial Decree.
During the Huangyou era, Emperor Renzong summoned Chan Master Da’jue Liaan to expound the Dharma in the Huacheng Hall. He also summoned the Master (Zhaoqing En) for an exchange of questions;

his spiritual sharpness was swift and incisive, leaving the Emperor greatly pleased. The imperial guards all raised their voices in acclamation. The Master immediately submitted a memorial recommending Liaan to take his place.
He waited for inquiries in the Forbidden Forest and discussed Chan in the Secret Hall. He requested to return to Mount Lu, but the Emperor, upon reading his memorial, did not grant permission.

An imperial decree was issued to build a vihāra outside the Cao Gate to invite the Master; it was granted the name Huayan Chan Temple. When he opened the hall for teaching, a monk asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "High and low. The monk asked, "What is one who walks the Way? The Master said, "Lean legs in the grass."
His feet were broad. When the Master was over eighty years old, he passed away during the height of summer. He sat upright for seven days; his hands and feet remained supple and soft.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa to the east of the temple.
A monk asked Chan Master Huinan of Huili at Linjiang Army: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed? The Master said:
"The iron ox does not eat the grass by the fence; it climbs straight up to sleep on the summit of Mount Sumeru. The monk said:
"If that is so, then in the past you personally received the essential meaning at Ruyang, and today at Linjiang you spread it forth greatly. The Master said: "After you have prostrated."
[The monk] withdrew. He asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Large head, small tail. The monk said, "I do not yet understand this profound word;

I beg the Master to point it out again. The Master said, "Eyebrows three feet two inches long. The monk said, "If that is so, then everyone will carry him upon their heads, and all who see him will knit their brows.
The Master let out a long sigh. The monk clapped his hands once and then prostrated. The Master said, "Feel free to leap about as you please."
A monk asked Chan Master Guanghui Dexuan of Ruizhou: "The patriarchs have transmitted one to another, passing down the seal of the patriarchs.
Under whom did you, Master, now receive the Dharma as a successor? The Master said: "When the younger brother blows the *xun* flute, the elder brother blows the *chi* flute.
The monk said: "If that is so, then you are the son of Guanghui and the direct grandson of Shoushan. The Master said: "You are sitting inside a stack of rafters; I will not strike you, lay brother."
The Layman Yang Yi, Duke Wen, whose courtesy name was Da-nian, was designated as a "divine infant" when young.

Upon reaching maturity, he bore a reputation for talent and fame, yet he was unaware of the existence of the Buddha. One day, while visiting a colleague, he saw him reading the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
Laughing, he censured him, saying, "How can this possibly surpass Confucius and Mencus? Why such extreme devotion? Thereupon, he read several fascicles himself.
He was bewildered and had only begun to develop a slight degree of respect and faith. Later, he met with Lord Li Wei of the Hanlin Academy, who urged him to seek out a teacher for inquiry.

When the Lord subsequently rose from his post as Director of the Imperial Library to serve as the Prefect of Ruzhou, he went first to visit Guanghui. Upon being received by Guanghui, the Lord immediately asked:

"A cloth drum is struck at the front of the hall; who is the one who knows the music? Guanghui replied, "The wind that comes is clearly discerned. The Lord said, "If that is so, then the Chan guest..."
When they met, Zhituan merely snapped his fingers. Huì said, "A gentleman may enter. Gong responded with two "yeses.
Huì said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated. During their conversation that night, Huì asked, "Director Mi, with whom have you ever had a dialogue?
Gong replied, "I once asked the Venerable Administrator Liang of Yunyan: 'What is it like when two tigers bite each other? Liang said, 'A unified whole. Gong continued, "I..."
The official said, "I simply watch over it. I do not know if speaking in such a manner is permissible. Huì said, "It is not so here.
The official said, "Please, Master, offer another turn of phrase. Huì made a gesture with his hand as if pulling a nose and said, "This beast is still leaping about!
At these words, the official was suddenly liberated from doubt. He composed a verse which says: An octagonal millstone is empty.
Running inside, a golden-haired lion transforms into a dog. If you wish to hide your body within the Big Dipper, you must join your palms behind the Southern Dipper.

Furthermore, he set forth his lineage and secret realization, addressing it to Li, the Hanlin Academician: "I, the sick man, have long been dull-witted and obtuse, yet I have received your kind favor and patronage.

I have heard in advance the essential teachings of the Southern School and have long accompanied you on your travels through the capital. In both my stillness and movement, I have sought your counsel."

I have consulted with you on these matters, revolving them in my thoughts and stimulating my resolve, so that my heart may reach its ultimate destination and I may stand before the wall without shame.
Truly, this has come about through your guidance during our time together. How much more so since the Great Master, the Honored An, constantly bestowed his instruction upon me;

yet since he vanished from the twin śāla trees and returned to the West in his single sandal, my inner mind has been vast and desolate, knowing no place of rest. Furthermore, for years I have suffered from chronic illness, and my spirit and thoughts—

In my confusion and bewilderment, I was nearly at a loss for a moment. Once again, I sought to determine the directions, and further encountered the Great Being Master Liang of Yunmen visiting me amidst the weeds and brambles.
Master Liang’s essential teachings were precisely on the same track as those of Master An;

both had come from Mount Lu—Yunjü and Guizong—and were all descendants of the lineage of Fayen. Last year, while serving as the acting governor of this prefecture, I happened to meet Chan Master Guanghui.
Baizhang succeeded Mazu; Mazu succeeded Baizhang; Huangbo succeeded Baizhang; Linji succeeded Huangbo; Xinghua succeeded Linji; Nan’uan succeeded Xinghua; the former Nan’uan succeeded Fengxue;

Fengxue succeeded Nan’uan; Nan’uan succeeded Nanyuan; Nanyuan succeeded Fengxue; Fengxue succeeded the former Nan’uan; Nan’uan succeeded Xinghua; Xinghua succeeded Linji; Linji succeeded Huangbo; Huangbo succeeded Baizhang; Baizhang succeeded Mazu.
The Patriarch [Huineng] received the Dharma from Master Ruang; Ruang was the direct, legitimate successor of Caoxi. In the midst of his vegetarian fasts, his duties were few.

During the leisure of his post-meal rest, he would sometimes sit and wait for [the Patriarch] to arrive, or at other times command his carriage to follow him. His requests for instruction were manifold, and his lingering obscurities were instantly dispelled.
After half a year, he was clear and free of doubt, as if forgetting something only to suddenly remember it, or as if waking from a dream. The blockage that had long constrained his chest...
Things fell away with a sudden crash. Matters that had remained obscure for accumulated kalpas were suddenly revealed in their vast clarity;
thus, there was a thorough and decisive discernment, and no further obstruction in responding to circumstances. Reflecting deeply, I note that former masters mostly engaged in extensive seeking:
Xuefeng ascended Mount Dongshan nine times and went to Touzi three times before finally succeeding to Deshan; Linji received the Dharma from Dayu and ultimately inherited [the lineage].
Huangbo and Yunyan both received much instruction and guidance from Daowu, yet they became the sons of Yaoshan.
Danxia personally received the seal of approval from Mazu, yet he ultimately became a descendant of Shitou. Such cases were many in antiquity; there is no contradiction in principle.
As for this infirm man, the karmic conditions for his succession truly belong to Guanghui, while the inspiration and stimulation [for this work] originate from Liang at Ao.

Feng: "How fortunate, how fortunate! Your Reverence asked Guanghui: 'I have heard your teaching that all sinful karma arises from wealth and treasures, and you urge people to distance themselves from profit and gain.
Yet, in the Southern Jambudvīpa, sentient beings take wealth as their very life; states and nations gather people through wealth.
Since the Teachings speak of two kinds of giving—material and Dharma—how can you urge people [to abandon material wealth]? "
Shucai asked, "What about the iron dragon-head atop the banner pole? Huì said, "The horse from Haitan is as large as a donkey.
Shucai said, "A chicken from Chu is not a phoenix from Mount Dan. Huì said, "Two thousand years since the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, and yet the bhikṣus lack a sense of shame.
Shucai set forth one hundred questions and requested that Guǎng Huì answer them. Huì answered each one in turn. Shucai then questioned Lĩ Dū.
The Commandant said, "What was accomplished by Śākyamuni through six years of ascetic practice? The Commandant said, "One knows the weight of firewood only when the carrying pole breaks.
Because of a slight ailment, the Official asked Master Huán, "I have suddenly fallen ill today.

Out of compassion, Master, how should I be treated? Huán said, "A bowl of cassia (dīngxiāng) decoction. The Official immediately made a gesture of vomiting. Huán said, "Affection and love are formed [of this]."
Fannian was boiling medicine. Yuanhuan called out, "Thief! He dropped the medicine before the official and stood to one side with his hands folded.
The official stared at him with wide eyes and said, "You little forest-dweller. Yuanhuan shook his sleeves and walked out.
On another day, the official asked, "My four great generals wish to disperse; how will you save me, Great Master? Yuanhuan then struck his chest three times.
The Official said, "I am fortunate to have encountered a master. Huán said, "How many years have you studied the Buddha-dharma? The vulgar air has not yet been removed.
The Official said, "Calamities do not come alone. Huán made a sound of sighing. The Official wrote a verse to leave with Li Dūwèi, saying:

"The arising of bubbles and the extinguishing of bubbles—these two dharmas are fundamentally equal. If you wish to know the place of true return, look to the east or west of Zhaozhou’s courtyard. When the Commandant saw it, [he was enlightened].
He then said, "I am selling spirit-money at the Temple of Mount Tai. The magistrate arrived immediately, but the Master had already passed away.
He was the dharma successor of National Teacher Shishuang Chuyuan, the eleventh generation descendant of the Southern Peak.
Chan Master Cuiyan Zhenke of Hongzhou was a native of Fuzhou. He once studied under Ciming and subsequently went to Jinluan, where he sat in summer retreat together with Attendant Shan.
Shan was a high-ranking disciple of Ciming; even Daowu Zhen and Yangqi Hui both held him in the highest esteem.
The Master prided himself on having personally seen Ciming and believed there was no one in the world who could satisfy his mind. When Shan spoke with him, he realized...
Shanshan had not yet attained thorough penetration; [Zhao] laughed at him. One day, while walking in the mountains, they engaged in a sharp exchange of debate.
Zhao picked up a piece of tile or pebble, placed it upon a flat rock, and said, "If you can utter a turning word regarding this, I will grant that you have personally seen Ciming.

The Master looked left and right, intending to respond. Zhao rebuked him, saying, "Your mind is stalled in deliberation; your intellectual consciousness has not yet penetrated. When have you ever even dreamed of it?"
The Master felt ashamed and terrified; he immediately returned to Shishuang. When Ciming saw him coming, he scolded him, saying, "A true practitioner on pilgrimage must know the proper timing.
What urgent business has brought you here so early, before the summer retreat is over? The Master wept and said, "My elder brother Shan harbors a poisonous heart that ultimately obstructs me;
therefore, I have come to see you, O Venerable One. Ciming suddenly asked, "What is the Great Matter of the Buddha-dharma?"

Yanyi said, "Cloudless sky arises over the peaks; the moon exists within the heart of the waves. Ming scowled and shouted, "With hair as white as snow and teeth falling out, you still harbor such a view!
How can you ever escape birth and death? Yanyi was struck with awe and begged for instruction.
Ming said, "You asked me; Master, please ask me the same question as before. Ming shouted with a thunderous voice, "No clouds arise upon the mountain peaks;

the moon descends into the heart of the waves. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. A clear and vigorous spirit issued forth from him, and his wit and eloquence became swift and sharp.
The monastic communities were wary of him. While he was residing at Cuoyan, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "In the same pit, there is no different soil.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Deep plowing and shallow sowing.
A monk asked, "What is the place where a student turns themselves around? The Master said, "One wall, a hundred walls in harmony. [The monk] asked, "What is the student’s point of application?"
"Regarding the place of power," the Master said, "A thousand days of gathering firewood are burned in a single day. [The student] asked, "What is the point of intimacy for a student?
The Master said, "The whole family is sent off on a boat at the river crossing. [The student] asked for a phrase to benefit people; the Master said:
"A three-legged frog flies up into the sky. [The Master] said: "Deep within the snow of the village ahead, last night a single branch blossomed.
The Master said: "When hungry, one encounters a king’s feast but cannot eat. [Someone] asked: "What is the Way? The Master said: "As soon as you step out the door, you see it.

[Someone] asked: "What is one who is on the Way? The Master said: "Carrying the cangue and passing through the legal proceedings. He ascended the hall and said: "The former sages said: 'This matter is like [a spark] exploding...'"
The patterns on a tortoise shell form omens as soon as it is heated; if it does not crack, it remains dull. Whether it cracks or does not crack, one must immediately grasp the point directly.
Shanglan was not like this: he had no fixedness and no necessity. It was like riding a horse through empty space or rowing a boat on dry land;

clouds rose from the South Mountain and rain fell upon the North Mountain. He then took up his staff and said: "Let this staff transform into the Celestial Great General and patrol the four directions."
Throughout the world, there are those who maintain their integrity and those who do not; there are those with disciplined conduct and those without.
At once, he reported this to Śakra, the Lord of Devas, and then let out a shout, saying: "A man of spirit possesses a will that pierces the heavens; do not walk where the Tathāgata has walked."
He struck the meditation desk once and ascended the hall. He raised the verse by Longya, saying: "Studying the Way is like drilling for fire;

when smoke appears, one must not yet stop. Only when the golden star manifests does one finally reach home. Shending said: "Studying the Way is like drilling for fire; when smoke appears, one should stop immediately.
Do not wait for the golden star to manifest, lest you burn your feet and then your head. The Master said: "If we speak in terms of the sudden [teaching], Long..."
Ya was on the way midway. If we discuss gradualism, even Shending still lacked some awakening.

Regarding this, how would you say it? Gentlemen, this year there are many fallen leaves; at how many places will they be swept back home? [He] ascended the hall: "Facing the enemy on the battlefield."
"Not fearing birth and death—this is the courage of a general. Entering the mountains without fear of tigers or rhinoceroses—this is the courage of a hunter.
Entering the water without fear of crocodiles or dragons—this is the courage of a fisherman. What, then, is the courage of a patch-robed monk?
He took up his staff and said, "This is the staff. Pick it up, hold it, and move it; with this, thirty thousand [miles]..."
The great trichiliocosm shook all at once. If it cannot be picked up, cannot be grasped, and cannot be moved—Wen-shu is Wen-shu, and liberation is liberation.
*Pause.* [He] ascended the hall and raised an example: A monk asked Ba-ling, "What is the Way?"
Ling said, "An eye-opening person falls into a well. He then asked Baoying, "What is the Way? Ying replied, "In front of the Five-Phoenix Pavilion.
He also asked Shoushan, "What is the Way? Shan replied, "Three feet deep beneath one's feet. These are the three turning words.
One phrase stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high; one phrase is a boat traveling on dry land; one phrase is the mutual interpenetration of guest and host.
Is there anyone among you who can discern these? Come forward and speak! If there is none, then for now practice the compassion of an Arhat, for it destroys the thieves of the fetters;
practice the compassion of a Bodhisattva, for it brings peace to sentient beings; practice the compassion of a Tathāgata, for it realizes the mark of suchness. Question: How is this so?

“This is the great purport of the Buddha-dharma. The Master said, “The worthies and sages of the five supernatural powers. The student said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “My tongue reaches up to the Brahma Heaven.
When the Master was about to enter nirvana, he manifested illness that was extremely arduous; he spread straw mats upon the ground and turned over and over without resting for even a moment.

Attendant Zhe wept and said, "Throughout your life you reviled the Buddhas and scolded the Patriarchs; why now have you come to this? The Master gazed at him intently and rebuked him, saying, "Do you also hold such a view?
He then rose, sat in the full lotus posture, and called for the attendant. When the incense smoke began to rise, he passed away.
He then entered nirvana.
Chan Master Zanyuan Juehai of Jiangshan was a native of Yiwu, Wuzhou. His surname was Fu, and he was a descendant of the Great Being (Avalokiteśvara).

Having cultivated the wisdom of the seeds from a long time past, he manifested birth in accordance with his vows. His parents were moved by auspicious signs, and the village praised him as extraordinary. At the age of three...
He left home to become a monk. At the age of seven, he joined the Sangha; at fifteen, he began his travels, eventually journeying far to visit Shishuang.

Upon entering the Master’s chamber, Ciming saw him and said, "Work well in the stable. The Master then brayed like a donkey. Ciming remarked, "Truly a vessel of the Dharma," and appointed him as his attendant.
For twenty years, he personally undertook all tasks—carrying water and hauling firewood—never shirking from cold or heat. He sought [the Way] with total dedication.
Later, he appeared in the world at Sutaianfeng Longhua Baiyun. The provincial governor invited him to reside at Master Zhi’s site of practice (*dōjō*).
He upheld the essential tenets of the school; his spiritual acuity was swift and sharp, and his realization corresponded with his practice, earning him the respect and admiration of all quarters.

Prime Minister Wang Anshi, deeply honoring his virtue and reputation, specifically submitted a memorial to grant him ceremonial robes and a posthumous title. The Master, however, firmly declined the position of the highest seat of government and instead constructed a hermitage.
In the mountains of Dinglin, he lived in carefree seclusion with the Master, engaging in pure conversation beneath the trees all day long.

He presented the Master with this verse: "Not opposing things, the True Way is vast; Seeking the arising of conditions, one's own meditation deepens. The faculty of the tongue is already purified—who could destroy it?
Footprints are like space—how can I find them? This, too, was a rare occurrence in the world. A monk asked: "What is harmony?"
[The monk] continued the family tradition. The Master said, "The eastern wall strikes the western wall. [The monk] asked, "How do you attend to a guest?
The Master said, "Firewood from the mountain; water from the well. He asked, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? The Master said, "The womb of a donkey or the belly of a horse."
A questioner asked, "Regarding Luzu’s facing the wall—what was his intention? The Master said, "The duties of the abbot are many. Another asked, "What is a great *kalyāṇamitra* (virtuous friend)?
The Master said, "Slaughtering oxen and flaying sheep. The questioner asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "The karma lies within.
He ascended the hall for formal instruction and said: "If this is it, it is like a tiger wearing horns. If this is not it, what would you call it?"
After a long silence, he said, "Feed the donkeys; feed the horses. Take care. In the first year of the Yuanyou era, the Master passed away.

Prime Minister Wang wailed in grief at his stupa and offered this eulogy for the Master’s portrait: "A worthy man indeed! His conduct was rigorous yet his countenance was serene. He understood speech yet was able to remain silent.
He did not rejoice in praise or honor; he did not grieve over disgrace or defamation. He was neither boastful nor self-aggrandizing, yet people naturally ascribed virtue to him."
The black has white within it; they come from the north and south. Neither following nor opposing, neither resisting nor suppressing—do not look at your flowers;
eat only your own fruit. Who shall succeed to this? I have left behind these rules.
A monk asked Chan Master Zheng of Wushan Mountain in Ruizhou, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, “Cloth makes a person;
water makes a field. He ascended the hall and said: “At the seat of Huangmei, there were a thousand followers of the sea.
To entrust the Dharma and transmit the robe to a laborer at the mill—this would be like the red sun rising in the west; this would not be like the moon’s orb ascending in the east. Examine this!”
Chan Master Shenghui of Shuangfeng Temple on Mount Nanyue ascended the hall and said: "A man from Nanfan sails his boat;
a man from the north of Sai waves the oars. A Persian enters the Great Tang; Mount Sumeru performs a dance. What kind of talk is this?

On the seventeenth day of the ninth month in the sixth year of the Yuanfeng era, the Master shaved his head, bathed, and took leave of the assembly, reciting this verse: "Ninety-two years of time have passed."
He spoke clearly to the assembly: "The distant void disperses the cold clouds; the secluded window passes the waning moon. Having finished speaking, he sat and passed away.
When cremated, his teeth and crown protrusion remained unharmed, and above them there was a wondrous light of five colors.
A monk asked Chan Master Daoning Daokuan of Hongzhou, "When Kāśyapa had the correct view, why did he see the flower being held up and yet smile?
The Master said, "Unable to restrain his brilliance. The monk asked, "When Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, why did the temple steward’s eyebrows and beard fall off?
The Master said, "Thieves do not strike the homes of the poor. The monk asked, "Since it is the one true Dharma-realm, why..."
"What is it that gives rise to these thousand differences and myriad distinctions? The Master said, "The roots are deep and the leaves are lush.
The monk drew a circle and asked, "Can one even transcend this? The Master said, "Seeking cleverness leads to clumsiness. Question: "What is 'three before three and three after three'?
The Master said, "Counting to nine, one does not reach nine. Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "A dot."
"Tea must be with water boiled a hundred times. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Drink it all up; leave no dregs behind.
A monk visited the Master’s quarters and asked, "What is the white ox on open ground? The Master stuck a fire-tongs into the brazier and asked, "Do you understand?
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The head is not lacking; the tail is not missing. While the Master was at Tong’an, at that time—
A monk asked, "Since you are Tong'an, why is it that there is still this sick monk passing away? The Master said, "Giving alms is not as good as repaying one's debts. He ascended the hall and said:
"The subtle secret of Shaolin and the ancestral style of the Buddhas of antiquity involve responding to circumstances as they arise; rolling up and unrolling [the teachings] is entirely at ease.
It is like a fist becoming an open palm—the opening and closing occur according to the moment. It is like water forming bubbles—arising and ceasing have no fixed pattern. Movement..."
Stillness and manifestation are both revealed; speech and silence are fully displayed. The myriad functions are spontaneous, requiring no exertion of mind or effort.

Reaching this point, it is called "letting the boat drift with the current. But tell me: who is the masterful hand when rowing against the wind? After a long pause, he said: "To play in the tide, one must be a player in the tide.
He gave a shout and said: "Be careful! He ascended the hall and said: "Non-thought is the宗 (zong); non-abiding is the 本 (ben)."
Emptiness is its essence; wondrous existence is its function. Thus it is said: "The entire earth is emptiness;
throughout the dharma-realm is wondrous existence. But tell me, who is it that can employ this? The four seasons operate; the sun and moon shine eternally.
The Dharma is fundamentally non-transient; the Way has no fixed location. It is free and sovereign according to conditions, rising and sinking along with things. Entering this land or other lands...
"Regarding entering the holy state: although it is thus, tell me—how do you express the phrase 'entering a village, one follows its customs'?
After a long silence, he said: "The Sanskrit language of the Western Heavens; the Tang language of this land."
Zen Master Wuzhen of Daowu in Tanzhou ascended the hall and said: "The sun and moon of ancient and modern times; the mountains and rivers remain as they were.
If you can understand this, then the Bhagavāns of the ten directions all enter the single path of the gate to Nirvāṇa. If you cannot understand it, you slander this sutra."
"Such is the nature of committing an offense. [The Master] ascends the hall. "A lion cub roars; a dragon-horse colt leaps. The mirror of the ancient Buddhas is bright;
the solitary moon over the three mountains is clear. He then performs a dance and descends from his seat. Ascending the hall again, he cites: "Dongshan said: 'On Mount Wutai, clouds steam rice;
before the steps of the Buddha Hall, it is a dog’s urination. On the top of the banner pole, a *jizui* (a type of fried cake) is being cooked. These three..."
"The monkey tosses coins at night. I, this old monk, am not like that: "The three-faced wildcat treads upon the moon; the two-headed white ox grasps smoke in its paws.
The crowned green hare stands atop the courtyard cypress; the shell-shedding turtle flies up into the heavens.
All of my old monk’s entanglements have been seen through by you all. The Elder of Dongshan is truly extraordinary. Although...
"Indeed it is so. Yet he can only walk three or four steps; at most, he does not exceed seven or eight leaps. Now tell me, where lies the crux?
Today, this old monk will not spare his eyebrows and will bestow [the answer] all at once. After a long silence, he said:
"Admonishing [others] harms your own virtue; silence truly possesses merit. Even if the vast ocean were to change, I would never speak for you.

A monk asked, "When one understands immediately upon encountering the state of profound stillness, what is it like? The Master said, "A rat carries a pestle on its tail. A monk asked, "What is the essence of True Suchness (*tathatā*)?

The Master said, "The yakṣa kneels, his eyes black. [The monk] asked, "What is the function of True Suchness? The Master said, "The yakṣa kneels, his eyes black. (Repeating the previous answer as a response to the question regarding its application.)
The Master said: "The vajra strikes and the iron mountain crumbles. A monk asked: "What is constant illumination? The Master said: "Mount Sumeru upon the tip of a needle.
The monk asked: "What is tranquil illumination? The Master said: "The seawater within the eyebrows. The monk asked: "What is primordial illumination? The Master said:
"Treading upon the *pe* [a type of insect] inside one's straw sandals. The monk withdrew. The Master said: "Tranquil illumination, constant illumination, and primordial illumination."
"Underneath his straw sandals he is constantly leaping; furthermore, he knows how to mount Mount Sumeru upon the point of a needle. Between his eyebrows the water is ever vast and flowing.
When asked, "What is the Buddha?", the Master said, "The Lake Dongting has no cover. Ascending the hall, he said: "The wheat ripens before the mountain;
the price of rice in Luling; the radishes of Zhenzhou—and yet there is something else. After a long silence, he said: "At times one gathers wild vegetables and boils them with their roots."
He took fresh firewood, split it while still green, and burned it with the leaves attached. Entering the hall, he said: "The ancients said, 'If you recognize it, it is as before—not it.

This is truly difficult to understand. The rustic hermit has a profusion of beard and mustache beneath his chin; the Persian has deep-set eyes and large nostrils. How extraordinary! In a flash, he passes through the borders of Silla.
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the Hall. The Master said, "What did the Holy Monk say?"
"What is it? A monk stepped forward and said, "I do not presume to ask. The Master said, "To be a donkey for the eastern neighbor and a horse for the western neighbor.
The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie? The Master said, "Ten thousand *li* away at Yuzhou. The Master was unwell.

A monk asked, "How is your venerable state these days? The Master said, "The head cook cannot handle his duties. The monk was speechless. The Master snapped his fingers once. He then ascended the hall to teach.
Puhua struck both openly and secretly; the Cloth Bag Monk scattered [his bag] horizontally and vertically; the Stone Chamber Practitioner trod upon the pestle—why did he forget to set his foot down?
He asked, "What is the First Mystery? The Master said, "The light of Śākyamuni Buddha shone upon Ānanda’s shoulder."
[The student] asked, "What is the second mystery? The Master said, "A solitary wheel, with all the elephants gathered around. [The student] asked, "What is the third mystery?

The Master said, "Weeping toward the withered mulberry tree, tears flow in endless streams. [The student] asked, "What is the first essential? The Master said, "Grasping the fine and the coarse with clarity.
[The student] asked, "What is the second essential? The Master said, "A flash of lightning; heaven and earth are filled with dazzling light."
[The student] asked, "What is the third essential? The Master said, "The road is lined with aged green pines. Ascending the hall, he cited a monk who asked Shoushan, "What is the Buddha?
Shoushan replied, "The daughter-in-law rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. The Master said, "Hand in hand holding the nose-ring, feet treading the tail;
looking up at the sky and listening to the flowing water; at dawn sent out by the roadside, returning at night when all is still."
He returned to his thatched cottage.
A monk asked Zen Master Baoxin of Jiangshan, "How is it when the moon is not yet full? The Master said, "Count forward.

A black-lacquered pillar. [A monk] asked, "How can one penetrate the two characters 'sound' and 'form'? The Master said, "With one hand blow, with the other hand clap.

I have annotated this for you all: "Tangled hair and thorn-leaf hairpins are rare in the world; her coarse cloth skirt is still the dress she wore at her wedding.

Question: "What will it be like when Dharma arrives in the future? The Master said, "Six times six is thirty-six. Question: "And after he has arrived?

"A person of the first rank. A monk asked, "To have the superior lead and the inferior follow is not yet to be a master; only by turning one's back on Chu and heading for Wu can one be considered a man of true attainment.

"Mountain. Again, how do you understand this? If you understand, the lanterns will laugh at you; if you do not understand, you have eyes but are like the blind.
A monk asked Chan Master Yunliang of Mount Xiangshan in Mingzhou, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya?

The Master said, "Dancing the *Santai* on the tip of the bannerpole. The monk asked, "What is the phrase for receiving beginners? The Master said, "The *Shang Daren* (The Great Person of the Top). The monk asked again—
"What is the final phrase? The Master said, "Beneath the twin *śāla* trees. [The student] asked, "What is the place where the student turns himself around?
The Master said, "In the mill. He ascended the hall. After a long silence, he laughed loudly and said, "What is there to laugh at?
I laugh because the wild geese soar toward the heavens, while the tortoise chases after fish at the bottom of the water. Three old women with six breasts."
The back of the vajra is as rotten as mud. A-he-he! Do you know? Or do you not? Chen Daqi of the Eastern Village enters.
Master Chan Master Weiguang of Nanfeng in Suzhou ascends the hall. One question, one answer—like a bell containing its resonance, like a valley responding to a sound.
This is because he has no choice in the matter; for the time being, within the gateway of transformation and edification, he lets down a single thread of the Way. If one were to rely on...

A monk asked Chan Master Daopei Deqian of Tanzhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Water flows down from the mountain. The monk asked, "What is the intent behind this? The Master said, "How could a stream or a gully retain it?
