"Virtuous ones, what more is there for you to ponder? Last night at the third watch, unable to sleep, I turned over and seized Samantabhadra, banishing him to the Land of Non-arising.

The Master said, "Brick heads and tile shards. The monk asked, "How is it when seeking stillness amidst the bustle? The Master said, "One must not harbor resentment.

[The Master] said, "Tong-er, smile and nod your head. [A monk] asked, "What is the matter that transcends [the world]? The Master said, "The sun, moon, and stars.

[The monk] asked, "What is the matter that descends [into the world]? The Master said, "The cauldrons and boiling water of hell. [A monk] asked, "What is it like when there are no clouds for ten thousand miles?"
The Master said, "A monkey endures hunger. [The monk] said, "I beg the Master for deliverance. The Master said, "What color is the fire?

[The monk] asked, "When the ancients brandished their mallets and raised their fly-whisks, what was their underlying intent? The Master said, "On a bright day, there are no idle people. [The monk] asked, "How does one take this up?"

The Master said, "Like the wind passing by the ear. A monk asked, "What is it like when one holds a sword across the chest? The Master said, "Crows flocking in a group. The monk said, "That is exactly where you, Master, see things.
The Master said, "A snake piercing through the nostrils. The monk shook his sleeves and departed. The Master said, [as he left].
The assembly met him and asked, "Where have all the sages of the past gone? The Master said, "At the crossroads. They said, "If that is so, then there is a deficiency.
The Master said, "I knew you had not yet reached this stage. They asked, "What is it like after reaching it? The Master said, "Everyday tea and rice.
They asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "Dry..."

“Ginger and Aconite. [The monk] said, “In that case, they are not the same. The Master said, “Camphor and balls of snow. Ascending the hall, he said: “The spring rain falls lightly; water drips from the eaves.

This would leave Zhushan with no opening at all. You all, try to open your mouths and see!
A monk then asked, "What is the Great Way? The Master said, "It cannot be carried. The monk asked, "Why can it not be carried? The Master said, "The Great Way.
He ascended the hall and said, "If one discusses this matter, one must not speak of it. To speak of it is for horns to grow. A monk came forward and said, "Horns..."
Jue was about to leave. The Master said, "A calamity! Jue replied, "It is my own fault. The Master said, "To have the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake. Take care of yourself.
On the evening of the twelfth day of the tenth month in the eighth year of the Yuanfeng era, the Master suddenly wrote this verse:

"With snow-white hair and frost-tipped beard for ninety-nine years, With a single shoulder of coarse robes, all conditions are exhausted. In vast silence, he smiles and points as the floating clouds disperse; The jade hare flows [across the sky]."
His light illuminated the great trichiliocosm, and he passed into stillness after casting down his brush.
Chan Master Dezhang of Lingyin Temple first resided at the Western Sutra Repository Hall of the Great Xiangguo Monastery.

On the first day of the ninth month in the eighth year of the Qingli era, Emperor Renzong summoned the Master to the Yanchun Pavilion for a banquet and proclaimed the *Puzhao Dajie* (Great Vow of Universal Illumination).
The Master asked, "What is the single phrase that meets the occasion? The Master said, "A single word transcends the azure heavens; one walks on the precipice before a ten-thousand-fathom peak.
[The monk] asked, "How does one walk on the precipice? The Master then gave a shout. [The monk] said, "How can you act like this in the presence of the Emperor?
The Master said, "I cannot let this pass either. The following year, he was again summoned to the inner palace for a vegetarian feast. Once more...
Xuanchuzhao asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'? The Master said, "The thunder startles the fine grasses and their sprouts emerge;
advance upon the high mountain without delay. He asked, "What is 'taking away the environment but not taking away the person'?
The Master said, "Wearing horns and shrouded in fur, he moves back and forth with total freedom. He asked, "What is 'taking away both person and environment'? The Master said:
"Stepping out the gate, one is far beyond the heavens; the flowing light and shadows are not real. Dazu asked, "What is it to have neither the person nor the environment usurped?
The Master said, "In the cold forest there are no overnight guests; in the great ocean one listens to the dragon's roar.

Later, when he was again summoned to the Huacheng Hall for a vegetarian feast, Xuanchou Shanxian asked, "As the vegetarian banquet is grandly opened, how do you repay the Sage Ruler? The Master said, "Seeking bird tracks in the sky."
[The student] asked, "What is the essential meaning? The Master said, "Seeking the tracks of a fish within the water. The Master then offered the *Song of the Mind-Jewel* (*Xin Zhu Ge*):
"The mind is as it wishes; the mind is as it wishes. Spontaneously following conditions, they never part. Know this, and do not seek elsewhere; Seeking elsewhere, one will ultimately fail.
To labor in vain is to obscure the True Principle. Recognize the mind-jewel, its radiance shining like the sun— A secret treasury, profound."
Secret and formless, brought forth within the palm, it startles all who behold it. How could those of the Two Vehicles, despite their diligence, ever fathom it?

The blue-eyed barbarian points it out; how could his wondrous application ever falter when the occasion arises? Ordinarily, one must take care not to show it to others; otherwise, the mountains and rivers of the great earth will tremble and quake.
In the second year of the Huángyòu era, the Master requested to return to the mountain forests to spend his final years. An imperial decree was issued for him to reside in Hángzhōu.

The Abbot of Lingyin Temple, who was granted the title Mingjue (Illuminating Awareness), was Chan Master Chaoxin Haiyin, a successor of Chan Master Jiao of Langye at Dinghui Monastery in Suzhou. A monk asked: "What is the true essence of the Buddha-dharma?"
The general meaning is as follows: A student asked, "Regarding the bamboo staff from Xiangyuan with its mottled spots—what is its underlying intent?
The Master said, "Every branch bears traces of tears. The student asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "Narāyaṇa in a fit of rage.
The student asked, "What is the second phrase? The Master said, "The patched-robed monk is at a loss. The student asked, "What is the third phrase? The Master said, "Western Heaven and this land."
Ascending the hall: A clay snake bites a stone turtle; the pillar chirps and squeals. Sumeru is struck with a single blow;
Old Yama laughs heartily. *Chan.* Ascending the hall: If you recognize Prajñā, you are bound by Prajñā.
If you do not recognize Prajñā, you are likewise bound by Prajñā. Setting aside both recognition and non-recognition, I ask you all: What is Prajñā?
If you are the substance itself, go to the hall; ascend the dais. The song of the oriole has ceased, the sound of the cicadas grows urgent. A tortoise entering the water does not get its head wet;
a heron flies into the reeds. The mutual radiance of snow and moon cannot compare to it. HŪṂ!
A monk asked Zen Master Letan Xiaoyue of Hongzhou, "The teachings of the sutras are like a finger pointing at the moon;
I wonder what it is that the finger points to? The Master said, "Please raise your eyes high. The monk said, "When the dawn light has not yet parted, all gaze upward;
once daybreak comes, it is as usual. The Master said, "In my declining years, ghosts are playing with me."
A monk asked Chan Master Fang of Jiangshan in Yuezhou, “What is the Venerable One of Immovability? The Master said, “Wearing only his cotton robe, he passes through the marketplace.
The monk said, “I do not yet understand. The Master said, “Riding a donkey, he tramples the waves of Lake Dongting.

[The monk] said, "There is no one who can advance toward it. The Master said, "Treading upon the ground, you address the void. [The monk] said, "Under the Gate of Thunder, a cloth drum is difficult to sound.

Xiaoyou asked, "What is 'arising from the samādhi of all motes of dust'? The Master said, "A turtle bites a fishing rod. Xiaoyou said, "If that is so, then east and west cannot be distinguished, nor can north and south be discerned."
The Master said: "A bowl of night-bright lamp before the hall; several stalks of green, slender bamboo outside the curtain. [A monk asked: "How was it before the Buddhas had appeared in the world?
The Master said: "I do not know the wine-scoop. [The monk asked: "How is it after they have appeared in the world? The Master said: [He did not speak.]

When asked, "Regarding 'rushing through a flowing torrent' and 'passing a blade' or 'swift flames overtaking the wind,' I wonder if you permit such borrowing under the gate of Jiangshan or not?"
The Master said, "The sky is cold, the days are short, and the nights grow longer. The monk said, "An embroidered phoenix and mandarin duck in a brocade curtain;

travelers find it difficult to see. The Master said, "Within the skull, the vital breath surges toward heaven. The monk called out, "Master! The Master said, "The head of a rooster and the tail of a phoenix.

"Ācārya, you have transmitted this well. Nevertheless, you must not let it pass; strike! He ascended the hall and said: "Passing through the clouds, one does not cross the water;
crossing the water, one does not pass through the clouds. Heaven and earth are held fast, yet they are not held fast; empty space is let go, yet it is not let go."

You people, tell me in a single phrase: "This rice is made from grain. It is indeed difficult to speak of. After a long silence, he said: "Private matters must not be settled by official means.

The questioner asked, "Then what is where the student establishes his body and life? The Master said, "The clouds have the power to leave the mountains; the water has no sound as it plunges into the ravine. Question: "As for suchness..."
"What is the meaning of the Teachings? The Master said, "The assembly at Laṅkā. "What is the meaning of the Patriarchs? The Master said, "Before Mount Xionger.
"How far apart are the meaning of the Teachings and the meaning of the Patriarchs? The Master said, "Cold pines join with lush bamboo;
autumn waters face red lotuses."
A monk asked Chan Master Zhiquan of Langya Mountain in Chuzhou, "What is the realm of Langya?
The Master said, "The pines, being finite, grow thin and old; the flowers, being insentient, bloom at random. The monk asked, "What is the person within the realm?"
The Master said, "Your hair is long and your monastic appearance is ugly. [The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s phrase for helping people?
The Master said, "Three feet of snow before one's eyes. [The monk] asked, "Is that not it? The Master said, "A single flower behind the head."
A monk asked Zen Master Yuan of Liangfeng Cave in Quanzhou, "What is nirvana? The Master said, "Cut by knife, split by axe. The monk asked, "What is liberation?
The Master said, "The shirt is long, the trousers are short. A monk asked, "Do you, Master, know that place where all the sages do not reach?
The Master said, "In my old age, I have no strength to descend from the meditation seat. A monk asked, "How is it to transcend the four propositions and cut off the hundred negations?"
"How is it at this time? The Master said, "The thatched gate is overgrown with weeds. "Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not? The Master said, "Pines are straight;
brambles are crooked. "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A reflection in the golden sand. "What is the Way?
The Master said, "A jade maiden casting her shuttle. "How far apart are the Buddha and the Way? The Master said, "Turtle hair is long."
The second was two *zhang* tall; the rabbit’s horns were eight *chi* long.
Chan Master Fang of Zhenru Temple in Zhenzhou went to study under Langye. He focused exclusively on the "Pine Tree" koan.

Whenever he entered the room to present his insights, he was unable to find words to express himself and was frequently shouted out of the hall. One day, he suddenly attained great enlightenment and went straight to Fang.
Zhaozhou said, "I understand. Langye asked, "How do you understand it? The Master replied, "Last night the bedding was warm;
I slept until dawn. Langye approved of this.
Chan Master Tan of Xingjiao Monastery in Xuanchou was the son of the Niu family of Yongjia. His occupation was silver-smithing;

while sharpening and polishing a metal vessel, he attained realization and immediately left the household life. He went to study under Langye, with whom his spiritual resonance and speech were suddenly in perfect accord. Later, he relied upon Chan Master Huai of Dayi.

At that time, [Fanyi] was residing at Xingjiao Monastery and had been promoted to the position of First Seat. Fanyi accepted an invitation from another location and intended to go to Wenzhou to request that Master [Tiantai] succeed him.

At that moment, Scholar Diaojingchun was serving as the governor of Wanling. Fanyi, fearing that Diaojingchun might raise objections based on external opinions, made a vow before Guanyin Bodhisattva, saying:
"If Head Seat Tan’s insight into the Way is clear and he is capable of serving as abbot, I pray that you will manifest a dream to Scholar Diaojingchun."

Tou was dreaming one night that a cow was sitting upon the Dharma seat of Xingjiao. The next morning, as Tou was about to take his leave of the State, he recounted his dream to Touzi Yiqing. Yiqing laughed heartily.
When Tou asked for the reason, Yiqing said, "The Head Seat Tan has the surname Niu (Cow) and was also born in the Year of the Ox.

Tou immediately went to the seat and issued an invitation for him to ascend. The Master accepted the invitation and ascended the seat. There, the Xuedou emissary Shengzong stepped forward and asked, "All Buddhas..."
Before he appeared in the world, everyone’s nostrils reached the heavens. After he appeared in the world, why was there no news at all?
The Master said, "Before Chicken Foot Peak, the wind is still. Yuanzong said, "Not yet; say more. The Master said, "Great snow fills Chang'an.
Yuanzong said, "Who knows this meaning? It makes me think of Nanquan. He then brushed out his sleeves, returned to the assembly, and did not prostrate again.
He bowed. The Master said, "The New Teaching has lost ground today. He then returned to his quarters and sent someone to invite Zong to see him.
The Master said, "Just now, you gave an incorrect response to a turning phrase before an assembly of devas and humans; why did you not simply bow to cover it over?"
Xuanzong said, "A true man has gold beneath his knees; how could he be willing to prostrate before a blind old monk?
The Master said, "I have another saying. Xuanzong then reasoned through the previous words until they reached the point where the Master had said, "Not yet—speak further!
The Master said, "I have thirty blows to spare; I entrust them to you to strike Xuedou. Xuanzong then prostrated himself.
Chan Master Guizong Ke Xuan of Jiangzhou was a native of Hanzhou. He became a monk in his prime and immediately crossed the gorges to rely upon Langya Huihong’s single phrase;
suddenly, his many doubts were instantly extinguished, and Langya approved him. Before long, he was ordered to share the seat [with the master].

When the lay practitioner Jingkong Guo Gongfu visited his door, he engaged the Master in profound inquiry and formed a deep friendship. By the time the Master took charge of Guizong, Gongfu was serving as...
The Magistrate of Nanchang was soon enraged that the Master did not pay him due courtesy and began to persecute him severely. He then wrote a letter to Gongfu, saying:
"My karmic destiny still has six years remaining, yet I am oppressed by the Prefectural Governor. I must therefore cast off my remaining breaths and take rebirth in your family."
"I hope there will be no obstacles. Gongfu was just then reading a book; startled and delighted, he nodded his head in agreement.
In the middle of the night, his wife saw the Master enter her bedchamber in a dream. Crying out in alarm, she said, "This is not where the Monk comes from! Gongfu shook her and questioned her.

His wife related the matter in detail. She called for a lamp, took out the letter, and showed it to him; they laughed together incessantly. Consequently, she became pregnant. When the child was born, he was named Xuānlǎo.
By the time he was one year old, his memory and responses were as they had been before. When he reached the age of three, Chan Master Báizūn arrived at their home and saw him for the first time.
He said, "My nephew has come! Báizūn asked, "How many years has it been since we parted, Master? Xuānlǎo counted backward on his fingers and replied.
"It has been four years now" (meaning he died exactly one year after parting from him). Yun asked, "Where did you part? He replied, "At Bailian Zhuang. Yun said:
"What will be the proof? he asked. [Dongshan] replied, "Father and mother, tomorrow we shall invite the Master for a meal.
Suddenly, they heard the sound of a cart being pushed. Yunwen asked, "What is that sound outside the gate? Xuan made a gesture with his hand as if pushing a cart.
Yunwen said, "What happens after it has passed? He replied, "Two ditches across level ground. Indeed, six weeks later, he passed away without illness.
The lecturer Ziqú of Chángshuì in Xiùzhōu was a native of Jiāxīng in the commandery. From the time he shaved his head, he recited the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* without ceasing.

While following the Dharma Master Hóngmǐn in lectures, he attained a realization upon reaching the passage: "When the two aspects of motion and stillness are clearly seen as not arising. He said to Mǐn:
"Even striking the air or hitting wood still falls within the realm of the trap and the snare; raising one's eyes or arching one's brows has already become a matter of deliberation and conjecture."
Only by departing from these two paths can one accord with this principle. Min Fu realized this for himself; yet, wishing to explore the source of Chan, he was at a loss as to where to turn.
Hearing that Langya Huijue was esteemed in his time, he immediately went to his seat. Happening upon the Master’s ascent of the hall, Min stepped forward and asked:
"The nature is pure and originally so; why do mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? Langya, responding with an air of authority, said: "Pure and originally so..."

"However, how is it that the mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? The Master attained realization and bowed in gratitude, saying, "I wish to serve you with the water jar and the alms bowl.
Langye said to him, "Your school has not flourished for a long time; you should rouse your resolve to support it and repay the Buddha’s kindness. Do not let differences in lineage be a hindrance.
The Master followed these instructions, prostrated twice to take his leave, and later resided at Changshui. One day, while receiving instruction, Langye looked back at him and said:

The assembly said: "The Way is not attained through words or symbols; Chan is not known through deliberation or conjecture. To realize the meaning and penetrate the source, there is never anything extraordinary.
Consequently, the two schools looked up to him. He once composed commentaries on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and other scriptures, which became widely circulated in the world.

Chan Master Wenyue of Yunfeng on Mount Nanyue was a dharma successor of Chan Master Dayu Zhi. He was the son of the Xu family from Nanchang. Initially, he went to visit Dayu, where he heard him address the assembly, saying:
"Everyone has gathered here to eat some vegetable soup. If you call it 'a bowl of vegetable soup,' you will enter hell as fast as a shot arrow."
He then descended from his seat. The Master was greatly startled. That night he went to the abbot’s quarters. Yunwu asked, "What do you seek by coming here?
The Master replied, "I seek the Dharma of the mind. Yunwu said, "The Wheel of the Dharma has not yet turned; the Wheel of Food must turn first. You are a young man with strong physical vigor;
why do you not go out for alms on behalf of the assembly? I am too busy enduring hunger to have the leisure to explain Zen to you. The Master did not dare to disobey. Not long after—
Several times the Fool moved to Cuiyan. After the Master had finished submitting his petition for ordination, he again went to Cuiyan to seek instruction.

Cuiyan said, "The Buddha-dharma has not yet reached you; it will only rot you away. The snow is cold; you should go and beg for charcoal for the sake of the assembly. The Master obeyed this command. When his duties were completed, he returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Cuiyan said, "The Hall Office is lacking personnel; I shall now trouble you with this task. The Master accepted it with displeasure, resenting that Cuiyan did not [grant him dharma instruction].
As he was leaving his seat on the rear rack, the rim of the bucket suddenly gave way and it fell from the rack. The Master was suddenly enlightened, instantly seeing the point of Yanguan’s teaching.
He ran back, put on his *kāṣāya*, and went up to the dormitory. Yanguan met him with a smile and said, "Venerable Vinaya Master, rejoice!

Your great matter is now complete. The Master bowed twice without uttering a single word and departed. He served under him diligently for eight years, after which he emerged into the world [to teach].
At Cuiyan, the head seat led the assembly out to welcome him. He asked, "I do not ask about the lineage of Deshan;
what is the great function of Linji? The Master said, "Where have you come from? As the head seat hesitated, the Master slapped him.
As the head seat was about to respond, the Master shouted, "Lead the assembly back! From then on, the entire assembly was awed and submissive. A monk asked, "What is the Way?"

The Master said, "On this road, nothing is left behind. The monk asked, "What is it like for one who is on the Way? The Master said, "The grass bandits have been utterly defeated. The monk bowed; the Master let out a long sigh.
The monk asked, "When the myriad dharmas return to the One, where does the One return? The Master said, "The Yellow River has nine bends. The monk asked, "What is the first phrase?
The Master said, "His hand hangs down past his knees. The monk asked, "What is the second? The Master said, [silence].
[The Master] said: "Ten thousand *li* away at Yazu. [The monk] asked: "What is the third phrase? The Master said: "A dustpan and a broom. [The monk] asked:
"What is the Buddha-dharma of the deep mountains and rocky cliffs? The Master said: "A monkey climbing a tree upside down.
[The monk] asked: "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? The Master said: "Skin and bone. [The monk] asked: "Without involving trivialities, please, Master, speak quickly. The Master—
[The Master] said, "Mount Sumeru. He was asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said, "Firewood, sun, reeds, and grass. Ascending the hall, he said:
"If speech does not leave the old nest, how can one transcend the entanglements? A single cloud hangs across the valley mouth; how many people have been led astray from their source?"
Therefore it is said: "Words do not unfold the reality; speech does not meet the occasion. Those who rely on words perish; those who linger in phrases are deluded.
When you all reach this point, upon what do you rely to discuss and understand? After a long silence, he said: "If you wish to avoid incurring karma of the Avīci Hell..."
"Do not slander the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata. He ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas of the past have already passed into extinction;
the Buddhas of the future have not yet been born. Right now, the Buddha-dharma rests entirely with Cuiyan. If one lets go, one benefits beings according to their capacities;
if one holds fast, everything dissolves like ice melting away. Now tell me: is holding fast better, or is letting go better? After a long silence, he said: "Tsk! You wild fox!"
[The Master] struck the meditation seat and descended from it. He ascended the hall and said: "All of you who come up here in this manner are much like thrusting your brains into a vat of glue;

to go down in this manner is likewise to fall flat on one's face on level ground. Even if you neither come nor go, I shall strike you three thousand times in the morning and eight hundred times in the evening.
He ascended the hall and said: "How distant is the Way? It is true in every encounter. How distant are the sages?"
Ah! To embody this is to attain the divine. Thus, in the Sahā world, the Buddha-work is performed through sound; in the Gandhavatī world, the Buddha-work is performed through fragrant food.

Here at Cuoyan, within the very process of inhalation and exhalation, one makes offerings to and serves the Buddhas of the past, present, and future, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, without missing even a single one. [The Buddhas] of the past, present, and future, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges...
"All Buddhas—this attendant of Cuiyan has reached every one of them. If there were even one who had not reached them, I would give him thirty blows of the staff.
Do you all understand, venerable elders? 'To offer this profound mind to the dust-motes and lands—this is what is called repaying the Buddha's kindness.
[He ascended the hall: "The root of sentient beings relies upon the ocean of wisdom as its source; the stream of conscious beings takes the Dharma-body as its totality."

The essence is simply this: when emotions arise, wisdom is obstructed; when conceptions shift, the essence becomes distinct. When one realizes the source, emotions vanish; when one knows the mind, the essence merges.
"Do you all understand, monks of the various dhyānas? The ancient Buddhas interpenetrate with the pillar; the Buddha Hall vies with the lantern for its forehead.

If you do not understand, you will suffer single and double layers of failure. [Ascending the hall: "The staff and wooden block follow me wherever I go, performing a play as the occasion arises. Even so, it is thus."
"A single hand cannot clap alone. Among this assembly, is there no masterly Chan guest or monk of the fundamental school who will come forth to join in this chant?
Is there anyone? At that time, a monk came forward and bowed. The Master said: "Vague and indistinct, like a melody just barely worth hearing."
Again, blown by the wind into another tune, he descended from his seat. He ascended the hall. At dawn, when all affairs were settled, there was long-grained rice in the land of Uttarakuru.
He descended from his seat. He ascended the hall. "Where a Buddha is, one must not dwell; where no Buddha is, one must pass quickly by.
You people, carrying your staffs slung across your shoulders—where will you go on your pilgrimage? After a long silence...
He said: "In Pūrvavideha on the eastern continent, he holds the bowl; in Aparagoyānī on the western continent, he eats his rice. He ascended the hall and said:

"Even if the mind were to penetrate through immeasurable time, throughout kalpas, how could it ever have been different from today? But tell me, what is the matter of today like? After a long silence, he said:
The turtle breaks through the wall. Entering the hall [the Master said]: "Seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are without obstruction; sound, fragrance, taste, and touch are always in samādhi.
If a patch-robed monk understands this path, mountains are mountains and waters are waters; when hungry, one eats; when weary, one sleeps.
"Suddenly, Mount Sumeru leaps into your nostrils; the makara fish pierces through your eyes. How will you deliberate upon this?
After a long silence, he said, "Go to the hall. Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "To cut things in two with a single stroke does not yet qualify one as a true master.
To level the high by means of the low is certainly not the work of a true adept. When I, Cuoyan, arrive here, my mouth is like a flat carrying pole. You all..."
"How do you all deliberate upon this? After a long silence, he said: "If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Dharma Wheel.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If you see that all marks are non-marks, then the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are entirely without fault.
You venerable elders, though you wear clothes and eat food all day long, you have never bitten into a single grain of rice, nor have you ever hung [a single thread]."
By applying a single strand of silk, one can transform the great earth into gold and churn the long river into cream and curd.
Although this is so, there is no lack of clothing and food; yet, as for the stench of sweat within the gate of the patch-robed monks, you have not even dreamed of it.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The practice of Samantabhadra, the wisdom of Mañjuśrī—on Mount Potalaka a pure breeze arises, and the blind donkey chases after the herd."
Passing through Silla, he reached Jiliao Shetou, three thousand li away. Entering the hall, he raised his staff and said:
"Holding the alms bowl toward the world of Fragrant Accumulation—why is there no way to emerge? Carrying the sun and moon upon the tip of the staff."

"Why is it that though they have eyes, they are as if blind? Even when one reaches the point where the wind blows and the grass bends, where echoes follow sounds in harmony, and not even a speck of dust remains—this is still a dharma of mutual contention. What is the dharma of non-contention?
He planted his staff and descended from the seat. He ascended the hall and said: "Linji’s vanguard lets one move pass; Deshan’s subsequent command sets it aside for a moment."

"Standalone and revealed, without partiality. [The Master asked: "How do you express this in a single phrase? After a long pause, he said: "It is lamentable that Zhongli under Chu was ignorant [of this].
He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat. He ascended the hall and said: "The teachings state: 'All manner of grasping and rejecting is samsara.
If one attempts to discern Perfect Enlightenment without having escaped samsara, that nature of Perfect Enlightenment will likewise flow along with it. If one wishes to avoid..."
“Samsara? There is no such place. You people here—how will you distinguish Perfect Enlightenment at this point?
After a long silence, he said: “The lotus leaf is round and round, as round as a mirror; the water chestnut is pointed and pointed, as pointed as an awl.
He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and ascended the hall. The Ancients said, “Mountains, rivers, and stone walls do not obstruct the eye’s light. The Master asked, “How so?”

The layman said:
"Wearing clothes and eating rice according to one's means. [The student] said, "If that is so, I shall step back three paces and join my palms at my chest.

The Master said, "It is better to have no wine at all than to add a cup after one is already drunk. Small Assembly (Xiao-can). He cited: "Baizhang addressed the assembly on the eve of the New Year, saying:"
"You lot, a group of young men: you certainly do not know the Sūtras, Vinaya, or Abhidharma; yet when it comes to entering the assembly to practice Chan, you do not understand Chan either.
On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month [the day of death], how will you resolve this? The Master said, "Truly so, all you Chan practitioners."
The time since the Sage departed is remote, and the hearts of men have grown indifferent. Looking at the monastic communities (*saṃghārāma*) of today, they are even more devoid of any true standing.
Whether gathering three hundred or five hundred disciples, they are merely vast crowds who regard a bountiful diet and comfortable quarters as signs of flourishing.
Among them, there is not a single person who strives diligently for the Way; even if there were ten or five, [they would be rare].
A person. Running up and running down; half green, half yellow. If you understand, everyone says, "I understand.
Each one claims to hold the jewel of the spiritual serpent. Who is willing to admit they are wrong? Yet when pressed and prodded, there is not even one in ten thousand who succeeds.
How bitter, how bitter! As it is said: "The groves of Prajñā wither year by year; the weeds of ignorance grow more lush each spring."

Among those who are elderly, there are especially those of the present day who, as soon as they enter the monastic community, sit upright with hands folded in a gesture of reverence and accept the offerings of others.
Everywhere they go, they do not select a single stalk of vegetables nor carry a single bundle of firewood;

their ten fingers never touch water, and they have no concern for any manual labor. While this may bring them a temporary sense of ease, how can it avoid burdening them with the three miserable realms? Is this not so?
I see it. In the teaching of the Middle Way, one would rather wrap one's body in glowing red-hot iron than accept the robes of a person of faith;
one would rather pour molten copper down one's throat than accept the food of a person of faith.

Now that you all have reached this place, the wind and clouds are spread across the earth; your tusks and claws are already formed, yet you merely lack the thunderous roar to "scorch your tails.
Now, for your sakes, I shall let loose a sudden clap of thunder! [He struck the meditation seat with his staff and descended from it. This was during the Shaosheng era.
On the eighth day of the tenth month of the second year, he spoke a verse without having been ill: "Last night at the third watch, wind and thunder suddenly arose;
the clouds dispersed across the vast sky, and the moon sank behind the front stream. After a long while, he took leave of the assembly and passed into stillness.

His cremation yielded about one *dou* of *śarīra*, each as large as a bean; his eyes, teeth, and nails remained uncorrupted. His disciples divided the remains and erected stupas in the capital and in Tan.
A monk asked National Teacher Chong’ao of Xilin on Mount Nanyue, “When there is a question and an answer, the guest and host are clearly distinguished.

When there is neither question nor answer, how are they to be distinguished? The Master said, “Those sitting sit; those standing stand. The monk said, “What is it like when one understands it in this way?
The Master said, “The tongue is pressed against the upper palate. The monk bowed. The Master said, “Do not try to hide it.”

Chan Master Xiyi Yingyue of Shaoshou was the son of the Dai family of Yihuang. He presided over Fuzhi. One day, he ascended the hall and said: "In my school, there is no..."
Words and phrases are but a weary search for a path; the public cases are already manifold. How can one bear to enter yet another gate?
When meeting face-to-face, seize the opportunity directly; what need is there to undergo such bitter toil? *Tu!* (A shout)
Chan Master Wenzan of Guangguo Temple in Langzhou, a successor of Chan Master Shuangfeng Hui, was asked by a monk: "The Dharma of non-duality—please, Master, speak of it quickly. The Master said:
The Governor said, "If that is so, then everyone has their share. The Master said, "Finished. [The Governor] said, "A brocade screen is rare throughout the world;
a light for the nation is seldom seen in this age. The Master said, "Withdraw."

Chan Master Zhiyuan of Qionglong in Suzhou, a successor of Chan Master Dinghuixin, ascended the hall and said: "When blessings arrive, I do not speak of Chan; with nothing to do, I sleep late in the day."
When someone asked about the meaning of the Patriarchs, he struck them two or three times in succession. Tell me, assembly, why did he act thus?
It was because that fellow would not stop disturbing my sleep.

Chan Master Qixiao of Shouning Monastery in Guizhou, successor to Chan Master Yunfeng Yue, ascended the hall and said: "If you do not understand the Way upon meeting it with your eyes, you are still somewhat ahead;
yet if you move your feet without knowing the path, you have wrongly applied names and words. You worthy ones, today this mountain monk shall take the wrong and follow the wrong along with you."
People such as these see that there are eyes, hear that there are ears, smell with the nose, and taste with the tongue;

why then do they fail to understand? After a long silence, he said: "Emperor Wu sought the immortal and did not find the immortal; Wang Qiao sat upright and ascended to heaven. He then exclaimed, "Duh! A monk asked:
"The great assembly has gathered like clouds; what should we discuss? The Master said: "A Persian enters a bustling marketplace. The monk said: "If that is so," [the Master continued: "Then..."
"The grass bows and the wind blows; he has departed. The Master said, "From ten thousand *li* away, gazing toward the home pass.
Zen Master Jingyin Zhen’s Dharma heir, Zen Master Huixian Wenhui of Changqing in Fuzhou, was asked by a monk: "Leaving the precious land of the Upper Birth, one ascends the invitation..."
"The Sage’s place of enlightenment—how is this the Venerable Acala? The Master said: "A solitary boat carrying the bright moon. [The student] asked:

"If one suddenly encounters a situation where both oars and rudders have been stopped, what then? The Master said: "The fisherman especially loves to stay overnight amidst the reeds. [The student] asked:
"Regarding the long-term advancement on the Path, in India they use a wax man as a test. I wonder, what is used here as a test? The Master said: "Iron."
Danzi asked, "What is the meaning? The Master said, "The large is large; the small is small.
Chan Master Jichao of Qisheng in Fuzhou ascended the hall, held up his staff, and after a long pause, said, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time..."
All is contained right here, leaping and bounding. Does the assembly understand? The Buddhas of the past have already spoken;
the Buddhas of the future have not yet spoken; the Buddhas of the present are speaking now. I dare ask you all: what is this matter that is being spoken?
He struck the meditation desk once and said: "Sūlu sūlu.

Chan Master Xinghua Shaoqing of Tanzhou, a dharma successor of Chan Master Xinghua Yue, ascended the hall and said: "In the school of the Patriarchs, the Buddha-dharma does not exist; even wholesome dharmas do not exist."

Before the hall, let us cease speaking of benevolence and righteousness. Although this is so, matters do not always follow a single direction. I have heard it said: "Alas, alas, our parents! Their toil in giving birth to us was great.
To repay their profound kindness, the vast heavens are insufficient; even a hair or skin of one’s body must not be harmed."
This was the filial piety of Zhongni of Lu. To revolve within the three realms and yet be unable to abandon one’s affection is not true repayment of kindness;

to cast aside such affection and enter the state of non-action (*asamskrta*) is the true way to repay one's debt of gratitude. Therefore, our Great Awakened World-Honored One practiced austerities on the Snowy Mountains and attained the Way at Magadha;
he then ascended to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to preach the Dharma for his mother—this was the filial piety of Śākyamuni. Having attained great liberation, he...
Possessing great supernormal powers, he held a golden staff in his hand and cradled a dragon-embossed bowl in his palm. He went to the gates of hell and stood there in solemn contemplation.
There he saw his compassionate mother, weeping boundlessly. This was the filial piety of Maudgalyāyana.
But what is the filial piety of Xinghua? After a long silence, he said: "Today, Xinghua does not ascend to heaven, nor does he enter hell; he is at the Hall of Good Dharma."
He ascended the Dharma seat at the center of the lamp-king altar and preached the Dharma for his mother to repay her labors. He then asked: "Tell me, where is my mother now? He replied:
"In her lifetime, my mother accumulated sufficient roots of goodness; there is no need to trouble the Buddha to ask—she has surely been reborn in heaven.
Among humans, a long life is rare in all ages; she reached ninety years, minus one. Having descended from the seat, he said: "I venture to trouble the assembly to offer incense."
A single stick of incense is offered to assist this mountain monk in repaying his filial debt. Since she was my mother, why then do you trouble yourselves to burn incense?
Have you not heard it said: "When a member of the eastern family dies, the members of the western family offer their condolences"?
With hands beating their chests, they cry out: "Heaven! Heaven!"

Chan Master Huilì Shànzhōu of Línjiāng Commandery, successor to Chan Master Fāng of Yùquán, ascended the hall and said: "A falcon from the vast heavens, amidst ten thousand layers of clouds, makes but a single dash."
"What is this? he asked. On the full moon day of the twelfth month in the first year of the Yuanyou era, the Master bathed and purified his hair, then spoke this verse:
"This mountain monk has resided at Ruijun; never before have I manifested words or phrases. Seventy-three years have come, and seventy-three years have gone.
Having finished speaking, he passed away. Five days later, his beard and hair grew back again.

The Dharma Successor of the Thirteenth Generation under Nanyue, Chan Master Daopei Zhizhai Purong of Zhihai in Dongjing, ascended the hall and said: "This mountain monk does not understand the Buddha-dharma; yet, for the sake of others..."
There is no underlying cause or reason. At times it is half-open and half-closed; at other times it is fully released or fully withdrawn.
It is like dropping a stone coldly into a crowd of ten thousand people: only when it suddenly strikes someone does one realize that [the Way] flows everywhere.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Zhaozhou has four gates; through every gate, the Great Way passes. Yuyuan has four roads; through every road, one reaches Chang'an.
Through every gate, the Great Way passes—after all, who has truly arrived? Through every road, one reaches Chang'an—look clearly as you take this step forward. He struck his knee once and said:
"For the traveler who has not yet returned at year's end, the autumn wind outside the gate is cold. Ascending the hall, he raised an example.
Panshan addressed the assembly, saying: "Like the earth supporting a mountain, one is unaware of the mountain’s towering loftiness;
like a stone containing jade, one is unaware of the jade’s flawlessness. When the ancients spoke thus, it was much like crying out for injustice while clutching stolen goods.
Under Zhikai, everyone is resolute and courageous—capturing tigers and rhinoceroses alive, seizing fierce dragons with their bare hands; they can accommodate Mount Sumeru within their eyes."
"Within one's ears, one can hold the waters of the great ocean. He then took up his staff and said, "This is not to show off my skills to others;
the bearing of a true man of spirit ought to be like this. He struck the ground with his staff and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Letan Jingsiang of Hongzhou was the son of the Fu family of Nancheng in Jianchang.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Ten fingers, eight of them forked. The monk asked, "How is my hand like the Buddha’s hand?
The Master said, "It is difficult to distinguish gold from brass. The monk asked, "How is my foot like a donkey’s foot? The Master said, "The road of Huanglong is perilous."
[The monk] asked, "Every person has their own karmic affinity for birth. What is the Master’s own affinity for birth?
The Master said, "I firmly guard the critical ford; neither ordinary nor sage may pass. On the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall and said:

"The discourse at Vulture Peak, the pointing at Caoxi—letting go of those who first saw [the moon] and then looked up with bated breath, before even asking the old, ancient adept of Longmen: 'Last night at the third watch, it turned toward the west. At this very moment..."
Someone asked, "What is the moon? [The Master] said, "At the place where light and dark have not yet been distinguished, utter a single phrase, and you shall join hands with the ancients.
If this is not yet the case, Bao Feng cannot help but follow the mold and draw the pattern to respond to the occasion.
He then drew a circle and said: "Its pure radiance lasts for ten thousand ages and again for ten thousand ages; how could it be limited to a single moment in the human world?"
[The Master] looked at him at night. In his room, the Master asked a monk, "When Bodhidharma returned to the West, he carried a single sandal in his hand.
Why did he not take both sandals with him then? The monk replied, "He needed to leave a trace of news here in this land.
The Master said, "One foot is in the Western Heaven; one foot is in the Eastern Land. What is the reason for this? The monk was speechless. The Master asked another monk, "The One Sole Solidity..."
"The body manifests within all dust. What is this body that manifests within the dust? The monk pointed to an incense burner and said, "This is an incense burner.
The Master said, "You bring the Buddhas of the three periods of time down with you; you shall fall headlong into hell. The monk was at a loss for words, and the Master struck him.
Later, while the Master was unwell, a monk asked, "How is your health these days, Master? The Master replied, "Dust."

Before ascending to the stage of the Bodhisattva grounds, he burned two bundles of paper money as offerings. The Master would constantly sit in meditation at night with his hands joined in the *añjali* gesture, as if facing a great guest.

When first sitting, his hands were level with his knees; by the fifth watch of the night, they would invariably reach his chest. Consequently, he was known as "Xiang Chashou" (Auspicious Hand-Joiner).
Chan Master Huilán of Kuàngxiào in Wèizhōu was a man of unknown origins. He styled himself the "Immortal of the Azure Void" (Bìluò Dàorén).
He once wrote the names of the Seven Buddhas upon his robe with ink; thus, the monastic community referred to him as "Lánbùkùn" (Lán the Tunic-Bearer).

A poem titled "Imitating the Song of the Thatched Hermitage" exists and is circulated in the world, recorded in full in the *Fǔdēng*. Toward the end of the Jiānyán era, when rebel invaders breached the Huái River, they captured the Master and presented him before their chieftain.
The official Chang asked, "Have you heard my name? The Master replied, "All I have heard is the name of the Great Song Emperor.

Enraged, Chang ordered his attendants to strike him with a hammer; yet every time the hammer reached him, it shattered into pieces. Chang was struck with wonder and marvel, and he summoned his subordinates to serve the Master with reverence.

After ten days had passed, the Master sought firewood to immolate himself, but none dared to provide it. He personally gathered the wood and constructed a niche for his own cremation, remaining serene.
He sat upright; immediately, smoke and flames rose up, and glowing embers surged in all directions. The barbarian knelt and prostrated himself; many had their skin scorched by the fire.
When the flames subsided, he obtained five-colored śarīras, which he took along with the bones and returned north. All the monks and nuns he had captured were granted their freedom.
The people of Hezhou have sung of this to this day.

On the day Chan Master Dongming Renshan of Tanzhou opened the hall for his formal sermon, a monk asked, "When the World-Honored One appeared in the world, Brahma led the way in front and Indra followed behind.
When you, Master, appear in the world, what auspicious signs are there? The Master said, "Even were it hundreds or thousands of Buddhas, I would drive them all at once into the cow-pen.
The monk asked, "What auspicious signs are there? The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, have never [seen any]."
A Flowering Eye.
A monk asked Chan Master Xiaoqin Mingwu of Puzhao Temple in Sizhou: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed?
The Master said, "Even closer to the east. [The monk] said, "You are the son of Guishan and the direct grandson of Zhihai. The Master—[remained silent].
He said, "I laugh at those bystanders who hold their fishing rods. Entering the hall, he said: "Reaching out a hand to grasp the void—how can it ever reach the mark?

Turning the body to cast a shadow—is this not merely exhausting one's own form? When the thing is brought forth right before one's face, one instead lets it slip by. After all, what is the ultimate reality?
He struck the meditation seat and said, "In the end, you have deliberated it all wrongly."
Master Zhengjue Chan from Donglin on Mount Lu ascended the hall and said: "Before the fifteenth day, I let one move pass by;
after the fifteenth day, it cannot yet be discussed. Right now, on the fifteenth day itself, try and speak a single phrase."
After a long silence, he said: "The mountain colors are lush and verdant as the spring rain ceases; the incense fills the cypress courtyard as the magnolia blooms.
Chan Master Zhi of Fuyan in Tanzhou ascended the hall and said: "On the peak of Fuyan Mountain, the clouds unfurl and roll up at will, morning and evening.
Suddenly they fall upon the level ground; when a guest arrives, it is difficult to find the gate."
Chan Master Dongming Qian of Tanzhou had long served under Zhenru. Later, he resided at Zhenru Hermitage on Mount Guiyang.

The practitioner Zhong held his character in high esteem and frequently visited him for instruction. One day, while reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, Zhong asked, "According to my understanding of the text, 'When I press my finger, the Ocean-Seal radiates light.
What was the Buddha’s intention? The Master said, "The old Śākyamuni deserves twenty blows. Zhong said:
"Why is it so? The Master said, "What need is there to press your fingers? [The monk] asked, "If you momentarily raise your mind, worldly toil arises first;
what then? The Master said, "That too is the radiance of the Ocean Seal."
Chan Master Puyin Cijue of Kuangxiao Monastery in Quzhou was a successor of Chan Master Xuedou Ya. He was the son of the Xu family of Quanzhou.
In his meditation hall, he would ask a monk, "Before your parents were born, where were you practicing? As soon as the monk attempted to answer, he struck him out. Or he would say, "Attain [it]!"
"Ma is under your feet. When the monk attempted to look, he struck him out as well. Someone said, "Speak! Speak! When the monk attempted to open his mouth, he struck him out again.
[This was] Master Chengshan Zhen, a successor of the Dharma lineage.
Chan Master Punen of Qingxian Monastery in Hangzhou ascended the hall. Having no choice in the matter, he entangles himself with you all:
All sentient beings suffer simply because the dust of their minds has not been shed and their emotional calculations have not been eliminated.

Seeing forms and hearing sounds, they go with the flow and drift upon the waves, transmigrating through the three realms and drowning in the four modes of birth. This causes right view to remain obscure and leads to stagnation at every turn.

If right and wrong are both obliterated and good and evil are entirely forgotten, one sits and cuts off the heads of the *nirmāṇakāya* and *saṃbhogakāya* Buddhas, severing the paths of the holy and the ordinary;
only then is there a slight degree of resonance. Even so, for a patch-robed monk, this is not yet extraordinary. Why is this?
As soon as there is right and wrong, confusion arises and the mind is lost. *Du!* [He] ascended the hall and took up his staff.

The staff said, "Before it entered the hands of this mountain monk, the myriad dharmas were perfectly present as they are. Now that it has entered the hands of this mountain monk, what further matter is there?
After a long silence, he said, "When there is spirit, one adds to that spirit; where there was no elegance, now there is elegance.
He struck the staff once.
Chan Master Fashun of Jingtu was the dharma heir of [Master] Sengcan.
Chan Master Fachen of Wanshou on Lingfeng Mountain in Hangzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "Hugging a post and paddling like a duck. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "A ball of yellow clay. The monk asked, "What is the Sangha?"
The Master said, "Having shaved off your hair and beard, do you have any other way of acting for others apart from the Three Jewels?

He held up one finger. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The finger is here; look only at the moon. When the wind comes, the banner does not move. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]:
"De Shan’s staff and Linji’s shout are both nothing but ripples on a windless sea. The lantern leaps across the green."
"O Heaven! The soul of the incense pillar is startled and its head splits asunder. Although it is thus, it is very much like adding salt to one's thirst.
(He lets out a shout.
On the day of the opening of the hall by Chan Master Shoulong of Qingshan in Hangzhou, a monk asked: "I know that you have long harbored a treasure within your bag."
"Today, at this banquet, I shall briefly borrow your gaze. The Master said, "How very clear! [The monk] said, "When the Lion Roars, it is fully revealed;

but what of Mañjuśrī wielding his sword? The Master said, "It would startle even this old monk. [The monk] asked, "When the thousand Buddhas appear in the world, each has their own extraordinary auspicious signs.
On this day, with what do you, Master, provide proof? The Master said, "A wooden man holds a board and strikes it amidst the clouds."
[The monk] asked, "What is the meaning? The Master said, "A stone woman picks up a flute and blows it beneath the water. He ascended the hall and said: "Flowers in clusters, brocade in clusters;
for years, salt and sauce have been sufficient for every need. We have kept the cauldron that Nanquan broke, and entrusted it to a novice to cook the morning congee.
The morning congee is at your disposal for all to eat, but how do you understand this one phrase: 'Washing the bowl'? [He added: "Much!"
Few people have doubted this.
Zen Master Yue of Huguo was a Dharma successor of [Master] Huiwen.
A monk asked Zen Master Huiguo Huiben of Hengzhou: "There is a thing prior to heaven and earth; it is formless and fundamentally quiescent."
Liao said, "I do not yet understand what kind of thing this is. The Master said, "A single stick of ink. Liao said, "If that is so, it illuminates the past and shines upon the present.
The Master asked, "What is it that illuminates the past and shines upon the present? The monk then gave a shout. The Master struck him.
He ascended the hall and said, "What a fine occasion! Who is willing to take responsibility for it? If there is no one, it is better to let it be as it is. After a long pause, he said:
A pearl from the night sea to catch a sparrow.
The Dharma successor of Chan Master Zhikai Ping of the fourteenth generation under Nanyue.
Zen Master Tan’an Jicheng of Jingyin Monastery in Tokyo was a native of the Liu family of Yichun, Yuan Province. One day, he ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said:
"The fundamental nature is pure and still; how is it that all of a sudden mountains, rivers, and the great earth arise? Look! Look!
Pūrṇa has pierced through the nostrils of Śākyamuni, and Śākyamuni has drilled through the belly of empty space. Now tell me—"
"Where are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth? He threw down his staff and called to the assembly, saying, "The void performs a somersault and departs for the kingdom of Silla.
This too is for you all; you must by all means avoid mistaking leaves for the crying-stopping [medicine], or marking the boat to seek the sword.
He ascended the hall and said, "Throughout the vast expanse, there are none but those seeking the Buddha; in all the world, it is difficult to find a man at ease. [They rely on] blows and shouts..."

Ascending the hall: A servant from Kunlun wears iron trousers; with every stroke of the staff, he takes a step. How does this compare to fishing for turtles amidst fire, or hiding ice in the sun?

Shadows at the gate turn into *wangliang* spirits; empty space is bound by hempen rope. Ascending the hall: Meeting on a narrow path, do not yet harbor doubt. It is like a flash of lightning striking a flint.
The fire has already been slow to ignite. If you were instructed to penetrate directly with the three minds, it would occur in this very moment.
Reaching this point, even if questions are posed and answers are given, sparks will fly and embers scatter;

host and guest will interchange, illumination and function will be gained or lost, waves will surge and peaks will stand firm, jade will turn and pearls will revolve. Before the eyes of a true monk, there is no connection whatsoever. Have you not seen it? [The Buddha] held up a flower.
On Vulture Peak, Kāśyapa alone was granted permission; at Vaiśālī, when asked about his illness, who else could he have been but Jintu (Golden Grain)?
How could one have known that the smile had already become a well-trodden path? Even if one remains silent, one cannot avoid the winds and waves.

One must meet beyond the ordinary to truly understand; therein lies the ultimate resonance. Do you understand? A single melody, vast and empty, moves through the ages: it rises from the thirty-six peaks west of Luoyang.
The Hall Master said: "To look back is already a deviation; to deliberate and ponder—when will you ever awaken? O Great Assembly! A withered mulberry tree knows the wind from heaven;
this is 'looking' and 'not looking. The ocean water knows the cold of heaven; this is 'thinking' and 'not thinking. But what do you call the principle of awakening?
Carrying the Dharma-realm on the tip of a rabbit-horn staff; dancing the Three Terraces with a tortoise-hair whisk. He ascended the hall. [He smelled] through his nose.
Sound is fragrance within the ear; saltiness and blandness are in the eye, while the tongue perceives the profound and the yellow. The mind can perceive touch, and the body makes distinctions.

In an ice chamber it is like spring; in the ninth month of summer it is cool. Seeing it thus, one finally knows that when entering meditative concentration within a man’s body, one emerges from concentration within a woman’s body.
The sunflower turns with the sun; the rhinoceros-patterned horn reflects the moon’s birth. Fragrant maples transform into old age.
People are like caterpillars becoming gall-nests. If you do not know this, how bitter it is, O Buddha! I grant you a single eye. Entering the hall [for formal teaching], he said:
"In a single thought-moment, when the mind is pure, the Buddha dwells in the Demon King’s palace; in a single thought-moment, when an evil mind arises, the Demon King dwells in the Buddha’s palace.
Master Huai said: "Simply believe in this way; this is called walking with one's feet firmly planted on the ground. At last—
There is no separate dharma, nor is there any separate principle. Having spoken thus, this old monk fears that you all will let the hawk fly after the rabbit, or mark the boat to seek the sword.
Why? Because a wise host accepts neither the Goddess of Merit nor the Woman of Darkness.
Ascending the hall, he raised up the staff held by Fenyang and showed it to the assembly, saying: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time are right here in this."
[The Master] said, "You people here have no openings; you have run right into the staff of this mountain monk and are needlessly creating complications.
The Master continued, "Fenyang’s way of instructing disciples is much like carrying snow to fill a well while acting as if no one else exists.
Today, I shall speak on behalf of all of you to clear the air. Raising his staff, he said, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time do not dare..."
Qiangsheng’s program: He emerged from within this mountain monk’s staff and said to everyone, "I do not dare to slight you;

Throwing down his staff, he said, "If you go to other places, present this clearly to them. Master [Dongshan] joined in.

When Yuanwu Fazhen, Cishou, and a thousand monks—both Chan and Dharma masters—attended a vegetarian feast at the residence of the Grand Marshal Chen Gong Liangbi, Emperor Huizong went there in private to observe them; the Grand Preceptor, Duke of Lu, was also present.
There was one named Shanhua, a "tiger of meaning" within the Xianshou school, who addressed the assembly of Chan masters and asked them:
Our Buddha established his teachings, ranging from the Small Vehicle up to the Perfect and Sudden. He swept away both emptiness and existence to realize alone the True and Constant;
only after being adorned with the myriad virtues was he named a Buddha. I have often heard it said that a single shout of the Chan school can transform an ordinary person into a sage.
This would seem to contradict various sutras and treatises. Now, if a single shout can enter the five teachings of our school, it is a correct teaching;
if it cannot so enter, it is a false teaching. The various Chan masters looked toward their teacher, who said:
"As the Dharma Master has asked, this is not sufficient to be answered by the three great Chan masters. The junior Elder of Jingyin may be sent to the Dharma Master."

There was no confusion. The Master called out, "Shan! Shan responded with a "Yes. The Master said: "What the Dharma Master calls the 'teachings of the foolish Small Vehicle' refers to the meaning of existence.
The 'Initial Teaching of the Great Vehicle' refers to the meaning of emptiness. The 'Final Teaching of the Great Vehicle' refers to the meaning of neither existence nor emptiness.
The 'Sudden Teaching of the Great Vehicle' refers to the meaning of being both existent and empty. The One Vehicle..."

The Perfect Teaching (Yuanjiao) is the principle that "it exists without existing" and "it is empty without being empty" (alternatively expressed as "it is empty yet not non-existent" and "it exists yet not non-empty").
For example, my single shout is not only able to penetrate the five teachings; it can even penetrate the arts and crafts, the various branches of learning, and the hundred schools of thought.
The Master let out a thunderous shout and asked Shan, "Did you hear it? Shan replied, "I heard it. The Master said, "Since you..."
Upon hearing this single shout, he said, "It exists," which allowed him to enter the Hinayana teaching. A moment later, the Master asked Shan, "Did you hear it? He replied, "I did not hear it.
The Master said, "Since you did not hear it, that previous shout was non-existent," thereby allowing him to enter the Initial Teaching (Shijiao).
Then, turning to Shan, the Master said, "When I first shouted, you said it existed; now that the sound has faded after the shout, you say it does not exist. To say it does not exist—"
Thus, when originally there was truly existence, because the Way exists, it is now truly real; it is neither existent nor non-existent, and one can thereby enter the Final Teaching (Jiàojiào).

When I let out a single shout, that existence is not existence, for existence arises because of non-existence. When there is no single shout, that non-existence is not non-existence, for non-existence arises because of existence.
Existence and non-existence are simultaneous; one can thereby enter the Sudden Teaching (Dùnjiào). You must know this one [shout] of mine...
"Ha! This is not used as a single shout; it transcends both existence and non-existence, and both intellectual understanding and conceptualization are forgotten.

When the Way exists, not even a speck of dust can stand; when the Way does not exist, it extends horizontally throughout empty space. This very "Ha! enters into hundreds of thousands of millions of shouts.
"Hundreds of thousands of millions of shouts are all contained within this one shout; therefore, one can enter the Perfect Teaching. Shan then rose and bowed twice.
The Master spoke again, saying, "It is not only the case with a single shout; it applies even to a single word or a single silence, a single movement or a single stillness."

From antiquity to the present, throughout the empty space of the ten directions, amidst the myriad phenomena of the universe, the beings of the six realms and four modes of birth, the Buddhas of the three periods of time, and all the sages and worthies—the eighty-four thousand Dharma gates, the hundreds of thousands of samādhis, and the immeasurable subtle meanings that accord with principle and respond to capacity—are one body with heaven, earth, and the myriad things;
this is called the Dharmakāya. The three realms are mind-only; the myriad dharmas are [mind-only].
Consciousness. Throughout the four seasons and eight nodes of the year, the Yin and Yang are of one accord; this is called the *dharmatā* (dharma-nature).

Therefore, the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* says: "The *dharmatā* pervades all places. Whether with form or without form, whether a single sound or a single color, it is entirely present within a single mote of dust.

It encompasses the four meanings of phenomena and principle; it is boundlessly pervasive without exception. They interpenetrate without being confused, and they blend together without becoming one. Regarding this:
All are fully contained within a single shout; yet this is merely the gateway for manifesting transformation, a provisional means according to capacity, termed a "small resting place.
It has not yet reached the Precious Abode. Little do they realize that within the gate of our ancestral masters, mind is transmitted through mind and the Dharma is sealed by the Dharma;
no reliance is placed on words and letters, for one attains Buddhahood by seeing one's nature. There is a supreme path that has not been transmitted by a thousand sages.
Zhashan asked again, "What is the path that leads upward? The Master said, "For now, you should understand it by looking downward.

the whisk leaps across the shifting sands and snatches away a single sandal from the barbarian monk. Thereupon, he passes away with serene composure.

where crows cry and magpies chirp, each sound is a wondrous melody. He struck his staff and said: "Tell me, what kind of Buddha-work is this?
There is no small amount of disorder here! He ascended the hall again and said: "Xiangshan has a *huatou* (critical phrase) that fills the four great continents. If...

The Head Seat Xingzhi Changqiong of Kasan at Jianning Fu was a native of Shangrao. The monastic communities honored him as a man of venerable virtue;
even Lengtian remarked that he had thoroughly completed his training and was fit to share the seat of the Dharma. One day, he cited the saying regarding the "single shoe returned to the West."

He said to the assembly, "To die while seated, to pass away while standing, or to manifest transformation while inverted—these are not non-existent. However, there has never yet been one who, having passed away, returned again leaving behind their sandals.
Is it that the descendants of later generations do not equal the Patriarch? Or is it that the Patriarch had this one extra trick up his sleeve?
He then laughed heartily and said, "Old wild fox! In the winter of the Gengshen year of the Xiangshi era, the Prefect of Xin invited [the Master] to Chao-hua.
He changed his monastic discipline to practice Chan and was welcomed as the First Patriarch. The Master said to the special envoy, "I originally had no intention of remaining in the human world;
I wished to be a mountain-dweller solely for the sake of the lineage. However, I fear I may not be able to go there often.

Having accepted the invitation, he took the portrait of Lestam that he had kept and the two characters "Mu'an" (Wooden Hermitage). He then wrote a verse to entrust to the elder Qingquan Heng and sent it. [The envoy] received [the items].
The Dharma-disciple Huishan said, "This fellow with the mouth of a crow is no vessel for auspiciousness; he loves to stir up disputes within the monastic communities.
Hand him over to the Chief Seat of Xuefeng Mountain and let him give him a thorough scolding—do not spare him! He then addressed the special messenger, saying, "Convey my words to the Minister:
my departure is so urgent that I have no time to compose a formal reply. With these words, his voice ceased and he passed away.
Jingchun, a native of Meizhou, received ordination at Huadu Monastery. He went to rely upon Letan;

upon entering the inner room for instruction, Letan asked, "How much does the iron ox of Shanfu weigh? The Master stepped forward with his hands folded and said, "Now tell me, how much does it weigh?"
Tang said, "The tail is in the north of the Yellow River; the head rests on the south of the Yellow River. Shancai has no nostrils, yet he continues to travel south in search of teachers.

Xinzhou Huaiyu Yongxuan was the son of Peng from Siming. He became a monk in his youth and proceeded directly to monastic centers.
He attended Litan at Huangbo; one day, returning from Linchuan with his alms bowl, he encountered Litan’s evening discourse, in which he said:
"A single leaf drifting through the air reveals autumn; the Dharma-body must penetrate the clamor and chatter. Upon hearing this, the Master understood the meaning, and Dan served as his witness.

Later, he relied upon Dahui, who also remarked that he was of the same caliber as himself. For this reason, although eminent officials and lords of great monasteries came to welcome and honor him, he did not accept their invitations.
He once composed a verse on the story of Dayu answering the Buddha, which says: "Sawing apart a scale-weight—this comes from Old Du."
