The monk asked, “What is the sphere of infinite space? The Master said, “Transcending all forms and perceptions, one dwells in the thought of infinite space. The monk asked, “What is the sphere of infinite consciousness? The Master said, “Transcending the sphere of infinite space, one dwells in the thought of infinite consciousness. The monk asked, “What is the sphere of nothingness? The Master said, “Transcending the sphere of infinite consciousness, one dwells in the thought of nothingness. The monk asked, “What is the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception? The Master said, “Transcending the sphere of nothingness, one dwells in the thought of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. The monk asked, “What is transcending all forms and perceptions? The Master said, “Transcending all forms and perceptions, one dwells in the thought of infinite space. The monk asked, “What is the thought of infinite space? The Master said, “The thought of infinite space is the thought of the nature of reality. The monk asked, “What is the nature of reality? The Master said, “The nature of reality is empty and quiescent. The monk asked, “What is emptiness? The Master said, “Emptiness is the absence of self and what belongs to self. The monk asked, “What is the absence of self and what belongs to self? The Master said, “The absence of self and what belongs to self is the ultimate truth. The monk asked, “What is the ultimate truth? The Master said, “The ultimate truth is beyond words and concepts. The monk asked, “If it is beyond words and concepts, how can one attain it? The Master said, “Attaining it is simply not seeking it elsewhere. The monk asked, “If one does not seek it elsewhere, where does one find it? The Master said, “It is found within one’s own mind. The monk asked, “What is one’s own mind? The Master said, “One’s own mind is the Buddha-mind. The monk asked, “What is the Buddha-mind? The Master said, “The Buddha-mind is the mind of awakening. The monk asked, “What is the mind of awakening? The Master said, “The mind of awakening is the mind of non-arising. The monk asked, “What is the mind of non-arising? The Master said, “The mind of non-arising is the mind of non-extinction. The monk asked, “What is the mind of non-extinction? The Master said, “The mind of non-extinction is the mind of the Middle Way. The monk asked, “What is the mind of the Middle Way? The Master said, “The mind of the Middle Way is the mind of equality. The monk asked, “What is the mind of equality? The Master said, “The mind of equality is the mind of liberation. The monk asked, “What is the mind of liberation? The Master said, “The mind of liberation is the mind of great compassion. The monk asked, “What is great compassion? The Master said, “Great compassion is to save all sentient beings without exception. The monk asked, “How does one save all sentient beings? The Master said, “Saving them is by means of the six pāramitās. The monk asked, “What are the six pāramitās? The Master said, “Generosity, discipline, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom. The monk asked, “What is generosity? The Master said, “Giving away all possessions without attachment. The monk asked, “What is discipline? The Master said, “Observing the precepts without violation. The monk asked, “What is patience? The Master said, “Enduring insults and harms without anger. The monk asked, “What is vigor? The Master said, “Exerting effort in the cultivation of goodness without laziness. The monk asked, “What is meditation? The Master said, “Concentrating the mind on a single object without distraction. The monk asked, “What is wisdom? The Master said, “Discerning the true nature of all phenomena without delusion. The monk asked, “If one practices these six pāramitās, will one attain Buddhahood? The Master said, “Practicing them leads to the attainment of Buddhahood. The monk asked, “What is Buddhahood? The Master said, “Buddhahood is the realization of the Dharma-body. The monk asked, “What is the Dharma-body? The Master said, “The Dharma-body is omnipresent and eternal. The monk asked, “If it is omnipresent and eternal, why do sentient beings not see it? The Master said, “Sentient beings do not see it because their minds are clouded by ignorance. The monk asked, “How can one remove this ignorance? The Master said, “Removing it is through the practice of the three learnings: precept, concentration, and wisdom. The monk asked, “What is the practice of precept? The Master said, “The practice of precept is to purify one’s conduct. The monk asked, “What is the practice of concentration? The Master said, “The practice of concentration is to still the mind. The monk asked, “What is the practice of wisdom? The Master said, “The practice of wisdom is to realize the truth. The monk asked, “If one realizes the truth, what is the fruit? The Master said, “The fruit is the liberation of the mind. The monk asked, “What is the liberation of the mind? The Master said, “The liberation of the mind is the attainment of nirvana. The monk asked, “What is nirvana? The Master said, “Nirvana is the cessation of all suffering. The monk asked, “If all suffering ceases, is there still birth and death? The Master said, “When all suffering ceases, there is no more birth and death. The monk asked, “If there is no more birth and death, where does one go? The Master said, “Where one goes is the realm of the Buddhas. The monk asked, “What is the realm of the Buddhas? The Master said, “The realm of the Buddhas is the realm of the Dharma-re
"Since you are a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), why do you still crave wealth and beauty? The Master said, "Those who recognize kindness are few.
The Master asked the fire-attendant, "Is the firewood ready? The attendant replied, "Lower your voice. The Master said, "From where did you get this news?"
[The monk] said, "There is no need for many words. The Master said, "It is easy to be full on cheap money, yet one is hungry again after eating.

[The monk] asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Long-simmered pickled vegetables and cold rice. [The monk] said, "That is far too desolate. The Master said, "This is how it ought to be for a monk."
A monk asked Chan Master Xing of Dajian Mountain in Anzhou, "The way is lost and I am bewildered; I pray the Master will point directly. The Master said, "Go forward through the three gates.
The monk asked, "I take a step toward the precipice; I pray the Master will point out the moon. The Master said, "I do not point out the moon.

The monk asked, "Why do you not point out the moon? The Master said, "When one is at the edge of a pit, one does not push others over. The monk asked, "Transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations—I pray [the Master to speak]."
The Master said, "In the treasury of our King, there is no such sword. Question: "When the successive gates and locks are closed and communication is cut off, what then?
The Master said, "How could you have reached this point? Question: "Once you have reached it, what then?
The Master said, "What is the situation over there? Question: "What is the truth within the truth? The Master said, "The clay Buddha at the crossroads."
The disciple asked, "As for the person of non-action and non-activity, they are still difficult to reach even with a golden chain; though pulled by the golden chain, they cannot be restrained.
What kind of person is this? The Master said, "It would be fine to tell you, O *dānapati*, but you must not let Mount Da'an fall into neglect."
Chan Master Baizhang Chao of Hongzhou was a native of Haidong. A monk asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the teachings the same or different?
The Master said, "The golden rooster and jade hare listen as they circle Mount Sumeru. The monk asked, "When the sun sets behind the western mountains, what is the state of affairs within the forest?
The Master said, "The cave is deep, so the clouds emerge late; the streambed is winding, so the water flows slowly. The monk asked, "I take my leave today..."
"Go. Suppose someone asks the Master, 'What Dharma are you teaching? What would you say to him? The Master said, "Just say:
'On the summit of Mount Daxiong, a tiger gives birth to a lion cub.'"
A monk asked the Master of Tianwang Monastery in Hongzhou, “Who is it that brandishes a sword within the realm? The Master said, “Tianwang.

The monk asked, “When the hundred limbs have all decayed and scattered, what is the one thing that remains eternally numinous? What is it like then? The Master said, “It does not fall into non-existence nor into decay.
The monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Wrong question. The monk asked, “What is the formless Dharma-hall? The Master said, “The gate.”
The outer perimeter is lined with vajras.
Chan Master Yun of Zhengqin Monastery in Changzhou was the son of the Han family of Weifu. He entered the monastic life in his youth; even in old age, he possessed the complexion of a child.
A monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? What is the nature of this ancestral wind? The Master replied: "It stands far beyond the *xiaoshao* music."
"How can the six musical scales surpass it? [The Master] asked, "What about that matter which cannot be surpassed? The Master said, "Before the sound, the beat does not disperse;
after the phrase, no trace can be found. [The monk] asked, "What is the single path of right effort? The Master said, "The mud is three feet deep. [The monk] asked, "How does one reach it?
The Master said, "From where have you come, O *śrāmaṇera*? [The monk] asked, "What is Chan? The Master said:
"A lotus flower atop a stone; a spring within fire. [A monk] asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "A single blade of grass on the peak of Laṅkā Mountain.
[The monk] asked, "How far apart are Chan and the Way? The Master said, "An earthen man falls into the water, and a wooden man retrieves him.

He passed away in the Tianfu era of the Jin dynasty. He was buried beside the monastery. After two years, his disciples opened the stupa and beheld his entire body, which remained perfectly intact, including his hair.
His fingernails were all long; he was then cremated, his śarīra relics and true bones were collected, and a new stupa was erected.
A monk asked Chan Master Rui of Dongshan in Xiangzhou, "When the Way is both existent and non-existent, what is it like?
The Master said, "A dragon's head and a snake's tail; a sword at the waist. The monk asked, "What is the song of non-arising? The Master said, "Before you have even asked."
A monk asked the Third Patriarch of Jingzhao Prefecture, “What is the seamless stupa? The Master said, “One cannot find a seam. The monk asked, “Who is the person within the stupa?
The Master said, “Facing each other, we do not see one another. The monk asked, “What is the meaning of the West?
The Master said, “The snow covers the solitary peak white; the fading light reveals the flaws.”
Chan Master Guangde Yan of Mount Wanguo in Xiangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Qinglin Qian. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Before the mountain, people do not stay; behind the mountain, people are even busier. The monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master...
[The monk] said, "I lack the strength to climb mountains or wade through waters; my thatched door is cut off from those who understand. He asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "First I lamented the falling leaves; now I see the willow branches turning green. He asked, "The entire earth is a single corpse; where shall it be buried?
The Master said, "Under Mount Beimang, there are thousands of mounds and ten thousand hills. The Master was unwell. A monk asked, "Master... [The text ends here.]
"What is there to worry about? The Master said, "That which cannot fall even when not thought of. The monk said, "If that is so, then I already know the source of the Master's ailment.
The Master asked, "What do you say the old monk is suffering from? The monk replied, "The Master should avoid certain foods. The Master then struck him. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "When the gate of the painted halberds opens, one sees the falling immortal. Later, the monk asked Wugong about this.
"The painted戟 (jì) gate opens and a falling immortal is seen. What is the meaning of this? Kōng said, "Even if one were to see Śākyamuni in person, the wise would all say he is not the Buddha."
Chan Master Xianyun of Shimen in Xiangzhou was a native of Jingzhao. Initially, he asked Qinglin, "How should one apply the mind to become equal to the various sages?
Qinglin looked up for a long while and said, "Do you understand? The Master replied, "I do not understand. Qinglin said, "Go."
Wuzi was focused on his practice when he paid obeisance to the Master and attained realization. He no longer traveled elsewhere but remained as a garden supervisor.
One day, while returning to stand in attendance, Lin asked, "What have you been doing today? The Master replied, "I have been planting vegetables.
Lin asked, "The entire world is the Buddha-body; where do you plant them? The Master replied, "With a golden hoe, I move not a speck of earth; the numinous sprouts—"
Lin was delighted that [the tree] had grown in its place. On the following day, he entered the garden and called out, "Master Yun! The Master responded.
Lin said, "I have planted an extra tree without a shadow, to leave for later generations to behold. The Master said, "If it is a tree without a shadow, how could it ever be planted?"
Lin said, "The planting has not yet taken root; stop for a moment. Have you ever seen its branches and leaves? The Master said, "I have never seen them.
Lin said, "Since you have never seen them, how do you know they have not yet taken root? The Master said, "Precisely because I have never seen them, they have not taken root.
Lin said, "So it is, so it is. When Lin was about to pass into parinirvāṇa, he called to the Master. The Master responded, "Yes. Lin said, "The sun..."
After turning the back to the western mountain, he need not settle haphazardly. The Master said, "Snow fills the golden sandalwood trees; the numinous branches are in spring for all eternity.
Lin asked, "If someone were to ask you about the matter of the golden needle and silk bag, what would you say?
The Master replied, "If it were something like feathers and fur, I would certainly never dare to act rashly. Initially, he resided at a hermitage on Mount Nanyue. [He had] not yet...
When Ji Qian was traveling through Tanzhou on his way to Jia Shan, the Prince of Chu, the Ma family, came out of the city to welcome him.

He immediately asked, "What is the Great Way of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied, "Good brother! Your Imperial carriage with its six dragons is a rare excellence for a thousand ages."

Processions lined the Jade Street as they emerged from the Golden Gate. The King was greatly pleased and invited him into the Tianche (Celestial Register) Palace to provide offerings for several days before he finally arrived at Jia Mountain to open the hall.
A monk asked, "How does this assembly today differ from that on Vulture Peak? The Master said, "The heavens drape jeweled canopies, layer upon layer;
the earth wells up golden lotuses, petal by petal, ever new. The monk asked, "I wonder what Dharma you will use to instruct people? The Master—
[The monk] said: "The melody of the stringless zither flows through the realms of sand; its pure tones universally respond to the capacities of the great thousandfold world-system.

I ask the Master: whose song do you sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed? The Master said: "Once the notes of the *gong* and *shang* scales are played upon the strings, it takes a blue-eyed barbarian to discern the treasure.
[The monk] said: "If that is so, then the clear stream divides beneath the cave, and the full moon shines upon the green forest. The Master said: "..."
The meaning of the portion [of the teaching] before the Many Sons Stūpa has, until now, transmitted its great resonance across different eras.
Question: "What is the true master of Jia Shan? The Master said: "A skilled hand must know that Luan Bu acted; Han Guang’s claims of merit are but empty delusion.
Question: "What is the meaning of the West? The Master said: "The jade seal never leaves the hands of the Son of Heaven; how could the golden casket be permitted to outsiders?"
[The monk] said, “I understand. He asked, “Without falling into the trap of the mechanism, I request that the Master speak directly.

The Master said, “The clear moon and swift trigger are beyond compare. How many people have you questioned thus far? The monk replied, “I am questioning the Master right now. The Master said, “Good brother!

When the clouds part, there is no need to hide the nine-tailed fox. I grant you the remainder of your life; return quickly to your grave. Because the barbarians were in rebellion, the Master subsequently departed from Jia.
Shan arrived at Xiangzhou and founded Shimen Temple, once again reviving the profound tradition of the Dharma. He ascended the hall and said:
"Upon the lapis lazuli palace, radiance shines daily without partiality; amidst the mountains of the seven treasures, brilliance dazzles with every step. The mud ox sets forth its stride."
The wooden horse neighs; the village elders sing and chant. Woodsmen wave their sleeves on the road of the great sun.
Ancient melodies and profound sounds meet beneath the trees—what more is there to do? A monk asked, "When the moon rises above the clouds, what is it like?
The Master said, "Three children embrace a flower drum. Good brother, do not come to block my path to the ball court. The monk asked, "What is [the meaning of] 'How is it'?"
"The style of our Master's house. The Master said: "Constantly riding a fine steed up the high tower, the iron whip points the way for all the Hu people.
[The monk] asked: "What is the realm of Shimen? The Master said: "Throughout the entire world, the golden color is of one hue;

the wandering travelers have ceased their pursuit. [The monk] asked: "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said: "Formless, they do not dwell in the ranks of ordinary beings or sages. (From the *Jingde Chuandeng Lu*)

When practicing the bird-path, there is no trace left behind. [A monk] asked: "What is it like when a fierce tiger stands before one's screen? The Master said: "Life and nature do not exist. [The monk] said: "In that case, one meets his deadly paw.
The Master said: "He bites and chews you right away. [The monk] asked: "What is it to be among those in the Pure Land? The Master said: "Wearing fur, they roam amidst the gathering flames;
wearing horns, they mingle with the dust and mud. [The monk] asked: "How is it that the realm of the Way has no boundaries? The Master said: [The same as above].
"How is it when the entire body is free from a single trace? The Master said, "Vast white clouds spread over the snowy peaks; turn back onto the dark path without delay.
[The student] asked, "I do not yet understand; where does the path of turning back lie? The Master said, "Observe clearly as the stone man raises his hand;
look at the withered bones of ten thousand years as they laugh. [The student] asked, "How is it when there is no movement from the state of suchness (*tathatā*)? The Master said:
"What end will there ever be? [The monk] asked, "How is it so? The Master said, "The stone door has no lock; the Prajñā Temple was consumed by fire.
Someone asked, "Since it is Prajñā (Wisdom), why was it burned by fire? The Master said, "A single iron bar stretching ten thousand miles.
The Master often responded to situations by saying, "Good brother," and thus he was known at the time as Brother Monk (Dage Heshang).
A monk asked Chan Master Longguang Yin of Shaoyou, "What is it like when the Human King and the Dharma King meet?
The Master said, "The King of Yue once brandished his sword; not a single word of Longguang has ever been deficient. He ascended the hall, and after a long silence, said:
"No need for further trouble. Take care. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "When the barbarian wind fans out, the Han land establishes its regulations.
A monk asked, "What is it like when one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha? The Master clapped his hands and looked around. A monk asked, "What is the single phrase of Longguang?
The Master said, "Amoghapāśa. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Oṃ. A monk asked, "What is it? The Master said, [as before].
[The monk asked: "This is the ultimate point for a person. The Master said, "I earnestly entrust this to those who come after.

[The monk] asked, "Why does Piṇḍola alone go to receive offerings from the four continents? The Master said, "A single moon is reflected in a thousand rivers; ten thousand households all encounter spring."
Thereupon, a verse was spoken: Upon the peak of Dragon Light Mountain is the precious lunar orb; It illuminates heaven and earth, piercing through the dark clouds.
The Venerable One does not shift from his original singular substance; A thousand households reflect his image, ten thousand households enjoy the springtime.
A monk asked Baizhao of Yingzhou, “How should one apply the mind throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said, “Gathering and spreading it all in a single wooden basin.
The monk asked, “What is the Way? The Master said, “Sometimes three across; sometimes five vertically. The monk asked, “What is one who is on the Way?
The Master said, “Ceasing to raise the clouds of faith; at midnight, the great sun shines.”
A monk asked Chan Master Huiju of Shizang in Dingzhou, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?
The Master said, "The trees bear the color of the Canglang River; the mountains stretch across as a single stroke of green. The monk asked, "What is the monastery? The Master said, "Just this.
The monk asked, "Who is within the monastery? The Master said, "What? What? The monk asked, "If a guest were to suddenly arrive, what would you do?"
He waited for him. The Master said, "Go and drink tea.
Chan Master Zhongyun Zhihui of Jingzhao Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Ren of Baishui. Born into the Gao clan of Xianqin, he enjoyed wandering about since his childhood.
At the age of thirteen, he resolved to leave the household life. His parents could not dissuade him, so he paid homage to Chan Master Wen of Guifeng for his tonsure.

Later, he visited Baishui, where he alone grasped the subtle words and secretly mastered the secret keys [of the Dharma]. He subsequently returned to Luo, selecting Zhongtan as his site to establish the Wenshi Monastery.
He made it his constant practice to provide water and administer medicine; once, there was a bhikṣu afflicted with white leprosy whom everyone loathed, yet only the Master [remained by his side].
He rubbed and washed it as usual. Suddenly, there was divine light and an extraordinary fragrance. Shortly thereafter, he marveled at this, and the object had vanished.
The scab from the wound remained, its scent pungent and intense; he gathered them together and fashioned a statue of Avalokiteśvara to enshrine them.

Later, the Master suddenly desired to return to his former residence at Mount Guifeng in Zhongnan. One day, while walking leisurely among the crags and ravines, he lay down to rest as he usually did. Suddenly—
He beheld a *dūṣya* robe, a rosary, a bronze water-pitcher, and a *tāla*-leaf umbrella; upon touching them, they immediately crumbled.
He said to his attendant, "These were the ritual implements from my previous life. I shall establish a temple here to repay my past causes.

While he was clearing away the weeds, auspicious clouds shrouded the sun and gathered atop the peak, lingering there without dispersing for a long time. Consequently, it was named Mount Chongyun (Heavy Clouds). Ferocious beasts all withdrew of their own accord.

He departed and blocked the dragon pond to open a path; the dragon also moved elsewhere. Later, Emperor Mingzong of the Later Tang bestowed upon it the name Changxing. Disciples gathered there in great numbers.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is it like to return to the root and attain the essential meaning? The Master said, "Already forgotten, not even remembering the arising of dust.
The monk asked, "What is it like to follow illumination and lose the source? The Master said, "The home has been plundered by bandits."
Question: "Dust does not arise from recollection; what is the single path for advancing the person? The Master said: "Grass has already grown beneath your feet;
ahead lies a pit ten thousand fathoms deep. Question: "The main road is level and smooth; how should one tread upon it? The Master said:

"If I were to point it out to you, you would go off toward the east, west, south, or north. Question: "What is the scale of the heavy clouds? The Master said: "Subject it to the scrutiny of the whole world as you will."
Question: What are words that cut through iron? The Master said: "Better to die than to transgress. Question:
What is the matter that Kāśyapa heard directly? The Master said: "Heavy clouds—I cannot remember. Question: What is the realm of Chongyun? The Master said: [Silence].
In the four seasons, flowers cluster thickly; throughout the three winters, the exotic grasses remain green. The Master propagated the Dharma for over forty years.

When he was a commoner, the Military Commissioner Wang Yanchao often accompanied the Master on his travels and wished to become a śramaṇa. The Master gazed at him intently and said, "Your worldly karmic ties are deep;
you shall serve as the protective wall for my household. Later, Lord Wang indeed governed Yongxing and performed the rites of a disciple toward the Master. The Master was about to...

In accordance with worldly custom, he first took his leave of the prince and entrusted him with the protection of the Dharma-gate. The prince wept and said, "Can you truly bear to abandon your disciple?
The Master smiled and said, "Even for a thousand years, this shall be but a single parting. Upon returning, he wrote a verse to show the assembly, saying:
"I have a small hut, Built for me by my parents. I have lived in it for eighty years; Recently, I have noticed its decay. [The text continues: "It is time..."
He intended to move elsewhere, as the matter involved attachment and aversion; he waited until the other [structure] was demolished so that there would be no obstruction for either party.
He then passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture, and his stupa was erected at his original mountain site.
Chan Master Youzhang of Ruilong Monastery in Hangzhou was the younger nephew of the Tang Prime Minister Xiahou Zhi.

At the beginning of the Dazhong era, when his uncle, the Grand Master of Works (Sikong), was stationed as governor in Guangling, the Master was only seven years old. While visiting Huizhao Temple, he heard the recitation of the *Lotus Sūtra* and resolved to seek ordination.
His uncle initially did not grant permission, but because the Master ceased eating and drinking, his uncle had no choice but to [comply].
He granted his request. Master Huìyuǎn later traveled to various Chan assemblies at Shùshān and Báishuǐ, where he received the essential instructions on the mind from all of them.
In the thirteenth year of the Xiántōng era, he arrived in Jiānglíng. The Venerable Téngtēng instructed him, saying, "Go to Tiantái and seek a place of stillness to dwell;
when you meet Ān, stop there. Later, he encountered the Venerable Hánhánhé, who patted him and said, "You..."
"Forty years hence, there will be a Bodhisattva-King under Mount Jingshan who shall rule over Jiangnan; at that time, my Way shall flourish.
Subsequently, he arrived at Mount Tiantai and founded Fudang Monastery in Jing’an Township, thereby fulfilling the words of "leaping and soaring.
He later resided at Yilong Monastery. In the fourth year of the Zhonghe era, when famine and pestilence ravaged the region of Zhedong, the Master [was in] Wenzhou, Taizhou, and Mingzhou.

He collected and buried the remains of three prefectures; at that time, he was called the Great Being of Profound Sorrow (Beizeng Dashi). Xuefeng once went to visit him and departed leaving behind his *tāla*-leaf whisk.
In the third year of the Tiānyòu era, Qián Shàngfù dispatched the envoy Tóngjiàn to bring clothing, incense, and medicinal herbs into the mountains to invite him to the provincial court.
He was appointed as the Grand Master Zhìdé and lodged in the Hall of Meritorious Ministers, where [the Governor] attended upon him daily.

He was asked about the Dharma and invited by the Master [the King] to establish a *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* (Golden Light) ritual site on Mount Tiantai every year, holding a great assembly of both clergy and laity from all districts that lasted over a month before dispersing. (The Great Assembly of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* originated with this Master.

As he was about to take his leave and return to the mountains, the King felt such deep affection and longing that he established Rui Long Monastery in the capital city (later renamed Bao Shan Monastery by Emperor Wenmu) and invited him to propagate the Dharma there. At that time, the Chan school was flourishing; thus it was:
"Hanhan’s prediction has indeed come to pass. He ascended the hall and said: "In years past, this old monk traveled abroad through Jiangwai, Lingnan, Jing, and Hu.
There was no monastery with a master of renown where I did not go to inquire and seek instruction. This was solely for the sake of gathering together with you all today."

Each must know this destination. Yet, throughout all quarters, there is ultimately no divergent teaching; it simply instructs the person themselves to bring their frantic mind to rest and cease seeking from others.
One merely follows conditions while abiding in reality, yet there is no reality to be so abided in. One makes use of things according to the occasion, yet there is no occasion that can be used.
Even if compassion were shown through bitter words, one still cannot call day night; even with further skillful means, it remains thus.
In the end, one cannot point east and call it west. Were one able to do so, that would merely be a supernatural feat of sorcery; it would have nothing to do with me.
As for those who merely parrot words, who fail to reflect upon themselves and recognize their error, they are simply attempting to pluck flowers from the sky.
"Can you take the moon out of the waves and put it back on? You must each now withdraw and reflect for a moment.
Only when you suddenly agree will you know that this old fellow Rui-long had no choice but to go to such great lengths.
Do you agree? At that time, a monk asked, "What is the realm of Rui-long? The Master said, "Do you not see it? The monk asked, "What is the realm?"

Another monk asked, "What is the sword of Xinwu? The Master made the gesture of drawing a sword.
A monk asked Master Shijing of Chenzhou, a successor of Chan Master Tong’an Wei, “Before the stone mirror has been polished, does it still reflect?
The Master said, “The previous life is the cause; the present life is the fruit.”
Chan Master Guoyin Zhiyan of Xiangzhou, a successor in the eighth generation under Qingyuan, was a native of Dengzhou. A monk asked: "Whose lineage does the Master chant?"
[The Master] sang: "Whose lineage of the school’s style do you inherit? The Master said: "White clouds to the south; a ceremonial parasol to the north. [A monk] asked:

"What is that matter which Kāśyapa heard directly? The Master said: "You must spit it out immediately. [Another] asked: "What is the place where all Buddhas cannot shine their light? The Master said: "..."
The Master said, "Why do you ask about this mountain-demon's cave? [The student] asked, "After one has been illuminated by it, what then? The Master said, "Hush! You little fiend!
[The student] asked, "How does one ascend through a thousand mountains and ten thousand waters? The Master said, "With every step, it is a thousand miles and ten thousand miles.
[The student] asked, "What is it like when one does not take a step? The Master said, "It is also a thousand miles and ten thousand miles."
A monk asked Chan Master Faxian of Puning Monastery in Xiangzhou, "We have lived together through past kalpas;
why do you not recognize who is close and who is distant? The Master said, "Who? The monk said, "Wait for me to say it. The Master said, "I thought you did not understand my words.

Another asked, "How does one ascend through a thousand mountains and ten thousand waters? The Master said, "The path in the blue sky has no gaps; those who reach it do not lose their functional responsiveness."

Chan Master Yuan Guan of Liangshan in Dingzhou was a successor of Chan Master Zhixian of Tong’an. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "The waters of Yiyang are swift, so the fish move with difficulty;
the pines of Bailu are tall, so the birds find it hard to perch. [The monk] asked, "When the household thief is difficult to guard against... at that moment...

"What? the Master asked. [The monk] said, "If one recognizes it, it does not become an enemy. The Master asked, "After recognizing it, what then? The Master said, "It is banished to the realm of non-arising.
[The monk] asked, "Is that not where one establishes one's dwelling and sustains one's life? The Master said, "A stagnant pool does not harbor dragons."
[The monk] asked, "What is the living water dragon? The Master said, "It stirs up waves but does not create billows.

[The monk] asked, "What is it like when suddenly the abysses are overturned and the mountains topple? The Master descended from his seat, seized him, and said, "Do not let it dampen the corner of this old monk’s *kāṣāya*.
[The monk] asked, "Whose song do you sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed? The Master said, "Dragons beget dragon cubs; phoenixes beget phoenix chicks."
Question: "What is the meaning of coming from the West? The Master said: "The Onion Range does not transmit the seal of the Tang lands;
the barbarian sings a song of peace in vain. Question: "What is the matter transmitted from of old? The Master said: "The barbarian monk crossing the water has no knee-breeches;
he carries Buddhist scriptures on his back but does not recite the sutras. Question: "What is the Eye of the True Dharma? The Master said: "Nanhua."
Li asked, "Why are you inside Nanhua? The Master said, "It is because you ask about the True Dharma Eye. Li asked, "What is the student's own self?
The Master said, "The Son of Heaven within the realm; the General beyond the borders. Li asked, "What is it like when one goes forth in this very manner?
The Master said, "The bright moon hangs in the sky; sitting in darkness within the room. Li asked, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? The Master said, [as before].

The Master said, "Secret. Once, while the Master was seated with Elder Rui, a monk asked, "Since two Honored Ones do not manifest their teachings simultaneously, why do you two both occupy the abbot’s quarters?
The Master said, "Even one does not exist. He added a verse: A single melody from Liangshan— A person outside the patterns finds it hard to harmonize.
For ten years I have sought a true friend, Yet never once have I met one. [The monk] asked, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go?"
[The Master] said, "Where did the deceased monk pass away? [The monk] replied, "How can one avoid having to escort him? The Master said, "A strand of silk thread upon the flames of a red furnace;
amidst the gathering clouds, it does not nod its head. He ascended the hall and said: "I cast my hook across the four seas only to catch the fierce dragon;
beyond the ordinary, this mysterious mechanism is for seeking those who understand. He ascended the hall and said: "The line hangs a thousand feet down; the intent lies in the deep pool."
A single phrase cuts across the void; white clouds are naturally distinct. A solitary boat with a lone oar does not disturb the clear waves.

Sailing freely across the sea, one rarely encounters a clear mirror. When asked, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? the Master said, "None of the sages can manifest it. Later, the Master revealed this verse:
"The red flames conceal my body; why need a new stupa? If someone truly recognizes its worth, it lies within the ashes."
Miaoquan Zhen.

Chan Master Changjue of Pujing Monastery in the Eastern Capital, a descendant of the lineage of Chan Master Guizong, was a native of the Li family from Chenliu. Initially, he visited Guizong and heard the Dharma.

He attained awakening and subsequently sought ordination. Not long after, Guizong was about to pass away; he summoned the Master and stroked his head, saying, "You have a karmic affinity with the Dharma.
In the future, you shall deliver the masses, and no one will be able to fathom your capacity. He then entrusted the matter of the Master’s tonsure to his other disciples.
In the second year of the Qianhua era of the Tang dynasty, the Master shaved his hair. The following year, he received the full precepts at Donglin Temple from Gan...
At the Lutan (Exposure Altar), he traveled to Mount Wutai and subsequently returned to the capital. He resided alone outside the Lijing Gate for two years. There was a lay devotee named Mr.
Zhang living to the north who invited the Master to receive his offerings. Mr. Zhang had long investigated the profound principles of the Dharma and thus sought the Master’s instruction.
The Master then provided guidance according to his needs, and Zhang attained realization upon hearing these words. He prepared a mat for the Master to stay overnight. When [the time came]...
Late at night, he and his wife secretly peered inside. They saw the Master’s body filling the entire bed, with both head and feet protruding.

When they ordered their maidservants and servants to look, however, everything appeared as it normally did. Struck with even greater reverence and admiration, they said, "We, your disciples, are advanced in years.

We now wish to offer the front hall of our residence to supplement your meditation chamber. The Master joyfully accepted it. This continued until the third year of the Tiānchéng era of the Later Táng dynasty.

It was thus established as a large monastery, and the imperial plaque was bestowed with the name Pujing (Universal Purity). The Master considered that because the capacity of the times was shallow and obscure, it would be difficult to sustain the ultimate teachings.

He feared that if he were to initiate [the transmission] to those who were not suitable vessels, it would cause them to incur the blame of slander and censure; therefore, he would rather not strive to open the Dharma.

Every month on the third, eighth, and eighteenth days, he provided ritual bathing for tens of thousands of monks and practitioners. The Master once said to his disciples: "If only the gate of wisdom remains unobstructed, then..."

How could merit be obstructed? One day, Secretariat Drafter Tao Gu entered the monastery to pay his respects and asked, "The scriptures state that when one is detached from all marks, one is called a Buddha.
Yet, right before our eyes, all manner of marks are in full disarray; how can one become detached from them? The Master replied, "Drafter, what do you see?
Tao was delighted and held him in high esteem. From then on, kings, dukes, and great officials recommended him repeatedly.
He declined all honors regarding ceremonial robes and titles. On the second day of the twelfth month in the fourth year of the Kaibō era, he manifested illness.
On the eleventh day, having finished his final instructions to the assembly, he passed away reclining on his right side.
Chan Master Defu of Yunding in Huainan was a dharma successor of Chan Master Huguo. When he first visited Huguo, he asked: "The direct source of the root is what the Buddhas have certified;
picking leaves and seeking branches is not for me. What is the case at such a time? Huguo replied: "Ceasing the climbing of the cloud-trees for three autumns."
"Indeed! Desist from playing with the solitary moon-disk in the azure pool. Thereupon, the Master suddenly resolved his doubts.
Later, while residing there, the Governor of Chengdu requested him to ascend the seat at the provincial office. A military officer from the music corps came forward to pay his respects;

as he rose, he looked back toward the mounting platform and said, "I do not ask about 'sucking dry the waters of the West River'—I ask you instead, Master, to swallow this mounting platform before my feet! The Master spread his arms wide.
He raised his hand and said, "Wipe it clean and bring it here. The attendant was suddenly enlightened.
A monk asked Master Shimen Cong of Xiangzhou, the Dharma heir of Chan Master Dayang Jian, "After Dayang has passed away, where has he gone? The Master replied:
Riding an ox without wearing a hat; sitting upright without walking crookedly.
A monk asked Chan Master Qianian of Beichen in Tanzhou, "What is the source of the Great Way? The Master said, "The myriad streams cannot mix it.
The monk asked, "How is it when one is uniquely liberated? The Master said, "Piercing clouds and penetrating rocks. [The monk] asked, "What is..."
"Not falling into the clichés of the ancients or the present. The Master said: "The fifteenth and sixteenth days of the month—the moon follows the moon.
Chan Master Shimen Shaoyuan of Xiangzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Shimen Cheshi. Initially, while Shaoyuan was serving as a field overseer at Shimen, Shimen asked him: "What is..."
[The Master] said, "A water buffalo at the edge of the field: its horns turn and thunder through heaven and earth; where the morning sun shines, there is spring everywhere.
On another day, the Gatekeeper asked again, "Is the water buffalo well? The Master said, "It has never lacked grass and water.

[The Gatekeeper] asked, "What about the work in the fields? The Master said, "Deep plowing and shallow sowing. [The Gatekeeper] said, "Is it done according to the Dharma? The Master said, "I have never acted with negligence."
While [Zhaozhou] was staying there, a monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he succeed? The Master said:
"Throughout the ten directions there is no divergent path; it surpasses Fenglin. The monk asked: "The former master has already returned to the Wild Goose Pagoda;

please, Master, proclaim the single phrase for Dangyang. The Master said: "A *asura* holds the sun and moon in his palms; a *yakṣa* treads upon a mud-dragon with his feet. The monk asked: "The Golden Dragon..."
He did not exhale the mists of the mundane world; I pray that the Master will raise the phoenix-like pivot of his teaching. The Master said: "The white-browed one does not extend his hand;
the road to Chang’an is level and plain. Question: "What is the meaning of the Westward Coming? The Master said: "A cloth bag containing a tortoise.
Question: "What is the realm of Shimen? The Master said: "A solitary peak facing Fengling. Question: "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said: [He]... (text breaks off)

[The student] said, "In the mountain crags, the remaining snow reflects light everywhere. He asked, "What is the Master’s secret functioning? The Master said, "Dripping water is not the essential point;
throughout the thousand mountains, he reveals no body. He asked, "When [disciples] come from the four quarters and eight directions, how do you respond?
The Master said, "A barefoot Persian sniffs at the sky. He asked, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? The Master said:
Ashes fly and smoke vanish; bleached bones reach to the heavens. While the Master was applying moxibustion to a sick monk, the monk asked, "What is it like at such a time?
The Master said, "The single thread of penetrating mystery is much like a shooting star. [Later] he asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddha?"
The Master said, "A white ox lies exposed on the ground by the green stream. Question: "How can one cross the river of birth and death?
The Master said, "The wind blows the lotus leaves and the duckweed. Question: "What is the single phrase transmitted outside the teachings?
The Master said, "A goat-headed cart enters Chang'an. Question: "How can one speak of the Way amidst the waves of birth and death? The Master said, "A fur bag hangs across."
His body was free from the need for food or drink; he would often lie in the blue stream under the spring sun. A monk asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "The mountains are deep and the waters are cold. The monk asked, "What is one who walks the Way? The Master said, "A golden mallet strikes a golden drum.

A monk asked, "When the sky is overcast and the sun does not appear, where has its radiance gone? The Master said, "An iron snake lies across the great road, its entire body black as smoke. A monk asked, "... [The text ends here].
"What is one phrase from within the Dharma-lineage? The Master said: "The spark of stone burns the mountain at night; the great earth joins its palms in unison. He asked:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "A stone ox blocks the ancient road; a wooden horse gallops atop the high tower."
A monk asked Chan Master Huigan of Beichen in Tanzhou, "What is the phrase by which all the sages benefit beings?
The Master said, "The red wheel faces ten thousand households; its light illuminates, yet it is fundamentally without mind. The monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing?
The Master said, "The stone door leaves no trace of intent. Dongxuan Tongmiao asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "One foot short, one inch long."
A monk asked Chan Master Shouzhen of Lingzhu in Ezhou, “What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, “The mendicant’s staff bears the snows of the barbarian heavens;
the almsbowl fills with the springs of the Han lands. A monk asked, “When neither delusion nor awakening enters into any state, what then? The Master said:
"Where do objects come from? He replied, "If that is so, then all objects have departed. The Master said, "A fellow who has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake.
Zen Master Jin of Mount Shimian in Shuzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The character for 'king' (王) without the dot.
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The dot. He was asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said:

The mountains are cold and the waters are frigid. The Master has a verse on his hanging staff which says: "A single staff extends in all four directions; it serves as the test for dragons and elephants.
When their heads and horns slightly rise or fall, a flash of lightning strikes upon their backs."
A monk asked Chan Master Yiqin of Chengtian in Jiazhou, "What is the realm of Chengtian? The Master said, "Two rivers hem in a blind fellow;
a range of mountains hides a barefoot barbarian. The monk asked, "What are words of ultimate truth?"
The Master said, "The scholar’s cap is black.
A monk asked Zen Master Yicheng of Qingfeng in Fengxiang Prefecture, "The non-arising of the three periods of time—of what person is this the realm?
The Master said, "White clouds join the snow-capped peaks; the bright moon blends with the fishhook. The monk asked, "I wonder if there is yet something further beyond this?"
[The monk] said, "There is not. The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter that goes beyond? The Master said, "The numinous light pierces through the color of lapis lazuli;
when the great earth becomes bright, it is free from even a trace of a spot. He asked, "What is the house style of Qingfeng? The Master said, "Facing the fire, eating sweet melons."
A monk asked Chan Master Zhidu of Guangde Mountain in Xiangzhou, "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "He put on his robes and ate his meals. The monk asked, "What was it like after he saw him? The Master said, "He put on his robes and ate his meals.
The monk asked, "What is Guangde Mountain? The Master said, "Flowers bloom easily in the sun; snow melts with difficulty in the shade. The monk asked, "What is..."
A man among the mountain people. The Master said: "If the morning mist does not emerge from the gate, the evening glow travels a thousand li.
The Head Seat Jūn was a native of Taiyuan; he had been at Shimen for over thirty years, and the monastic communities admired him.
Once, while a monk was invited for tea, he asked, "What is the one stroke by which the Head Seat acts for others?
The Master said, "I still remember it from just now. The monk asked, "And how about right now? The Master said, "Serve some good tea.
One day, as he entered the garden carrying a hoe, a monk asked, "Among the three bodies, which one goes to perform manual labor? The Master stood with his hoe propped up. The monk...
He said, "There is no such thing as 'just so'. Master [Xuefeng] took up his hoe and departed.
He was the Dharma heir of Chan Master Yanyuan of Guyin, the ninth generation descendant of Qingyuan.
A monk asked Chan Master Qichong of Guyin in Xiangzhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The barbarian wears a fur cloak; the foreigner puts it on. The monk said, "I do not understand. What is the principle here?
The Master said, "The deaf man leans his ear; the mute man sings."

Chan Master Jingxuan of Dayang Mountain in Yingzhou was a successor of Chan Master Liangshan Guan. He was the son of the Zhang family of Jiangxia; he left home to become a monk under Chan Master Zhitong.

At nineteen, he received full ordination as a bhikṣu. Having heard the definitive meaning of the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* (the *Yuanjue jing*), no one could surpass him in his lecture halls. He subsequently traveled to various regions to seek further instruction.
When he first arrived at Liangshan, he asked, "What is the formless site of enlightenment?
Liangshan pointed to Guanyin and said, "This was painted by the scholar Wu. As the Master was about to offer a reply, Liangshan hurriedly asked, "This one has form;
which one is formless? The Master then attained realization and prostrated himself. Liangshan said, "Why do you not utter a single phrase? The Master—
The Master said, "I would not refuse the Way, but I fear it would take up too much paper and ink. Shanshan smiled and said, "These words shall be inscribed upon a stele.
The Master offered this verse: "In my former days as a beginner, I studied the Way in delusion; I sought out knowledge across ten thousand waters and a thousand mountains.

Though I tried to discern the ancient from the present, I could never comprehend it; To speak directly of 'no-mind' only made my doubts increase further. Now, having been pointed out by the Master like the mirror of the Qin era, I behold my own father."
Before his mother had even given birth, what could he have attained that he now so clearly realizes? At night, he releases a black hen to fly off with the snow.

Yanshou claimed that the lineage of Dongshan was worthy of reliance, and for a time his reputation spread far and wide. After Yanshou passed away, he took leave of the stupa and traveled to Dayang to pay his respects to Chan Master Jian.
Jian yielded the seat to him, and he presided over it. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Dayang? The Master replied, "Emaciated."
Cranes age and old monkeys cry; the valley resonates with their calls. Lean pines and cold bamboos lock in the blue mist. [A monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person within this realm?
The Master said, "How so? How so? [The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s house style? The Master said, "A full jar cannot be poured out;

throughout the great earth, there is no hungry person. [The Master] ascended the hall and said: "Staggering ten thousand fathoms high, the bird-path is difficult to traverse; it is like a blade's edge or thin ice."

Who would dare to tread this path? The wondrous phrases of the *zong* (essence) vehicle are difficult to express through the pathways of speech; even Vimalakīrti fell silent at the Gate of Non-duality.
Therefore, when Bodhidharma came from the West, he sat facing the wall for nine years before finally meeting one who understood him.
Today, Dayang is also most unaccountably bold. Take care! Question: "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said: "Red dust at the bottom of the great ocean."
Water began to flow horizontally from atop the summit of Mount Sumeru. The Master asked, "Monk, where have you come from? He replied, "From Hongshan. The Master said, "Is the late master still there?
He replied, "He is. The Master said, "His presence is not lacking; please ask him to come out so that I may meet him. The monk said, "What?
The Master said, "This one is merely an attendant. The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Go and drink tea. He then ascended the hall for the formal discourse.

All those with the virtues of dhyāna must clearly understand these three phrases: the phrase of ordinary non-arising, the phrase of wondrous mystery without partiality, and the phrase of essential clarity that is inexhaustible.
The first phrase penetrates a single path; the second phrase has no guest or host; the third phrase carries both together.
To speak the first phrase is for the lion to stretch and yawn; to speak the second phrase is for the lion to turn and leap back; to speak the third phrase is for the lion to roar.
Crouching on the ground: it is expansive, pervading the ten directions; it is seizing, cutting off everything at once.
At this very moment, how can you communicate a single message? If you cannot communicate a single message, tomorrow morning you shall present it to the King of Chu.
Question: "What is the ordinary phrase of non-arising? The Master said: "White clouds cover the green mountains; atop the green mountains—"

[The student] did not respond. [The Master] asked: "What is the phrase of wondrous mystery that is without partiality? The Master said: "In the jeweled palace, there is no one who does not stand in attendance;
if you do not plant the *wú-tóng* tree, the phoenix will have no reason to come. [The student] asked: "What is the phrase of the luminous essence that is inexhaustible?
The Master said: "When the hand points to the void, heaven and earth turn; returning to the path, the stone horse emerges from the gauze cage. [The student] asked: "What is the lion’s yawn?"
The Master said, "In the end, there is no intention to look back; how could one willingly fall into the ordinary? [The student] asked, "What is 'the lion’s backward leap'?
The Master said, "Moving to and fro, everything returns to the Father; though great functions arise in profusion, the essence remains undiminished.

[The student] asked, "What is 'the lion crouching on the ground'? The Master said, "Utterly transcending the mechanism of coming and going; throughout past and present, it never changes. [The student] asked, "What is..."
A person from Dadi asked, "The Master says that it cannot be categorized as being like empty space. [The monk] asked, "What is the pure *dharmakāya*?
The Master said, "A white ox vomiting snow-colored foam; a black horse with a black rooster on its back. He ascended the hall and said, "Letting go of the hand there, beyond the thousand sages."
In the ancestral hall, the roots and sprouts of Shao-shi grow long. A heron perching in a snow nest is still tolerable;
look further at the white horse entering the reeds. Entering the hall, he said: "At midnight, a black hen broods over a crane’s egg; when dawn breaks, a stork is born.

With feathers like a crane, a beak like a hawk, and a body like a heron, it yet keeps company with crows and ravens. It soars high into the misty heavens and flies low along the willow banks. Toward...
Returning late, he examined it closely; it was vaguely like a wild goose in the clouds. The Master once explained Cao Shan’s "Three Kinds of Falling":
"These three phrases must be understood through the transformation of positions before they can be mastered. First, 'becoming a water buffalo' is falling into the category."
The Master said: "This is the speech of a śramaṇa’s transformation-body; it is a matter among those of different species. If one does not understand this meaning, one will be obstructed.
It simply requires that one’s single thought be free from self-interest, and then there will be a way to emerge.
Second, 'not accepting food' is falling into nobility. The Master said: "You must know how to finish matters on that side before coming to this side to practice. If you do not [do so]..."
"This stage is precisely sitting in the state of honor. Third, not severing sound and form is 'following along and falling. The Master said:
'Because one does not understand sound and form, one falls wherever they arise. One must find a way to emerge from within sound and form. What is the phrase beyond sound and form?
He then said: 'Sound is not of itself sound; form is not of itself form. Therefore it is called 'not severing the pointing.'"
"Palms"—which palms does this refer to? The verse on the Five Ranks says: *Zheng zhong pian* (Deviation within the Center): A single wheel, pure and bright, is centered in the sky;
Its winding, void, and mysterious nature is not manifest. Light and darkness are complete only within its shadow. *Bian zhong zheng* (Center within Deviation):

Cease looking at the bright moon in the mirror of the Qin era; It is dimly present like a lamp beneath the sun. Light and darkness are blended together—who can distinguish the shadow? *Zheng zhong...* (Within the Center... [The text continues:]... *zheng zhong* (Center within the Center).
Come! The channels of the pulse are profound and mysterious, winding and turning back upon themselves. In silent illumination, there is no partiality; it manifests everywhere.

It is like traveling the path of birds, entering where the [fence] is opened. Reaching within the partial: every dharma is without dependence, which is itself wisdom. Lying across the body beyond all things, neither is harmed. Its wondrous function is profound and subtle, perfectly complete.
Reaching within the inclusive: the shared path meets the wind, yet there is no middle way. Do not cling to the cold crags.

The wild grasses turn green. Sitting amidst the white clouds, the essence of the school is not subtle. The Master’s spiritual countenance was extraordinary and magnificent, possessing a profound dignity.

From his childhood, he took only one meal per day. Considering the gravity of the transmission from the former masters, he did not step beyond the boundary of his dwelling, nor did his side ever touch the mat.
At the age of eighty, lamenting that there was no one to succeed him, he composed a verse and presented his leather sandals and cotton cassock.
He sent a messenger to Chan Master Yuan of Fushan to seek a vessel for the Dharma. The verse said: "The grass upon the peaks of Mount Yangguang— I entrust it to you to await its true value.
Where the extraordinary sprouts flourish most luxuriantly, The profound and secret roots of the spirit remain firm. At the end of the verse he wrote:

"One who attains the Dharma must remain hidden among the multitude for ten years before they may propagate it. Yuan bowed and accepted it, then praised the Master’s portrait, saying: "The black dog is rotten..."
Silver Hooves. Riding a white elephant from Mount Kunlun, he was unimpeded in these two realms; a wooden horse neighed amidst the flames.

On the nineteenth day of the seventh month in the fifth year of the Shengtian era, the Master ascended the seat to bid farewell to the assembly and entered nirvana. His stupa was erected at his native mountain.
A monk asked Chan Master Lian Shan Yan of Dingzhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Ginseng from Silla; *anggui* from Shu."
Master Liyu of Yaoshan in Lizhou ascended the hall and said: "The mountains, rivers, and great earth;
the sun, moon, and stars—these were born together with you, venerable ones. The Buddhas of the three periods of time—these have practiced together with you, venerable ones.
The holy teachings of the Tripiṭaka—these are contemporary with you, venerable ones. Can you believe this? If you can believe it, the iron ox of Shanfu will swallow you up."
Heaven and Earth. Although it is thus, one is obstructed by the Dharmakāya and cannot turn about;
you must know that there is a path for emerging from it. What is this path for the emergence of the venerable monks? Speak! Speak! After a long silence, he said:

"If you cannot speak, you will sink forever into the sea of suffering. Take care! A monk asked: "Regarding discourse beyond the categories, I beg the Master to grant us an instruction. The Master said:
"The essential Way is not difficult. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then even a ten-thousand-fathom blue abyss may allow for a single thread to hang down.
The Master said, "The assembly will laugh at you.
A monk from Mount Dezhen in Dingzhou asked, "I beg the Master to point out the place of intimacy. The Master said, "Old..."
Sengyuan was a native of Guangnan.

He was a disciple of Chan Master Daowu Qichuan of Tanzhou, who himself was a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Shimen Yuan. A monk asked him: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he inherit?"
The Master said, "The Phoenix Ridge is free from partiality; today it is transmitted throughout the world. [The monk] asked, "What is the realm of Daowu?
The Master said, "Rivulet flowers hold the jade dew; courtyard fruits fall upon the golden terrace. [The monk] asked, "Who is the person within that realm? The Master said:

Embracing the brazier, he donned his ancient patchwork robe; basking in the sun, he rested his head against the mountain root. [A monk] asked, "What was it like before the Fourth Patriarch saw Niutou?
The Master said, "A blue fly on a piece of jade. [The monk] asked, "What was it like after he saw him? The Master said, "Ice within the flames of a red furnace."
A monk asked Chan Master Jian of Mount Yunding in Huai’an Army: “Snow falling on a red furnace—please, Master, verify this for us.
The Master said, “The old woman is cooking porridge. The monk said, “What can be done about the present moment? The Master said, “You still find it too little.”
A monk asked Chan Master Guangji Fang of Dengzhou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Riding an ox chasing spring grass;

Regarding the meaning of his coming: the Master pointed to the cypress tree in front of the courtyard. The Official asked this three times, and the Master answered this three times.
The Official was delighted and composed a verse, saying: "Appearing and disappearing amidst the clouds, filling the vast void; The original true form has never had a single speck of dust.

When Chan Master Xianru of Mount Luofu in Huizhou first arrived at Dayang, Dayang asked, "Who are you? He replied, "A man from Yizhou.
Dayang asked, "How many li is it from here? He replied, "Five thousand li. Dayang said, "Coming as you have, have you ever trodden upon this ground?
He replied, "I have not trodden upon it. Dayang asked, "Are you able to fly through the air? He replied, "I am not able to fly."
Kongyang said, "How did you manage to reach this point? He replied, "Step by step, I am not lost in direction; throughout my entire being, there is no place for discrimination.
Yang said, "Have you attained the samādhi that transcends all quarters? He replied, "The Sage’s mind cannot be grasped; how could samādhi manifest a name?
Yang said, "So it is, so it is. You should believe this: the original substance is fully revealed, and principle and phenomena are non-dual. Be skillful in this for yourself."
[He] protected and maintained [the teachings]. Later, while staying there, a monk asked, "What is the realm of Luofu? The Master said, "Lofty, it reaches the limits of heaven;

When Chan Master Guixi of Baima in Xiangzhou first questioned Dayang, he said, "I am a dull-witted student;

At these words, the Master had an awakening. Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "A good dog."
[The Master] wore his name-tag. A monk asked, "What is it like when a tortoise hides its six limbs? The Master said, "An arrow and bow inside a cloth bag.

A monk asked, "If one does not seek in the Buddha and does not seek in the Dharma, where should one seek? The Master said, "A villager kneeling and prostrating before a stone lion. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "A vegetarian feast is being held beneath a village tree. Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "To walk hurriedly is to miss it; to walk slowly..."
They cannot catch up. There are countless great monks who are at their wits' end. One with many mouths and a glib tongue came forward, and a monk asked:

[The Master] said, "Do not clamor, do not clamor.
