"Facing him face-to-face, yet not a *śrāvaka*; with much sleep, there is an abundance of drowsy chatter. Ascending the hall, he said: "The nature of returning to the source is non-dual; the expedient means have many doors.
If you simply understand the nature of returning to the source, why worry about the gates of expedient means? Do you all wish to understand the nature of returning to the source? It is revealed."
He takes a pillar and makes it into a wooden ladle; bystanders are unwilling to comply with him. Do you wish to understand the gate of expedient means?
He takes a wooden ladle and makes it into a pillar; it is equally suitable for propping up heaven and supporting the earth. But tell me:
how do you speak that phrase which does not fall into the gate of expedient means? After thirty years, do not let it be cited incorrectly.
Chan Master Weizhao of Baofeng in Hongzhou, whose secular surname was Li, was a native of Jianzhou. From his youth, he was exceptionally transcendent and loathed the vulgar ways of the world.

One day, while being taught the *Analects*, he reached the passage: "By nature, human beings are nearly alike; by practice, they become far apart. He suddenly exclaimed, "The ordinary and the sage are fundamentally one body;

it is only due to habitual practice that they appear differentiated. I have understood this! Thereupon, he went to Chengdu and studied under Master Qingtai at Luyuan. At the age of... [text fragment ends].

At nineteen, he shaved his head, received the full precepts, and ascended to the status of a monk. Daoyi ordered him to listen to the *Awakening of Faith* (Dacheng qixin lun), but the Master immediately retired to lie down.

Daoyi questioned him about this. The Master said, "Since it is called 'right faith,' how can the Mahayana be fully understood through mere words? Thereupon, he set aside his mind and traveled to various regions.
He visited Furuong at Dahong. Once, while sitting in meditation at night, the gallery was suddenly shaken by wind and snow.

Hearing the shouts of guards patrolling for thieves passing by, he immediately attained realization. He took his leave. During the Daguan era, when Furuong was embroiled in difficulties, the Master intended to travel from the Three Wu region toward Yishui.
His servant became lost in the way; the Master raised his staff and struck him, whereupon he suddenly attained great enlightenment and sighed, saying: "This is it!"
Is it not that the earth is indeed Mount Ao? When [Furong] reached Yi, Furong looked at him and said with joy, "Those such as you will surely cause my school to flourish.
He then remained there for many years, personally tilling the land by the lake. Once his realization was perfected, he emerged to lead a monastery.

The Third Patriarch, Qianguanlu, was summoned by imperial decree in the *Renyin* year of the Xuanhua era to serve as the abbot of Yuan Tong. He declined the appointment and returned to reside at Letan.

Upon ascending the hall, he said: "The ancient Buddha said: 'When I first attained perfect enlightenment, I clearly saw that all sentient beings throughout the great earth had already attained perfect enlightenment.'"
Later, he spoke again: "Profound, firm, secluded, and remote—no one can reach it. [He struck the meditation seat with his staff.

"You fellows of no discernment, you are like those who have a dragon's head but a snake's tail. He then descended from the seat. Entering the hall, he said: "The Buddhas of the past have already entered nirvana;
you people should not dwell on them with longing remembrance. The Buddhas of the future have not yet appeared in the world; you people must not engage in idle speculation."
“Contemplate! Right now, who are you? *Chan* (Investigate). Ascending the hall, he said: “Bo Yi was narrow-minded; Liu Xiaohui was lacking in propriety; the gentleman does not follow either of them.
When neither of the two extremes is established and the Middle Way is not settled, what then? Holding up his staff, he said: ‘The embroidered mandarin ducks are for you to behold;

the golden needle is not passed on to others. Ascending the hall at Dayang Monastery, he said: [He continued with the verse: “The Great Sun illuminates all things; The Great Earth supports all beings. If one can understand this principle, Then there is no need to seek the Buddha.”

The lower notes sing exquisitely as they soar ever higher. Before the Hall of the Bright Moon, those who truly understand are few. Having no choice but to proceed, the boat is moored at the river islet;
as the oars are raised upon the clear waves, we sing of celebrating the years of Yao and harmonize with the *Qingping Yue*. Announcing this to you all, I ask that you each take it up.
In the mere interval of a moment’s hesitation, white clouds stretch ten thousand miles away. Entering the hall, [he said]: "Originally unborn, now likewise without cessation—this is death."
The pattern that has been attained is born in this very place and extinguished in every circumstance; this is the model for living and receiving existence.
A great man must directly enter the stream of birth and death, lie within the forest of thorns, and—bending, stretching, looking up, and looking down—apply means according to the occasion.
Being able to act thus through immeasurable skillful means, one adorns the samādhis and the gate of great liberation, until all is vast and suddenly clear.
[The Master] opened [the door]. "If this is not yet so, then immeasurable afflictions and all worldly defilements stand like mountains before one's face, blocking the ancient path.

He ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said: 'To cast off the limbs and body, to discard the cleverness of the intellect, to leave behind form and depart from wisdom—to be thus is to be one with the Great Way.'"
At this very moment, tell me, who is it? He edited the *Shi* and *Shu*, and codified the rites and music.
Do you understand this thoroughly? As for "Rites, O rites!"—are they merely jade and silk? As for "Music, O music!"—are they merely bells and drums?
It is said that the Master once remarked: "Where the clouds are dark, Mount Duxiu towers forth; amidst the hazy moonlight, the waters of Lestam flow. Do you comprehend this?
Guangsheng asked, "Is this not the realm of Baofeng? The Master said, "If it is the realm of Baofeng, rely on you, sir, to examine it closely.
Guangsheng asked, "What is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Look at the time when the command is being carried out.

Guangsheng asked, "As for the saying, 'One must understand the source when receiving the words; do not establish your own rules,' what is the Master's source? The Master said, "You must know that beyond the clouds..."
On the mountain peak, there was a particularly sacred pine tree, cold with clinging dew. When snow fell, a monk asked, "I do not ask about the Patriarch’s coming from the West;
what is the matter of the seasonal conditions? The Master replied, "One piece, two pieces, three or four pieces—falling right into one's eyes, yet still not realized.
On the seventh day of the first month in the second year of the Jianyan era, he passed away. Upon cremation, śarīra relics were obtained that resembled pearls.
Běi. His tongue and teeth remained unimpaired. He was enshrined in a stupa on the western peak of the monastery.
Chan Master Yuanyi of Shimen in Xiangzhou, a son of the Xuè clan of Tōngchuān, ascended the hall and said: "The ten directions assemble together."
Each and every one studies non-action; this is the field for selecting Buddhas. With the mind empty, one returns having passed the imperial examination. Great assembly, how about this:
since seeing, hearing, perceiving, and knowing have never been interrupted, how can you explain the principle of "the mind being empty"?

Is it because you see yet do not see, hear yet do not hear, that the mind is said to be empty? That would be a mistake. Is it because you have forgotten artifice and stilled your thoughts... ten thousand [phenomena]...?

When both phenomena and their counterparts are abandoned, one dissolves the capacity for agency to enter the Profound Mystery; by extinguishing both nature and characteristics, one returns to the Dharma-realm.
Is this because the mind is empty? No, it is a mistake. It cannot be so, nor can it not be so;
it cannot be both so and not so. I wonder, in the end, how is it? Do you understand? After a long silence, he said: "If truly there is no action..."
It is not so; heaven and hell follow one another for all time. With a three-foot staff, he stirs the Yellow River;
with cold eyes, the eight-armed Nātha gazes upon it. Limitless fish and dragons all flee in haste, yet he catches a three-legged tortoise that follows the river.
He strips away its shell with an iron awl; the signs of good and ill fortune are thereby distinguished. I ask the white-haired old man of the eastern village: before good and ill fortune [are known]—

"What is the omen? Auspicious! Auspicious! Auspicious! From antiquity to the present, spring follows autumn. The bright sun rises and passes its time as it pleases; what more could one wish for that is not elegant?
*Du!* [He] ascended the hall. "The bright moon hangs in the sky; the clear pool has no reflection. Where the Purple Microcosm turns, the evening sun shines;
when the colored phoenix returns, the heavens are about to dawn. Beyond the clouds in the azure void, the stone pillar stands horizontal."
Emptiness. Amidst the waves of green water, a clay ox rides the billows; the pregnant jade hare passes over the western peak at dawn;
the golden cock cradling its chick roosts on the eastern ridge at night. If one attains clarity here, one will finally know that beyond the "Night-Bright" curtain, there is a distinct family style;
within the palace of the Empty King, both sages and commoners leave no trace. But tell me, what is this matter beyond the Night-Bright curtain? Do you understand?
Simma. Just as the autumn wind enters the door, a single sound of a mortar and pestle falls—who’s house is it?
A monk asked, “How is it when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master said, “The spirit frowns. The monk asked, “How is it after it has been polished?
The Master said, “The Persian snaps his fingers. The monk asked, “Why is it so? The Master said, “Good things do not leave the gate. The seventh month of the Dingchou year of the Shaoxing era.
On the twenty-fifth day of the month, he entered nirvana while seated in meditation. After the cremation, his *śarīra* (relics) were collected and enshrined in a stupa on Mount Xueshe.
Chan Master Zizhao of Jingyin Monastery in Dongjing was the son of the Wang family of Qingzhou. From his youth, he was recognized for his Confucian studies by Sima Guang;
however, he pursued a life of noble refinement and had no interest in fame or official rank. One day, he shaved his head and followed Fuyong.

His conduct was precise and meticulous, and his realization was transcendent. During the Chongning era of the world-transcending Great Vehicle, he was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Jingyin Temple.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Patriarch came from the West specifically to proclaim this matter. Since then, people have been unwilling to grasp it fully;

instead, they have sought it outwardly, like casting oneself into clear water to search for pearls or visiting the Jingshan mountains to seek jade. Little do they realize that [it is right] through the gate..."

To enter [this state] is not to possess one’s own family treasure. To mistake the shadows for the head is surely a great error. It is simply this: when the teachings of the Zen school are proclaimed, the essence is quiescent and without dependence;
conceptual thoughts do not arise. There is no interval between past and present; the myriad phenomena of the universe are the ancestral style encountered at every turn.

The bird-path stretches across the vast void; there is no hindrance to taking a step. The golden cock announces the dawn; the vermilion phoenix soars aloft. Flowers bloom upon the jade tree; fruit forms upon the withered branches.
Only beneath the Gate of the Sun does every day become three autumns; before the Hall of the Bright Moon, every moment becomes nine summers.
Do you understand? On the shadowless tree hangs the moon over the cold stream; the ocean tide flows east while the Dipper shifts west.
Chan Master Tianning Xipu of the Western Capital was the son of the Song family from Caizhou. Having previously resided at Shaoshan, he subsequently moved to Tianning Danxia.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Lately at Shaoshan, there has been no trace of anything. Hearing sounds with the eyes and tasting flavors with the nose;
sometimes waking up until dawn, neither on the bed nor on the ground. Tell me, everyone, where is he?"
At this point, if anyone can offer a turning word, they will not only save Shaoshan but also ensure their own journey was not in vain. If you have not yet attained this, then:
"The waves grow high at the third level and the fish transform into dragons; yet the fool still uses a bucket to bail out the water from a night pond."
Question: "What is the Lord? The Master said: "In the universe there is no second sun; in heaven and earth there is but one person.

Question: "What is the Minister? The Master said: "Virtue clearly distinguishes the transformation of the sovereign; the Way accords with the mechanisms of things and circumstances. Question: "What is the Minister facing the Lord? The Master said:
"With a sincere heart returning to the sun of Shun; exhausting one's integrity to repay the sky of Yao. Question: "What is the Lord looking upon the Minister?"
The Master said: "The dark pupils are fixed and do not blink; the wondrous body reflects what comes from the side. [A monk] asked: "What is the unification of the Way between ruler and subject?

The Master said: "The banners and seals separate the noble from the lowly; the secret correspondence passes and returns in communication. On the fourth day of the ninth month in the fifth year of the Zhenghe era.

Suddenly, he summoned the administrative official and ordered him to divide a paper bag into four parts—one for each of the assembly of monks, the novices, and those in training, and one for the maintenance of the monastery.
Afterward, he said again, "Danxia has a public case that from of old has been knocked down and raised up;
today it is shown universally to all people. Tell me, what is it? He looked left and right and asked, "Do you understand? They replied, "We do not understand."
The Master said, "How magnificent, this great man! He did not understand the final phrase," and then he passed away while lying on his right side.
Later, Chan Master Dayong Qilian of Tianting in Chang’an ascended the hall and said: "The principle of pure emptiness is where Buddhas and Patriarchs alike return."
Ultimately there is no body; the holy and the ordinary are one essence. Such is the principle. When the myriad phenomena fill the eyes, what of their functioning?
Not even a speck of dust exists at the limit—those people possess eyes; how could they look on from the side? Officially, not even a needle is permitted; privately, carriages and horses pass through.

If you reach such a state, only then can you respond to conditions as they arise and employ them at hand; wondrously responding without fixed direction, you stand upon the mysterious path in the wind.
It reaches the point where the seams and threads of the golden needle and brocade are no longer visible, and the jade palace, the jeweled steps, and the pearl curtains remain unrolled.
At this very moment, tell me: whose realm is this? The autumn wind blows cold across the ancient ferry.
*Sā*. Red pampas grass and *liǎo* reeds fill the river bends.
A monk asked Master Jǐ of Mèishān in Tóngchuān Prefecture, "What is the matter of the Dharma-body?
The Master said, "A withered tree sprouts flowers, yet it does not offend the spring. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter beyond the Dharma-body? The Master said, "The stone woman..."
Applying eyebrow makeup.
A monk asked Chan Master Shanshou of Puxian in Fuzhou, "What is 'the partial within the central'?
The Master said, "The dragon roars after the first watch; the tiger howls before the fifth watch. The monk asked, "What is 'the central within the partial'? The Master said, "Light mist envelops..."
A bright moon; thin mist locks the cold crags. [The student] asked, "What is 'coming from the center'? The Master said, "How could the withered pines ever grow old?
The flowers bloom though they have not yet sprouted. [The student] asked, "What is 'arriving at the convergence'? The Master said, "The sound of the howling monkey cannot be distinguished."
The cry of the crane resounds, yet its meaning is difficult to clarify. [A monk] asked, "What is it to arrive within the 'Concurrent'? The Master said, "Clearing the path beyond the clouds;
shedding oneself before the moonlight.
Chan Master Faden of Lumeng in Xiangzhou was the son of the Liu family of Chengdu. He became a monk under Daci Baofan.
He enabled those who heard the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* to grasp its essential meaning, and subsequently left to visit Fuyong.

Fuyong asked, "What is one's own self prior to the empty kalpa? At these words, the Master’s mental traces vanished. He replied with composure, "A single phrase, numinous and transcendent, surpasses all phenomena;
it stands far beyond the Three Vehicles and requires no cultivation. Fuyong patted him and certified his realization. He later propagated the Dharma at Lumeng. A monk asked: [text continues]
"Vast and profound, it is not transgressed; the precious mirror reflects a cold light. "How is it? the monk asked. The Master said, "Dig a deep hole and bury it.
The monk asked, "What is one who roams freely beyond the mundane world? The Master said, "His entire body is raw and festering, beyond all support."
At the Jiansheng Nanchan Temple in Jianchang Commandery, the Master ascended the hall on the occasion of the Emperor’s birthday and, looking around at those present, said:

"Do you all understand? The Lord outside the curtain of night-brightness does not change throughout the myriad transformations; the Honored One upon the crystal palace is not obscured by the four ministers.

He governs with effortless composure, and his commands are carried out without being issued. His longevity exceeds that of a hundred billion Mount Sumerus, and his transformative influence permeates the great trichiliocosm."
Throughout the sands of the world. But tell me, at such a time as this, how does one conduct oneself? "The rustic elder knows not the nobility of the imperial palace;
he is too weary to listen to the sound of the quiet-whip in the six streets."

Chan Master Weizhou Dongshan Wei ascended the hall for the discourse: "The sun is warm and the breeze gentle; the willow eyes are green. The ice melts and the fish leap; the waves give birth to flowers.
At the vanguard, he wondrously attains the Seal of the Empty King; In the dead of night, Kunlun walks bearing snow upon his head.
A monk asked, "What is the matter of silent resonance? The Master said, "A mute man eats bitter melon."
The Grand Tutor Gao Shize, a lay practitioner (jushi) whose courtesy name was Zhongyi and sobriquet was Wugong, initially attended Fuyong to seek the essential point of the mind.

Fuyong instructed him to set aside what he valued and investigate himself through inquiry. One day, he suddenly attained the subtle and profound; he presented a verse, saying: [Verse omitted as per instructions]
Casting off one's hands at the precipice, one moves freely and unrestrained; the great earth and empty space are naturally level and plain.
Illuminating the valleys and shining upon the crags without borrowing from the moon, within the hermitage there is another screen of light.
Chan Master Shousui of Dahuang, a successor of Chan Master Dahong En, was the son of the Zhang family of Suining. He ascended the hall and addressed the assembly:
"With one punch, he toppled Huanghe Lou; with one kick, he overturned Yingwu Zhou. He is accustomed to galloping a jade horse atop high towers. He had once...
One strikes a golden ball in swift-flowing water. Although it is thus, what can be done? There are five-colored silk cords binding one’s hands and feet, and three golden locks fastening one’s throat.

Even if you were to smash the golden locks to pieces and cut through the silk cords, you must know that there is yet another layer obstructing you. Tell me, what is this other layer? Do you understand? Subhūti.
Mātaṅga could not reach it; Maudgalyāyana and Śāriputra looked upon it as if they were blind. He ascended the hall and said: "I cite the case where Prefect Li asked Yaoshan, 'What is your surname?

Yaoshan replied, 'It is precisely this. At that time, Li could not fathom it, so he asked the monastery attendant, 'Just now I asked the Elder what his surname was, and he answered, "It is precisely this.
What exactly is his surname? The attendant said, 'He simply has the surname Han.'"

Shanwen said, "If you were questioned by him during the sixth month, you would have simply said his surname was 'Heat' (Re). Furthermore, Yantou asked a monk who was lecturing, "I hear it is said that you understand the teachings;
is this true? The monk replied, "I dare not say so. Yantou raised his fist and said, "What kind of teaching is this?
The monk said, "It is the provisional teaching (expedient teaching). Yantou said, "How tragic! If I had asked you with my legs extended, you could not have said it was the 'leg-teaching'!"
The Master said: "How extraordinary! These two venerable elders possess the 'knife that kills' and the 'sword that gives life.

One turn of phrase is like planting flowers upon a stone; another turn of phrase is like hanging a sword in mid-air. Had there not been their subsequent words at that time, the entire school of Bodhidharma would have been swept away to the very dust.
Do you wish to see these two venerable elders? It would be better to cut out one's tongue than to violate the national law."
Posthumous name:
Chan Master Danxia Chun, thirteenth generation descendant of Qingyuan and successor to the Dharma.
Chan Master Zhenxie Qingliao of Changlu in Zhenzhou was the son of Lady Yong of Zuoyuan in Mian. He entered the monastery while still in his swaddling clothes;

upon seeing the Buddha, he was moved with joy, his eyebrows and eyelashes twitching, which caused everyone to marvel at him. At the age of eighteen, he underwent the *śrāmaṇera* ordination by reciting the *Lotus Sūtra*.

He went to Daci Monastery in Chengdu to study the sūtras and śāstras, grasping their essential meaning. Leaving Sichuan, he traveled to Mian and Han, where he sought out the quarters of Danxia. Danxia asked him: "Like what..."
"What is this self prior to the kalpa of emptiness? The Master was about to respond when Xiang said, "You are being too noisy;
go away for now. One day, while ascending Mount Bowu, he attained sudden enlightenment. He went directly back to stand in attendance. Xiang struck him with his palm and said, "I thought you knew."

The Master bowed joyfully to him. The following day, Yunxia ascended the hall and said: "The sun shines upon the solitary peak’s emerald heights; the moon descends upon the mountain stream’s chill waters.
The profound and wondrous secret of the Patriarchs—do not seek it within a single inch of the mind. He then descended from his seat.

The Master stepped straight forward and said, "Today you have ascended the hall; you can no longer deceive me. Yunxia said, "Try to cite my words from today's ascent to the hall and see. The Master...
After a long silence, Huixia said, "I thought you had already seen through it. The Master then departed. Later, he traveled to Mount Wutai and then to the capital.

He journeyed along the Bian River until he reached Changlu, where he visited Zu Zhao. They attained mutual accord in a single word, and Zu Zhao appointed him as his attendant. After more than a year, he was assigned a seat alongside the master.
Before long, Zhao cited illness as a pretext to retire from his post and requested that the Master succeed him on the seat. Students flocked to him like people returning home.

At the end of the Jianyan era, he traveled to Siming, where he presided over Putuo, Tianfeng in Tiantai, and Xuefeng in Min. By imperial decree, he was appointed to reside at Yuyang, and subsequently moved to Longxiang in Wenzhou and Jingshan in Hangzhou.
Empress Dowager Cining commissioned him to be the founding abbot of Chaoguang on Gaotingshan. He ascended the hall and said: "I..."
Under the single blow of my former teacher’s palm, all my cleverness was exhausted; I could find no opening through which to speak.
Is there anyone today who is so swift and yet not thoroughly satisfied? If there were none, each would have to take up the bit and the saddle for themselves.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "I have long kept this essential matter silent, not wishing to speak of it hastily. The Old Śākyamuni waited to sell it with full detail."
"Playing! Alas, even before leaving the mother's womb, one has already been seen through. But tell me, what was it that was seen through? One cannot deceive Xuefeng. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Climbing to the peak of a solitary mountain, crossing a single-plank bridge—walking straight ahead in this manner is still where people’s feet are high or low.
If you see through to the bottom, without leaving your room your body pervades the ten directions. Unfinished.
"Entering the gate, one is always inside the house. If this is not yet so, take advantage of the coolness to go fetch some firewood.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "If you can utter the first phrase, you will not be deceived by the staff. Even recognizing the staff is still a matter of being on the path.
What is the phrase for reaching the destination? [He] ascended the hall and said: "It cannot be found anywhere; there is only one..."
Seeking it nowhere, one finds it spontaneously. But tell me: in which place is it? After a long silence, he said: "The thief’s own body has already been revealed. Ascending the hall, he said:

"Only when the white mold from the corners of your mouth has gone away, and you have entered the gate with your entire body drenched in blood and pus, will you finally know the matters within the gate."
Furthermore, you must know there is that which does not go out the gate. He then said, "What do you call the gate?
A monk asked, "The Buddhas of the three periods turn the Great Dharma Wheel within the flames; is this truly so? The Master laughed loudly and said, "I, however, have my doubts.
The monk asked, "Why, Master, do you have doubts? The Master replied, "Wild flowers fill the path; the secluded birds..."
[The monk] said, "I do not know spring. [The Master] asked, "If one does not fall into the traces of wind and color, is it permitted to turn back?

The Master said, "Where the stone man walks, his way differs from that of ordinary effort. [The monk] asked, "What of the matter beyond this? The Master said, "The marvel lies before a single bubble; how could it admit the eyes of a thousand sages?
The monk bowed. The Master said, "I only fear it is not so. One day, the Master entered the kitchen to watch the noodles being cooked.
Next, suddenly the bottom of a flour bucket fell out. The assembly all cried out in dismay, "What a pity! The Master said, "The bottom of the bucket has fallen out;
you ought to rejoice. Why, then, do you feel distressed? A monk said, "The Master may have attained it.
The Master said, "Truly, what a pity—a whole bucket of flour! He then asked a monk, "After you die and are burned to ashes and scattered away, where will you go?"
The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "A fine shout! But you must not reverse the case. The monk shouted again.
The Master said, "The public case is not yet complete; you must shout once more. The monk was speechless. The Master struck him, saying, "You dead man! He ascended the hall and said:

"Moss seals the ancient path, yet it does not fall into empty stillness. Fog locks the cold forest, yet it willingly reveals the essential wind. The hook and needle are steady and subtle—who would dare say otherwise?"
The fisherman dwells in his nest; by simply accepting things as they are, he is naturally content and at ease.

Is there anyone here who possesses the eye that penetrates the barrier? After a long silence, he said: "Even if one hears of it early and returns home immediately, how can that compare to never having left the door at all?
Ascending the hall, he said: "The rain comes and goes, the weather shifts between cold and heat. As for this mountain monk’s own state, I alone know it; as for yours, you yourselves must know."
"Aha! You all speak for yourselves. Now tell me, aside from eating his meals, what did Xuefeng intend to do with his mouth? He asked a monk:
'When a jade maiden on a lapis lazuli palace throws her shuttle, what matter does she clarify? The monk replied: 'To avoid conflict when facing the immediate occasion.

The Master said: 'Is there still continuity or interruption here? The monk replied: 'From ancient times to the present, it has never been interrupted. The Master said: 'Precisely at that moment, it was not interrupted.'"
"How is it now? Monk Zhenzhong bowed respectfully and departed. The Master ascended the hall, shook his staff, and said:
"Look! Look! The trichiliocosm shakes all at once. Master Yunmen was indeed capable of this. Xuefeng, however, was not so.
He struck the ground with his staff and said: 'Where has the trichiliocosm gone? Do you understand? One must not encounter heavy plum rains twice."
The seedlings vie to show their greenness. He ascends the hall and says: "The illusory, transformed empty body is itself the Dharma-body. He then performs a dance and asks: "Do you see? Do you see?
If you see in this way, the village wine by the bridge is delicious. Again he performs a dance and asks: "Do you see? Do you see?
If you do not see in this way, the wild flowers on the opposite bank are fragrant. He ascends the hall and asks: "Is there anyone who is not defiled by the profound and the subtle?"
After a long silence, he said, "This single drop would exhaust the waters of the four oceans; it is already too much for one to wash away.
A monk asked, "What is the self prior to the empty kalpa? The Master replied, "A white horse enters the reeds. He ascended the hall and said, "To investigate the subtle is to lose the root."

The essence is subtle, yet its fundamental principle is lost; a single phrase cuts off the current, reaching the ultimate depth of the profound and mysterious. Therefore, where the golden needle is held in secret, its sharp edge is not revealed;
when the jade thread passes through, it silently displays its extraordinary luster. Although this is so, it still involves a mutual illumination of both aspects.

Furthermore, tell me: when skill and clumsiness do not reach [the mark], how can one be entrusted with it? After a long silence, he said: "Where the cloud-vines are exquisite, the green shadows close together;
the heights and depths of the cliff-trees are locked deep in emerald. Entering the hall, he said: "To turn function to accord with the position is for those who are heading forward;

'Jade hidden in the Jingshan mountains' is precious. To turn the position to accord with function is for those who are returning; 'A flake of snow on a red furnace' is spring. Function and position..."

Simultaneously turning, the entire body passes through without obstruction; letting go, one is free from dependence. The barren woman ascends the loom at night; the secret chamber has no one to sweep it.

At such a time, how can one entrust oneself to a single word that cuts off the breath? After a long silence, he said: "Returning to the root, the wind falls the leaves; the moon shines until the pond is empty.
The Master passed away at Chongguang on Gaoteng Mountain and was interred in a pagoda to the west of the temple among the flowering paulownias.
His posthumous title was Chan Master Wukong.
Chan Master Hongzhi Zhengjue of Tiantong in Mingzhou was the son of the Li family of Xi Prefecture. His mother dreamed of a monk from Mount Wutai who untied a ring and fastened it upon her right arm;
she then conceived. She subsequently observed the precepts of fasting and purification. Upon his birth, his right arm rose up prominently as if...
He was of a round face. At seven years of age, he could recite several thousand words daily. His grandfather was Ji, and his father was Zongdao, who had long studied under Chan Master Fotuo Xun.
The master once pointed to him and said to his father, "This boy possesses an exceptionally superior aura of the Way;

he is no one from the midst of worldly dust. If he leaves the household life, he will surely become a vessel for the Dharma. At eleven, he received ordination at Jingming Monastery under his own lineage; at fourteen, he received full precepts. Ten...
Eighth, regarding Youfang: he took leave of his master, saying, "If I do not realize the Great Matter, I vow never to return.
Upon reaching Xiangshan in Ruzhou, Cheng Kumu saw him at once and held him in high esteem. One day, while hearing a monk reciting the Lotus Sūtra, he reached the passage:
"The eyes born of one’s parents can see the three thousandfold world-system. At that moment, he had a sudden realization. He immediately went to the master’s quarters and presented his understanding.
Wu pointed to the incense box on the altar and asked, "What is inside? The Master replied, "What kind of mental activity is that?
Wu asked, "And how is it at the place where you have attained awakening? The Master drew a circle with his hand and presented it; he then threw it behind him.
Wu said, "You fellow who plays with mud balls—what limits do you have? The Master said, "Wrong. Wu said, "I see it differently."
The Master first attained it. The Teacher responded, "Yes, yes," and immediately went to see Danxia. Danxia asked, "What is one's own self prior to the empty kalpa?
The Master said, "A frog at the bottom of the well swallows the moon; at the third watch, one does not borrow the night-bright curtain. Danxia said:
"I have not yet spoken further. As the Master hesitated, Xiang struck him with a whisk and said, "I have also said 'not borrowed'.

At these words, the Master was suddenly enlightened and prostrated himself. Xiang said, "Why do you not utter a single phrase? The Master replied, "Today I have lost my money and incurred this punishment.
Xiang said, "I have no leisure to beat you; go for now. Xiang took charge of Dahong, while the Master served as the head of the administrative records (*zhānjì*).

Later, he was appointed as the head of the assembly. Those who had attained the Dharma numbered several people. In the fourth year, after [the Master] had passed through Yuan Tong, Zhenxie was newly residing at Changlu and sent a monk to invite him there.
When the assembly came out to welcome him, they saw that his robes and sandals were tattered and worn; they wished to change them for him.

Zhenxie ordered an attendant to replace them with new shoes, but the Master declined, saying, "Did I come here for the sake of shoes? Upon hearing this, the assembly was filled with admiration and submission, and they earnestly [requested him to remain].

He sought to propagate the Dharma and occupied the foremost seat for six years. He subsequently resided at Puzhao in Sizhou, followed by serving as the abbot of Taiping, Yuan Tong, Nengren, Changlu, and Tiantong.
In these monasteries, the buildings were cramped and dilapidated; upon the Master’s arrival, he renovated them all anew.

Monks vied with one another to join his assembly. Entering the hall, he said: "The yellow palace curtains hang down—who transmits the family message? The purple silk screens are closed—darkly, true pearls are scattered."
At this very moment, there is that which hearing and sight cannot reach, and that which words and explanations cannot attain. How can one transmit this news?
Returning from a dream, the night colors are faintly bright; smiling, he points to the family tradition—a spring in full bloom. [He ascends the hall.]
The mind cannot perceive it; the mouth cannot discuss it. Even if you were to step back and take it upon yourself to carry it, you must strictly avoid hitting upon its tabooed name.
"Wind and moon, cold and clear, at an ancient ferryhead; the night boat turns over the crystal ground. Entering the hall, he said: "In the empty kalpa there is a true school;
before the sound, inquire of your own person. This is a fresh livelihood for those utterly destitute; it is the old family style of purity and clarity. It is the very essence of the Three Vehicles."
Outside. Within this vast, solitary seal, he instead comes to practice among the diverse classes of beings; ten thousand streams naturally flow toward the east. [Ascending the hall:
Today is the anniversary of Śākyamuni Buddha’s birth. Changlu does not understand how to preach Chan; instead, I shall draw a likeness for you all.
Suppose he were in Māyā’s womb—how would it be? With his whisk, he drew this symbol (a circle with a dot inside) and said:
Suppose one were to bathe the golden body with pure water—how would you do that? Furthermore, he drew this symbol of water [○@水] and said:

"As for taking seven steps, looking in the four directions, pointing to heaven and pointing to earth, attaining enlightenment, preaching the Dharma, performing supernatural transformations, and possessing wisdom and eloquence;
throughout forty-nine years and over three hundred assemblies, speaking of blue and explaining yellow—" Pointing...
[The Master] drew a circle to the west. [A monk asked: "When entering parinirvāṇa, how is it? Why then do you draw this ⊕-sign? The Master replied:
"If one is a monk with eyes, they will surely grant their assent; if not, one must pass through each and every stage before it can be attained.
He ascended the hall. A monk asked: "What is one who goes forward? The Master said: "The white clouds have vanished into the ravines; the green peaks lean against..."
Konggao asked, "What is the person who returns? The Master said, "With a head full of white hair, he leaves the mountain valleys;
at midnight, he pierces the clouds to enter the marketplace. He asked, "What is the person who neither comes nor goes? The Master said, "The stone woman calls back the dream of the three realms;
the wooden man sits and cuts off the mechanism of the six gates. He then said, "It is easy to clarify the essence within the words."
It is difficult to discern the essential point within the school. After a long silence, he said, "Do you understand? The frozen rooster has not yet crowed, yet the dawn breaks in the home-grove;
silently, the traveler passes over the Snow Mountains. A monk asked, "What is it like when not a single thread is attached?
The Master said, "He travels side-by-side with the boatman, heads together. The monk asked, "What is the matter therein? The Master said, "A swift blade or a sharp axe cannot cut into it."
A questioner asked, "What is it like when the mouth of the cloth bag opens? The Master said, "Fill the ditches and block the ravines as you please.

A questioner asked, "When the principle of pure emptiness ultimately has no body, what is it like? The Master said, "Before a trace of literary color appears, the message is difficult to transmit at its limit."
[The student] said: "A single step secretly shifts, and the profound path turns; the entire body is cast down, and the kalpa-jar is empty. The Master said:
"When the newborn meets the father, the whole being is merged without a trace of separation. [The student] said: "If the principle is thus, what of the phenomenon? The Master said:

"As soon as one returns clearly to the differentiated phenomena, how could the responsive functioning throughout the ten directions be an obstacle? [The student] said: "In that case, every dust mote manifests [the truth]."
"The original body has already departed. The Master said, "It penetrates all forms and transcends all minds. [The monk] asked, "What about 'according to principle and according to fact'?
The Master said, "When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it; carry it home in a bottomless basket."
[The Master] said: "Entering the marketplace, he can let out a long whistle; returning home, he puts on his short shirt. The Master continued: "The wooden man sings atop the ridge;
the stone woman dances by the stream. Entering the hall, he said: "O Zen practitioners, why is it that those who have swallowed up the Buddhas of the three periods cannot open their mouths?
Why is it that those who have illuminated the four worlds cannot close their eyes? Such are these many ailments."
"I have already removed them for you all at once. But how can you attain complete and unimpeded mastery? Do you understand?
'He splits apart Mount Hua, reaching to the color of the heavens; he releases the Yellow River, its sound reaching the sea. Since the Master took up residence [at this monastery]..."

He received offerings without attachment and gave in charity without weariness. During years of hardship when food was exhausted, he relied on his own possessions and the surplus from providing for the assembly to save tens of thousands of lives.

Daily, he did not eat after noon. In the ninth month of the Dingchou year of the Xiangshu era, he paid visits to his local officials and donors, and subsequently visited Zhao Gong Lingchun, the Regional Commander of Yue, with whom he took leave. On the seventh day of the tenth month, he returned to the mountain.
On the following day, during the hours of the Dragon and Snake (7–9 AM), he bathed, changed his robes, and sat upright.

Addressing the assembly and looking toward his attendant monks, he requested a brush and wrote a letter entrusting Master Dahui of Yuwang to preside over his funeral affairs. He then inscribed a verse, saying: "Like a dream, an illusion, or a flower in the sky;

Sixty-seven years have passed. The white heron vanishes into the mist; Autumn waters reach the heavens. Having cast down the brush, he passed away. His coffin remained for seven days, and his countenance—
His countenance remained as if alive. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at Donggu, and he was posthumously titled Hongzhi;
the stupa was named Miaoguang. Chan Master Huizhao Qingyu of Dahuang Monastery in Suizhou ascended the hall and said: "To take one step forward is to tread upon the water and grass of another king;
to take one step back is to trample upon the ancestral fields and gardens. To neither advance nor retreat is to remain right within the waters of death. Do you understand?"
Is there a path for those who have left the household life? Or is there not? The late autumn wind whistles through the pines, their needles short;
the spring breeze drifts over the willows, their filaments long. [He] ascends the hall and cites the boatman’s instruction to Jia-shan:
"You must leave no trace where you hide yourself; do not hide yourself where there is no trace. For thirty years I was at Yaoshan, clarifying only this matter. People of the present day...
What is there to be done in haste? The Cinnabar Mountain has no painted phoenixes; the precious palace does not retain its crown. At times I am dull-witted, at times I am deluded;
who among those on their own paths could know this?

Chan Master Wuyi of Chuzhou ascends the hall for the *shangtang* ceremony: "Leisurely dwelling in the wondrously luminous realm of ultimate reality, he shifts his step and turns his body to point toward the setting clouds.
Though boundless white clouds remain unseen, he rides the bright moon at night out into the reeds."
Chan Master Zigui of Tianfeng on Mount Tai, successor to Chan Master Jingyin Cheng, ascended the hall. He struck his staff once and called to the assembly, saying:
"The eighty-four thousand Dharma gates have been flung open with eight characters. Do you see them? The golden phoenix rests at night where there is no shadow."
The trees stand; the peaks and ridges have just appeared, yet they are shrouded by sea clouds.
A monk asked Chan Master Faxian of Jixiang in Taiping Prefecture, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "A long drought has left no sweet rain; the rice stalks in the fields are withered. The monk asked, "What is the underlying intent? The Master said, "This year..."
The price of rice is high; if it is coarse, do not disdain it.
Chan Master Shouchang of Huguosi in Taizhou ascended the hall, held up his staff, and struck the ground, saying:

"It is the beginning of the thirty-six decades of the year, the origin of the seventy-two seasonal signs, the time when the myriad realms welcome the harmonious breath, and the Eastern Emperor spreads life."

By imperial decree, Heaven spontaneously bestowed auspicious radiance and Earth gathered signs of sublime fortune. A fine drizzle washed the cold sky, and a faint spring light enveloped the wild landscapes.
It may truly be said that blessings were received in accordance with the season, and every celebration was most appropriate. All people throughout the great earth have added one year to their lives.

I dare ask you all: tell me, how many years does that one person have? After a long silence, he said: [The following line is omitted as it appears to be a non-sequitur or a scribal error in the source text. He then said: "One hundred and twenty years."
The thousand-year-old man’s countenance is like jade; the ten-thousand-year-old boy’s hair is like silk.
Master Chan Master Puyue of Danxia in Dengzhou ascended the hall and said: "Before the time of Vipaśyin, who could discern the truth?

After the time of Dīpaṃkara, who was a true connoisseur? Even if one were to take responsibility for that which lies beyond, it would still not avoid being split into two pieces. Even if you were to..."
Even this current practice has likely not yet attained perfection. This is because the silence at Vimalakīrti’s abode already betrayed the celestial mechanism;

even if one were to remain in seclusion like Mahākāśyapa in the Makhadeva cave, in the end the seams and gaps would inevitably fray and open. Do not say that the true permanence is manifest in its essence.
It is simply pure clarity, utterly free of a single speck. What need is there to speak of "shedding skin and fur"? It naturally functions alone as solitary luminosity.
Although it may seem fresh in this way, it does not yet accord with the spirit of a monk. Only when the five eyes are opened together and the three lights are fully revealed can it be so.
From this point on, with the thread upon the pole, one naturally does not offend the waves. One must clearly understand the shifting of positions and the turning back of the faculty;
only then can one resolve to enter the marketplace and extend the hand. Therefore it is said: "Even if the teeth grow hair, do not let the eyes look back.
To recognize it is like the confusion of floating flowers in the sky; to speak of it is for the paths of language to diverge. Since this is so, I dare ask you all:
"A person does not encounter even a single sharp edge of the Way. How do you say it? After a long silence, he said: "At midnight, the tortoise’s eyes open wide;
at dawn, the myriad phenomena are all of one color."
Chan Master Huiguang Jingzhi, the Nun Miaohui of Tokyo, ascended the hall and raised the story of Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman.
He said: "Zhaozhou’s tongue reaches the heavens; the old woman’s brow-light covers the earth. Having clearly seen her through upon his return, countless ordinary people fall into a daze."
Chan Master Qinggu Zhenji Dezhi of Yuan Tong Temple in Jiangzhou was a dharma heir of Chan Master Baofeng Zhao. He was the younger son of Xu Hongzhong, who held the rank of Jinzi.

His family had resided in Liyang for generations. The Master’s eyes were a deep azure-blue, and his spiritual radiance struck those who beheld him. At the age of ten, he knew nothing of writing and spent much of his time...
He was fond of sleep, so his father called him the "Dullard. By the time he reached the age of maturity, his retentive memory surpassed that of others;
when he studied literature, he produced extraordinary phrases. In his early twenties, he dreamed of a strange monk who bestowed upon him a four-line verse.

Shortly thereafter, someone presented him with a statue of the Master of Nanyue Rock, which bore inscribed upon it the very same "Verse of Intelligence" (*cintāmaṇi-gāthā*). From then on, he recited it constantly without forgetting. Five years later, he followed King...
Zijiang was transporting grain to Western Luo. One night, he suddenly attained great enlightenment and composed several gāthās in succession.

One said: "Not because of words or phrases, not because of a person; not because of objects or colors, not because of sound. At midnight, I blew out the lamp and lay down upon my pillow; suddenly, here, it was already dawn.
He continued to sing and chant as usual, and the crowd could not fathom him. He then earnestly sought to leave the household life, but his father would not permit it.
The Emperor granted his request and intended to bestow an official rank upon him. The Master said, "I am about to cast off the worldly net and shall not dwell within the three realms;
how could I again thrust my head into the midst of profit and fame? I pray that you instead confer this upon my cousin, Jue. Thereupon, he shaved his hair and received full ordination.

Within a few years, his reputation resounded throughout the capital. In the spring of the third year of the Xuande era, Emperor Huizong conferred upon him the title Zhenshi (True Limit) and commanded him to reside [there].
Yuantong ascended the hall and said: "Twenty years ago, this mountain monk was blind in both eyes and could see nothing at all.
I only heard people say that above the blue sky there is a great sun-wheel that illuminates the three thousandfold world system, leaving no place unpenetrated.
Though I devised every possible strategy, I ultimately could not see it. Twenty years later, my visual faculty gradually..."
It opened. Furthermore, it happened that the sky was overcast with continuous gloom and thick clouds surging in disarray. He observed the four directions and investigated from above to below.
When he saw the clouds moving, he made calculations regarding their movement; when he saw the clouds staying still, he established a conceptual trap at the place where they rested.
Just as he was in this state, he suddenly encountered a man of great knowledge who asked him: "Do you not wish to see the sun?"
"Lunma, why do you not go to the summit of a high mountain? The mountain monk then questioned him, saying, "Where is the summit of a high mountain?
He replied, "It is where the red dust of the world does not reach. O virtuous ones, what an excellent and authentic message!
Do you understand? On the long continuous bed, it is Buddha. Entering the hall:
Last night, the Yellow-Faced Gautama took the three thousand great thousandfold world-system and swallowed it all in a single mouth, like a person drinking hot water;
no trace remained, and it was instantly dissolved. At that moment, the great Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Arhats, and all sentient beings—
None of them perceive or know it at all; only Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra catch a fleeting glimpse of it.
Although they see it, it is vast and boundless, as if emerging from and submerging into the great ocean. You people, tell me: what kind of news is this?
If you can examine and penetrate it, I grant that you possess the single eye atop the crown of your head. Thus he showed.
The cremation was performed in silence; wherever the smoke reached, it all became *śarīra*. A stupa was built at Mount Kongshan, and the remains were interred separately on the Shidai Stone Plain.

Zen Master Zhennu Daohui of Taizhou ascended the hall and said: "If one is willing to take responsibility for the affairs of the empty kalpa, they are fully manifest in daily life—what leakage could there be?
It is exactly right to return home and sit in peace, letting the snow cover the green mountains, leaving nothing behind."
The original word remains hanging in the mind. Who would care about the waves turning over the surface of the water? But tell me:

when the orthodox does not establish the mysterious and the partial does not cling to things—how can you bring up this single phrase? When the shuttle-head is free from the threads of the loom, the patterns may run wild, yet the meaning remains distinct.
Chan Master Jingshen Zhitong of Xingguo Army was the son of the Wang family of Taizhou. From his youth, he was extraordinary among his peers.
At the age of eighteen, he received the tonsure under Master Dezhi at Guangdu Monastery. He first visited Chan Master Xiang of Jingci Monastery.
One day, hearing Xiang say, "To think and seek through knowledge, or to resolve through deliberation—these are all the livelihoods of ghosts," his inspiration could not be restrained; thus...
He went to Baofeng to seek entry into the inner circle. Baofeng said, "You must sever the thoughts of arising and ceasing; clear away all traces of the profound path before the void kalpa;

do not involve yourself in the orthodox or the biased; exhaust the present moment entirely. Only when you have let go of your whole body, letting go until it is utterly exhausted, will you have a share of true freedom.
Upon hearing this, the Master suddenly grasped its essential meaning. Baofeng beat the drum and announced to the assembly, "He has deeply attained the state of an icchantika."

This is the Way of the Great Death; those who have newly entered the study should rely upon it. For this reason, he was titled the Old Man of Great Death. In the first year of the Jiānyán era, he opened the Dharma for Zhìtōng.
Entering the hall, he said: "Coming, one does not enter the gate; going, one does not leave the door. Coming and going leave no trace—how can one proclaim this?"
It has reached the point where the ancient path is sealed with moss, the wild sheep leave no tracks, the moon of Cangwu is locked away, and the vermilion phoenix does not alight.
Thus it is said: "Where the body is hidden, there are no traces; where there are no traces, do not hide the body.

If you can act in this way, then going and staying will be without dependence, and there will be no turning toward or away. Do you understand this? Now we are scattered like clouds and cranes; you and I...
[The Master] forgot the profoundity of the sense-base of touch. A monk asked, "What is 'the partial within the central'?
The Master said, "An old woman with a black face wears a white silk sash. [The monk] asked, "What is 'the central within the partial'? The Master said, "A white-haired old man wears a black robe.
[The monk] asked, "What is 'coming from the central'? The Master said, "Performing somersaults in excrement. [The monk] asked, "What is 'arriving at the combined'? The Master said—
[The Master] said, "Snow-bladed weapons encircle his body, yet he is not wounded by them. [The student] asked, "What is 'reaching within the integration'?

The Master said, "Kunlun walks through the night. [The student] asked, "Is there anything further above this? The Master said, "To catch a turtle and call it a soft-shelled tortoise. [The student] asked, "I beg the Master to grant me another expedient means.
The Master said, "Entering the mountains, one encounters a tiger and lies down; leaving the valley, a ghost comes to pull one away. [The student] asked, "How can this be?"

They confronted one another with weapons. The Master said, "Three or two strands; a catty of hemp. At the beginning of the Xiangshu era, he returned to reside at Baocangyan, where he lived among the common people in their attire.
In the second month of the Ren-shen year, he manifested a slight ailment and said, "My worldly ties are exhausted.
On the thirteenth day of the third month, he gave a small-scale sermon (xiaochan) for the assembly and spoke this verse: "No need to shave the head; why bother to bathe? A single heap..."
"Red flames! A thousand feet, ten thousand feet! Although it is thus, tell me: is there still something further above?
Thereupon, he closed his eyes and passed away.
Zen Master Huayan Zhipeng of Hengzhou was the son of the Huang family of Siming. He relied upon Baofeng for many years without attaining realization.

Because the various bowl-holders [had gathered], Feng himself inscribed his own portrait, saying: "Rain-washed, the tender petals of the pale-red peach; Wind-swayed, the light filaments of the shallow-green willow.
Within the shadows of white clouds, strange rocks are revealed; In the luster of green waters, ancient trees are clear. Alas! Who are you?
When he arrived at Mount Jiao, Chan Master Kumu Cheng saw it and sighed, saying: "Only today do I finally understand."
This old man personally saw his former teacher arrive. The teacher then requested instruction on the latter’s eulogy.
Cheng said, "Have you not seen how Fayan took up the story of Jianshan’s 'scenery' and said, 'For twenty years I have only understood it as scenery'?

At this, the teacher attained awakening. (The *Luohu Yalu* states: Cheng pointed his finger and asked the teacher, "Do you understand? The teacher said, "I do not understand. Cheng said, "Do you remember Fandeng’s imitation of Hanshan? The teacher then recited [the verse] until he reached the line, "Who knows this meaning? It makes me recall Nanquan," at the character "recall" [yì]).
While at Chushi, Cheng suddenly covered the Master’s mouth with his hand, saying, “Stop! Stop! At that moment, the Master had a sudden realization and said, “So this is how it is!

Cheng asked, “How do you understand this? The Master replied, “In spring it grows; in summer it matures; in autumn it harvests; in winter it stores. Cheng said, “You must maintain this realization. The Master responded with an affirmative nod.

At the beginning of the Shaoxing era, he went forth to reside at Huayao and Tianning in Wuzhou, later moving to Qingliang. While presiding over the assembly, he ascended the hall and said: “The sea wind...”
"Blowing through dreams; the gibbons of the ridges cry to the moon. I dare ask you all: what season is this?

If you can understand it thus, you may roam freely beneath the shadowless tree. If not yet, you must strike through to the bottom beneath the three rafter-poles. Later, he retired to Ruiyan in Mingzhou.
Qingliang of Jiankang again entreated him to return, and the Governor of Ming also urged him to go; however, the Master would not.
He then composed a verse to send with the messenger, saying: "Troubled by your commission, you envoy have entered the misty clouds; The embers are cold, there is no broth, and I cannot brew tea.
I send these words to the worthy Governor of Yongdong: It is difficult to make a withered tree bloom again. Not long after, he passed away.
Chan Master Qingyuan Qi of Qizhou was a successor of Chan Master Shimen Yi.
He was the son of the Chen family of Fuzhou. At the age of twenty-eight, he took leave of his father and elder brother to enter the monastic order under Chan Master Yungai Zhi.
He served as the head assistant (shouzuo). One day, after the master had finished presiding over the *bifu* (the distribution of the Dharma), the teacher asked him: "I..."

Hearing what the Head Seat had said, he did not understand its meaning and humbly hoped for compassionate instruction. The Head Seat exhorted him earnestly, leading him to investigate this Dharma of non-attachment.
After two days, he attained realization and presented his understanding in verse, saying: "In expounding the Dharma, nothing is as intimate as this:
The ocean of lands in the ten directions is but a single mote of dust. If one can clearly realize the True Principle herein, The great earth..."

"Since when have you ever seen a single person? [The Master] was startled by these words. Consequently, he spoke to Zhidu and attained liberation. He traveled extensively, visiting various masters everywhere, until he finally arrived at Shimen, where he deeply received the master’s recognition and approval.
He left to reside at Qingyuan for barely twelve years. On the day of his passing, he spoke a verse to the assembly, saying:
Last night, past the third watch, I crossed a swift rapids; at the head of the rapids, clouds and mist were vast and black.
With a single staff as my true companion, I shattered a thousand barriers and ten thousand gates.
Chan Master Tianyi Facong of Yuezhou ascended the hall and said: "The cold lamp in the dark chamber needs no lighting;
the bright moon in the void pierces the clouds and sky. If you wish to know that daily life is ever without interruption, a strange sprout emerges from within the blazing flames.

At that time, while preparing to open the eyes of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, the Master climbed the ladder and took up his brush. Looking at the assembly, he said: "If you can speak [the truth], then..."
He prepared to take up his brush, but the assembly was speechless. The Master called to his attendant, saying, "Help this old monk firmly hold the ladder," and then he proceeded to dot it.
Chan Master Futtong of Xiangshan in Suining Prefecture attained realization while reciting the Lotus Sūtra. She subsequently went to visit Shimen.
He then said, "One cannot eat at Chengdu; one cannot eat at Suining. He then struck him with his staff.
Tong suddenly attained awakening and said, "Those who prosper do so of their own accord; those who decline do so of their own accord. Autumn dew and spring winds—how convenient they are!"

He shook out his sleeves at the gate and returned to the abbot’s quarters; the Master likewise turned away and departed. From this, both clergy and laity followed him in admiration, and many attained the Dharma.
He was a successor of Chan Master Jue of Jingyin.
Chan Master Huayan Zhenyi Huilan ascended the hall at Tōkyō. "The Great Master Bodhidharma sat facing the wall for nine years;

even before he had opened his mouth, he caused people to be filled with doubt. Yet, as soon as he was glanced at by the Dharma Master Shen Guang, his hands and feet fell into a state of frantic confusion, and he immediately declared:
'I have come to this land from afar / To transmit the Dharma and save deluded beings. / One flower shall open into five petals.'"

The result was naturally accomplished. At that time, had there been a man with eyes behind his head capable of illuminating past and present, and with tongs and hammers in his hands capable of severing through space, as soon as he heard such words, he would have grabbed him by the chest and asked:
"He said 'one flower, five petals'—set that aside for a moment; what is it that you transmit?"
This is the fundamental principle. Waiting for him to open his mouth, [Huayan] immediately overturned the meditation seat.

Even if it were Bodhidharma himself with his full capacity, he would have been forced to retreat three thousand li. This was to spare future generations from being burdened by the legacy of the past. How could Huayan remain idle today?
Not only did he restore the collapsed order of the Dharma, but he also sought to vindicate the wrongs of all people. He then took up his staff and held it across [his body].
He called to the assembly, saying, "Where has Master Bodhidharma gone? He then threw down his staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said, "At the assembly on Vulture Peak, it was called 'Plucking the Flower. Before the peak of Shaoshi, it was named 'Attaining the Marrow.
The virtuous ones of antiquity could only look on from the sidelines; the patriarchs of this final age all simply fold their hands in submission. Now, Huayan..."
The sun cannot be pursued by following the waves and ripples. If you intend to point out the springtime colors of the whole world before the ten-thousand-fathom peak, do you understand?
The skull has no joyous consciousness; the withered tree has the dragon’s cry.
