Daguang was truly a disciple of the Great Master Zibai from the Shen clan of Jigu. By nature he was fierce and bold; at seventeen, he shaved his head and traveled to study under various masters.
Upon hearing the recitation of Zhang Zhuo’s verse, when it reached the line, "Eliminating delusive thoughts increases the illness further," he rushed toward True Suchness.

This was wrong; he harbored great doubt. One day, during a vegetarian feast, he suddenly attained enlightenment and said, "Had I been under the seat of Linji or Deshan, a single slap would have awakened me.

Why did I need to travel to the capital asking 'how' and 'what'? Because Emperor Shenzong had personally transcribed the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* with ink so heavy it soaked through the paper, [the Emperor] suspected it might still be incorrect and urgently dispatched an attendant to consult the Master. The Master—

He offered this verse: "A single drop of the Emperor’s sweat shall serve as a bridge for ten thousand generations; from this, the inexhaustible treasury of Dharma shall radiate light. The Emperor was greatly pleased.
In the autumn of the *gui-mao* year, a seditious book suddenly surfaced. When the Emperor saw the memorial regarding [the Master], he felt great pity for him;

yet, as the laws could not be evaded, the Master was consequently arrested and subjected to interrogation. At that time, his countenance remained composed, and he refused to yield even unto death. On the fifth day of the twelfth month, he entered...
In prison, when the judicial authorities had sentenced him to death, the Master spoke a verse, saying: "A single laugh has its own underlying cause;
Who would have known that the Great Mass does not admit even a speck of dust? From this moment on, I shall gather up my mother-born feet; The iron stake shall blossom without waiting for spring."
On the seventeenth day, after finishing his bath, he instructed his attendants, saying, "I am departing. Please convey my thanks to all the Dharma protectors of Jiangnan.
Having spoken these words, he sat upright and passed away. He was sixty-one years old. His stupa was enshrined at Shuangjing.

Because the master felt that the scrolls of the Great Canon were too numerous for widespread circulation, he presided over the carving of the *Banzhe* (square-bound) edition to facilitate its dissemination throughout the four quarters. Furthermore, the master... [text continues].
His collected works comprise fifteen volumes and are widely circulated throughout the world.
The Great Master Lianchi Zhu Hong was a native of Renhe in Guhang. His surname was Shen. At the age of seventeen, he entered the local school (xiang).

Although he pursued the study of Confucianism, his aspiration lay in transcending the mundane world; he would frequently write the four characters "The Matter of Birth and Death is Great" upon his desk to admonish himself. (3)
At age eleven, upon the death of his mother, he went directly to Mount Xi (Xishan) to receive the tonsure under the Venerable Xing Tianli.

He received full ordination from the Vinaya Master Wuchen at Zhaokong Temple. Later, he traveled north to Mount Wutai to visit Bianrong. Subsequently, he visited Xiaoyan at Liuxiang Lane to seek instruction.
Xiaoyan said, "You have come three thousand *li* away seeking my instruction; what instruction do I have to give? The Master [remained silent].
Suddenly, he prostrated himself and took his leave. While traveling on the road through Dongchang, he heard the sound of the watchtower drum and was suddenly enlightened.
He spoke this verse: "The events of thirty years ago are still questionable; What marvel is this meeting three thousand li away? Incense burned and halberds cast—altogether it was like a dream."
The Mara and the Buddha vainly contended over right and wrong; he then returned south to reside at Yunqi. There he opened the gate of the Pure Land to gather those of the three capacities.
Consequently, the fourfold assembly flocked to him in great numbers. When Minister Wang Zongmu asked, "Last night the mice were chirping and recited the entirety of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra;
what happens when the cat suddenly appears? The Master said, "Wang! The Minister had no reply.
[The assembly] spoke. The Master himself provided a substitute reply, saying: "The Dharma Master has run away, leaving behind only his lecture desk.
He then recited this verse: "The mouse squeaks; the *Avataṃsaka* is clearly manifest. How strange! Minister Wang has been deluded by a beast. A cat suddenly leaps out before the painted hall;
At the head of the couch, he preaches the Dharma—no news of him. No news of him: the *Mahāvaipulya Buddha-avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the World-Ruling..."
The First Chapter: Wondrous Adornment. At the time of his passing, half a month prior, he addressed the assembly, saying, "I wish to depart for another realm.
The assembly could not fathom this. On the fourth day of the seventh month, he indeed manifested a slight illness and passed away while facing west.

His worldly age was eighty-one; his years as a monk were fifty. The Master had previously selected a site at the foot of a ridge to the left of the monastery, where his entire body was subsequently enshrined in a stupa.
His authored works, including commentaries on the sutras and various miscellaneous records, number more than twenty kinds and circulate in the world.
The Great Master Hanshan Deqing was the son of the Cai family of Quanjiao in Jinling. His mother conceived him after experiencing a miraculous dream.
At the age of twelve, he received the tonsure at Xilin Monastery in Baoguan Temple in the capital. At nineteen, he received full ordination and listened to lectures on the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.

In the School of the Mysterious (Xuánmén), he attained realization at the place where the Sea-Seal (Hǎiyìn) eternally abides amidst the arrayed phenomena. He subsequently traveled to various regions and became friends with Miaofeng.
Initially, he visited Bianrong and requested instruction. Bianrong received him by gazing directly at him in silence. He then read the *Zhàolùn* (Treatise by Sengzhao);
upon reaching the passage concerning the Brahmin who left home and returned with white hair, a neighbor saw him and said, "Is that man still here? The Brahmin replied: [The text ends here].
"I am still the person of old, yet I am no longer the person of old. Suddenly he attained awakening and said, "Today I have finally realized that my nostrils point downward.
At that time, Miaofeng saw him and asked joyfully, "What have you attained? The Master replied, "Last night two iron oxen fought."
He entered the water and was never heard from again. To this day, there has been no news of him. Master Feng laughed and said, "I am glad you have the capital for living on the mountain.
He then went to visit Xioayan. Xioayan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From the South. Xioayan asked, "Do you remember the path by which you came?
The Master replied, "Once passed, it is left behind. Xioayan said, "In that case, you understand the place from which you came clearly. The Master then prostrated. This was at the beginning.
He resided at Mount Tai, where he prayed for the Emperor’s succession. His reputation was immense. Later, to avoid notoriety, he went into seclusion on Laoshan in the East Sea.
Empress Dowager Lizheng treated him with profound reverence and personally bestowed upon him the purple robe and the Tripitaka. Subsequently, he suffered groundless slander;
a Daoist falsely submitted a memorial to the ancestral temple. Many of the ministers and high officials in the court deeply lamented this. Because...
Having received this imperial decree, he was censured for privately establishing a monastery and was sentenced to military exile in Leizhou.
Upon reaching Shaoyang, he paid homage to the Patriarch and subsequently remained at Caoxi. In the winter of the Bingchen year, he ascended Mount Shuangjing to carry the torch for Master Daguan;

monks and laypeople gathered in great numbers, causing the mountains and valleys to resound with their clamor. Later, he lived in seclusion on Mount Kuang for six autumns. [The Prefect of] Shaoyang and his own...
The provincial officials urged him to remain, but he firmly declined, requesting instead to dwell at Caoxi. The Master said, "Caoxi is where I formerly restored the Dharma.

He then took up his staff and traveled south. In the tenth month of winter the following year, on the thirteenth day, he suddenly addressed the assembly, saying, "My karmic conditions conflict with the times;
where can my transformation be entrusted? My work for this one period is finished; I shall return. After noon, he requested a bath and changed his robes.

The senior master, Xinxin Chan Master, said, "This old teacher has something to rely upon from my elder brother.

Xinxin refused on the grounds of mourning, but Huang insisted. Xinxin took up a torch and called to the assembly, saying: "It is not that remaining karmic retribution has accrued to me; my sins are as vast as the heavens and cannot be pardoned.
Now, with both legs kicking at the empty air, I shall surely become an ox or a donkey. He then [lit the funeral pyre] with fire.
Jù struck a circle with his staff and said, "I shall vindicate my grievance right here. He threw the staff, which ignited upon contact with his hand.
His remains were interred to the east of the Pujue Pagoda, and he was posthumously titled Chan Master Baojue.
Chan Master Changzong Zhaojue of Xinglong Temple in Donglin, Jiangzhou, was the son of the Shi family of Yanping.

Having long relied upon Huanglong, he received the secret transmission of the essential principles of the Great Dharma. He subsequently resided at Letan and later moved to Donglin; both appointments fulfilled ancient prophecies.
A monk asked, "Within the realm of heaven and earth, amidst the expanse of the universe, there is a single treasure hidden within the mountain of form.
What is this treasure? The Master said, "The bright moon appears; the dark moon vanishes. The monk said, "I have not merely heard its name; today I have seen it directly.
The Master said, "Tell me, where is the treasure? The monk said, "The doors of the ancient hall open, radiating brilliant light, beside the pond of white lotuses."
A person from within the assembly stepped forward. The Master said, "One who recognizes a treasure returns it to the blue-eyed barbarian.

Another monk came forth from the assembly, lifted up his sitting mat, and said, "I ask the Master to answer my question. The Master said, "Put it down. The monk then made a gesture as if to unfold the mat.
The Master said, "Withdraw it. [The monk] said, "In years past I sought the sword-wielder; this morning I have met the master. The Master said, "What place is this? The monk then...
"Ho! The Master said. The monk also shouted. The Master said, "Even if you let me go, how could you have won? He then struck him. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The great earth and the heavens constantly proclaim the perfect sound; the sun, moon, and stars always discourse upon the true mark (*dharmatā*).
I recall the former Huanglong saying: 'The autumn rain pours down, continuing from night until dawn; drop by drop it is impartial, falling nowhere else. He then added: "Furthermore..."
[The Master] said: "Drops [of water] pierce your eyes; they soak and rot your nostrils. Donglin, however, was not like this: "In the end, they return to the great ocean to become waves and billows.

He struck the meditation seat and descended from it. He ascended the hall and said: "Old Lu did not know how to read, yet he suddenly realized the Buddha’s intent. This is because the Buddha’s intent transcends words and ink.
Baizhao did not know how to write, yet he fully awakened to the school of the patriarchs. This is because the patriarchal school is not something that can be conveyed by speech."

With such a grandmotherly heart, he clearly entered the mud and water. People of the present day still cling to the bridge pillar to wash themselves and hold onto the mooring rope as they let their boat drift away.
After a long while, he said: "How can you blame the old monk?"
Chan Master Yun’an Zhenjing Keben of Baofeng in Longxing Prefecture was the son of the Zheng family of Shanfu.

While sitting out the summer retreat at Daguai, he heard a monk cite a question asked of Yunmen: "Is it true that the Buddha-dharma is like the moon in water? Yunmen replied, "In the clear waves, there is no path through.
The Master attained realization upon hearing this and went to see Huanglong, but they did not reach a mutual accord. He then remarked, "I have a fine point here."
"This old fellow does not recognize me," [he thought]. He then went to Xiangcheng to see Master Shun. Shun asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Huanglong.
Shun asked, "What sayings or phrases has Huanglong been uttering lately? The Master said, "Recently, the local government commissioned the Elder of Huangbo.
Huanglong gave a turning word, saying: 'Reciting hymns on the bell tower; planting trees beneath the bed frame.'"

Regarding the "Vegetables" (Cai) case: Someone offered a phrase that was in accord with the truth, so he went to take up residence as the abbot. The Senior Seat (Sheng) said, "A fierce tiger sits blocking the road.
Long then ordered him to go and reside at Huangbo. Shun, unaware of this, remarked, "The Head Seat Sheng only managed to offer a single turn of words."
He immediately attained realization at Huangbo’s place, yet he had not even dreamed of the Buddha-dharma. Only upon hearing these words did the Master attain great enlightenment;
he then realized the scope of Huanglong’s application [of the Dharma]. He subsequently returned to see Huanglong. Huanglong asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Master. Huanglong said, "It happens that I am away. The Master asked, "Where have you gone? Huanglong replied, "To Tiantai."
During a communal labor session while traveling the mountains at Mount Nanyue, the Master said, "If that is so, then this student has attained mastery.
Yunyan said, "Where did you get those shoes on your feet? The Master replied, "I bought them for seven hundred and fifty cash at Mount Lu. Yunyan said:
"How have you ever attained mastery? The Master pointed to his sandals and said, "How have I ever lacked mastery? The Dragon was struck with awe.
On the day he opened the hall, after offering incense for the Emperor and concluding the exchange of questions and answers, he said: "Let us cease this questioning.

You know only to ask about the Buddha and the Dharma, yet you do not realize the source from which the Buddha-Dharma comes. Tell me, from where does it come? He extended one leg and said, "In the past, Huang..."
Long! He personally carries out this command. Not one of the Buddhas of the ten directions dares to disobey; not one of the successive patriarchs or all the sages and worthies dares to overstep it.
It is the tongue of the old monks of the world regarding the immeasurable Dharma-gates and all their wondrous meanings.
From beginning to end, there is but one seal; none dare differ from it. Since there is no difference, let us set that aside for a moment.

Where does this seal reside? Do you see it? If you see it, you are neither monk nor layman; without partiality and without faction, it is bestowed upon each and every person. If you do not see it, I shall take it back myself.
(He then withdraws his hand and gives a shout, saying: "The army follows the seal’s turn; the general marches according to the talisman. Buddha’s Hand, Donkey’s Head.
"Feet are conditioned by old age; I would give thirty blows for such a painful statement. Is there anyone in this assembly today who does not find this bitter?
If there is, it is truly extraordinary. If there is not, then the new Elder is deceiving you all.
Therefore, our Great Awakened World-Honored One, in the past, on the eighth day of the twelfth month in the kingdom of Magadha, when the morning star appeared, suddenly..."
“The realization of the Way means that all sentient beings on this great earth attain Buddhahood at once.

Now, here is a śramaṇa, a son of the Śākya, in the city of Jinyang in the Great Song of Eastern Zhendan, on the thirteenth day of the sixth month, when the blazing sun is present—what else has he realized?
(He draws with his whisk and says: ‘I do not dare to look down upon you; you shall all become Buddhas.’”
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master laughed loudly. The monk said, "Why do you laugh? The Master replied, "I laugh because you produce interpretations based on words.
The monk said, "It was merely a chance failure. The Master shouted, "Do not prostrate! The monk then returned to the assembly.

The Master laughed again and said, "Producing interpretations based on words. You ask about the 'Buddha’s hand' and 'donkey’s feet' with which the masters of Jiangxi receive people—what about you, Master?"
"How do you receive people? The Master said, "A catfish climbing a bamboo pole. [The monk] said, "It is entirely because of today. The Master said, "A tortoise entering the water.

He asked about the "New Song" (Xinfeng yin) and the "Yunmen Tune" (Yunmen qu): "Throughout the world, those who know the music can harmonize and continue it; when the assembly is at the banquet, [how will they respond?]"
"I pray that you will clear my ears and eyes. The Master struck the meditation seat with his right hand. The monk said, "The wooden man claps his hands; the stone woman raises her eyebrows.
The Master struck the meditation seat with his left hand. The monk said, "This is still a point of doubt for a student.
The Master said, "Why do you not realize it beneath the heels? The monk gave a single sweep with his sitting cloth. The Master said, "What can you do about being beneath the heels? He asked.
From afar, the imperial edict was dispatched; the Chan Master humbly responded to the occasion. The Patriarch’s command was being put into practice.
Using skillful means, he pointed toward the deluded masses. The Master said: "Profound. [The student] asked: "What is the meaning of 'profound'? The Master said: "Shallow. [The student] asked:

"How should a student understand this? The Master said: "A dot. He asked about the venerable elders under Mazu: "Each and every one of them is thoroughly soaked, yet only Old Guy Guizong remains dry."
"Only slightly inferior. The descendants of Huanglong—each and every one of them is stark and bare.
Only Old Teacher Zhenjing is slightly inferior. Can you, student, support him like this or not? The Master said, "Clear away that heap of refuse right before you.
The monk said, "If one does not sleep in the same bed, how can one know there is a hole in the bedding? The Master did not answer. The monk said, "This..."
"For those of the highest capacity, it is one thing; but when suddenly encountering those of middling or inferior capacity, how can they be guided and received?
The Master did not answer. The monk said, "It is not only the Master who is at a loss; I, too, have met with a failure. The Master said, "In thirty years, you will realize it.
The monk asked, "I have heard it said in the past that sentient beings use it every day without knowing it. I do not yet understand this 'not knowing.'"
"What is it? The Master said, "Speak. The monk asked, "What is it like after suddenly attaining realization? The Master said, "One hundred and eight thousand [miles].
The monk held up his sitting cloth and said, "What about this? The Master then gave a shout. He ascended the hall and said:
"Heaven and earth share the same root as I; the myriad things are one body with me. From head to tail, they are horizontal and vertical, three by four. In the continent of Uttarakuru, fire..."

It ignited, setting fire to Śakra’s eyebrows. The Dragon King of the Eastern Sea could not endure the pain and let out a thunderclap so powerful it overturned the mountain peaks and emptied the deep pools, darkening the vast sky.
At that moment, Old Man Liao at the crossroads was startled awake from his drunken stupor;
he rose, clapped his hands, and laughed heartily, saying, "Recently there have been few thieves in the city of Jinyang. Thereupon, he picked up [his staff].
Holding up his staff, he said, "Thief! Thief! Ascending the hall, he said: "When the Way prevails, the Son of Heaven’s edict is not transmitted;
all travelers sing songs of Great Peace. 'Five nines make forty-five. Has anyone come from Huai Prefecture? If so, you must not forget the fermented soybeans of Linjiang Commandery.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The World-Honored One held up a flower; Kāśyapa smiled. Holding up his staff, he said, "Dong..."
Shan picked up his staff and said, "What should you all do about this? He struck the incense table and descended from the seat. He ascended the hall and said:
"The trousers have no crotch; the breeches have no opening. On their heads are three or five pecks of green ash. Old Zhaozhou is showing off too much."
Thus it is said: "When the nation is clear, the man of talent is esteemed; when the family is wealthy, the young child is arrogant. Yet, alas, the grain and millet do not flourish in the sunlight;
instead, people compete to plant peach and plum trees in spring. This causes those who toil in the fields to become, for the most part, peddlers of human faces.

Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "The two words 'Buddha-dharma' are truly difficult for people to grasp. Some do not believe in their own Buddha-work, relying instead solely on a few shadows of the ancients."
Echoes. This is similar to prajñā; regarding the objects of knowledge and the dharmas of fixed characteristics, if one moves, one immediately turns one's back on awakening and joins with the dust.
One becomes stuck and cannot escape. When students come, it is like using a seal to stamp clay—successively sealing and transmitting it to one another.
Not only do they deceive themselves, but they also deceive others. Under Dongshan’s gate, there is no Buddha-dharma to give to people; there is only a single sword. All...
Each of those who come here shall be severed one by one, so that their very lives shall not remain and both seeing and hearing shall be extinguished;
instead, you shall meet them before their parents were yet born. As soon as they step forward, they shall be severed.
Now then, though a sharp blade may be keen, it does not strike one who is innocent. Is there anyone who is innocent? Even so, thirty blows are well-deserved!
[He] leaned on his staff and ascended the hall. "Under the gate of Dongshan, if you wish to walk, you walk; if you wish to sit, you sit.
To defecate in the alms bowl and spit into the water pitcher while practicing by clinging to the Dharma is like an ox pulling a millstone. [He] ascended the hall. "Under the gate of Dongshan..."
Sometimes he blends mud with water; sometimes he stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
If you all intend to see Dongshan in the place where he blends mud with water, Dongshan is not to be found in that place where he blends mud with water.

If you intend to see Dongshan in the place where he stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, Dongshan is not to be found in that place where he stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. If you intend to see him in any place at all—
When you see Dongshan, Dongshan is not to be found anywhere at all. You intend not to see Dongshan, yet the nose-rope is already in Dongshan’s hand.
Even if you intend to nod off to sleep, he will give a tug on the nose-rope; you will only see your eye-sockets twitching, and still you will not recognize him.
I do not require you to recognize Dongshan; it is enough simply to recognize your own self. (End)
In the Hall: "Fenyang, do not harbor deluded thoughts! Juzhi’s finger—here, the matters of the Buddhadharma of all time and antiquity come to rest at once.
Rest, rest! Yet I recall Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman; even where there is no elegance, there is elegance.

He took up his staff and said, "Exerting one's utmost strength for the sake of the assembly. Ascending the hall: "The head-dhūta rock is enveloped in moss; the Throwing-Pen Brush Peak is overtaken by *bìlì* vines."
At the Chan Hall of Luohan Temple, three practitioners are ordained each year. At Guizong Temple, after the formal session, they drink tea.
Entering the hall, [the Master says]: "The lion does not eat the leftovers of the eagle; the swift falcon does not strike a dead rabbit. Let forth Linji, the Great Dragon!"
[He] drew it out. Yunmen glanced at him once, picked up his staff, and said: "The clouds move and the rain falls; the three types of grass and two types of trees [all receive its nourishment].

On the first day of the tenth month in the first year of the Chongning era, he manifested illness. On the *wang* day, he recovered. He brought forth his ritual implements and distributed them among his disciples.

The following night, at midnight, he bathed, changed his robes, and sat in the lotus position. When the assembly requested him to preach the Dharma, he presented a verse and his final instructions. This is the Great [Master of the] School Gate.
Briefly: Having finished speaking, he passed away. At his cremation, the flames formed five colors; a white light ascended upward, and wherever the smoke reached, there were śarīras.
His bones were divided and enshrined in stupas at Letan and Xinfeng.
Chan Master Yuandao of Yunju Zhenru Monastery in Nankang Commandery was a native of the Wang family in Xinzhou.
A monk asked, "What is the essential meaning of Daolin? The Master said, "Zha! [The monk] said, "Recognizing one's nature as it flows with the current, there is neither joy nor sorrow.
The Master said, "How heavy is your skin bag? [The monk] said, "Look up with high eyes. The Master said, "Go out by yourself. [The monk] asked.
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The heavens of Hu are weighed down by snow; the jade qilin.
"How is it when [the mind] is like a tortoise withdrawing its six limbs? The Master said, "The patterns are already manifest. "Despite this, how can one avoid leaving no trace anywhere?
The Master said, "I leave you free to drag through mud and water. "If one goes in this very way, what then? The Master said, "As expected. (He ascended the hall.)
The Hall. The Tathāgatas of the past have not re-examined this; the Bodhisattvas of the present cannot let it pass;
and those who practice and study in the future must not deceive themselves by even a single point. Therefore, the teachings state:

"If one wishes to fully understand all Buddhas of the three periods of time, one should contemplate the nature of the Dharma-realm: all is created solely by the mind. Although this is so, [the matter remains as follows].

Under the Yunju Gate, it is truly like gold dust falling into one’s eyes. [He] ascended the hall and said: “The vision of the ordinary and the vision of the sage are like spring clouds flashing with lightning;
true speech and false speech are like flowers in the sky or the moon reflected in water. This makes me recall when Longbeard saw Shitou, who could say: ‘A single point of snow upon a red furnace.
He struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall. [He] ascended the hall again and said: “Using tortoise hair for arrows and hare horns for a bow—Narāyaṇa is enraged.”

In a fit of rage, he shot an arrow that pierced through space; space collapsed, causing mountains and valleys to crumble. Walls, tiles, and rubble emitted brilliant light as they took refuge in the Tathāgata’s Great Perfect Enlightenment.
Striking his meditation seat, he descended from it. Entering the hall, he said: "The moonlight blends with the clouds into white;
The sound of pines carries the chill of dew. What a truly marvelous message! Rely on you gentlemen to examine it closely. Master Huanglong [previously] harmonized his entire being...
"Knock it down! Is there anyone who can pick it up again? When the patriarchs and ancestors could not finish their work, the calamity falls upon their descendants.
[He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it. Ascending the hall, he said: "All sounds are the voice of the Buddha.

With his whisk, he struck the meditation seat and said, "The Brahma-sound is profound and far-reaching, causing those who hear it to rejoice. He further said, "All forms are the form of the Buddha," and then held up the whisk, saying, "Now..."
The Buddha emits radiance to assist in the unfolding of the meaning of the true mark (*dharmatā*). Those who have already arrived should receive it upon their heads and practice it;

those who have not yet arrived should know it thus and believe it thus. Striking the meditation seat, he descended from his position. The three pagodas currently found in various regions were first established by this Master.
Chan Master Daopei Huaixiu of Tanzhou was the son of the Ying family of Yingzhou.

A monk asked, "In the past, the Water Buffalo of Mount Gui was let loose and its traces were lost; today we are fortunate to meet the Master ascending the seat—where, then, should people of this age seek it?
The Master said, "One must not trespass upon the crops. The monk said, "If that is so, then its horns and head are already clearly manifest."
The Master said: "In vain you hold the iron whip given by the mountain boy.

Chan Master Huangbo Weisheng Zhenjue of Ruizhou was the son of the Luo family from Tongchuan. While he was residing at a center for scriptural study, his fan happened to strike against a window lattice with a sound.
Suddenly, he recalled a passage from the teachings: "When drums are struck in all ten directions, they are heard in all ten places as one..."
Upon hearing this, he attained great enlightenment. He informed his original lecturer, who instructed him to go and inquire further. The Master went directly to Huanglong.
Later, because the Governor of Ruizhou commissioned Huanglong to select a successor for the abbotship of Huangbo, Huanglong assembled the assembly and posed this koan:
"Reciting hymns on the bell tower; planting vegetables beneath the bed frame. If anyone can explain this, they shall go to serve as the abbot. The Master stepped forward and replied: "Fierce! (Měng).
The tiger sat blocking the road. Long was greatly pleased and consequently sent the Master [Huangbo] there. From this, Hui-fang came to revere him. Entering the hall, he said:
"Linji’s shout and Deshan’s staff are left for Zen practitioners as models. Gui-zong grinds the Xuefeng ball; this kind of teaching style receives those of superior capacity.
If it were Huangbo, however, it would be otherwise—there would be neither shout nor staff. Furthermore...
It is not ground by a millstone, nor is it rolled like a ball. Before you is the front mountain; behind you is the main mountain.
It blocks your eyes and crushes your face. If you can see this, you will attain the stage of non-retrogression and, until the end of time, seek nothing from others.
If you cannot see this, the supreme flavor of *amṛta* (clarified butter) turns instead into poison. [He] ascended the hall and said: "Silent..."
Vast and silent! The bright moon descends into the empty valley. Expansive and wide! The blazing sunlight flows across the four seas.
On the road to Caoxi, the passage of people is cut off; before the Many Sons Stupa, the crowds are as dense as a marketplace.
Even if you can realize it here with such distinct clarity, it is not yet the livelihood of a patch-robed monk. A man of great character must turn toward the darkness.
In the dark prisons, shackles are struck and fetters are beaten; within the ranks of hungry ghosts, fire is set and drink is snatched away.

The Tower of Maitreya is toppled, and the Hall of the King of Emptiness is demolished. The auspicious sprouts and rare grasses are uprooted by the roots, leaving thorns to grow across the entire earth.
Chan Master Yousheng Fazhu of Longxing Prefecture was the son of the Zheng family of Chaoyang. In his later years, he met Huanglong, under whom he received profound certification.
He ascended the hall and said: "This matter is like a physician’s prescription for diagnosing an illness. Furthermore, when one's belly is filled with various poisons, it is not easy to treat;

it requires a medicine that causes dizziness and nausea before recovery can be achieved. Even if one were to administer it according to one's own whims, it would only serve to further delude and confuse them."
To aggravate his chronic ailment while seeking to cure it—is this not perverse? The weeds before the Dharma Hall grow deep, yet he feels no shame in his heart.
Chan Master Ziqi of Kaiyuan Temple in Qizhou was the son of the Xu family of Quanzhou; he relied upon Kaiyuan Zhina to undergo the scriptural examination.

Having attained liberation, he refined his practice in the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and the *Awakening of Faith*. He went to visit Chan Master Zhen of Cuishan and asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma.
Zhen spat on the ground and said, "Where does this single drop fall? The Master rubbed his chest and said, "I have a stomachache today.

Zhen smiled. He took his leave and went to study under Jicui. After more than a year, he fully mastered the Way. On an occasion when there was leisure time, he attended Jicui to discuss and deliberate upon the teachings.
In ancient and modern times, it happened that there was a heavy snowfall. Cui-zhi said, "Can this be swept away with a single broom? The Master said, "It cannot.

[Cui-zhi continued,] "Then when the sky clears and the sun rises, and the clouds and vapors disperse, would they exist again? For one who knows this, regarding all words and phrases, it is like splitting bamboo;
though there be a hundred joints, each shall be severed at the blade's edge as it meets them—how could there be any room for sound in deliberation?"
One day, Cui sent a monk to inquire, "What are the meanings of the Old Monk’s Three Barriers?

The Master replied with a stern voice, "Why do you concern yourself with matters from long ago? Upon hearing this, Cui marveled all the more at him; thus, his fame spread throughout the monastic community.
When Cui passed away, Zen Master Si Zu Yan appointed him to share his seat. In his quarters, the Master posed this koan: "There is one person who has a mouth but cannot speak; what is his name?
Later, when the lineage reached Donglin, Zen Master Zong sighed, "The Head Seat Qi is like a ten-thousand-fathom iron mountain;
it will be difficult indeed to engage his verbal pulse. Not long after, as Kaiyuan was being established as a Zen monastery, they invited the Master [to serve there].
On the first day of the month, he ascended the hall and said: "Space has no interior or exterior; phenomena and principle have their long and short.
To follow [the Way] is to realize Bodhi; to oppose it is to produce affliction. The lantern-lamp is always dozing; the pillar is likewise vexed.
The Great Way is right before one's eyes—where else would you go to seek it? He struck the meditation seat with his whisk. Ascending the hall, he said: "The four sides have no doors; the ten..."
There are no walls or fences; their hair is disheveled and their ears stick out. Every one of them is a true man, a great hero. How can they be without ropes yet bind themselves?
Tell me, how would you express the single phrase of total liberation? After a long silence, he said: "The straw sandals are worn through;
walking barefoot. A monk asked: "I do not ask about Mount Sumeru containing a mustard seed. But regarding the turning of the Great Dharma within a mote of dust—"
"How is it when turning? The Master said, "One step forward, one step further. He asked, "If that is so, then arriving in India in the morning and returning to the land of Tang in the evening?
The Master said, "Being away as a guest is not as good as returning home. He said, "I have long admired your reputation for the Way; I pray that you will grant me an audience."
The Master said: "The clouds and moon are the same; the streams and mountains are each different.

Chan Master Xingwei of Yangshan in Yuanzhou was a native of the Hexi region. He received full ordination at Daci Temple in the Eastern Capital and studied the *Complete Enlightenment Sutra* (Yuanjue), yet harbored some slight doubts.
He took up his traveling bag and journeyed to various quarters, single-mindedly seeking the meaning of the Patriarchs' intent. Eventually, he arrived at the Dharma of National Teacher Nan.

While seated, as the stars shifted six times in succession, he once more requested instruction. He was immediately shouted out; just as his feet were about to cross the threshold, he suddenly realized the profound essence of the Way.
He went on to Mount Yangshan, where his reputation for the Way became widely renowned. Entering the hall, he said: "Do you all understand?

The affairs of antiquity cannot be concealed; the affairs of daily life cannot be hidden. Since they cannot be hidden or concealed, they manifest before us in our daily activities. Now, let me ask you all—"
"Person! As for the matter before you, how is it? *Chan!* Entering the hall, he said: "Does the assembly see? When the eyes are open, one universally contemplates the ten directions;
when the eyes are closed, one encompasses all existence. What is the appearance when neither opened nor closed? Do you still see that appearance?
Those of long-standing practice and high virtue will understand as soon as it is raised. For those who are beginners and new to the path, recognize this appearance; do not merely keep on..."
You are addicted to sleep. When you are asleep, what do your eyes see? If you say you see nothing, how are you any different from a dead man?
Even if the Master of Painted Colours were to paint green waters and blue mountains, or peaches and apricots amidst bamboo on the tip of his brush, it would still be merely a semblance.
Even if a stonemason were to carve out herds of sheep and running beasts with the point of his chisel, they too would be merely a semblance.
This is its true form. Even if it were a master craftsman or a stone mason, there would be no place for them to apply their tools.
If you all wish to see it, you must truly open your eyes. After a long silence, he said: "Broad, it is a single thread;
narrow, it is an inch and a half. He struck the meditation seat with his whisk. As the drum sounded, the assembly gathered like clouds. Everyone ascended...
[The Master] looked up. "When this mountain monk looks down and looks up, what does he look at? What does he look down upon? After a long pause, he said:
"Facing each other, we do not recognize one another. He ascended the hall and said: "The Way is not in sound or form, yet it is not separate from sound and form.

Every word and every silence, every movement and every stillness—whether hidden or manifest, whether expansive or transverse—all are nothing other than the Buddha-work. It is present in daily life, throughout the ages."

He remained in profound stillness. How could the principle be otherwise? The Master himself inscribed his own portrait, saying: "My true likeness is difficult to capture; it is mottled and variegated.
If I wish to arrange it, the moment I set down my brush, I err. He passed away. Upon cremation, five-colored śarīras were obtained, and his bones and stones were found linked together by cords.
He was enshrined in a stupa to the east of the temple.
Chan Master Cigan of Fuyan on Mount Nanyue was a native of the Du family from Tongchuan. He ascended the hall and said: "The heart of the ancient Buddhas is right here and now.
If you do not understand it, you will suffer in deep reflection. The autumn rain falls gently; the autumn wind blows briskly. Shifting here and there, how can one respond?

Chan Master Shouzhi of Yungai in Tanzhou was a native of the Chen family in Jianzhou.

In this final age, when the Buddha-dharma has become diluted and corrupt, there is no use for the patriarchs' nostrils, no use for the adamantine eyes, no use for the lion’s claws and fangs, and no use for the staff that kills or brings life. There is only a single fly-whisk used as a path;

it can manifest in all manner of transformations at will, rolling up or unfolding according to its natural course, and it can also tower high above gods and humans, standing like a cliff ten thousand feet tall.

At times, when encountering strength, one yields; at times, meeting with nobility, one appears base. When picked up, the hosts of demons vanish from sight and the Buddhas and Patriarchs hide their tracks.
When set down, it blends with water and mud, such that sages and ordinary people share the same path. Now tell me: is it better to pick it up?
"Let it go—excellent! From the tip of the pole, you may play with the silk line; without disturbing the clear waves, your intent is naturally distinct.
[He ascends the hall. "Form and mind are not different; self and other are without distinction. Raising his whisk, he said: "If you call this a whisk, you will enter hell like an arrow.
If you do not call it a whisk, you have eyes but are as if blind. Even if you manage to escape both extremes, it is still black."
A cow lay dead in the water.
Chan Master Qingyuan Weixin of Jizhou ascended the hall and said:
"When I was thirty years ago, before I had studied Chan, I saw mountains as mountains and waters as waters. Later, when I personally encountered a teacher and attained a point of entry..."
Seeing mountains as not mountains; seeing waters as not waters. Now, having attained a place of rest, one sees mountains as simply mountains again, and sees waters as simply waters.
Great assembly, are these three kinds of understanding the same or different?
If there is someone, whether monastic or lay, who can discern this, I grant that you have personally seen the old monk.
Chan Master Xiaochun of Lingquan Monastery in Jiashan, Lizhou, once carved a creature out of wood with the head of a lion, the hooves of an ox, and the body of a horse.
Every time he ascended the hall, he would hold it up and show it to the assembly, saying: "If you call this a lion, it is also..."
It has the body of a horse; it is called a horse’s body. Yet it also has the hooves of an ox. Tell me, ultimately what should it be called?
[The Master] had the monk offer a response, but none were in accord. The Master then presented this verse: "A majestic lion’s head, With ox-hooves and a horse’s body."
The three paths are as they can be entered; the profound gate opens layer upon layer. [Ascending the hall: There is a man who, since vast kalpas past, has had neither dwelling nor reliance.
Above, there is not a single tile to cover his head; below, there is not an inch of earth for him to stand upon.
Tell me, in the twelve hours of the day, where does he establish himself and sustain his life? If you can know this, then morning you go to the Western Heaven, and evening you return.
In the eastern land, there was Chan Master Jichang of Sansheng in Hanzhou, a native of the Li family in Pengzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "The wooden Buddha does not pass through fire;
before the Terrace of Ambrosia, he meets Bodhidharma. Alas, the people of Luoyang have not yet arrived; for nine years, facing the wall, all is empty and cold."
Seated. A golden Buddha does not cross the incense burner. Seated, he sighs over the toil of life as one races along the road.

Had he not looked upon the painting at Mount Hua, how could he have known Pan Gu riding a donkey backward? A clay Buddha does not cross water. A single ray of numinous light illuminates heaven and earth.
One can truly admire the old "ancient spike" Xuan Sha, who did not want the South Mountain but wanted the turtle-nosed snake. [He] ascends the hall and cites Zhaozhou’s visit to the two...
The abbot said, "The young masters of the Five Tombs vie with one another to boast of their wealth; the high monk in his hundred-fold patched robe does not disdain poverty.
Lately, the ways of the world have become much inverted: people value only the clothes they wear, not the person within."
Chan Master Shuangling Hui of Longxing Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Green bamboos and yellow flowers are not external objects;
white clouds and the bright moon reveal the complete reality. Every single thing is a possession of our own house; picked up at random by hand, it is no mere dust.
He then raised his whisk and asked, "Do you understand? If you recognize it, it is as before—not it. He struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall.
A monk asked Chan Master Xiaozhin of Guishan Shuilu Monastery in Sizhou, “What is the guest within the guest?
The Master said, “Chao Fu feeding his ox. The monk asked, “What is the host within the guest? The Master said, “Xu You washing his ears.
The monk asked, “What is the guest within the host? The Master gave a shout. The monk asked, “What is the host within the host? The Master said, “Having finished prostrating.”
[The Master] withdrew. He ascended the hall and said: "The ground is firm and secure; yet transgressions fill the heavens. It is evident that one cannot lift one's feet.
To play with supernatural powers is to wound oneself where there is no wound; thus, one cannot even set foot down. Now tell me, where does the fault lie?

Let those who possess the eye of a seeker of the Way come forth and debate this together. If you wish to see the mountain of your own true nature, do not take the forked paths. Do not [dwell in delusion].
They merely continue to nod their heads, wasting the years and months. At some future time, when the blow of the staff descends upon the crown of your head, do not say that I did not warn you.
Chan Master Benquan of Baofu in Zhangzhou was a native of Linzhang. By nature he was straightforward and courageous in the Way. Thus...
At Huitang’s place where he raised his fist, [Dongshan] thoroughly realized the root source. His wit and eloquence emerged with swift brilliance.

When Huang Shan谷 (Shan Gu) had first attained some entry into the Way, he asked Huitang, "Who here is capable of engaging in discourse? Huitang replied, "Quan of Zhangzhou. At that time, the Master was supervising laborers while they were clearing land for fields.
Shan Gu, together with Huitang, went to pose a question, saying: "Head of the quarters, do you know of the pillar giving birth to a child? The Master—
He said, "Is it a man? Is it a woman? Huang hesitated. The Master struck him. Huang said, "You must not be so discourteous.
The Master said, "This blockhead! If I do not strike you now, when shall I? Huang laughed heartily. Later, ascending the hall, he cited a verse by Hanshan, saying: "My mind is like the autumn moon;
/ A clear, bright pool in a deep abyss. / Nothing can be compared to it; / How can I tell it to others? Old [Master Huangbo].
The monk, however, was not so; he said, "My mind is like a lantern: when the fire is lit, it is red both inside and out. There is something that can be compared to it:

tomorrow morning, the sun will rise in the east. Those who heard this took it as a joke. When Master Sijian saw it, he sighed and said, "If Brother Quan’s teaching is such as this, he truly does not fail the entrustment of his former master."
Chan Master Jingqi of Shuangfeng on Mount Wudang in Tanzhou ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said:

"Held horizontally or used upside down, throughout all quarters it is wielded with the gait of a tiger and the stride of a dragon; for beating dogs and propping doors, Shuangfeng has cast himself into the armor of non-action.
Letting the wind blow the fire—this is a family tradition of its own. Leaning the staff against his shoulder, he looked at the assembly and said: "To call this 'non-action'—"
"Is it so? After a long silence, he said, "The blade and the ruler hang high; look with your own eyes. Master Zhigong was no ordinary monk.
He struck his staff once.
Chan Master Jingxin Jitang of Huguo Temple in Wenzhou, a native of the Chen family of Jun, ascended the hall and said: "In the three realms there is no..."
Dharma. Where shall one seek the mind? If you wish to know the "phrase of facing Yang" for protecting the state, look at the grove of bamboo before the gate.
One day, when the assembly had just gathered, Chan Master Huanglong Zhiming of Ezhou ascended the hall and said, "I cannot go on opening my eyes to speak of dreams.
He then descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "A single secret of the north and south—cutting through nails and severing iron."
"Be absolutely careful not to engage in deliberation; it will only turn into a habitual track. The Master, together with Inspector Hu, arrived at the Two Sages Temple in Gong'an.
Inspector Hu asked, "Dharma said to Emperor Wu of Liang, 'Vast and empty, there is no sage. Why is it that there are two sages here in Gong'an?"
The Master said: "A single drop of ink forms two dragons.
Chan Master Zhongyuan Daowu of Tanzhou ascended the hall and said: "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing.
When the ancients spoke thus, it was like peering at a leopard through a tube; one sees but a single spot. Even if one enters the forest, one must remain unmoving."
Grass. Entering the water without stirring the waves; it is also like riding a horse across jagged ice.
If one were a master at shooting down a vulture, why not rub an itch on the head of a snake? Let those who possess the true eye try to discern this. After a long while, he said:
"The embroidered mandarin ducks emerge from the golden needle."

The Grand Historian and Layman of Shanyu Valley, Huang Tingjian, styled Lüzhi, possessed the karmic predispositions of Prajñā from former lives; thus, though he held high office, he remained detached.
He entered and exited various Buddhist schools without finding a definitive direction, and he was fond of composing flowery verses. Once, he visited Chan Master Yuantong Xiu, who rebuked him, saying:
"A man of such noble character—how can you be content to apply your exquisite skill in calligraphy to such things? It was then that Xiu began to admonish him.
Regarding the matter of Li Bashi’s painting of horses, the Master (Dongshan) rebuked him, saying, "Are you not placing me once again within the belly of a horse?

Xiu replied, "You stir up the lustful hearts of all people under heaven with your lewd words; it is not merely a matter of being in the belly of a horse—I fear you will actually be born in the *niraya* hells.
The Master was struck with awe and repented, apologizing for his error. Thereupon, he ceased his brushwork and devoted himself solely to the Way, composing the *Fayuan* (Vow of Aspiration).

The text records: [Wen] strictly observed the precepts against wine and women, eating only morning congee and the midday meal. He went to rely on Huìtáng to request instruction on the direct and swift path.
Huìtáng said, "As for what Zhòngní said, 'Do you think, my disciples, that I am hiding anything from you?
I hide nothing from you,' how would you, the Grand Historian, explain this in your ordinary discourse? Wen attempted to respond, but Huìtáng said, "Not so, not so. Wen—
He remained in a state of persistent bewilderment. One day, while attending to the assembly during a mountain walk, the fragrant osmanthus was in full bloom.
Master Tang said, "Do you hear the fragrance of the osmanthus flowers? The official replied, "I do. Master Tang said, "Is there anything I have hidden from you?

The official felt a sudden release and prostrated himself, saying, "How can the Master possess such a compassionate and earnest heart? Master Tang smiled and said, "It is simply that I wish for you to reach home. Long ago...
When he went to visit Yunyan, Chan Master Sixin Xin received him with the assembly. As Xin entered the room, he opened his eyes wide and asked, "Elder Xin has died, and you, Scholar, have died.
Once we have been cremated into two mounds of ash, where will we meet? The official was speechless.

Xin Yuochu remarked, "What you attained while practicing under Huītáng has not yet truly settled. Later, when you were demoted as an official to Qiānnán, your power of the Way grew even more superior.
Amidst a state of non-thought, you suddenly clarified what Sīxīn had asked. He sent a letter in reply, saying:

"In years past, I was constantly subjected to your rigorous prodding, yet for a long time I remained like one in a drunken dream, with things appearing only vaguely within a realm of light and shadow. This was because my doubts had not been resolved."
My life-force remains unbroken; thus, I have merely retreated from the precipice. While in exile in Qian-Nan, as I lay sleeping during the day and awoke, I suddenly reflected:
"How much have I been deceived by the old monks of the world? Only the monk Sixin refused to grant me his seal of approval;
this was truly the greatest act of compassion toward me, and I consider myself most fortunate. Later, he composed the inscription for Huichang’s stupa.

The inscription reads: "I, [Name], have long since received the seal of transmission and am capable of upholding the Great Dharma. Yet, as my eye of the Way has not yet reached full perfection, I come now to gaze upon this stūpa;
truly, I am moved by a profound sigh of veneration and admiration. Therefore, I have engraved these words upon solid jade to reverently praise his enduring excellence.

The Master further prepared an offering of water plants and wild vegetables, making sacrifice with a prose text and offering consolation with a verse, which says: "The wind of the sea blows down Mount Laṅkā; the Chan of the four seas..."
Look directly with your own eyes: A handful of willow threads cannot be gathered; they are draped with mist upon the jade balustrade.

Wenwang Shao, a lay practitioner whose style name was Zichun, was appointed as the Governor of Hongzhou. He then invited Huìtáng to inquire about the Way, and through silent realization, he attained a profound accord.
Consequently, he composed a verse on seizing the vital point, which says: "By day I forgot to eat, by night I forgot to sleep; I have grasped the pearl from the dragon's jaws."

When wishing to ascend to heaven, one must instead cast everything down within oneself; the four corners collapse to the ground, yet it remains perfectly round. He presented this to the Hall Master (Huitang), who deeply approved.
Layman Wu Xun, a secretary and a man of virtue named Defu, was once staying in Huitang’s inner quarters. Huitang said to him: "Throughout your life..."
He was learned and possessed great memory and erudition, yet he did not inquire [further]. [Zhaozhou] said, "Before your parents were born, bring me a single phrase.
As the official hesitated, the Master struck him with his whisk. He immediately grasped the profound meaning and presented three successive verses.
The last of them read: "Ha! This worldly fellow of vast knowledge, who has chewed through all the public cases of past and present, suddenly picks up [a jewel] from amidst a heap of refuse."
He obtained a dung-ball from a dung beetle; it was so utterly worthless that it was not worth a single coin. Ten thousand taels of gold could not buy it.

He casually picked it up and showed it to others, simply because the "running plate" (the shifting focus) is difficult to observe. *Ei!* Tang replied: "To find fire in water is rare indeed in this world."
Looking at this, one cannot help but harbor doubts. Since ancient times, there have been no masters and disciples; yet now, it is permitted that the Old Barbarian knows.
—The Dharma Heir of Chan Master Donglin Zong.

Chan Master Letan Yingqian of Longxing Prefecture was the son of the Peng family of Yuanzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "The numinous light shines through with penetrating clarity, utterly transcending the sense organs and their objects.
Its essence reveals the true permanence, unconstrained by written words. The nature of mind is unstained; it is fundamentally perfected from the very beginning."

"Simply by being free from delusive conditions, one is the Buddha of Suchness. When the ancients spoke thus, they did not realize it was a pitfall—a flesh-bound undershirt that one cannot strip off nor pass through.
You must be like a lion cub, standing upright like a thousand fathoms high, before you can utterly sever [delusion].
Even so, such a person is still an old crow in a cloth bag. [The Master] struck the meditation seat and descended.
The Record of Chan Master Guangjian Xingyuan of Mount Lu. He was the son of the Mao family of Guizhou. A monk asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "Ten thousand acres of fertile fields. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not plow in spring, you will have no hope in autumn."
A question was asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Junshan pierces through Lake Dongting. The monk asked, "What is the intent of this?
The Master said, "White waves surround on all four sides; from where does the red dust come? He ascended the hall and said:

"To discuss the profound and explain the wondrous is like painting a cake to satisfy hunger. To enter the holy and transcend the mundane is much like a moth flying into a flame. To proceed in this manner..."
This matter is like rotten seeds and scorched sprouts; to seek it further is like grasping at the moon in water.
With a single sweep of his whisk, he said: "All those views you had just now have been swept away. What is the one phrase through which all of you must penetrate?
After a long silence, he said: "The iron ox does not eat the grass by the fence; it sleeps directly atop the summit of Mount Sumeru. He struck with the whisk.
Zuochan (Zen) Hall. Ascending the hall, he drew the bow of Shigong and nocked the arrow of Xinghua; exerting the strength of Nārāyaṇa, he fixed the gaze of Śakra.
He did not shoot the great hero-tiger, nor the deer of Yaoshan, nor the lion of Yunyan, nor the monkey of Xianggu.

But tell me, what was he shooting at? After a long silence, he said: "I let this one point pass. Ascending the hall. *Note: The term "shàngtáng" (ascending the hall) refers to a formal discourse given by a Chan master from the high seat in the meditation hall.*
One must reach the summit of the mountain; one must reach the bottom of the sea; in studying the Way, one must reach the place where even Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot speak it.
If one does not do so, one is nothing but a spirit clinging to grass and wood, a ghost-child consuming the spittle of wild foxes.
When Huayan speaks thus, it is like a potent medicine; though it may be bitter to the taste, it is intended to cure the illness. A-ye, a-ye!
Chan Master Fajing (法鏡) of Lushan Yuancongkeqian was the son of the Chen family of Yanzhou. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "An inch nail and an ox’s strength. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Go and study that which you do not understand."

Chan Master Xiangtian Fanqing of Shaoxing Prefecture was a native of Jiaxing. His secular surname was Qian. A monk asked, "For what purpose does the Bodhisattva Mahākaruṇā employ so many hands and eyes?
The Master said, "The wealthy man finds even a thousand mouths too few. The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is the True Eye?

The Master said, "We have lived together from the beginning, yet you do not know its name. [Another] asked, "A cold wind has suddenly arisen; what of the patch-robed monks? The Master said, "... (text fragment).
The furnace was opened. Suddenly, he recalled how Danxia burned the wooden Buddha; why did the temple steward fall out his eyebrows and whiskers?
The Master said, "When Mr. Zhang drinks, Mr. Li gets drunk. [The student] asked, "Is this yielding to strength when encountering it, or is it the exercise of wondrous spiritual power?"
The Master said, "The Holy Monk in the hall understands this matter. A monk asked, "Xiangtian possesses the sword for slaying dragons;
how would it be to borrow it for a moment? The Master held his staff crosswise. The monk then shouted. The Master threw down the staff.
The monk was speechless. The Master said, "This dead shrimp! He ascended the hall and said: "Spring is already fading; fallen flowers fall in profusion like a crimson rain."
Whether travelers from north and south return or not, thousands upon thousands of forests resound with the cries of the cuckoo. I have no home; where shall I return?
In the lands of the ten directions, upon what can I rely? This old man has a true message: last night at the third watch, the moon was reflected in the pond.

[Ascending the hall: The Buddha-Dharma has reached this point; life is as precarious as a thread hanging from a string. Even those of extraordinary vision who transcend their lineage find it difficult to inherit and sustain it.
He held up his whisk and said: "Fortunately there is this which can serve as a means for its transmission.

If you can perceive it here, you will see that the Buddhas of the three periods of time turn the Great Dharma Wheel within the lanterns and the pillars; that sentient beings of the six realms hear the essentials of the Dharma within the Iron Ring Mountains;
and that through sound and non-sound, and seeing form and non-form, each according to their various types of fourfold birth, attains liberation."
"Deliverance! To raise such a cry is not only to bury the ancestral style, but it is also to sink oneself into oblivion.
Now tell me, how can one avoid transgressing the command? [He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
At Hōshin Shōtokuin in Tokyo was Zen Master Raibutsu Kaishin, a native of the Chen family of Xinghua Commandery. He first visited Zen Master Nanyuan of Huanglong.
Huanglong asked, "Have you come for the sake of human affairs, or have you come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma? The Master replied, "I have come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma.
Huanglong said, "If you have come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma, I shall grant it to you right now," and he struck him with his whisk.
The Master said, "Even a monk must not trouble others. Long immediately took this to heart. Later, under Zhaojue, he profoundly realized the profound mysteries.
He ascended the hall and said: "In the Buddha-worlds, the Buddha-work is performed by means of every speck of dust and every hair.

To cause those who see a single dharma to be fully endowed with all dharmas, it is provisionally established as a 'storied pavilion. Within the realm of the Buddha’s transformation, one transcends words."
Silent stillness constitutes a great Buddhist service (*buddhakārya*). It causes those who study it to depart from all marks (*lakṣaṇa*); this is precisely what is called being a Buddha.

Therefore, I am fond of bestowing the "three strikes" and the "flaming ladle. In certain Buddha-lands, yellow flowers and green bamboo constitute the Buddhist service, causing those who behold these forms to see that form is itself emptiness (*śūnyatā*).
For this reason, I have entrusted [the Dharma] to Maitreya. In other precious Buddha-fields, the emptiness of phenomena (*dharmasūnyatā*) serves as the service.
Seated, he manifests Buddha-activities so that practitioners do not cling to seeking the Buddha; thus, having thoroughly investigated and realized it, there is a Buddha-field within the hook.
Through the four requisites of offering, he accomplishes Buddha-activities, causing those who know contentment to sever divergent thoughts;
thus, one may descend with him. There is a wondrous realm of the Buddha where all speech and samādhis perform his Buddha-activities, causing—
As for those who enter spontaneously, they do not abandon movement or stillness; thus, they serve as the channel for the cargo. The assembly, tell me:
is there any distinction of superior or inferior within this? After a long silence, he said: "Those who arrive must know they are masters. *Chan*.
A monk asked Chan Master Kechang of Huili Monastery in Linjiang Commandery, "I do not ask about the power of the Buddha or the power of the Dharma;
what is the power of wisdom? The Master said, "To trample down the mountain of self and person, and to raise up the tree of Bodhi.

The monk asked, "Since Bodhi is fundamentally no tree, where does one apply effort? The Master said, "Where there is no place to apply effort, that is precisely where one must exert effort. The monk said, "Now..."

Today I have heard what I had not heard before. The Master said: "Do not mistake pure gold for brass. Entering the hall, he said: "The source of the Buddha-dharma cannot be realized through anything other than right faith;
even wondrous wisdom cannot bring about its awakening. The pivot of the Patriarchs' teaching cannot be opened by anything other than great compassion; how else could it be unlocked?
When one possesses both faith and wisdom, the provisional and the real are practiced together, like gold within its ore. When one possesses full compassion and vows, [the good...]"

Evil can be discerned; it is like the moon emerging from the clouds. Great assembly, suppose it were before your parents were even born—where would you have these many metaphors to express yourselves?
After a long silence, he said: "Nine out of ten words being correct is not as good as one moment of silence."
Chan Master Desong of Qizhen Monastery on Mount Bazhi in Huangzhou ascended the hall and said: "Heaven and earth are but one finger—there is no heart of contention.
The myriad things are but one horse—there is no discourse of right and wrong. Thus, the Māras hide their tracks and the Buddhas and Patriarchs flourish.
Hanshan claps his hands in joy; Shide laughs out loud. O assembly, these two ancient sages laugh!"
"What is it? After a long silence, he let out a great laugh and said, "A single *tánhuá* flower meets spring once more.
Chan Master Shao Ci of Wanshan Monastery on Mount Lu was a native of the Zhao clan from Guizhou. He studied under Chan Master Zhaojue.
Shao Ci asked, "Aside from the golden robe bestowed by the World-Honored One, what else did he transmit? Zhaojue raised his whisk. The Master said, "Ultimately, how is it so?"
Jue struck him across the mouth with his whisk. As the Master prepared to open his mouth, Jue struck him again.
At this, the Master attained realization; he then seized the whisk and prostrated himself. Jue said, "What principle have you seen that you prostrate yourself?
The Master replied, "The whisk now belongs to me. Jue said, "A veteran of thirty years has been defeated today by a mere recruit. He then departed.

This profound style of teaching spread far and wide, and he was ranked as the foremost leader of Donglin. When ascending the hall, [his teaching] was such that "the initial practice had not yet reached its limit," like Mount Sumeru standing amidst a vast river;
yet "the final conclusion went too far," like a fierce warrior loosing a wild arrow. Sometimes high, sometimes low, there was no fixed standard;
thus, what was affirmed here was negated there, leading him to be scrutinized by others. Now tell me, how can one attain resonance? This is truly so.
Jiur said: "In the flames of the red furnace, more fire is added; the blazing vajra-eye opens of its own accord. *Duḥ*! He ascended the hall and said:
"The supreme mechanism of our Ancestor’s distinct practice is纵横 (transverse and vertical) in life and death, leaving no room for suspicion. Although it blocks the path of the foxes,"
"The counter-throw must be returned to the lion cub. Is there anyone among this assembly with golden fur blazing forth, with fangs and claws fierce and formidable?
Try coming forward and letting out a single roar! After a long silence, he said: "Even if you were to do so, you could not escape the hook and the snare of Master Liáo of Yùxī. *Cán* (Enter)."
A monk asked Chan Master Daobian of Nanyue Hengyue Monastery, "Setting aside for a moment the raising of the mallet and the brandishing of the whisk, how do you, Reverend, guide others?
The Master said, "When a guest arrives, one must receive them. The monk said, "Is this not the very point of guiding others?
The Master said, "Coarse tea and plain rice. The monk bowed. The Master said, "You must know its true flavor before you have attained it."
In the lineage of Chan Master Zhizhuan of Mount He in Jizhou, a monk asked: "A single-stringed lute—please ask the Master to play a melody.
The Master said, "This mountain monk is deaf. The monk said, "I am here seeking instruction. The Master said, "Go away. The monk said, "Where is your compassion?
The Master said, "There are eyes everywhere in all directions."
Master Yulu of Baqin Jingde Temple in Tokyo ascends the hall: "The drum is beaten in Silla; the assembly enters the hall in Great Song.
The cypress tree in front of the courtyard poses its question; the lanterns and the pillars are in a flurry. The incense stand and the staff rise to perform a dance;
the sick Vimalakīrti still remains upon his bed. You old fellow! I know your ailment well. Do not be surprised by my boisterousness. *Duḥ*!"
Chan Master Kūi of Longquan on West Mountain in Longxing Prefecture ascended the hall. When the assembly had gathered, the Master said:
"To disperse just as you are would be quite marvelous. Nevertheless, even so, it is already like stirring up waves where there is no wind, or driving a stake into empty space;

how much more so to drag in branches and extend vines, speaking of the marvelous and discoursing on the profound? This is truly like gold dust becoming an obscuration in the eye, while the pearl remains within one's own garment."
"The Dharma is the dust upon the mirror. Now tell me: who is it that sweeps away the dust and removes the dross? [The Master] plants his staff upright and descends from the seat.
Chan Master Zhien of Doushuai in Nankang Prefecture ascends the hall and says: "Loose and easygoing, dwelling in the village or the city;
vast and unrefined, what is now and what is ancient? Do not value your own spiritual essence; cease talking of Buddhas and patriarchs. I seize Śākyamuni by the nose!"
A hole! Uncover the ears of Avalokiteśvara; let him roll his ball on the snowy peaks. Do not concern yourself with Heishan beating the drum.
If one is a monk of true substance, one will never sit and wait by a stump for a rabbit. *Chan*.
Chan Master Kangyuan of Xingfu Monastery in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "I, this mountain monk, possess a secret method that I have never leaked in the past;
today I shall not conceal it, but will explain it clearly for you. After a long pause, he said: "When it is cold, it is cold; when it is hot, it is hot."
The Venerable Huìyuán was the son of Mr. Suān of Zhūnzǐ. His family had been farmers for generations. In his youth, he relied upon Déguāng of Jiànfú Monastery in his native district as his teacher.
By nature he was blunt and simple, yet he was diligent in the ancestral Way, sitting steadfastly without lying down. After several years, he received full ordination.
He traveled to Mount Lú and reached Dōnglín, where he frequently inquired about his own spiritual practice. When his peers observed his appearance...
He was humble. His deportment was unconventional and coarse, so everyone mocked and ridiculed him. One day, while walking through the palace courtyard, he suddenly tripped and fell.

At that moment, he attained sudden enlightenment. He composed a verse and had an attendant write it upon the wall, saying: "This one fall, this one fall— Even ten thousand taels of gold would be worth it!
A hat upon my head, a bundle at my waist; I carry the clear wind and bright moon upon my staff. Thus it was.

The sandalwood tree: "When there is spirit, it adds to one's spirit; where there is no elegance, it is elegant nonetheless.

The Master said: "Entering this contemplation of the nose, one personally realizes the unborn. Furthermore, the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* asks: "How does the hearer hear?

Regarding the sense-faculties: the ear-faculty lacks cognitive awareness; therefore, it cannot hear. If it were the ear-consciousness that hears, because the ear-consciousness lasts for only a single moment, it could not perform discrimination and thus should not be able to hear.

"Dust. [The Master said: "If the five objects of the past and future were merely consciousness, and if the mental consciousness (*manovijñāna*) could perceive the five objects of the present, then even the blind and the deaf should be able to perceive sound.
