It is indestructible. Whether following or not following, it is merely a matter of forcefully pricking with needles and awls based on what one hears and sees.
"The Taihu Lake spans thirty-six thousand acres; the moon is at the heart of the waves—whom does it speak to? A monk asked, "What is a guest among guests?

The Master said, "Wearing straw sandals and carrying a bamboo staff, one wanders through the red dust. The monk asked, "What is a host among guests? The Master said, "Meeting the Patriarch at the crossroads. The monk asked, "..."
“What is the guest within the host? The Master said, “The golden whip guiding the horse mingles with the four classes of people.
“What is the host within the host? The Master said, “Who would dare lift their eyes to gaze upon the golden gate? “I have already received the Master’s instruction on guest and host;
as for the supreme vehicle (zōngchéng) beyond this, what is it like? The Master said, “Last night the frost wind scraped the earth with its cold; an old monkey cries atop the ridge.”
*Can Yue* (The Waning Moon).
Zen Master Shouzhuo Changling of Tiantong Monastery in Dongjing, a native of the Zhuang family of Quanzhou, ascended the hall and said:
"Among three thousand swordsmen, only Zhuang Zhou was permitted [to pass]. Why could he not leap out? The gate of a skilled physician is filled with many patients. Because...
What need is there for even a single note? Those who have already passed through the barrier, please examine this further with discernment. Entering the hall, he said:
"It is like the faculty of sight, which cannot see its own nature. When one is spontaneously equal and there is no 'equality,' then one proceeds in this very way—like an unperforated iron hammer."

For the time being, let us set this aside. It must simply be that entering the forest without stirring the grass, or entering the water without ruffling the waves—this too is but a provisional expedient for the duration of one’s life.

If, however, the bamboo shoots within the fence emerge as sprouts outside the fence, and the flowers on the east side of the stream bloom red on the west side, then we shall wait to examine him further before striking.
A monk asked: "When Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, why did the temple master's eyebrows and beard fall off?"
The Master said, “A cat can climb a tree. [The monk] said, “Had I known it was thus earlier, in the end it would not have been so.

The Master said, “Spare your eyebrows. [The monk] asked, “What is the matter beneath the patched robe? The Master said, “When the heavens are parched, one grieves for the people. [The monk] asked, “How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world?
The Master said, “Not a hair’s breadth, not a speck of dust. [The monk] asked, “How was it after he appeared in the world? The Master said, “It fills [the void].”
He blocked the ditches and filled the ravines. Someone asked, "How far apart are 'already emerged' and 'not yet emerged'? The Master said, "When a person is level, they do not speak;

when water is level, it does not flow. He ascended the hall and said: "Leveling the high to accommodate the low is to invite a thief to ruin one's house; cutting through iron and chopping through nails—yet the fox still clings to its den."
It is not like that at all. How should one act? Therefore it is said: "To personally let go at the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff requires such a person.

As for the single phrase regarding holding the alms bowl in the Land of Fragrant Accumulation—how do you speak of it? After a long silence, he said: "One must strictly avoid being blown by the wind into another tune.
He ascended the hall and said: "Śākyamuni’s closing his room was an offense as vast as the heavens; Vimalakīrti’s refusal to speak..."

He was unable to save himself. How tragic, how tragic! His faculty of speech was too narrow. On the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month in the fifth year of Xuande, he suddenly manifested his passing into nirvana.
On the day of his cremation, the Emperor dispatched an imperial messenger to bestow incense; holding a golden platter, the messenger sought for *śarīra*.
Once the incense had been burned, there was a metallic *keng* sound within the platter. Upon inspection, several five-colored grains, each as large as a bean, were found therein.
The messenger returned with it, and when the Emperor saw it, he was greatly pleased.
On the New Year’s Day, Chan Master Jing of Boshan Wuyin in Xinzhou ascended the hall and said: "Harmonious breath arises from withered stumps;

cold clouds disperse across the distant outskirts. The wooden man divines the auspicious omen; at midnight, the tortoise-shell reveals its lines. All you venerable Chan practitioners, the tortoise-shell has revealed its lines."
The patterns are already manifest; one sees the twelve months of the year, each month being thus; the twelve hours of the day, each hour being the same.
Reaching this point, it is truly like the yellow of gold and the whiteness of white jade;
from the beginning of vast kalpas, it has never been of a different color. Do you see it? If not yet, then for now follow Zhang San’s three breaths.
Regarding the sequence of the seasons, let us follow the teaching that Li Si’s hair has turned white and disheveled.
At Baizhang in Longxing Prefecture, there was Master Qiseng, a native of Xinghua. He ascended the hall and said: "Kāśyapa Mātanga came to the Han, and Bodhidharma came to the Liang;
once the tracks have been laid, the descendants of later generations open their eyes and lose their way. If you are one who is truly alert and aware—"
In the end, one never picks flowers from the sky or grasps the moon in the waves; such toil of mind and body is ultimately for what?
Today, I, this mountain monk, have already raised a pile of bones upon level ground. As you all walk along, each of you must exert your full attention and look closely.
Chan Master Tanqing of Guangxiao Monastery in Shaoshan ascended the hall and said: "Killing one's father and mother is repented before the Buddha;
killing the Buddhas and the Patriarchs does not require repentance. Why does it not require repentance? It simply allows the enemy to find liberation."
Chan Master Guangxiao Deyou of Wenzhou was the son of the Qu family of Xingzhou. He received the tonsure at Zunsheg Monastery in Jingde.
After several years of seeking the Way, he went to Huanglong. Upon hearing the teaching on the sudden enlightenment through the wall-gazing of Shaolin, he composed two verses to present to him.
Huanglong approved them. From then on, his reputation spread throughout Jiangzhe. He ascended the hall and said: "The entire body is revealed, majestic and vast. Ten...
Just so, there is no obstruction; a thousand sages cannot transmit it, and ten thousand spirits wear it upon their crowns.
If you wish to deliberate upon it together, open your mouth and it will shatter into a hundred fragments. But what is it like before the mouth has even opened? *Pah!* [He] ascended the hall and said:
"Mutual accommodation or non-accommodation—look and there is nothing to be seen. Having penetrated the barrier of the Patriarchs, one tramples the path of gods and men. A-he-he!"
Whether awakened or not, where do the falling petals drift upon the flowing water?
The temple official, Layman Dai Daochun, whose courtesy name was Fuzhong, sought instruction from Lingyuan. One day he attained realization and presented this verse:
"At the bottom of the profound and dark source, where the total function resides, A single petal of the mind-flower reveals its imprinted pattern. I know how many lifetimes it has taken..."
He had once made offerings [to him]. From time to time, he would smile, causing clouds of incense to stir.
Chan Master Tang Daozhen of Huanglong Mountain in Longxing Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Letan Qing; he was the son of the Zhao family of Jinling. In his youth, he relied upon Jueyin.
Master Ying was a youth. When Ying moved his residence to Puzhao Temple in Si, it happened that the Imperial Consort was selecting youths for ordination;

thus, the Master received full ordination (*upasaṃpadā*). After some time, he took his leave and went to visit Chan Master Danxia Chun. One day, while discussing the fundamental tenets of the Dongshan school, the Master presented this verse:
"Thick white clouds deeply shroud the ancient, cold crags; Strange herbs and numinous flowers, with the auspicious phoenix riding upon them. At night..."

Half a day later, when it was near noon the following day, he was riding a cow with his back turned and wearing boots and a robe. Ch’un (Yunju) esteemed him; the Master himself felt that this was an obstacle and abandoned him to rely on Cao Tang (Dongshan Liangjie).
Upon their first meeting, they were in perfect accord. Every day he would take the Tripitaka to read. One night, hearing the drum for the evening sermon, he stepped out from the sutra hall.
Looking up, he saw the moon and attained great enlightenment. He hurried at once to the abbot’s quarters. From afar, Cao Tang saw him and immediately—
To certify this, he first resided at Cao Shan and subsequently moved to Guangshou and Huanglong. He ascended the hall and said: "I cite an ancient precedent to question you, *ācārya*.
You must not interpret it as something of the past; if you interpret it as something of the past, you lose the eye right before your face.
I cite a present-day precedent to question you, *ācārya*. You must not interpret it as something of the present; if you interpret it as something of the present..."

"Meeting. It obstructs the *ācārya*’s original eye. Even if it were neither lost nor obstructed—being neither ancient nor modern—it would still be a matter of medicine and disease counteracting each other, a mere teaching to stop a child’s crying.
As for that single phrase of total transcendence, can you say it, *ācārya*?
If you cannot, wait until I am at the summit of Luohan Peak, deep in discourse on the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*), and I shall speak to you then. [He] ascended the hall.
At Shaolin, he sat in cold silence, while his disciples each propounded divergent views—much like a group of blind men groping for an elephant.
When Shen Guang performed three prostrations and stood in his place, Bodhidharma said, "You have obtained my marrow. Yet this dark-faced Brahmin had not even touched the ground with his heels.
Entering the hall, a stone man asked a withered stump, "When will you bloom? The withered stump grew angry.
The stone man—how could he fail to speak? The stone man laughs aloud; the withered stump puts forth strange blossoms.
Crimson clouds illuminate the jade elephant; white jade grinds against golden sand. I ask the master who has penetrated the profound: who is there that has not returned home?
Chan Master Fayi Xuechao of Wanyan in Taizhou was the great-great-grandson of Li Gong Zunmian, the Grand Preceptor and Duke of Xiangyang.

His family had resided for generations in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng. His mother dreamed that an elderly monk arrived before she gave birth to him. At the age of seventeen, he sat for the imperial examinations at the Upper School (Shangxiang).
When his paternal uncle held office in Huainan and sought to appoint him to an official post, he did not accept. He was then about to renounce his home and serve under his elder [uncle].
Cijue Ze, the Zen Master, was not permitted by his grandfather. His mother said, "This child must have been a śramaṇa in a previous life;

I pray you do not thwart his resolve. Not long after, Cijue passed away. At the beginning of the Daguan era, he went to Lingyan to take the tonsure and receive full ordination under Zen Master Tongzhao Yuan.
He stayed with Yuan for ten years, yet he remained bewildered and unable to enter [the Way]. He then visited Yuanwu at Jiangshan, who said:

This man was a vessel of the Dharma. Upon receiving the imperial decree to move to Tianning Monastery in the capital, the Master attended him on his journey. At the end of the Jingkang era, he visited Caotang at Shushan;

after being instructed with a single phrase, he attained a sudden and complete realization of the Great Dharma. In the seventh year of the Shaosheng era, Liu Gong Yanxiu, the Governor of Quan and a recipient of the Baowen title, invited him to reside at Yanfu Monastery.
Later, he successively moved through four great monasteries. Once, ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "The staff..."
At times this staff becomes a water-dwelling dragon; then for ten thousand *li*, clouds and mist never cease. At times it becomes a crouching lion;
then for a hundred years, the tracks of monsters vanish. At times, mind and dharmas are both forgotten, and it stands alone as the manifest essence.
At times, illumination and function are simultaneous, and host and guest are used interchangeably. [The Master] drew with his staff and said: "Under the gate of Yanfu, all these are employed."
[He] struck [the seat]. "Tell me, what does Yanfu usually use? He planted his staff upright, gave a shout, and descended from the seat. He ascended the hall for formal instruction:
"Looking up, one does not see the sky; looking down, one does not see the earth. Before the ancient sword and the skull, the great ocean’s waves boil.
He retired from Changlu to the Wannian Guanyin Temple on Mount Tiantai. Suddenly, he manifested a slight illness. He wrote a verse, saying: "Now..."
At the age of seventy-five, he returned to serve as the abbot of the hermitage. "Precious and weighty is Avalokiteśvara! A clay snake swallows a stone tiger.
He entered his coffin, sat cross-legged, and passed away.

Chan Master Huikong of Dongshan Xuefeng in Fuzhou was a native of the Chen family of that same prefecture. At fourteen, he shaved his head and immediately traveled to various regions to visit many veteran masters.
In his later years, he attained realization at Caotang. In the *Guiyou* year of the Shaoxing era, he began teaching the Dharma at Xuefeng.

On the day he accepted the invitation, he ascended the hall and said: "Those who are quick-witted and spirited act as soon as they are pointed toward the truth; those who are dull and obtuse cannot be moved by being pushed or pulled."
If he moves, everyone rejoices; if he does not move, everyone feels resentment. I, this mountain monk, shall now transform this dull stupidity into a state of swift agility.
(He snaps his fingers once. Previously, though pushed and pulled, I could not come forth; now I have come forth.
Previously, there was a monastery where I would not dwell; now I dwell there. Previously, I loathed being a Buddha and would not act as one; now I act as one.

Previously, because of mutual dislike, I did not speak; now I shall speak. Setting aside for a moment the questions of whether one emerges or does not emerge, whether one abides or does not abide—let me ask you all:
what kind of Buddha is it that you have made? Is it the Buddha Akṣobhya (Empty-King Buddha)? Is it the Buddha Dīpaṃkara (Lamp-Lighter Buddha)? Or is it Śākyamuni Buddha?
"Maitreya Buddha? What dharma is that which you speak? Is it the fundamental dharma? Is it the dharma of non-arising?
Is it a worldly dharma? Or is it a supramundane dharma? Is there anyone in this assembly who can speak of it?
If you can speak of it, my work in appearing in the world is finished. If not, do not misrepresent it when you meet people. He gave a shout and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the example of Yunmen addressing the assembly, who said: "This very thing brings suffering upon people.
The Master remarked, "Yunmen’s usual bearing was like that of a king; to speak in such a manner is much like a poor man lamenting that he has too many bodies.
I, this mountain monk, am not so: this very thing brings joy to people. Why? Because when the heavy rain finally stops, one sits inside the house, free from the karmic winds."
He blew [his nose]. Then he walked around the mountain. Yet, even though it was thus, this too was like a beggar seeing small profit.
How would you express the phrase: "Furthermore, not harming the principle of things"? He ascended the hall and said: "One punch knocks down Yellow Crane Tower;
One kick overturns Parrot Isle. When there is spirit, add to that spirit; Where there is no elegance, there is elegance nonetheless. How magnificent! How magnificent!"
Ah! What joy, what joy! He is just like a seventeen or eighteen-year-old crown prince. Who cares for heaven? Who cares for earth?
When the sovereign mind does not move recklessly, the six realms are simultaneously penetrated. Lay down the three-foot sword; cease playing with the bow.
Free and easy, free and easy! What joy, what joy! It is just like an eighty- or ninety-year-old man acting as a ruler.
The signs are in accord: the winds blow at their proper time and the rains fall at their proper time; the five grains flourish and the myriad people live in peace.
Holding up his staff, he said: "O Great Assembly! These two, together with this mountain monk’s staff, shall together become a single patch-robed monk.
Upon reaching the gate of Xuefeng, he will simply know how to follow the custom and eat his fill; he will also have three coins to buy straw sandals. He gave a shout.
[Zhuo] leaned on his staff and descended from the seat. A monk asked, "What was it like before the Master had seen Caotang? The Master said, "It is there in Jiangnan.
The monk asked, "What is it like after seeing him? The Master said, "It is not there in Jiangbei."
Chan Master Yetao Puchong of Yuwang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture was a native of that same region. Addressing the assembly, he cited the words of Master Baling:
"It is not the wind moving; it is not the banner moving. If it is neither the wind nor the banner, where then does one place it?
He said, "If there is someone who can speak on behalf of the Patriarch, come forth and meet with Baling. Master Xuedou then said:
“The wind moves, the banner moves. Since it is both wind and banner, where else can they be placed?

Someone came forward to speak on behalf of Ba Ling, saying, “It is neither wind nor banner; there is nowhere for them to be placed. It is the banner and it is the wind; there is no place for them to rest.
The swift falcon soaring through the vast heavens loses its tracks; the golden-haired lion crouching on the ground likewise falls into confusion. Hehe!
Whether rebuked or awakened, it causes one to recall Master Xie Sanlang: "A single thread of line, fishing alone in the cold river rain.

Regarding the Dharma successor of Chan Master Qingyuan Xin, Chan Master Liangshan Huan of Tanzhou, a monk asked: "The great assembly has gathered like clouds; we pray that the Master will grant us instruction. The Master said: "Heaven..."
"In stillness, one knows not where the clouds have gone; because the ground is cold, the snow remains for a long time. The student said, "I do not yet understand these profound words.
I beg the Master to grant me further expedient means. The Master said, "Behind each mountain range lies another person."
Chan Master Zhengfa Ximing of Chengdu Prefecture was a native of Hanzhou. On the occasion of the lifting of the retreat restrictions, he ascended the hall and said:
"Leaves fall in profusion; heaven and earth announce the early autumn. This is clearly the meaning of the Western Patriarch—what need is there for further seeking?
If you can understand it thus, you will finally believe that the Way of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is fundamentally level and plain; the gate of great liberation has never had a lock or key."
It encompasses the universe and fills the void; its measure is inexhaustible and its wisdom unfathomable.

If one has not yet clarified this principle and reached its source, then even with the merit cultivated over a hundred kalpas and practices refined through a thousand lifetimes, one will merely exhaust oneself in vain suffering.

There is no mutual interaction whatsoever. If one deeply clarifies this principle and thoroughly penetrates its source, one will know that every movement and stillness, every action and undertaking, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, accords with the Way at every point and returns to the fundamental source in every thought. As the Patriarch said: "Delusion gives rise to stillness and agitation;
awakening is free from likes and dislikes. Let gain and loss, right and wrong, be cast off all at once. If this is so, who is deluded and who is awakened? Who is right?
Who is at fault? It is simply that these people alone have given rise to divergent views. They observe the great as small, and cling to existence and non-existence.

Their numinous spirit shines alone, yet they refuse to accept it; the moon of the mind is solitary and perfect, yet they naturally turn away from it. How is this different from abandoning one’s father within one’s own home?
A pearl was forgotten within one’s robes, causing thorns to form a forest upon the Path to Bodhi and clouds of delusion to shroud the sun in the sky of liberation.
Today, it is my good fortune that the Sangha has completed its *prātimokṣa* ceremony and the patron has returned to the mountain.
Since you virtuous ones have taken the trouble to visit me, I cannot remain silent; I shall, according to my capacity, engage in some discursive talk and provide a slight expedient for these times.
"You must all open your eyes and observe each of you with careful attention. If you further hesitate or engage in discursive thought, there will be ten thousand miles of white clouds.
He then took up his staff and said, "At this moment, you may clearly perceive that the assembly on Vulture Peak is solemnly present before you.
If this is not yet so, wait for tomorrow morning to receive my instruction."
After seeing Qingyuan, the Master of Zu’an built a hut among the peaks of Mount Heng. For over thirty years, no one knew of him. One day, moved by inspiration, he composed a verse:
"A small cauldron boils vegetables while rice steams above; The vegetables are cooked and the rice fragrant, yet people are still hungry.
Once the hunger-wound is healed, there is nothing more to do; Tomorrow morning, I shall paint a cat after this model. From this, the monastics [came to know him].
He struck it with a hazel stick. Master Zhang Wujin exerted great effort to persuade him to open a Dharma hall, but he did not comply. He ultimately passed away on this very mountain.
Chan Master Qinshan Qianming Puchu, a successor of Chan Master Jia Shan Chun, ascended the hall. After a long silence, he said: "To proclaim the fundamental tenet..."
I pray for the imperial foundation. I humbly wish that auspicious clouds and the celestial star may appear together; that the spring of nectar and the sweet dew may manifest as one.
May the sovereign be a ruler like Yao and Shun, and the customs of the people those of Cheng and Kang. Let this rustic hermit beneath the forest trees unconsciously compose a song of Great Peace.
But what, then, is this song of Great Peace? To act through non-action, to transform through the divine, and to dispense virtue.
The rain falls in torrents; the wind of benevolence blows in harmony and prosperity. The people are like wild deer; the sovereign is like the branches of a tree.
Whether the eighteen disciples know or do not know—*liri la*! *la li ri*! (A single clap of the hands. Descent from the seat.

Chan Master Xiyu Xianjing of Shengyin Monastery in Chu Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Ledan Qian. He was the son of the Gao family of that same prefecture. Once, he ascended the hall and said:

"Having traveled throughout the world, you should know that not a single step has ever been moved. Having passed through every gate and courtyard, you must find that in every household there is at least some smoke rising from the hearth."
Therefore, with staff over shoulder and rugged sandals on feet, he travels according to his inspiration; casting his hook and letting the line sink, he dwells as he pleases.

He does not seek out fine fields and lands in his native village; wherever the conditions are ripe, there he makes his home. Today, he picks up whatever comes to hand—how many times has he done this before?
His calculations never depart from the old patterns, yet every time it is raised, it is new again for those with clear eyes.
Upon a mere glance, he turned back. Let those who have not yet awakened recognize his true face. Now tell me: what is this original face? After a long silence, he said:
"The flowers bloom on the front stage, yet are seen from behind; the bell tolls in the upper realm, yet is heard in the lower.

He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended. Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: When the World-Honored One was in the kingdom of Magadha, preaching the Dharma for the assembly...
As the summer retreat was about to begin, he said to Ānanda, "My great disciples and the fourfold assembly of devas and humans have never shown reverence or respect as I constantly preach the Dharma.
I shall now enter the *iṃśa*-mortar chamber to observe the ninety-day summer retreat.
Should anyone come to inquire about the Dharma, you must speak on my behalf: 'All dharmas are non-arising; all dharmas are non-ceasing.'"
"Extinction. Having finished speaking, he closed his room and sat down. The Master called to the assembly, saying:

"When Śākyamuni first attained the Way of the Buddha, for the most part he had no choice but to do so. As soon as he had established this community, he already conceived a mind of weariness and retreat.
If Shengyin had seen him at that time, he would have driven a nail through the door of the room, leaving him with no way out for the rest of his life."
This is to prevent future generations from imitating one another. Have you not heard it said:

"If one does not transmit the Dharma to deliver sentient beings, one cannot be called a repayer of gratitude"? [He] struck the whisk and descended from the seat. Later, he lived in seclusion at Tianning in Lianyi.
Manifesting a slight illness, he wrote a verse, saying: "The shadow-play has ended; seventy-one years have passed. If you ask further what it is like, come back for another performance.
Having set down his pen, he passed away.
Chan Master Longya Zongmi of Tanzhou was a native of Yuzhang. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "Do not speak in your sleep. He asked, "What are all dharmas? The Master said, "Already fallen into the secondary. One day, he ascended the hall, and the assembly had gathered.
The Master said: "It is already a perfect whole; there is no need for carving or polishing. Return to the hall for tea. He ascended the hall and said:

"Do not take the flowers in the courtyard to be like this body. When the courtyard flowers have fallen, spring comes again. But once this body has departed, who knows where it will go? The vast expanse of the three realms brings nothing but sorrow to the heart."
Chan Master Zujian Congmi of Dongchan Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of Tingzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "To open one's mouth is not Chan;
to close one's mouth is not the Way. If you step forward with the intent to advance, your whole body will fall into the weeds."

Chan Master Putong Jiao of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture was the son of the Bi family from Wanling in the same prefecture. From childhood, he was exceptionally intelligent; before reaching the age of twenty, he received full ordination.
He went to Nanping to study the teachings of the Tiantai school and subsequently served as a patron for performing *chánmó* (confessional repentance) rites. Someone asked him:
"Regarding the sins you confess through this rite, are you confessing for yourself or for others? If you are confessing your own sins, from where does the nature of sin arise?"

When he attempted to repent for another’s transgressions, the other said, "How can you possibly repent for someone else's offense? The Master was unable to respond and subsequently changed his robes to travel as a wandering monk.
Upon arriving at Letan, his foot had barely touched the threshold when Letan scolded him. As the Master prepared to ask a question, Letan immediately brandished his staff and drove him away.
One day, Letan suddenly called out, and when the Master arrived in the master’s chamber, Letan said, "I have an ancient kōan that I wish to discuss with you."
As the Master was about to offer a word in response, Xuedou Tan suddenly shouted. The Master attained sudden enlightenment and burst into loud laughter.
Tan descended from his rope seat, took the Master’s hand, and asked, "Do you understand the Buddha-dharma? The Master then shouted and pushed him away. Tan laughed heartily.

Thereupon, his fame spread in all directions, and students revered him as their master. Later, he returned to his hometown; while staying at Tiantong, he remained in seclusion behind closed doors, sweeping away all worldly concerns.

In the eighth year, as the seat at the monastery happened to be vacant, the local officials ordered the Master to expound the Dharma. Fearing that he might flee, they had previously dispatched an official to wait for him on the road;
thus, he could not decline. On the day he accepted the invitation, he ascended the hall and said: "Alas, you old man with the yellow face! You have entrusted the Buddha-Dharma to kings and ministers.
This dispassionate guest beneath the forest trees is being driven to his death by an official summons. Is there no one who knows the bottom of the heart? Pray, save me from this!"
"Ma! If there were not [this], one could not help but take a wrong for a right. He then descended from his seat. Whenever the Master saw a monk approach, he would invariably scold him, saying:
"When you had not yet taken up the walking staff, I had already explained it for you. But tell me, what did I explain? He would then beckon with his hand or wash his bowl.
"Holding up a fan, drawing a bow; Zhaozhou’s ‘cypress tree,’ Lingyun seeing the peach blossoms—set these aside for a moment.
This mountain monk has no such leisurely lips to engage you in such tangled webs. Why not simply rest? With these words, he took up his staff and drove them out.
On the twentieth day of the third month in the sixth year of the Xuande era (1124), he bathed, ascended the hall, and spoke this verse, departing with ease.

Ji. The verse says: The jeweled staff knocks upon the void; wherever it touches, spring arrives. Within this, the message is uniquely all-encompassing. Last night the wind stirred, and the cold crag grew chill;
A clay ox was startled awake to plow the white clouds. His age was seventy-seven; his years since ordination were fifty-eight.

Chan Master Yuantong Daomin Yuanji of Jiangzhou was popularly known as an "Ancient Buddha. He was the son of Cai of Xinghua. His mother dreamed of swallowing a *maṇi* jewel before she became pregnant.
When he was five years old, his feet would not touch the ground and his mouth would not speak. His mother carried him to visit Ximing Temple;
upon seeing a Buddhist statue, he suddenly stepped onto the floor, pressed his palms together and recited, "Namo Buddha," and then performed a prostration. This greatly amazed the people.
Disgusted with this, he went to study in Daliang, where he relied upon Master Dexiang at Jingde Temple to take ordination. He passed the scriptural examinations and received full ordination.

He traveled everywhere to seek out and challenge masters, gaining a taste of their teachings from all. He stayed with Chan Master Zhe of Mount Wei for the longest period; later, admiring Letan, he went there to pay his respects.
Datan saw that the Master was silent and respectful. When the Master recounted the realizations he had gained from his various teachers, he did not receive Datan’s seal of approval.

Datan brought up the story of the World-Honored One holding up a flower and Kāśyapa smiling, and asked about it; again, the Master did not accord with him. Later, while attending Datan as they were walking along, Datan rested his staff on his shoulder, sighed deeply, and said, "Do you understand?
As the Master was about to respond, Datan struck him. After a short while, he again held up a blade of grass and showed it to him.
[Zhimen] asked, “What is this? The Master was about to respond when Tanzhu gave a shout. Thereupon, the Master suddenly attained clarity regarding the Great Dharma;
he made the gesture of holding a flower and said, “This time I cannot deceive Upāsaka Min. Tanzhu pulled him back and said, “Say more! Say more! The Master said, “Clouds rise on the South Mountain;
rain falls on the North Mountain,” and then prostrated himself. Tanzhu nodded in approval. Later, the Master propagated the Dharma at Guankxi.
Next, he resided at Yuantong, in accordance with the prediction of Chan Master Daoji. Students flocked there to study under him.
When the imperial court heard of his realization of the Way, the ministers petitioned once more on his behalf. He was granted ceremonial robes and the title "Yuanji" (Perfect Mechanism).

Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddhas appearing in the world have no dharma to give to others; they merely extract nails and pull out wedges, removing doubts and severing delusions. For those who study the Way..."
Do not deceive yourself. If you have even a single doubt the size of a mustard seed, this person is your true spiritual friend.
He gave a shout and said: "What is it? Do not, for heaven's sake, thrust your head into a vat of glue!"
The Abbot Zhìhuó of Ēlíng in Qìngyuán Fǔ was the son of the Zhāng family of Yùfēng on Sūtái. As a child, he had practiced seated meditation;

once, while sitting upright, he suddenly leaned forward as if falling. His parents thought he would surely die, but the Master remained with his eyes closed and composed. Consequently, they allowed him to enter the monastic order.
Having reached the age for full ordination, he went to visit Letan. Upon seeing him, Letan asked, "What are you doing?

As the Master was about to answer, Letan struck him and shouted, "What do you call this 'Chan'? The Master suddenly grasped the essential meaning and immediately said, "Chan has no beginning and no end;
the waves settle in the great ocean, and the moon is reflected in the blue sky. Letan further asked, "What is the Way? The Master replied, "The Way is within the dust of the mundane world."

Vast and expansive, it requires no contrivance; fundamentally, there is nothing lacking. It is profoundly still. Next, he visited Chan Master Bian of Mount Heng, who held him in particularly high esteem.
During the Yuánfú era, he stayed at Zhōngfēng and Qīyún, two hermitages at Xuědòu, for over twenty years.
He once composed this verse: "Two or three shēng of wild water from the bamboo pipes, Seven or five pieces of idle clouds at the pine-window. The Way..."
A person’s livelihood is just like this; it is left for those in the world to see and hear. Many who are resolved upon the Way went to visit him.
When a monk arrived to pay his respects, the Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "Tiantong. The Master asked, "How high is Mount Taibai?
The monk made a gesture of looking upward by striking his forehead with his hand. The Master said, "There is still this one remaining. The monk said, "However..."
"Please, Abbot, speak. The Master instead made a gesture of tilting his head upward. The monk hesitated; the Master struck him immediately.

At the beginning, the Master entered into a covenant with Chan Master Jiao of Tiantong to seek the Way, saying: "In days to come, the two of us should occupy the solitary peaks and highest summits, gazing at the heavens and the Milky Way as men of the world beyond.
We must not register our names in government offices of this age, nor should we bend our wills to submit to them."

Regarding his relationship with others: later, when the covenant was renewed, the Master ultimately did not receive him. Zhengyan stated that Lord Gong had used stratagems to entice the Master out of the mountains to reside at Er-ling.
For thirty years, he lived there without any possessions beyond his basic necessities; only two tigers attended to his right side.

One day, they became more aggressive than humans, so he dismissed them with a verse. On the twelfth day of the fourth month in the seventh year of the Xuanhua era, he passed away while seated in meditation.

He passed away while seated. Chen Gong Zhengyan composed a formal biography detailing the Master’s life and deeds, as well as his final illness and extraordinary manifestations with great thoroughness.
Furthermore, he had a statue of him fashioned, attended by two tigers, which remains extant to this day.

Chan Master Cishi Ruixian of Shaoxing Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Kaixian Ying. A native of his own prefecture, he left home at the age of twenty to undergo the tonsure after passing the scriptural examinations.

Jian said, "This is still just the conventional exchange of the monastic groves (congregations). Ultimately, are they the same or different? The Master then gave a shout; Jian then struck him.
The Master said, "The kindness is so great it is difficult to repay," and then prostrated himself. Later, upon returning to his hometown, he established the Dharma there.

[The student] said, "I do not ask about the seasonal causes and conditions; how is it with the 'Buddha-talk' of Hui-chao?"
The Master said, "A Persian draws his bow, his face turning black. [The student] asked, "What is the meaning? The Master said, "It pierces through the skull; the laughter does not cease.
[The student] said, "I ask this question in good faith. The Master said, "In the Yellow Springs there are no inns; tonight, in whose house shall you stay?"

Master Shi Fo Yi of Shaoxing Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "A single leaf falls and the world turns autumn; a single speck of dust rises and the great earth is gathered.
One Dharma penetrates and the myriad dharmas are complete. Now tell me, which Dharma does it penetrate?
He then gave a shout and said, "Be careful not to mistake the bridge of a donkey’s saddle for your father’s chin! Thereupon he descended from his seat.
Chan Master Daowan of Shouning Temple in Yingcheng, Anzhou, successor to Chan Master Baqin Rui. A monk asked, "Clouds follow the dragon and wind follows the tiger;
I wonder, from what do you, Reverend, emerge? The Master said, "A single stroke drawn in the void. The monk said, "How extraordinary! The Master [said], "..."
[The student] said, "The Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot lift it up. He asked, "In all the lands of the ten directions, there is only the Single Vehicle Dharma (Ekayāna).

What is this Single Vehicle Dharma? The Master said, "It cannot be exhausted even when measured with bushels. [The student] said, "If that is so, then 'moving one's countenance reveals the ancient path.'"
He did not fall into the trap of the "silent mechanism. The Master asked, "What is the silent mechanism? The monk looked up. The Master raised his whisk.
The monk let out a shout. The Master said, "Truly excellent silence! He ascended the hall and said, "The ancients saw this moon..."
People today see this moon; this moon remains forever constant. Yet people of past and present come and go.

If the human mind were like the moon—its light bright and pure within the azure pool—that would surely be the source of the mind. This teaching cannot be further explained. *Du!* [He] ascended the hall. "All you practitioners of Zen:
the three months of winter are coming to an end, and the thirtieth night of the twelfth month is approaching. How will you manage it? After a long silence, he said:
His robes were worn through, revealing his gaunt bones; when the roof leaked, he slept gazing at the stars.
When a monk asked Chan Master Liaochang of Shushan in Fuzhou—successor to Chan Master Yuexi of Tuṣita—“What is the phrase by which Shushan benefits others? the Master said:
He said: "The jade ruler in my breast has not been lightly cast away; the golden hammer in my sleeve comes crashing down upon the face. Entering the hall, he said:
"If you let it go casually, even the Buddha’s hand cannot cover it; if you bring it forth with purpose, the great earth is utterly free of even a speck of dust.

I tell you: do not doubt or speculate. Everywhere, at every turn, one sees Sudhana. When struck by the hammer, it is as clear as receiving the essential meaning—limitless are the eyes of those who toil in birth."
Spontaneously Opening.
Chan Master Huizhao of Doushuai in Longxing Prefecture, a native of the Guo clan of Nan’an, ascended the hall and said: "The roads crisscross beneath Mount Long’an;
the pavilions and towers are layered within the Doushuai Palace. Though it is not the heavens, it is not of this human world."
Upon arriving, the mind is at peace and all discursive thoughts are completely forgotten. A "skilled practitioner" does not shift his feet; a "skillful enterer" does not move the double doors.
Able to naturally laugh and enjoy the misty thickets, who cares? He sits and lets the years and months pass away. Since this is so, tell me: how would you put it?
"Is there anything further above? After a long silence, he said: 'Do not let it be pushed down by the rocks before the cliff;

break through the clouds below that screen the sun. He ascended the hall and, raising his whisk, said: 'On the Dragon Boat Festival, Longan also rows the oars; amidst the clouds of the green mountains, one finds carefree ease.
Eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty is infinite joy—who would love to vie for the first place and snatch the silken banner? He then turned toward..."
Rowing a boat upon dry land; waves rising atop high mountains. Striking the jade drum clearly; unfurling the iron banner in secret. A cup of calamus tea;
several sugar-filled *zong* dumplings. Let us first move north to Uttarakuru, then go and compete for the forehead-mark with Jambudvīpa in the south.
[He struck the meditation seat and descended. Entering the hall: "Tushita has no skill at all; he merely imitates others."

This is a model for the present day. Once every five days he ascends the hall to stir up these many dragons and elephants. Yet, as for the Way of Chan and the Buddha-dharma, they have not yet arrived here;
with what, then, can one make an offering? You must know that when Bodhidharma came from the West, he entrusted us with a single staff.
He then held it up and said: "Therefore it is said: 'If you have a staff, I give you a staff; if you have no staff, I take away your staff.'"
“Cajun, I have taken away your staff. Now tell me: which is the guest phrase? Which is the host phrase?
If you can decide this, then you may make use of it on the road; if you cannot decide it, then let it circulate as a mere worldly convention.
Having said this, he threw down the staff.
The Prime Minister, Layman Zhang Shangying, styled Tianjue and nicknamed Wujin, was nineteen years old when he entered the capital to take the imperial examinations.

On his way, he passed by the home of the Xiang family. The Xiangs had previously received a dream in which a divine being announced, "Tomorrow you shall receive a high official. At dawn the next day, the official arrived;

the Xiangs were struck by this and attended to him with great hospitality and diligence. They then said, "As the young scholar has not yet married, we shall offer our daughter to serve as your attendant."

The Duke declined with repeated humility. Xiang said, "If this mission is not successful, I shall not fail to fulfill my previous agreement. Later, when he indeed passed the imperial examination, he married her.

He was first appointed as a District Magistrate (Zhubù). While visiting a Buddhist monastery, he saw that the Sanskrit palm-leaf manuscripts of the Tripitaka were written in gold characters with perfect alignment;
he then sighed in resentment and said, "The books of our Sage Confucius are not equal to the teachings of these barbarians."
I respectfully acknowledge your weighty favor. Sitting in the study at night, grinding ink and dipping my pen, I lean over the paper and chant long verses.

Not sleeping until the middle of the night, Lady Xiang called out, "Sir, it is late; why do you not go to sleep? The Master informed her of his previous intention, saying, "I am precisely here composing the *Wufo lun* (Treatise on the Non-existence of Buddha).
Lady Xiang replied immediately, "If there is no Buddha, what is there to discuss? You ought rather to compose a *Youfo lun* (Treatise on the Existence of Buddha)."
The discourse had just begun. The Duke doubted its words and consequently stopped it. Later, while visiting a fellow practitioner, he saw a scroll before a Buddha niche.
He asked, "What book is this? His companion replied, "It is the *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa Sūtra*. The Duke took the scroll in hand and opened it;
upon reading the passage, "This illness is not the earth element, yet it is not separate from the earth element," he sighed and said, "How could a foreigner..."
"Could you do the same for this text? He asked how many fascicles the scripture contained; the other replied, "Three fascicles. He then borrowed it and returned home to read it.

Later, Xiang asked him what book he had been reading. The Master said, "The *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-sūtra*. Xiang said, "You should read this sutra thoroughly before composing your *Treatise on the Non-existence of the Buddha*.
The Master was struck with awe by these words and marveled at them. From then on, he placed deep faith in the Buddha Vehicle and devoted his mind to the Patriarchal School.
In the sixth year of the Yuanyou era, while serving as the Transport Commissioner for Jiangxi, he first visited Chan Master Zhaojue of Donglin.

Zhaojue interrogated him regarding his realization, and finding it to be in perfect accord with his own, he granted him formal certification (*inka*). Zhaojue said, "I have a disciple who has attained the Dharma and resides at Yuxi;
this is Cigu Jing. You may also speak with him. Subsequently, while on official circuit, he passed through Fenning. All...
Chan welcomed him. When the Duke arrived, he first paid his respects to Chan Master Ci of Yuxi, then to the various mountain masters, and finally inquired after Chan Master Yue of Doushuai.
Chan Master Yue was short in stature; the Duke had previously heard Gong Dezhuang say that he was intelligent and likable.
He then said, "I have heard that you, sir, are skilled in literature. Yue laughed heartily and said, "The Commissioner has lost one of his eyes!

Congyue was the ninth-generation descendant of Linji; when discussing literature with the Commissioner, he was indeed like the Commissioner, but when discussing Chan with Congyue, he was like Congyue.
The Commissioner did not agree with these words, so he forcibly counted on his fingers and said, "It is the ninth generation. He then asked about Yuxi.
"How far is it from here? he asked. "Thirty *li*," they replied. "And Tusita? he asked. "Five *li*," they replied. That night, the Master arrived at Tusita.
This was because he had previously dreamed one night that the sun ascended into the sky and he took hold of it with his hand.
He then explained the significance of the sun’s revolution to the Head Seat, saying, "I have heard that Commissioner Zhang will pass beyond this place before long; I shall [prepare] deeply."
"A sharp prick of pain! If you are willing to turn your head, it would be a fortunate event for our school. The Abbot said, "The gentlemen of today are accustomed to being served and honored;
I fear that if their resentment is provoked, they might cause trouble. Yuanze said, "Even if they were to become vexed, at most they could only leave my monastery;
there would be no other harm. While the Abbot was conversing with Yuanze, he praised Donglin, but Yuanze did not yet approve of him.

"Not seeking its place of descent on Mount Lu, the Elephant King’s nostrils needlessly pierce the vast heavens. This was intended as a satire of his refusal to accept [the invitation to] Donglin.

When the Official conversed with Yue, they discussed matters of the Chan school until late at night. Yue said, "Since Donglin has already certified the Provincial Commissioner regarding the Buddha..."
"Is there any slight doubt regarding the teachings of our Patriarchs? The Master said, "There is. Yuanze asked, "What words do you doubt?

Take, for instance, what Yantou spoke of as the 'Final Word'—does it exist or not? The Master said, "It exists. Yuanze...
He laughed heartily and returned to his quarters, closing the door behind him. That night, Master Gong could not sleep peacefully;

at the fifth watch, he rose from his bed and accidentally knocked over his urinal, whereupon he attained great enlightenment. Suddenly realizing the meaning of the previous conversation, he composed this verse:

"The drum falls silent and the bell has ceased; returning with his alms bowl, Yanhou’s single thrust was like thunder. Indeed, he shall live for only three more years—could it be that he met his match?"
Shouji arrived and knocked on the door of the abbot’s quarters, saying, "I have already caught the thief. Yuan Yue asked, "Where is the stolen property? The official was speechless.
Yuan Yue said, "Commissioner, please leave for now; let us meet tomorrow. The next day, the official recited the previous verse.
Yuan Yue then said to him, "The reason you practice Chan is precisely because your life-root has not been severed and you produce interpretations based on words. Such as this—"

It turns according to the person; though possessing great majestic light, it cannot manifest. Suddenly, with one shout, both ears go deaf; Nata’s eyes open and Huangbo’s face appears.
Sishin took up the case, saying: "Yunyan wished to ask. Since Xuedou is refined gold from a great furnace..."
"One should not change one's facial expression. [The Master asked: "Why, then, were his ears deaf for three days? "Do you all wish to know?
'From of old, no one has recognized the merit of those who have sweated horses in battle'; it was simply to re-examine his epoch-making achievement. The Master struck the table and said:

"Were it not for your words, how could we see the application of Zhenjing and Sijian’s death-mind? Were it not for these two great elders, it would be difficult to manifest the functioning of Xuedou and Mazu. The Master [concluded].
At dawn on the fourth day of the eleventh month in the fourth year of the Xuanhua era, he dictated his final testament with his own hand and instructed his disciples to write it down.

Suddenly, he took up his pillow and threw it against the door and window; the sound was like a peal of thunder. When the assembly looked, he had already passed away. He also composed verses on ancient precedents (*gū*).
[His] activities in the world are not recorded here again.
Chan Master Suizhou Dongshan Bian, successor to Chan Master Fayun Gaoming, ascended the hall and said: "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing. It pierces the heavens."
The hawk soars through the vast heavens; neither fire, nor water, nor earth can contain it. Like an arrow released from a bow, once launched there is no returning.
Even if you were to understand this to the full extent, you would still leave the blue-eyed barbarian from the West laughing to scorn.
Chan Master Huihai of Dongjing ascended the hall and said: "The formless Tathāgata manifests his body; he shatters the hosts of Māra’s armies, leaving not a speck of dust behind.
Where the seven stars cast their slanted reflections and the wind arises, the four seas return to their original master. O virtuous ones!"
On the assembly at Vulture Peak, Mahākāśyapa saw the Buddha hold up a flower; seizing the opportunity, he smiled.

Subhūti, hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, deeply understood its meaning and significance; he wept with tears of sorrow. Now tell me: who is it that smiles, and who is it that weeps? Have you not heard it said:
"The myriad streams flow crosswise, yet all head toward the east; transcendent on all eight sides, one is naturally lucid. The courage of ten thousand people is shattered like sand."
On the platform: "A single arrow brings down two eagles from the azure sky. Ascending the hall, he raised the following case:
While Guishan was sitting, Yangshan asked him, "After you have passed away, if someone asks how you would respond regarding the Dharma-way of our late teacher, Master, what will you say?
Guishan replied, "One bowl of porridge, one bowl of rice. Yangshan said, "If those ahead of us do not approve, what then? Guishan replied, "An adept monk, Yangshan."
He then paid his respects. Guishan said, "When you meet people, do not misrepresent [the teaching]. The Master said, "From antiquity to the present, how many have offered these words:
'Strict yet without severity; reverent yet without formality'? Or they cross their staffs and raise their fists.
But if it were merely like that, how could one know the place where father and son reach mutual accord? Today, this mountain monk also wishes to..."
This is known to all; do not distinguish between "self" and "other. There is no difference between self and other. A weary fish stays in the shallow pool; a sick bird perches on the reeds.
Hesitating and unable to advance, one’s sandals sink into the mud. How can one obtain the single scroll of a Master’s teachings?
The Dharma Master Luán of Xīshǔ was proficient in both Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna teachings. When Fózhuàng retired from his duties, he resided at Jìngdé Temple.
The Master asked Fózhuàng, “Why is it that those of the Chan school often speak without grounding in the scriptures? Fózhuàng replied, “What sutras and śāstras have you studied?

The Master said, “I have a rough knowledge of various sutras and am somewhat versed in the *Śata-dharma-prakāśamukha-śāstra*. Fózhuàng said, “Just as it rained yesterday and is sunny today—into which category of dharma does this fall?”
The Master was bewildered. Zhao raised his *yǎnghézi* (itching-comforter) and struck him, saying, "Do not say that what the Chan school speaks of lacks a foundation.
The Master said indignantly, "Yesterday it rained, today it is sunny; ultimately, in what dharma is this subsumed? Zhao replied, "It is subsumed within the twenty-fourth category:
the category of non-correspondence (*asaṃprayukta-dharma*). The Master attained sudden enlightenment and immediately prostrated in gratitude. Later, he returned to Shu and resided there.

During his lectures, he taught his disciples through the direct path (*ṛju-mārga*) and did not adhere to names or conceptual characteristics (*nāma-lakṣaṇa*). Consequently, many people left. He then delivered a verse to conclude the lecture, saying:
"The multitude sell flowers; I alone sell pines. Their green hues do not match the red. In the final reckoning, they never harmonize with the times.
Return, then, into the midst of the verdant mists. Thereupon, he lived in seclusion for twenty years. Monastics and laypeople alike followed him.
Mù was summoned again to expound the Dharma. He smiled and replied with a verse: "I sought refuge by hiding my traces on a high peak, yet even that high peak would not tolerate me.
It is better to return to Jinli and, as before, sell my green pines. The assembly prostrated themselves in repentance, and lecturers from the two rivers vied with one another to rely upon him.

Chan Master Tianyou Dinyu of Yunyan in Longxing Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Leduan Zhun. He was the son of Zheng of Chengdu. Initially, he sat for the examinations at the local prefectural school; subsequently, he went to sit for the examinations in Zizhou.

In both places, his name appeared on the list of candidates for the imperial examination. The Master did not dare accept these honors; he concealed his identity and departed through the frontier passes, arriving by chance—
When the Wayman of Shangu returned from the West, [Dongshan] saw that his bearing was extraordinary and his discourse was transcendent;
he therefore traveled down the river with him as a fellow passenger and eventually went to Mount Lu to seek out a teacher and shave his head. He did not change his original name.

He first visited Sīxin but did not find accord, so he subsequently relied upon Zhantang at Letan. One day, during a general sermon at the pond, Zhantang said: "Everyone is struggling and striving to conform to the standard..."
The Elder sought the Buddha-dharma; he then struck his knee and said, "Do you understand? It is like adding frost to snow.

Again he struck his knee and said, "If you do not understand, have you not seen Qianfeng address the assembly, saying: 'If you raise one, you must not raise two. To let pass one move is to fall into the second.
Upon hearing this, the Master attained sudden and clear enlightenment. He appeared in the world at Yungai, and subsequently moved to Yunyan. Once, he...
Heshang Zhongdao’s *Ode on Herding an Ox* says: "Two horns point to heaven; four hooves tread the earth. Having snapped the nose-rope, he herds his own dung and urine.
When Zhang Wujin saw this, he struck his hands together in approval. Later, Zhongdao retired to Yunyan and passed through Lu Shan to Qixian.
The abbot there was unwilling to accept him as a resident, saying: "Old and decrepit as you are, you are truly like an ox pledged in a pawnshop."
When the Master heard of this, he composed a verse and departed, saying: "What treasury has ever known how to pawn an ox?
It is simply because the price is so high it is difficult to repay. I suspect your capital is not very great; In the end, you will find it hard to keep this one beast.
He subsequently established a hermitage at Wuning, which he named "Pawning the Ox," and never left it for the rest of his life. When Tudu saw him there, he was already ninety-three years old.
Ascending the hall, he struck the meditation staff and said: "A long rain has not cleared; a note! The golden crow flies upon the corner of the bell tower. He struck once more and said:
"It is still within the eggshell. Striking again, he said: "Let the monks do as they please with their names and reputations.
Ascending the hall, [he said]: "Mazu’s single shout—Bazhang missed it. Linji, that little fellow, picked up a broken [potsherd] from a heap of refuse."
"Straw sandals! 'Hu-he! Lu-he! (Huh! Lah! The Master roared with a thunderous voice and said, 'Can you call this "Hu-he!
Lu-he!"? Ascending the hall, he said: 'Xianggu’s rolling the ball has exhausted its skill; Xuansha’s chopping the plaque has also reached its limit. Do you know? The fire-star enters the trousers;
the matter of the mouth brings trouble to the family gate. Ascending the hall again, he said: 'Three hundred, five hundred—copper heads and iron brows. The wooden flute... "
"Who comes to take up the beat for this horizontal flute? At that time, a monk stepped forward. The Master said, "This too is drawing the bow after the thief has fled.

He ascended the hall and said: "Baofeng has a secret method; I shall explain it clearly before the assembly. Last night before the third watch, a tortoise swallowed a turtle. On the winter solstice, he ascended the hall and said:
"The movement of the celestial dial shifts; the sun reaches its longest path southward. My cotton trousers have not been washed; there is no one to come and change them."

In place of [the previous statement], both the Great and Small Yuquan [say]: "When there is no wind, waves arise. Yunyan saw the road and, unable to bear it, struck directly downward with a single blow that shattered everything to pieces.
He then cried out in a loud voice, "Look beneath your feet! Ascending the hall, he cited Liangshan, who said: "To those coming from the south, I give you thirty blows;
to those coming from the north, I give you thirty blows. Although it was thus, it did not yet accord with the essence of the school. Later...
Lanxi Heshang said, "Liangshan is good. [This is] taking a single piece of pure gold and treating it as dull iron.

To sell out Lanxi is not so; to those coming from the south, I give you thirty blows of the staff; to those coming from the north, I give you thirty blows of the staff—let the whole world criticize and denigrate me as they wish.
The Master [Zhaozhou] took up the case and said: "One person can extend but cannot retract; one person can retract but cannot..."
He was able to relax. At Yunyan’s gate, let people come from the south or the north; just pass by like this. Suddenly, while washing his face, he felt his nose.
He then came forward and said, "I’ll give you thirty blows. Ascending the hall, he said: "The sun may grow cold, the moon may grow hot, and the various māras cannot destroy it.
But what is 'true speech'? This is the first thirty blows. One strike in the center, nine below, and seven above. If...
"I do not believe you. Yunyan said to you, "Where ten thousand people point with one finger, a single wild goose falls into the cold sky.
Rising from illness, he ascended the hall and cited Mazu Daoshi’s "Sun-Face Buddha, Moon-Face Buddha. Later, Master Yan of Dongshan composed a verse on it: "A young girl paints her eyebrows;
before the phoenix-mirror stand, her speech is like that of a madwoman. She says of herself, 'My jade face...'"
"Difficult to compare! Yet he comes back and puts on his gauze robe. The Master said, "The old man of Dongshan praises him with his whole mouth;
this is indeed a thorough inspection. Bringing it forward, one cannot avoid having a sense of local attachment toward Yunyan.
Furthermore, it is not so: 'Strike down the yellow oriole, lest it sing upon the branch. How many times has it startled my lady’s dreams, preventing her from reaching Liaoxi.'"
Chan Master Sanjiao Zhiyao of Tanzhou ascended the hall and said: "Molding earth to weigh a thousand *jin*—the scale-head allows not even a fly to rest upon it.
Within this, there is a certain matter that would cause those capable of it in Lingnan to run to their deaths. Do you recognize it?
Even if you were to recognize it, it would still be but the second moon."
Chan Master Fachuang (Zujian) of Jiuxian in Longxing Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Huiriyu. He was a native of Yanling.
Once, while sitting at Tianning Monastery in Chi with his *kāṣāya* draped over his head, Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zeng Gong asked him, "Where is your native place?"

[The official] said, "Yanzhou. He asked, "Is that the same as here, or is it different? The Master pulled his *kāṣāya* robe down, stepped off the ground, and bowed, saying, "Sir, have you ever been to Yanzhou?
The official was at a loss for what to say. The Master said, "Wait until you reach Yanzhou, and then I will tell you.
Later, after he had taken up residence, he ascended the hall and said: "Ten thousand willows and a thousand flowers bloom in the warm sun; upon each flower, there is..."
The One Tathāgata, wondrously discoursing on the non-dual treasury of space, moves with subtle words throughout the nine realms.
With a broad smile—tell me, what is it that he smiles at? His feet do not touch the ground in the Garden of Awakening.
Ascending the hall, he cited Muzhou’s instruction to the assembly: “All of you have not yet attained a point of entry; you must attain a point of entry. Once attained...
This is the point of entry; you must not forget it. I, this old monk, have told you clearly, yet you still do not understand—how much less can you cover it over?
The Master asked, "When Muzhou spoke thus, where did his meaning lie? If you have not yet realized this, listen as I provide a footnote from Jueyuan:
When the monk Zhang saw Wang’s companion, Wang’s companion called out, "Zhang! Last night...
"At the place where the oxen graze—on the ridge above and in the village below—the water west of the stream is not drunk, and the grass east of the stream is not swallowed.
How can one awaken to this garden? Do you understand immediately? One cannot help but go thus. Thereupon, he pressed both hands against the air and descended from his seat.
A monk asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'? The Master said, "Vigilant yet tranquil.
The monk asked, "What is 'taking away the environment but not taking away the person'? The Master said, "Tranquil yet vigilant. The monk asked, "What is 'taking away both person and environment'?"
The Master said, "Alert! Alert! Alert! Alert! [The student] asked, "What is it that is neither taken away by the person nor by the environment? The Master said, "Silent!
Silent! Silent! Silent! [The student] said, "Today this student has bought iron and obtained gold. The Master said, "Where did you get this head-word?"

The Abbot of Juehai Fayin Hermitage in Pingjiang Prefecture was a member of the Zhu family from Yushan in the prefecture. At the age of twenty-four, he donned the black robes and received full ordination. Traveling to Donglin, he went to visit Huirui. Huirui brought up the pivotal words regarding Lingyun’s realization of the Way and questioned him. As the Master was about to respond, Huirui said, "Not so, not so. Suddenly, the Master attained a profound realization and composed this verse: *The old fellow Lingyun,* *In one word, penetrated the source.* *The spring breeze blows over the peach blossoms;* *The fragrance fills the entire valley.* Huirui approved his understanding. He then took leave and traveled to Mount Tiantai, where he stayed at the Shifang Cloister. Later, he visited various masters, including Xuedou Chongxian, Fayan Wenyi, and Yunmen Wenyan, all of whom praised his realization. Subsequently, he resided at the Fayin Hermitage on Mount Jing in Pingjiang. One day, while sitting in meditation, he suddenly experienced a great awakening. He then composed another verse: *The mountain peaks are high and steep;* *The path is difficult to traverse.* *If you do not see through the barrier,* *How can you pass through?* *Now that I have seen through the barrier,* *I know the road is not far.* *The spring breeze blows over the peach blossoms;* *The fragrance fills the entire valley.* He then returned to the Fayin Hermitage. When he was about to depart for the West Lake, he composed a final verse: *The mountain peaks are high and steep;* *The path is difficult to traverse.* *Now that I have passed through,* *I know the road is not far.* *The spring breeze blows over the peach blossoms;* *The fragrance fills the entire valley.* *If you wish to see the Buddha,* *Go look at the peach blossoms.* Upon reaching the West Lake, he stayed at the Lingyin Monastery. One day, he suddenly felt a sense of urgency and composed a verse: *The mountain peaks are high and steep;* *The path is difficult to traverse.* *If you do not see through the barrier,* *How can you pass through?* *Now that I have seen through the barrier,* *I know the road is not far.* *The spring breeze blows over the peach blossoms;* *The fragrance fills the entire valley.* *If you wish to see the Buddha,* *Go look at the peach blossoms.* Having finished, he threw the verse into the lake and passed away. His remains were enshrined at the Fayin Hermitage. He was seventy-two years old. His dharma heirs included the Abbot of the Tianlong Monastery in Hangzhou, the Abbot of the Xuefeng Monastery in Fuzhou, and others. His lineage flourished greatly. His secular surname was Zhu. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Huishen (Wisdom-Enlightenment). His stupa was named "Juehai" (Ocean of Enlightenment). The Emperor bestowed upon him the posthumous title "Chan Master Huishen. His disciples numbered over a thousand. Among them, those who achieved enlightenment were more than ten. His teachings spread throughout the world. His legacy remains unsurpassed. Rujing said, "What you have seen has indeed penetrated the subtle, yet you must further spur yourself on to clarify the Great Dharma.

The Master followed this instruction and resided on Mount Lu for thirty years, never interacting with the world. The monastic community held him in the highest esteem. During the Jianyan era, bandits arose along the Yangtze River...
He turned left and returned eastward along the current. The local villagers built a hermitage for him to dwell in, and both monastics and laypeople followed one after another to seek his instruction.
He once said to the assembly, "If you maintain the power of meditative concentration with full vigor, you need not worry about morning meals or engage in the pursuit of worldly gain.
In his later years, he wandered freely as he pleased, calling himself the "Man of Five Loose Ties."
Chan Master Longya said:
"Chan Master Zheyuan of Dongshan in Ruizhou was a dharma successor [of mine]. A monk asked, 'What is the Tamer of the Ten Bodies?
Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there. I do not know what the underlying meaning was. The Master said, "Under his heels, there are holes through seven and eight."
On the day Chan Master Deqiong of Deshan in Changde Prefecture was invited by Chan Master Wenmu Nengchan, he ascended the hall and said: "The master craftsman casts his net, yet they refuse to stay;
he calls out, yet they do not return. Why does the head pass from east to west? He answered on their behalf: "Look after five days."

Chan Master Zhongxuan of the Fourth Patriarch [Monastery] in Qizhou, successor to Chan Master Qinghai of Zhihai, ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas appear in the world for the sake of the single great cause and condition."
The Patriarch came from the West to point directly to the human mind as Buddha. Ordinary beings and sages are fundamentally non-dual;
how could there be divergent paths between delusion and awakening? There is nothing in nirvana to rejoice in, and nothing in birth and death to loathe. It requires only a single word of realization.

Without rising from one's seat, one immediately realizes the non-arising of phenomena. With a single thought, one turns the light back within; without taking a single step, one pervades the entire dharma-realm of the sands of the Ganges.
As this essential sutra quotes: "Once a mountain monk of the ancestral school has arrived here, he must not remain idle.
He then raises his whisk and says: "Look! Look! At the mountains, rivers, the great earth, the sun, moon, and stars—whether ordinary or sagely, whether human or..."
All things are entirely within a single hair-tip atop the whisk; they enter and exit, playing freely. Do you all see this?
Even if you were to see it here with such clarity and distinctness, you must further know that there is a path that transcends this.
He asked the assembly, "What is the path that transcends all? After a long silence, he said: "In the midsummer sky, great snow falls;
on the mountain ridges of deep winter, fiery clouds fly."

Chan Master Yuanhui of Qianfeng in Quanzhou ascended the hall and said: "The orthodox lineage of Bodhidharma, the very nostril of the patch-robed monks—how lamentable that those who are deluded form such a multitude!
With eyes wide open, they nod off to sleep. Above their heads is heaven; beneath their feet is earth; with their ears, they hear sounds."
Breathing out through the nostrils, I dare ask the disciples of the Cloud Hall: where do you place yourselves during the course of daily life?
Do you see it? How pitiful! Yet the Great Master of Shuanglin said: "This very sound of speech is 'tut'!"

Once, while wandering through a mountain temple, he saw a collection of Chan texts; upon reading them, he felt as though he had attained some realization.
He immediately tore off his official cap and received full ordination. Carrying a single bowl, he traveled through various regions, first visiting Chan Master Baosheng Chengfu;
his inclination was quite different from that master’s. Upon reaching Jinghu, he called upon Yong’an Xi, Zhenru Zhe, and Deshan Hui, and his realization grew even more profound.
When he finally arrived at Da Mí, Mí asked, “Where is your home district, Upāsaka? The Master replied, “Western Sichuan. [Mí continued], “I have heard that in Western Sichuan there is...”

A monk asked, "After Huang Chao passed by, was there anyone who could retrieve his sword? The monk held up his fist. Baizhang said, "That is just a kitchen knife.
The monk said, "But it is still of great practical use. Baizhang gave a shout and sent him out.
Next, he asked the Master, "After Huang Chao passed by, was there anyone who could retrieve his sword? The Master also held up his fist. Baizhang said, "That too is just a kitchen knife."
The Master said, "If you can kill someone, then stop. He then stepped forward and struck him across the chest with his fist. Guishan said, "For thirty years I have been riding a horse;
today I have been thrown by a donkey. Later, he returned to the old site of Shan'an in Shu at the request of the fourfold assembly.
Emerging from his quarters to dwell in gratitude for the patronage, he ascended the hall. Longji said, "The myriad dharmas are the light of the mind; all conditions are but the awakening of nature.

Originally there is no person who is deluded or awakened; it simply requires realization this very day. The Master said, "If there is neither delusion nor awakening, what is there to realize? *Du!* (A shout of exasperation)."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this story: One day, while on a work assignment carrying firewood, Xuefeng saw a monk along the way and dropped a piece of wood down, saying, "The entire Great Canon of Teachings speaks only of this.
Later, Zhenru Zhe said, "The entire Great Canon of Teachings does not speak of this.
Based on the words of these two venerable masters, are they the same or different? As for me, the mountain monk, I do not...
He then held up his whisk and said, "To lift it up is 'Thus have I heard'; to let it down is 'faithfully receiving and practicing.
In the room, he asked, "Chongzhen Zhan-tou, who is your parent from before the empty kalpa?
Chongzhen attained realization and said, "Venerable Teacher, please lower your voice. He then offered this verse of resonance: "In the Myriad-Year Granary, I once suffered famine; Great..."

Dwelling in the midst of the sea, one’s thirst remains ever great. At first, when seeking it, one could not find it; now, when trying to avoid it, one cannot escape it. The Master granted this as his seal of approval.
One day, while playing a game of Go with Magistrate Huang, Huang asked, "Among all these games, there is not a single one that is the same.
While a thousand moves and ten thousand moves are indeed as they are, what is that one move? The Master picked up a Go stone.
The Master showed it to him. Huang stood there lost in thought. The Master said, "Have you not heard that from of old, nineteen out of twenty people have been killed by delusion?
The Master served as abbot for over thirty years; whenever he preached the Dharma, he did not permit his words to be recorded. At the time of his death, he wrote this verse:
He passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture. When his body was cremated, a violent wind suddenly arose; wherever the smoke reached, it rained down śarīras.
Monastics and laypeople alike dug into the ground and obtained them all. His heart and tongue remained uncorrupted. He was enshrined in a stupa at his original mountain.
Chan Master Zongyin of Yunjing Baojue in Huai’an Army ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said, 'If you recognize the bench, it is more than sufficient for all around.
They also said, 'If you recognize the bench, heaven and earth are vastly different. I, this mountain monk, do not agree with either of these."
"Recognizing the bench—what a trivial piece of furniture! One day, after finishing his general discourse, the Master said, "Sons, do not disperse yet;
listen to one more verse. He then said: "For forty-nine years, a single scene of clamor;
For eighty-seven springs, this old man has played alone. Who is less, who is more? All alike are dreaming. Go back! Return! Upon the plum branch, the snow."
"Important! Having finished speaking, he descended from his seat, leaned on his staff, and passed away.

Chan Master Zongxian Zhengjue of Xinsiang Monastery in Chengdu Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Zhaojue Bai. He was a native of the Wang family of Tongchuan; as a youth, he served as a civil examination candidate (jinshi).
There was a man who once played by scooping up mountain stream water with his cupped hands during the day. At night, he thought of it, and suddenly saw the water filling the room, cool and clear.
He tried to draw some up, but could not; at that moment, the dusty world vanished of its own accord. He exclaimed, "The net of worldly existence has been torn asunder!

He went to rely upon Master Zhaojue for ordination and received the full precepts. Later, while among the assembly, he engaged in inquiry and consultation. One day, Zhaojue asked the Master, "Upon the high, high peak summit..."
[Guishan] stood up. "Walking on the bottom of the deepest sea—how do you understand this? The Master suddenly attained awakening upon these words and said, "My heels have been nailed down!
Guishan picked up his whisk and asked, "And what about this one? The Master smiled and departed.
He served diligently for seven years. He traveled south to the capital, passing through the regions of Huai and Zhe. Later, he met the Venerable Wuzu Yan at Haihui Temple.
He stepped forward and asked: "I do not yet know the pivot; it is difficult to cross Zhaozhou’s bridge. I shall not ask about Zhaozhou’s bridge for now."
"What is the pivotal bolt? The Patriarch said, "You stay outside the door for now. The Master stepped forward, gave a kick, and withdrew.
The Patriarch said, "For so long, you have been eating this very meal; someone has already known its flavor. The next day, he entered the inner room.
The Patriarch said, "Are you the monk who questioned me yesterday? I certainly know where your understanding lies;
it is simply that you have not yet passed the White Cloud Barrier. The Master said, "I take my leave," and departed. At that time, Yuanwu was serving as attendant.
The Master probed him regarding the meaning of the White Cloud Barrier. Yuanwu said, "You should simply realize it directly. The Master laughed and said, "It is not I."

The Master replied, "I have been keeping watch all along. Linji looked at Wujin and said, "This fellow is talkative. From then on, [Wujin] was known as Laoren (The Old Man).
