Later, when he took his leave to return to the West, the Patriarch gave him a small discourse (*xiao can*) and further sent him off with a verse, saying: "I have been away from my hometown for over forty years; For a time, I forgot the dialect of Shu.
When you, O Chan practitioner, return to Chengdu, You must take care to remember the dialect of Lu. At that time, Huairang was still in good health.
The Master served him again, and his reputation spread widely. He subsequently left to reside at Changsong, and later moved to Baofu Xinsiang.
A monk asked, "The Buddhas of the three periods and the six generations of patriarchs all fail to get out of this circle;
what is this circle? The Master replied, "The rim of a well. He ascended the hall and said, citing Yangshan’s question to Zhongyi: "What is the meaning of Buddha-nature?"
Yi said, "I shall give you a parable; you will understand it immediately. It is like a room with six windows.
Inside there is a monkey, and outside there is a monkey. From the eastern side, someone calls out, 'Singing-sing! and the monkey inside responds.
In this way, as he is called from all six windows, he responds to each. [Yangshan] then prostrated himself, saying: 'I have just received the instruction of the Master. I have something [to say]...'"
Doubting, Yangshan said, "What is it that you doubt? Nanquan replied, "Suppose the inner monkey is asleep while the outer monkey wishes to meet him;
what then? Nanquan descended from his meditation seat, took Yangshan by the hand, and said, "The *xingxing* has met you.
The Master [Baizhang] said, "Do you all wish to see these two elders? I shall tell you about it as well."
This is an analogy. In the town of Zhong, there was a man who closely resembled a goldsmith. Yangshan brought a piece of gold and asked the goldsmith to appraise it;
the goldsmith offered a full price in return. As they were about to complete the transaction, the seller of the gold gave him an extra amount of gold to add to the scale.
Although the goldsmith was inwardly delighted, he could not help but harbor a secret suspicion in his heart. Why? If this were not a spy, he must surely be a thief.
[The Master] descended from his seat.
Chan Master Dayuan Zhi of Daping Monastery in Tanzhou, a dharma heir of Chan Master Daolin Yi, was a native of Siming. He ascended the hall and raised the example of Nanquan’s saying: "Three..."
"The Buddhas of the world do not know there is the 'tawny cat and white ox,' yet they do know [of them].
The Master said, "Since the Buddhas of the three periods do not know there is [the tawny cat and white ox], when have they ever even dreamed of them?

It is clear that you must first know there is one who knows there is, before you can attain it. But what kind of person is one who knows there is? He replied, "He drinks the official wine and lies on the official street."
To be executed on the spot. To be buried on the spot. Countless heroic men upon the battlefields; their corpses pile up like mountains and accumulate like peaks.

Wendeng Gong Hu Anguo was a lay practitioner (jushi) surnamed Kanghou. Having long relied upon Shangfeng, he attained the meaning beyond words.
During the Chongning era, while passing through Yaoshan, a Zen practitioner raised the story of Nanquan killing the cat to question him.
Gong replied with a verse: "In hand, he holds the pivot of life and death for heaven and earth; His arrangements, whether expansive or restrictive, depend on the moment. The Jade Hall..."

A hare or a horse is not a dragon or an elephant; the grand function is majestic, yet none understand it at all. Again, in a letter sent from Shangfeng, he said: "The Peak of Zhurong resembles the sky above Ducheng;
The mountains and rivers of ten thousand ages are before one’s eyes. One must believe that the Dead Heart has never been dead;
Last night, the autumn moon was once again full."
Chan Master Fuzhou Puxian Yuansu, a successor of Chan Master Shangfeng Cai, was a native of Jianning. He ascended the hall and said: "The army follows the seal’s turn;

beyond three thousand li, all smoke and dust have ceased. The general pursues the talisman’s movement; throughout the six periods of the day, one is utterly naked and bare. There is no need for iron banners."

When the iron drum resounds, all naturally bow like grass and move like the wind; what need is there for seven times releasing and seven times capturing? It reaches the point where none fail to submit without even thinking of it.
As the saying goes: "The Great Man wields the sword of wisdom; the blade of Prajñā has the brilliance of a Vajra.
Not only can it shatter the minds of externalists, it has long since struck terror into the hearts of celestial Māras. At such a time, tell me: who is the commanding general?
[The Master] lets out a shout. He ascends the hall and says: "Nanquan said, 'At eighteen, I already knew how to make a living.
My bag had no thread to tie even an ant; my kitchen lacked even the crumbs to gather flies. Zhaozhou said, 'At eighteen, I already knew how to break up the family and disperse the household.
I bought cheap at the southern end and sold dear at the northern end. When one examines these two cases, they both deserve thirty blows of the staff."
Let this one move pass for now. Why? "As a wanderer once, I felt special pity for travelers; loving wine myself, I cherish those who are drunk. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Before a word is spoken, the instruction is already given; when you attempt to deliberate, ten thousand mountains stand between you.
Do not say that the Buddha-dharma is not much—it is also very difficult to penetrate the profound barrier. But how does one penetrate the profound barrier? *He let out a shout.*
A shout. Chan Master Shantang Sengxun of Gushan in Fuzhou, a native of the Ruan clan of that prefecture, ascended the hall and said:
"Huangbo’s sixty blows from his staff—had he not understood the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, it would have been somewhat more effective. But as for Dayu’s ribs..."
He threw up three fists and said, "Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is nothing more than this. This is truly a case of being driven to desperation.
You must know there is one person who, when struck over the head with a great club, does not turn his head; when struck across the face with an old fist, he likewise pays no heed.
But tell me, who is it? Ascending the hall, he said: The north wind sweeps the ground, rolling up the yellow leaves; Outside the gate, a thousand peaks show their chilling colors. At night...
A half-turtle flies with snow; the stone woman frowns her two brows by the stream. [He] plants his staff and says, "Everyone is here.
Now tell me, is it the sky that is cold or the people? He gives a shout and says, "Return to the hall!"
Chan Master Biefeng Zuozhen of Gushan in Fuzhou was a native of the Lin clan of Xinghua.

A monk asked, "Zhaozhou circumambulated the meditation seat once and said that he had finished reciting the entire Tripitaka. What is the principle behind this? The Master said, "When painting a dragon, look at its head; when painting a snake, look at its tail.
The monk asked, "The old woman said, 'I have come to request the recitation of the complete canon. Why did he only manage to recite half of it?"
"What do you think about this? The Master said, "If a person lacks far-reaching foresight, they will surely have immediate anxieties.

[The monk] asked, "I do not yet understand: where is the place where one turns the *Prajñāpāramitā* in its entirety (*Banzang*)? The Master said, "If it is not a true connoisseur, it is merely a vain labor to speak of the cold of winter.

He ascended the hall and said: "Seeking the ox, one must inquire after its tracks; studying the Way prizes the absence of mind. When the tracks exist, the ox is present; when there is no mind, the Way is easy."
[He] searched. Holding up his whisk, he said: "This is the track; where is the ox? Even if you can see its horns clearly, its nostrils are still in the hands of Fashí.
Ascending the hall, [he said]: "The one path that leads upward is not transmitted by the thousand sages.
He struck the ground with his staff and said: "If you understand it this way, you are already ten thousand miles away. But in the end, how is it? Peach red, plum white.
The white rose is purple; when questioned about the spring breeze, it knows nothing at all. He addressed the assembly, saying:
"The Great Way is right before one's eyes, yet for now it is difficult to behold. If you wish to recognize the true essence of the Great Way, it is not separate from sound, form, and speech.
He struck the meditation staff and said, "This is sound. He held up the meditation staff and said, "This is form. What do you call the Great [Way]?"
The true essence of the Way: even if you were to see it here, it would still be like "leaving Cao’s Gate from Zhengzhou.
To the assembly: if one discusses this matter, it is like a person eating a meal; when full, one simply stops. If one is not yet full, there will surely be a mind that longs for food.
Yet if one eats too much, there is the affliction of indigestion. Arriving at this point, how can one attain the state of being just right?
He departed. After a long silence, he said: "For now, return to stay beneath the cliff; let us watch together when the moon is bright.
Chan Master Chéng'ān Zéchóng of Jiànfú Monastery in Ráozhōu, a successor of Chan Master Hóngfēng Wǔyuè, was a native of Níngguó Prefecture. He ascended the hall and, citing a monk’s question, said:
An ancient worthy asked, "When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them? The Worthy said, "The firewood crackles and the bamboo bursts, startling the ears of men.
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Worthy said, "The house dog’s barking is fierce and does not cease at night. The Master said, "Do you all wish to understand?
The firewood crackles and the bamboo bursts, startling the ears of men; red dust rises from the bottom of the vast ocean. The house dog’s barking is fierce and does not cease at night."

whose is this immeasurable compassion? After a long silence, he says: "Long head, short legs; little joy, much anger."
Ascending the hall, he asked the attendant, "Do you still remember the circumstances from yesterday? The attendant replied, "I do not remember.
He then looked toward the assembly and said, "Do you remember? The assembly remained silent. He raised his whisk and asked, "Do you remember?
After a long silence, he said, "It has been forgotten as well. Not established in three places, nor existing as one—since you all do not understand, [this is precisely it]."
"Regarding the pillar, do not open your mouths. [The Master] struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat.

Chan Master Wushi Jiechen of Yuyang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Zhuo of Tianning; he was a native of the Zhang family of Wenzhou. He offered thanks to the administrators.
In the hall, there is an inch at the head of the foot-measure; those who can discern it are still rare. At the tail of the scale, there is no star; do not mistake it for one.
If you wish to determine the lightness or heaviness of past and present, or to compare the strengths and weaknesses of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, simply place a single eye upon it.

If you can truly return ten inches to the one foot, and recognize that eight *liang* is originally half a *jin*, then naturally all will be harmonious within and without, and there will be no [disturbance] in the family or the state.
Matters. Today, this mountain monk has already handed everything over with both hands. Do you all yet consent to believe, accept, and practice it?
Measuring with a ruler and cutting with a knife pervades the world; Master Zhigong was no idle monk. [Ascending the hall:
"The wisdom of Mañjuśrī and the conduct of Samantabhadra are the almanacs of many years. Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout are the heroes of a chaotic age. You..."
When people like you pass through the Sangha Hall and enter the Buddha Hall, do you realize you are traversing a perilous passage beyond the Iron Ring Mountains?
Suddenly, you might step upon the crown of Śākyamuni’s head or bump into the forehead of the Holy Monk; you cannot avoid a great disaster. Entering the hall, [the Master said]:
"If I say 'it exists,' you will be hindered by existence. If I say 'it does not exist,' you will be hindered by non-existence. If I speak crosswise..."
Furthermore, you cannot step across it; if I speak vertically, you cannot leap out.
If you wish for the monastic groves to be level and peaceful so that everyone may be at ease, it would be better to topple King Aśoka. But tell me, how can King Aśoka be toppled?
He called to the assembly, saying, "Exert yourselves! Exert yourselves! Then he said again, "Alas, alas! King Aśoka has been toppled by others."
Is there not one who, seeing injustice, draws his sword to come to the aid of another? If there were none, this mountain monk would have no choice but to fall down by himself and rise up again.
(He strikes the whisk and descends from the seat. The Master was of a stern and resolute character; he presided over the assembly with ancient methods, and was at that time known as "Iron Face Chen."
Chan Master Puming Huilin of Daochang Monastery in Anji Prefecture was a native of Fuzhou. He ascended the hall and said:
"The leaking bamboo fence and the non-leaking wooden ladle; the white peonies in the courtyard and the red peonies in the railing.
Thinking back on the man who sat facing the wall for nine years, in the end he did not recognize this one point. Now tell me, what is this one point? He struck the meditation seat with his staff.
The seat below the platform; ascending the hall: One is many, and many are one. Upon the crown of Vairocana, it is as bright as the sun—neither one nor many.
This manifest case is free from confusion; picking up the old felt clappers, we sing the song of peace together in this enlightened age.
Chan Master Wuchuan Ju-hui of Daochang Monastery in Anji County was the son of the Wu family of that same prefecture.
He ascended the hall and said: "Zhong Kui sings the Liangzhou melody in his intoxication; The younger sister at the gate merely nods her head.
After the sea-roaming yakṣa has met him, Everyone claps their hands atop the high tower. If you, the assembly, can understand this, you will lock the tongues of all people in the world. If..."
"I could not have known this. I thought the old monk had some other extraordinary secret. [The Master] ascends the hall and says:

"Performing shadow-play atop a hundred-foot pole not only deceives you, but it deceives Heaven as well. I laugh at myself for my whole life on the divergent paths; now that I have returned in my old age, I possess not a single coin.
[The Master] ascends the hall and cites Linji’s instruction to the assembly: "One person stands atop a high peak, with no way to emerge."
The Road. One person stands at a crossroads; there is neither front nor back. Tell me, which one is in front? Which one is behind?
The Master said, "There is yet another person who is neither on the high mountain peak nor at the crossroads.
Why does the old fellow Linji not know this? Having said this, he descended from his seat.
Chan Master Yuanchi of Songtang at Xianning Temple in Lin’an Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "The reeds are white, the smartweeds are red;
by the stream, the tall bamboos are enshrouded in green mist. Idle clouds embrace the secluded rocks; jade dew drips upon the mountain thickets.
Last night the tortoise transformed into a turtle; this morning the water buffalo realized perfect penetration. Tsk!"
Chan Master Liaofan of Weian in Wuhui, Anji Prefecture, ascended the hall and said: "The events prior to kalpas of dust are majestic and manifest, with no front or back.
Movement and stillness cannot encompass them; their unfolding and rolling up are as swift as lightning. Do not say that ordinary people do not know them—the Buddha himself cannot see them.
Where exactly do they reside? Close these two flaps. Whether you realize it or not, for your sake I shall speak further."
He passed through the single line. After a long silence, he said, "The world is at peace; the imperial wind fans forever. He ascended the hall and raised the following case:
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "The Supreme Way is not difficult; it simply dislikes picking and choosing. Is this the nest of people of these times?
Zhaozhou replied, "Someone once asked this of me, and for five years I could not resolve it. The Master called to the assembly, "Zhaozhou possesses the eye on the crown of his head."
With the eye, one distinguishes the black from the white within the spark struck from flint; within the flash of lightning, one clarifies the principles of giving and taking.
Why, then, was he unable to discern this for five years? Do you understand? It is easy to distinguish flour in the snow, but difficult to identify soot in ink.
Chan Master Wen Guan Lingguang of Benji was the son of the Ye family of his native district, Wenzhou.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Tathāgatas of the past have already perfected this gate; better not to have done such a thing. The Bodhisattvas of the present each now enter perfect clarity;
better not to have done such a thing. Those who practice and study in the future should abide according to this; better not to have done such a thing."
"If there is nothing, do you still understand? Aside from Master Chen of Mount Hua, who among men does not carry along right and wrong?
*Chan.* Chan Master Wuzheng Huichu of Deshan in Changde Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Huanglong Zhen, was a native of Jingjiang Prefecture. He ascended the hall and looked around.
The assembly asked, "Do you see? In heaven, it forms the celestial bodies; on earth, it forms all shapes.
In the sun and moon, it is the waning and the waxing; in the four seasons, it is the cold and the heat. It is stirred by thunder and lightning, and moistened by wind and rain.
But tell me, as for the realm of the patch-robed monk, how is it? With a single kick, he overturned the four great oceans; with a single punch, he felled the Vulture Peak.
Mount Wutai. One cannot remain within the station of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Furthermore, he blows his fishing flute at the Bay of Mulu. Entering the hall:

he merely won the right to sing village songs and perform communal dances. A-he-he! Luo-lo-li! Thereupon, he performed a dance and descended from the seat.
Seat. The Head Seat (Shouzuo) Fachang of Ba’en Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Wanyan. He was a native of Kaifeng and a descendant of the Prime Minister Xue Ju-zheng.
In the seventh year of the Xuanhua era, he received the tonsure under Huiyuan of Huayan Temple in Yiyang, Changsha.

He traveled extensively among the monastic communities and entered deeply into the ocean of meaning within the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*. From Huxiang to Wannian, he visited Xuechao, with whom his spiritual resonance was established;

Xuechao appointed him to oversee correspondence. Later, he led the assembly at Baoyuan Monastery. In his quarters there was only a single low couch, and he possessed no other belongings. In the Gengzi year...

In the ninth month, he told the monks of the monastery, "After one month, I shall no longer remain here. On the twenty-first day of the tenth month, at dawn, he went to the abbot’s quarters to pay his respects for a meal.
He wrote a *yúfǔ* (Fisherman) lyric on the door of his room, then sat upon his couch with his legs drawn up and passed away.
The lyric reads: "This matter has often been laid bare in the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*; Where the plum blossoms, snow, and moon intermingle their radiance, A single laugh rings out vast and empty."
The wind-chimes of ten thousand ages speak; afar, the Milky Way stretches across the heavens. In the *Nanhua*, the butterfly’s dream is still fluttering;

who is it that treads upon the brindled tiger of Fenggan? Now, one has forgotten the path by which they came; at twilight, mountains and rivers stretch to the ends of the earth as the eyes watch the wild geese fly away.
Zen Master Shu of Yanqing on Mount Lu, a dharma successor of the founding abbot of Yue Shan, was asked by a monk: "Before the Many Sons Stupa, what did they discuss together? The Master said:
"Each time we meet, we grow older; how long can we remain brothers? The monk bowed, and the Master said: "Tangxing."

Day by day they increase. If one attempts to reconcile them with the seasons, what then becomes of the Buddha-dharma?

Tell me, are the causes and conditions of the seasons the same as or different from the principles of the Buddha-dharma? After a long silence, he said: "The shadowless tree is planted where no one sees;
its blossoming and fruition are naturally fragrant."
Chan Master Xingdao of Meian at Huiji Temple in Pingjiang Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "The gathering clouds are about to snow but have not yet snowed;
the beloved sun seems radiant but does not truly shine. Cold sparrows chirp noisily among the fences, and the biting north wind dances through the curtains.
If you wish to understand Shaoyang’s intimate verse, today I shall bring it forth for you face-to-face. He struck his staff and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Guangxiaoguo Min of Guangde Army was a native of Taoyuan in Changde. Ascending the hall, he cited the story of Nanquan’s “Beheading the Cat” and said:
“Nanquan raised it up and brought down the blade to execute it; even a six-armed asura could not have saved it.”
Even if both halls were to speak the Way, blood would surely flow to fill the streets.
Chan Master Huizhong of Xuefeng Qiutang in Fuzhou, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Xuefeng Niu, ascended the hall and said: "All day long one is in a constant bustle; yet that matter remains unimpeded."
"What is that matter? After a long silence, he said: "The heart bears no grudge against others; the face shows no color of shame.

Master Yuan of Penglai, a Dharma successor of Chan Master Jiao of Tiantong, resided on the mountain for thirty years without his feet ever crossing the threshold. He was revered by both monastics and laypeople.
Looking up at him, the Master spoke a verse: "A newly-sewn paper quilt is warm when lit; A peaceful sleep lasts through the fifth watch.
Hearing the bells and drums of the upper realm stir, Yet another day is added to this floating life."
Chan Master Shouhui Chongzhen Miyin Tonghui of Yuan Tong on Mount Lu in Jiangzhou, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Yuantong Min, ascended the hall and said: "One merely knows today and then tomorrow;
one does not realize that the early autumn has passed into the late autumn. Walking with steady steps upon the level path, one returns to one’s native village. Then...
Riding the bright moon across the Cangzhou isles. *Ei!* Those who have not undergone bitter toil do not know this.
The Chan Master Huanglong Daoguan of Longxing Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "An ancient said, 'The eye and form, the ear and sound—by these, the myriad dharmas are accomplished.
Yet why is it that from morning until evening, you all find these various dharmas failing to reach one another? He then gave a shout.
With a single shout, he said: "The ox is led into your nostrils; misfortune does not enter the door of a cautious household.

Yi suddenly attained great enlightenment. He thanked him, saying, "It is clear that the Buddha-dharma is not so very much. Tong shouted, "Put it down!

The Layman Du Xiang, Director of the Left Bureau, asked Yuan Tong, "This Dharma cannot be understood through thought or discrimination;
how should one approach it? Yuan Tong said, "Enter the mass of fire with your whole body. The Layman said, "Ultimately, how does one comprehend this?
Yuan Tong said, "Go straight ahead. The Layman hesitated. Yuan Tong said, "Would you like some more tea? The Layman said, "There is no need."
Tong said, "Why do you not understand it in this way? Gong realized the meaning and said, "It has always been so near.
Tong said, "A hundred thousand eight thousand [miles]. Gong then offered a verse: "Inconceivable! This is a great mass of fire.
To go thus is not to leave this very place. Tong said, "Ei! There is still this thing remaining. Gong said, "I beg the Master to grant me further instruction. Tong said, "Just so!"
"Go thus. The cauldron is cast of iron. The Master bowed his head in thanks.
Zen Master Xuanmi Li of Shitai in Yangzhou, a successor of Chan Master Mingzhao Hui, was asked by a monk: "Are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth the same as oneself?"
"This is different. The Master said, "In the cool night at the long pavilion, the moon is often spread out for travelers.

The monk said, "I thank the Master for his reply. The Master said, "The net is vast, making it difficult for birds; the line is thick, only then catching fish. The monk performed a dance and returned to the assembly.
The Master said, "The long river serves as a inkstone, frequently writing letters of severed ties. He ascended the hall and, citing the story of Baizhang’s wild fox, said, "It is not so."
The hand that turns back the waves need only boast of leaping over the sea; when Yi Ji draws his arrow, the many monkeys on the branches are startled.
Entering the hall, the Master seized a monk before reaching the seat and ascended the Dharma throne. The monk, terrified, was about to run away, whereupon the Master pointed to the seat and said:
"If one were to lead a donkey up onto this shed, it too would surely defecate upon it.
Why, then, do you all refuse? [The Master] drove them all away at once with his staff and said to his attendant, 'That was close!'"
Chan Master Lingyan Hui of Mount Emei, a successor of Chan Master Zhen of Fushan, was asked by a monk: "Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the seven Buddhas;
I wonder who is Mañjuśrī’s teacher? The Master replied: "The young woman at the sands of Jinsha."
Chan Master Chūn of Bào-cí in Hún-nán, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Lì of Xiáng-fú, ascended the hall and said: "A single glance from the blue eyes, and the Golden One knows where to return.
Coming with hands extended, it is like a king’s precious sword. Yet nowadays, people open up their own schools and each propounds different doctrines; this may indeed be called 'the ancient road.'"
When the ground is level, thorns grow; when the Dharma-eye is upright, it blinds itself. Thus one fails the former sages and buries one’s own spirit. But tell me:
without being buried and without failing, how can the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye be revealed?
Is there anyone who can reveal it? Come forth and reveal it! If there is none, take your poetry and books back to your old retreat; let the wild flowers weep.
The Chan Master Tudu Zhice of Mount Jing in Lin’an Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Youyun of Yunyan, was born into the Chen family of Tiantai.
In his youth, he relied upon [Master] Huguo. (In the *Lian deng hui yao*, this is recorded as the words of Master Wuhui. He was a native of Tiantai. From childhood, he followed [Master] Huguo.

The monk Chuguang shaved his head. At nineteen, he went to Guoqing Temple to pay his respects to Jishiguan. He experienced a sudden, clear realization. Next, he visited Dayuan at Wanshou Temple in Mingzhou.
Dayuan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Tiantai. Dayuan asked, "Have you seen the Great Master Zhiyi?
The Master replied, "Even now, there is no shortage of him. Dayuan asked, "Why is he right under your own feet?"
The Master said, "You have missed it right before your face. Yuan said, "This Honored One is luxuriant without weeding and straight without being propped up.
One day, he took his leave. As Yuan saw him off at the gate, he patted the Master’s back and said, "The treasure house is near;
this city is not real. The Master nodded in agreement. He then went to Yuzhang to visit Dian-niu, traveling via Yunju. Snow and wind blocked the road, and he sat there for forty-two days.
One day at noon, as the sound of the wooden board rang out clearly, he attained a sudden and great awakening.

When he arrived at the gate, Dian-niu pointed specifically at him and said, "Where have you seen gods and ghosts come from? The Master replied, "I heard the sound of the board at Yunju and came. Dian-niu asked, "What is that?"
The Master said, "Shatter empty space; it has no handle at all. Niuzhu said, "The matter beyond this is not yet settled.

The Master said, "The neighbor to the east sits in the dark; the neighbor to the west curses one another. Niuzhu said, "Rising far above Buddhas and patriarchs, a single unicorn in the future will suffice for you to establish your school.
Later, while presiding over the assembly, he ascended the hall and cited the teachings, saying: "If one sees me by form, or seeks me by sound..."
"I am one who walks the path of deviance; such a person cannot see the Tathāgata.
Although it is thus, it is truly like catching a rat and breaking an oil jar. Master Huai said, "Where are your eyes? Although he thus exposes the old Śākyamuni, what can be done?
He is still picking up the crumbs and licking his fingers. If it were Tuidu, it would not be so: "Seeking through form or sound..."
"It is not an obstacle. Amidst the shadows of a hundred flowers, one embroiders mandarin ducks. Since learning the secret of the golden needle, let the wind blow as it will;
the fragrance fills the sleeves. When the Master was about to pass away, he ascended the seat to bid farewell to the assembly and instructed his disciples to offer a written memorial for him.

As the disciples sat upright and listened intently until the words reached "May this offering be enjoyed" (*shàng xiǎng*), the Master broke into a smile. Two days later, he bathed, changed his robes, and gathered the assembly.
He spoke in verse: "The four elements have now dispersed; smoke and clouds return as they please. Under the autumn sky, the frosty night moon casts its brilliance across ten thousand *li*.
In an instant, he passed away in stillness. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the foot of the eastern ridge."
Master Xinxiang Xian was the dharma heir of Master Jinsheng Wen of Chengdu Prefecture. A monk asked, "What is the source of the Great Way?

The Master said, "The Yellow River has nine bends. The monk asked, "What is the decree that cannot be transgressed? The Master said, "An iron snake cannot penetrate it. The monk prepared to speak further.
[The student] deliberated [on this].
The Master then struck him. This is the lineage of Chan Master Huichen of Yuwang, the sixteenth generation under Nanyue.
Chan Master Wanshan Xinwen Tanben of Taizhou was a native of Yongjia. While residing at Jiangxin, he ascended the hall after recovering from an illness and said:
"Vimalakīrti, when ill, exhausted all principles of reason. Longxiang, when ill, suffered from incessant coughing; though his coughing did not cease, he exhausted all principles of reason.
Though he exhausted all principles of reason, his coughing did not cease. Do you all recognize the meaning within this?"
The meaning is not yet there. Originally, the long river gathered the cold wind; instead, it causes the pillar to suffer from a headwind. Entering the hall: "To see once is to see at all.
An octagonal millstone turns in the void. "To attain once is to attain forever. Vermilion cinnabar from Chenjin is as black as ink.
The autumn wind blows over the Wei River—this has already fallen within Yunmen’s three phrases. Fallen leaves fill Chang’an; how many [can truly perceive them]?
"And now you have been deceived by your own eyes. Holding up his whisk, he said, "Whether you can be deceived or not, it all rests in the hands of Wanyan.
Do you see? The moon embraces the Peak of Flowers while the Stone of the Waving Hand beckons; the bridge is broken as the water falls over the Cliff of Self-Sacrifice.
A monk asked, "What was the meaning of Baizhang rolling up the mat? The Master said, "Drawing the bow after the thief has fled. The Governor of Siming presented snow...
Dong commanded the Master to take charge. The Master declined with a verse, saying: "In the midst of the noisy basket, I have just found relief;
But now the drum has been withdrawn, yet its beat does not cease. Do not take the thousand-fathom snow of Nanyue Peak To come again and exchange for my pair of eyes."
Chan Master Liaopu Tianhong of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture was a native of Fuzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "The scorching heat is like being burned, impossible to restrain;
it blazes so fiercely it seems to melt gold. Beyond the curtain of the night-bright moon, no one arrives; the numinous tree stands remote, turning its shade green.
He ascended the hall again and said: "Long rains have not ceased; half-asleep, half-awake. One might say that heaven and earth are in harmony."
"Virtue! The sun and moon harmonize their brilliance; the four seasons harmonize their order; the ghosts and spirits harmonize their auspiciousness and misfortune.

He then shouted, "Stop! Stop! The inner trigram is already formed; why seek further external images? He struck his staff down and said, "Just now I cast the hexagram *Leitian Dazhuang* (Thunder under Heaven, Great Strength);
now it has transformed into *Dihuo Mingyi* (Earth over Fire, Illumination). He ascended the hall and said, "The ox-hide drum is the pillar; the pillar makes a chirping sound."
A chirping sound. The lantern pretends not to know; its empty brightness shines upon itself. The old *chifen* dragon on the roof of the hall hears it and laughs aloud.
At the side gate, they lean their ears to listen, then climb up and circle about, striking it. It is like the chrysanthemum of the tenth day: who is it that slightly opens it?
"Ah-he-he!"—it is not necessarily the case that the autumn fragrance withers in a single night. The *wei-dou* for brewing tea is not the same as a small cauldron. The chamber.
He asked the assembly: "When a thief comes, you must strike him; when a guest comes, you must welcome them.

But what if at the hour of midnight, a person’s face resembles a thief’s and a thief’s face resembles a person’s? How do you distinguish between them? He ascended the hall and said: "The Guanyin Cliff rings out with clear, tinkling sounds;
the Taishi Rock resounds with sharp, clattering echoes. The weeds in the West Garden look as if they were unfit for eating, yet the flowers blooming in the East Valley are truly reckless."
"Red. Now tell me: is this the meaning of the Patriarchs or the meaning of the Teachings? Is it for practical use on the journey, or is it merely the circulation of worldly conventions?
If you cannot discern this, Xuefeng will overturn your rice bucket; if you can discern it, Ganji will prostrate before the steamer. *Pauses.* Ascending the hall:
When Deshan enters the gate, he immediately strikes with his staff; when Linji enters the gate, he immediately shouts. At the place where Linji shouts, it is Deshan’s staff that reaches his ears.
Deaf. When Deshan wielded his staff, Linji’s eyes were blinded by his shout. Although one strikes and another lifts, within this there is total life and total death.
[The Master] then let out a shout and struck the ground once with his staff, saying: "I dare ask you all: is this life or is it death?
After a long silence, he said: "A gentleman may enter."
Chan Master Zonghui of Xiyuan in Nanjian Prefecture was a native of Wuzhou. Having long relied upon Master Wushi, he attained a profound realization of the Dharma-patience (*dharmakṣānti*).
Once, when a temple monk reported a violation of the tea prohibition to the authorities, the officials arrested the monastery administrator.

The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "If we do not plead his case, the guilt will fall upon me; yet if we plead it ourselves, he will instead suffer punishment. I cannot bear to do this. He then ordered—
The drum was struck and he ascended the seat. He spoke a verse, saying: "The county magistrate’s summons does not cease for a moment; how can it compare to the clarity of long-past affairs?
Previously there was a song of non-arising; rejoice that today its melody has been completed. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
National Preceptor Tantan of Goryeo succeeded to the throne at a young age. He deeply revered the Vehicle of the Patriarchs (Zongsheng).

Through a maritime merchant, Fang Jingren, he reached Siming and recorded the words of Wushi to bring back home. Upon reading them, the Master attained awakening; he immediately abdicated his position and shaved his head.

He composed a letter containing the essentials of the teachings and verses on the four modes of deportment, instructing Jingren to present them to Wushi. Wushi replied: "The Buddhas and Patriarchs..."

Appearing in the world, he did not bestow a single dharma upon others; rather, he truly caused them to have faith in themselves, to awaken on their own, to realize for themselves, and to arrive at realization by themselves.

Possessing great knowledge and vision, he spoke according to what he saw and acted according to what he spoke. Mountains, rivers, the great earth, grasses, trees, thickets, and forests all bear witness to this together;
it has been thus for a long time. Later, there was also the transmission of the Dharma, the text of which briefly states: "Birth..."

Throughout vast kalpas, the cycle of birth and death exhausts all possibilities; yet to encounter a master of the fundamental school who, with the seal of the three essentials, verifies and certifies this Dharma—this is truly what is meant by the blind turtle encountering the floating hole in a piece of wood.
Chan Master Wuzhu Ben of Longhua in Lin’an Prefecture was a native of Guǎngdé.

He ascended the hall and, citing Grand Master Yúnmén, held up a sesame cake and said, “I only provide offerings for those of the Two Zhè regions; I do not provide offerings for those from the north. The assembly remained silent.
Yúnmén himself provided a substitute response, saying, “The weather is cold and the days are short; two people share one bowl. The Master [Wuzhu] said, “The old man of Shàoyáng...”
In the Han language, it is called "an echo within. To apply an awl to the spot where one feels pain—when examined closely, this turns into a poisonous drug.
Do you all understand? Half is south of the Yellow River, half is north of the Yellow River; a single expanse of empty stillness, as black as ink.
To contemplate this in cold silence brings nothing but sorrow. How vexing is this old thief Yunmen! Thief! Thief! [He] descended from his seat and did not even go on rounds of the hall.

Chan Master Ji of Dongshan in Linjiang Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Lin of Daochang. Once, when Li Chaoling and his nephew, the lay practitioner Xianglin Jushi Xiang Gongzi Yin, went to visit him, they asked:
"When the 'house-thief' troubles one, what then? The Master said, "Who is the house-thief? Li [replied].
[The Master] raised his fist. The Master said, "The thief’s identity has been revealed. Li said, "Do not deceive people. The Master said, "The evidence is right here.
Li was speechless. The Master showed him with a verse: "The domestic thief vexes the person—what can be done? Even the thousand sages turn their faculties back for his sake.
Pervading the world and pervading space, yet leaving no trace; Without support and without dwelling, he is beyond all nets. "Thief! Thief!"
Fierce generals and heroic soldiers cannot capture him; he suspects and slays the old Chan monks of the world. He makes the ancient Maitreya in the bustling marketplace burst into laughter.
Enough, enough! There is no need to seek with the mind outward. In a single glance, the thief’s own body is revealed;
caught with the stolen goods, he has no peer in the world. No peer in the world—truly worthy of veneration. From now on, he will no longer boast of his skills; he remains settled and at peace.
When the family business flourishes, the myriad phenomena of the universe clap their hands in unison.
Chan Master Lǎn’ān Dàoshū of Língyǐn Monastery in Lín’ān Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Huì of Dào-chǎng. He was the son of the Xú family of Sī’ān in Wúxīng. Initially, he resided at...
At which mountain? He subsequently moved to Huazang and Longxing. Initially, he was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Lingyin.

Emperor Xiaozong invited him to the inner palace and inquired about the essentials of the Way of Chan. The Master replied: "This matter lies within Your Majesty’s own majestic daily life where you respond to circumstances;

fundamentally, it is free from the confusion of arising and ceasing in knowledge and views, and devoid of the distinction between sage and ordinary, delusion and awakening. It simply requires that you protect right mindfulness."

In accord with the Way, when the mind withdraws from external objects, karma cannot bind one. Having completely eliminated the maladies of dullness and agitation, one naturally forgets the intent of question and answer;
how much more so now, in the presence of the Buddha who is currently in his place of succession—what could not be accomplished within the radiance of Prajñā?
"Did you see him? he asked. The other nodded his head four times. The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "The immortal Zhang Guolao rides a donkey through the marketplace;
one hears only the clatter of its hooves—who would have known it was made of paper? Later, he retired to the Yongan Hermitage at Mingjiao, living in carefree contentment.
He inscribed a verse upon the wall, which read: "The plum blossoms in the snow are the message of spring; the pond..."
In the moonlight of mid-autumn, his spirit was clear; for years, it seemed there had been no finer delight. "Do not speak of our family tradition to others.
In the eighth month of the Bingshen year of the Chunxi era, he manifested a slight illness, wrote a verse, and passed away. He was interred at Yong’an.

On the day that the Head Seat Wuchu of Guangxiao Temple in Guading Commandery, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Guangxiao Min, was assigned to share the seat, he addressed the assembly. He raised the dialogue concerning the wind and the banner, and upon reaching the point, "Where the mind of the person moves," he said:
"The Patriarch spoke thus, yet he has deceived an entire shipload of people. As for the patch-robed monks of the present day..."
Nor can it be understood in such a way. Since it cannot be understood in such a way, after all, how is it? After a long silence, he said:
"In the sixth month, it is good for making sauce; one must simply take care not to put too much salt in it."

The Dharma successor of Chan Master Wannian Ben of the seventeenth generation under Nanyue, Chan Master Xian of Lin’gang Hermitage in Wenzhou, ascended the hall and said: He cited Chongshou’s instruction to the assembly, which said: "Recognize the bench."
"It is more than a full circumference. Yunmen said, "If you recognize the bench, heaven and earth are vastly different.
The Master said, "Old man Chongshou sits people to death; Great Master Yunmen runs people to death. Longming, however, is not like this:
"If you recognize the bench, its four legs rest firmly on the ground; when you wish to sit, you sit; when you wish to rise, you rise. He ascended the hall and cited [this].
The Story of Zhaozhou’s Examination of the Old Woman. The verse says: A lady of snow and ice, her countenance most extraordinary; She constantly takes up her jade flute to blow for others.
Within the melody, boundless hearts are moved; To the Lord of Spring alone, she grants the honor of being the foremost branch.
Chan Master Daopeiyi of Daming Monastery in Tanzhou was a native of Kuaiji. He ascended the hall and said: "The trees have shed their leaves and the sky is empty;

the heavens are cold and the waters are frozen. Śākyamuni has nowhere to hide his body. Demolishing the eastern fence to patch up the western wall, he runs straight into Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Unempty-Vision and requests instruction on the Samādhi of Buddha-Recitation. How extraordinary! Yet he then says: 'Golden light...'"
Mingyun, come forward. [The Master] steps back and says, "Go have some tea. He ascends the hall and says: "The Old Barbarian opened a single path;
how direct it was! He simply said: 'Rest is Bodhi; the nature-pure, luminous mind is not obtained from others.
Yet later generations failed to find its gate, racing north and south, traveling east and west, throughout the years and seasons, without a single place of rest. Do you all still..."
“Can you rest? Rest! Rest! He ascended the hall and raised the following case: One day, Master Huìtáng asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk replied, “From Nánxióng Prefecture.
Huìtáng said, “What did you come here for? The monk said, “To visit venerable elders. Huìtáng said, “It would be better for you to return home.
The monk asked, “I do not know what the meaning of the Master’s instruction to return home is. Huìtáng said, “Three [generations] in one’s native village.”
He bought a piece of salted fish, about the size of a palm. The Master said, "I would rather have my body shattered into fine dust than ever blind the eyes of a monk.
Huìtáng was slightly more experienced; some people say that for such a man, it is difficult to forget what he is familiar with.

There was no place for further conversation. He ascended the hall and presented the kōan of the King of Kasmira questioning Venerable Siṃha regarding the emptiness of the aggregates (*skandha-śūnyatā*).
The Master offered this verse: "When did the Venerable One ever attain the emptiness of the aggregates? The King of Kasmira needlessly slew the spring breeze himself.
After the rain, the peach blossoms have already fallen; They have dyed the flowing waters of the stream crimson."

Ming said, "You should step aside for a moment; I have somewhere I must go. The Master returned home.
The next day, the Master prepared his formal robes and went to the abbot’s quarters to offer thanks. Yuanmiao scolded him, saying, "Not yet.

From then on, whenever Yuanmiao went out for walks in the mountains, the Master would watch for his departure; even if it was late, he would invariably strike the drum to assemble the assembly. When Yuanmiao hurried back, he said angrily, "This is a minor monastery!
Why have you begun the practice of ascending the seat at dusk? Where did you get such a rule? The Master replied, "This is the 'evening session' (wanchan) of Fenyang. What do you mean?"

Is this not like being bound by a measuring line? One day, Ming ascended the hall. The Master stepped forward and asked, "When the dark birds warble their cries and leave the clouds to enter the tangled peaks, what then?
Ming said, "I walk amidst the wild weeds; you, moreover, have entered a deep village. The Master said, "The official does not permit even a needle to pass;
let me ask one more question. Ming then gave a shout. The Master said, "A fine shout! Ming shouted again. The Master also shouted.
Daming let out two consecutive shouts. The Master prostrated himself. Daming said, "This matter can only be shouldered by one who is a true person.
The Master shook his sleeves and departed. When Daming moved to Xinghua, the Master took his leave to return to Jiufeng. Later, monastics and laypeople welcomed him to reside at Yangqi.
Next, he moved to Yungai. On the day he accepted the invitation, he held up his dharma robe and showed it to the assembly, saying:
"Do you understand? If you do not, today you will have no choice but to run headlong into the herd of water buffalo. Do you know where? At Jiuxiu in Yunchang, Pingshi, and Yangqi.
He then ascended the seat. At that time, a monk stepped forward; the Master said: "Before the old fisherman has even cast his line, a leaping scale leaps forth..."

A wave came. The monk then shouted. The Master said, "I did not believe you. The monk clapped his hands and returned to the assembly. The Master said, "How much wind from the Dragon King can you endure?
A monk asked, "Whose song do you sing, Master? Whose ancestral style do you succeed? The Master said, "If there is a horse, I ride it; if there is no horse, I walk.
The monk said, "An elder with such youthful vigor possesses truly clever stratagems. The Master said, "I am mindful that you are advanced in years."
"I grant you thirty blows. He asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A three-legged donkey prancing on its hooves.
The monk asked, "Is this not it? The Master said, "Elder of Hunan. Then he asked, "Is there anyone else who wishes to ask a question?"
Come forth and meet me! Yangqi’s life today rests in your hands; you may drag him about as you please, pulling him this way and that. Why is this so?
A true man of great character must make a definitive judgment in public; do not act like pressing a gourd under water in secret.
Bring it forth for inspection before the assembly; do not let your face turn red. Is there anyone who can do so?
"Is there anyone? Come forth and let us resolve this! If not, Yangqi has lost face today. The Master then descended from his seat.
Monk Jiufeng Qin held him back and said, "Today I am delighted to find a fellow practitioner.
The Master asked, "What is the matter of being a fellow practitioner? Qin said, "Jiufeng plows the furrow; Yangqi drags the plowshare. The Master said, "At such a time as this..."
Yangqi was before him; Jiufeng was before him. As Qin hesitated, the Master pushed him away and said, "I thought we were fellow practitioners;
it turns out you are not. A monk asked, "When both person and dharmas are discarded, that is not yet the ultimate standard of a patch-robed monk.
When both Buddhas and patriarchs have perished, that is still a point of doubt for a student. I wonder, how do you, Reverend, guide people? The Master said, "You simply want to test me."
The new elder said, "If that is so, then freshly cut green wood is burned with its leaves still attached. The Master said, "Seven times nine is sixty-three.
A monk asked, "What was the intent behind the ancients' 'facing the wall'? The Master said, "The people of the Western Heavens do not understand the language of Tang.
He ascended the hall and said: "Mist locks the long sky; wind arises in the vast fields. The hundred grasses and trees all let out the great lion’s roar, expounding the Dharma."
The Great Mahāprajñāpāramitā: the Buddhas of the three periods of time turn the great wheel of Dharma beneath the very feet of you all.
If you can understand this, your efforts will not have been in vain; if you do not understand, do not say that the mountain terrain of Yangqi is steep—there is yet a higher peak ahead.
Entering the hall, he cited an ancient kōan as a gift for the assembly.
Jiur said: "The mouth is fit only for eating rice. [He] ascended the hall and said: "Treading upon a scale-weight, as hard as iron; a mute man has a dream—whom can he tell it to?

Zen Master Zhuiyuan of Shousheng on Mount Yuezhang in Yingzhou, a successor of Zen Master Yong of Baoning, was asked by a monk: "I do not ask about the Patriarch’s intent coming from the West;
what is 'one color'? The Master said, "Before my eyes there is no *śrāmaṇera*; here there is no old monk. [The monk] said, "Since it is neither..."
"It is so. How can this be understood? The Master said, "Receive the meaning at the tip of the hook; do not fixate on the zero point of the scale.

He then continued, "In every instance of question and answer, it is like striking a stone to spark a fire, flowing forth inexhaustible treasures of the Dharma for the three types of grass and two types of wood."
"Universally moistening its bounty"—this is letting go. "Clouds arise at the valley mouth; mist shrouds the vast sky"—this is holding fast.
Even the blue-eyed barbarian monk would be left at a loss. Such proclamations as those of Shousheng are merely the gate of transformation;
yet they still lack the very core of a patch-robed monk’s realization. I dare ask you all: what is this core of a patch-robed monk? After a long silence, he said: "Spread."
The needle opens both eyes; toward which end do you look?
Chan Master Chuwen of Shousheng Monastery in Wuzhen, Anji Prefecture, ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said: "This wooden *zhilu* from Huazang—casually I draw it forth.
It is not that I am unwilling to spare my hands; it is simply that those of our mountain school have no fixed attachments. He then tapped the mountain.
The mountains shook; the waters were stirred until the waves overflowed. Suddenly seizing [the staff] firmly, he applied the laws and regulations to every matter:

where one wished to lean, one could not lean; where one wished to bend, one could not bend. He suddenly called out to the assembly, saying: "Do not say that there are eyes upon the tip of the staff as bright as the sun;
the radiance shining above is nothing but lacquer. With these words, he struck once. Entering the hall, he made a piercing thrust with his staff.
Skin and bone joined together; every pull and every lift. Sticking to the hands and adhering to the feet. A flash of lightning, a spark from flint. Head drooping, tail drooping.
Faster than a split arrow or a chasing wind. Half-alive, half-dead. Bumping into it, knocking against it—what eyebrows can one find? Bright head, dark head.
What kind of eyes are these? It is not like this at all. You are right in the middle of the path;

even if your total capacity has not yet reached the further shore, and even if you are completely naked and bare, with nothing to grasp, there is still a trace of lingering attachment. When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, [it is so].
Furthermore, tell me: what is the use of having a mouth? After a long silence, he said, "Heh! Keep it for eating.
On the day of the opening of the hall, Chan Master Baoji Zongying of Lingjushan in Xingzhou held his staff crosswise and said:
The great assembly has arrived here. Without kinship or estrangement, one is naturally not alone. Without interior or exterior, one moves with sovereign ease.
In this sovereignty, there is no loneliness. Pure Vairocana issues the command; Śākyamuni proclaims it; Maitreya explains it.
Adapting the teaching to the faculties, they mutually interact. Look at the staff of Ratnakūṭa: its black lacquer shines, its two ends perfectly matched.
"A-he-he! What words are these? After a long silence, he said, "Matters of the world are simply to be judged by the path of righteousness;
the human heart is difficult to align with the full moon. He struck the ground once and descended from his seat.
A monk asked Zen Master Jingfu Riyu of Longxing Prefecture, “What is the Way? The Master said, “The heavens dawn with the white clouds;
the waters flow with the bright moon. The monk asked, “What is one who is on the Way? The Master said, “One has already set out, yet has not yet arrived.”
This was ultimately excessive. Furthermore, a monk stepped out from the assembly and drew a circle. The Master made a single stroke with his hand.
The monk performed a dance and returned to the assembly. The Master said, "In a household that possesses the White泽 (Bai Ze) map, there will certainly be no such demons.
He then took up his staff and said, "Countless Buddhas have turned the Great Dharma Wheel here; the patriarchs of past and present have expounded the Great [Dharma] here."
Regarding the meaning of the Dharma: if you can believe and attain this, then every phenomenon is inherently perfected from the beginning, and every moment of thought is entirely complete.
If you cannot believe this, then as I walk along today, I shall not hesitate to swing my arm; I shall further recite these verses for you once more. (He strikes the meditation seat once.
He descends from the seat.
On the day of the opening of the hall by Chan Master Riyi of Shangfang in Anjì Prefecture, after the head monk had finished striking the gavel, the Master said:
"Before the gavel was struck, observing 'one' was already not accomplished; after the gavel was struck, observing 'two' was likewise not right.
Reaching this point, even those with iron eyes and copper pupils must be shattered into a hundred pieces. Is there any monk who does not shrink from peril? Come forth and try!"
[The Master] went to look. At that time, two monks came out together. The Master said, "One arrow brings down two birds.
A monk said, "I have not even asked my question yet; why are you in such a hurry? The Master said, "Are you perhaps a monk from Silla? The monk hesitated. The Master said: [He struck him.]
[The Master] struck the pillar. [A monk] asked, "What is the matter on the side before one has appeared in the world? The Master said, "A shrimp at the bottom of the well swallows the moon.
[The monk] asked, "What is the matter on the side after one has appeared in the world? The Master said, "A heron steps on a broken stalk of withered reed.
[The monk] asked, "Setting aside these two paths, what is the Master’s way of benefiting people? The Master said, "A perfectly complete, fine fellow."
A diamond drill. Laid out on the street, to whom would it be sold? He asked, "What is the many-year-old water buffalo? The Master said, "Teeth sparse and eyes dim.
He asked, "When meeting in a bustling marketplace, what is the matter? The Master said, "Going east, buy cheap; going west, sell dear.
He said, "If suddenly one neither acts as if it were dear nor acts as if it were cheap, then what? The Master said, "Zhengzhou."
"Radish. He asked, "All sentient beings possess Buddha-nature. Since they possess Buddha-nature, why do they nevertheless enter the wombs of donkeys and horses?
The Master said, "They know it and yet deliberately commit the offense. [The monk] asked, "In what place, then, should one repent?"
The Master struck him, saying, "For now, it is like trying to treat a dead horse with medicine. He asked, "What is it like when presented face-to-face?
The Master said, "Half a catty in the left eye; eight taels in the right eye. The monk lifted up his sitting mat and said, "What about this one? The Master said, "No need to bring it out.
Then, looking around to the left and right, he said, "When the Yellow-Faced Old Man took seven steps, the very spot beneath his feet was just right for a..."
A needle. That blue-eyed barbarian sat upright for nine years; what a pity for that single notch upon the crown of his head!

Had there been at that time a monk who exerted himself for the sake of the assembly and applied this lethal blow, we would have spared the picking of flowers and the smiling, which needlessly broke his countenance, and the standing in snow waist-deep, which merely became a worn track. From then on, taking error for truth, they have struck one another with their baskets.
The basket eventually bore five fragrant leaves; a thousand lamps continued their flames. Upon the curved wooden frame, he sang two as three;

at the tip of his *khakkhara* staff, he pointed south as north. Even when pressed to advance or retreat, there were those who questioned the Dharma and questioned the mind, leaning against the gate or the wall—those seeking the Buddha and seeking the Patriarch—who, upon seeing the cypress tree in front of the courtyard, would immediately call it by name.

"The Patriarch’s intent in coming from the West was 'gazing at the mountains in broad daylight. Yet you further mistake this for your own self. Little do you realize that this Great Matter is inherently numinous and luminous;
it has never been interrupted throughout the bounds of the future. It does not depend on cultivation or realization, nor does it reside in thought.
Though Śāriputra may have had things he did not know, it was not something Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra could have debated. Have you not seen [the words of] Mazu?"
A single shout left Baizhang deaf for three days; Bao-shou’s command was carried out, and the entire city of Zhenzhou was blinded.
Such great capacity and great function are like a sudden clap of thunder—unstoppable. A single call and a single response are like a precipitous cliff—impossible to tread upon.
At such a moment, the Buddhas of the three periods can only look on from the sidelines; the Patriarchs of the six generations have the right to bear witness. Great!
"Everyone, tell me: is there anyone present today who can provide proof? After a long silence, he said: "A note! He ascended the hall and said:
"Shi-de carries the firewood; Han-shan burns the fire. Only Feng-gan sits coldly within his cave. Now tell me, what excellence does Feng-gan possess? After a long silence, he said:
"If one has no servants for small errands, one cannot be considered a gentleman."

Chan Master Foguo Keqin of Zhaojue Monastery in Chengdu Prefecture was the dharma heir of Chan Master Wuzu Yan, the fourteenth generation descendant of Nanyue. He was the son of the Luo family of Pengzhou; his lineage followed the Confucian tradition.
When the Master was a child, he could memorize a thousand words a day. Once, while visiting Miaoji Temple, he saw a Buddhist scripture;

after reading it three times, he felt a sense of profound longing as if he had recovered a long-lost possession, saying, "I am surely a śramaṇa from a past life. He immediately left home and, under Zhixing, received the tonsure.

He followed Wenzhao to master the exegesis of the sutras and received the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* from Minxing. Shortly thereafter, he fell ill and was on the verge of death, whereupon he sighed and said, "All..."
"The Buddha’s true path to Nirvana does not reside within words and phrases. Since I sought it through sound and sought to see it through form, it is only fitting that I have failed to find it.
He then departed and went to the seat of Chan Master Zhenjue Sheng. At that time, Sheng was freshly cutting his arm to draw blood.
The Master pointed and said, "This is a single drop from Caoxi. The Master was startled; after a long while, he said, "Is the Way truly like this?
He then set out on foot and left Sichuan. First he visited Yuquan Hao, and subsequently relied upon Jinluan Xin, Dayue Zhe, Huanglong Xin, and Donglin Du.
All of them designated him as a vessel for the Dharma, yet Huitang remarked, "In the future, he will be the one who carries on the lineage of Linji."
He was now under the care of his father. Finally, he went to see the Fifth Patriarch and exhausted all his skillful means; yet the Patriarch would not grant him approval.

He then remarked, "The Patriarch is forcibly changing people," and spoke insolent words, departing in a fit of indignation. The Patriarch said, "Wait; when you are struck by a severe fever, you will finally think of me.
When the Master reached Mount Jin, he contracted a case of smallpox and was extremely ill. Recalling what he had seen on ordinary days...

He tested him in various situations, but the man showed no signs of progress. Tracing back the words of the Fifth Patriarch, he made a vow to himself, saying, "When my illness subsides slightly, I shall return to the Fifth Patriarch.
Once his illness was cured, he returned immediately. Upon seeing him, the Patriarch was pleased and ordered him to enter the hall at once.

He then entered the quarters of the attendants (*śayanāsana*). Only half a month had passed when an imperial commissioner arrived, returning to Shu after resigning his office. He went to the Patriarch to inquire about the Way, and the Patriarch said:
"Director of Judicial Review, have you ever read the *Xiaoyan shi* (Poems of Minor Elegance) when you were young? There are two lines that are quite similar:

'Frequently calling for Little Jade is originally a matter of no concern; it is simply that the husband desires to recognize the voice. The Director of Judicial Review responded, 'Yes, yes. Zuzhao said, 'But listen carefully.'"
Just as the Master returned and stood in attendance, [Dongshan] asked, "I heard you, Venerable, recite a poem with a hint of sensuality. Does the Provincial Inspector understand it?
Jue said, "He only recognizes the sound. The Master said, "It is precisely because the husband must recognize the sound. Since he has already recognized the sound..."
"Why is it not so? The Patriarch asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
It is the cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master suddenly attained realization. He hurried out and saw a rooster fly onto the railing, spreading its wings and crowing.
He said to himself, "Is this not sound? He then tucked incense in his sleeve, entered the room, and presented what he had attained, offering this verse: Golden Duck...
The incense has faded within the brocade curtains; amidst the sounds of flutes and songs, he is supported home by those who have drunk too much.

This one episode of youthful elegance can be known only by the beloved woman alone. The Patriarch said, "The great matter of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is not something that those of inferior capacity or weak roots can attain.
I rejoice with you. The Patriarch then addressed the elders of the mountain community at large, saying, "My attendant has realized Zen."

Based on this, he was promoted to the position of head of the community. During the Chongning era, he returned to his hometown to visit his parents; the fourfold assembly came out to welcome and pay their respects to him.
Guo Gong Zhizhang, the Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and Governor of Chengdu, invited him to propagate the Dharma of the Sixth Patriarch at the re-established Zhaojue Monastery.

During the Zhenghe era, he retired from his duties and traveled south across the gorges. At that time, Zhang Wujin was residing in Jingnan, where he considered himself a master of Daoist learning; [Zhang] had rarely seen [the Master].
He granted his approval. The Master moored his boat and went to visit him. They engaged in an extensive discussion on the essential meaning of the *Avataṃsaka*, saying:

"The realm of direct perception (*pratyakṣa*) in the *Avataṃsaka* is the total reality of both principle and phenomena; there is not the slightest element of artificiality therein. Thus, within the one, there are the myriad, and through the myriad, one is fully realized.

One follows upon one, and the myriad follows upon the myriad, vast and inexhaustible. Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings—these three are without distinction. Their contraction and expansion are entirely sovereign."
"Unobstructed and perfectly interfused. Although this is the ultimate principle, it is ultimately just ripples in windless water. At this, the Official involuntarily drew his seat closer.
The Master then asked, "At this point, is this the same as the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, or is it different?
The Official replied, "It is the same. The Master said, "That still does not touch upon it. The Official’s expression turned sullen. The Master said, "Have you not seen the clouds..."

The gateways, the mountain ranges, the rivers, and the great earth—wherein not even a hair’s breadth of fault or affliction exists—are still merely turning phrases (*zhuǎn jù*). Only when one reaches the point where not a single form (*yī sè*) is seen does one begin to grasp half of the teaching.
Yet, one must further know that there is a time for the full presentation of the ultimate truth (*xiàngshàng quán tí*). This was the case with Deshan and Linji.

"Is this not the total presentation? The Duke nodded in agreement. The following day, the Master again raised the topics of the *dharmadhātu* of phenomena (*sāṃvṛtika-dharmadhātu*) and the *dharmadhātu* of principle (*pāramārthika-dharmadhātu*), up to the *dharmadhātu* of the non-obstruction between phenomenon and principle.
The Master asked again, "Can these be called Chan? The Duke replied, "It is precisely where Chan can be spoken.
The Master laughed and said, "Not so. This is still within the measure of the *dharmadhātu*. For as long as the measure of the *dharmadhātu* has not been extinguished," [it is not yet Chan].

Upon reaching the Dharma-realm of the non-obstruction of phenomena and phenomena (*dharmadhātu-pratītyasamutpāda*), where the dimensions of the Dharma-realm are extinguished, only then can one properly speak of Chan.
Thus, [the masters ask]: "What is the Buddha? A dried-up dung pellet. "What is the Buddha? Three catties of hemp. For this reason, the verse by Zhenjing says:

"Phenomena and phenomena are unimpeded; Spontaneous and sovereign as one wishes. In hand he grasps a pig's head, Yet from his mouth he recites the pure precepts. He chases people out of the brothels, And comes back to pay off his wine debts. (10)

He resided at Ziji Street. Opening the cloth bag [of his belongings], the Duke said, "How magnificent is this discourse! How rarely can such words be heard? Thereupon, he retained him with the etiquette due to a teacher.
He lived at Biryam and later moved to Daolin. The State Councilor Deng Gong Zichang memorialized the Emperor to grant him purple robes and a formal title.
By imperial decree, he was appointed to dwell at Jiangshan in Jinling. Students flocked there until there was no room to accommodate them. By another edict, he was appointed to Tianning Wan...
The Emperor summoned him for an audience and bestowed upon him exceptional favor and patronage. At the beginning of the Jianyan era, he was further appointed to Mount Jinshan.

When the imperial carriage visited Weiyang, he entered the presence of the Emperor, who conferred upon him the title of Chan Master Yuanwu. He was later transferred to Yunju, and after some time, he again took charge of Zhaojue.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of Yunmen’s statement regarding Mount Sumeru? The Master replied, "He cannot be pushed forward, nor can he be held back. [The monk] said, "Not yet..."
"Does this still involve a transgression? The Master said, "Sit upon your tongue. The monk asked, "The Dharma does not arise in isolation; it is born only by relying on conditions.
He then lifted up his sitting cloth and said, "This is the condition; which one is the Dharma? The Master said, "You have been robbed of your spear by the *dārala* (monk).
A monk asked, "An ancient said: 'Carrying my staff slung across my shoulder, heedless of others, I go straight into a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks.'"
[The monk] asked, "I do not know where his dwelling place is. The Master said, "A soaring serpent winds around his feet; a spreading vine encircles his body.
[The monk] said, "In the morning one gazes upon drifting clouds; in the evening one listens to the murmuring stream. The Master said, "But you must cut it off completely before you can succeed.
[The monk] said, "This time it is no dream; I have truly arrived at Mount Lu. The Master said, "Keep your eyes wide open. [The monk] asked, "The monkey carries its young back to the green peaks."
Later, a bird dropped a flower before a green cliff. [The monk asked,] "This is where the Master formerly established his dwelling and sustenance.
What is the realm of Daolin? The Master said, "The temple gate stands high, opening onto the wilds of Dongting; the base of the hall plunges into the Chisha Lake.
[The monk asked,] "What is the person within the realm? The Master said, "The Jewel of the Sangha: every person is a pearl from the ocean. [The monk said,] "This is..."

[The student] said, "Take it away. The Master said, "Retain it. [The student] asked, "What is 'neither taking nor retaining' both person and environment? The Master said, "Release it. Question:

"Regarding the phrase 'the phrase with and the phrase without are like a vine leaning against a tree,' how can one attain liberation from this? The Master said, "A long sword leaning against the sky makes people feel cold.
[The student] asked, "As for the tree falling and the vine withering, why did Muzhou laugh so heartily? The Master said, "He loved him."
[The Master] was about to strike him when the student suddenly overturned the meditation seat and snapped the staff in two. [The student] asked, "What further trick could you possibly perform?
The Master said, "It is like drawing one's bow after the thief has already fled. A questioner asked, "When it is clear and bright, and manifest and vast, why can heaven and earth not contain it?
The Master said, "The eight-sided staff in the hands of Vajrapāṇi. [The student] said, "Suddenly..."
"If he were called back immediately, would he still be able to live? The Master said, "Even Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana could do nothing about it.

[The monk] asked, "If it does not fall within the realm of illumination, nor within the realm of function, how should one deliberate upon this? The Master said, "Drop the clouds from your head. [The monk] asked, "What if you suddenly encounter such a person?
The Master said, "Riding atop the Buddha Hall, he goes out through the mountain gate. [The monk] said, "While the myriad phenomena do not come, he speaks alone."
"Who would you teach to raise their hand toward the high peak? The Master said, "A mistaken use of names and phrases. He ascended the hall and said:

"The whole body is eyes, yet they do not reach what is seen. The whole body is ears, yet they do not penetrate what is heard. The whole body is mouth, yet it does not touch upon what is spoken. The whole body is mind, yet it does not discern what is reflected.
Even if one were to realize this throughout the entire world without the slightest leakage, one would still be only halfway there. According to [the truth]..."
"Let it be fully brought forth. Now tell me, how is it displayed? 'The sun and moon hang crosswise within the realm; throughout the vast void, ten thousand ages are spring.
[He] ascended the hall: 'Waves surge upon the mountain peak; dust rises from the bottom of the well. Hearing with the eyes is like the pealing of thunder;
seeing with the ears is like the unfolding of brocade. Within the three hundred and sixty joints and bones, each and every one manifests the boundless wondrous body. The eighty-four thousand..."
Four thousand hair-tips, each manifesting oceans of jewel-kings’ lands—this is neither the wondrous function of supernatural powers nor the mere nature of things as they are.
If one could suddenly open a thousand eyes, one would directly cut off the ten directions. Yet, regarding that single phrase of transcendent liberation, how would you speak of it?
"To test jade, it must pass through fire; to seek pearls, one does not leave the mud. [He] ascended the hall and said: "The original..."
