The pine wind clears the ears and eyes; it is truly superior to the human world. He called to the assembly, "This is the final word of my late teacher. A short while later, he passed away.
He then departed.

Chan Master Qing Su of Jiuding Peak in Jiazhou was the son of the Guo family of that prefecture. He received the tonsure and ordination at Qianming Temple and traveled extensively, knocking at the gates of various Chan masters.
Later, he visited Wuzu and, upon hearing Wuzu cite the words of Shoushan regarding the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, he attained sudden enlightenment.
He spoke a verse, saying: "Inverted, inverted, inverted! The new bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. To act so is utterly groundless;
Turning one's head, one does not realize one’s robe has been torn. When the Patriarch saw this, he asked, "As for Baizhang’s story of the wild fox, what do you say?
The Master replied, "Those who come to speak of right and wrong are themselves the people of right and wrong. The Patriarch was greatly pleased. After some time, the Master took his leave.

He returned and stayed at Qingxi. Later, he moved to Jiuding. When Governor Lü arrived to visit the Great Image, he asked, "Since this is the Great Image, why does it carry two pillars on its shoulders?

The Master replied, "There are no idle hands on a boat. When he went down to the pavilion and beheld the Avalokiteśvara image, he asked again, "In the realm of Maitreya’s transformation, why has Avalokiteśvara come here? The Master replied, "When a family is wealthy, the children are spoiled."

Shou then paid his respects. When Qin Laosu arrived, the Master asked, "When the sword is at the throat during a dance, what then? Qin replied, "I humbly pray that you will graciously accept [this offering].
The Master scolded him, saying, "Old thief! Go die! You ask me! Qin then repeated his previous words and questioned him again. The Master folded his hands, bowed, and said, "Drag it apart.
On the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month in the year of Yimao (1135) of the Xiangxing era, he contracted a slight illness. He wrote this verse:
He addressed his followers, saying: "The wooden man prepares the boat; the iron man prepares the horse. The child of the Bing and Ding stems mounts steadily;
with a shout, he scatters the white clouds and returns. Thereupon, he finally passed into stillness.
The head seat Yuanli was a native of Min. He had studied under Jiaoshan and first visited Master Yan at Baiyun.
Whenever he entered the room for instruction, Yan would invariably say to him, "Monks, you must clearly distinguish between the black and the white. The Master harbored this doubt without ceasing.
One day, as Yan ascended the hall, he cited the saying of Shoushan: "The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. He then said, "If you all wish to understand..."
"Do not ask about the new bride; let the mother-in-law be spared the trouble. On the road, when encountering rice, eat rice; when encountering tea, drink tea.
Those who enter and exit the same gate are enemies from past lives. At these words, the Master was suddenly enlightened and said, "Today, the distinction between the monastic and the lay is clear.

Two years later, when Fayan moved his seat to the ancestral mountain (Mount Guishan), he invited [the Master] to share the teaching seat, but [the Master] did not accept. When Fayan passed away, [the Master] immediately...
In the Chongning era, he went back to Wuzu. A monk asked, "Where has Wuzu gone since his passing?
The Master said, "He has eyes but no ears; he sits by the fire in the sixth month. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Poverty at home is still bearable;
poverty on the road is what kills one with grief. Or, when asked, "The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* says, 'All wholesome dharmas'—how [should one regard them]?"
"This is the Dharma," the Master said. "Above is heaven; below is earth. As for that which sits in the middle—if it is sitting, let it sit;
if it is standing, let it stand. What do you call 'wholesome Dharma'? The monk had no reply. The Master struck him. Later, he passed away at Ruiyan in Siming.

Puyong Zhizang was a native of Fuzhou. Upon arriving at the Fifth Patriarch’s hall to enter the inner room for instruction, the Patriarch raised the story of the "Two Women and the Divided Soul" to question him.
Zhizang attained a realization and presented this verse: "The two women merge into one daughter-in-law; The turning wheel is severed, impossible to reverse.
From the beginning, all coming and going is traceless; Let the traveler not ask the way back. Whenever there were monks from his home province...
He came to pay his respects and, speaking with a Min dialect, recited in colloquial verse: "At the beginning of the letter, I instruct my mother-in-law to be diligent in her rest;
at the end of the letter, I instruct my mother-in-law not to doze off. Now tell me, what was said in the middle? As the monk prepared to respond, the Master immediately pushed him out.
The Elder Fashu had long relied upon the Fifth Patriarch, yet he had not yet attained realization. One day, he entered the patriarch’s quarters.
The Patriarch asked, "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as his companion? Fashu replied, "Fashu is not like that. The Patriarch pointed his finger and said:
"Stop, stop! The Dharma-multitude is not so; how is it? At these words, the Master was awakened.
Later, he went to the seat of Chan Master Xianming Du at Donglin, where he saw that Du had attained the essence of the "plain and real.

One day, [the Master] held up a flower, walked once around Chan Master Du’s meditation seat, and with his back turned, thrust it into the incense burner, saying, "Master, tell me: what is the meaning of this? Du [replied repeatedly].
His responses were entirely discordant. After two months had passed, he finally questioned the Master, who told him to try explaining it.
The Master said, "I simply took some flowers and inserted them into the incense burner; you yourself are suspicious—what business is there for me to come here?"
A monk asked Zen Master Zixian of Chengtian Monastery at Mount Heng in Tanzhou, successor to Zen Master Yungeben: "The assembly has already gathered to listen to the thunderous voice;
now that you have ascended the lion throne, we pray that you will reveal the truth. The Master said, "Performing somersaults atop the top of the pagoda pole. The monk said, "In that case..."
"Then auspicious mists will rise before Mount Yue-lu, and auspicious clouds will form beneath Mount Zhurong. The Master said, "Bright pearls within a purple silk curtain.
He ascended the hall, took up his staff, and said: "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing."
He struck the meditation seat once and said, "I have shattered the cave of your spiritual essence for you; though dust is scattered and clouds are raised, there is nowhere to seek it.
Ten thousand mountains stand empty and towering. He struck once more and said, "Return to the hall. Go and practice. Ascending the hall, he said: "A solitary figure deeply hidden, only Nan-yueh;
laughing at myself, even this lone cloud is not yet at ease. He who sits upright beneath the pines and by the water—him too [I see]."
"One should explain it according to precedent as dwelling in the mountains. *Tut!* He ascended the hall. "The waning moon falls at the end of the fifth watch; at daybreak, white clouds fly.
This is a matter clearly before one’s eyes, yet it is not the mechanism of the present moment. Since it is a matter before one’s eyes, why is it not the mechanism of the present moment?
After a long silence, he said: "To wish to speak, words fail; beneath the trees, they deliberate."

"If it were not for Liu Yi transmitting this letter, by what means could I have reached Lake Dongting? Suddenly she attained great enlightenment; she threw the tray of rice cakes to the ground.
Her husband looked on askance and said, "You have gone mad. His wife slapped him and said, "This is not within your realm of understanding. Go and see Langya.
They looked up at him with longing expectation. Knowing his level of realization, they asked, "Who is the Unranked True Person?
Ba responded immediately, saying, "There is an unranked person with six arms and three heads; he exerts himself in anger. With one strike, he split Mount Hua into two paths;
the waters of Wan-nian flow on, unaware of spring. From this, his reputation spread far and wide. Whenever a monk arrived, he would say, "Boy! Boy! The monks [would respond].
As he was about to deliberate on this, the woman immediately closed the door. Chan Master Fodeng Xun went to investigate her. When the woman saw him, she asked the same questions as before.
Xun said, "Where is your father? The woman turned around and bowed toward a pillar. Xun immediately kicked it over and said, "I thought there was something truly extraordinary here.
He then departed. The woman scrambled up and said, "Child, child, come back! I pity you! Xun, however, did not return.
When the head seat An arrived, the old woman asked, "Where have you come from? An replied, "From De Shan. The woman said, "De Shan Tai is a son of an old woman.
An asked, "And whose son are you, old woman? The woman said, "Having been questioned by you, Senior, I am driven to stand right here and urinate.
The woman once composed a verse on the occasion of Mazu’s illness, which begins: "The face of the sun, the face of the moon; empty..."
A flash of lightning in the void. Although it cuts off the tongues of all the patch-robed monks under heaven, it clearly expresses only half the truth.
[This is from the lineage] of Chan Master Zhaojue Qin, the fifteenth generation descendant of Nanyue.
Chan Master Dahui Pu-jiao Zonggao of Mount Jing in Lin’an was the son of the Xi family of Xuancheng. From his youth, he possessed a brilliant spirit.
At the age of twelve, he entered the local school. One day, while playing with his classmates, he threw a inkstone at one of them by mistake and struck the teacher’s hat.
He returned home after paying the gold for the damage and said, "For a man of great character, why study worldly books rather than investigate that which transcends them?"
Regarding worldly affairs, he went directly to Huíyún Yùán on Mount Dōng to serve Huìqí. At the age of seventeen, he shaved his head and received full ordination in the *vinaya*.
While casually reading the records of the ancient Yúnmén, he felt as if he were encountering something familiar from his past training. He then went to rely upon Chán Master Chéng of Guǎngjiào;

subsequently, he traveled through the four directions, following various elder masters of the Cáo-dòng lineage. Having mastered their teachings, he departed for Bǎofēng Mountain to pay his respects to Chán Master Zhàntáng Zhǔn.

When Master [Wuzu] first saw him, he found him extraordinary and had him attend to his handkerchief and robe, pointing him toward the swift path for entering the Way. The Master’s responses were bold and unyielding;
thus, Wuzu rebuked him, saying: "You have not yet attained awakening; your illness lies in the functioning of consciousness. To merely understand this would become an obstacle of knowledge."

When Master Tang was on his deathbed, he instructed the Master, saying, "After I am gone, you should go see Chuan Qin; he will surely be able to fully employ your spiritual faculties. (Qin was Yuanwu.

After Master Tang passed away, the Master hurried to visit the Layman Wujin to request an inscription for Tang’s stupa. Wujin maintained a high standard in his teaching and was rarely one to grant approval;
however, upon a single word of mutual accord with the Master, he offered him lodging and invited him to stay. He named the Master’s hermitage Miaoxi. Subsequently...
He visited him again and instructed him to go see Yuanwu. When the Master arrived at Tianning, one day he heard Yuanwu ascend the hall and cite a monk’s question to Yunmen:
“What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? Yunmen replied, “On the water above the Eastern Mountain. “If it were Tianning,” [Yuanwu] said, “it would not be so.
If someone were to suddenly ask me, ‘What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? I would simply tell them:”
The Way: "A fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool. Upon these words, the Master suddenly severed the continuity between past and future.
Nevertheless, though the appearance of movement did not arise, he remained seated in a state of pure nakedness. Wuzu said to him, "This was no easy matter."
"You have obtained this field; it is a pity you have died and cannot live again. To have no doubt regarding words and phrases is a great illness. Have you not heard it said:
'Letting go at the edge of a precipice, one spontaneously accepts the responsibility; after death, one revives once more—this cannot be deceived.
You must believe that such a principle exists. Consequently, he had him reside in the Jue-mu Hall (Hall for Selecting Trees) as the attendant-in-charge of non-affairs.

One day, Rujing entered the room of Wuzu Fayan (the "room" being where the court officials rested after choosing their trees). Wuzu habitually raised the question, "There is a phrase with no phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree," to inquire of his students.

As soon as Rujing opened his mouth, Wuzu would say, "Not so, not so. After half a year had passed, Rujing finally asked Wuzu, "I have heard that when you were at Wuzu [your former teacher], you once asked this same question. I do not know what Wuzu said in response."
Mò laughed and did not answer. The Master said, "The Master ought to have asked this before the assembly at that time;
what harm is there in saying it now? Nanyue, having no choice, said, "I asked: 'What is the meaning of the phrase, "having a phrase and yet no phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree"?
The Patriarch replied, "'It cannot be traced out, nor can it be painted. He asked again, "When the tree falls and the vine withers..."
"How is it now? the Patriarch asked. Nanquan replied, "I have come along with you. At these words, the Master was immediately relieved and said, "I understand.
Baizhang then cited several *nidānas* (causal anecdotes) to interrogate him, and the Master responded without any impediment.

Baizhang said, "Now I know that I did not deceive you," and he subsequently composed the *Record of the True Lineage of Linji* and entrusted it to him, appointing him as the head of the secretarial office (*jishi*). Not long after, he ordered him to share the seat [in the meditation hall]. In the room, he held...
He used his bamboo staff to test his students; thus, the monastic communities universally accorded him great respect, and his fame resounded throughout the capital.
Prime Minister Lü Shuntú submitted a petition to grant him the purple robe and the title "Buddha-Sun" (Fórì). During the Jurchen upheaval, the chieftain intended to take several dozen Chan monks;
the Master was among those selected, but he managed to escape and traveled to Wú. There, he spent the summer retreat at Hùqiū and subsequently studied the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.

When the Bodhisattva ascends to the seventh stage and realizes the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), he thoroughly understands the previously inquired-about causes and conditions concerning Caṅkramana (Yaṅjue Moluo) carrying his alms bowl to the home of a woman in childbirth. At that time, Yuanwu was summoned to reside at Yunju; the Master went there to pay his respects.

On the second day of his arrival at the mountain, Yuanwu immediately appointed him as the First Seat (*prathama-āsana*). At that time, the assembly was filled with many "dragons and elephants" [of great spiritual caliber].
Yuanwu had long held the position of Seat-Holder (Zuoyuan) and had been waiting for the Master’s arrival, harboring a sense of resentment.

When it came time for the Master to hold the whisk on the winter solstice, Chan Master Zhaojue Yuan stepped forward from the assembly and asked, "What is it like when a sword is suspended between the eyebrows?
The Master replied, "Blood splatters against the Brahma Heaven. Yuanwu, from his seat below, gestured with his hand, saying, "Stop, stop! That was a most excellent question, but the answer—"
Even more extraordinary was that Yuan returned to the assembly, and from this point on, the monastic community underwent a transformation.
When Yuanwu returned to Sichuan, the Master established a hermitage at the ancient site of Yunmen behind Mount Yunju to reside there. Students gathered like clouds;
after some time, he entered Min Province and built a thatched hut at Changle. Yangyu followed him, and thirteen people attained the Dharma. He later moved to Yunchu at Xiaoxi.
[The Master] was at Men’an. Later, he accepted the invitation from Chancellor Zhang Wei-gong Xu to Mount Jing-shan. On the day he ascended the hall, a monk asked:
"The assembly of humans and devas has gathered; the field for selecting Buddhas is opened. The Patriarchal Command is being enacted—how should one proclaim it?

The Master said: "A dull bird flies against the wind. The monk said: "Throughout the entire realm there is nowhere to seek; clearly, a single point is perfect within the seat. The Master said: "People..."
There is no water that does not flow eastward. Furthermore, as monks vied with one another to emerge, the Master restrained them, saying: "Suppose the entire great earth were ground into dust;
suppose each grain of dust possessed a mouth, and each mouth were endowed with the mark of a broad and long tongue free from obstruction;
suppose each such tongue produced immeasurable varieties of sound, and each sound gave rise to immeasurable varieties of speech."

"Words. Each and every word possesses immeasurable varieties of wondrous meaning. Suppose as many monks as there are motes of dust each possessed such a mouth, such a tongue, such a voice, such words, and such wondrous meanings;
and suppose they were to simultaneously pose hundreds of thousands of difficult questions, each question distinct from the others—none would be resolved by the Elder’s single cough. All at once...
The answer is finished. Taking advantage of this opportunity, within that interval, he performs immeasurable, boundless, and vast Buddha-works.
Each and every Buddha-work pervades the entire Dharma-realm; that is to say, a single hair manifests spiritual transformations, and all Buddhas simultaneously preach the sutras.
Even throughout immeasurable kalpas, one cannot reach their limit. If you proceed in this manner, you will immediately attain the right eye upon entering the bustling gate and courtyard.
"Come! This is precisely the state where karmic consciousness is vast and empty, with no fundamental basis to rely upon. Under the gate of the Patriarchs, not even a single point is of use;
how much less so these pedantic phrases and sharp verbal jousts? Not only do they bury the ancestral vehicle of the past, but they also bring laughter to the nostrils of the patch-robed monks.
Therefore it is said: 'A thought tied to a hair’s breadth is the cause for rebirth in the three miserable realms. In a mere flash—"
Sentiments arise; ten thousand kalpas of bondage ensue. Holy names and mundane titles are all but empty sounds;
extraordinary features and inferior forms are all illusory colors. If you seek them, will you not be burdened? When you grow weary of them, they again become a great affliction.
Observe how the former sages issued such warnings: they were like the weapons of a state, used only when there was no other choice. This is the fundamental matter.
Above all, there is not even this kind of news. That I, a mountain monk, today proclaim it in such a manner is much like speaking a dream while dreaming, or gouging a sore upon healthy flesh.
When scrutinized, I deserve to be struck with a staff. Is there anyone present now who can bring down that lethal blow?
If there were, one would be worthy of repaying the unrequited debt of gratitude and assisting in the transformation of non-action. If there is none, then [it is as it is].
"By practicing this, one causes [delusion] to depart. He suddenly picked up his staff and said, "Transversely grasping the Mohe sword, he maintains the full authority of the True Command;
throughout the realm of Great Peace, he slays the dull-witted and obstinate. He planted the staff on the ground, gave a shout, and then descended from the seat.

The flourishing of the Dharma reached its peak at that time, with more than two thousand followers, all of whom were eminent talents from various regions. Zhang Gong Jiucheng, the Minister of the Board of Civil Office, also studied under him.
He attained a clear and sudden realization. One day, due to discussions regarding state affairs, he incurred trouble along with the Master.
In the fifth month of the *xīnyǒu* year of the Shaoxing era, he surrendered his monastic certificate and retired to live in seclusion at Hengyang.

There, he compiled the recorded sayings of former virtuous masters, interspersing them with his own comments and insights, arranging them into three volumes titled *Zhèngfǎyǎnzàng*. Ten years passed, during which he moved his residence to Mei-yang; another five years elapsed under Emperor Gāozōng.

The Emperor granted him special favor and released him from his vows. In the spring of the following year, he donned the *saṃghāṭī* once more. Monastic seats were vacant in all directions, and invitations were extended to him, yet he did not accept them.

Later, he received an imperial decree to reside at Yuwang Monastery; after more than a year, an edict was issued for him to move to Mount Jing. Monastics and laypeople admired him as they had at the beginning.
When Emperor Xiaozong was still the Prince of Puan, he dispatched an inner palace supervisor to enter the mountains to pay his respects to the Master.

The Master composed a verse as an offering. While residing at the Imperial Residence, he was again dispatched by the Inner Chamber’s Guest Officer to the mountain to provide offerings for the five hundred arhats and to request the Master to preach the Dharma in order to pray for the Emperor’s long life.
The Emperor personally inscribed the three characters "Miaoxi An" (Wondrous Joy Hermitage) and composed a eulogy, graciously entrusting them to him.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If you wish to understand the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should observe the conditions of time and season. When the time and season arrive, its [nature]..."
The principle is self-evident. He raises his whisk and asks, "Do you see it? He strikes the meditation seat and asks, "Do you hear it?
Hearing and seeing are distinct and clear; what is this? If you can grasp it here, the imperial grace and the Buddha’s grace will both be fully repaid at once.
If not, then Jingshan shall spin out some more entanglements. Again, he raises the whisk and says, "Look, look!"

The World-Honored One Amitāyus, atop the whisk of Mount Jing, radiates a great light that illuminates worlds as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable, yet again unspeakable, Buddha-fields.
Therein he turns the Great Dharma Wheel and performs immeasurable, boundless, and vast Buddha-works. Among them, whether mundane or sagely, orthodox or heterodox, or even mere blades of grass—
Whether sentient or insentient, all who encounter this light shall attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

It is for this reason that the Buddhas attain it here and become endowed with the knowledge of all modes; it is for this reason that the great Bodhisattvas attain it here and accomplish the various pāramitās;
and it is for this reason that the Pratyekabuddhas and Solitary Realizers attain it here, appearing in worlds devoid of Buddhas to manifest supernatural powers.

Radiant light! Here the assembly of śrāvakas obtained it; even those who came by night to offer invitations—the five hundred arhats—attained it here, achieving the eight liberations and possessing the six supernormal powers. Here the devas and humans attained it, increasing the ten wholesome actions.

[He] assented. Upon being struck by Wuzhuo, the Master suddenly cast off all that had been obstructing him. He attended Wuzhuo while residing at Tianning Temple, where he was appointed to oversee the secretariat.

Soon thereafter, he shared the teaching seat; his reputation for the Way resounded widely. The Regional Inspector of the West of the Capital invited him to open a Dharma hall at Danxia. Subsequently, he moved to Huqiu and then to Jingshan.

Upon retiring from these duties, he acceded to the request of the clergy and laity of Pingjiang and built a hermitage at Xihua. After several years there, he was by imperial decree appointed to reside at Bao’en Temple in Jiankang.
He subsequently moved to Wanshou in Suzhou, then to Xuansha in Min, and to Xishan Chan. He was again appointed to Lingyin by imperial decree.
When Empress Dowager Cining visited the residence of Prince Wei, she summoned the Master to expound the Dharma and bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered *kāṣāya*.
He requested to return to his former hermitage at Xihu. In the autumn of the Wuchen year of the Shaoxing era, he accepted the summons to Yewang Monastery and ascended the hall, saying:

"Deshan’s 'stick upon entering the gate' mostly conceals one's tracks within the skin-bag; Linji’s 'shout upon entering the gate' is entirely a matter of appearing and disappearing within the realm of sound.
If you are a truly heroic monk, you must have the wind blowing beneath your feet, transcending the ancients."
Now, regarding this path: [The Master] picks up his staff, strikes once, and gives a shout, saying: "What is this?
If you call it a staff or a shout, you are still drowsing and have not yet awakened. If you do not call it a staff or a shout, you do not yet know Deshan or Linji.
After all, how is it? He strikes once again and says: "Do not touch it at all. [On another occasion,] he ascended the hall and said: "The entire great earth is sand."
The gates and eyes are one's own light pervading the ten directions. Why is it that when the drum is beaten in Pūrvavideha in the east, it is not heard in Aparagoyānī in the west?
When a lamp is lit in Jambudvīpa in the south, those in Uttarakuru in the north sit in darkness?
Even if you could speak perfectly within this realm, it would still be a livelihood within the shadows of light and reflection. [Zhaozhou] struck his whisk and said: "It is all smashed to pieces!"

Furthermore, what is the single path for manifesting one's true self? [He] threw down his whisk and said, "Investigate! Ascending the hall, he said: "If there is movement, a shadow appears; if there is awakening, ice forms.
Even if you remain unmoving and unawakened, you are still like a carriage wheel from the Qin dynasty grinding on a grindstone.

Reaching this point, you must discern a thousand differences and illuminate secretly so that ten thousand doors open simultaneously. At the tip of a single hair, you must pivot the mechanism of the wheel; the life-vein must not..."
Sinking into the sea of poison: sometimes one awakens like still, clear water; sometimes movement is like stars flying; sometimes both movement and awareness are forgotten;
sometimes illumination and function are sovereign. Tell me, at such a time as this, is it movement or awareness?
Is it illumination or function? Is there anyone who can distinguish them? An iron ox bars the ancient road; when touched, the hair on one’s skin stands cold. *Upa* (above).
The Hall Master said: "When acting, there is no trace of action; when speaking, there is no mark of speech. If action and speech reach their destination, one sets up a butt that invites the arrow;
if action and speech are not yet clear, the divine blade cuts them asunder. Even if one’s speech is without leakage and one’s action does not lose its direction,"

It is still stuck in the shell and remains as a leak. If one were a great Garuḍa, soaring through hundreds of thousands of *yojanas*, or a divine horse with ten shadows, galloping across the four quarters and the eight extremities—neither pecking at things one by one nor burying its body wherever it lands, but rather not relying on anything at all—would there still be any portion for such a one to tread upon?
Every moment and every speck of dust is the essential ford. He ascended the hall and said: "Easy."
To fill a vast chasm is difficult; to fill a leaking cup is even harder. Yet, if one possesses the capacity for sustained practice, there is neither difficulty nor ease.

If one sets aside the entire earth, there is ample room to spare; if one lets out even a single hair’s breadth, there is no way to pass through. Suddenly, if one neither sets it aside nor lets it out, where does one tread?
Sharing the same sincerity and common joys and sorrows, even drinking water must nourish you. A monk asked: "What is the guest within the host?"
The guest asked, "Master, you are a slave from the fields. The Master said, "What is the host within the guest? He replied, "Meeting yet still coarse and rough.
The Master said, "What is the guest within the host? He replied, "The radiance of the sword slashes through the clouds of sorrow.

The Master said, "What is the host within the host? He replied, "Beating the bones and breaking the marrow. Whenever the Master presided over the assembly, his countenance was invariably stern; he never turned away from his proper conduct regarding sleep or food.
The assembly sang the Way without weariness. In the tenth month of the Gengwu year of the Xiangshu era, he manifested a slight illness.

On the eighteenth day, the head seat Faquan requested his final instructions. The Master said, "Exhaust this mind and will, and support one another with the Way. Having spoken these words, he passed away.
After the fire, his eyeballs, teeth, and tongue remained undamaged. That spot on the ground emitted light throughout the night.
Those who obtained *śarīra* (relics) were beyond counting; they continued for over a month without ceasing. Huang Guan Luo Zhao had regularly sought the Way from the Master.

Once, returning from outside, he alone had obtained nothing. His aspiration for the Way was earnest and intense; just as he was eating with a guest, while chewing, there was something in his mouth. Upon spitting it out, it was a relic.
It was beneficial. It was as large as a bean and its color was like amber. Those who cherished such things took it away. He then prostrated twice at the site of the cremation.
Hearing a sound from the incense casket, he opened it immediately; what he obtained was as before, yet somewhat reddish and lustrous.
His disciples enshrined the remains and divided them to be interred in stupas at Mount Mao and Xihu. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Dawu.

Chan Master Fóxìng Fǎtài of Dàméi in Tánzhōu was a native of the Lí family in Hànzhōu. A monk asked, "When principle follows the transformations of phenomena, it encompasses all existence yet remains a single, void stillness;
when phenomena follow the fusion of principle, they equalize all differences and return entirely to the ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
What is the realm of principle (*dharmadhātu*)? The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. The monk asked, "What is the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*)?"

The Master said, "The myriad phenomena are densely arrayed. [A monk] asked, "What is the dharma-realm of the non-obstruction between principle and phenomena? The Master said, "East, west, south, and north.

[Another monk] asked, "What is the dharma-realm of the non-obstruction between phenomena and phenomena? The Master said, "Above, below, and the four intermediate directions. He then ascended the hall for instruction.
Pushing to the limit of truth, truth has no marks; exhausting delusion, delusion has no form. When both truth and delusion are non-existent, the eye is revealed in vast emptiness.
Once the eye is revealed, what do you see? The morning sun melts the snow upon the crags;
the northern wind blows open the wax-plum blossoms. [Ascending the hall: When the precious sword is drawn, it is used immediately—how could there be any hesitation? [He points to his eyebrows.]

Lifting up the whisk, he immediately departs; there is no further turning back or evasion. In every place, he soars through the present and illuminates the past; in every place, he cuts off all nets and cages.
He does not strike against the sharp edge, nor does he look into the mirror. Let us set aside for a moment his solitary transcendence beyond all things.

But when the ten thousand functions have been utterly exhausted—how is it then? "In the autumn of the eighth month, where is it hot? He ascended the hall and said: "Nirvana has no other path; expedient means..."
[The Master] uses many approaches. Holding up his staff, he said: "Look, look! This monk’s staff swallows the waters of the West River in a single gulp.
The carp of the Eastern Sea leaps and bounds up to the Thirty-three Heavens. Indra, filled with wrath, seizes Mount Sumeru."
A single blow shatters it to pieces. The Earth-Goddess Sthāvarā joined her palms and praised him, saying: "I observe the Dharma of the Dharma-King; such is the Dharma of the Dharma-King.

Striking the meditation seat with his staff, he descended from the seat. Entering the hall, he said: "To realize the emptiness of persons and the emptiness of phenomena does not yet accord with the ancestral style of the Buddhas.
To embody total function and total illumination is likewise not the essential subtlety of a monk. You must simply strike!"
Breaking through the sturdy barrier, one recognizes the single aperture above. What is this single aperture above? "The spring cold is piercing;
it freezes the young to death. Ascending the hall, he said: "Today is the halfway point of the first month. Everywhere the lanterns flicker and swirl;

throughout the city, silks and brocades are gathered in throngs. People come and go, mingling as they enjoy the festivities. Mañjuśrī has entered the midst of the bustling crowd, while Samantabhadra..."
Sitting atop a high tower, look out. Tell me, where is Avalokiteśvara? Thundering drums are beaten, shaking the heavens;
flutes and songs resound, deafening the earth. Entering the hall [he said]: Vast and remote, encompassing the ten directions; level and expansive, beyond form and beyond appearance.
The eyes wish to see, yet the pupils wither; the mouth wishes to speak, yet words fail. Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra possess no skillful means whatsoever;
Linji and Deshan, however, do not hesitate to proclaim the Dharma. A tortoise swallows the iron ox of Shanfu; a snake bites the Great Image of Jiazhou.

So terrified were the carp of the Eastern Sea that they remain bloated to this very day. [The Master] laughs and ascends the hall. "Blazing fire-clouds scorch the field crops; the springs have ceased their flow.
Where is the Great Dragon King Sāgara? He does not know where he is! Striking the meditation seat with his staff, he says: "Look here!
Clouds rise from the Southern Mountain, and rain falls upon the Northern Mountain. Let the Old Monk further shake it for you!"
The sound of thunder helps to manifest majestic brilliance so that it may spread afar. Then, in a loud voice, he said: "Chanting! Chanting! Ascending the hall, he said:
"Opening one's mouth is sometimes wrong; opening one's mouth is sometimes right. Whether coarse words or subtle speech, they all return to the primary meaning.
Old Śākyamuni’s bowl rings out; Bodhidharma’s coming from the West is the stench of excrement. Only the water buffalo before the mountain..."

Light from the hair-tuft on his body radiates, illuminating heaven and earth. Entering the hall, he said: "Whether mindfulness is attained or lost, there is nothing that is not liberation. What kind of talk is this?
Whether phenomena are established or destroyed, they are all called Nirvana—this is a matter of no connection. Whether wisdom or folly, both are collectively Prajna.
Even the crude and indistinct Buddha-nature and the dharmas accomplished by non-Buddhists are all Bodhi. As for this...
It is but a trifle. Nevertheless, even so, it is like Emperor Yang of the Sui losing his camel. Entering the hall, [the Master] said:
"If you wish to know where the Buddha has gone, it is simply this very sound of speech. *Cluck!* "Master Fu did not recognize good from evil;

by teaching people to seek that which is 'bright and numinous,' he corrupted the men and women of the world. He was rebuked by Master Zhigong, who said: "Great Master, do not speak thus! [Zhigong] departed.
"Recite it again. The Great Being (Mahāsattva) spoke another verse: "Holding a hoe in empty hands, Walking while riding a water buffalo.
A person passes over the bridge; The bridge flows, but the water does not flow. Master Zhigong laughed heartily and said:

"The first part was still somewhat bearable, but the last part is even more distressing to people. He ascended the hall and said: "I recall in days past when I traveled abroad, I obtained two things. The first is..."
The Vajra Hammer. It is the single bone of the thousand sages; I have carried it through the universe, its majestic presence towering and abrupt.
Thus for thirty years, I used it as my standard. Now that I am old, what do I know of this one thing?
I cast down the Vajra Hammer, shatter the bone of the thousand sages, and hurl it onto the crossroads; I can no longer cherish it, so let it go as it will.
Passing through this floating life, I point south when intending to go north; I call a tortoise a soft-shelled turtle and name beans millet.
May those of clear-sighted wisdom laugh at me for lacking the guiding line and square.
Chan Master Cihu Guo Cigan Jingyuan of Taizhou was the son of the Zhang family of Nanxi in Yongjia.
At the age of eighteen, he received full ordination under Xigong at Lingshan. He subsequently studied the Tiantai teachings for three years, after which he left them to visit Yuanwu at Zhongfu.
The Master read from the recorded sayings of Sīxīn’s *Small Public Sermons*, saying: "Since one is deluded, one must attain awakening.

Since one has awakened, one must recognize delusion within awakening and awakening within delusion. When both delusion and awakening are forgotten, one establishes all dharmas from the place where there is neither delusion nor awakening."

Upon hearing this, the Master was filled with doubt. He immediately hurried to the Buddha Hall and pushed open the door panels with his hands; at that moment, he attained a sudden and great enlightenment.
Thereafter, as an attendant, his intellectual eloquence and wit burst forth brilliantly. Yuanwu called him "The Stubborn Attendant Yuan," and subsequently inscribed his own portrait with these words.

He entrusted him with these words: "Throughout my life, I have spoken nothing but 'head-gossip' (sheng-tou chan). When I encountered those who were stubborn as iron walls, I stripped them of their cages and cut off their heels.
I gathered up the entire earth and it was pitch black. In my later years, I became even more 'knife-less' (mei-dao-dao);
wielding the Vajra mallet, I shattered all nests and lairs. If you wish to recognize the face of Yuanwu at some other time, I shall set it forth for you all at once. Yuan.
Wu returned to Shu, while the Master returned to Zhedong. He concealed his brilliance and buried his reputation, seeking neither fame nor advancement.

When Governor Geng Yongxi of Kuacang—who had once sought instruction from Yuanwu—read the Master’s recorded sayings, he gained insight into his character upon reaching the inscription for his portrait.

Consequently, he invited the Master to propagate the Dharma at Nanyue Mountain (Nanming Shan) and dispatched an envoy to search for him. Upon arriving at Ba’en Temple in Tai, the envoy found the Master among the assembly.
The abbot’s quarters were cramped, so he was pressed to accept the position. The former head monk, Gugu, was a high-ranking disciple of Lingyuan;
upon hearing his proclamations, he too was deeply struck by their extraordinary nature. A monk asked: "Sansheng said, 'Whenever I meet a person, I come forth;

having come forth, I do not act for others. What is the meaning of this? The Master replied, "An eighty-year-old old man chewing raw iron. [The monk] asked, "Xinghua said, 'Whenever I meet a person, I do not come forth.'"
[The monk] asked: "As soon as it comes out, it becomes a person. Furthermore, how is this so? The Master said: "Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, waves overturn the void;
heaven cannot cover them, and earth cannot support them. What thing is this? The Master said: "A seamless iron hammer. [The monk] said:

"All classes of beings, including devas and humans, all receive the power of this grace. The Master said: "Do not engage in false conceptualization. [The monk] asked: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time speak..."
“This is a phrase that does not reach the bottom; I beg the Master to speak quickly. The Master said, “Blinking one’s eyebrows. [The student] asked, “In years past, the site of Sanping was restored.
On this day, Yuanwu held high the ancestral seal, beginning its transmission from you. What is the Linji school?

The Master said, “Killing people or bringing them back to life without blinking an eye. [The student] asked, “Among those who currently grasp it by looking into the mirror, is there anyone who has truly understood?”
"Rare! What is the Yunmen school? The Master said, "The three eyes on the crown of the head shine throughout heaven and earth.
[The student] said, "To know before it is raised; to see before it is spoken. "What is the Miaoyang school? The Master said, "Pushed forward, he does not go ahead;
restrained from behind, he does not retreat. "The triple world is mind-only; the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only. "What is the Fayen school? The Master said, "The point of the arrowhead."

Facing one another directly, they do not yield to each other. [A monk] asked: "In establishing transformation, how does it not obstruct walking the Bird Path? Returning to the original way, how does one further manifest the family style?
"How is the Cao-Dong school? The Master said: "Holding a night-bright talisman in hand, how many know the dawn of heaven?
"Is there still a path above this? The Master said: "There is. "What is the path above? The Master said: "A vast blackness."
Man-di. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "For the sake of another's single grain of millet, one loses half a year’s rations.
He ascended the hall and said, "Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvaranāda, this group of fellows was off by seven or eight.
After King Bhīṣmagarjitasvaranāda, this group of fellows was off by two or three. Now, this group of fellows sits and stands with solemn dignity. Tell me, are they off by seven?"
Eight errors, two falls, three falls. Will you still be able to attain liberation through stabilization? [The Master] raises his whisk and says: "Hūṃ, hūṃ.
On the occasion of the Buddha-bath ceremony, he ascends the hall and says: "This old Śākyamuni, as soon as he was born, made himself a laughingstock; with one finger he pointed to heaven..."
He pointed one finger at the ground and said, "Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored.
Later, Master Yunmen said, "Had I seen him then, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to a dog, so as to bring peace to the world."
Yet there are still those who refuse to let it go, saying instead, "To praise the Patriarch, one must be Yunmen. But tell me, where is it that he praises him?
Is it at the point where [Yunmen] strikes with a single blow? Be glad, for there is no connection there.
Today, as I, Nanming, have just assumed the abbacy here, I can only let it pass. If I did not let it pass, then all the people in the entire world would—
Only by begging for their lives can they be saved. Now, as the matter has come to this, let us join the assembly and go toward the Buddha Hall;
give each of them one ladleful. Why? Have you not heard it said: "It may be better to violate a rule than to overstep a precedent"?
With his whisk, he struck the meditation seat and descended. He ascended the hall and said: "The jackal howls; the lion roars. His eyes are wide open."
"Moving the Southern Star, staggering the Northern Dipper. Great assembly, do you know where it lands? A Vajra-knife crouches beneath the steps;
a divine tortoise runs through the fire. The Master retired to Mount Xishan. Gentle Longxue invited him to ascend the seat at Jingguang Temple.
Master Lingfeng Gu cited the kōan of Baiyun seeing Yangqi, in which Yangqi instructed him to recite the verse on the realization of the Way by Chaling. He requested—
The Master criticized them. He said, "O practitioners of Chan: Yangqi’s great laughter—his eyes look to the southeast, yet his intent lies in the northwest.
Baiyun’s realization was incomplete; he heard the matter incorrectly and called a bell a jar. When scrutinized, even the old fellow Yangqi is on the same shelf.
To take a mistake and turn it into a success—if it were Nanming, it would not be so. I have..."
"A single bright pearl—take care not to let it slip past you. Even so, though it is presented face-to-face, it must still be shattered with a single blow.

Raising his whisk, he said, "Do you understand? When a chess game meets a worthy opponent, one cannot hide one's clumsiness; when a poem reaches the point of being recited repeatedly, its merit finally becomes apparent.
The Master fell ill and requested Chan Master Ying’an Hua of Xitang to serve as the Seat-Holder (Zuoyuan) and to take charge of the monastery affairs.
As for his final affairs, he gave instructions as was his custom. Suddenly, he clenched his fist and passed away. Upon cremation, five-colored śarīras were obtained;
his teeth, tongue, and right fist remained entirely undamaged. He was enshrined in a stupa before Lian-Ruan Cave at Dongsi Temple. His age was fifty-three.
Chan Master Xiansha Shengzao of Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "In the heavens there is no Maitreya; on the earth there is no Maitreya.
Tell me, where is Maitreya? After a long silence, he said: "When walking at night, do not step on white;
it is either water or stone."
Chan Master Yunbian of Nanfeng in Pingjiang Prefecture was a native of that region. He received the full precepts under Master Zhang of Ruifeng in Min.

Upon returning home, he visited Master Yuan of Qionglong and suddenly attained realization. He subsequently shared his insights with Yuan, who said, "Although you have gained entry, you have not yet reached the proper state.
You must truly spur yourself forward. Thereupon, he took leave and visited various seats of practice. Later, he attended upon Yuanwu; while entering the inner quarters for instruction, as soon as...
He followed him to the door. Wuzhuo said, "Look beneath your feet. The Master struck a pillar once. Wuzhuo said, "Why do you not speak a single word to the point?
The Master said, "If the teacher shakes his head, the disciple wags his tail. Wuzhuo said, "Try wagging your tail for me."

The Master performed a somersault and exited. Wuzu laughed heartily; from this, he became renowned. Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'?
The Master said, "The Hegemon reaches the Wu River. The monk asked, "What is 'taking away the environment but not taking away the person'?
The Master said, "Building the altar to invest the generals. The monk asked, "What is 'taking away both person and environment'? The Master said, "Ten thousand *li*..."
"The mountains and rivers attain great peace. [The student] asked, "What is it like when neither the person nor the environment can be taken away?

The Master said, "When the dragon roars, the mist rises; when the tiger howls, the wind arises. [The student] asked, "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "You have missed it right before your face.

[The student] said, "Truly a master craftsman! The Master said, "A ghost deludes people in broad daylight. One day, he entered the city and was walking with monastics and laypeople when they reached the tenth...
Langxiang. Someone asked, "The lane is right here; where is Shilang? The Master raised his arm and said, "Follow me.
Lingyin Huaiyuan Fohai Chan Master of Lin’an Prefecture was the son of the Peng family of Meishan. At the age of thirteen, he took the precepts under Zongbian of Yaoshi Temple.
He went to Daci to study, but later left to rely upon Chan Master Hui of Lingyan. Wei... [text fragment ends]
He had a realization. When Yuanwu returned to lead Zhaojue, the Master went to him. Hearing Yuanwu’s general discourse (*pǔshuō*), he cited the karmic cause concerning Layman Pang’s question to Mazu:
“Not being a companion to the myriad dharmas. The Master suddenly attained sudden enlightenment and collapsed among the assembly.

The assembly helped him up, whereupon the Master said, “I have awakened from my dream. Later, during the evening *xiǎocān* (small formal address), the Master stepped forward and asked: “Naked and bare; empty...”
"I have not a single thing. I am but bare bones; poor as I am, I have not a single coin. My door is broken and my family is ruined. I beg the Master for relief.
Wu said, "The seven treasures and eight jewels are all seized at once. The Master said, "Calamity does not enter the door of a prudent house.

Wu said, "If the pivot does not leave its station, one falls into the sea of poison. As soon as these words were spoken, the Master let out a shout. Wu struck the meditation seat with his staff and said, "Eat!"
"Have you obtained the staff yet? The Master shouted again. Wuzhuo shouted twice in succession. The Master then bowed.
From that time on, his spiritual acumen became sharp and piercing, meeting no resistance. After Yuanwu passed away, the Master retired from office.

He moved through several famous monasteries, starting from Huqiu, then by imperial decree resided at Gaoting Chongxian, and was subsequently appointed to Lingyin by another edict. Emperor Xiaozong summoned him for an audience and bestowed upon him the title "Buddha."
Chan Master Hai ascended the hall and said: "The new year has its reasons: brewing tea and ascending the wine tower. A pair makes two feet; half a thing has three heads.
Suddenly appearing, it is difficult for spirits to discern; meeting it, even ghosts feel sorrow. He plays the holeless flute backward."
To the accompaniment of the *liángzhōu* dance, he cried out, "Duo! and ascended the hall. "How pleasant it is that mid-spring is gradually warming;

how much more so on the days of Cold Food and Qingming! Ten thousand layers of cloud-capped mountains tower with emerald green; the wind and moon fill the heavens as noble neighbors. Everywhere, flowers are red and willows are green;

the lake and sky are calm, with steady waves and gentle breezes. The mountain birds on the branches warble repeatedly—once, twice, thrice—with their trivial and fragmented chatter, offering earnest instructions."
"Listen closely, listen closely! You must say: what was it that he cautioned and entrusted [his disciples] with? He strikes the meditation staff and says, "Remember this:
next year on this very day, it will still be the Cold Food Festival and Qingming. He ascends the hall and cites a monk’s question to Muzhou:
"I do not ask about 'removing one layer after another'; but when one does not remove one layer after another, what then? Muzhou said, "Yesterday..."

"Planting eggplants; today I am planting winter melons. The Master said: "The questioner asks well but does not understand the answer; the respondent answers well but does not understand the question.
Today, this mountain monk plunders meat from the talons of a hungry hawk and thrusts his body across the mouth of a fierce tiger to show you all a model.
The robe of the altar-climbing Daoist is light; though his power of incantation may be exhausted..."
The Dharma turns anew. The thumb splits open the darkness of heaven and earth; the serpent’s head falls, and ghosts and spirits are startled.
A monk asked, "Throughout the twelve periods of the day, how should a student apply their mind? The Master said, "Dipping into the snow to eat a winter melon.

He asked, "In the midst of vast dust and turmoil, how does one distinguish the host? The Master said, "At the tip of a wooden ladle, a sickle cuts vegetables. [The monk] said, "Is this not the Harmony itself?"
"Furthermore, there is no place for a person. The Master said, "Grinding the pestle to stir the noodles. The student asked, "What is it like when 'this very mind is Buddha'?
The Master said, "A topknot with three points. The student asked, "What is it like when 'neither mind nor Buddha'? The Master said, "Earrings of gold rings.
The student asked, "When it is 'neither mind, nor Buddha, nor anything else,' how is that? The Master said, "A shaven-headed monk practicing meditation."
[The Master] was performing the *zhazhi* dance. [A monk] asked, "Regarding the meaning of the saying, 'On the mountain of Dongshan, one walks upon the water,' what is its intent?
The Master said, "The third day of the first month; there is no need to choose a specific day. [Another monk] asked, "Manjusri is the teacher of the seven Buddhas.

Why was he unable to emerge from the woman’s samādhi? The Master said, "No needle is hanging from his shoulder. [Yet another] asked, "In the past, there was a scholar who composed a 'Treatise on the Non-existence of Ghosts. Once the treatise was completed..."
There was a ghost who scolded him, saying, "What can you do about me? What do you think? The Master struck his forehead with his hand and said, "How does it compare?
The ghost asked, "As for Wuzu, who made the gesture of a magpie’s beak and said 'Gu-gua,' what of that?
The Master replied, "Go away and take care of yourself. He then asked a person inside the hermitage, "Why do you not know what happens outside the hermitage? The Master [replied].

[The Master] said: "With a staff slung across one's shoulder, one carries iron caltrops. When asked, 'Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as a companion? the Master replied: 'His feet tread upon the revolving wheel. One day, as the drum was beaten for the assembly to enter the hall, the Master sat hidden within the curtain. A serving monk went to search for him. The Master suddenly pulled back the curtain and said, "He is right here! Why do you not see him? The monk had no reply. The Master [continued]: "An ancient worthy once said: 'If you wish to know the Buddha, look at the ox; if you wish to know the ox, look at the traces. If you wish to know the Buddha, look at the ox—this is the ox itself. If you wish to know the ox, look at the traces—these are the traces of the ox. If you wish to know the ox, look at the ox itself; if you wish to know the ox itself, look at the traces.
