Whenever anyone questioned him, he would invariably reply, "Do not try to understand. Therefore, his contemporaries all called him "Mo-li-hui" (Do-not-understand). Later, while presiding over the assembly in the Dharma Hall, he said: "You..."
There is one pair of eyes; I too have one pair of eyes. If you deceive others, you deceive yourself.
If you become a Buddha or a Patriarch, I, this old monk, shall have no share in it. If you become a donkey or a horse, I, this old monk, will be unable to save you.
A multitude of donors entered the mountain to invite him to ascend the hall. He spoke a verse, saying: "I have no superior qualities; my reputation is but empty fame.
I thank you for coming here with such earnest devotion. Since I have no Dharma to entrust, I merely open the mountain gate for you."
Chan Master Xueting Yuanjing of Huqiu, Pingjiang Prefecture, was a native of Shuangxi. He ascended the hall and said:
"For one who knows there is [the Way], ten thousand years pass as if they were a single day; for one who does not know there is [the Way], a single day passes as if it were ten thousand years.
Have you not seen how Master Sishin said: 'I have been traveling on pilgrimage for over thirty years, yet I regard ninety days as a single [unit]'?"
In summer, one cannot increase it by a single day, nor can one decrease it by a single day. One cannot grasp it, nor can one let it go.
It is attained precisely within that which is unattainable. Yet, from the perspective of Cuiyun, this is not so.

For thirty years or more of traveling on pilgrimage, I, this mountain monk, have had no concern for a single day or ninety days; there is neither attainment nor non-attainment. At every place, I simply act as the occasion demands.
"Come to see Maitreya. But tell me, where is Maitreya? "The golden wind blows over the Wei River;
fallen leaves fill Chang'an. Ascending the hall, he said: "To speak, one must first see; to see, one must also be able to speak.

To see but not be able to speak is to fall into the realm of shadows, where one's understanding is biased and withered. To be able to speak but not see is to fall into the trap of timing and circumstance."
A Sea of Poison. If you are under the gate of Cuiyun, even if you can explain it or perceive it, I shall give you thirty blows;
if you cannot explain it or perceive it, I shall also give you thirty blows. For Cuiyun to speak thus, I shall also give him thirty blows.
Then, calling out loudly to the assembly, he said: "Dangerous! He then ascended the hall and said: "Day after day the sun rises in the east, day after day the sun..."
It sets in the west; at that time, people know it exists. From antiquity to the present, like hemp seeds or millet, suddenly the pivot of the discourse shifts:
it does not emerge from the east, nor does it set in the west. Tell me, from where does it emerge and where does it set?
If one is a person who has penetrated the barrier, upon hearing such words, they will certainly know that the five-li milestone stands outside the city gate. If one is a person who has penetrated...
Regarding "Not Passing Through," it is often said that Ban-shan was hotly deceiving people. A monk asked, "What is the phrase for arriving home?
The Master said, "Sitting and watching success and failure. He asked, "Who is the one who does not take the myriad dharmas as a companion? The Master said:
"Distant relatives are not as good as neighbors," he said. [The monk asked: "When you say, 'I wait for you to suck dry the waters of the West River,' then I will tell you—how about that?
The Master said, "Neighbors are not as good as distant relatives. [The monk] asked about a deceased monk who had passed away:
"Where has he gone? The Master said, "On top of a pile of dung. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Striking it, bumping into it."
Chan Master Nantang Fansi of Tiantong Monastery in Quzhou was the son of the Zhu family of Sutaishan.
He ascended the hall and said: "He kicks over the sea of birth and death; he tramples down the shore of nirvana. There are no living people in the world, and no dead men in the Yellow Springs.
He then took up his staff and said: "Today, Nantang’s staff has something to entrust. Is there anyone who can take it up?"
"Is there anyone? Come forth and take up this burden! Is there anyone? Is there anyone? After a long silence, he threw down his staff and descended from the seat.
He entered the hall and said: "Those who know it eat porridge and rice; those who do not know it also eat porridge and rice.
How can you directly verify whether they have it or not, whether it is right or wrong, whether it is deviant or correct? If you cannot verify this, [you have failed]."
The matter of studying the Way is vast and far-reaching. (He lets out a shout. He descends from his seat. Entering the hall, the mountain monk says:

This old fellow here is the fourth-generation descendant of Yangqi. Regarding the koan of "the three-legged donkey kicking up its heels as it walks," although everyone can cite it, [it remains difficult to master].
It is simply that you do not know where it lands. This mountain monk, without sparing his own eyebrows, shall provide a footnote for all of you:
"An octagonal millstone rolls in the void."
Chan Master Fozhao Jue of Mount Yu’s Junshan Monastery ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said: 'The higher one looks up at it, the higher it rises;
the harder one drills into it, the firmer it becomes. One gazes for it to be in front, and suddenly it is behind. Do you all recognize this? If you do not recognize it, I shall explain it for you:
'The higher one looks up at it, the higher it rises'—not separated by so much as a hair’s breadth. At the vital ford, the way is cut off; even Buddhas and Patriarchs find it difficult to pass."
He flees; the harder one drills, the more solid it becomes. The true body is spontaneous: the birds sing and the flowers smile before the green cliff.

Looking for it, it seems right there—neither orthodox nor biased. It cuts off the ten directions and its majesty subdues the great thousandfold world-system. Suddenly it is behind you—a total leakage!
How laughable that Yunmen hides his body in the Big Dipper! *Du!* (A shout of rebuke)
Chan Master Xian of Baohua in Pingjiang Prefecture was a native of that same region. He ascended the hall and said: "The rice gruel has been eaten; to place a head upon a head.
Go wash the alms bowl; to draw legs for a snake. Furthermore, how can you ask such a question? You are bringing about your own defeat.

After a long silence, he called out loudly to the assembly. When the assembly raised their heads, the Master said, "Return to the hall to drink tea. He then ascended the hall again and said: "Do not practice Chan."
Cease from studying the Way; let the mind rest and forget its artifice, for it is ever vast and open. The ready-made koan is already too much complication;

even this very "mindlessness" is already a fabrication. Even if you were to sit and cut off all existence before birth, it would still be difficult to penetrate—this old monk says: "Wrong! Wrong! Wrong!"
Chan Master Jue of Mount Dongshan in Shaoxing Prefecture later resided at Yingsheng. He ascended the hall, and after the three rounds of drums had ceased, he said:
"Everyone has come forward one by one, intending to investigate the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West. Do you know that the sword has long since been lost?"
Even if one were to attain awakening directly, it would still be like cutting off one's own head to seek life. Dongshan had no choice but to press the matter toward the "second head.

[He] struck the meditation seat with his hand and descended from the seat. "Vice-abbot! When the flowers are in full bloom and the scenery is warm and radiant, do not speak of there being another heaven within the flask.
If you can recognize it at the tips of the hundred grasses, then the East is three *zhang* high and the West—"

Width: eight inches. Entering the hall, he raised an ancient case: Once, the butcher Guang’e went to where the Buddha was, cast down his butcher’s knife, and said, “I am counted among the thousand Buddhas.

The World-Honored One said, “So it is, so it is. Nowadays in the monasteries, people assume that Guang’e was actually one Buddha in a past life who manifested as a butcher by means of expedient means. To see Guang’e in such a way is truly a cause for regret.
Shel said: "Guang'e was precisely a man who would not blink when killing people; yet he cast down his butcher's blade and became a Buddha on the spot.

For now, let us say there is no connection. He also said: 'Guang'e cast down his butcher's blade and said, "I am counted among the thousand Buddhas"—how distinct this one Buddha is! For now, let us say there is no connection. Do you wish to recognize Guang'e?"
Peach blossoms line the road after wind and rain; where can a horse's hoof avoid the remaining petals?
Master Jue of Tiantong on Mount Tianfeng ascended the hall and said: "Within the realm of non-arising, there is yet no place of rest;
atop a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, how could one find a footing? For now, cast your hands free into the void and turn yourself over directly beneath. How shall you speak this single phrase?"
When a person encounters good fortune, their spirit becomes refreshed; entering the fire, his true golden color grew even more brilliant.
When the Head Seat Daozu of Chengdu’s Zhaojue Monastery first met Yuanwu, he attained enlightenment under the phrase "Mind itself is Buddha.
After some time, Yuanwu ordered him to share the seat [of the Dharma hall]. One day, while leading the assembly into the inner quarters, there were about twenty people remaining. The Master...
Suddenly he asked, "When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them? The monk had no reply. The Master threw down his whisk and passed away suddenly.
The assembly was all struck with astonishment. They immediately informed Wuzu. When Wuzu arrived, he called out, "Head Seat Zu! The Master opened his eyes and looked at him.
Wuzu said, "Rouse your spirit and pass through the barrier. The Master nodded his head and finally entered nirvana.
The head seat Yunju Zongzhen of Nankang Commandery was a native of Danqiu.
While attending Yuanwu at Yunju, one day as he gazed up at the bell pavilion, he suddenly attained realization. When someone questioned him about it, the Head Seat responded with three verses.
The last of them read: "I have a single device; I show it directly to you. A thunderclap in the blue sky—lightning rolls and stars race. (As for Deshan’s [approach]...)
Ji replied, "The mere application of staff and shout does not detract from the ineffable mystery that is not transmitted; what loss is there for you? Upon this realization, he was greatly delighted.

Ultimately, he maintained his integrity with high self-respect, and his reputation for the Way grew ever more profound. He once wrote on a wall: "Dwelling upon the highest peak among a thousand crags, With years approaching sixty, I let myself go in ease.
I shall avoid having my name linger on people's tongues; I am content to be a monk of a hundred clumsinesses this very day."

Xu Fu, the Grand Councilor, styled Shichuan and known as the Layman of East Lake, would often attend upon his father, the former Dragon Diagram (Longtu) official, as they visited Fachang and Lingyuan.

Although they engaged in discourse all day long, the official regarded it with indifference. Yet, when Fachang passed away amidst casual conversation, the official was struck by this and began to place deep faith in this Way.
Later, while observing the mourning period for his father, he felt that there was no way to repay his boundless debt of gratitude.
He summoned Lingyuan to the site of Xiaozhi to preach the Dharma. Once Lingyuan had ascended the seat and finished the exchange of questions and answers, he said:

"Virtuous ones, as for Longtu, who in his daily life read ten thousand scrolls of books—passing them from one vessel to another like water, without leaving behind a single drop—tell me, where did he usually keep them?
Now that he has cast off his consciousness, what about those ten thousand scrolls?"
"Where would you place it? Upon hearing this, the Duke was suddenly enlightened and said, "I have no further regrets.
When Yuan descended from his seat, he asked, "Scholar, what did you just see that you speak in such a manner? The Duke replied, "If there were anything seen..."
"Then you have left the Master behind," Yuan said. Gong replied, "In that case, I am not as good as the old monk. Yuan asked, "What kind of mental state is yours, Master?

Yuan laughed heartily. At the beginning of the Jingkang era, while serving as a Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, he joined with several fellow officials who shared his aspiration to hang his alms bowl in Zemo Hall at Tianning Temple and apply himself diligently to the study of Yuanwu. Yuanwu also rejoiced in his insight.
Dichao Mai went to the Secretariat one day and pointed at Wuzhu’s cranial protuberance (*uṣṇīṣa*), saying, "This old fellow has not yet planted his heels on the ground.
Wuzhu struck him in the face and said, "How could a turtle ever have escaped from the jar?
Dichao Mai said, "I am glad that this old fellow has now planted his heels on the ground. Wuzhu said, "Do not slander him. Dichao Mai then withdrew.
The Prince of Jun, Zhao Lingqin, styled Biaozhi, was known as the Recluse Chaoran. While serving as the magistrate of Nankang, his administration was successful and his affairs were simple;

he frequently associated with Chan monks. He occasionally converted the public hall into a "room of Moke" (a Zen meditation space). It happened that Yuanwu was residing at Mount Ou; the Prince joyfully submitted himself to his guidance.
Yuanwu did not grant him any concessions, but when the Prince pressed his request persistently, Yuanwu said: "In this matter, one must..."
[The Master] replied, "It must simply be that one dies once before it can be attained. The Duke (Gong) understood this intuitively and once wrote a brief account of it himself, which said in part:
"When my house was poor and plundered, who knew that nothing remained? The empty house was uninhabited; how many times have robbers come and ransacked it?

Having realized this, he instructed [the Master] to provide him with further protection. In the winter of the Gengshen year of the Shaoxing era, the Duke was together with the Imperial Secretary Wang Zao and the Vice President of the Council Li Bing.
When Minister Ceng Kai went to Mount Jing to visit Dahui, Dahui, hearing of his arrival, ordered the drum to be beaten to summon him into the room.
The Minister joyfully approached with incense tucked in his sleeve. Dahui said, "Regarding the story of Zhaozhou washing the alms bowl, how do you, Layman, understand it?"
The Duke said, "What bowl are you looking for? He brushed out his sleeves and went out. Huì rose and grabbed him, saying, "The ancients attained enlightenment right here;
why do you not attain it? As the Duke was about to respond, Huì struck him and said, "What bowl are you looking for?"
The Duke said, "Only by returning this old man can it be accomplished.
Li Mison, the Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, was styled the Layman Puxian. In his youth, he could read five lines of a text at once.

At the age of eighteen, he passed the provincial examination and attained the jinshi degree in the capital. He subsequently rose through various important positions until, at twenty-eight, he became a member of the Secretariat.
The Retainer (Sharen) frequently entered Yuanwu’s quarters. One day, returning from the morning court audience, he reached Tianjin Bridge when his horse leaped;
he suddenly attained realization, and sweat poured from his entire body. He went straight to Tianning Monastery, where it happened that Yuanwu was stepping out the gate.

Seeing him from afar, Yuanwu called out, “Layman, congratulations! Your great matter is now finished. The Retainer replied with a stern voice, “Monk, why are you blinding me? Yuanwu then gave a shout.
The Duke also shouted. Thereupon, their exchange of spiritual sparks was swift and incisive; in all his dialogues with Wuzhuo, he never yielded when the occasion demanded.

Later, the Duke was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and requested a stipend from the state temple lands. He returned to Lianjiang in Min, where he built a hermitage to enjoy himself. One day, he suddenly manifested a slight ailment.
He suddenly requested a bath. Upon finishing his bath, he sat cross-legged and composed a verse, saying: "In vain have I spoken of Muku from the past; today it is clearly revealed.
The void topples Mount Sumeru—what need is there to speak of the path beyond? Having cast aside his brush, he passed away.
The Daoist woman Zu of Ju’ān was the niece of You Chayuan of Jian’ning. From her youth she had no desire to marry and devoted herself to the Way of the Patriarchs.
Upon hearing the words of Yuanwu’s public address, she attained clear and thorough understanding.
Yuanwu said, “You must cast away what you have seen before you can attain true freedom. Zu replied with this verse: “The pillar puts forth its horizontal bones; Space plays with its claws.”
"Teeth. Even if you were to understand this through the profound mystery, it would still be like sand in your eyes.

Lingren Benming styled himself "The Illuminated Chamber. He spontaneously attained a karmic resonance with Yuanwu and traveled extensively to consult renowned masters, all of whom granted him their seal of approval.
On the full moon of the second month in the Gengshen year of the Xiangxi era, he personally wrote three verses and sent them to Caotang Qing, subtly revealing his intention to pass away.
At the end of the month, he bid farewell to his relatives and passed away. Caotang appended a colophon to the verses and had them published;
Dahui also once offered words of praise to bring out their meaning. The verses say: "I do not recognize afflictions as bodhi; if one follows after afflictions..."
This is ignorance. At the moment of arising and ceasing, one must understand it. When a hawk flies over Silla, the people do not know it;
they do not recognize that afflictions are bodhi. Pure flowers grow from the mud. When someone comes to ask me what I am doing, I eat porridge and eat rice.
Once you have finished washing the bowl, do not concern yourself with it; do not concern yourself with it. All day long you are foolishly playing with sand on the seashore.
If you wish to recognize your original true face, it is precisely the patriarch’s single liberation.
Those who cannot speak it die beneath the axe; those who can speak it also die beneath the axe. Ultimately, how is it? Do not travel by night; at first light, you must arrive.
Lady Fan of Fanyang in Chengdu Prefecture had lived as a widow for many years. She would often sit and never lie down.

Hearing that Yuanwu was residing at Zhaojue Temple, she went there to pay her respects and requested instruction on the causes and conditions for entering the Way. Yuanwu instructed her to contemplate: "It is not the mind, it is not the Buddha, it is not a thing—what is this?
For a long time, she found no point of realization. Lady Fan wept and said to Yuanwu, "What further method does the Master have?"
[The Master] employed a skillful means to make it easy for him to understand. Wù said, "There is indeed a skillful means. He then had him look directly at "What is this?
Later, he attained realization and said, "I never realized that it was so near all along!"
Chan Master Wenshu Xindao of Changde Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Taiping Qin. He was the son of the Xu family of Meizhou. At the age of thirty, he received full ordination.

He traveled to Chengdu to study the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi* (Consciousness-Only), believing that he had reached the ultimate understanding. A fellow student challenged him, saying: "The three realms are mind-only; all phenomena..."

"Only consciousness! Now that the myriad phenomena before our eyes are so vividly manifest, where does the mind-consciousness reside? The Master was at a loss for an answer and did not know how to respond;

he subsequently left the mountain pass and wandered throughout the Yangtze and Huai regions. Upon arriving at Taiping in Shu, he heard of Chan Master Fojian’s night discourse, in which he raised the story of Zhaozhou’s "Cypress Tree.
When it reached the point where Jue Tiezui remarked, "The former master did not say such words; do not slander the former master," [the Master attained realization].

"Excellent. Because of his great doubt, he maintained this state of alertness for a long time. One night, it suddenly dawned upon him; he immediately rushed to the master’s quarters, intending to recount what he had realized.
As soon as Yuanjian saw him coming, he closed the door. The Master said, "If you still have something to say, do not deceive me.
Yuanjian replied, "The ten directions have no walls—why do you not enter through the door? The Master punched a hole in the window paper. Yuanjian immediately opened the door, grabbed him, and said:
"Dao! Dao! The Master held up a mirror with both hands, blew into it with his mouth, and stepped out. He then presented this verse: "Zhaozhou has that story of the cypress tree;
Zen practitioners have passed it down throughout the world. Most merely pluck leaves and seek branches, Unable to understand it directly at its very source.
Jue says there is no such thing as 'no such words'— This is truly reviling me to my face with foul speech."

"If a Zen practitioner possesses the eye that penetrates all quarters, they should well examine the true and the false within this. Jia Shen (Jiàshēn) agreed with this, praising it whenever he encountered guests.

Later, he was appointed to share the seat [of the abbot]. When Liu Xiang (Liú Xiāng), the regional governor, invited him to open the Dharma at Tianning Monastery, before long he was promoted to Wenshu Monastery on Mount Dabie.
He ascended the hall and said: "The lion yawns; the elephant king roars. Yunmen hid his body within the Big Dipper. White.
For what reason is a cloud called a "hand"? The Buddhas of the three periods of time cannot know it; yet the striped cat and the white ox do know it exists.
But tell me, what is this matter of their knowing it? Rain beats upon the pear blossoms and butterflies fly; the wind blows the willow catkins and they roll away like balls of wool.
Ascending the hall, he took up his staff and pointed directly upward, saying: "At such a time as this, [the staff] pierces through pride."
Śakra’s heel strikes down once and says: "At such a time, it shatters the crown bone of King Yama. Then, pointing to the east, he says:
"At such a time, it pierces through the eyes of the carp of the Eastern Sea. Pointing to the west, he says:
"At such a time, it blocks the nostrils of the Queen Mother of the West. But tell me: what is it like when it is not so at all? This year's rain.

There is much moisture; each [item] should be dried frequently in the sun. In the first year of the Xuanhé era, an edict was issued to change the title of monks to "Virtuous Practitioners" (Deshi). He ascended the hall and said:
"The meaning of the Patriarchs' coming from the West is, this very day, exceptionally new. Formerly you had the appearance of a Bhikṣu; now you have the form of the Old Lord (Laojun)."
Clad in a silver-brown crane-feather cloak, with a banana-leaf turban wrapped upon his head, this guest of the forest and springs has received the sovereign’s grace twice over.
Thus it is said: "If you wish to know the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should observe the conditions of time and season.
But tell me, what is the current season? Vairocana wears a jeweled crown to manifest the mundane within the ultimate; Mañjuśrī is old...
Old man, draped in a crane-feather cloak, you must likewise conform to the exigencies of the times. As it is for one person, so it is for all; together we shall establish a monastic grove (conglin).
How joyful it is that a gathering of immortals has been assembled! Let us together sip the immortal wine of delusion and jointly chant the *Buxu* hymns.
At times we shall read the *Lingbao Duren Jing*, or discuss the elixir of longevity and immortality. Under the moonlight, our fingers pluck the zither.
The sound of the primordial antiquity issues forth; the pieces are arrayed like a chessboard before the hall. Their wondrous manifestations transcend the realm of divine mechanisms:

take one step forward and you arrive at the heavens of the Great Luo; retreat one step and you enter the city of the Nine Shades. As for that phrase of neither advancing nor retreating—how would you speak of it?
Even if one were to transform into an immortal on the path to the Three Clarities, in the end, it remains but a cycle of saṃsāra.
The Illusory Body. In the ninth month of the second year, he was reinstated as a monk. Ascending the hall, he said: "Unadorned by the field-robe (kāṣāya), he wears the feathered robe;
the countenance of the Old Lord (Laojun) is quite fitting for him. For over a year and a half, I have reflected idly: in general, prosperity and decline each have their own time.

That our Buddha, the Tathāgata, foretold that the Dharma would encounter difficulties is clearly recorded in the teachings; there is no one who does not know this in detail. When calculating the years and eras..."
It is precisely here that Māra finds his opportunity to confuse the orthodox tradition: monks alter their monastic forms, Buddhas change their names, and they give rise to false interpretations.
They edit and excise the scriptural texts; the sound of the gongs and cymbals ceases, while the begging bowls are made to appear full. Such are their manifold deceptions.

Having deceived and misled the Sagely Sovereign, we rely upon the Sage Virtue and Sage Wisdom of our Emperor, Your Majesty, who has not forgotten the sacred entrustment and has not abandoned these teachings.
He has specially bestowed his Imperial Calligraphy for circulation throughout the world, and further permitted monks and nuns to once again don the monastic robes.

This is truly like cold ashes catching fire once more, or withered wood flourishing again; without leaving one’s secular form, one assumes the form of a monk, yet without departing from the realm of Māra.
He enters the realm of the Buddha, resounds the Dharma drum once more, and re-establishes the sagging cords of discipline. The delusive elixir of immortals is transformed into ambrosial jade nectar;
the "Verse on the Void" is turned into a "Song of Returning Home. He sets down the silver wooden tablet and picks up the *niṣīdana*.
"Yesterday morning I bowed my head and raised my hands; today I offer my greetings. I wonder: is it merely that the old appearance has changed, or is it that the old person has not changed?
I venture to ask the assembly: is the old person one, or is he two? After a long silence, he said: "Even the autumn wind understands how to loathe disorder;
it blows away the ashes of the Way from those years. In the spring of the third year of Jianyan, he addressed the assembly, citing:

Regarding the circumstances of Linji’s entry into extinction and his entrustment to Sansheng, the Master said: "The treasury of the true Dharma-eye was extinguished by a blind donkey. Where did Linji ever say such a thing?
People of all times, past and present, have all falsely transmitted this. Do not believe it; simply wait and see after three months.
When the intercalary third month arrived, the rebel Zhong Xiang rose up, and his followers wished to lead the Master away to the south. The Master said: "In studying the Way..."
"Since I have thoroughly understood birth and death, what is there to avoid? When the bandits arrived, the Master said, "Kill me quickly to satisfy your hearts.
The bandits immediately raised their spears and struck him; his blood was all white milk. The bandits were terrified; they covered him with their mats and departed.
Chan Master Zhibing of Nanhua in Shaoyou was a native of Yongkang in Shu. He ascended the hall and said: "This matter is most extraordinary; it is not obstructed by direct speech.
The old farmer next door has, according to custom, obtained a piece of the truth. It not only penetrates sound and form, but also accords with the times.
If you ask what school this belongs to, the eight characters do not fit [the mold]. He struck the meditation seat and descended.
[The Master] ascends the hall. "I speak of it day after day; I raise it up from moment to moment. It is like the earth supporting a mountain—how much difference does that make?
The parrot of Longxi is beloved by people; it is mostly because he can speak. Cease your deliberations and keep company with him.
When the wise hear this, they should seize it with vigor. There is yet another thing, most wonderful: the cat is uniquely adept at catching mice. [He] ascends the hall. With...
He brandished his staff toward the air and stirred it, saying, "Stirring the long river into butter and milk, yet the shrimp and crabs still have their eyes covered in rheum.
He struck the ground once and said, "Transforming the great earth into gold—yet the destitute fellow remains as before, bare-boned and skeletal. Is it that he himself has no share?
Or is it that he refuses to accept responsibility? Among them, there must be a man who can shoulder and carry this out to some extent.
When a person loses their money, they meet with calamity. [The Master] strikes the desk once more and says: "Do you understand? When you reach the Treasure Mountain, you must open your eyes;

do not let yourself return in haste with empty hands. He ascends the hall and says: "The spring light is lush and the flowers vie to bloom; the nightingale cries as the moon sets behind the western mountains.
The foreigner Panthaka sticks out his tongue in long astonishment. To whom can this clear matter be explained? *Sha!*" He ascends the hall.
Delusion does not delude itself; it is established in opposition to awakening. Awakening does not awaken itself; it is spoken of because of delusion.

Therefore, awakening is the substance of delusion, and delusion is the function of awakening. Both delusion and awakening are non-existent; from within this, there is neither distinction nor commonality.
Without distinction or commonality, one cannot be moved by any negation. The Patriarch did not bring it here; his nostrils weigh a thousand catties.
Chan Master Longya Zhicai of Tanzhou was the son of the Shi family in Shuzhou. Early on, he served diligently at the Dharma seat of Fojian, never shirking from difficult administrative duties;
his reputation had already spread throughout the monastic community. While traveling, he arrived at Huanglong at dusk and happened upon Sishi Xin at the main gate.
When asked where he had come from, he stated his name, and it was then known that he was from Shuzhou.
Taiping was a man of refined character. The following day, he entered the room. Sishin asked him, "If you understand the first phrase, you understand the final phrase;
if you understand the final phrase, you understand the first phrase. Setting aside both the first and the final, how do you understand Baizhang’s story of the wild fox?
The Master replied, "I have known his provenance upon entering the door. Sishin said, "Your understanding is still within the realm of views."
Xuefeng said, "Why must you further tread upon the mud in the middle? Xinghua said, "The new elder has died; he is now in the hands of the senior monk.
Xuefeng said, "Though the words differ, the ultimate principle is without discrepancy. Xinghua asked, "What is this matter that is without discrepancy?"
The Master said, "If one does not strike the horn of Huanglong, how can one know the pearl beneath its chin? He then struck him.
When he first resided at Yuelu, on the day he ascended the hall, a monk asked, "Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout—today I request the Master to extract their meaning for us.
The Master said, "Suru suru. The monk said, "Suru suru. Is there still the meaning of the West [coming from India] within this? The Master said, "Suru suru."

A monk asked, "When Ānanda questioned Kāśyapa, 'Aside from the transmission of the golden robe, what else did the World-Honored One transmit?'"
[The Master] said, "Object. Kāśyapa called out, "Ānanda! Ānanda responded. [The Master asked,] "I do not yet understand what this means.
The Master said, "By all means, do not touch it. [The student] asked, "As for Kāśyapa saying, 'Throw down the bannerpole in front of the gate,' how is that?
The Master said, "A stone ox lies across the ancient road. [The student] asked, "As for you, Master—within the Buddha-sun—is there still this [same thing]?"
“Is there no news? The Master said, “There is no such news. The monk said, “But what can be done? Dingguang beckoned from afar at Jindi, and Zhiyi nodded his head in secret at Jiangling.
The Master said, “Do not take the cypress by the courtyard and lightly compare it to the mugwort by the roadside.
The monk bowed, and the Master then said, “Dingguang beckoned from afar at Jindi; Zhiyi nodded his head in secret at Jiangling—this has already been said.”
These white clouds stretch for thousands of miles; how can one bear to remain here without knowing when to rest?
Even if one were to rest right here, the resulting mess would not be small. Is there anyone who can examine this and find the truth? If there is none, then this mountain monk has lost today.
A monk asked, "The Buddhas hand over to the Buddhas, and the Patriarchs transmit to the Patriarchs. I wonder, what exactly is being transmitted? The Master said:
He quickly prostrated three times and asked, "Since you have not deployed even an inch of blade, I request that you meet with me. The Master said, "When encountering strength, one yields weakness.
The monk asked, "How can you speak of burying troops and engaging in combat? The Master said, "It is precisely because you, O *jiaoli*, have not deployed even an inch of blade.

The monk asked, "I do not yet know whether there is anything further beyond this or not. The Master said, "There is. The monk asked, "What is this matter beyond? The Master said, "A defeated general."
"Not cut. He asked, "At the front of the ancient Buddha hall, who arrives first? The Master said, "The blind old villager.
[The monk] asked, "I do not understand how one should proceed. The Master said, "Carrying my staff slung across my shoulder."
Chan Master Daokuan of Kaishan in Jianning Prefecture was a native of that region. He first went to the capital to rely upon Yuanwu, yet he attained no realization.
Later, he followed Miaoxi as the latter resided in a hermitage in Southern Fujian; when Miaoxi took charge of Mount Jing, the Master also attended him there.
Before long, the Master was ordered to go to Changsha to deliver a letter to Layman Zhang of Ziyuan.

The Master said to himself, "I have practiced Chan for twenty years without reaching a point of entry; if I undertake this journey now, it will surely lead to further neglect and ruin. He intended not to go.
A friend of his, Zongyuan, scolded him, saying, "It is not permissible to practice Chan while on the road; come, let us go together.
The Master had no choice but to proceed. While on the way, he spoke weeping to Yuan, saying, "I have spent my entire life practicing Chan."
There is absolutely no place where you have gained strength. Now, moreover, you are rushing along the road; how can you achieve realization? Yuan told him:
"You simply need not concern yourself with anything you have studied under various masters, anything you have awakened to, or anything that Yuanwu or Miaoxi has explained for you.
Regarding matters on the road that can be substituted, I will substitute for you entirely—there are only five such items."
"Affairs cannot be handled on your behalf; you must attend to them yourself. The Master asked, "What are these five matters?
I wish to hear their essentials. Yuan said, "Wearing clothes and eating food; defecating and urinating; carrying a corpse along the road.
At these words, the Master grasped the essential meaning and, without realizing it, began to dance with joy. Yuan said, "Only now may you send a letter."
"You should proceed. I shall return first. Yuan immediately returned to Mount Jing, while the Master did not return for half a year.
Upon seeing him, Miaoxi said with joy, "Son of Jianzhou, this time you are truly different. Later, after taking up residence there, he ascended the hall and said:

"The mind of the Great Sage of the Land of Zhuzhi was secretly transmitted from east to west. What is this mind that was secretly transmitted? After a long silence, he said: "In the eighth month, autumn..."
"Abiding in heat. Ascending the hall: "A thousand fathoms of sheer cliff—where the Buddhas of the three periods have no place to set foot.
This is so, yet it is far too remote from human feeling. "Opening a single thread of the path—the oceans of lands in the ten directions emit light and shake the earth. This is so, yet it is so.

Alas, it is like mixing mud with water! You must know that where there is a single thread of passage, the wall stands ten thousand fathoms high; where the wall stands ten thousand fathoms high, there is a single thread of passage.
Held crosswise and used inverted, pressed straight and lifted from the side—like a flash of lightning or a roll of thunder, like a collapsing cliff or splitting rocks.
Though this may be so, it still falls within the gate of transformation. Reaching this point, even "the wall standing ten thousand fathoms high" has no relevance at all.
Even if you pass through a single lane, there is no connection. It is unfeeling; it muddies and waters everything down, yet there is still no connection.
This very lack of connection is itself a lack of connection. While this may be so, it nonetheless lacks the principles of the Buddha-dharma.
If you can emerge from these four paths, you will surely stride alone across heaven and earth. But as for that phrase, "striding alone"—what does it mean?
The Path of Birth. Do not be surprised that I have been so full of spirit lately; my house has long since ascended the highest pass.
Entering the hall: Last year there was a June fifteenth; this year there is also a June fifteenth.
Last year’s June fifteenth lacked this year’s June fifteenth; this year’s June fifteenth exceeds last year’s.
On the fifteenth day of the sixth month: where there is much, there is no need to subtract; where there is little, there is no need to add.
Since there is neither addition nor subtraction, then where there is much, one uses much; where there is little, one uses little. Then he gave a shout and said: "Which is much? Which is little?"
After a long silence, he said: "As for this message within, how many people could possibly know it? He ascended the hall and said:

"Dongshan’s 'three pounds of hemp'—take it and weigh it on a scale without a single star [of precision]. Every pound is exactly sixteen taels; it weighs two hundred coins, not even a hair’s breadth less.
It is exactly the same as that which was in Zhaozhou’s hall. It simply did not happen to be caught by..."
Dagyū’s sawing apart the scale-weight leaves people unable to understand it. If you wish to understand it now, simply ask Yunmen about the "dry dung pellet.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A phrase, no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree.
It knocks over the lanterns and shatters the pillar. The Buddha Hall scurries about; the Sangha Hall looks back. Look closely: what is this?"
Furniture! Tsk! It is fit only for beating rats. [The Master] ascends the hall and says: "All you people have come up here from the Sangha Hall in this manner;
in a short while, you will go down from the head of the Dharma Hall in this same manner. You have never taken a single step out of place.
Why, then, do you not understand? After a long silence, he said: "It is precisely because it is so utterly clear that what is attained is made all the more delayed."
Chan Master Fozhao Deguang of Yuyang in Qingyuan Prefecture was the son of the Peng family from Linjiang Commandery.

At the age when he resolved to study the Way, he relied upon Chan Master Ji of Guishua Temple on Mount Dongshan in his native prefecture to receive the tonsure. One day, while entering the master’s room for instruction, Ji asked him:
"It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing. What is it? The Master was at a loss; he remained in doubt throughout the night and could not sleep.
The following day, he went to the abbot’s quarters to seek further instruction, saying, "Yesterday, I received the Master's question: since it is neither mind nor Buddha..."
"It is neither Buddha, nor is it an object. Ultimately, what is it? I hope the Venerable Master will compassionately point this out to me.
Ji-zhen gave a shout and said, "You novice monk! Do you want me to provide a commentary for you? He then took up his staff and struck him across the back, driving him out.
At that moment, the Master attained realization. Later, he visited Yue-an Gao, Ying-an Hua, and Bai-zhang Zhen.
He ultimately could not bring himself to accept it. Just then, Daohui was presiding over the Yuyang Monastery, where the elite talents from all quarters gathered like scales of fish;
the Master was among them. In Daohui’s room, he questioned the Master: "If you call it a bamboo stick, you commit an offense; if you do not call it a bamboo stick, you turn your back on the truth.

You may not utter a word, nor may you remain silent. As the Master prepared to respond, Daohui struck him with his staff. At that moment, the Master attained a sudden and great awakening. From before...
That which was attained has crumbled like a wall and melted away like ice. Initially residing at Guangxiao Temple on Mount Tiantai, a monk asked:
"In the midst of vast confusion, how does one discern the Master? The Master replied: "At the very tip of the spire atop the central peak.

He then ascended the hall and said: "Linji received three severe blows; under Dayu, he knew his place of return. Xinghua, through the staff of Dajue, clearly realized the intent of Huangbo. If one were to..."
"Meeting the staff. Entering hell is like an arrow shot. If one does not meet the staff, entering hell is like an arrow shot.
Everyone in the assembly deliberated and said, "Heart exposed piece by piece; the kindness is great and difficult to repay. All of this is merely intellectual speculation;
it has not yet emerged from the realm of the shadows. For instance, when Linji attained enlightenment, was it through the power of Huangbo? Was it through the power of Dayu? If...
I see it clearly. I grant you that the eye atop your head is upright and the talisman behind your elbow is efficacious.
If this is not yet so, I shall, for the sake of all of you, provide a further message regarding great fortune: "The spirit of a man of worth pierces the ox and the dipper;

with a single tread, the two gates of Hongmen fly open. [He] ascended the hall and said: "Seven hands and eight feet; three heads and two faces. The ears hear nothing, and the eyes see nothing. Suffering!"
Blissful in both the contrary and the compliant, forged into a single whole. Tell me, what is it? When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it;
carry it home in a bottomless basket. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "To awaken to the Way upon hearing a sound is to fall into the second or third stage.

To clarify the mind by seeing form is to err sevenfold or eightfold. Even the single path of the living mechanism is still but halfway there. But tell me, how does one pass through the diamond circle and swallow the chestnut?"
"Among the thorns and brambles—who is this person? Clad in a raincoat, he stands askance beyond a thousand peaks; leading water to irrigate vegetables before the Five Elders.
When the Master resided at Lingyin, Emperor Xiaozong once summoned him to inquire about the Way and invited him to stay overnight in the Neiguan Hall.
The details of their dialogues and encounters are fully recorded in his own collection. Later, when he passed away, his entire body was interred in the Dong'an Pagoda on Mount Mao.
Chan Master Zongyan of Huizang Duan’an in Changzhou was the son of the Zheng family of Fuzhou. He ascended the hall and, raising his staff, said:
"If you recognize this, the task of a lifetime of study is finished. When the ancients spoke thus, I, Huizang, am not like that.
If you recognize this, you must still buy straw sandals and travel on foot. Why? Because when you reach the river, the land of Wu ends."

The other shore and beyond the mountains are many. On the morning of the first day of the twelfth lunar month, he ascended the hall and said: "In the first nine and the second nine, when we meet, we do not take our hands out of our sleeves.
In the mundane and the supramundane, there is neither excess nor deficiency. He then took his hand out and said, "Huazang does not spare his life; for all of you, I shall now take my hand out!
He struck three punches to the face and a single palm across the jaw. "A keen and intelligent patch-robed monk will know this for himself."
"Pain and itch. Now, regarding this turning-the-body phrase—how would you say it? "Go to the hall to drink tea. Ascending the hall, the Master cited Nanquan’s words:
"At eighteen, I already understood how to make a living. He then cited Zhaozhou’s words:
"At eighteen, I already understood how to break up the house and scatter the family. The Master said: "Nanquan and Zhaozhou were like Xu Liu carrying a single board."
I see only one side. Flower Treasury (Huazang) has no livelihood to be established, nor any home to be destroyed.

Whenever he encounters someone, he strikes them with an old fist, seeking to have them arrive directly at the moment. But tell me, what is it like after arriving? "The thirty-six peaks are not enough to gaze upon;
one turns back to ride a donkey backward across level ground."

Chan Master Jingquan Wuyong of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture was the son of the Wang family of Yuezhou. He ascended the hall and said: "In studying the Buddha, one merely says that 'the True' cannot be established;
in practicing Chan, one often acts in contradiction to the Way. Forget the mind and forget the environment, then quickly turn back;
when there is no ground and no awl, take a step and return. The Buddha is not it, nor is the mind it; receive it directly in its very essence, free from all dependence. Ten thousand...
The ancient emerald pool is the empty realm of the moon; only after thrice stirring and scooping can one truly know it. [He] ascends the hall.
After a long silence, he calls to the assembly, saying, "Do you understand? He speaks again: "The flaws are not few. [He] ascends the hall. He cites Changsha’s address to the assembly:
"Those who sit atop a hundred-foot pole—though they have gained entry, it is not yet the truth. One must advance further from the top of that hundred-foot pole. Throughout the ten directions..."
"The entire body manifests throughout the world. Great Wisdom (Mahāmati), the former master said: "Do you wish to see Changsha? Take another step forward.
Baoning, however, was not like this: "Do you wish to see Changsha? Take another step back. Ultimately, how is it? "Change the bones and wash the entrails, then reorganize;
though the whole body is eyes, one must still investigate further. When the Master arrived at Lingyin, he was invited to ascend the hall. At Lingshan...

A true school. Even those who have attained realization are still deluded. When light comes and darkness comes, who can discern it? When both are gathered and both are released, who can distinguish their source?
Even if a thousand sages were to appear, they would only end up with their tongues tied. Why? Because a person becomes noble only upon returning to the great kingdom;
water is truly clear only when it reaches the Xiao and Xiang rivers. He spoke again: "Just now, Master Songyuan cited the bamboo..."
The "Bamboo Rake" Case. This was intended to cause Tiantong to suffer defeat. Do you all wish to know? Listen to this verse:

Grasping the black-lacquered bamboo rake, it is like a sudden thunderclap that leaves no time to cover one’s ears. Deshan and Linji were left utterly bewildered; how could those who are dazed even open their mouths?
Dahui once raised the question regarding Lingyun’s awakening upon seeing the peach blossoms and asked the Master about it. The Master said: "Lingyun saw them once, and his two eyebrows..."
Transverse! It drew forth the old fisherman’s clever stratagem: when the white waves rose, he cast a single hook, letting the fish and turtles compete for it headlong.
The Master praised himself, saying: "A rustic fellow who cannot be lifted by a spoon; there is not a single speck of literary refinement in his breast."
He once squeezed the very bones out of empty space; his ill repute won him a place throughout the rivers and lakes. Later, he entered nirvana and was interred in a stupa at his home mountain.
Chan Master Da-mei Fabao was a native of Fuzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "To call it a bamboo stick is to encounter obstruction; not to call it..."
To make a bamboo comb is to turn one’s back [on the truth]. You must truly be like a lion biting a man; do not act like a Korean hound chasing after clods of earth.
A-he-he! Do you understand? Under the feet of the Vajra, there is an iron Kunlun; he has caught the doltish Bagua of Mingzhou. Entering the hall:
A thousand words and ten thousand metaphors are intended only to teach you to return home early. Last night a great mass of black clouds arose—do not...
"The teaching has mistaken the path ahead of the mountain.
*Du!* (A shout). Chan Master Tanyi of Yushan in Fuzhou had long relied upon Yuanwu, considering himself free from doubt.

At the beginning of the Shaoxing era, he went out to reside at Xiangyun in Xinghua, where his Dharma assembly was quite flourishing. When Dahui entered Min, he realized that Tanyi’s realization was not yet definitive and sent for him.
The order arrived: "The Master is delaying. Huì gave a small-scale sermon (*xiao can*) and severely rebuked him; he then posted a public notice for the fourfold assembly.

The Master, having no choice, broke his summer retreat to visit him. Huì interrogated him regarding his realization. Afterward, he said, "With such a view as yours, how dare you claim to be the successor of Old Man Yuánwù?
The Master withdrew from the monastery to attend upon him. One day, during a private interview (*ru shi*), Huì asked, "I want someone who does not..."
One who had mastered Chan became a National Teacher (Guoshi). The Master said, "I am going to become a National Teacher. Huì shouted him out.
Not long after, he said to him, "Xiangyan’s place of awakening was not at the point where the bamboo was struck; Juzhi’s attainment was not on the tip of his finger.
Thereupon, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. Later, while residing at Yuyuan, he offered incense for Huì. He subsequently visited Xinghui at Xiaoxi.
Hui ascended the seat. He cited an occasion when Yunmen one day held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying:

"Ordinary people truly take it to be existent; those of the Two Vehicles analyze it and take it to be non-existent; Pratyekabuddhas take it to be illusory existence; Bodhisattvas realize that its very substance is emptiness.
When a patch-robed monk sees this staff, he simply calls it a staff. When walking, he simply walks; when sitting, he simply sits. In all cases, he must not move."
Chaozhe said, "I am not like the old man Yunmen, who carves a hollow in empty space.

He then suddenly took up his staff and said, "This staff does not belong to existence, nor does it belong to non-existence; it does not belong to illusion, nor does it belong to emptiness. He struck the ground once with it and said:
Ordinary beings, followers of the two vehicles, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas—all turn toward this very place; each, according to their own capacity, attains its full utility.
Yet, within the sphere of the patch-robed monk, it acts as a harm and a grievance: when one wishes to walk, one cannot walk; when one wishes to sit, one cannot sit.
To take a step forward, you are bewildered by the staff; to retreat a step, your nostrils are pierced by the staff.
Is there anyone here now who cannot accept this? Come forth and meet the staff!
If there is none, next year there shall be new branches once more; the spring wind’s vexation will never cease. It is exactly thus.
"At such a time, how should one act? He descended from his seat and requested, "I ask Yquan to bring this forth for the sake of the assembly.
After the Master had ascended the seat and finished his expressions of gratitude, he took up the previous dialogue and said:
"Just now, the Abbot’s critique was much like a weary fish resting in a pond or a sick bird perching on reeds. If it were Yquan, it would not be so. He held up his staff and said: "This staff can—"
There is. It can be non-existent. It can be illusion. It can be emptiness. Ordinary beings, those of the two vehicles, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas—[the Master] struck the desk once and said:
"Right here, all are shattered into a hundred fragments. Only within the domain of the patch-robed monk is it like a dragon finding water or a tiger relying on a mountain;
when he wishes to walk, he walks; when he wishes to sit, he sits. To take one step forward, heaven and earth tremble; to take one step back, the weeds..."
Walking against the wind. Now tell me: how do you express the phrase "neither advancing nor retreating"? After a long silence, he said:
"Holding a scripture in hand, leaning against a pine tree, I smile and ask the guest from where they have come."
Chan Master Wuben of Jianfu Temple in Raoyou was a native of Jiangzhou. Having followed Yunmen of Jiangxi and attended upon Miaoxi, he eventually reached Xiaoxi in Quannan.
At that time, men of outstanding talent had all gathered there, and many received his seal of approval.
The Master felt privately slighted and wished to depart; Miaoxi, knowing this, said to him, "You need only focus your mind on practice."
"Exhaustively! If there were anything to be attained, I would have recognized it even before you opened your mouth.
Later, when he heard that the Master had entered the room, he said to him, "Attendant Ben has been practicing Zen for many years, yet day after day he says nothing but 'I do not understand.
The Master rebuked him, saying, "You little devil! Even before you were born, I have already [visited] the temple of Mount Huo three times."

His doubts were resolved. "I shall let you know," [the Master] said, whereupon [the student] further sharpened his resolve. Taking up the saying, "The dog has no Buddha-nature," he focused on the word "Mu" (無) for contemplation.
One night, at about three *geng* (hours before dawn), while leaning against a pillar in the hall and drifting toward sleep, the word "Mu" involuntarily escaped his lips.
Suddenly, he attained sudden enlightenment. Three days later, Miaoxi returned from the prefectural city. The Master hurried to the abbot’s quarters.
No sooner had he crossed the threshold than, before he had even uttered a word, Miaoxi said, "Old Bearded One, this time you have finally reached the very end.
Later, while presiding over the assembly, he ascended the hall and said: "To give thirty blows of the staff to one who bows high to Śākyamuni but does not bow to Maitreya—why?
Because such a person only knows how to climb higher step by step, but does not know how to let go from the void. While the neighbor to the east pulls the plow, the neighbor to the west..."
"One who drags a rake home shall receive thirty blows of the staff. Why? Because he only knows how to let go from the void, but does not know how to ascend step by step.
When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, is there any fault in it? Is there anyone among the assembly who can discern this?
If you can discern it, you shall walk hand-in-hand with me on the southern side of Mount Sumeru. If [you can discern it]...
Nothing can be found. An old crow in a cloth bag; though alive, it is as if dead. Entering the hall, [the Master said]:
"Śākyamuni closed his room in Magadha; Vimalakīrti sealed his mouth in Vaiśālī; Subhūti proclaimed 'no-speech' to manifest the Way;
Śakra and Brahmā ceased seeing and hearing as they rained down flowers. O Great Assembly! This crew of incompetent fellows has, for no reason, taken the ancestral fields..."
Garden. When private lands were partitioned by contract, each side was demarcated according to its four boundaries—square, round, long, or short—and everything was settled at once.
This has caused our descendants in later generations, even after a thousand years, to have not a single tile to cover their heads above nor a spot large enough for a锥 (chui) to rest upon below.
Had Boshan seen this at the crossroads at that time, he would have dug a bottomless deep pit and called out:
Let us bury this matter once and for all, so as to avoid mutual stagnation and frustration. Why is this? Have you not heard it said: "When the family prospers, filial sons are born;
when a state becomes hegemonic, there are strategic ministers"? [The Master] ascends the hall: "The Gandharva King once performed music, and the mountains, rivers, and the great earth all danced.
How can these compare to the lame old Yunmen, who could say, 'The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month'?"—Boshan.
Today there is no precedent to follow; where there is no precedent, one must follow the example. Yet, one must also respond to this particular occasion.

[The Master] suddenly picks up his staff, rests it horizontally across his knees, and makes the gesture of playing the lute, saying: "Is there anyone here who hears the strings and appreciates the music? After a long silence, he says:
"Even if you were to immediately cry out like a phoenix, who in the end would know the method of pointing? *He strikes once.* He descends from the seat.
Chan Master Dayuan Zunpao of Yewang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture was a native of Fuzhou. In his youth, he studied the Way alongside Yuquan Yi under Yuanwu.
After several years, he returned to his hometown and assisted Yi at Xiangyun in Pufeng. In the Jia-yin year of the Shaoxing era, Da...
Huìjū was staying at Yangyù. When the Master went to visit him, as they were entering the room, Huìjū asked:

"Regarding the dialogue concerning whether the Three Sages and Xinghua ‘came forth’ or ‘did not come forth,’ and whether they were acting as men or not acting as men—tell me, do these two old fellows have a way to manifest themselves, or not?"
The Master struck Hui once upon his knee. Hui said, "Was this single punch of yours to avenge San-sheng, or was it to avenge Xing-hua?
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! As the Master hesitated, Hui struck him again and said, "You must not, under any circumstances, forget this blow.
Later, while in his quarters, Hui asked a monk, "When De-shan saw a monk..."
As soon as [a monk] enters the gate, [Linji] strikes him with his staff. When Linji sees a monk enter the gate, he shouts.
When Xuefeng sees a monk enter the gate, he says, "What is this? When Muzhou sees a monk, he says, "This is a ready-made case; I grant you thirty blows.
Do you say that these four old fellows have any way of benefiting others? The monk said, "They do. Huì said, "Zha! The monk hesitated.
As they were deliberating, Huì let out a shout. Upon hearing it, the Master immediately grasped the subtle intent. Dàhuì joyfully granted him permission.
Cānmen Kùmù Zǔyuán, a Chan master from the Wēnzhōu Yànshān Néngrén Monastery, was the son of the Lín family of Fúmiǎn.
He first visited Xuěfēng Yù and subsequently relied upon Fóxīn Mù; with both, his spiritual faculties were in accord. Later, while relying on Dàhuì at the Yúnmén Hermitage, one night—
While sitting in the assembly hall, he saw a monk trim a lamp and attained sudden realization. He spoke a verse, saying: "Trimming up the lamp reveals the fire;
The ignorance of kalpas is shattered by its light. Entering the hall, I bump into the Holy Monk; I nearly let him slip right past me. If I do not let him slip—what is it?
What was marvelous fifteen years ago Remains, as before, just this very thing. Hui presented him with a verse in response:
Releasing the body atop a ten-thousand-fathom cliff, one rises and remains as alert as ever. Eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty, there is nothing at all to do;
what need is there to discuss whether one is the person of old or not? In the spring of the Yisi year of the Xiangxing era, [the Master] went forth to reside at Nengren Temple.
He ascended the hall and said: "Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; treading upon a scale-weight, it is harder than iron. Where there is no Buddha, pass by quickly; beneath one's feet..."
The grass is three feet deep. Three thousand miles away, do not mistake your words when meeting people. The Northern Dipper hangs from Mount Sumeru.
If it is so, then one does not go. With the staff, one lifts the sun and moon. Plucking the willow flowers—plucking the willow flowers! The pupils in the eyes wear embroidered shoes.
(He strikes his staff and descends from the seat. Ascending the hall: "The withered talent and true head of Chan at Yanshan does not reside in the sharp point."
At the edge of a new phrase, one suddenly reaches out with one's back turned and grasps it. A great whale swallows the moon as the waves overflow the heavens.
Zen Master Liaoxing of Dong’an at Lingyan Temple in Zhenzhou ascends the hall and says: "He has been thoroughly seen through; let him pass with one move."
This patch-robed monk wears tattered straw sandals; manifesting the form of an asura, he performs a woman’s bow.
This is a wild fox spirit; drawing a circle and placing a dot within empty space is the mere dexterity of a child.

Blocking the cheek with a slap and brushing the sleeves to depart is precisely the state of "vague karmic consciousness," having no foundation to rely upon. Even if one were to turn toward it before the black bean has yet sprouted—
The previous moment was already cut off; there was as yet no part of one’s share to eat of Lingyan’s staff. I dare ask the assembly:
tell me, where does the essential point of guiding others lie? Do you understand? Since the spring colors first came to Songshao, the thirty-six peaks have remained green until this day.
Entering the hall: On the riverbank, willows bloom in spring; in the heart of the waves, the traces of the past are not seen.
People of this time, you who seek to recognize the man of peace of mind in the snowy courtyard—your nostrils remain fixed upon your upper lip.
Raising his whisk, he said: "The Patriarch has arrived! Do you see him? If you can see him, realize it right now. If not, then [it will be as before]."
"The road from here to the Western Heaven is long, more than a hundred thousand miles. A monk asked, "When humans and devas meet, how do you instruct them?
The Master said, "The eight-sided staff in the hand of Vajrapāṇi. The monk said, "If a student suddenly pierces through both the mundane and the sacred, penetrating the profound barrier, what then?

Pervading all places throughout the *sāhasra-lokadhātu*, his entire body is eyes; facing the student directly, he is like lightning rolling and stars racing—how can one ever catch up?

The full majesty of life and death: which of those shouts is that which even Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot discern? Which of those shouts is that which leaves one vulnerable on all sides?

Whether you have escaped or not yet done so, this mountain monk will speak a dream while in a dream. Holding up his whisk, he said: "Do you see it? If you see it, you are obstructed by the thorn of seeing.

[The Master] made a sound. Fully releasing and fully gathering, host and guest interchange. Thus it is said: "If you wish to know the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should observe the conditions of time and season.

He became renowned for his mastery of both the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna teachings. At twenty-nine, a merchant returning from the Central Kingdom spoke of the flourishing state of the Chan school.
Jue’a was inspired and, accompanied by his dharma-brother Jinqing, sailed across the sea to China. There, he carried incense in his sleeve and paid homage to Master Fohai of Lingyin Monastery. Fohai—
When asked about his origins, Ache always wrote down his responses. He further wrote: "In my country there is no Chan school; we only lecture upon the sutras and śāstras of the five schools.
Our sovereign has no surname or given name and is titled the Golden Wheel King (Cakravartin). He changed the reign title to Jiaying and subsequently abdicated the throne to become a monk."
His name is Xingzhen. He is forty-four years old. When the Prince was seven, he was invested with the throne; it has now been five years.

Although he has not yet presented any offerings for the ordination of monks, those whose exegesis of the teachings is eminent are granted such honors. We, [the undersigned], look up to and revere the fame of the Venerable Master Cien of the Sagely Court.
We have come specifically to the chamber to pay our respects, wishing to receive the seal of the mind so as to cross the ford of delusion. Furthermore, as for the mind and the Buddha...
"And sentient beings—these three are without distinction. They are free from marks and free from words; they are manifested through provisional speech.
The Zen Master asked, "How would you instruct them? Hai replied, "Sentient beings have false views; they see Buddhas and they see worlds.
Ao asked, "From what cause does ignorance arise? Hai struck him. Ao then requested Hai to ascend the seat to resolve his doubts. The following autumn, he took leave to travel to Jin.

Ling arrived at the riverbank of Changlu. Upon hearing the sound of drums, he suddenly attained great enlightenment. He then realized the essential intent behind the Buddha’s reaching down with his hand.
He immediately composed five verses at Lingyin Temple to describe what he had perceived, and took leave of Hai to return eastward. The verses say:

"I sailed across the sea to seek the transmission outside the teachings, Seeking only to leave behind knowledge and views, and cast off the trap and snare. Having traveled everywhere and exhausted my straw sandals, The water remains in the clear pool."
The moon is in the sky. (I) Having swept away all entanglements and dualistic views, whatever is grasped by the hand is the total manifestation of reality.
The orb of light behind the head penetrates the great void; a thousand mechanisms and ten thousand functions are turned all at once. (II) How can this wondrous place be explained to others?
Falling to the ground and rising again, one is naturally clear; suddenly treading upon one’s own original ground, one walks alone on a solitary path with the official cap wrapped around the head.
(III) Seeking the true to extinguish the false is not at all subtle; to take the false as the true to clarify the real is entirely an error.

How laughable is that ancient master of Mount Lingyan, who cast down a broken wooden ladle right before our eyes! (IV) Raising a fist and letting out a shout is but a slight display of skill; to speak of it...
It is said that he did not enter the mud and water; cutting off a thousand differences, he ceased pointing and directing. With a single sound, he returned to "Di-luo-luo-li.

(Verse Five). Genshō Hōshi praised him as excellent and presented this verse as a parting gift. When he returned to his native country and resided at Enzan-ji, the letter conveying the succession of the Dharma arrived, but Genshō had already entered nirvana.
The Gentleman-in-Attendance, Layman Zeng Kai, whose style name was Tianyou, had long studied under Yuanwu and had been visiting Dahui’s gate for some time.
In the *Xinwei* year of the Shaoxing era, Fohai was appointed to Guangxiao Temple in Sangu.
Layman Gong and the Layman Zhao Chaoran went to visit him and asked, "What is a true spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*)? Fohai replied, "Lanterns, pillars, and cats."
“Dog! The Official asked, “Why is it that praise brings joy while disparagement causes affliction? Hai replied, “Minister, have you ever met a true teacher (kalyāṇamitra)?
The Official said, “I have been seeking instruction for thirty years; how can you say I have not seen one? Hai said, “Look where there is joy; look where there is affliction.
As the Official hesitated, Hai let out a thunderous shout and struck him. Before the Official could respond, Hai—
He said, "The one who opens his mouth is not [the true one]. Gong was bewildered. Hai called out, "Where did you go, Minister? Gong suddenly awakened and nodded his head.
He then spoke a verse: "Alas, blind donkey! A pestilence to the monastic groves. With a single sound that shakes the earth, the celestial mechanism has been leaked.
If anyone asks further what the meaning is, I will lift up my whisk and strike them across the mouth."—Hai.
He said, "I have only attained one peg.

The Prefect Ge Tan, a lay practitioner whose courtesy name was Qianwen and whose style name was Xinzhai, had achieved high honors in the civil service examinations in his youth; he devoted himself to the joy of Chan meditation.
He first visited Chan Master Wuan Quan to seek guidance. Wuan instructed him to investigate the saying, "The very mind is Buddha. After a long time, he remained without realization.
He requested, "Master, what skillful means can you provide so that I may gain entry? Wuan replied, "Layman, you are truly insatiable!"
Subsequently, Fohai came to reside at Jianchi. The Master followed him on his travels and brought up the words shown by Wuan, requesting that he preach them for the assembly.
Fohai expounded upon them, saying: "Mind is Buddha, eyebrows trailing the ground; not mind, not Buddha, two eyes staring wide.
Amidst the butterfly’s dream, home is ten thousand miles away; on the branch of the night-bird, the moon is already in the third watch. He remained there for ten days.

He returned after a day. One day, he raised the question: "It is not the mind, it is not the Buddha, it is not a thing. Suddenly, he attained clear and immediate enlightenment. He spoke in verse: "Not mind, not Buddha, nor yet a thing;
Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, the mountain looms high. In the midst of the brilliant sun’s shadow, he turns his body upside down;
The wild fox leaps into the golden-haired lion’s den. Wu’an approved of this and immediately sent a letter with the verse to present to the Buddha.
Zhaozhou Hai said, "This matter cannot be fully expressed by paper or brush. Layman, if you can pass me, you shall have something to hear.
He then went back to Huqiu. When he arrived, Zhaozhou Hai met him and said, "Your understanding, Layman, is sufficient only to enter the realm of the Buddhas."

He had not yet entered the realm of the Māras. The Official continued his courtesies without ceasing. Guishan Hai said with a composed countenance, "Why do you not say, 'The golden-haired lion leaps into the wild fox's den'? The Official then deeply understood. He once asked the various Chan masters, "If a husband and wife are fighting, and their son serves as witness—tell me, does he bear witness for the father, or does he bear witness for the mother? Oran said: "If he bears witness for the father, he is not the son. If he bears witness for the mother, he is not the son. If he is not the son, who then is the witness? If he is the son, why is he not the witness? If you can answer this question, I will grant you a bowl of rice. The Official was speechless. Later, he sighed and said, "This old fellow has truly broken my head. He then composed a verse: "The father and mother are fighting; The son stands as witness. If he bears witness for the father, he is not the son. If he bears witness for the mother, he is not the son. If he is not the son, who is the witness? If he is the son, why is he not the witness? If you can answer this question, I will grant you a bowl of rice. He then went to see Guishan Hai, who asked him, "What did you say when you were at the various monasteries? The Official replied, "I said, 'The father and mother are fighting; the son stands as witness... Guishan Hai laughed heartily and said, "The Official has indeed broken his own head. The Official then prostrated himself and said, "Please, Master, save me. Guishan Hai said, "The golden-haired lion leaps into the wild fox's den. The Official was greatly enlightened. He then composed a verse: "The golden-haired lion leaps into the wild fox's den; The wild fox's den is suddenly overturned. The father and mother are both dead; The son is left alone, weeping bitterly. He then went to see Oran. Oran asked, "What did you say when you were at the various monasteries?
