The Chan Master added a comment, saying: "A small emergence meets with a great occasion. In the sixth year of the Chunxi era, he governed Linchuan; in the eighth year, he was stricken by illness.
One night, he suddenly asked for a brush and wrote this verse: "Beating the drum within the vast ocean, Hearing the bell atop Mount Sumeru."
The karmic mirror suddenly shattered; he turned his body around and emerged into the void. He summoned his subordinates and showed them [the mirror], saying:
"Life and death are like day and night; there is nothing strange about this. If one speaks from the perspective of the Way, how could there be life and death?
To interpret it in terms of life and death is to distance oneself far from the Way. Having finished speaking, he sat upright and passed away.

Chan Master Biefeng Baoyin of Mount Jing in Lin’an was a successor of Chan Master Huazang Min. He was the son of the Li family of Jiazhou. From his youth, he mastered the Six Classics but grew weary of worldly affairs;
he subsequently received the tonsure under Qing-su of De-shan. After receiving full ordination, he studied the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* under Master Qi.
Xin, having exhausted his explanations, abandoned his reliance on Mimi at Zhongfeng. One day, Mi raised a case: A monk asked Yantou, "What is it like when arising and ceasing do not cease?
Yantou shouted, "Who is it that arises and ceases? At this, the Master attained enlightenment and immediately nodded in agreement.
When Yuanwu returned to Zhaojue, Zhimen Yin sent the Master there to pay his respects. Consequently, he entered the room with the assembly.
Yuanwu asked, "How did the sages of antiquity receive people? The Master held up his fist. Yuanwu said, "That is what I, this old monk, use.
What is it that the sages of antiquity use? The Master struck him with his fist. Yuanwu also raised his fist and crossed them, then laughed heartily.
He stopped there. Later, he went to Mount Jing to visit Dahui. Dahui asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From West Sichuan.
Dahui said, "Before you even left Jianmen Pass, I would have given you thirty blows of the staff! The Master said, "It was not fitting for me to trouble the Master."
Huì was delighted and swept his quarters to welcome him. Huì moved southward, and the Master then returned west. He presided over several monasteries in succession.
Later, he crossed the gorges again and resided at Baoning, Jinnshan, Xuedou, and Jingshan. Opening the hall and ascending the seat, he said:
"When the World-Honored One first attained perfect enlightenment, he turned the Dharma wheel of the Four Noble Truths within the Deer Park. The bhikṣu Kauṇḍinya was the very first to realize it."
Later, when Chan Master Zhenjing first resided at Dongshan, he took up the case and said: "Today, inside this New Fengdong, I am merely turning over a walking staff.
He then held up his staff, placed it to his left side, and asked: "Is there anyone here who attained enlightenment from the very beginning?
If not, a man of spirit has the will to charge toward the heavens; do not walk where the Tathāgata has walked. He then let out a shout.

“Ha! Descend from your seat. If it were Master Yin, it would not be so. Today, within this Phoenix Mountain, there is no leisure to turn the Dharma wheel of the Four Noble Truths, nor is there the strength to turn the staff; I simply instruct all of you to walk.

One must walk slowly; one's speech must be in a low voice. Why? Because one wishes not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell. Do not slander the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata. Upon ascending the hall [he said]:

"The Buddhas of the three periods of time expound hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of phrases with a single phrase, and they condense those hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of phrases into that very same single phrase.
Under the gate of the Patriarchs, however, there is not even half a phrase. It is simply thus. He then closed the door.
How many painful blows have you received, worthy sirs? Now, as for the Buddhas and the Patriarchs:
if you say the Buddha is right and the Patriarch is wrong, or the Patriarch is right and the Buddha is wrong, you have not yet forgotten grasping and rejecting.

If you say the Buddha and Patriarch are both right at once, or the Buddha and Patriarch are both wrong at once, your negligence is no small matter. Cut off this entanglement immediately! How do you speak this one phrase? Great!
A worm wrapped in a paper hat—truly laughable yet startling. Again, he raised an instance: A monk asked Yantou, "In the midst of vast confusion, how does one discern the master?
Yantou replied, "A copper gong filled with oil. The Master said, "Big or small, Yantou has lost his nostrils.
If someone were suddenly to ask Baoning, "In the midst of vast confusion, how does one discern the master? I would simply answer him: [a copper gong filled with oil].
The weather was so cold that he did not even remove his hat before ascending the hall. On the first day of the sixth month, the sky is scorched by a crimson sun;

at the crossroads, the snow is a foot deep. There is no time to sweep it away, nor can one avoid it. It freezes the old man Liao of the eastern village until, in the dead of night, he puts on his boots and stands upon the water.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If you try to use the mind to eliminate delusion, delusion is difficult to eliminate; realize the mind within delusion, and the Way is revealed."

He turned his course toward Yuyuan. Having kicked through the bottom of the bucket, he was free from all inhibitions; with every casual step, a lotus flower bloomed. When the Master arrived at Mount Jing, he was received with great favor.
Emperor Xiaozong summoned him for an audience in Xuande Hall, and he pleased the Emperor’s mind. On the day of the audience, the Emperor granted him a palanquin within the Donghua Gate.

In the second month of the tenth year, the Emperor annotated the *Nirvāṇa-samantabhadra-bodhi-citta-śāstra* (Yuánjué jīng) and dispatched an envoy to present it to him, ordering him to compose a preface.

The Master was advanced in years and grew increasingly weary of serving as abbot. In the winter of the fifteenth year, he submitted a petition requesting to live in seclusion in a hermitage, and his request was granted.
In the eleventh month of the first year of the Shaoxi era, he went to see the incoming abbot, Chan Master Zhice, to bid him farewell. Zhice asked him the date of his departure.
The Master said, "When the water arrives, the channel is completed. He returned and requested paper to write the nine characters: "On the seventh night of the twelfth month, at the hour of cockcrow.
As scheduled, he passed away. His physical remains were brought back to the Dharma Hall of the monastery and remained there for seven days, their complexion bright and lustrous.
His hair grew long and his head remained warm. Seven days later, he was buried on the western ridge of the hermitage. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Ciben, and his stupa was named Zhiguang.
He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Zhaojue Yuan.

Master Fengxi Huiquan ascended the hall and said: "In the villages ahead, the fallen leaves are gone; in the deep courtyard, the osmanthus flowers have withered. This night marks the onset of early winter;
from now on, it will grow especially cold. Therefore it is said: 'If you wish to know the meaning of Buddha-nature, observe the conditions of time and season.
When the time and season arrive, the principle reveals itself of its own accord. He gave a shout and said, "To speak in such a manner is to become a person."
Few succeed; those who ruin themselves are many.
Chan Master Huifang of Chuan, of the Xu clan of that prefecture, was a successor of Chan Master Daowen. He went to Mount Dabi to attend upon Chan Master Daowen.

Before long, the temple was converted into a Shenxiao Palace. While traveling south along the Xiang River on a merchant vessel, he heard a person on the bank speaking in his native dialect and shouting, "Jianna!
At this, he attained sudden enlightenment and immediately spoke this verse: "A single shout from the heart of the river at Mian— Only now do I realize my lifelong purpose.
After many years of separation, we meet again; The myriad sages return to the same source."
Traveling along the way, he arrived and ascended the hall to teach. Only in his old age did he assume the title of Abbot; he possessed not even a trace of profound mystery.

When he opened his mouth, nine out of ten things were perverse. Asked about the east, he would answer regarding the west. One who enters the world in such a manner—what profound subtlety could there be to seek?
At times he sets aside three and releases two; at times he acts according to the established command. Although it is thus, only those of the same path truly know. Moreover—

This is the matter of knowing the Way. How is it so? You must strike the nostrils clean out before you will succeed. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The Patriarch Bodhidharma is beneath one's feet;
if you cannot tread upon him, you cannot lift him up. Look closely at what is right before you and let it drop away. As for where the illness lay back then, who held it in their hands?
Zhang Gong was skilled at diagnosing the pulse; Li Gong was skilled at administering medicine. The two of them vied with one another to treat it."
At one time, it was not of use; the medicine did not harmonize. A mistake, a mistake! "Go drink tea.
Master Wenshu Siye of Changde Prefecture was a butcher by trade in his worldly life. One day, while slaughtering a pig, he suddenly attained a thorough penetration of the source of the mind.
He immediately abandoned his occupation to become a bhikṣu and composed a verse, saying: "Yesterday was the heart of a yakṣa; this morning is the heart of a Buddha."
The Master faced [the Buddha]. The Bodhisattva and the yakṣa were not separated by even a single thread. He went to see Mañjuśrī, who said, "When you were just slaughtering the pig, what did you see?
That is why you have shaved your head and set out on pilgrimage. The Master then made the gesture of brandishing a butcher's knife.
Mañjuśrī shouted, "This butcher! Go to the hall for instruction! The Master then went down to the hall. While staying at Wenshu, he ascended the hall and raised [this case]:

Regarding the story of Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman, it is said: "The old woman was thoroughly exposed; her face turned green and her eyes blackened. This old fellow Zhaozhou could not deceive me.
He was a successor of Chan Master Heshan Xun.
Chan Master Liaoyun of Chouyan in Yiwu, Wuzhou, ascended the hall and raised the koan of Zhaozhou’s “The dog has no Buddha-nature.
He then said: “Zhaozhou says the dog has no Buddha-nature; Ten thousand layers of green mountains conceal an ancient mirror.
A barefoot Persian enters the Great Tang; Eight-armed Nalakūvara executes the true command. Huh!”
The lay practitioner Pan Lianggui, whose courtesy name was Yirong, was forty years of age when he turned his mind toward the ancestral gate.
Wherever he went, he hung up his alms bowl and joined the assembly to seek instruction through inquiry. Later, he relied upon Fodeng; after a long time, however, there was no resonance.
He therefore complained, saying, "I only wish to know: at the moment of death, what is it like? Fodeng said, "A fine envelope; keep it for future use. At present, it is not yet resolved.
Later, when he went there, he suddenly found that the envelope had been switched out by someone else, leaving him with no way to rectify the situation.
The Master then asked about the story of Nanquan killing the cat: "I have contemplated this for a very long time, yet I have never fully penetrated it. I beg the Venerable One’s compassion."
Fandeng said, "You have merely managed to understand the cats of others' houses; you do not realize that you have lost your own dog. At these words, Fenyang was as if awakened from a drunken stupor.
Fandeng spoke again, saying, "It is no small matter for you to have taken this one step forward, yet you must still know that there is a stage beyond this before you may truly attain it.
Nowadays, when scholars and officials speak of Chan or the Way, they rely solely upon intellectual principles."
"He is simply happy. For the most part, it is like buying oil-cakes with money: once eaten, one is no longer hungry;
as for everything else, they say it is deceiving him, which is also quite laughable. Gong replied, "Yes, yes."

Chan Master Shouyuan of Shuian, known as Wúwéi of Hánzhōu, was a dharma successor of Chan Master Lètán Míng. He was a native of his own prefecture and belonged to the Shǐ clan. At the age of thirteen, he suffered from blindness in his eyes;
he subsequently went to rely upon Chan Master Huìmù Néng of Qīchán. After receiving full ordination, he traveled out of the gorges to Bǎofēng, where he encountered [Master] Fēngshàng.
The Master ascended the hall. Yongjia said, "The single moon universally appears in all waters; all water-moons are subsumed within the single moon.
Upon hearing this, the Master attained realization with complete clarity. Later, when he ascended the hall, he said: "Unify the myriad through the one:

the single moon universally appears in all waters. Convergence of the myriad into the one: all water-moons are subsumed within the single moon. When extended, it encompasses the entire Dharma-realm; when withdrawn—"
Not even a hair’s breadth remains. Although the paths of gathering and unfolding differ, this matter fundamentally has no diverse causes.
Only when you can fix a single eye upon the root source will you see that all Buddhas of the three periods and the patriarchs of successive generations have all manifested from within this;
that the Tripiṭaka, the twelve divisions of the canon, and all the sūtras have all flowed forth from within this.

Heaven and earth, the sun and moon, and the myriad phenomena of the universe are all established from within this. The three realms and nine stages, the seven destinies and four modes of birth, all emerge from and dissolve back into this.
The hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates and immeasurable subtle meanings—even down to the worldly arts and crafts—are all manifested and practiced herein.
For this reason, when the World-Honored One held up the flower, Kāśyapa immediately [smiled].
The Buddha smiled; Bodhidharma faced the wall. Thereupon, the Second Patriarch attained peace of mind. Peach blossoms bloomed in full splendor;

Lingyun’s doubts were completely purified. Striking bamboo produced a sound; Xiangyan suddenly forgot all that he knew. This extends even to Panshan awakening to the Way at a meat stall, and Maitreya meeting people in a fish market.
Truly it can be said: "In moments of haste and in times of distress, one must always rely on this. Thus it is in the Sūtras.
Walking, sitting, and lying down are all contained within it. Since it possesses such wonders, and further such radiance;
since it possesses such vastness, and furthermore such universal pervasiveness—why is it that you people still have both delusion and awakening?
Do you wish to know? "Fortunately, there is no place where it shines partially; yet, there is indeed a time when it is not clear."

Chan Master Wuan Desheng of Yunju in Nankang Commandery was a dharma heir of Chan Master Longxiang Gui. He was the son of the He family of Hanzhou. At the age of twenty, he received full ordination and studied the exegesis of the scriptures.
After some time, he abandoned that path to visit Chan Master Wenshu Dao, asking for the essential points of the Buddha-dharma. Wenshu showed him this verse:
The Khitans broke the Persian camp and seized a precious pearl, which they sold in the village.

At the crossroads, a destitute beggar had a "fashionable pouch" hanging from his waist. As the Master was about to offer a reply, Shu said, "Do not err. The Master withdrew and practiced for three years.
Only then did he grasp the essential meaning and go to see the Buddha-nature; however, his faculties were not in accord. He traveled to Fuzhou and went to Mount Gu to pay his respects.

[The student] asked: "Yantou said, 'This old fellow has not yet realized the final word. What about that? The Master said: "He followed along. [The student] asked:

When the Master passed away, [the disciples] asked, "Is there still a definitive point? The Master said, "Mānīdarī hūṃ phaṭ.

As he was about to pass into nirvana, he ascended the hall and held up his staff, showing it to the assembly, saying, "Apart from form, sound, and speech, bring forth a single phrase! The assembly remained silent.
The Master said, "Beyond movement and stillness, beyond sound and form—people of this age refuse to respond. [This applies to] both the mundane and the supramundane. He then finished.
"Ultimately, who can understand this? Having said this, he leaned on his staff and passed away.
Chan Master Zu Zheng, an old monk of Dahuang in Suizhou and a native of the Pan family of Tanzhou, ascended the hall and said:
"Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed. How can one speak of the principle of this 'alone being revealed'? Raising his whisk, he said: "Reaching the river..."
The land of Wu has come to an end; across the shore, the mountains of Yue abound. A monk asked:

"Yunmen once asked a monk, 'The luminous, silent illumination pervades the sands of the Ganges—this is surely the speech of the scholar Zhang Zhuo, is it not? The monk said, 'It is. Yunmen said, 'Your words have fallen.
I do not know where this monk’s words fell. The Master said: "A catfish climbing a bamboo pole. [The monk] asked: "Setting aside words and phrases, please—"
The Master pointed directly at him. The Master held up his whisk. The monk asked, "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "There is.
The monk asked, "What is this thing further beyond? The Master said, "Quickly, prostrate three times."
Chan Master Shantang Dechun of Letan Mountain in Longxing Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "One finger of Juti; a single hair pulls nine oxen.
The Flower Peak reaches the azure heavens; the Yellow River flows from its very depths. Cut off the finger and quickly turn your head back.
Before the green bamboo hat, there are infinite matters; beneath the green straw raincoat, everything ceases at once."
Chan Master Bokuan Ke-feng of Bāo'ān Temple in Yixing, Changzhou, was a native of the Lin family of Fuzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "The heavens are vast and the earth is wide;
the wind is clear and the moon is bright. This is the season when the world is at peace and its foundations are firm.

Yet when a patch-robed monk is questioned casually about it, out of ten there are perhaps five or six who truly know it. It is just like the night when the pond of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra swallowed up Yangshan."
"Subhūti, when Kaibō Bridge struck down the Hiraizumi Pagoda, did you all know it?
If you do know, try and utter a single phrase from the Heaven of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception. If you do not yet know, [the Master] threw down his whisk and said:
'It must be this mountain monk’s whisk that can do so.'"
Chan Master Zuxuan of Shiting Wild Hermitage in Longxing Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "Have you finished eating your congee yet?
Zhaozhou had no taboos, yet he further ordered the washing of the alms bowl—truly, how utterly groundless! To claim one has attained awakening based on this is not the mark of a true man.
This monk could not bear to be smeared with such nonsense. Whether there is an instruction or no instruction, the four corners of Mount Shao have completely collapsed."
The ground. Entering hell is like an arrow being shot. From the clouds and ravines, a pure breeze arises in the great hall. Meeting, they take each other’s hands and ascend the high mountain.

Chan Master Shishuang Zongjian of Tanzhou ascended the hall and said: "Sending off the old year and welcoming the new year—its active functioning never departs from within the light and shadow.
Its radiance is clear and its brilliance profound as the night hall grows cold. I ask you all, do you understand? If you do understand, you increase your flaws;
if you do not understand, you remain as before in ignorance. I shall point out for you the mechanism that cuts off the flow: the white clouds..."
Outside the Green Mountains:
Chan Master Nankang-jun Yunju Peng’an Dēhuì, a successor of Chan Master Shítóu Huí, was the son of the He family of Chóngqing Prefecture. He ascended the hall and raised [the following case]:
The teaching points to the Middle Way: if one sees that all marks are non-marks, then one sees the Tathāgata. What is the principle of these "non-marks"?
He feigns flight, feigns shame, and casts a sidelong glance: the bamboo gate is half-closed, and a single branch of flowers remains.
Chan Master Zhong’an Huikong of Fashi Monastery in Quanzhou,

a descendant of the seventeenth generation under Nanyue and a dharma heir of Chan Master Jiaozhong Guang, was a native of the Cai family in Ganzhou. On a spring day, he ascended the hall and held up [the whisk].
[The Master] takes up his staff, strikes once, and says: "First, strike the head of the Spring Ox. He strikes again and says:
"Afterward, strike the tail of the Spring Ox. Startling the void, he enters within a lotus fiber. Śākyamuni has no way to hide his tracks; Maitreya flees in haste for a thousand miles.
Mañjuśrī, however, knows where it lands; he claps his hands and laughs with joy. But tell me, what is there to be joyful about?
"The spring breeze entered the gate last night; immediately, a thousand flowers bloom upon the tip of the pestle. Entering the hall, he said:

"In the pavilions and towers of a thousand homes, a single gust of autumn wind blows. One only knows that a coolness arises in the sleeves and bosom, unaware that the leaves are falling from the gardens.

If you can realize this, then everywhere you touch is entirely true. If not yet so, let us meet with formal greetings of 'how are you? Entering the hall, he cited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*:"
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "In all those lands, the Tathāgata fully knows the various kinds of minds of all sentient beings.
Why is this? The Tathāgata says that all these minds are 'not-minds'; it is for this reason they are called 'minds. Do you understand the essential point?
'When the spring breeze brings joy, the horse's hooves race; in a single day, one views the flowers of Chang'an. A monk asked: "The Buddhas of the past..."

[The Master] established a precedent. Regarding the *kaṭhina* retreat (*jinzú ān-jù*), I do not yet understand what its fundamental principle is. [The Master] said: "Within a lapis lazuli bowl, Mount Sumeru is leveled.
The monk then gave a shout; the Master then struck him.
Chan Master Huyen Tanmi of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an was the son of the Lu family of Tiantai. He left home life under Dao-rong of Zifusi.
At the age of sixteen, he received full ordination and studied the Tiantai teachings. Later, he abandoned that path to visit Dahui at Mount Jing. There, he called upon Xuechao Yi and Ciyuan Yuan.
Upon entering Min, he stayed at both Donglin and Xichan monasteries but had no realization. He then traveled to Quannan, where Jiaozhong instructed him to study with Yue.

The assembly [was present]. Having resigned from his office and returned to his former position, he happened to raise the karmic occasion of Xiangyan striking the bamboo. He attained sudden enlightenment and composed a verse to present to Zhong.
Zhong questioned him with the words, "Xuansha has not yet reached the ultimate," but [Xuedou] was unhindered.

Zhong said, "Only then may you see Miaoxi. He immediately took leave and went to Mei Yang, where he served diligently for four years. Later, upon ascending the hall, he said: "When the Buddhas appear in the world, they commit a robbery."
"Killing people! When the Patriarch came from the West, he blew wind and set fires. The spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) of past and present have the mouth of a Buddha but the heart of a snake.

The monks of the world throw themselves into cages and traps; is there not a man of natural magnanimity, a truly outstanding hero, who will extend a hand for the sake of the ancestral school and uphold the Buddha-dharma?
After a long silence, he said: "Even if there were such a person, they would still have to be cut into three pieces."
Section. Ascending the hall, [Deshan] said: "Deshan’s informal teaching (*xiao can*) does not answer questions; for a thousand ages, the monastic communities have made this a subject of idle talk.
To those who ask questions, he gives thirty blows of the staff. When he was accustomed to speaking with such harshness and bluntness, a monk came forward, able to break through [his defenses].
Deshan then struck him—a gesture both elegant and refined. [The monk said: "I have not even asked a question; you have placed a cangue upon my head and shackles upon my feet. You—
"Where are you from? Every time we meet, it breaks my heart. "I am a man from Silla; I smile with joy as I hold your hand.

"Before he has even stepped onto the ship's railing, he deserves thirty blows for still deceiving one another as before. Today, Huiyuan makes such a critical judgment and reprimands him on his feelings;
he too deserves thirty blows. Now tell me: is this a reward or a punishment? Those who possess the eye of a true student of the Way—try!
Discerning Observation. Ascending the hall, the Master raised the karmic occasion of Yunmen’s question to a monk regarding the saying: “Luminous, silent illumination pervades the sands of the Ganges.
The Master said: “Sifting for fish and shrimp on level ground; shooting a soaring falcon across the vast heavens. The lame-legged old Yunmen—thousand errors and ten thousand mistakes!”
Later, he passed away and was interred at his home mountain.

Chan Master Duan’an Zu Zhu of Gong’an in Jingnan Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yan of Donglin. He was a native of Nanping. Once, while ascending the hall, he said: "It is not mind. It is not...

This is the Buddha; it is not a thing. Having drained the drool of the wild fox to its dregs and kicked over the den of the mountain ghost, a scorched-tail tiger is revealed amidst the level fields and shallow grass, and a magnificent falcon from the vast heavens is unleashed within the empty expanse of space. A-he-he!
Revealing the very bones and marrow, he casually brings it forth before the multitude. Ultimately, what exactly is this clear thing? *Du! Du!* Ascending the hall, he said:
Jade dew hangs upon the green grass; The golden wind stirs the white duckweed. A single cry from a cold wild goose Awakens those who have not yet awakened.
Chan Master Fayuan of Ba’en in Tingzhou was a native of Guozhou. One day he ascended the hall and, citing the karmic occasion of Juzhi’s raising of a finger, said:
"A beautiful woman rises from sleep too lazy to comb her hair; she takes up her golden hairpin and inserts it, and that is all.
Generally speaking, it is because her natural form and bones are so excellent that she is elegant even without applying rouge or powder."
Chan Master Kengtang Yanchong of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an was the son of the Sheng family of Yuqian.
In his youth, he relied upon Master Yikan of Mingkong Monastery as his teacher. He first studied under Dayu Hongzhi and Zhengtang Dayuan. Later, he heard Donglin say to the assembly:
"In this place of mine, there is nothing else mysterious or subtle; there is only gruel made of wood shavings and rice made of iron nails—enjoy them as you please."
[The Master] chewed [the words]. The Teacher secretly rejoiced in this. He went directly to pay his respects and set forth his insights and understanding.

Lin said, "Based on your point of view, you are sitting right within the realm of reflective awareness. The Teacher’s doubts did not cease; he cast away everything he had previously acquired all at once.
One day, he heard a monk cite Nanquan’s saying: "When people of this age see this single flower, it is like being in a dream. Thereupon, he silently attained something.
Jue said, "Striking the grass is only intended to startle the snake. The next day, when entering the room, Lin asked, "Where is it that Yantou secretly revealed his meaning?
The Master said, "Today I have caught this old thief red-handed. Lin said, "The life of the Great Master Bodhidharma rests in your hands.
As the Master was about to open his mouth, he was suddenly struck a fist to the chest. He attained great enlightenment immediately, such that—
Sweat poured down his back. Nodding his head, he said to himself, "When Linji said, 'Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is not much,' was that empty talk?
He then presented this verse: "To act for others, one must act thoroughly; To kill, one must see blood.
Deshan and Yantou— Ten thousand miles, a single line of iron. After Linran took up residence there, he ascended the hall and said: "The World-Honored One spoke what is not spoken; Kāśyapa..."
"Leaves do not hear hearing. [Xuedou] struck the meditation staff and said: "Where do the yellow leaves come from as they drift in the water?
A cow with crows perched upon it passes through a distant village. Ascending the hall, he raised the case: Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying, "The entire earth is this gate of liberation.
Why, then, cannot one pull it open by the hand? The Master said, "Great Xuefeng has split his talk into two pieces. Since the entire earth is..."
"What is the use of dragging this gate of liberation? He ascended the hall and said: "If you go on exclusively like this, the grass before the Dharma Hall will grow a fathom deep.
If you come back exclusively like this, the mud underfoot will be three feet deep. Tell me, what then is the way? Every third year there is an intercalary month;
the rooster cries at the fifth watch. He ascended the hall and cited: "The late Master Wan’an said: 'Sitting upon the Buddha’s seat.'"
He hacked at the Buddha’s feet; he showed no reverence for Confucius, the Master of his own house, yet went abroad to practice ritual and music.

The Teacher said: “To enter the mud and the water—there is nothing that the former Master cannot do. Yet, alas, the cold cicada clings to the withered tree; its weeping is exhausted, but it does not turn back.”
Zhuo leaned on his staff and said, "It is evident that there are those who do not turn their heads back. "Ningci will offer you three prostrations from within this incense burner," he said.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Buddhas of the three periods speak of existence within non-existence—like picking up a needle from a heap of flowers.

The Patriarchs of the six generations seek non-existence within existence—like a monkey reaching for the moon reflected in water. Setting aside these two paths, how can one discuss and realize the truth? As for us..."
He manages the affairs of rise and fall; all day long, he occupies himself with the clouds over Lake Dongting. Yuan’an, having accepted the invitation of Zhìzhě, took the seat and said:
"On South Mountain there is an old Demon King. His piercing eyes flash with lightning; his mouth is like a blood-basin as he scolds the Buddhas and Patriarchs;
his teeth are like sword-trees as he reviles the various quarters. Several times the gale of karma has blown against him, yet he remains unmoved. But when it blows him away—clouds turn yellow!"
At Mount Pan, he and Sengtou-tuo and Master Fu shared a single fire to break down a door.
It was just like the old Meng Bala, who deceived countless foolish men and women; with eyes wide open, they entered the boiling cauldron in full view.

Suddenly, if a monk were to come forth and ask, "Since you are a *kalyāṇamitra*, why did you deceive people into entering the boiling cauldron? one should simply say to him: "This is not within your realm."
[The text continues with] the *dhātu*. Later, he entered nirvana and was interred in a monastery south of the temple.

Chan Master Zhuan'en Zhenci of Zhiye Monastery in Wuzhou was a native of Tongchuan. His secular surname was Li. Initially, he relied upon Chengdu Zhengfa Monastery to renounce the householder’s life and receive full ordination.
Later, he traveled to lecture halls and listened to discourses on the *Awakening of Faith* (*Yuánjué*). When he reached the passage: "The four great elements are each separate; now..."
"This false body—where could it possibly reside? Ultimately, it has no substance; in reality, it is just like a magical illusion.
With this, he attained realization and composed a verse, saying: "A single bright pearl is here within me; Touch it or move it, and it emits light that shakes the earth.
He presented this to various lecturers, but none were able to understand it. He returned home and presented it to his own teacher, who then brought up the "dog has no Buddha-nature" koan.
The master pressed him on this point, saying, "Even hundreds of thousands of ten-thousands of koans do not go beyond this verse. The teacher considered this insolence and dismissed him with a shout.
Consequently, the master traveled south and took up residence at Yuan Tong on Mount Lu. At that time, Wan’an was the West Hall Master;
he entered the room for the assembly and raised the following case: A monk asked Yunmen, "When one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha, what then? Yunmen said—
[The monk] said, "Even the Buddha is a dust-mote. As soon as [the Master] heard these words, he shouted and pointed at his chest, saying, "Even the Buddha is a dust-mote.

The Master then composed a verse: "Pushing away dust to see the Buddha—the Buddha too is a dust-mote. Question finished, answer finished; turn yourself around right here and now. I urge you to drink one more cup of wine;
once you have passed the Yang Pass to the west, there will be no old friends left. He further composed a verse on the Samādhi of Dust-to-Dust: [Verse omitted in source].
Rice in the bowl, water in the bucket; a discerning Kunlun sits at the bottom of the abyss. Upon a single mote of dust, Mount Sumeru runs upward.
A clear-eyed Persian laughs and snaps his fingers. As he laughs and snaps his fingers, a pure breeze rises from the branches of the coral tree.
Wan-an deeply approved of this.
Chan Master Shao Yuan of Zhaojue in Chengdu Prefecture ascended the hall and said: A monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall?
Yunmen replied, "The golden wind reveals its essence. The Master said: "To understand the mechanism of falling into the tiger's trap, one must be a patch-robed monk of genuine substance.
Great Master Yunmen possessed the samādhi that transcends the common herd; he struck the joints and knocked upon the gates within a flash of insight."
From amidst a flash of lightning, a single hand emerges to untangle the sticky and remove the bonds for people, pulling out wedges and extracting nails—a truly skilled hand indeed.
Yet, if one examines this closely, it is much like lending a ladder to a thief. Zhaojue was not so;
when a monk suddenly asked, "What is it like when the tree withers and the leaves fall? he simply replied to him: "The setting clouds and the solitary wild goose fly together."
"The autumn waters share the same color as the vast sky. Tell me, is this the same as Yunmen’s [teaching], or is it different? He further said: "Cease, cease!
There is no need to speak; my wondrous Dharma is inconceivable."
Chan Master Mu’an An Yong of Gushan, Fuzhou, was a dharma successor of Chan Master Xun of Xichan. He was the son of the Wu family from Min County.

Having become a monk at the age of twenty, he soon visited Lan’an at Yunmen. One day, upon entering the inner chamber for instruction, Lan’an said: “I do not ask about words; I do not ask about no-words.”
He said, "World-Honored One. After a long silence, [Zhaozhou] realized that he could not meet the World-Honored One while He remained silent; he then followed him and gave a shout.

Suddenly, he attained awakening and prostrated, saying, "Had I not questioned you today, how would I have lost the opportunity before my eyes? Zhaozhou granted him permission. Later, when he ascended the hall, he said:
"To clarify this matter, one must possess the skill of the spark struck from flint and the flash of lightning; only then can one..."
On the precipitous peak of the crag, one lets go of everything; in the depths of the white clouds, one attains great stability.
If you peer into the ground searching for a golden needle, your skull must split right open.

At this point, even if you could adapt according to the situation and avoid the sharp edge of the blade, being entirely liberated would still involve wading through mud and water. As for that single phrase of the fundamental function held up in its entirety—how about it?
"How would you say it? [The Master] struck the whisk and said: "A flash of seven-star light, brilliant and dazzling; having mastered the art of wielding it, one may roam freely throughout the world.
Ascending the hall, he raised an example, citing Muzhou’s instruction to the assembly: "If you have not yet attained an entrance, you must attain an entrance.
Once you have attained an entrance, you must not forget me, the old monk. The Master said: "Speaking in such a manner..."
"How thick is the skin? A wooden hermitage is not like this. You all have not yet attained a point of entry; you must attain a point of entry.
Once you have attained a point of entry, you must cast that very point of entry away before you can succeed. [The Master] ascended the hall, took up his staff, and said:
Linji, that little fellow, has never spoken directly to the point. Today he lets loose his whole being in feigned innocence, wishing for everyone to know that there is something more.
He threw down his staff and descended from the seat. A monk asked, "What is it like when one turns over and stands upside down atop Mount Sumeru?
The Master said, "I have never seen the Morning Star appear. The monk said, "In that case, the mountain torrents will overflow and the peaks will topple."
The Master said, "Do not act recklessly. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "The sound of thunder is vast, yet there are no drops of rain.
Zen Master Nanya of Longxiang Baitang in Wenzhou ascended the hall and said: "Upon the summit of Rui Peak, by the Phoenix Pavilion, we rely on each other with a bowl of plain congee.
With our heads covered by a hundred-seam robe, we sit in meditation. The Second Patriarch paid three prostrations and remained in his place."
To establish this has already been thoroughly covered. Old Dharma—the bald barbarian—has exhausted his marrow and skin; it was a scene of total disorder.
As for the rest of such types, what is there to say? When Potaṅga speaks thus, will he escape the censure of the various quarters? Or not?

Striking the meditation bench, he said: "It would have been better to let the prisoner remain so that his wisdom might grow. He ascended the hall and said: "The great capacity values directness; the great function values sudden manifestation.
Even if there were a 'biting the arrowhead' capacity, it must be struck down with a single blow. Why? Because within the armory of our King, there is no such blade. He ascended the hall and said:
"Purple ferns stretch out their fists as bamboo shoots break through the tips; the willow blossoms have flown away, and the green shadows interlace."
This is clearly the single-line transmission of the Western Patriarch: the yellow oriole sings as it settles in its nest.

If you can see this here and believe it with certainty, then according to the standards of other quarters, you would surely be settled beneath a bright window. But in the school of Longxiang, we simply strike them dead with a single blow of the mallet.
Why? It is not that we find it difficult to dwell together with others; rather, for the most part, the distinction between the ordained and the laity must be made clear.
Chan Master Tianwang Zhiqing of Fuzhou ascended the hall. Holding up his whisk, he said: "This very thing cannot be covered by heaven, nor can it be supported by earth.
It pervades the world and pervades space; it forms a mass and forms a lump. Reaching this point, where can the Buddhas of the three periods of time go to search for it?
Where can the Patriarchs of the six generations go to grasp it? All you patch-robed monks under heaven..."
Monk, where would you find "reaching out"? Unless one attains realization for oneself, one cannot simultaneously practice both "striking" and "singing.
Even so, this is not yet the place where a patch-robed monk walks. What, then, is the place where a patch-robed monk walks?
"Casting one's body across the sea of right and wrong; walking freely through the thicket of jackals and tigers."
The Master of the Anfen Hermitage at Jianmen in Nanjian Prefecture had, in his youth, studied under Mukan at Anguo Temple alongside others.

Later, he relied upon Lan’an, yet he had not yet attained profound realization. He took leave of his teacher to visit Dahuai of Jing Mountain; while traveling along the Jiangyu River, he gazed up at the imperial palaces.
Hearing the street official shout, "The Minister is coming," he was suddenly and completely enlightened. He composed a verse, saying: "For many years this matter has hung in my breast;
I have questioned all quarters, yet my eyes remained unopened. Now, liver and gall are both rent asunder— A single cry:
'The Minister comes upon the river! He then went straight back to Xichan. Lanna welcomed him and bestowed upon him the *kāṣāya*. From that time on, he no longer followed formal regulations.
Yu later lived as a hermit at Jianmen, where his transformative influence spread throughout the regions south of the passes. Students followed him;
the gāthās and verses he composed were produced spontaneously by the hand, totaling over a thousand pieces that circulated widely in the world. Addressing the assembly, he said:
"As for this very field of land, you all—tell me, before heaven and earth were yet divided, where was it? To penetrate directly [to this] is already dull.

Set it aside. You have already exhausted the capacity of the senior monks (upādhyāya). If you were to further deliberate or reflect upon it, it would be no less than ten thousand miles of white clouds.

Suddenly, he took up his staff, dispersed the assembly, and addressed them: "From the Buddhas above down to all sentient beings below, their very lives are entirely in the hands of this mountain monk.
If one were to examine this thoroughly, there would be immeasurable transgressions. Is there anyone who can examine [this]?"
"Is this it? He struck his staff once and said, "The wrongdoer has a head; the debt has an owner.
He then looked left and right and said, "Since coming out of the cave, there has been no rival hand. Where one can yield to another, one should yield. He addressed the assembly:
"Before the fifteenth day, all the stars in heaven bow toward the North Star. After the fifteenth day, among humans, there is no water that does not flow toward the sea."
"East! Both what has come before and what follows after are entirely cast aside. The local dialects differ in every place. Then, counting on his fingers, he said:
"One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen.
Brothers, what is today's date? After a long silence, he said: "In our shop, we do not sell anything on credit for even a single coin."
Chan Master Zongdai of Gushan, Fuzhou, a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Dongchan Yue, ascended the hall and said: "The World-Honored One said: 'One should know thus; one should see thus.'"
Understanding it thus, he did not give rise to the notion of dharmas. He then shouted, saying: "Jade is originally without flaw, yet it has flaws.

Chan Master Shiguan Zhishi of Gushan in Fuzhou addressed the assembly, citing the story of Caoshan’s “not as good” remark, and offered this verse: Jade is originally without flaw, yet it has flaws; The moon is naturally bright, yet there is a shadow. If you wish to see the Buddha-nature, Look at the face of the person before you.
Caoshan is not as beautiful as the flower’s root; he is not as beautiful as Caoshan himself. The tiger’s body is naturally striped.
It is warm in Jiangnan, cold in the northern frontier. A handful of willow threads cannot be gathered; they are draped with mist upon the jade balustrade.
Chan Master Zongying of Qianyuan in Fuzhou, a successor of Chan Master Jing of Xichan, ascended the hall. He struck his staff and said, "A man of impatient temperament needs only one blow.
He leaned on the staff and said, "A person of keen intelligence need not have it mentioned twice. Is there anyone here now who is so keen?"
After a long silence, he said, "Even the hare that compared itself to the mythical beast *zhānglín* never met its match.

This was said regarding the lay practitioner Wu Shisang of Mount Xiánzhou in Jian’ing Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Kaiśan Qiān, who constantly used his own spiritual affairs to question various Chan masters until he reached Kai[śan].

"Excellent," [Zhaozhou] said. He then settled in a thatched hut to the left of Xuanzhao’s quarters and went to serve him. On the eighth day of the third month in the Gengshen year of the Xiangshi era, he suddenly attained enlightenment.
He composed a verse and presented it to Xuanzhao, saying: "Originally there were no seams or gaps; Upon being touched, it immediately shines forth.
Since this is a treasure worth a thousand pieces of gold, Why need one use it to shoot at a sparrow? Xuanzhao replied: "The moment it snaps like a 'chui'—how truly joyful! To die..."
Ordinary beings and sages alike sink into the same stillness; beneath Mount Xianzhou, he laughs "he-he. He does not fail the heart we pledged to one another long ago.
Chan Master Miaofeng Zhi of Lingyin Temple in Lin’an Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yuwang Guang. Born into the Liu family of Huzhou, he received the tonsure at the age of thirteen.

Upon seeing a single passage from a sutra or treatise, he immediately grasped its essential meaning. He studied under Fozhao at Mount Mao, where [Fozhao] tested him with the "wind and banner" dialogue—a direct, arrow-pointing pivot of the teaching—and certified him with this verse:
"Today I have opened a single thread for you; Cut through the nails and sever the iron to revive my school."
He subsequently entered Mount Kuanglu, where he planted his staff and sat facing a blank wall for ten years at Miaogao Peak. Later, he resided first at Huíyīn and finally at Línghyìn.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Responding to things and manifesting form is like the moon in water; picked up with a casual hand, it is revealed all at once."

At the moment of death, karma-consciousness is vast and boundless; let the various quarters of the world speculate as they please. Thereupon, he passed away.
Chan Master Kongcou Zongyin of Yuyang in Qingyuan Prefecture cited this case: A monk asked Changsha, "What is the sphere of activity for those of the highest caliber?

I, Zen Master Jie, shall tear my own face to pieces; I cannot avoid suffering a defeat here, so that all quarters may examine it. He then called to the assembly.
It is said: "This old woman’s inner chamber is deep and secure, impenetrable as a sealed vessel; yet she scatters flowers upon withered trees and kindles flames within cold crags.

"A shout is like a probing rod or a blade of grass in the shadow," he said. The Master replied, "Neither in front nor behind. [The monk] asked, "How is it that one shout does not function as a single shout?
The Master said, "You must investigate it further before you can understand. [The monk] said, "A probing rod or a blade of grass is used to test those who come."
"A single shout must cause the seas and mountains to darken; were it not for one who is a true son of the Dharma King, who would dare to tread upon his gate?
The Master said, 'For now, proceed slowly. Ascending the hall, he said: "The mind is the root, and dharmas are the dust; these two are like scars upon a mirror.
Once the mirror is broken, the dharmas no longer exist. [He recited: "Sparse shadows slant across the shallow, clear water; a faint fragrance drifts as the moon turns yellow."
Dusk. Because I saw them playing puppet theater, I have ascended the hall [to speak]. Ghost faces and god heads are pulled by strings; god heads and ghost faces pull the strings.
How many of those who watch and observe take them for beautiful ladies in red powder?
On the stage, there is a wondrous dance, and in their hands they hold light silk white fans. This mountain monk cannot help but pull back the curtain for you all.

"Depart! Zhuo leaned on his staff and said, "A clever monk sees it at the very first glance. He ascended the hall and said: "The white ox in the open field is pitch black; one cannot find it anywhere.
The mountains are green and the waters are blue—seeming to exist, yet as if non-existent. Seen by the eyes and heard by the ears, it is dim and indistinct.
When one does not look for it at all, the hooves and horns remain; the moment one stirs, its tracks have already vanished."
Under the moon, I idly play the short flute; before the wind, I need no longer hold the long reins. Hehehe! How extraordinary! Now, though one tries to follow, he will not go;
he is free and easy in the east, west, south, and north. Without restriction, he lifts the incense and says:
"Everyone says the former master died today; who knew it was his birthday? I do not know what evidence there is for this. Purple...

He burned the cypress, yellow sandalwood, and other woods together. He wrote a true eulogy and entrusted it to Gaofeng, saying: "The Great Master is now without anyone [to succeed him]; Xueyan knows the proper etiquette.
He then entrusted the original manuscript to Attendant Yuanmiao, saying: "Empty fame fills the heavens and earth."
Chan Master Bieshan Zuozhi of Tiantong in Mingzhou was the son of the Yang family of Shunqing.

At the age of fourteen, he received full ordination. Hearing a monk recite the words of Sixyan, he was filled with joy; at that time, Sixyan was residing at Qionglung in Suzhou, so he went there immediately to follow him.
Later, he met Wuzhun at Xuedou. Recognizing him as a vessel for the Dharma, Wuzhun treated him with even greater severity, occasionally striking him with the staff or shouting "Katsu! at him.

He did not spare a single word of censure. As the Master prepared to respond, he was suddenly silenced and unable to utter a word; through this, his intellectual understanding was completely lost. After some time, he said:
"All the skills I have cultivated throughout my life were but dead methods; it is only now that I have seen this old man that I have begun to walk upon the path of life.

Subsequently, when Zhuan moved to Jingshan, he ordered the Master to share the seat with him. In the Bingchen year of the Baoyu era, he received an imperial decree to reside at Tiantong. [With] but a single bag...
He lived in a hut made of bound straw. Once, he ascended the hall and raised this case: Mazu Gu asked Linji, "Of the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion, which one is the True Eye?
Linji said, "Of the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion, which one is the True Eye? Speak quickly! Speak quickly!"
Tang stepped forward, pulled Linji down from his meditation seat, and sat back down himself. As Linji stepped forward and said, "How do you do?
Tang hesitated, whereupon Linji gave a shout, pulled him down from the seat again, and sat back down. Tang then went out. The Master said: "The midnight hour when two bands of thieves meet;
They scramble for the banners and seize the drums to gain the advantage. Suddenly, at dawn, they encounter one another again— Their faces covered in shame."

They each returned to their quarters. On the first day of the ninth month, the gengchen day, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The clouds are thin and the moonlight is fresh; the trees have shed their leaves, and the mountain’s bones are exposed.

Since heaven and earth first came into being, how many have had eyes that truly see? To those who asked for instruction, the Master said: "I cannot wait to meet you again; each of you must exert yourselves.
Ten days later, at the hour of midnight, after giving instructions on his final affairs, he folded his hands and passed away.
Chan Master Huanxi’s verse on the saying “Mind is Buddha” says: “Mind is Buddha—arsenic and wolfsbane!
To raise the dead and restore life, it takes no more than a single dose.”
Chan Master Duanqiao Miaolun of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou was the son of the Xu family of Huangyan in Taizhou.

Initially, he visited Guyuan at Ruiyan Monastery and encountered the "three pounds of flax" koan, which left him in doubt. Later, while reading the *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra*, he came across the passage concerning mosquitoes, insects, and ants.
Without the use of words, he was able to accomplish his task and attained a sudden realization. Next, he visited Wuzhun at Xuedou.
Wuzhun asked him, "Why does a dog have karmic consciousness? and commanded the Master to provide a response. He offered thirty variations of answers without success. The Master said:

"Is there no expedient means? he asked. Zhenjing answered him with a verse. The Master stood in rapt attention; after a long while, hearing the sound of the wooden board, sweat broke out over his entire body, and he was suddenly liberated from all intellectual views.
He emerged into the world at Jiyuan, moved to Ruiyan and Guoqing, and finally reached Jingci. There, ascending the hall, he said:
"In the mountains of Jing there is jade, yet the one who obtains it does not remain in the mountains of Jing. In the waters of Chi there is a pearl, yet it is picked up [by one who goes elsewhere]."
"He is not at the Red Water. Zen monks possess the True Person of No-Rank; for those who have realized this, their coming and going do not occur through the face-gate.
[The Master] suddenly picked up his staff, held it horizontally across his chest, and asked, "Do you understand? A stone man crouches at the mouth of the River in Youzhou.
He then ascended the hall and recounted how Yongming Qian first visited Fayan. Fayan asked, "Aside from your formal inquiries, what sutra are you studying? Qian replied, "The *Avataṃsaka*..."
Yan’yan said, “The six characteristics—totality and particularity, identity and difference, formation and disintegration—to which category do they belong?

Qian replied, “All phenomena, both mundane and supramundane, possess these six characteristics. Yan’yan asked, “Does emptiness also possess the six characteristics? Qian was unable to respond. Yan’yan said:
"Why do you not ask? Xuanque asked. "Is emptiness endowed with the six characteristics? Wuzhuo said, "Emptiness. Xuanque attained awakening.
Wuzhuo asked, "How do you understand this? Xuanque said, "Emptiness. Wuzhuo approved. The Master said: "Emptiness, oh emptiness! It has no front or back."
Picking it up, he suddenly split it into two pieces; he carried them to the corner of Nanping Mountain. For ten thousand generations, few have seen them.
Do you wish to see them? He drew a circle with his whisk and said: "The golden crow flies onto the crystal palace.

At the time of his death, he gathered the assembly, entered his room, and wrote a letter bidding farewell to the various mountains as well as the Duke of Wei. The Duke sent an envoy to inquire, saying: "The Master has passed away..."
Tiantai. For what reason did he die at Jingci? The Master said: "The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night. Having written this verse, he passed away.
Zen Master Xiyuan Hui of Tiantong in Mingzhou addressed the assembly, citing: "Jinpeak was asked by a monk: 'This body is without...'"
"Know! Like earth, wood, tiles, or stones. What does this mean? Under Feng’s meditation seat, he twisted a monk’s ear.
The monk, suffering the pain, made a sound. Feng said, "Today, for the first time, I have caught hold of an ignorant fellow.
The monk bowed and departed. Feng called out, "Acarya! The monk turned his head. Feng said, "If you go into the hall, you must not mention this. The monk asked, "Why? Feng—
[The Master] said: "Many people laugh at the 'old woman’s heart' of Jinfeng. The Teacher said: "A small boat cuts through the morning river clouds;
a single song of high melody sends you off into the distance. Startling the wild ducks on the bank, they fly away across the sea and sky, no longer in their flock."

A verse on the Sixth Patriarch’s discourse regarding the transmission of the robe says: He did not become a woodcutter, but became a miller; He used only his physical strength to test for refinement or coarseness.
Whether he knew he had trodden upon it or not, The rice and the husks alike reached the alms bowl.
Master Chan Yuepo Ming cited a monk who asked Zihu: "Since ancient times, have the supreme sages attained the true principle?

Zihu replied, "They have. The monk asked, "How do they attain the true principle? Zihu said, "Who was it that wrote the treaty for Huo Guang when he sold a counterfeit silver city to the Xiongnu? The monk was speechless. The Master composed a verse: In his hand...
The silken threads roll up and then unfurl; a small boat ripples across Lake Dongting. Suddenly, the fierce waves overturn the void;
gathered back, there is not a single skill remaining.
Master Xishi Tan cited this: A monk asked Nanquan, "When the Master returns to his chamber, what will he point to as guidance?
Nanquan said, "Last night at the third watch, I lost my ox; when I rose at dawn, I had lost my fire. The verse says: With servile faces and cringing knees, one runs through the world;
Ashamed to see him in sheepskin robes on the Qili滩 (Qili Rapids). Though Emperor Wen-shu is noble as a Son of Heaven, Zi-ling remains a man of the common people.
View this as a look at an old friend.
Master Ning, known as Tui-geng of Lingyin in Hangzhou, ascended the hall and said: "After the rains, the mountain colors before one's eyes are verdant;

amidst the seats, the wind is warm and the birds' songs are clamorous. He struck the meditation seat once and said: "It is laughable that the Old Barbarian (Bodhidharma) lacked the wisdom of transformation. Shaoshi..."
Sitting before the peak for nine years, he ascended the hall and said: "A thousand peaks stretch to the horizon, locked in emerald green; the sky is filled with willow catkins drifting like cotton.
Alas, the True Man of No Rank has been sleeping under the dew and lodging in the grass all along. *Ayya!* This spring watches another pass away; when will it be the year of our return?"

Chan Master Yujie Hui of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Lingyin Xun. He went to study under Shitian, who brought up the "Seventh Case" of Yunmen, for which no one could provide a response.
Suddenly, as a monk stepped across the threshold, Shitian said, "Xuefeng rolls the ball. Hearing this, the Master attained realization while standing by his side.
He spoke in verse: "Yunmen’s 'Seventh of the Month'; Xuefeng’s 'Rolling the Ball. White artemisia and red smartweed; the bright moon and a solitary boat. Tianwei approved this.
Zen Master Xuewu Ke of Zhongzhu in Hangzhou ascended the hall and said: "Withered mulberry trees know the wind from heaven; the sea knows the tide."

"Cold! Now tell me: what does this patch-robed monk know? He knows that rice is made from grain. Even if one knows as much as that, there will come a day when Old King Yama demands the price for the meal.
In the inscription for the First Patriarch, he said: "A single reed cuts across the current; his profound mind is unfathomable.
The land of Liang enjoyed peace, while the state of Wei harbored a thief. The Master, seeing that the throne of the Song dynasty had already shifted, immediately resigned from his monastic duties.

Chan Master Jue of Mount Jinshan, Moe’an, already knew the Master well. At that time, as the Yuan troops were descending upon Jiangnan, Moe’an was taken into the command tent of the Generalissimo Bayan and placed within his inner circle.
They traveled together to Wulin. Moe’an spoke to Bayan, requesting that the Master take up residence at Lingyin Monastery.
He personally carried the letter of invitation to the Master’s door. The Master pulled back the bolt of the gate and revealed half his face, asking: "Who are you?"
"Who is it? An asked. "It is a certain person from my old acquaintance," he replied. The Master closed the gate, saying, "I do not know you.

Although the Master lived beyond the secular world, he maintained his integrity through loyalty and principle; thus, he felt no need for the summons from Lingyin. Later, Chan Master Duang Jiang En praised him, saying:
"Forty years have passed since the Snow Hut is no more, yet his lofty spirit remains as stern as ever."—Prime Minister Buyan.
He prostrated beneath the meditation platform. He was unwilling to come to Cold Spring for his sake.
Zen Master Xingchuan Ruogong of Mount Yuyang in Mingzhou, a successor of Zen Master Nong of Tiantong, addressed the assembly. He cited the story of Xuansha regarding the three types of sick people.
The Verse says: Employing many indirect means to test those who are masters— Who has ever personally seen the ancient Xuan Sha? Deaf in his ears, mute in his mouth, and blind in his eyes;
Sentient beings in this age of five turbidities are as numerous as sesame seeds. Night Session: Shaoshi has no gates or doors; how can one immediately gain passage?
Standing patiently at nightfall, listen as I speak of the East and West.
Chan Master Xing Gong of Shilin at Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou ascends the hall and says: "The mountains are still and the bees gather pollen with heavy thighs;
The forest is empty and the bamboo shoots reveal their bright flesh within their sheaths. Leaning on the railing, I am unaware that I have become dazed; Then a yellow oriole calls out once more."
If Sike had spoken thus, he would have deserved thirty blows of the staff. Why? Because he was unfit to follow after sounds and pursue forms.
Entering the hall, he raised this case: "Xuefeng was burning fire inside the monks' hall; having closed both the front and back doors, he then cried out:"
"Extinguish the fire! Extinguish the fire! Xuansha took a piece of firewood and threw it through the lattice window.
Feng immediately opened the door. The Master said: "A high-burning log warms the whole body; its joy is difficult to contain, like spring in every room.

Had it not been for the arrival of Master Xie to join the fire, who would have known there was a person shivering outside the gate? He ascended the hall and said: "In the land of waters, the water is vast and the ground is damp. Six...
The moon-flower mosquito’s proboscis is like iron; rising at midnight, it causes endless vexation. What is the use of this endless vexation?
There is a fan on the head of the bed; for no reason, it has been broken again.
Chan Master Xuzhou Pudu of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou was a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Huazang Tong. He was a native of the Shi family of Jiangdu. He went to visit Wu’ai, who asked him:
"Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as companions? The Master said, "An iron Kunlun under a golden incense burner.
A monk asked, "I thought this short man had some merit; it turns out his understanding is only like this. The Master bowed and said, "Thank you, Preceptor, for your testimony.
Later, while presiding over the assembly in the Dharma hall, he said: "The myriad dharmas are the radiance of the mind; all conditions are only the awakening of nature. Originally there is none..."
For those who are deluded or awakened, it is enough to realize this very day. Since there is no one who is deluded or awakened, what is there to realize?

(He plants his staff upright and says: "A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands; they merely follow the warbling orioles over the low wall. Ascending the hall, he cites the story of the World-Honored One pointing to his chest and showing it to the assembly.
He offers this verse: At the twin śāla trees, he points to his chest with his hand; Speaking of existence and discussing non-existence, he is unrestrained and liberated.
Emptiness. If one were to say that Gautama once entered extinction, it would be a mistaken teaching—a bird crying out and laughing at the spring breeze.

In the Dingshou year of the Zhiyuan era, he was summoned to Mount Jingshan. Finding the mountain in the aftermath of a fire, he resolved to restore it; as his efforts were nearing completion, he suddenly manifested a slight ailment.

He asked for his brush and wrote in large characters: "Eighty-two years, I have steered the bottomless boat; now I tread it over and return. The bright moon fills the sky. Having cast down his brush, he passed away.
He passed away.
Chan Master Jue’an Zhen of Chengtian Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Xuedou Qian, had a Huayan lecturer who, carrying an imperial mandate, was about to replace him.
He established a lecture hall. The Master said, "If you can expound on Chan, I shall follow your lead; if I cannot expound on the teachings, you may take my place.
Thereupon, he beat the drum and ascended the hall, entering the five teachings with a single shout to reveal the ultimate point—the crown jewel of a thousand sages—of our school.
The lecturer wept and prostrated himself in repentance before withdrawing.

Chan Master Xutang Zhiyu of Jing Mountain in Lin’an Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Daochangyan. He was a native of Siming. Once, while presiding over the assembly, he raised an old case:
When Xuedou was residing at Cuifeng, several monks arrived. Xuedou asked, "New arrivals, is that so? They replied, "Yes. Xuedou said, "Go to the meditation hall. The monks...
Just as he was walking away, Dou called out again, "Come, come! The monk turned his head back. Dou said, "It is rare for a master monk to reach Lake Dongting; I will give you a cup of tea to drink.
The Master replied, "The sentence for entering the gate has already been answered; calling me away and summoning me back is a secondary matter.
Those who do not know the taste of the tea upon reaching this place are merely wandering about in vain, buying boats on Lake Dongting. The Master first resided at Jing...
Compassion. A celestial messenger delivered a message inquiring: "Zhaozhou was eighty years old when he went on pilgrimage; why did Xutang remain in the mountains until he was eighty?

The Master cited the story of Zhaozhou’s pilgrimage to Linji and offered this verse: Zhaozhou was eighty before he set out on his travels; Xutang was eighty before he returned to dwell in the mountains.
There is another function that expands upon the Buddhas and Patriarchs; Within the nine-layered capital, it moves the countenance of the Dragon.
The messenger returned with this verse, and the Emperor was greatly pleased; he bestowed upon him most generous gifts. The Master once gave this informal instruction in his room:
"Why is it that those whose own eyes are not yet clear take empty space and wear it as trousers? Why is it that those who draw lines on the ground to make a prison [remain there]?"
Those who fail to penetrate this matter are like those who enter the sea to count its sands. Why? Because they stand on tiptoe upon the point of a needle.
Chan Master Shifan Yan of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou addressed the assembly, citing a case: A monk asked Baizhang, "What is the true person of Baizhang?
Baizhang descended from his meditation seat and stood with his hands folded. The monk then asked, "What is the true person of the Master? Baizhang sat back down. [The Master] offered a verse:
It is said: An old woman applies her makeup, staining her lips vermilion; before others, she displays her own fine spirit.
Her frowning brows and cold smiles are most striking, yet she pays no heed to those nearby who cover their noses.
Chan Master Shixi Xin Yue of Mount Jing in Lin’an Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Jinshan Kai. He was a native of Meizhou. A monk asked: "What is the Buddha?"
The Master said, "A short man watching a play. He ascended the hall and, citing Mazu’s instruction to the assembly—“Whatever words or phrases are spoken belong to the school of Deva;
take this as the primary principle”—the Master said, “Like jade turning and pearls rolling, look with clear eyes. Where there is involvement, there is no involvement.
Simply take this as the primary principle. He let out a shout and said, “A single sword leans against the heavens, and the stars and constellations tremble.”

Cold. Recorded by Chan Master Jingci Jianweng Jing of Hangzhou, successor to Chan Master Chong of Mount Jingshan. Yunmen addressed the assembly, saying: "Awaken to the Way through sound; see [the Way]..."
Shexian Mingxin then raised his hand and said, "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva buys sesame cakes with money. Lowering his hand, he said, "It turns out they are actually steamed buns.
The Master composed a verse: Who is it that plays this tune before the wind? Its melody is so sublime, who would deign to join it in these times?
Seeing no one understands the meaning within the song, He takes up his cloud-flute once more and blows it deliberately.
Chan Master Beishan Long’s verse on the story of Niaoke blowing on a tuft of cloth says: An eighty-year-old old man still insists on physical exertion;
The tuft of cloth is blown up, and calamity is reborn. A man who has shed blood for three thousand miles— An old monk upon the branch of a withered tree.

Chan Master Gaofeng Yuanmiao of West Tianmu Peak in Hangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Yangshan Qin of the twenty-first generation under Nanyue. He was a native of Wujiang in Suzhou; his secular surname was Xu. His mother...
Zhou Shi dreamed that a gaunt monk boarded her boat to stay the night, and she subsequently gave birth. From childhood, she delighted in sitting in meditation (dhyāna).
At the age of fifteen, she followed Fazhu at Miyin Temple in Jiahe and shaved her head. At twenty-two, she requested instruction from Duangqiao Lun, who commanded her to investigate the koan:
"From where does life come? To where does death go? Subsequently, she visited Xueyan at Beijian; as soon as she had exchanged greetings and offered incense, Xueyan—
He immediately struck him out. Thereafter, whenever anyone entered the gate, Yunyan would ask, "Who has brought this corpse here for you?
Before the sound of these words had even faded, Yunyan would likewise strike them out. One day, seeing the eulogy for Master Wuzu Faian, he read: "In a hundred years, thirty-six thousand mornings;
turning it over and over, it is originally just this fellow. Suddenly, he shattered his doubts regarding the corpse. At that time—
Yan was staying at Nanming. The Master went to visit him. Yan asked, "Who brought this corpse here for you? The Master gave a shout. Yan raised his staff;
the Master seized it and said, "You cannot strike me today. Yan asked, "Why can you not be struck? The Master shook out his sleeves and departed.
Yan subsequently went to Tianning, and the Master attended him there as an attendant. One day, Yan—
Question: "During the vast expanse of the day, can you maintain mastery? The Master said, "I maintain mastery. Question: "In the midst of sleep and dreams, can you maintain mastery?
The Master said, "I maintain mastery. Question: "When one is fast asleep—without dreams, without thoughts, without seeing, and without hearing—where is the master?
The Master was speechless. Yan instructed him, saying: "From this day forward, I do not require you..."
In studying the Buddha and the Dharma, you need not exhaust yourself investigating the past or the present; simply eat when hungry and sleep when weary.
As soon as you wake from sleep, shake off your lethargy and ask: "Where, ultimately, does this master of mine—the one who just woke up—dwell and establish his life?
The Master then resolved to enter Longxu, traveling for five years until he met a companion with whom he stayed overnight.

As he pushed his pillow off and it struck the floor with a sound, he attained great and sudden enlightenment. Later, when he moved to Shuangji Peak in Wukang, his quarters were so crowded that his door was filled with visitors' shoes;

he was unable to attend to them all. The Master fled by night to Lion Rock on the Western Tianmu Mountains, where he constructed a small hut shaped like a boat and inscribed it with the name "The Barrier of Death.
He severed all worldly ties and dismissed his attendants. He had three "Gates" (kuan) of teaching, and addressed the assembly, saying: "A person of ultimate penetration is fundamentally liberated..."
Regarding birth and death: for what reason does the life-faculty not cease? The public cases of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are but a single principle;
for what reason are there those who understand and those who do not? A great practitioner of the Way should follow the conduct of the Buddha; for what reason do they fail to observe the *vinaya*?

If one does not accord with the truth, one should refuse entry as if closing the door. In the Dingwei year of the Zhiyuan era, Xueyan sent a bamboo whisk and a dharma discourse; when these arrived, the assembly again...
He was invited to open the hall within the Stone Grotto. A monk asked, "What is the assembly where the ten directions gather together?
The Master said, "Dragons and snakes are mixed; ordinary people and sages intermingle. The monk asked, "What is it that each and every one studies as non-action?

The Master said, "The mouth swallows Buddhas and patriarchs; the eyes cover heaven and earth. The monk asked, "What is the field for selecting Buddhas? The Master said, "Ten thousand miles east and west, south..."

The monk from Beibakian asked, "What is it like to 'return home having passed the imperial examination of the emptiness of mind'? The Master said, "Moving one's countenance to reveal the ancient path; not falling into the trap of silence.
The monk said, "If that is so, then every word reveals the ultimate truth, and every phrase points toward the source. The Master said, "Where have you seen this? The monk gave a shout.
The Master said, "That too is like swinging a club to strike at the moon. The monk said, "Let us set aside this matter for a moment. But as for..."
"Today at West Peak, the assembly from the ten directions has gathered; the Field for Selecting Buddhas is opened. Ultimately, what auspicious signs are there?
The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, the great earth, and the myriad phenomena—sentient and insentient alike—all attain Buddhahood.

[The monk] asked, "If all have attained Buddhahood, why is it that this student does not attain Buddhahood? The Master said, "If you were to attain Buddhahood, how could you cause the great earth to attain Buddhahood?"
[The monk] asked, "Ultimately, where does the fault of the student lie? The Master said, "South of Xiang, north of Tan.
[The monk] asked, "Is it permissible to repent? The Master said, "Prostrate yourself. As soon as the monk prostrated, the Master said, "A lion bites; the Han dog chases after clods of earth.
He ascended the hall and said, "Last night in a dream I composed a verse; I shall recite it for the assembly. After a long pause, he said, "I have forgotten it."
He finished speaking. Suddenly picking up his staff, he said, "Does this staff remember? After a long silence, he said, "In the same pit, there is no different soil.

At Zhongxia, he ascended the hall and, brandishing his whisk, said, "If you realize it before forty-five days have passed, not only will you be able to consume ten thousand taels of gold daily, but you will also be able to respond to the offerings of the four worlds. Forty-five days...
Later, he was recommended for ordination. "Even a single thread of silk or a drop of water shall require you to pull the plow and drag the harrow to repay him.
He struck the meditation seat once and said: "Having passed through the place where the monkeys cry out on the cliffs of Ba, even one who is not a sorrowful person would break their heart.

He ascended the hall and said: "The mud ox at the bottom of the sea chews the moon as it runs; the stone tiger before the eaves sleeps while cradling its cubs; the iron snake drills into the Vajra-eye; Kunlun..."
"Riding an elephant, leading a heron. Within these four lines, there is one phrase that can kill and can give life, can release and can seize.
If you can discern it, I grant that your lifelong study of the Way is complete. Ascending the hall, he said: "The sun is at its peak, spring is already fading;
fallen petals drift away with the current. He took up his staff and said: "Upon the tip of this staff, a single dot of red—its fragrance..."
"Perfume pervades the realm, yet no one looks upon it. Great assembly, whether you look or do not look, let us stop for a moment.
In the end, where does it all return? He then cast down his staff and ascended the hall. "Outside the gate, there is a person who exhausts every stratagem wishing to enter, yet cannot enter.
Inside the gate, there is a person who employs every skillful means wishing to exit, yet cannot exit. Cannot exit. Cannot enter."
It is attained. Set that aside for now. But tell me: when the person outside the gate meets the person inside the gate, what then?
"Do not speak of your sorrows to one who is already sorrowful; to speak them to such a person would be to kill them with grief. When the robe and cap were presented, he ascended the hall:
Cutting Sichuan brocade, clipping Wu silk, Wearing white jade interspersed with gold. When it is forged into a single whole, Not even a needle can pierce it. The cross-stitch pattern...
At the point where the joints meet, the lines of the path are difficult to find. Although it is just like Xifeng, he takes the emptiness of all dharmas as his seat and uses his staff as his robe.
He says, "Can you still wear this? Leaning on his staff, he says, "The fragrance of heaven disperses its shadow upon the mossy stones;
the five-leaf flower blooms in the campaka grove. The Master’s appearance was ancient and his spirit was pure; his practice and realization were authentic and sincere. Monks and laypeople alike...

Everyone placed their palms together at their foreheads in praise, saying, "An ancient Buddha, a true spiritual friend. On the first day of the twelfth month in the year of Yiwu (1295), during the Yuanzhen era, he ascended the hall and said:
"For thirty years on West Peak, I have spoken falsely of Prajñā; my offenses fill the heavens.
