Due to delusive thoughts and attachments, they are bound by the shrouds and entanglements of affliction; Deluded, they take on bodies within the six realms and vainly endure the sufferings of the three miserable paths. I contemplate only the past..."
To show contempt for the Buddhas of the future is to harbor enmity toward the Buddhas; it may even lead to the slaughter and killing of sentient beings.

Failing to realize that the characteristics of sentient beings are entirely the Dharma-nature body, one fails to see that in the past there was the Bodhisattva Never-Disparaging, who prostrated to all and said, "I do not slight you;
you shall all become Buddhas. If one can keep in mind that oneself and others are equally future Buddhas, merit will increase in the present life.
“May you have blessings and long life; may you be born in the Buddha-lands in birth after birth. The Emperor, looking up with delight, asked: “The precept against killing is the way of the sages.
Please explain this for me. The Master replied: “There was once Emperor Renzong of the Song dynasty, who one day said to his ministers:”
"I am very hungry tonight," the Emperor said. "I am thinking of roasting a sheep. The ministers submitted, saying, "Your Majesty, why not issue an order to the relevant authorities to prepare it?
Renzong replied, "I am merely hungry at this moment; I fear that if I grant this, it will become a constant precedent. I would rather endure this temporary hunger than initiate an endless slaughter.
The princes all cried out, "Ten thousand years! The Emperor graciously accepted their advice and immediately received the Imperial Preceptor (Di-shi).

*Jie*. Chan Master Xianji Yun, a successor of Chan Master Yu of Mount Jing, cited the three turning words of the "Empty Hall" and composed a verse on them, which says: "Sewing up the void, calculating the sands to their end."
Drawing lines on the ground with a needle is one’s lifelong vocation; though heads are changed and faces renewed, no one sees it. How many times the spring breeze has blown the flowers down.
Master Baoye Yuan addressed the assembly, citing the story of Deshan’s staff upon entering the gate, and composed this verse: “Bright and pure under the clear sky...”

The heavens roar with thunder; ten thousand layers of iron mountains are all startled open. Reflecting on these days of scattered rain and gusty winds, how could such a "total presentation" have come to pass?
He further composed a verse on the saying that "the three minds cannot be found," which says: Last year, in the spring breeze, the swallows were many;
they arrived before the Qingming festival to their old nests. This year, the spring colors have returned by half; the curtains hang desolate and still.
[End of] the Preface.

Master Nanrong Sou, a successor in the Dharma lineage of Chan Master Yue of Mount Jing, addressed the assembly. He raised an example: Once, a scholar said to Zhaozhou, "The Master is an ancient Buddha."
Zhaozhou said, "The scholar is a new Tathāgata. The Master said, "The palace of the Broad Cold is pure and free of dust; you have already encountered him as his eight characters unfold.
There is no need to pluck the moon-plant in fragments; simply uproot it together with the tree at your leisure and bring it here."
Chan Master Mingben of Mount Zhongfeng in Hangzhou,

a descendant of the twenty-second generation of the Nanyue lineage and a dharma heir of Chan Master Gaofeng Miao, was born into the Sun family of Qiantang. His mother dreamed that a gate opened without a door.

As for Daozhe: he was born carrying a lantern to his home. His divine appearance was exceptionally extraordinary; as soon as he left the swaddling clothes, he delighted in sitting in the full lotus posture and chanting Buddhist hymns.
He first visited Gaofeng at the Shiguan (Dead Gate). Gaofeng was solitary, lofty, stern, and cold, never bestowing a word or a look upon others.

Upon seeing the Master, he was filled with joy and wished to have him tonsured. One day, while reciting the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, when he reached the passage on "shouldering the Buddha," [Gaofeng said: "The Tathāgata..."

Regarding the place from which he came, he attained a sudden and profound understanding. The following year, he shaved his head and received full ordination. Not long after, while observing flowing water, he had an awakening;

he immediately went to Gaogong to seek verification, but Gaogong struck him and drove him out. Subsequently, a rumor spread among the common people that the government was selecting young boys and girls.
The Master asked, "Suppose someone were to come and ask the Abbot for a young boy or girl; what would you do? Guishan said, "I would simply hand him a bamboo comb.
At these words, the Master was suddenly enlightened, penetrating to the very source of the Dharma. Guishan then wrote a true eulogy and gave it to the Master, saying:
"My appearance is inconceivable; even Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot behold it. I grant that only my unworthy son has been able to catch a glimpse of it."

One half of his nose was missing. When someone asked Master Gaoyuan about the relative merits of his various disciples, Gaoyuan said, "As for the Head Seat Yishou, he is truly a single-stemmed old bamboo;
yet it is bent seven ways and eight ways. Only the Rector Ben, however, is like a fresh shoot on the stalk."

In days to come, his achievement as a man of talent will be difficult to measure. In the autumn of the sixth year of the Yan’you era, Prince Wang Zhang—the Prince of Shen and Imperial Son-in-law and Grand Marshal—submitted a memorial requesting that the Master ascend the seat with imperial incense in accordance with a sacred edict. The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "The Great Way is non-action;
the Great Achievement does not preside over it. The Great Goodness leaves no trace; the Great Position is not occupied. In every place, the Sea-Seal Samādhi radiates light; ten thousand..."

In ancient times, the golden branches flourished with brilliance. One visited the Great Being of Perfect Penetration within the Chao-yin Cave, where by purchasing stones one gains an abundance of clouds.
One cultivated the Rucira-cakra rites within Ming-ch’ing Temple, where moving flowers brought butterflies along with them.

Fragrant winds played the music of the Four Heavens, and the sounds of the *brahman* resonated like thunder across the great earth. For two thousand years, the King has already appeared; for five hundred kalpas, he has constantly...
Acting as a sovereign of the world, the entire Great Canon of the Teachings is set in motion according to the capacities of beings; hundreds of thousands of virtuous deeds are freely manifested.
May ten-thousand-year reigns be prayed for within the Nine Palaces, and may the Three Han kingdoms be protected by the Superior State.

These are the ordinary practices of the Grand Marshal, Prince of Shen, the Layman Haiin. Furthermore, regarding a single phrase that accords with the Buddha-dharma, how can it be pointed out? It encompasses heaven and encompasses earth...
Auspicious clouds arise from the earth; from time immemorial until now, auspicious vapors have ascended. On the anniversary of High Peak’s passing, the Master held up the incense and said:
"Within Sūnxīn Hermitage, in the center of Lake Tai, suddenly encountering this memorial day, the phenomena of the world cannot yet be forgotten.
Great Assembly, Old Monk Gāofēng has arrived! Rain steams the green of sprouts and leaves; wind shakes the fragrance of rice flowers. He addressed the assembly: "Spring enters..."
The cold crags cannot be added to; withered stumps and rotten trunks all sprout new buds. The workings of the Great Transformation leave no trace of their form or activity;
red and white flowers alike bloom as one. Monks, of the year’s affairs, already one month has passed. Do you still perceive the meditation cushions and the Zen boards?
Have the alms bowls, spoons, and chopsticks come to rest? The straw sandals and bamboo staffs—[are they at peace?]
Have you been able to let go? Have the lanterns and the pillars forgotten the distinction between object and subject?
If you do not yet understand this, you will know that the past month was spent in vain.

If you do not take the impermanence of birth and death as your primary responsibility and apply yourself with diligent vigor to establish a new way of life, then the next month will likewise end in empty loss.
It will not take more than a few moments of dozing. In twelve months, it will merely pass away through successive cycles of waste.
Having shaved your head and dyed your robes, transcending the mundane and the worldly—what is it that you seek? Do you still know that life exists only as long as the breath remains?
That the vigor of youth does not stay, but is like a galloping horse? If you do not seize this opportunity while the breath has not yet ceased, this vigor of youth...
When practicing, one must stake one's very life. Seize the *huatou* (critical phrase) and engage with it; seek a clear understanding.
As for the analogy of the "crab falling into the boiling water," whom would you blame? Have you not seen how Shigong was in Mazu’s assembly?
While he was performing chores in the kitchen, Mazu asked him, "What are you doing here? Shigong replied, "I am tending the ox. Mazu asked, "How is the ox?"
Mugong said, "Once he has entered the grass, I will pull him back by the nose. Nanquan said, "You truly know how to herd an ox.
Observe these predecessors: even during their daily labors, they never for a moment forgot this Way. How could they be like people of today?

He would not pluck a blade of grass lying horizontally, nor would he step on one standing upright. For his two daily meals of gruel and rice, and for all manner of necessities, he could act as he pleased.

Yet, upon hearing the sound of the head seat striking the board, a sense of revulsion suddenly arose within him, and a flurry of astonishment welled up. Having no choice, he ascended to his meditation cushion;
there, the monkey of emotion and the horse of thought galloped without ceasing. If he did not fall into dullness, he would immediately lapse into distraction. Occasionally, there was a person...
Those who do not forget their original resolve for renunciation must forcibly seize a phrase from the *kōan* to maintain it as their master.

Yet, before they have even begun to raise it, they are blown by the wind into another tune. If one calls such a person a superior practitioner of the mystery (*xuan*), it is no more than a case of leaving Zhengzhou to enter Cao’s gate.
Compared to the ancient worthies who were never apart from [the practice] even in their most casual moments, how could the difference be anything less than that between heaven and earth?
How vast is this! O practitioners of dhyāna, you who are true streams of the Way—there is no room for even a moment’s hesitation before you.
How could you permit yourselves to deliberate, only to act upon what you have grasped? When a thousand peach trees bloom within the Xuan-du Monastery, one simply picks them up and runs;

when the moon is at its third watch over the apricot branches, the swallows seek their nests in the halls of the Wangs and Xies. Hooves tread the paths by the stream of Liu and Ruan. There is no [stopping].
Not a single blade of grass fails to contain its fragrant purity; not a single flower does not bear the countenance of spring.
Brocade clouds surge toward the sky of the First Principle; jade waves swell upon the ocean of true samādhi. Yet, how can one point out that which transcends the workings of the celestial artificer?
A heron stands with feet upraised on the riverbank; a butterfly cries out once within the garden. On a snowy morning, he addressed the assembly: "The frozen clouds close in from all four sides."
The snow falls thick and vast. Who can, at the moment of encounter, perceive it as water? It is only because the flowers in one’s eyes have not yet been glimpsed;

opening the window, one still beholds the jade-like *langgan* (crystal bamboo). Small Sermon: The Great Way is right before one's eyes. Mountains are mountains; waters are waters. The profound mechanism transcends all things;

the sage is not merely a sage, and the ordinary person is not merely ordinary. In a single thought, all is transparently clear; with ten thousand conditions, all is vast and open. This is the autumn of the Crystal Palace.
The countenance is serene and subtle; the myriad phenomena of the universe swallow and spit out the bright moon-jewel. In the Snow-Pine Studio, the vast atmosphere is profound and still.

Screens, desks, and six windows interpenetrate like a precious silken net. There is not a single thing that does not manifest the ultimate essence; there is not a single event that does not expound the True Vehicle.
Although Zhuang Zhou awakened to his identity as a butterfly by his pillow, I dare not guarantee that he was at a loss when the opportunity arose. Zishao was indeed a frog...
I have heard this said under the moon. It was not permitted for him to present himself face-to-face. This one move cannot be named and cannot be described;

even at the point of knowing it, one has already fallen into the trap of emotion. It is so with phenomena, and so with principle. When you understand it in such a way, you have already sunk into the sea of consciousness.
Therefore it is said: "The divine light shines alone; its glorious legacy endures for ten thousand ages. Having entered this gate, do not harbor the thought of 'knowing.'"
[The Master] replied: "Furthermore, since there is no state of knowing or understanding at the ultimate point, how can one point it out? The jade palace is high in autumn without boundaries;
the golden garden’s spring affairs are in full bloom. The Master has no fixed dwelling; wherever he stays in a hermitage or hut, he calls it 'Abiding in Illusion' (Huazhu)."
Noble elephants from the four quarters rushed toward him from all directions. When Emperor Renzong heard of this, he sent envoys to invite him, but he did not come.
The Emperor bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered *kāṣāya* and conferred the title "Buddha-Care Compassionate Perfect Illumination Vast Wisdom" (*Foci Yuanzhao Guanghui*).

When Emperor Yingzong succeeded to the throne, his favors and gifts were identical to those of the previous reign. He once rebuked scholars for failing to seek genuine awakening, saying: "The Chan practice of today is not efficacious."
First, they lack the true spirit and resolve of the ancient sages. Second, they do not regard birth, death, and impermanence as a matter of the utmost gravity.
Third, they are unwilling to sacrifice what they have long practiced and cherished over kalpas, nor do they possess a body and mind that is enduring and non-retrogressive.
Ultimately, where does their ailment lie? It is simply that they do not recognize the root of birth and death.
This was because of his fundamental nature. Whenever he saw a student, he would invariably ask, "What do you call birth-and-death?

Often they were left bewildered with no response, whereupon he would immediately exhort and instruct them. In the autumn of the Guihai year of the Zhi-zhi era, he manifested illness. When someone came to inquire after him, [he spoke as follows].
The Master said, "Huanzhu Hermitage has leaks above and holes on the sides; the fences have collapsed and the walls have fallen, so it cannot be inhabited for long.

He spoke and laughed as he had in his usual manner. Again, there were those who announced their intention to return to Wumen. The Master said, "Why not wait until after the Mid-Autumn Festival before departing?
On the morning of the fourteenth, he wrote a verse to bid farewell to the assembly, saying: "I have one phrase to entrust to the great assembly. If you ask what it is, there is none."
He was able to rely on his fundamental [attainment]; setting down his writing brush and sitting upright, he passed away. On that day, a white rainbow pierced the mountain.
He was sixty-one years of age and thirty-seven years since his ordination. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the West of the Temple, by the Stone overlooking the River.

In the second year of the Yuantong era, he was further conferred the title of National Teacher Puying, and his thirty volumes of writings were designated as the *Guanglu* (Extensive Record), with an imperial decree that they be included alongside the Tripitaka.
This is a popular account.
Chan Master Duanya Liaoyi of Xitianmu Mountain in Hangzhou was surnamed Tang. A native of Deqing in Huzhou, he was first able to speak at the age of six;
regarding worldly affairs, he remained utterly ignorant. At the age of seventeen, a monk passed by his door and recited the teachings of Gaofeng.
Ascending the hall, he spoke these words: "If you wish to exhaust the view for a thousand li, go up one more story. The Master suddenly remarked, "This is a great *kalyāṇamitra*;
I ought to go see him. His mother was startled and marveled at this; she immediately sent him up to the Dead Gate (Sīguan) to serve as a novice.
Feng ordered him to contemplate the koan: "Where does it all return? Consequently, he was given the name Congyi. One day, while passing by the Basu Pond, he saw the tips of pine trees.

Upon the falling of snow, he attained a realization. He went to Feng and presented this verse: "Regardless of north, south, east, or west, the great earth, mountains, and rivers are all one expanse of snow.
Feng struck him with a severe blow and drove him away; unconsciously, he fell over the edge of a cliff. His fellow students climbed by grasping at vines to rescue him.
He pulled him back with force, and the Master again sat upright and firm, making a vow to limit himself to seven days.
Before the period had even elapsed, he attained a sudden and great enlightenment. He rushed to see Feng and said, "Old Monk, you cannot deceive me today.

He presented another verse, saying: "The mountains and rivers of the great earth are all one mass of snow; once the sun shines upon them, they leave no trace. From this day forth, I have no more doubts regarding all things."
The Buddhas and Patriarchs have no north, south, east, or west. On the Peak, he ascended the hall and said:
"I have spread a vast net across the heavens to catch phoenixes and dragons, yet I have never encountered so much as a single shrimp or crab. Today, a tiny gnat has flown right into it!
Thirty years from now, atop a solitary peak at the very summit, I shall raise my voice and cry out loudly. Now tell me, what will it cry? He raised his whisk.
The Master said, "The great earth, mountains, and rivers are all one sheet of snow. The Teacher (Shishuang) then seized the whisk and, for the sake of the assembly, proclaimed:
"If there were but one person throughout the entire earth who had awakened to the true source, they would know it from the very beginning.

Later, he returned to Deqing and, together with his mother, settled in a thatched hut at Wukang. After five years, he returned to the mountain. Xuefeng said, "Many people say you are dragging through mud and carrying along..."
Shui. The Master said, "Two eyes facing two eyes. Thereupon, he requested ordination and changed his name to Liaoyi.
When Feng retired from his position, the two masters Ben and Yong also passed away in succession. The Master then complied with the requests of the assembly; he once addressed the assembly, saying:

If you wish to transcend the mundane and enter the sacred, to forever escape the toil of worldly dust, you must strip away your skin and change your bones, passing through death to be revived anew—like embers from cold ashes suddenly bursting into flame, or withered wood flourishing once more. How can you regard this as an easy matter?
I have been in the presence of the Old Master for many years; though I was struck with great blows that pierced to my very marrow, I never once harbored a thought of leaving. Directly...
Up until this day, whenever I have touched upon a painful point, tears would involuntarily flow; how could this be like your state of joyful exultation?
Upon encountering even a trace of bitterness, you immediately turn your head away and disregard it. Little do you realize that the bitter taste is capable of eliminating a hundred ailments.
On one occasion, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Set aside speech and silence, movement and stillness; bring forth a single phrase! He also said:

"When this single breath does not return, where will you find a place to settle your body and establish your life? When the Master preached the Dharma in response to the capacities of his listeners, he often used coarse words and vulgar expressions that others found unbearable.
On the eve of the New Year in the first year of the Yuantong era, he said to the assembly: "There is one matter as vast as heaven; you..."

"Have you understood it thoroughly? After a long silence, he said, "Tomorrow is the New Year. Six days later, while conversing with a monk at night, he said, "I, the old monk, am going to Tiantai tomorrow.
The monk replied, "I will go along with you. The Master said, "Even if you were to run like a horse, you could not catch up to me.
At noon the following day, he sat in the full lotus posture and passed away. He was seventy-two years of age and forty-nine years since his ordination. At first...
Zhongfeng passed away. During the vegetarian feast held for his funeral, the Master smiled and said to the assembly, "Twelve years hence, there shall be another gathering for this old monk.
This present moment marks exactly twelve years since then. His entire body was enshrined at Lion Rock.
He was posthumously granted the title Dharma-Wisdom Perfectly Enlightened Universal Deliverance Great Master.
Chan Master Puna Zuoyong of Tiantong Dayue Monastery in Hangzhou was a native of Ninghai, Mingzhou.

Having received the essential instruction from Gaofeng, he personally performed the tasks of pounding grain, cooking, and gathering firewood; his appearance was extremely thin and dark. He was blunt and possessed little literary refinement.

Once, he composed a verse in response to Yongming’s “Verses on Mountain Dwelling,” which begins: "If I wish my mind to be extinguished, it shall be extinguished at once; why need I seek a go-between elsewhere? Amidst a thousand differences..."

All crossroads are simultaneously closed and severed; the myriad distinct mechanisms are entirely cut off and destroyed. Building dwellings by binding reeds to trees, they gather thorns to weave fences opening beside the stream.
It was because this Lazy Zan lacked spiritual efficacy that he provoked the Celestial Writings to descend three times.
It is further said: "Ordinary cold understanding, I know myself to be mistaken; I retreat and sink my traces, dwelling in the azure mists.

Sweeping away the hundred-year dream of honor and disgrace, I turn back to the original mechanism of many kalpas. The ant follows the steps to seek its hole; The butterfly flies through the garden to seek its flowers.
One must believe that before heaven and after earth, Every single thing has a true home. Later Dwelling.
In Central India, at Guizidang (Pine Seed Hall), he wrote a gāthā and passed away while sitting upright.
Chuzhou’s Baiyun Kongzhong received the Dharma from Gaofeng under the guise of being a Chan master; later, he resided at Mount Baiyun.

When his reputation spread among fellow practitioners, their sandals filled the space outside his door. On one day in the summer of the *wuzi* year of the Zhizhi era (1276), he took up his brush and wrote a gāthā, saying: "The earth..."

Water, fire, wind, and earth—these were predicted by the Buddhas of the past. To bury him deep in the ground is the primary principle (*paramārtha*). First, it spares the donor from having to provide even a few pieces of firewood;
second, it avoids the public criticism that there are no *śarīra* (relics). He passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture.

Chan Master Jue Xue Shicheng of Panyu Monastery in Hongzhou, a successor of Chan Master Lingyun Ding, addressed the assembly: "Brothers, you have been practicing the Way for three or five years, yet you have found no point of entry.
You have cast aside your previous *huatou* (critical phrase), unaware that you have reached the halfway point of your journey."

Abandoned! What a pity that so much mental artifice has been expended previously. A person of true resolve, seeing that firewood is dry, water is at hand, and the monks’ hall is warm within the assembly, should make a vow not to go outside for three years; they will certainly attain a state of realization.

There are some who, as soon as they begin their practice, find their minds pure and clear, yet as soon as objects appear before them, they immediately form fourfold conceptualizations, taking these to be [the truth].
A person of great potential, quick of speech and clever of tongue, has wasted a lifetime. When the three-inch breath fades away, with what will they sustain themselves?
If a son of the Buddha wishes to transcend, he must practice authentically and realize authentically.

Chan Master Zhuyuan Zhengyuan of Jingshan in Hangzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Ling of Jingshan. He was the son of the Ouyang family of Nankang. Having heard of Xuguzhi’s reputation for the Way, he went to rely upon him.
One day, Xuguzhi brought up the story of Longtan extinguishing the paper candle and questioned him about it. The Master replied, “A scorched stone.”
"You may break through the layered ice. Gu said, "What will you do after breaking it? The Master said, "One must explore to know. Gu asked, "What is it that is known?
As the Master was about to respond, Gu struck him. The Master then attained realization of the teaching with clarity.
Later, he presided over five great monasteries and was titled Chan Master Fohui Cizhao Puying. He passed away at the age of seventy-three; his stupa was erected at his native mountain.
Chan Master Shao Da of Baolin on Mount Huang at Yunhuang in Jinhua Prefecture was surnamed Wu and hailed from Fengshan.
While still a śrāmaṇera, he reflected privately to himself: "Would a fish destined to become a dragon deign to seek its livelihood in a puddle at a horse's hoofprint?

He immediately traveled to Shuangjing to visit Xugou, who pointed him toward the swift essentials for entering the Way. After some time, he took his leave and, with a single staff, journeyed through Huxiang.

He knocked at the gates of Chan everywhere, yet found no difference in the flavor of the Dharma. He then returned to Xinggu Valley, where he redoubled his diligent efforts and eventually attained the Dharma of sovereign fearlessness.
Initially residing at Wulong, he later lived at Baolin. When he manifested his passing, the assembly requested that he write a verse.

The Master took up his brush, threw it to the ground, and said, "Even if I were to write until Maitreya descends to be born, how could I ever leave this place? Thereupon, he passed away peacefully. The funeral rites were performed.
The śarīra obtained was the color of a deep blue bead; his teeth were threaded through a pearl and remained unbroken. He was seventy-four years of age and fifty-one years since his ordination.
Chan Master Jueyin Bencheng of Suzhou was a native of Yuxi in Jiahe. He once composed a verse on living in poverty to express his contentment.
He said: "I find joy only in my leisure; how could poverty be considered a hardship? The poorer I become, the fewer my concerns; with no concerns, my mind becomes even more at ease.
Though I dwell within the human world, it is as if I have transcended the mundane realm."
Chan Master Shiwu Qinggong of Fuyuan Temple in Jiaxing Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Daochang Xin. He was the son of the Wen family from Wenshu in Changshu, Suzhou.
Initially, he visited Gaofeng, who gave him the koan "The myriad dharmas return to one. He served him diligently for three years, after which he went to Xifeng in Jianyang.

He visited Chan Master An, but they did not reach a mutual accord; he suddenly gave rise to a sense of indignation and departed. While on the road, he abruptly raised his head and saw a pavilion by the wind;

he was instantly awakened to realization. Upon returning, he spoke of this to Master An, who nodded in approval. The Master established a hermitage at Tianhu, where he personally labored at gathering firewood and vegetables.

In the intervals between meditation, he delighted in composing "Mountain Dweller's Verses," and thus formed the resolve to spend the rest of his life there. Shortly thereafter, a special messenger from Fuyuan arrived, yet the Master remained firmly reclining in bed.
He did not rise. Someone urged him, saying, "A śramaṇa should take the propagation of the Dharma as his primary responsibility.

What is the point of dwelling in seclusion for one's own private perfection? Thereupon, he turned over and accepted the invitation. He ascended the hall and said: "Bodhidharma dwelt at Shaolin for nine years facing the wall; his defenses were not secure.
Shushan sold his bedding and traveled a thousand miles to see people; the paths were crowded and complex. But here at Fuyuan, the walls—"
The moat is firm and secure; the road is level and straight. Everyone travels every day upon this very path and dwells in a place of stability and security.
Yet, for what reason do you not tread upon that single plot of land in the middle? [He] ascended the hall and said:
"I have a phrase that I wish to break open and explain for all of you. However, I fear that you might revile me, so I shall not break it open for you. Furthermore—
Fearing that the people might doubt me, I shall simply say this now: whether I speak or do not speak, I strike my knee and say, "Know me or blame me;
I have no words of excuse. Entering the hall: movement is like drifting clouds; stillness is like the spirit of the valley. It is like the salty taste within water.
Indigo dye within the pigment; when fine rain wets one’s robe, it cannot be seen. When withered flowers fall to the ground, one hears no sound. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]:
"I am originally a clumsy bhikṣu of the mountains and forests, who has come here at leisure to join the company of fellow meditators.

Even if we gather together and our relations are cordial, what human sentiment can last to the very end? Rest! Rest! Rest! Green mists and red clouds form a brocade of a thousand peaks; the western wind—"

Yellow leaves fill the sky—a day of autumn. Ascending the hall, he said: "To establish knowing and seeing within knowledge is the very root of ignorance; when knowing and seeing are free from the act of seeing, this is nirvana.
The spring mountains layer upon layer in wild green; the spring waters ripple with empty azure. Vast and silent between heaven and earth, standing alone, what limit can one’s gaze reach?
Holding up his staff, he said: "I let Śākyamuni Buddha pass. Striking the ground with the staff, he said: "He has been pierced through by Xuefeng!"
Doubting the nostrils, he remained silent for a long while and then said: "The sword leaves its precious sheath because of injustice; the medicine emerges from the golden jar to save the sick.
On the anniversary of the Master’s passing, he offered incense, saying: "In this place where we meet in misfortune—Xifeng and Jianyang—how many matters of injustice are there?

They are all contained within this single burner of incense. At the New Year’s Eve small *can*, he presided over the year-end ceremony at Beichan, where the rituals and music of the three dynasties were fully realized.
"Old Wang burns paper money; it is all a scene of disarray with cups and dishes strewn about. Upādhyāya Gōng, however, maintains his austere poverty.

Furthermore, encountering a year of famine, he cannot compete in wealth with those from other quarters. From the beginning of the year until its end, he has lived as one family together with everyone else, providing according to the abundance or scarcity of the times.
In the end, he will never go away with a forced smile, borrowing ground to plant flowers and falsely posing as a fine man."
Furthermore, stay within your own home; measure the water and operate the mortar yourself, so as not to have to beg from others.

If you can simply manage by mending things twice a day, you will be able to fulfill your responsibilities as abbot. As the ancients said: "Sometimes I pick wild vegetables and boil them with their roots;

I chop fresh green firewood and burn it with its leaves. It is not that the father is poor and the son suffers together; rather, it is to avoid the situation where the family is wealthy and the children are small."

Erjiao lived there for seven years before retiring due to old age and returning to Tianhu. During the Zhizheng era, the imperial court heard of the Master’s reputation and sent down incense to honor his excellence.
The Empress Dowager bestowed upon him a golden-brocade robe. When he manifested illness, he wrote this verse: "The green mountains do not accommodate a stinking corpse;

they claim to have attained enlightenment. The Master was deeply moved. Tianshan then revealed to him the subtle and vast Dharma gates.

Later, while residing at Kuangzhou, he practiced alone in walking and sitting for seventeen years before finally attaining liberation. He gave a general discourse, saying: "Dharmas have no fixed characteristics; when they encounter conditions, they immediately..."
The Patriarch wields the Vajra sword and swallows the *liji* thorn, severing the tongues of the monks and sitting upon the very crown of Vairocana.
He plants a single blade of grass and makes it the sixteen-foot golden body; he takes the sixteen-foot golden body and makes it a single blade of grass.
This is neither the drum-beat of Heyshan nor a separate transmission outside the teachings; it simply leaves not even a thread of silk hanging, as the moon grows cold in autumn.
Cold ashes suddenly flare into flame. To call this "Buddha-dharma" at such a point is to fall into hell as swiftly as an arrow.
Not to call it "Buddha-dharma" is likewise to fall into hell as swiftly as an arrow. How, O worthy ones, will you ultimately understand this?
Open your mouths and your tongues will be scorched to cinders. Have you not seen how the Boatman said: "For twenty years at Yaoshan, I have hidden my body"?
Where there is dwelling, there are no traces; where there are no traces, there is no place to hide the body.

Even so, to proclaim and reveal the Buddha’s knowledge and vision, to establish the Great Perfect Mirror, to raise the banner of Nirvāṇa, and to exalt Prajñā—to strike and sing together, to integrate and harmonize, and for illumination and function to occur simultaneously—all these, when viewed with the True Eye, are merely idle furnishings. As for our own monastic station, what need have we for them?

Master Wujian Xiandu of Huading Peak on Mount Tiantai was a successor of Chan Master Baoshui Ruiyan; he was a native of the Ye family from Xianju in Taizhou, and his natural disposition was refined and outstanding.
Min was fond of reading; he could recite anything from memory after a single glance. He received the tonsure under Gu Tianhou and studied under Fangshan.

His feet never once crossed the threshold of the door. Baizhang Congzhan asked, "I do not know what the secret meaning of the West is like.
The Master said, "Wait until Mount Śāla nods its head, and I shall tell you."
National Teacher Musō Soseki of Tōzai-in in Japan was a dharma successor of National Teacher Kōfū Nittetsu. He was of the Minamoto (Genji) clan and a native of Settsu Province.

He was the ninth-generation descendant of Emperor Uda. His mother conceived him after dreaming that she had swallowed golden light. He grew up to become a great monk and devoted himself to the study of the teachings.

Dian, fearing that he might become mired in names and forms, flew across the mountains to travel south. He met Master Shanneng, who said, "In my school, there are no words or phrases, nor is there a single dharma to give to others.

"Casually shattering the very bones of empty space. He hurried to see Dayue, who certified his realization. Thereafter, his reputation for the Way flourished daily;
he was granted the title "Purple Robe" (Cizhi), and at the age of seventy-seven, he passed away.
Chan Master Dazong Xing of Mount Jing in Hangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Zituo Dao; he was a native of Taizhou. At the time of his death, he suddenly sighed and said, "I am thirty years old."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "The sweet rain has been overdue; the fields have cracked like tortoise shells. The nostrils of the patch-robed monks are parched with heat and smoke is rising.

Su Zhuangjian ascends the hall: "Yesterday, this mountain monk dispatched several veteran generals to campaign against those who have not yet submitted.

Chan Master Nantang Qingyu of Benjue Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Baoning Moshan. He was the son of the Zhu family of Linhai. Having first resided at Kaifu Monastery, he ascended the hall and said:

In the midst of manifestation, there is a single sphere of radiant light that is neither form nor non-form. Yongjia was much like a beggar who suddenly becomes wealthy;
Kaifu said: "Who does not recognize the mani-jewel? Once shattered, it is not worth a single coin. Thrown into the void, it goes even further beyond."
This was to prevent people of the time from harboring doubts in their hearts. Thus, when the clouds part and the sun emerges, one’s own function reaches fulfillment and majesty is achieved.

While attending to minor affairs, he rolled up his robes and crossed the river to visit Nanjian Quan. Quan appointed him to keep the keys to the storehouse.

One night, under the moonlight on the pines, he heard the sound of flowing water and attained a realization. He went to inform Quan, who sent him to visit Gulin. Gulin asked, "What do you intend to do by coming here?
The Master replied, "It is solely because the matter of birth and death is so great that I have come to seek liberation. Gulin said, "You clearly understand the four..."
"The great five aggregates are the root of birth and death. For what reason have you entered this leather bag? As the Master was about to open his mouth, Lin raised his staff and struck him;

he thereby attained the profound mystery. In the Renwu year of the Zhizheng era, while residing at Ruiyun, there was a monk who asked a question and their dialogue had not yet concluded when Lin slapped the ground and laughed.
The Master said, "Why trouble yourself to bring out such stale merchandise? The monk let out a single sigh.
The Master then gave a shout, and the monk attained realization. Later, Master Liang welcomed him back to Tiantong. Before long, he manifested illness.
His attendants prepared paper and brush and requested a verse. The Master pointed his finger at his heart and said, "Within this of mine, all is vast and empty; what need is there for a verse?"

At dawn the next morning, he sat upright, clenched his fists, and rested his forehead upon his arms on the armrest; thus he passed away. He remained for seven days, his countenance radiant and the crown of his head warm.
Upon cremation, auspicious celestial flowers appeared, and countless *śarīra* relics were obtained. A stupa was erected on the western ridge of Ruiyun Mountain. His age was eighty-five.

Zen Master Yue-lin Jing of Mount Jing in Hangzhou was a successor of Zen Master Hai of Lingyin. He left home to become a monk in his youth and occasionally visited renowned and eminent masters, who directed him to investigate the "original person.
After a long time, he attained realization and composed a verse, saying: "The original person, the original person—without head and without brain, what can one do?"
He searched for it, then suddenly grabbed his own nostril. Look closely; it turns out he was just an unlettered commoner. Shuo saw him staring askance and said, "Is that so?
The Master gave him a slap.
Chan Master Dàqiān Huìzhào, the Great Teacher of Yùwáng in Míngzhōu, was the son of the Mǎ family of Yǒngjiā.

He first visited Huìméi at Jìngcí Monastery, yet he had not yet attained perfect realization. One day, while reading the *Record of Zhēnjìng*, he reached the passage concerning the head-shaven ascetic’s stone being enveloped in moss;
suddenly, sweat poured down his back. He went to see Dōngyǎ, who asked him, “Rushing east and west, what do you intend to do?”
The Master said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects. Xiyu said, "Heaven has no four walls; the earth extends beyond the eight frontiers. Upon what ground would you set foot?
The Master slapped the table with his palms and withdrew. Later, when Xiyu moved to Jingci Monastery, he invited the Master to share the seat [of the abbot].
At the beginning of his life in the world, he experienced the joy of clarity and purity; subsequently, he resided at Potalaka, and later presided over Yuhuang Temple.

He once offered three "gateless barriers" (san guan yu) to test practitioners, saying: "The fierce tigers in the mountains feed on meat; for what reason do they not eat their own cubs? Space has no front or back;
by what cause are there north, south, east, and west? [One] drinks milk equal to the waters of the four great oceans, and piles up bones..."
Like Mount Vipula, who were your original parents? Having resided there for nine years, you retired to the bank of the Miaoxi Spring, where you built the Meng’an (Dream Hermitage) to dwell in.
In the tenth month of the Gui-chou year of the Hongwu era, you passed away.
The laywoman San-kong was among the most virtuous disciples of Chan Master Tian-ning Tan. Possessing the resolve of a heroic man, she was not swayed by wealth or status.
She practiced the "Mu" (無) koan under Master Zhu-yun for thirty-six years. One day, she suddenly asked:
"When birth and death arrive, what then? Yun said, "Who is it that is born? Who is it that dies? The layman bowed his head in greeting.
Yun, suspecting him of being extraordinary, pressed him further, saying, "Who is it that gives birth?
Who is it that dies? The layman again bowed his head in greeting. Yun said, "Be careful not to die right here. The layman raised his prayer beads and counted them.
[He held] one hundred and eight beads. Before long, he manifested a slight illness; he spoke a verse and departed. Upon cremation, countless śarīras were obtained.
Chan Master Tánfāng Zhōng of Jīnlíng Jiāoshān was a successor of Chan Master Yùshān Zhēn. He was a native of Nánkāng. When the Prince of Liáng arrived at Jiānkāng, that evening the temple...
The next day, the King visited the temple and asked, "How is the restoration proceeding? The Master replied, "We rely on the presence of a great donor.
The King said, "Since the temple has been destroyed, upon what does the Buddha now reside? The Master replied, "The Buddhas of antiquity have passed away; the Buddhas of the present have come again."
The King was greatly pleased. He asked again, "What is meant by the 'Jiang-bu porridge' spoken of by the patch-robed monks?
The Master said, "I thought Your Highness had forgotten. The King asked, "What is meant by the 'three pairs of socks' spoken of by the patch-robed monks?

The Master said, "Having traversed every mountain and river within the realm, today I have personally arrived at the house of the Emperor. [The Emperor] bestowed upon him the title of Great Chan Master Guanghui Yuanwu.
Chan Master Nan-chu Yue of Mount Jing-shan in Hangzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Fu of Mount Jing-shan. He was a native of Long-xing. Once, ascending the hall, he said:
"Awakening to the Way through sound; clarifying the mind through form. Suddenly picking up his staff, he said: "This is form. He struck it once and said: "This is sound. [He continued: "All you..."
People all see and all hear. But which is the luminous mind? Which is the path of awakening? He let out a shout and said:
"To covet another's single grain of rice, one loses six months' worth of provisions."
Chan Master Fuzhong Huixin of Tianjie Monastery in Jinling was a dharma successor of Chan Master Tiantong Tan. He was the son of the Jang family of Fenghua. He went up to Tiantong to visit Xizhu Tan;
Tan, recognizing him as a vessel for the Dharma, treated him with a stern countenance. One day, while ascending the hall, [Tan] raised the case of Xinghua striking...
In the "Kebin" public case, he questioned the Master. The Master said, "How magnificent! You are a lion cub. Thereupon, [the Master] attended him closely and served as the *karmadāna* (Vina).
In the Bingyin year of the Taiding era, he emerged into the world at Guanyin Temple in Mingzhou, and subsequently moved to reside at Mount Luojia.

The two kings first added their highest honor and respect. Later, when he presided over Longxiang, the Ming Taizu personally visited the temple to listen to the Dharma and specially changed its plaque.
He became a great deity in the celestial realm. One day, while seeking a bath and changing his robes, he summoned the assembly and said, "I am about to depart.
You should all take it upon yourselves to uphold the Dharma; you must exert yourselves with diligence. Having finished speaking, he closed his eyes.
An attendant shook him and called out, "Master, why do you not leave behind a few words for us? The Master then took up his pen and wrote: "Throughout my life, I have..."
The man has violated the covenant. After seventy-eight years of leaking [the truth], this morning he cast off his hands and departed;

ten thousand *li* of clear sky, a single flake of snow. Having finished writing, he closed his eyes once more. One day prior, while the Great Ancestor was supervising the army at Jiangyin, he dreamed that the Master entered.

The Great Ancestor asked, "For what purpose have you come, Master? The Master replied, "I am coming to bid farewell before returning to the West. Not long after, the imperial carriage returned to Jin.

When Emperor Ling heard the news of the Master’s passing, it coincided exactly with his dream. The Emperor was struck with wonder and issued an edict to release funds from the imperial treasury to assist with the funeral arrangements.
A stupa was erected at the foot of Mount Niushou, and portions of the Master’s fingernails, hair, robes, and sandals were interred at Tiantong Temple.
The Five Lamps Adorning the Lineage, Volume Twenty-One;
The Five Lamps Adorning the Lineage, Volume Twenty-Two:
The Linji School.

Chan Master Wuming Huiweng of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture, a native of Fuzhou and a successor in the eighteenth generation under National Teacher Yong of Gushan in the lineage descending from Mount Nanyue, ascended the hall and spoke, citing Changqing: [Changqing said: "When you see the mountain, do not say it is green; when you hear the river, do not say it is blue. Wuming said, "If you say it is green, you have already missed the mountain; if you say it is blue, you have already missed the river. If you can speak without missing them, then you may truly be called a person of the Way. He then added, "But even so, you must still pass through the three barriers before you can be called a true patch-robed monk. He then descended from the seat.
"In general, it seems today that the Old Barbarian has hope," Baofu said. "In general, it seems today that the Old Barbarian is without hope.
The Master said: "The heavens are high as wild geese rise into the clouds; the earth is solemn as crickets enter the grass to cry. All is within the scenery of autumn;
how many times does the traveler’s sorrow follow the feelings of a foreign land? He compiled the *Candeng Huiyao* (Essentials of the Lamp of Zen), which was circulated in the world.

Chan Master Zangcou Shanzen of Xuefeng in Fuzhou was a successor of Chan Master Lingyin Shan. He was the son of the Lü family of Nanan. Entering the hall, he said: "The entire great earth is the purple-golden body.
All of you spend your days with eyes wide open, looking right at the heart and liver of Old Śākyamuni. He raised his staff and said:
Stepping forward, he struck the nose of the Old Śākyamuni: "To speak of existence or non-existence is deception; to speak of arising or ceasing is slander;

to speak of 'this mind' or 'not this mind' is delusion. Without deception, without slander, and without delusion—spring winds blow down the peach and plum blossoms, while thin mist and sparse rain enshroud the green peaks.
He inscribed his own portrait, saying: "In Zen practice there is no awakening; in literacy there is a limit."
His eyes were like those of a sorrowful foreigner from Mount Yan; his face was as wrinkled as Zhao Po drinking vinegar.

He stood far above all others in every respect, and dared to say that rice is made from grain. Later, by imperial decree, he moved to Mount Jing. He passed away in the Dingchou year of the Jiading era.
Chan Master Youyun Zongmou of Longji Mountain in Jixian Prefecture was a native of the Wang family of Luling.
At the age of nineteen, he shaved his head and received full ordination. Hearing that Miaofeng was expounding the Dharma at Lingyin Monastery, he went there to rely upon him.
One day, as Miaofeng ascended the hall, he held up his staff and said, "The Elder Śākyamuni has arrived; do you all see him? His subtle, wondrous, and pure Dharma-body..."
[The Master] displayed the thirty-two marks [of a Buddha]. Putting down his staff, he said, "None of you understand; I am entering nirvana. At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
Shortly thereafter, he took leave to return home. He obtained the ruins of an old temple from the mountain master Xiuxiu, where he lived on wood and drank from mountain streams.
Sometimes, during snowy cold weather when there was no fire for the night, he would pass the day by eating several inches of sweet flag (*achangchu*) root.
He composed these lines on the spot to console himself: "The mountain monk has his lot dwelling among the misty vines; lacking both rice and coin, I need not concern myself with them.

The water is like lapis lazuli, the mountains like jade; before my eyes, there is more than enough. Thereafter, his transformative influence spread somewhat, and within a few years, it became a great monastic center. Because of this—
He resumed the old name and posted a sign reading: "Longji Qingliang Temple. He once wrote on the gate:
"Setting aside the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind—what is your own self? If you can speak to this, I grant that you have personally seen Longji;
if not, then stay outside the gate for now. A monk asked, "How many people has the Master ever received? The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, since..."
"One who comes will not be forced to eat grass against their will. When asked, "What will it be like when the thirtieth day of the twelfth month arrives?

the Master replied, "There will be no debt collectors at the gate. He manifested illness and gathered the assembly to entrust them with his final affairs. Tapping his fingers once, he said, "This alone is my parting message to the assembly.
When the assembly requested that he leave a verse, he took up a brush and wrote: "A single lamp remains in sight; there is nothing more."

As he spoke, the great earth sank level and the void split asunder; all became still and silent. He remained in the world for eighty years, and his entire body was enshrined in a stupa upon a mountain peak.
Chan Master Dongsou Zhongying of Jingci Temple in Hangzhou ascended the hall and said: "Above all, do not seek by following others;
there is no need to look within yourself. Transcendent and lively, there is letting go and there is gathering in. What is this? A single leaf falls, and autumn comes to all under heaven."
Chan Master Wuchu Daguan of Yuyang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Jingci Jian. He was the son of the Lu family from Ning County.

Having studied under Beijian at Nanping, their spiritual resonance and words were in perfect accord. Later, while presiding over the monastery, he ascended the hall and said: "One winter, two winters—you and I, you and I, in the darkness..."
A secret smile. To speak empty words face-to-face—though this may be but ordinary family fare, who knows there are worms within the rice?
A fine wind blew last night, blowing down a pine branch before the gate. Ascending the hall, he said: "The events of kalpas of dust are but the present moment.

If one hesitates to sever what must be severed, the constellations will shift and the stars move. He took up his staff and struck it, saying: "The flowers must bloom through the night; do not wait for the dawn."
The wind blows. Ascending the hall: The orthodox lineage of Bodhidharma, the very core of the patch-robed monks, fills the void; there is nowhere to take refuge.
How laughable that those deluded by the current keep their eyes wide open under the bright sun and clear sky, yet do nothing but nod off!
Furthermore, the Elder of the Yellow Face, failing to distinguish good from evil, plunges into the mud and the water, yet says: "At the place of Dīpaṃkara Buddha, I did not possess a single dharma."
It may be so; yet you would grant me a prediction of enlightenment. Why must you gouge a sore from healthy flesh and seek a calyx from a flower of the sky?
Ultimately, how is this? *Siri siri*. After his passing into the world, he was interred in a hermitage to the west of the monastery.

Chan Master Yankxi Guangwen of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an was a successor of Chan Master Jingshan Yan. He was a native of the Lin family of Houguan. He went to consult with Zhe’ung, who brought up the koan of Zhaozhou washing his alms bowl.
Just as the Master was about to open his mouth, Zhe’ung suddenly stopped him; all the doubts and obstacles of his life were instantly cleared away like ice melting.
Commentary: In the Wuzi year of the Shaoding era, [Zhaozhou] appeared in the world at Jingci Temple. Ascending the hall, he cited Zhaozhou’s instruction to the assembly, which said:
"Thirty years ago, when I was at the hearth in the south, there was a 'foot' of neither guest nor host; even until now, no one has brought it up. The Master (Xuedou) commented:
"The myriad phenomena of the forest and the ten thousand images—brightness and darkness, form and emptiness—proclaim it day and night. Zhaozhou..."
The Buddhas of antiquity were not ignorant; it was simply that they were rushing too quickly toward their destination. Entering the hall for instruction:
"At the crossroads, there is the stone pillar where you have no place for concealment. When one hears 'The Minister comes upon the river,' there is no place for evasion.
You monks go out in the morning and return in the evening; you must be meticulous with every step you take. Suddenly, if you stumble or strike against something, [the truth] is revealed."
The staff of compassion has been separately entrusted. Ascending the hall: "Zhaozhou says, 'Go and drink tea'; Nanguan says, 'Come and eat rice. At Longmen there are many guests;
if anyone can provide the final phrase, I shall permit them to enter the Dharma-gate of the letter 'A'. Ascending the hall.
A verse on the occasion of State Preceptor Wang’s meeting with Master Mi: The wheel of spiritual mechanism turns freely like beads on a board;
The wondrous point lies entirely at the tip of the brush. Upright, it remains as it was, yet is set down again; The numinous blade of the precious sword leans against the cold heavens.
He passed away in the fourth year of the Jingding era.
Chan Master Dongshan Yuan’s verse on Master Xiandeheshang says: "Pitiable life amidst heaps of paper money; The moment that foul mouth opens, there is entanglement.
Having swept away the impoverished livelihood of the ghostly realm, To this day, no one passes by the ancient temple."

Chan Master Pengl of Shuanglin in Wuzhou cited Mingzhao’s discourse on “The Cold Wind” given while ascending the hall. Just as the assembly had gathered, Mingzhao said, "The wind at the peak is somewhat harsh;
this is not a place for you to settle your body or establish your life. Return first to a warm room to deliberate. He then returned to his quarters.
The great assembly followed him there and stood in formation. Mingzhao spoke again: "As soon as you arrive in a warm room, you immediately fall asleep."
He drove them all down at once with his staff. The Master composed a verse, saying: "The head was already perverse enough when it was somewhat stiff;
Yet you further buried yourself in a warm place. This has caused a trail of traces to remain for a thousand ages; In vain did you eat the white rice of Luoshan."
Chan Master Yuanzhao of Huaihai, originally from Tongzhou and a member of the Pan family, resided at Jingshan in Lin’an Prefecture.
He went to visit Zhe’ung, who asked, “Where are you from? The Master replied, “A man of Huai. Zhe’ung said, “Why did the Great Sage of Sishui appear in Yangzhou?
The Master said, “Today he has run into him again in Hangzhou. Zhe’ung said, “That still lacks connection. The Master said, “By myself—”
He hurried from afar to follow the Master’s teaching wind. The Master, recognizing his sharp intelligence and wishing to greatly stimulate him, did not allow him to enter the hall;
as soon as he saw him, he said, "Give me a turning word. As the Master was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him with a shout. The Master then presented a verse, the end of which read:
"In vain one turns the head to gaze toward Chang'an. The Master said, "What kind of place is this? The Master replied, "I thank you, Preceptor, for hanging [this verse]."
"Step forward. Only then was he permitted to enter the room.
Chan Master Qian of Bian Shan composed a verse on the occasion of Li Ao’s visit to Yaoshan, which says: "Valuing the ear while disparaging the eye;
drawing the golden arrow behind one's back. Looking up at the blue sky, the arrow has already passed beyond the kingdom of Silla."
Chan Master Dajian Putong Cuiji of Lingyin Temple in Lin’an Prefecture was a native of Fenghua, Mingzhou. He inscribed the following on a portrait of the World-Honored One leaving the palace:
"Dragon-like markings and phoenix-like essence, he departs the royal palace; Elbows bare and robes tattered, he emerges from Snowy Peak.
His wisdom-vow must surely empty all realms of existence, Yet one knows not when those realms will be emptied. He compiled the *Wudeng Huiyuan* (Compendium of the Five Lamps) in twenty fascicles.
Wandering in the world.

On the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month, Chan Master Wuliang Chongshou of Ruiyan in Qingyuan Prefecture, successor to Chan Master Ruyi of Emperor Yuezhang, ascended the hall for the lecture. He raised the example of the World-Honored One beholding the light.
The Public Case of Xing’s Enlightenment. The Verse says: Upon seeing the morning star, his eyelids were pierced through; In Chinese and barbarian tongues, there were tens of thousands of words.
Beggar, you who have suddenly grown rich—do not speak of dreams; In whose hearth is there no smoke from the fire?
Chan Master Wujing Che, a successor in the lineage of the Tiantong school, cited the following case involving Yantou: A monk asked, "How does one discern the host amidst the dust?
Yantou replied, "A copper sand-pan filled with oil. He then offered this verse: "A million brave soldiers enter the Han Pass; Their majesty is like a fierce tiger in battle."
Like a mountain, he took Yan Liang’s head with a single blade; had it not been Lord Guan, it would have been most difficult indeed.
Zen Master Shantong Guanzhi, a successor of Zen Master Hantang Shanji of Huqiu Temple in Pingjiang Prefecture, praised the image of Guanyin Carrying a Fish Basket, saying: "Cloud-like hair..."
Heavy makeup and forced smiles; for the sake of trivial matters, one enters the dusty world. Though they bring what is truly alive, no one buys it;
it is viewed merely as a common dead commodity.

Chan Master Lingyin Jingshou Rujué of Lin’an Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Tiantong Xing. He was a native of Wuzhou. Because he was dull-witted, his master asked him in the meditation hall, "What is the Buddha?
The Master replied, "A rotten winter melon. He then offered this verse: "What is the Buddha? A rotten winter melon. If you try to bite it, your teeth will break."
The frost clings to it, piercing the teeth; though its root has no storehouse, it blooms once a year.
After his stay, he ascended the hall: "A new year strikes a new drum, universally bestowing the fresh rain of Dharma. All things are renewed, each and every one conforming to the rules.
The Great Being Samantabhadra, rejoicing and seizing the moment, opens the gate and lets forth the white elephant."
"O King, throughout the entire earth there is nowhere to be found. [The Master] picks up his staff and says, "Only this one thing does not belong to the old or the new.
To casually open your mouth is to swallow the Dharmakāya. He throws it down and says, "What is this? Within a thousand-year peach pit, there is still the original kernel of the past."
Chan Master Wumen Huikai of Huanglong, a dharma successor of Chan Master Wanshou of Wannian Monastery, was the son of the Liang family of his native district in Hangzhou.

He studied under Yue-lin, contemplating the "Mu" (No) koan, yet for a long time he failed to achieve awakening. Thereupon, he resolved with great determination and vowed that his side would not touch the mat. One day, by the side of the Dharma seat...
Standing there, he heard the sound of a drum and went out to look. He composed a verse, saying: "In the blue sky and bright sun, a clap of thunder;
the eyes of all living beings on the great earth are opened wide. The myriad phenomena and the forest of forms all bow their heads together; Mount Sumeru leaps and dances through the three stages.

The next day, he entered the room wishing to communicate what he had attained. Lin [Jiurong] suddenly said, "Where have you seen gods or ghosts come from? The Master then gave a shout, and Lin likewise...
"Ho! The Master again shouted. In the sixth year of Chunyou, by imperial decree, he opened the mountain at Huguo Renwang Temple.

Ascending the hall, he said: "Right and wrong, long and short—these are but the wind passing by one's ears; do not seek out differences within them. If you wish to remain unmoved even when blown by the eight winds,"
Therefore, the teaching that the mind-ground is like space was understood by the Elder Ciyun only as setting sail with the current;
he could not steer the rudder against the wind. Huanglong, however, was not so: having cast away both right and wrong, he invites you to realize it within right and wrong.
Why is this? "How many times have black winds overturned the great ocean, yet never have we heard of a fishing boat capsizing. It was during a year of great drought.
Emperor Lizong of the Song dynasty summoned the Master to pray for rain. Upon his return, he sat in silence. The Emperor sent an inner attendant to inquire about him, to which the Master replied:
"Tranquil and unmoving; stirred, it immediately penetrates. Thereupon, a great rain fell. The Emperor conferred upon him the title Chan Master Fuyan.
Chan Master Miaoyin of Zhushan in Tanzhou, while reading the scriptures by moonlight, spoke this verse: "Before the tongue moves, the patterns and colors are revealed;
The five thousand scrolls are fully encompassed at once. If you say you must wait for the moon to open the volume again, I dare guarantee that even in a donkey’s lifetime you will not reach the end."

Chan Master Xuanzou Xingduan of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou, a successor in the nineteenth generation under Nanyue and a dharma heir of Chan Master Zhen of Jing Mountain, was born into the He family of Lin’an. From birth, he was exceptionally distinguished and outstanding. When he was over...
He mastered the recitation [of the scriptures] by sight. At the age of twelve, he left home to become a monk at Huacheng Monastery; six years later, he received full ordination.
Hearing that Zang-sou was propagating the Way at Jingshan, he went there to rely upon him. Zang-sou asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Taizhou. Zang-sou gave a shout.
The Master spread out his sitting mat. Zang-sou shouted again. The Master withdrew his sitting mat. Zang-sou said, "I grant you thirty blows; go to the meditation hall."
The Master attained sudden enlightenment upon hearing these words. One day, while attending [the master], the Old Man said, "There are no monks in Southern Fujian.

The Master asked, "What about you, Preceptor? The Old Man struck him with his staff. The Master caught it and said, "Do not say there are no monks. The Old Man nodded in approval. Subsequently, the Old Man passed away.
The Master went to Jingci Temple and relied upon Shilin Gong, who appointed him as head of the secretariat. He then studied under Xueyan. Xueyan...
The Master asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "From the Two Zhe regions. Yan said, "Why is it that your speech differs [from ours]? The Master said, "Shut your stinking mouth!
Yan said, "The Tadami Bridge is high and the Jūun Peak is steep; I do not yet know where the Secretary resides.
The Master clapped his hands and said, "A duck swallows a snail; its eyes pop out! Yan laughed and, looking toward his attendant, said, "Serve some fine tea."
The Master said, "It is not necessary. In the year of the Metal Rat (Gengzi), he took up residence at Zifu Temple on Lake Tai. By special imperial decree, he was granted a posthumous title.

He subsequently moved to Tianzhu, then to Lingyin, and finally filled the seat at Jingshan; thus, he received the gift of the golden brocade robe three times. His reputation and spiritual radiance were widely renowned. A monk asked:
"On this clear morning of the first day of the month, you ascend the precious throne; we pray that the Master will first offer blessings for ten thousand years of spring. The Master—

[The student] said: "The qilin appears; the phoenix manifests. [The student] asked: "Regarding the single phrase 'Wishing Longevity to the Sage' pointed out by the Master, what is the matter of the upward-pointing lineage?
The Master said: "The winter melon is straight and clumsy; the gourd is curved and winding. [The student] asked: "As for the old woman of Mount Tai..."
Whenever a monk asked, "Where does the road to Tai Shan lead? the old woman would say, "Go straight ahead.
As soon as the monk took a step, she would say, "What a fine monk, going off like that! The Master said, "Blind!
[The monk] asked, "Zhaozhou said, 'The old woman has been tested by me. What was the meaning of this? The Master said:
"The bandit is a petty person. The monk bowed. The Master then shouted. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The straw sandals have no heels. A monk asked, "What is the phrase that hits the mark? The Master said, "A blade cannot cut it.
He asked, "What is the phrase that misses the mark? The Master said, "Fire cannot burn it. He asked, "What is the phrase that is neither missing nor hitting the mark? The Master said, [silence].
"This is truly one phrase. The Master said: "Be most careful not to seek it from another; to do so is to distance yourself from me. [A monk asked:
"The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas, yet the Buddha-dharma did not manifest before him, and he could not attain the path of Buddhahood.
Yet the outcaste (caṇḍāla) Wide-Face of India, upon laying down his butcher’s knife, was told: 'You are counted among the thousand Buddhas. Why is this so? The Master said: "Water."
The waters flow toward the Yangtze and Han; the clouds head back toward the Imperial Capital. [A monk] asked, "What is the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye?
The Master said, "The *Shigan-dang* at the crossroads. [The monk] said, "Is it not this very thing? The Master said, "The moon is like a drawn bow; little rain, much wind.
He ascended the hall and said: "Mind is not Buddha; rabbits and horses have horns. Wisdom is not the Way; oxen and sheep have no horns."
Suddenly picking up his staff, he drew a line and said: "A night of falling blossoms and rain; the entire city is filled with the fragrance of flowing water.

On the occasion of the Eighteenth Day of the Twelfth Month, when ascending the hall, had you not yet reached the heels beneath the Snow Mountain, I would have given you thirty blows. Now that you have reached the heels beneath the Snow Mountain— [he paused].
"Thirty blows for him! [The Master said: "Last night, when I saw the morning star, thirty blows for the soles of his feet!
And another thirty! The mountain monk shall eat them himself; even Śākyamuni has no share. Why? Because merit must be rewarded. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The entire earth is a single lamp. The Buddhas of the three periods, the six generations of patriarchs, and all the old monks of the world are within this lamp."

At the beginning of the Hongwu era, he responded to the imperial summons and entered the capital. His views were in accord with the Emperor's wishes, and he remained there for three years before being granted leave to return home. He presided over two monasteries.
At Jingshan, one day his illness became severe. His attendant requested a verse, but the Master rebuked him, saying, "I still have three years of worldly life remaining.
It turned out exactly so. On the day of his passing, he suddenly clapped his hands and said, "A-he-he! O assembly, what is this?"
Look at this! It is ultimately still and silent.

Zen Master Xiyuan Xi of Mount Yang was the dharma heir of Zen Master Xiaoyin Dayin of Longxiang in Jinling. He was a native of the Chen family of Nanchang. He went to study under Huiji, who asked him:
Huanglong had received the essential meaning from Letan; leading his disciples on a journey to seek instruction elsewhere, he encountered Ciming.

His spirit was drained and sweat poured from him. [Ciming asked: "Where does the fault lie? Huanglong replied, "In a thousand-year-old peach pit, what old kernel do you seek? On another day, [Ciming] asked:
"Not falling into cause and effect," and one falls into the body of a wild fox; "not being ignorant of cause and effect," and one sheds the body of a wild fox.
Tell me, where does the point of benefit and harm lie? As the Master was about to respond, Ji gave a shout, and the Master finally attained sudden enlightenment.

On the occasion of the Emperor Wenzong’s memorial service, when the *Tripitaka* was being recited for the dispersal of merit, he ascended the hall and said: "Venerable and unsurpassed, transcending the primordial ancestor beyond the realm of form; noble..."

One may name it thus: it sits, severing the summit of Vairocana. As for the magnitude of that summit, it encompasses the ten voids; as for the breadth of its function, it includes all myriad categories.

It is like the moon reflected in many waters, making no distinction between the pure and the defiled; it is like springtime in a hundred flowers, where neither the central nor the peripheral aspects can be seen.
It is wondrous existence that is not existent, and true emptiness that is not empty. Therefore, it is said: "Boundless..."
The realms of the buddha-fields are not separated from one another by even a hair’s breadth; ten eons of past and present do not depart from a single moment of thought.
To cast the great trichiliocosm beyond the four quarters and to contain Mount Sumeru within a mustard seed—when one perceives this, one sees Emperor Wen-zong.
Formerly descending from the stage of Buddhahood, he manifested in a royal palace to govern the state and stabilize the ancestral altars, thereby guiding and transforming all beings.
Having completed the cycle, he returns once more to the station of the Buddha. He is serene and unmoving; his wisdom universally responds throughout the ten directions.
Vast and impartial, his measure encompasses the sands of all worlds. Longxiang offers this praise in such a manner—tell me, does it accord with the Sage’s intent or not?
After a long silence, he said: "The *utpala* flower blows on without ceasing; again descending from Tuṣita to Jambudvīpa.
