"I am in urgent haste precisely because of the matter of birth and death," the monk replied. "What is this urgent matter of birth and death? the Master asked. The monk made a striking gesture with his sitting cloth (*zuoju*).
The Hall Master said, "Dare you come here to pull at a tiger’s whiskers? Go to the hall for your practice.
One day, while in the hall, the Master raised the koan of the cypress tree in the courtyard. As the teacher was about to open his mouth, the Hall Master struck him across the face with his palm.

He attained sudden enlightenment. When he first entered the world, he resided at Beichen Monastery in Fuzhou. Addressing the assembly, he said: "Yesterday we cleared the wasteland; I ask all of you to clear away the thorns and briars."

The rubble has been cleared away; the original foundation is now clearly visible. Only the central tree remains, which no one can uproot. Today, this mountain monk cannot help but employ another expedient:
with a sharp blade, he shears away all the profuse branches and leaves; with a blunt hoe, he deeply digs out the crooked and inverted roots.
The work upon the solid ground becomes a single expanse; the pickaxe used for dwelling in the mountains leaves no trace. *Chao*.
While resting by the grass. A monk asked, "When will this patch of ground be cleared until it is perfectly clean?
The Master raised his hoe and said, "It must not be called a hoe. I wonder, Elder, what would you call it? The monk was speechless.
The Master threw down the hoe and said, "When will this patch of ground be cleared until it is perfectly clean? [The monk] asked, "What is the realm of Yunju?"
The Master said, "The road turns and the stream winds back; the empty courtyard is still. [The student] asked, "What is it like to be a person within this realm?

The Master said, "In an era of Great Peace, one’s body is free and at ease. [The student] said, "I have already received your instruction regarding the person and the realm; I now wish to hear a single phrase for those at the beginning stage."
The Master said, "A hairless hawk soars through the heavens. [The monk] asked, "When one encounters a person who has attained the Way, one does not respond with speech or silence.
What is the situation then? The Master said, "Only one who has attained the Way knows. [The monk] said, "How can you, Master, meet me with such conflict?
The Master said, "To capture a thief is not as good as to frighten him. [The monk] said, "An eye-opener cannot be deceived by even a single point. The Master said, "..."
"I know full well that you do not have good intentions. In the spring of the twenty-sixth year of the Hongwu era, an imperial edict was issued to summon eminent monks from throughout the realm.

The Master was among those selected; his responses at court were in accord with the Emperor's wishes. In the autumn, he was dispatched by imperial decree to perform a sacrificial rite at Mount Lu, where the ceremony was successfully completed.

Upon his return, he was further granted a set of monastic robes. That winter, he received an imperial decree appointing him as the abbot of Jingshan. Ascending the hall, he said: "A person comes from Mount Lu, bringing the summit of Huading."
Faith. Report: The white-browed tiger of Nanshan is actually within the Dragon Abyss, hiding its fangs and crouching its claws.
The red-fin carp of the Eastern Sea has ascended straight to the peak of Vulture Mountain; how fine it is to leap over waves and charge through billows!
O Great Assembly, throughout the entire Tripitaka, when has it ever spoken to this point? Nevertheless, the staff of Jingshan refuses to let it pass. (He raises his staff and draws a line.)
One day, the immortal Zhang Guolao said, "I have no use for a medicinal gourd; I rely instead on my staff. He then descended from his seat.
Suddenly, on the twenty-third day of the tenth month, he addressed the assembly, saying, "Difficult, difficult! A beautiful young maiden of sixteen ascends a high mountain;
even this old monk cannot support her. Having spoken these words, he passed away.

Chan Master Jianxin Laifu of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yue of Mount Jing. He was the son of the Wang family of Fengcheng in Nanchang. While in retreat behind closed doors, he addressed the assembly:
"My body is like withered wood and my hundred thoughts are as ashes; the mountain monkeys and wild cranes suspect me with distress. I shut the door and alone conceal my green [robe]."

Pine Rain. Even when meeting people, my smiling mouth is too weary to open. I composed the "Verse of the White Ox": Plowing and weeding ceaselessly to the east of Haimen, I have gathered it back toward the small peak of Laṅkā.
On the open ground, the power of taming has already been forgotten; Who on the Snowy Mountains recognizes the traces of its coming and going?
Released back to the Jetavana grove, it hangs among the sheep and deer; Having cultivated the *tamdala* flower, it accompanies the elephants and dragons. A single color fills the courtyard of heaven.

His character was extraordinary; he was like a jade lotus in a crystal pond. In the winter of the first year of the Hongwu era, he was summoned for his noble conduct to preach the Dharma at Zhongshan Mountain and was granted a meal in the inner court.
At that time, Prince Chuang of Shu was the object of Emperor Taizu’s greatest affection;

he commanded Confucian scholars to debate the Way with the Master every day without fail. In the twenty-fourth year, when the "Hu" faction was apprehended in Shanxi, the Master and others were among those arrested.
He traveled back and forth to the Hu residence. Having been convicted of a crime, he entered extinction.
Chan Master Wuzhi of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou, a dharma successor of Chan Master Ming of Lingyin, was the son of the Li family of Linhai in Taizhou. At nineteen, he attained...

After his ordination, he traveled with staff in hand to visit various regions. While in the presence of Pujue, during their exchange of questions and answers, his doubts were suddenly dispelled. Pujue approved of him.
On the day of his passing, the assembly requested a verse. The Master said, "In our school, there is fundamentally no speech," and then, joining his palms, he passed away.
Chan Master Wansong Shiwu of Mount Dengwei in Suzhou,
the twenty-fourth generation descendant of Nanyue and successor to Chan Master Fulong Chang, was a native of Leqing in Wenzhou. His secular surname was Jin.
His mother dreamed that two men, one a Confucian and one a Buddhist, entered her chamber; upon waking, she gave birth to two sons. The Master was the younger. A white light illuminated the room.

Even as an infant, whenever he saw a monk, he would smile and assume the gesture of joining his palms. At thirteen, he received full ordination. Once, while reciting the *Lotus Sūtra*, he reached the passage:

"All dharmas, from their very origin, are eternally in a state of quiescent extinction. He attained a profound realization thereupon and subsequently went to Hangzhou to receive [further instruction].
He visited Zhuyan. Zhuyan showed him the "Three Not-Sos" (San-bushi) dialogue. He then departed for Mount Dapeng, where he built a hermitage.
One day, hearing a temple monk cite the koan of Muzhou kicking over the water pitcher, he suddenly attained enlightenment. Later, he went to Huading to visit Wujian Du.

Du instructed him, "For now, stay in the mountains and preserve what you have realized. Subsequently, he heard the verse of Qianyan, which contained these words of entrustment: [Verse omitted per instructions]
To those students from all quarters who have come to study, do not let them miss this precious time.
He went straight to Fulongyan and asked, "With what will you meet this old monk? The Master raised his fist and said, "I meet the Master right here."
Yan said, "Once dead and cremated, where does one establish a dwelling and sustain one's life? The Master said, "The bubble arises and the bubble perishes, yet the water remains;
the wind ceases and the waves subside, while the moon reflects in the pool. Yan said, "It is not the mind, it is not the Buddha, and it is not a thing."
"What is this? The Master drew a circle with his sitting cloth and stood with his hands folded.
One day, while they were working together to cut pine trees, the Master picked up a round stone and, making a gesture of offering a pearl, said, "I ask the Master to set its price.
Yunyan said, "It is not worth half a copper coin. The Master said, "Blind! Yunyan said, "I am blind too; you are blind too. The Master said, "Blind, blind! Yunyan then...

The Abbot appointed the Master as the First Seat in the Hall. The Master declined, but could not avoid it. One day, when Master Yan ascended the hall and raised the koan: "The lotus leaf moves though there is no wind;

there must surely be a fish swimming," the Master let out a thunderous roar and strode out with his sleeves brushed back. Master Yan then presented this verse: "The lotus leaf moves though there is no wind; There must surely be a fish swimming. A single shout, like a dragon’s roar, Startles the fish and the dragon both."
Lush yellow flowers fill the eyes; autumn is here. Baizhang sits upright atop the green peaks.
Lightly bringing forth the phrase of "no host and no guest," A single shout makes the waters of a thousand rivers flow backward. The Master received this verse and retired to Mount Song at Lanxi.
The assembly requested him to open the hall for formal teaching. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Mount Song? The Master said, "On all four sides, fine mountains support the sun and moon. One...
"The lake's autumn waters soak the blue sky. [The monk] asked, "What is it like to be a person within this realm? The Master said, "The three immortals could not paint it;

I shall never transmit it to you. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter at hand right now? The Master said, "Eyebrows cross above the eyes. [The monk] asked, "Is this not where he establishes his dwelling?
The Master said, "You have mistaken the zero point on the scale. He then said, "Difficult for a thousand sages..."

Clarifying the cause of non-comprehension, it has been passed down from generation to generation from antiquity to the present. Today, on Mount Song, it is raised once more: when the flowers bloom upon the iron tree, it is a spring of a different kind.
Facing the shadowless tree, he does not strike out in sleep; he opens a vast restaurant in the void.

Walking back and forth upon his own back, he extensively expounds the vehicle of the school. In every atom and every land, all is fully revealed; in every object and every instance, all follows the same track. Strike!
Shattering the old nests of the Mara-king, severing the life-root of the patch-robed monks; neither engaging in extraordinary deliberation nor arriving at mysterious and subtle interpretations.
It reaches the point where Vimalakīrti remains silent, together praising the peace and prosperity of the age, while Yantou attains secret resonance, all proclaiming the supreme transformation.
At such a time as this, how do you speak the single phrase for the opening of the hall to offer blessings to the Sovereign? After a long silence, he said: "A single piece."
The numinous light illuminates the universe; solemnly, the myriad nations receive the sovereign’s grace. Entering the hall: At the beginning of the month is the first day;
the radiance gradually emerges. At the end of the month is the thirtieth day; where can the radiance be sought? Even the aged Śākyamuni would say it cannot be brought forth.
If it could be brought forth, all matters would be concluded. Great assembly, if there is anyone who can speak of this, come forward and speak!
Look! As if there were nothing, Mount Songshan reveals a message to you all. Spreading his two hands, he said:

"I saw that the fundamental radiance and auspicious signs of Dīpaṃkara Buddha were like this. Later, while residing at Dengwu, the fourfold assembly flocked to him in response. He constructed a great monastery called Sheng'en.
When he was about to enter nirvana, his disciples asked, "In the Master's assembly, how many people attained the Dharma? The Master showed them [his hands].
The verse says: Compassion and kindness are without conceptual thought; the flower blooms and the fruit ripens. The ground of practice is clearly defined; entrust this treasure of wisdom.
A single stream flows on, pure and transparent, continuing from age to age, from eternity to eternity. He spoke another verse, saying: "In seventy-nine years..."
With a single flavor he cleared the weeds; with a hand-dropped leap from the precipice, the bright sun shone upon the day. He passed away while sitting in meditation.

His coffin remained enshrined for thirteen days, his countenance appearing as if alive. His entire body was interred in a stupa to the west of the monastery. His portrait was painted by all the people of Wu.
Chan Master Wuyou Shouzhe of Tiantong in Hangzhou was surnamed Zhen by birth. His family’s livelihood was farming and wood-gathering;
he was frequently sent to carry food to the fields, a task for which he felt deep distaste. Upon reaching the age of twenty, he became a bhikṣu and visited Qianyan, attaining profound realization.
Next, he went to visit his former teacher, knocking on the door and saying, "Though a thousand rivers differ, the bright moon remains one.
From this day forward, I have no more doubts. Later, he resided at Tiantong, where he restored all that was in ruin. On the day of his passing, he wrote a verse:
"A single snail’s stinking shell, Inside and out filthy and foul. Casting it aside, I go forth; The void rings with the bell. Tiantong’s single finger is as it was yesterday."
He cast aside his brush and passed away. The Chancellor Dashi Temür erected the Ciji (Compassionate Aid) Stūpa on the western ridge of Tianlong Mountain and interred his entire body there.
Chan Master Weian Deren of Songyin in Songjiang Prefecture was the son of the Zhang family of the local district.
In his youth, he received the tonsure under Master Guyong Wuyong. Later, he visited Qianyan and, upon hearing his formal teachings (*tichang*), suddenly realized the profound essence.

Thereupon, his reputation rose high; he succeeded to the seat at Shengshou Temple. He ascended the hall and said: "The hook is cast into the four seas, accustomed to catching whales and turtles; among the assembly, there is none who..."
"If you are one who does not begrudge life or limb, come forth and speak a word. A monk then asked, "Leaving the pines and waters behind, you have come to occupy Long Peak.
The assembly is gathered before the dais; we pray that the Master will offer a blessing for the Emperor. The Master said, "The ten-thousand-year-old pine stands upon Mount Zhurong."
The monk said, "I have already received the Master’s instruction regarding the invocation of the Sage; as for the ancestral style and affairs, what are they like?

The Master said, "When spring arrives, it is the one hundred and fifth day of the Cold Food Festival. The monk asked, "Is this not precisely where you, the Monk, benefit people? The Master said, "The axe-head is made of iron.
The monk said, "If that is so, then there are no overnight guests at Longmen. The Master said, "He has already been branded on the forehead. The monk said, "If not..."
Climbing the tower to gaze afar, who would have known the depth of the blue sea? The Master said, "Tell me, how many strands of eyebrows does this old monk have?
[The monk] replied, "In one hall, the wind is cold and still; through the ages, the meaning is clear. The Master said, "You have missed it by no small measure.
He then said, "The primary truth (the First Principle) has already been smashed to pieces by Dongbai’s single blow. We cannot help but turn toward the secondary truth (the Second Principle)."
The Gate. To reveal a bit of news: for several years, this mountain monk has been twisting a rope made of tortoise hair.

Today, I have taken it up and threaded through it in a single string the noses of the Buddhas of the three periods, the forty-seven patriarchs of the Western Heaven, the twenty-three patriarchs of this land, and all the old monks throughout the world.
Now tell me: do the mountains, rivers, the great earth, the grasses, trees, and forests, and the myriad phenomena of the universe [have a nose as well]?
"Sentiment and insentience—where did they come from? After a long silence, he said: "Do not take your idle scholarly interpretations and bury the mind of the Patriarch.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The wax man serves as the test; it begins this very day. At the end of the ninety days, we shall assess the merit and discern the mark.
The old, yellow-faced Gautama tied up the mouth of his sack, causing all hundreds of thousands of devas and humans to suffer indignity. Today, at Songyin, the retreat is established."
"Not at all like that. Making a gesture of rowing with his hands, he said: "I, this mountain monk, am now launching an iron boat without bottom;
I invite the great assembly to enter together into the Great Perfect Enlightenment Ocean to sport therein. He gave a shout and said: "Look! Take hold of the fixed compass.

Ascending to the top of the pagoda, he took up the precious rope and addressed the hall: "The hook and the rope are linked in a continuous chain; the continuous chain is the hook and the rope—this is the manifestation of the essence itself."
Fully revealed! Eye meets eye. When horizontal, it pierces through the nose of empty space; when vertical, it locks the iron pillar of Mount Sumeru.
Having been personally forged upon the fierce tongs of the Patriarchs, how can this be compared to the ordinary wrapping of hemp and paper?
This is the work of Layman Gu Baotang, a magnificent stupa that soars through the present and spans from antiquity. Although...
It is indeed so. But tell me: how shall one present this single phrase of being suspended high and hung upside down? "The four eaves are level and calm, encircled by clouds of incense;
for ten thousand ages the Buddha-sun shines with eternal brilliance."
The verse of farewell by Master Chang’an Ming-sǒu of Huāshān in Jīnhuá Fǔ, as he sat upright and passed away, says: "Birth is fundamentally not birth;
extinction likewise has no extinction. Casting off the hands, one simply goes forth—a sliver of moon in the void. Thus he passed away while sitting upright.
Chan Master Konggu Jinglong of Zhengzhuan Yuan in Hangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Bailian An. He was the son of the Chen family from Mount Dongting in Suzhou.
Once, a Japanese monk asked him, "What is Chan? The Master replied, "The Great Ming Country facing the Fusang Country. The monk said, "If that is so..."
"The wind blows the willows on the southern bank; the rain beats the lotuses in the northern pond. The Master said, "You are still clinging to external objects.
The monk asked, "What is it like to not cling to external objects? The Master said, "If you try to describe it as a single thing, it is no longer it.

The monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "This question is most intimate. The monk said, "Face-to-face, it is revealed in its full majesty. The Master said, "On the road..."
"The path is not yet the truth. He said, "If a man from the south were to ask about the snow, I would say it is *yanghua* (willow catkins).
The Master said, "Let him call a bell a jar as he pleases. He spoke this verse to his disciples: "The spring warmth and the vast winds blow;
In heart-rending pain, one seeks the Dharma like Sadāprarudita. Behold him turning and leaping in the void— He is truly a golden-maned lion cub. He also said, "Even regarding words..."
Externally, he accepted the responsibility; yet it was not granted that his magnificent writings could be measured. His transcendent single pivot is unfathomable by the spirit;
even when picked up, a piece of rubble gives off radiance.
This is the Dharma successor of Chan Master Fulin Du.
The Chan Master Wujie of Baofeng Mountain in Fanchang, Taiping Prefecture, went to consult Master Guzhu. The Master asked him, "Return to me the essence of illumination and function.

Wujie replied, "If there were illumination and function, they would immediately constitute an obstruction. The Master said, "This fellow clings to emptiness; even a Buddha could not save him. Wujie said, "Both existence and non-existence are quiescent; both emptiness and Buddhahood are entirely non-existent.

Later, the Master showed him this verse: "Existence and non-existence are both extinguished; Emptiness and Buddhahood are equally non-existent. If you wish to know the Way of the Buddhas, Do not seek it within the scriptures."
It is said: "Recalling the time of our parting at Fan-chang, how many people could have known this heart? This zither-less melody is truly worthy of continuation;
to whom shall this precarious life-intelligence be entrusted?"

The Dharma successor of Chan Master Wei of Dengwu, the twenty-fifth generation under Nanyue, was Chan Master Baozang Puchi of Mount Dengwu in Suzhou. He studied under Wanfeng, who bestowed upon him a verse of transmission, which began: "Dayu..."
Pain in the armpits and the clenching of the fist; the Three Essentials and Three Mysteries transcend both the orthodox and the biased. Within the lair of Linji, there are the cubs of the lion;
lamp after lamp continues the flame, transmitted through ancient and modern times. When Xubai visited the Master, he asked: "The mind is not the Buddha; wisdom is not the Way."
"How do you understand this? Baizhang replied, "I have come forward to inquire after your health," and stood with his palms joined.
The Master rebuked him, saying, "After all this time, you still hold such a view? Baizhang then became so indignant that he forgot to eat. By the second night, he attained great enlightenment.
The Master smiled and said, "Even though it is so, you must still protect and maintain it well yourself. He then sent forth a verse, which began: "The realization is clear and distinct..."
This is Chan. Advancing beyond the tip of the staff, transcending thought and speech, he proclaimed the ancestral Way, the doctrine of our school.
He entered the mountains again for twenty years and then passed away. A stupa was erected at his native mountain.
Chan Master Wunian Shengxue of Jiufeng in Wuchang Prefecture was the son of the Chen family of Yingshan in Suizhou.
In his youth, he took refuge with Master Wuji of Baolin Temple in his native prefecture as his teacher. Initially, he could not read a single character;

yet, after years of diligent practice, he realized that his own fundamental matter remained unclarified. He went to visit Master Wumen, who gave him the koan: "Where does it all return? Later, he entered Mount Song to dwell in seclusion.

He had a realization. A verse says: For many years on East Mountain, the mist hung thick; Leaning on the railing all day, I waited for the clear sky. Last night, suddenly I beheld the moon in the frosty heavens;
The myriad phenomena were fully revealed within a single mirror. Thereupon, he traveled extensively to visit veteran masters until he arrived at Dengwei to study under Wanfeng.

Wanfeng brought up the story of "the Ox Passing Through the Window Frame" and asked him to compose a verse upon it. The Master said: "The horns and head protrude with towering majesty... (The text continues with "four...")

Hoofprints. Throughout his entire life he passed through the fleeting moments as the moon sank in the west. If one can understand the pivotal moment and turn back, let out a roar once more without doubt. Feng certified this.
During the Hongwu era, the Taizu summoned him to the Fengtian Hall and personally questioned him on the essentials of the Dharma.

The Master offered this verse: "In the leisure between myriad affairs, investigate the true mystery; at the tips of the hundred blades of grass lies the Zen of Buddhas and Patriarchs. [The Emperor asked: "What about when a hair..."

The universe, with its dust-motes and lands, is entirely contained within a single pore; at the tip of a hair, the sky of one’s true nature appears. In meditative stillness, he sat watching clouds drift across the valley;

in the midst of his travels, he leisurely observed stones and bubbling springs. How may the patch-robed monks beneath the forest trees repay him? May they pray for the Emperor’s sacred life to endure for ten billion years.
The Emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed upon him a poem composed by His Imperial Majesty. In the third year of the Yongle era, he passed away, reciting this verse: "The World..."
Venerable Master Seventy-nine (79). Non-thought (80) at the limit. He shattered the Flower-Treasury Ocean; as before, the waters connect with the heavens. He passed away with solemn dignity.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at Shizi Rock. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Qingfu Guanghui.
When the head seat Guolín was visited by a monk for an interview, the Master threw down his meditation cushion and demanded a verse.

The monk said, "This very message is fundamentally beyond words; upon this broken meditation cushion, earth bursts forth and heaven splits asunder. The Master asked, "Tell me, what is it that splits?"
The monk was about to offer a word, and the Master struck him.
Chan Master Xizhu Benlai of Shutian Futi was a successor of Chan Master Cizhou Ji; he was a native of Chongren in Fuzhou. His secular surname was Pei. At the age of...
Thirteen: Setting out on foot, he went to pay his respects to Yifeng. Later, he went to Jinshan and saw Cizhou Ji, saying, "I, this student, have caught the thief;
I ask the Master to deliver a final judgment. Ji said, "I shall not question the thief; where is the stolen property?
The Master struck the incense table once with his fist. Ji shouted, "You have become so impertinent! The Master said, "The Monk has reached such a state..."
Bān was insolent. Zhòu asked, "I hear that when you first saw Yìfēng, it was true? The Master said, "It is true; I received thirty severe blows from him.
The official document has long been in my possession. Today I have come specifically to the Master’s place to seek a seal of approval."
Zhaozhou pointed to the flower in the pure vase and said, "Try to compose a verse on this. The Master said: "When the opportune moment strikes, he shatters the very bones of heaven and earth;
He scatters marrow across the sky, brilliant and flawless. Startled, the pure vase opens its mouth to laugh, Constantly spreading the flowers of the four seasons beyond the kalpas."

Zhaozhou said, "The Buddhas have not spoken it; the Patriarchs have not transmitted it. Setting aside the flapping of lips and the drumming of the tongue, and the blinking of eyes and the raising of eyebrows—bring me back the words for reaching home.
The Master remained silent. Zhaozhou approved of this. Not long after, he withdrew from view at Shousheng Temple on the Jian River.

When Prince Ning heard that the Master’s Way was transcendent, he dispatched an envoy with a letter, inviting him three times, but the Master did not go. The Prince sent another letter inquiring further.
The Emperor bestowed the honorary title "Master Chongxi" upon him. At Shouchang in Lichuan, during an assembly on the lecture hall, after finishing the offering of incense, he said:

"The heavens and sun are bright and the heat gradually intensifies; Pomegranate flowers erupt like fire, shining within the courtyard. Within the eyes of the patch-robed monks, the true mechanism is revealed; The person of no station is encountered face-to-face.
If you know the essential point directly, Any deliberation creates a thousandfold barrier. To reach the matter of one's own body, [look to] Huanglong."
At Mount Zuishang, he descended from his seat. Later, while residing at Futián Monastery at Shànguān in Mǐn, he restored a great monastery.
One day, as he sat in meditation with incense burning, he wrote this verse: "This old beggar—when will his teaching ever end? Tumbling and turning, he lets himself drift with the current;
Whether he is a sage or an ordinary person, no one understands. Ha! Come, come, come! Go, go, go! The ocean is still, yet the waves rise."
The air was clear and the moon was bright; he passed away silently. His worldly age was sixty-eight, and his monastic seniority was fifty-five.
Chan Master Wujì of Dōnglín in Pǔzhōu, a successor of Chan Master Jùn of Fánchāng, was a native of Shǔ. Chūshān went to visit him and asked: "In the years since you have resided here..."
“Where do you dwell? Baoshan said, “My dwelling is vast and empty; it has no fixed location. The Master asked, “What have you attained?
Baoshan said, “Originally there was nothing lost; what is there to be attained? The Master asked, “Is it not something learned?
Baoshan said, “Since not a single dharma exists, from where could learning come? The Master asked, “Have you fallen into emptiness? Baoshan said, “I am not even that.”

"I—who falls? Who is empty? The Master said, "Ultimately, what is it? Shanshan said, "The water is shallow and the stones appear; the rain has cleared and the clouds have dispersed. The Master said, "Do not speak in such confusion.
Even if the Buddhas and Patriarchs were to come, I would not permit you to let them loose. You have already swallowed the Tripitaka scriptures crosswise."
He manifested a hundred thousand supernatural powers. When [Nanquan] arrived there, he was no longer permitted to enter.

Nanquan said, "Although you, Master, hold fast to the essential pass, it is nonetheless a laborious and difficult task. The Master struck his knee once and asked, "Do you understand? Nanquan then gave a shout.
The Master laughed and said, "One who can sustain the family must be one who can break the family; doing so to manage the household affairs is truly effortless. Nanquan covered his ears and departed.
[He] emerged.
The lay practitioner He Mimian asked the Dharma heir Yangzhou Su’an Tian Dasheng: "By which gate does one exit onto the road to Putuo? The Master said: "Right here."

"From which gate do you enter now? he asked. The monk said, "Why do you restrain me so? The Master said, "Look beneath your feet. The monk raised his head, took three steps forward, and the Master said, "Wrong.
The monk stepped back three paces, and the Master said, "Wrong. The monk was at a loss. The Master said, "It is your fault; it is my fault as well.
The monk said, "Before you even raised [your hand], I already knew it was wrong. The Master pointed to his knee and said, "Right."
"You deserve a good beating," he said. The monk was speechless. The layman continued, "If you travel to other places, remember this clearly.
[This concludes the record of] Chan Master Chichi of Dengwu, the twenty-sixth generation descendant of Mount Heng (Nanyue), and successor in the Dharma lineage.
Chan Master Xubai Huichan of Dongming Temple in Hangzhou was the son of the Wang family from Huguang.
At the age of fourteen, he received the tonsure under Zhanran at Miaojue Temple in Danyang. One day, while he was engaged in manual labor, Zhanran asked him, "What are you doing here?
The Master replied, "I am slicing radishes. Zhanran said, "You only know how to slice radishes. The Master said, "I also know how to kill."
Ran invited Xuefeng to stay with him. Xuefeng said, "I do not execute surrendered generals. Ran then stayed at Shushan.

Hearing that Songyin was propagating the Way in Yunjian, he went there to seek instruction. Upon seeing Song, he attained realization. Later, when he met Baozang, he fully recounted the cause of his awakening.
Baozang rebuked him, whereupon the Master became so determined that he forgot to eat. On the second night, he suddenly penetrated to the very bottom of the Dharma source.
The verse says: With a single fist, he shatters the vast void; The ten billion Sumeru mountains leave no trace.
I ask you: who is the master within? A single red orb surges forth from Fusang. After receiving this entrustment, the Master went to Anxi and established a meditation hall (guan).

For over thirty years, his shadow did not leave the mountain. His reputation for the Way spread far and wide, and veteran practitioners vied with one another to seek instruction at his feet. Addressing the assembly, he said:
For thirty years I have dwelt alone among the forests and springs; a single staff in hand, my two brows knit together. Coming and going requires not the slightest effort.
I ask you, those who dwell amidst the waters and clouds: has the Dharma ever been transmitted to Hai-zhou? Ascending the seat, he said:
"Gautama had an intention to transmit it to whom? Kāśyapa needlessly broke into a smile. Reaching this point, how could even the Seven Buddhas claim superiority? Mañjuśrī’s face turns red."
I am utterly bewildered. Today’s amusing matter concerning Dongmyeong causes people to waste their saliva for a thousand ages. Fortunately, Master Haengwang forgot both self and other;
thus the single thread of the Jeongseon lineage continues unceasingly. He threw down his staff and said, "The burden of a thousand catties is now fully entrusted to you.
The mysteries and essentials shall now be discussed by means of this staff. He struck three times with his whisk and descended from the seat. Xuande.

On the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month in the year of Xinyou, he expressed his intention to pass away. When the assembly requested that he leave behind a verse, the Master said, "The entire Tripitaka has no one who can truly look upon it;
what need is there for these few idle words? Two days later, he passed away while sitting in the lotus posture.
His stupa was enshrined at Dongwu in Anxi.

The Chan Master Da-chan of Xuegu at Tianjie Mountain in Jianning Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Shouchang Lai, went to consult the Master. The Master showed him this verse: "All conditions arise together in competition;
Let them go and do not be startled by the cold. Simply take all the dharmas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges And gather them back into a single mass. [He] then lifted [the verse].
He overturned all obstacles and shattered the gates of the five aggregates (*skandhas*). Having fought back and defeated the demonic armies, the weapons of war were laid aside in peace.
Chan You was enlightened, and the Master praised him, saying: "Truly, the golden-haired lion has emerged from its den; The Wheel of Dharma has already turned as he enters the marketplace.
With a single roar, sudden and piercing, echoing through the vast sky, The wild beasts who hear it know their brains will split open."
Chan Master Chushan Shaoqi of Chengdu’s Dongshan Tiancheng Temple was a successor of Chan Master Wudeng of Donglin. He was the son of the Lei family of Tang’an.
Initially, he went to Xuanji Tong to study the world-transcending Dharma. Later, he visited Wuji, who assigned him the "Mu" (No) koan. One day, while listening by chance...
The wooden board rang out; the obstruction in his breast melted away like ice. He went to see Xuanji, who said, "Give me back the meaning of the word 'no'.
The Master replied, "This monk’s place of questioning is overly complicated. What did Zhaojue ever involve himself with through thought? A single word spoken from the mouth reveals everything."
[The Master] said, "This turns out to be in vain, causing people to doubt. He asked, "What is that place where you have no doubt? The Master replied, "Green mountains and blue waters;
swallows chirping and orioles singing—all distinct and clear. What more is there to doubt? [The Master] said, "Not yet. Speak further. The Master replied:
His head reaches the void; his feet tread upon solid ground. Xuanji said, "Not yet. The Master then prostrated. Xuanji said, "So it is, so it is. He resided at Touzi.
A monk asked, "Having distanced yourself from Mount Huan, you have come to occupy Touzi. The assembly of disciples is gathered before you."

"Please, Master, offer prayers for the Emperor. The Master said, "The long-life script within the cauldron; the ageless pine atop the peak. [The student] said, "I have already received the Master's instruction regarding the prayers for the Emperor.
As for the 'house style' (jiafeng) of Touzi, what is it like? The Master said, "Carrying a pitcher through the marketplace; he is not the oil-seller.
[The student] said, "As for the Patriarch’s saying, 'Do not travel at night; you must arrive by dawn,' is this truly so? The Master said, "He who travels at night does not see the moon."
[The student] said, "There is none. The Master said, "Though there may be sinews in the eyes, what can one do about the tongue having no bone?
[The student] asked, "Zhaozhou said, 'I have already had enough of Hou Bai; I have even more of Hou Hei. What was his meaning?

The Master said, "Had it not been for the exhaustion of arrows from the bow, he would not have consented to raise the flag of surrender. The Master entered the garden and saw the gardener tying a gourd vine. Pointing to a gourd, the Master said, "This..."
The head monk said, "This servant has no mouth. For what reason is he so tall and large?
The Master said, "Does your master ever exert any effort on your behalf? The head monk said, "I rely entirely upon his power.
The Master said, "Invite him here to meet with this old monk. The head monk bowed. The Master said, "He is still but a slave or a servant."

While the Master was present, he held a strip of bamboo in his hand and tied a gourd to a vine frame. The Master laughed heartily and, looking back at his attendant monk, said, "The vegetable garden has insects;
they have become numerous. On the fifteenth day of the third month in the ninth year of the Chenghua era, he manifested a slight illness. The assembly requested the Master’s final words.
The Master spread his two hands and asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not. The Master spoke again: "On this very day this year, pushing a cart, he crashes into a wall;
he knocks over empty space. A thunderclap in the blue sky! Ha ha ha! The mud ox swallows the old dragon’s pearl; the tranquil ocean of nature’s nature stills the foam-flowers.
Thereupon, he passed away with serene composure.
The verse of transmission from Chan Master Guangshan Baoyuetan of Mount Bafeng in Taipingfu to Dahui says:

"Though heaven and earth are vast, they cannot conceal it; Though the sun and moon are bright, their light cannot surpass it. The lamp of wisdom shall be perpetuated and never extinguished, Flowing through the ages to succeed the various schools."
The Dharma-transmission verse of Chan Master Cheng of Taigang and Yuexi in Nanjing says: "The mind is that which can know the mind;
Dharmas are that which can know dharmas. The Dharma-mind now transmitted is neither mind Nor is it dharma."
Chan Master Yuanxin of Funiu Mountain was the son of the Gao family of Jintai. He relied upon Master Wuji for investigation and study, later attaining liberation.
His verse says: "The Kunlun Mountains are overturned as the pure breeze dances; At the bottom of the ravine, the clay ox battles the stone tiger.
Striking the ancient pine, the eyes meet above the brows; The gnat tramples through the belly of empty space."
Chan Master Xuefeng Rui of Xichan Monastery in Chongqing Prefecture was visited by Tianqi, who had been contemplating the "Mu" (No) kōan.
After some time, Tianqi suddenly attained realization and replied: "Hard ice at the bottom of the ravine swallows the universe; the bright moon in the lake of nature fills the sky with cold.
The Master roared, "Do you still have a mind that detests the mundane and loves the sacred? Do you still have a view that sweeps away delusions to seek the truth? Tianqi said: "I do not."
The Master said, "If you detest the mundane and crave the sacred, you sever the roots of goodness of Prajñā.
If you sweep away delusion to seek the truth, you cut off the life-vein of all Buddhas. Shaking his voice, he shouted again, "Who is the 'true' one? And who is the 'deluded' one?"
"Who, indeed, is the ordinary person? Who, again, is the sage? At this, Qi was suddenly enlightened.
Master Shanjian Guting of Fushan was a native of Kunming in Yunnan. He took up the koan, "Where does the 'one' return?
One day, while in meditative concentration, he heard a monk say, "To see nothing is true seeing. Suddenly, he experienced a total liberation. Later, he went to...
Lung'en met Wuji; their words and spirits were in perfect accord. One day, Lung'en took his leave. Wuji asked, "Where will you go?
The Master replied, "I shall go to the crossroads to revile the Buddhas and curse the Patriarchs. Wuji asked, "Will you come back? The Master said: [Silence].
Without disobeying the venerable countenance of his *upādhyāya*, he liberated the floating mountain of the Dharma.
He was the twenty-seventh generation descendant of the Nanyue lineage and the dharma heir of Chan Master Dongming Chai.
Chan Master Haiming Zhou Puci of Dongming, Hangzhou, was the son of the Qian family of Changshu, Suzhou. His family had followed the Confucian tradition for generations.

He left the household life at Poshan Mountain and studied the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*. When he reached the passage stating, "Where there is only verbal expression, there is no real meaning," [he attained realization].
Having doubts, he went to visit Wanfeng. Wanfeng asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "Changshu. Wanfeng asked, "What brings you here?
The Master recounted his previous conversation and sought instruction. Wanfeng struck him twice on the head and said, "This very thing is the true meaning. The Master attained realization.
He subsequently built a thatched hut in a valley of Mount Dongting. Later, a monk scolded him, saying his realization was not yet free from attachments.
The Master then went to visit Dongming. One day, Dongming asked, "Have you ever seen a person? The Master replied, "I have seen Wansong.
Dongming said, "Where is Wansong right now? The Master was at a loss. Dongming said, "If that is so, when did you ever see Wansong? He then returned to his quarters.
For three days and nights, he forgot both sleep and food. By chance, a lapis lazuli lamp fell to the ground, and he suddenly attained great enlightenment.

He went to present his realization to Master Ming, who said, "Old *jiaoli*, you shall succeed Wanfeng. The Master replied, "Since you, Preceptor, have brought me to full penetration, how could I merely succeed Wanfeng?
Thereupon, Ming left the meditation hall, ascended the seat, and transmitted the Dharma to him. Not long after, Ming passed away, and the Master remained.
Taking his place on the seat, the Master addressed the assembly. He cited the case of Zhaozhou arriving at Huangbo; when Huangbo saw him coming, he immediately closed the door of his quarters.

Zhaozhou entered the Dharma Hall and cried out, "Put out the fire! Put out the fire! Huangbo opened the door, seized him, and said, "Speak! Speak! Zhaozhou replied, "Drawing the bow after the thief has fled.
The Master said, "These two elders would have caused the whole world to fall into doubt. At that time, there was a monk who asked, 'Does the Master have any doubts?'"

"What is it? The Master said, "If you fail to catch the thief when he is caught, you will be laughed at by the thief. The monk said, "The Master must also possess the eye of discernment to begin with.
The Master then struck him. The monk bowed. The Master offered this verse: "One capture, one release; two skills displayed.
Spears fly and lances come; two armies arrayed. Who can recognize the secret mechanism of both? To this day, it leaves General Li in doubt. [This was shown to Chun.]
The Master related: A monk asked Muzhou, "What is it like when a single word exhausts the Way? Muzhou said, "The old fellow is inside your bowl bag.
The Master said, "Look! This monk was like a tiger emerging from the forest; Muzhou gently drew him back into a heavy net and buried him in a deep pit.
A monk asked, "What is the place of the heavy net and deep pit? The Master said, "I will tell you after you have prostrated."
The monk bowed and rose. The Master asked again, and the monk wept, saying, "My father! My mother! The monk was at a loss for what to do. The Master struck him, saying:
"I will not go out. Come back another time. The verse says: "Questioning people is easy; grasping the pivot is difficult. It lies merely within their snapping of fingers.
If one awakens to the sound of wailing in the alms bowl, The seventeen hundred cases are all pierced at once. [He] addressed the assembly.
A monk asked Touzi: "Vague and indistinct like a half-moon, faintly resembling three stars; neither heaven nor earth can contain it—where does the Master perceive it?
Touzi said, "What are you saying? The monk said, "I suspect the Master has only the ripples on still water."
"Moreover, there is no wave that floods the heavens. The Master said, "Idle talk. The teacher said, "This monk’s literary style is brilliant;
Touzi has maintained his fundamental standard. If he were a descendant of Linji, he would have been given a severe beating and driven out. He then offered this verse:
In the inner palace, the night is still and the hundred flowers are fragrant; wishing to roll up the pearl curtains, one finds the spring resentment long.
Slantingly embracing the three stars, their light rivals the sun; the hazy tree colors conceal the Shaoyang Palace. In the first year of the Jingtai era, he entered nirvana, uttering this verse:
"For ninety-six years I have been in the world; for seventy-four years I have been a monk. Amidst these many complications and contradictions, a single glance at Dongming brings them to an end."
He passed away. Taking his whisk, he drew a circle and said, "From Śākyamuni to me, there have been sixty-two generations of innumerable old monks who mostly established themselves here.
With a shout of "Tut!", he passed away peacefully. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa to the left of the mountain.
Chan Master Da-chan Huitong of Juefeng Peak in Shaozhou, a successor of Chan Master Tianjie Zhong, was the son of the Shao family in Zhenghe, Jianning. He left the household life at Doufeng.
Initially, he studied under Zhou the Mountain Master and stayed in seclusion at Yantou Hermitage. Subsequently, he studied under Xuegu, where one night he attained realization.
He immediately presented this verse: "Holding the axe of pure wind in hand, The crown of Vairocana is split open.

The teachings of the Buddhas of the three thousand worlds— I bring them all forth, string upon string. Guke approved it. In the autumn of the Gui-si year of the Chenghua era, he arrived at Yanjing (Beijing).

The eunuch Huang Gao built a temple for the Master and memorialized the Emperor, who granted it the name Zhengfa (Orthodox Dharma). On the day of the opening of the hall, a monk asked: "How does one without eyes blow [the conch]?"
He heard the sound of a flute. The Master said, "Prostrate yourself; I shall speak to you. The monk prostrated. The Master said, "The sound! The sound! How could one be without eyes?

At this, the monk was suddenly enlightened. Later, he resided at Junfeng. On the seventeenth day of the second month in the fourteenth year of the Hongzhi era, he recited his verse of departure from the world, saying:
"In human life, reaching seventy is rare since ancient times; To add another year is even more extraordinary. If..."
Question: "Where has the old monk gone? Answer: "He is laughing heartily within the great void. He bathed and passed away.

Chan Master Xing of Dayun Monastery in Xiangyang Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Qi of Tiance. He followed Chushan down the mountain; upon returning along the way, his nature became empty. Original Text.
Jie [the temple attendant] and three others from Duan’an came to welcome him. Yanshan asked, "Tell me, where have I come from? Kōng said, "I know where the Master has been.
Jie said, "The weather is bright and warm today. An said, "It was no easy matter for the Master to climb the mountain.
Yanshan looked at the Master (Shishi) and asked, "What do you say? The Master replied, "The assembly has been standing for a long time; please return to the temple, Master. Yanshan [departed].
[The Master] asked, "Where is the temple? The Master said, "The sound of the bell rings well. Yunmen laughed and said, "The horns are somewhat similar;
the nostrils are the same. Upon arriving home, each shall receive thirty blows of the staff. The assembly bowed together once. Yunmen turned his body and departed.
Chan Master Jinshan Bao of Zhuozhou went to visit Chushan. Chushan asked, "Facing south to gaze at the Northern Dipper, lingering to look at the blue sky—what matter does this statement clarify?
The Master said, "It would be better if you, Reverend, would simply close your mouth. Chushan said, "Not yet.
The Master said, "One might get away with deceiving others. Chushan said, "As for the application of differentiation, nothing can be done without the eye of wisdom."
[The Master] was perplexed. [Zhaozhou] said, "If you wish to penetrate and clarify the true teaching of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, you must possess the correct eye that passes through the barrier.

I wonder, what is this 'correct eye that passes through the barrier'? The Master let out a thunderous shout. Shanshan said, "Having attained the correct eye, one should clarify the ultimate pivot beyond.
[Zhaozhou] asked, "What is this ultimate pivot beyond? The Master said, "The sun at high noon in a clear blue sky. Shanshan said, "I have not yet dreamed of it."

[Zhaozhou] was present. The Master said, "The wooden man picks up the jade thread; the stone woman passes the golden needle. Zhaozhou asked, "How do you understand this wondrous secret that has not been transmitted by the Buddhas and Patriarchs since antiquity? The Master stepped forward and bowed. The Master said, "Speak quickly that turning-phrase. The Master said, "The rain makes the mountain colors more exquisite; the wind comes and the shadows of the grasses shift. As the Master was about to pick it up [to strike him], Zhaozhou said: [Zhaozhou said: "If you had spoken before I had even finished my question, I would have struck you dead on the spot. "Where does the resonance return? The Master said, "After the sound of the bell has arisen. Shan said, "The ear is the faculty (*indriya*); the resonance is the object (*viṣaya*). What is it that knows the resonance?
The Master said, "It is not the mind that does not resonate; it is not the resonance that is not the mind. Shan said, "How could the mind have resonance?
The Master said, "Although the mind is not the resonance, the place of resonance is distinct and clear. The Master said, "At a time when there is no resonance, where is the mind?"
Dazu said, "The essence of the mind is profoundly still; it does not arise following an echo, nor does it perish following an echo. This is because the two ears are empty and penetrating;
therefore, its application is unimpeded. Shanshan asked, "Are you speaking of principle? Dazu replied, "How could I not speak of it?"
Shan [Buchu] struck him. The Master prostrated.
While Zhuzi Chan Master Shijing Haiju was closing his retreat, Chushan knocked on the gate once and said, "I request the master within the gate to come forth and see me.
The Master stood with hands clasped and body bowed. Shan asked, "How do you conduct yourself in your daily activities?"
The Master said, "Look at the word 'wu' (no). Zhaozhou Shan asked, "What is the meaning of the word 'wu'? The Master said, "An unperforated iron hammer is hurled right in your face.
Shan asked, "What was Zhaozhou’s intention? The Master said, "It is simply because his compassionate heart is so earnest that he pours out his very liver and gall toward others.
Shan asked, "How can one realize that which does not involve existence or non-existence? The Master said, "When I reached this point..."
"There is no place for the application of mind. Shanshan said, "Already you have applied your mind. The Master said, "I do not even know [how to apply it].
Shanshan said, "Who says you do not know? The Master said, "Even 'saying' is not it. Shanshan said, "Wait until I have passed through the pass, and I will give you a blow."
The Master said, "I am not even within the pass right now. He struck the gate once and said, "What about here?
The Master let out a shout. Xishan said, "Not yet; speak further. The Master said, "The spiritual mechanism is without obstruction; walls provide no hindrance. Xishan also shouted.
The Master stepped forward, made a formal inquiry, and said, "Thank you for your instruction. Xishan said, "The weather is sweltering; take care."

Zen Master Chōsō Daishin Shingen was the son of the Zhang family of Sanchi.

He visited Chusan and asked about the point where the words and deeds of the Buddhas and patriarchs of antiquity do not reach, requesting that the Master point it out directly. The Master held up his staff and said, “Huh? The Master gave a shout, and Chusan—
[Shishuang] struck him. The Master shouted again. Shishuang struck once more and said, "Do you say that this was a good blow? The Master then seized the staff and asked, "What are you hitting?
Shishuang gave a shout. The Master prostrated himself. Shishuang asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "Fundamentally, there is neither movement nor stillness.
Shishuang asked, "Why have you come here? The Master replied, "The place of arrival is also not [existent]. Shishuang asked, "With whom [are you speaking]?"
They were traveling together. The Master said, "A wild crane soars alone beyond the Milky Way; a clear moon shines solitary within the realm.
Sansheng said, "If one suddenly encounters a fierce tiger on the road, how does one avoid it? The Master asked, "Where is the tiger? Sansheng then made the sound of a tiger.
The Master acted out a gesture of fear. Sansheng said, "In that case, have you personally seen a tiger come? The Master then acted as if he had seen one.
Heshan made a tiger’s roar. Shishuang laughed loudly and said, “In the course of your daily activities, what do you employ as your mind?
The Master replied, “I open my two eyes wide alone; I stretch out my two feet and sleep. Shishuang asked, “Is there anything further beyond this?
The Master said, “Under a clear sky, the moon shines upon the cold plum blossoms; in a freezing night, frost strikes the sparse wood leaves. Shishuang said, “Just so...”
"Is this it? Is there anything else? The Master said, "A red bird flies from the branch of an ancient tree.
Yunmen said, "The final phrase is where one first reaches the secure barrier; it blocks the essential ford, allowing neither ordinary person nor sage to pass. How do you understand this?"
The Master said, "The clay ox enters the sea and swallows the old dragon’s pearl. Yunshan said, "Not yet.
The Master stepped forward, crossed his hands, and stood in silence. Yunshan said, "So it is, so it is."
Stonejing Huotang Zu’an Chan Master was the son of the Ju family of Chengdu. He went to attend upon Chushan.
At a time when Chushan was reading a scripture, the Master stepped forward and, holding up the scripture, asked, "What is this? Chushan gave a shout and said, "Tell me, what is it?
The Master also shouted. Chushan then snatched the scripture away, held it up, and said, "The hundreds of thousands of samādhis and the immeasurable wondrous meanings."
"All have flowed forth from this sutra. Do you, my son, know the source from which this sutra emerges? The Master snapped his fingers once.

Xuefeng Shan said, "The functional application of Prajñā-wisdom—you have now attained it. He then handed the sutra to the Master, saying, "You must still read through every single character and phrase from the beginning;
come back and deliberate with me. The Master took the sutra, prostrated, and departed.
Chan Master Changyun of Yingshan in Zhongxi went to visit Chushan. Chushan asked, "What is your name? The Master replied, "Changyun.
Chushan asked, "What is your style (hao)? The Master replied, "Yingshan. Chushan said, "Clouds are hidden within the mountains; why then do they emerge from the mountains?
The Master replied, "It is simply because last night a crane carried them across the highest barrier. Chushan said, "Perhaps they will become rain for the fields."
"What is it like at that time? The Master said, "It is spread throughout the entire world. Xuefeng said, "What is it like when it is suddenly blown apart by a fierce wind?
The Master said, "As before, it is a clear blue sky and bright day. Xuefeng then laughed.
Chongshan Yitian Zhi, the Imperial Preceptor from Pengxian, resided at Beici Monastery in Songpan. He possessed extraordinary features from birth.

At the age of twelve, he took Yueguang as his teacher. Later, he settled in Songpan; at that time, the local tribes were inconsistent in their allegiance, sometimes rebelling and sometimes submitting.
The Master governed and transformed [the people] through his compassion; there were none who did not submit to him. During the Tiānshùn era, he was repeatedly conferred the title of National Teacher.

When Chūshān came to visit him, the Master presented the details of his realization. Chūshān asked, "What is the meaning of 'Mu' (No)? The Master replied, "A hair-piercing sword drawn from its scabbard;
its cold light shoots toward the Dipper and Ox. Chūshān said, "Why did Zhàozhōu say 'Mu'? The Master replied, "A Persian chewing ice and snow does not even realize it."
Shangzhi said, "Chilly teeth! Setting aside 'existence' and 'non-existence,' how can you find a place to settle?
The Master said, "In the deep of night, who holds hands to stroll together through the imperial street? Shangzhi said, "Is there anything more extraordinary beyond this?

The Master said, "Every house has its moon in autumn; everywhere there are flowers in spring. With a pair of clear, bright eyes, where could one scatter a grain of dust? Shangzhi said, [and remained silent].
"Excellent.
Chan Master Yueguang Changhui of Sanchi, a native of the Li clan of Jianzhou, went to visit Chushan.
Chushan asked, "How do you apply yourself to practice throughout the six periods of the day? The Master replied, "I look at the word 'wu' (no). Chushan asked, "What is this word 'wu'? The Master—

[The Master] said, "Just now, as you went up the mountain, you were so overcome with drowsiness. Mountan said, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The autumn moon is cold as the wind blows;
the old plum tree is frigid under the weight of snow. Mountan said, "Give me back your verse on the word 'Mu' (No). The Master said, "No, no—where there is no 'no,' there is likewise not even 'no.
The clouds disperse across the vast sky and the moon stands solitary. From antiquity to the present, it has never been obscured; if one wishes to..."
His name was inscribed in the lineage charts of the patriarchs. Mount Ken approved of this.
While Chan Master Gaoyin Shao of Tianning was in retreat behind closed doors, Chushan knocked on the gate three times with his staff and said:
"Is the master of the gate here? The Master said, "He never comes or goes; who says he is present or absent? He immediately opened the gate and prostrated himself.
Yunmen said, "This is still the business of servants and slaves. I ask to meet the master of the gate. The Master stood with his hands folded in silence.
Yunmen said, "In that case, you have gone into silent oblivion. The Master asked, "What did you just ask, Master? Yunmen—

[The Master] said, "I ask you, the master of Guanzhong. The teacher replied, "Can it be called 'silent stillness'? He then presented a verse, saying: "This very silent stillness is not silent stillness;
Within what is not silent stillness, even 'not' is cut off. His true face has already been presented to the Master;
In movement and stillness, how could there ever be a distinction? The Master said, "If that is so, then you are not within Guanzhong? The teacher replied, "I am."
Jiashan saw that Jiawu was also not outside the barrier. He struck the gate with his hand and said, "What can be done about this?
As the Master was about to respond, Jiashan rebuked him.
Cuiwei Wukong Chan Master was a native of Shaanxi. Chushan asked him, "When the great earth is overturned, there is not an inch of soil remaining;
when the source is thoroughly exhausted, there is not a single thing left. How do you understand this? The Master said, "All stars bow toward the North;
no water does not flow toward the East. Chushan asked, "In this matter, is there still any need for the practice of cultivation and effort?"
The Master said, "There is no lack of actual practice, yet its functioning cannot be grasped. Shanshan said, "Even this very 'cannot-be-grasped' state cannot be grasped.
What about you, sir? As the Master prepared to open his mouth, Shanshan let out a resonant shout. The Master said:

"There is no dharma outside the mind; before one's eyes are green mountains. "How do you understand this? The Master said, "There is no mind outside the dharma;
green mountains fill the eyes. Thereupon, they met like a needle and its eye. He then entered the room with the assembly. In the fifth year of the Tiānshùn era, he resided at Gāozuò Monastery.
Small Assembly Sermon at the Opening of the Retreat: Sitting in a dense mass beneath three rafter-beams, I have stilled body and mind like cold ashes.
Yet, from within the hearth, I stir forth a spark of fire—a single clap of thunder that startles heaven and shakes the earth.

Within this hall, everyone is a sharp-witted monk, a practitioner of the fundamental Dharma. Is there anyone here who does not spare their eyebrows? Come forward and ask a question! Is there such a person?
Is there such a thing? Before the fifteenth day, you are not permitted to touch it; after the fifteenth day, bring forth a single phrase.
Someone said, "Every day is a good day. If that were so, it would be far too clear-cut—what more would there be to discuss?
Whether in a small or great assembly, speaking horizontally or vertically, there are times when the Buddhas of the three periods of time preach the Dharma to a pillar;

one finds the fire along with the smoke. There are times when the brazier preaches the Dharma and the Buddhas of the three periods of time listen intently; one returns carrying spring water and wearing the moon.

If you can understand it in this way, you will also be able to contain Mount Sumeru within a mustard seed; the infinitesimal becomes identical to the immense, and all boundaries are forgotten and severed.

Mount Sumeru can contain a mustard seed; the vast and the minute are one, their boundaries and surfaces unseen. Just as the large and the small contain one another, the one and the many are without obstruction.
When the tree withers and the leaves fall, its essence is revealed in the golden wind. How would you deliberate upon this? Beneath the gate of the great sun, every day is mid-autumn;
before the hall of the bright moon, every moment is mid-summer. Viewed through the correct eye, these two are fires.
The furnace: the Buddhas of the three periods dwell within it. Within the *qīngzhōu* cotton robe, there is no room for a head to emerge;
within a single grain of mustard seed, ten billion Mount Sumerus are contained. Within Yunmen’s “millet cake,” there is not even space to open one's mouth.
You two halls of wandering monks—try to pierce it, yet you cannot pierce it; try to bite it, yet you cannot break it. At this very moment, tell me: is this small? Or is it large?
"San" is the Great San. Do you understand? From between his eyebrows, he squeezed forth adamantine flames; the lamp-stands and lanterns all emitted light.

In the autumn of the Gui-si year of the Chenghua era, he passed away while seated. The assembly was all deeply moved by grief. The Master slowly opened his eyes and said, "There is no need for this," and then closed them again.
Chan Master Rulin of Yufeng in Shanfu was asked by Chushan, "Where do you apply your mind? The Master said, "There is no place where I apply my mind.
Chushan said, "If that is so, then you are wasting your time in vain. The Master said, "The void shatters into a hundred fragments."
"Vastly clear and utterly distinct. Mount said, "What is this matter of being distinct? The Master said, "If you recognize the countenance of the Lord of Spring, heaven and earth are all spring.
Mount said, "Not yet. The Master said, "The face-gate and nostrils hang down with great weight."
Mount [Dayang] said, "Have you reached the ground of non-doubt in this way? The Master replied, "I do not dwell here either. The Mountain asked, "Where, then, do you dwell?
The Master said, "Neither clinging to existence nor to non-existence; my entire being is utterly beyond conceptualization.
The Mountain said, "At this very point where there is no conceptualization, you should now properly engage in conceptualization. The Master then assented.
"Agreed," [the Master] said. Shanshan asked, "Tell me, at the point where thought is cut off, how can one think? The Master replied, "Not thinking, not thinking.
Shanshan nodded his head in approval.
Attendant Zujié of Guian was very ill and made sounds of pain. Chushan asked, "Does the phrase upon which you have relied for strength during your daily practice still serve you well at this moment?
The Master replied, "It serves me well. Chushan said, "If it serves you well, why do you cry out in pain?
The Master replied, "When it hurts, one cries; when it itches, one laughs. Chushan asked, "As for this laughing and crying, who is it that does so?"
"Who is it? the Master asked. "The four elements are without self; even the one crying out is not real. Within the essence of quiescence, there is truly no experiencer.
Shan said, "The master of the house—where is he right now? The Master replied, "The autumn wind does not fan; the cassia blossoms waft their fragrance."
Mount Shandao said, "If that is so, then the entire world is free from concealment. The Master said, "Even with eyes, one cannot see it.
Shandao said, "As for the moment when the three-inch breath is extinguished—where will you establish yourself and find your life?

The Master said, "When the rain has passed and the sky is clear, the green mountains remain as they were. Shandao said, "After we part from now on, will we meet again? The Master said, "Throughout kalpas beyond measure."
"Not so," [Zhaozhou] replied. "What interval is there now? Shishuang said, "If that is so, then you have never been ill.
The Master said, "Illness and non-illness—neither concerns me. Shishuang then took his hand and asked, "What is this? The Master said, "It is the Patriarch."
Jie touched the mountain with his hand. The Mountain asked, "Who is this Jie? The Master said, "Jie is certainly not me, yet he is not separate from me.
The Mountain sighed and said, "Excellent! This very state of being neither identical nor separate perfectly accords with the non-arising of phenomena.

Since you have now clearly realized the principle, though you are young in years, you will have no regrets even in death. The Master then joined his palms and told the Mountain, "Please quickly urge me to take my seat."

The shrine arrived. Master Shan ordered it to be carried to him. The Master looked at the assembly and said, "I am departing. He then straightened his body, sat upright, closed his eyes, and passed away.
[He was] a Dharma successor of Chan Master Guanshan Tan.
Chan Master Dahui Juehua of Chongfu Temple in Nanjing was the son of the Liu family from Wiyang.
Initially, he sought instruction from Haidan Ci and attained a realization. Subsequently, he went to Fanchang in Taiping to visit Baoyue, whereupon he received certification of his realization.

Later, while presiding over the temple, he ascended the hall and, raising his whisk, said: "Beyond the limit of Vītarāga, it has always been this very thing; even now, before our eyes, it is likewise this very thing."
This very thing—this mountain monk brings it forth and sweeps up and down, sweeping left and right.
If you call it a whisk, you blind the eyes and ears of humanity and the heavens. If you do not call it a whisk, you likewise blind the eyes and ears of humanity and the heavens.
O Great Assembly, what ultimately shall you call it? If you can understand this, then you will know why Kāśyapa smiled and why the Second Patriarch sought his mind.
"An unattainable place. He transmits the lamp of the Tathāgata and continues the orthodox lineage of the Patriarchal Hall;

"All things are without remainder; all things are without obstruction. All things are without obstruction; all things are without remainder. If one can penetrate this...

the winding waters are like brocade, a single bay of green. To the assembly: Everyone’s nostrils reach toward the heavens;

Xuán. Dōngshān forcibly divided the five ranks; only when one breaks through the "water-buffalo of Mount Huìshān" does one realize that Sēngcǎn was without fault.

"Existence! It is as if one has perished on the other side of the kalpa of emptiness; do not come here to engage in forced discourse. He then took up his staff and said:
"It once accompanied me on night journeys, startling at fierce tigers; how many times have we ascended together to the peaks of emerald vines?"
Chan Master Fashou Daoji of Tianning Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture was a dharma heir of Chan Master Jigan Zuo. He was the son of the Zhang family of that same prefecture.

Having relied upon Chan Master Dong of Dongchan Monastery to become a bhikṣu, he later visited Jigan. While walking along the corridors, he suddenly heard the sound of a *qing* bell and attained awakening. He then proceeded to the Dharma hall.

As he entered the hall, Zen Master An looked at him and smiled, saying, "You have been caught by the thief. The Master said, "The thief has already been apprehended. An asked, "Where is the stolen goods?
The Master held up his sitting cloth (*zuoju*) and said, "A mess! A total mess! An said, "You empty-headed charlatan! What is there to be a mess about?
The Master gave a shout and returned to the assembly. Zen Master An was pleased and certified him. At the beginning of the Jiajing era, he emerged from seclusion at Jinling. The monk—
Question: "What is the realm of peace and security? The Master said: "Three mountains half-fallen beyond the blue heavens;
two waters dividing White Heron Island. Question: "What is the family style of peace and security? The Master said: "A stone tiger fights before the mountain;
a clay ox sleeps at the bottom of the water. Question: "I do not understand. The Master said: "What is there to understand? Not long after, he returned to Tianning and addressed the assembly, citing:

Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty asked Bodhidharma, "What is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths? Dharma replied, "Vast emptiness; there is no sage. The Emperor asked, "Who is it that stands before me?
Dharma said, "I do not know. The Emperor did not attain realization. The Master [Zhaozhou] composed a verse on this: "Vast emptiness—no sage; the wheel of activity ceases.
The hundred thousand gates of the heavy barrier are shattered. After the rain, fallen flowers cover the ground in red; Walking..."
People still do not know that spring has come. Addressing the assembly: In Jingyan Temple the bell is struck; atop the watchtower of the prefectural seat the drum is beaten.
Simultaneously manifesting great spiritual powers, they penetrate through a thousand gates and ten thousand doors. Does the assembly hear them? If you say you do not hear them—
"But how can one deny that the bells and drums are distinct? Everyone has ears. If you say you hear them, with what do you hear?
Right now the drums have ceased and the bells have faded; as for the matter of hearing, what is it? He said, "Speak quickly! Speak quickly!
He then struck the meditation staff and said, "Gold has its own price; it is never sold to others mixed with sand. A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Full."
The words did not issue from his mouth. The monk asked the Master again, "One time you raised it; one time there was a new question: 'How was it before Bodhidharma had not yet come?
The Master said, "The ancient mirror is clear and distinct, containing the myriad phenomena. [The monk] asked, "And after he had come? The Master said:
"The myriad phenomena are clearly revealed within the ancient mirror. [The monk] asked, "What is its use? The Master said, "If it did not come forth, the ancient mirror would be buried.
[The monk] asked, "The Buddhas hand over to the Buddhas; the Patriarchs transmit to the Patriarchs. I wonder, what is it that they transmit? The Master said, "Sulu sulu, sili sili.
While sitting by the stream, a monk asked, "What is the phrase for 'following the waves and drifting with the current'?"

The Master said, "On both banks, the spring breeze carries fragrance without ceasing; in the single stream, the falling petals are ever fresh. The monk asked, "What can be done, Master? I do not understand.
The Master said, "The dragonfly flies still slowly; the butterfly dances all too busily. The monk said, "The Master is merely showing me the scenery.
The Master let out a thunderous shout. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Not yet. Speak further. The monk was speechless. The Master [said], "..."
He said: "To cry until the blood flows is of no use; it is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring.
A scholar playing chess asked, "How must one move the pieces to be truly skillful? The Master said, "Look at making that first move when black and white have not yet been distinguished.

The scholar made the gesture of placing a piece. The Master said, "A marvelous hand! A marvelous hand! Lu Wutai asked, "Was there originally the *Yi* (the Book of Changes) before the lines were drawn?"
The Master said, "If there were no Fuxi, what would one have to paint? [The student] asked, "What is it like after the painting? The Master said, "Originally, there was not a single stroke.
[The student] said, "There are currently sixty-four hexagrams; how can you say they do not exist? The Master said, "Do not cling to words and letters.

[The student] said, "I ask the Master to set aside words and letters and manifest a single line for me to see. The Master called out, "Tai! Tai responded, "Yes. The Master said, "This is that one line."
From where does it arise? The Master showed a verse to a young man, saying: "To study the Way, one must have a youthful body;
yet often because of youth, one wastes the prime of spring. If one says that youth can be relied upon, then there should be no young people in the desolate graves.
When a monk from India arrived, the Master provided him with a mat to sit upon. At the second watch, he saw three divine beings enter, wearing tall caps and crimson robes. The Master...
He questioned them in astonishment, and they all replied, "We are the guardian deities of this monastery. We have come to visit you because you had entered into profound meditative absorption.
Thereupon, they vanished. Later, in the autumn, his illness became critical. When someone requested that he speak a verse, the Master said, "These are merely literary embellishments;
there is no need for such things. He passed away while gesturing with his hand. He was seventy-four years old and had sat in meditation for fifty-two summer retreats.

those who heard him were filled with joy and satisfaction. Entering the hall for discourse, he said: "The swift passage of time is like flowing water;

There is no tail. Nevertheless, though the ink may stain the paper and turn to ash, what can be done? The original life-source (*mìngběn yuánchén*) of everyone is entirely contained within it.

Chan Master Wansong Huilin of Jingshan in Hangzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Jintai Jue. He was the son of the Shen family from Renhe.

While staying overnight at Tongtang in the capital, he heard a monk reciting the words of Danxia’s discourse on the hall and attained great enlightenment. Later, he visited Jintai and presented his understanding; thereupon—
He attained the Dharma. Later, he resided at Mount Jing. One day, he wrote a verse: "For seventy-six years, my life has been like a drifting weed—upon what can it rely?
Fundamentally there is no coming or going; it merely responds to conditions. Having said this, he passed away peacefully.

Chan Master Wuyue Xiao, surnamed Ye’weng, a successor of Chan Master Tianmu Jin, came to attend upon the Master. The Master instructed him to contemplate the koan: "Where does the one return? Later, Xiu attained realization.
The Master bestowed upon him a verse, saying: "Not dharma, not non-dharma; Not nature, not non-nature; Not mind, not non-mind."
The Mind. I have now finished transmitting the Dharma of the mind to you.
Chan Master Gu-yin Jing-qin of Dou-feng in Jian-ning Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Shou-tang Song. He was the son of the Cai family of Jian-yang. He studied under Wan-fa Gui...
