The Master said, "I am not deceiving you; I am striking you because you do not know the phrase that encompasses them both. The Lecturer said, "What is it? The Master said, "Strike! The Lecturer said, "This is the phrase that encompasses them both. The Master said, "You have been struck by the phrase that encompasses them both. The Lecturer said, "Master, why do you deceive people? The Master said, "I am not deceiving you; I am striking you because you do not know the phrase that encompasses them both. The Lecturer said, "What is it? The Master said, "Strike! The Lecturer said, "This is the phrase that encompasses them both. The Master said, "You have been struck by the phrase that encompasses them both. The Lecturer said, "Master, why do you deceive people? The Master said,
"Qian and Kun. At such a time as this, where would the Dharma Master begin? The host had no reply. After a long silence, the Master said, "Welcome, Dharma Master!
You have returned from the city of Hangzhou. He then addressed the assembly: "While I was within the realm of Lake and Mountains, I composed a piece on the Buddha-dharma."
"This was indeed straightforward, pertinent, simple, and clear. I longed to return and show it to the assembly, but when we met today, I had forgotten it.
He then raised his whisk and asked, "Do you remember? In the winter of the Jia-mao year of the Wanli era, I said to my disciple Xingchong:
'Between the fifth and sixth days of the Mid-Autumn Festival next year, I wish to depart.'"
"You should come. On the sixth day of the eighth month of the following year, Chong arrived as previously commanded. The Master manifested a slight ailment, spoke a verse, and passed away.
The verse says: "Coming from birth and going to death are like empty flowers; From death returning to birth is but a single dream. This skin bag is entrusted to the god of fire (Cing-ding-kung);
These white bones shall cross the broken bridge with the multitude. Hehe! Under bright moon and clear wind, one plays the lute. His stupa was erected at his own hermitage.
Chan Master Daixiu Zonglong of Qijian Peak in Suizhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Shimen Hai. He was the son of the Jia family of Yidu in Qingzhou.
While serving as the head cook at Beisi Temple in Chengdu, he suddenly struck a wall while carrying water and attained realization. He then went to visit Wujin at Qianming Temple.
At the temple, he eventually received the seal of approval and transmission. After taking up residence there, he presented three "gateless barriers" (huatou) to instruct his students, saying:
"A precious sword that shaves hair as it flies has been taken away by a stone man and hung atop a ten-thousand-fathom peak; the four walls offer no path. How can it be recovered?
There is a wish-fulfilling jewel that has been brought forth by a wooden man and cast into the waves of the great ocean; without relying on a boat or oars, how can it be retrieved?"
He found it. The entire earth is a pit of fire; everything has been burned away, leaving only a single strand of eyebrow hair.
I wonder: who can see this? His verse on entering nirvana says: "Grasping the three periods of time as a staff, The ten directions are originally one’s old kashaya robe.
The clay ox and stone tiger know the news: Treading through empty space, one arrives home. He sat upright.
He passed away.

Chan Master Tianzhen Daojue of Doupeng in Jianning Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Doufeng Qin; he was the son of the Zhang family of that same prefecture. While contemplating "Where does the one return?"—
While staying there, he had an awakening and composed a verse, saying: "One hand claps, one hand drums; The person of no-position performs a dance beyond the ordinary.
From the mouth, a tuneless song is sung; The three thousand Buddhas share the same mother. He presented this "ancient sound" and immediately received the Master’s seal of approval.
The Five Lamps Adorning the Lineage, Volume Twenty-Five;
The Five Lamps Adorning the Lineage, Volume Twenty-Four:
The Linji School.

Chan Master Xiangyan Yuexin Debao of Beijing, a successor of Chan Master Longquan Cong of the thirty-first generation under Nanyue, was the son of the Wu family of Jintai. His lineage was that of the Jin-yi (Silk Guard) nobility; his mother was...
He was born on a clear day when a great thunderclap suddenly shook the earth. After he had reached the age of capping, he could not bear remaining in the secular world.
At twenty-two, he paid homage to Guanghui Daji, shaved his head, and received full ordination. He first visited Guzhuo Dachuan, and later went up to Guanzilizheng to visit Wumen.
When he presented his previous realizations, Wumen certified them all. Suddenly, hearing the sound of the pestle in the mortar room, he immediately raised [the koan].

The Master answered him accordingly. Wumen said, "What you have attained is correct. The next morning, as [Wuzu] entered the room, Wumen suddenly asked, "Where has all that entanglement of yours gone?
As the Master was about to respond, Wumen laughed and said, "The hawk has already flown beyond New Liao.
He then asked, "The Ten Sages and Three Worthies have fully realized sage-wisdom; why do you say they do not understand this?"

The Master [Nanquan] heard this and said in a stern voice, "The Ten Sages and Three Worthies already know this. What is the meaning of it? Speak quickly! The Master offered a response, but it did not accord with the truth.
One day, while washing vegetables, a single stalk suddenly fell into the water and began to swirl around with the current;

he tried to catch it but could not grasp it. At that moment, the Master had a realization. Overjoyed, he returned home carrying his basket. Nanquan saw him and asked, "What is this? The Master replied, "One."
Lancai said, "Why not offer another statement? The Master replied, "Please ask something else, Reverend.
Later, while standing in attendance, he heard [Master] Wumen raise the story of Lingyun seeing the peach blossoms and questioned the Master about it. The Master answered according to the question.
Lancai asked, "As for Xuansha’s refusal to accept it, what was his meaning? The Master said, "A thief enters an empty room. Wumen remarked, "This public case—"
He was not permitted to join the assembly. As the Master’s voice fell, he immediately shouted and swept his sleeves, departing.
He went to study under Dajue. Over a year later, he returned for an audience. It happened that they were sitting around a brazier when the Master asked him:

"Everyone has their original parents; where are your parents now? The Master replied, "A single fire has burned them away. The Master said, "If that is so, then you have no parents? The Master replied, "I do."
"It exists, yet it is simply that the Buddha-eye cannot see it. The Master asked, "Do you see it? The Master replied, "I do not see it either.
He asked, "Why do you not see it? The Master said, "If I were to see it, it would not be the true parents. He said, "Excellent! The Master presented a verse, saying:
"The original true parents Have never been separated throughout kalpas. In rising and sitting we rely on their power; In cold and warmth they are shared with us."
"Know this: meeting yet not seeing, seeing yet not recognizing. To ask where one now is—present it clearly to the Master. Hearing this, he said, "So it is, so it is.
Later, while presiding over the assembly, the Master took up his staff and said, "Is there anyone? Is there anyone? At that time, a monk prostrated himself.
The Master struck him across the back and said, "Why such talkativeness? The monk replied, "I have not even uttered a single word."

“What is this excessive talk? The Master struck him again, saying, “A second offense will not be tolerated. Ascending the hall, he said: “The path to the courtyard is wet; the moss on the steps is slippery.

Walking the way, the vines entangle; the mountain trails are lost. Zen practitioners often inquire about the intent of the True Patriarchs, But last night, carrying his sandals, he returned alone to the West.
He held up his staff and pointed, saying: “Look, look! The Patriarch has come over the mountain gate once more! He then called to the attendant boy.
"Even though he has driven me out, tell me: while you were just about to seek the Patriarch, now that the Patriarch has arrived, why did he drive you out?
After a long silence, he said: "This is for you all to take responsibility for yourselves; such things are not to be treated with casual indifference."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] cited Yunmen’s saying: "The Buddha-dharma is exceedingly abundant; it is only that the tongue is too short.
Juefan said: "The Buddha-dharma is truly great; it is only that the teeth ache. The Master said: "In this place of mine, fortunately my teeth do not ache, and my tongue is quite adequate;
however, there is simply not much Buddha-dharma to be spoken. Ascending the hall again, he said: "A single arrow at the gate; whoever comes toward it..."
Observing the expedient means, he prepared to step forward and ask how it was. [The Master] pierced through the surface of the skull.
A monk asked, "What is the matter regarding the benefit you obtained in years past? The Master hung his whisk upside down and looked at the monk, saying, "Do you understand?
The monk replied, "I have already recognized your way of acting. The Master said, "Tell me: when Jingzhou’s Huang Siniang prostrated before the Buddha, what did she seek?"
"What is it? The monk had no reply, and the Master struck him. He asked, "What is the house style of Caoxi? The Master said, "Flowing and surging.
He asked, "What is the house style of Linji? The Master said, "Liu Xuande planting a garden.
He asked, "What is the house style of Yunmen? The Master said, "Da Yu observing the river. He asked, "What is the house style of Caodong? The Master said—
In the willow alleys and flower streets, the young gentlemen are drunk. "Do the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings share the same or different?

The Master said, "Willow shadows stretch across the pond as fish climb trees; locust-shade covers the earth as horses mount branches. [The questioner] said, "If that is so, then form and shadow are divided into two."
The right and wrong are naturally revealed. The Master said, "I have never eaten my fill of the rice of Luling;
I merely take this sitting cushion to be the sky. He asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A black-skinned slave and a white ox. He asked, "What is the Patriarch? The Master said:
The dark-skinned slave and the white ox laugh heartily. [A monk] asks, "What is original spiritual power? The Master says, "The rooster knows how to announce the dawn;
the dog knows how to bark. [Another] asks, "In my mind, I have long harbored a doubt. I have come specifically to beg the Master to resolve it for me. The Master says:
"You may still be deluded, but do not let your delusion infect this old monk. He said, "The Master’s mind is like empty space; how could it be deluded? The Master said, "Have you eaten yet?
He replied, "I have just received a meal at a layperson's house. The Master said, "No wonder you smell of raw entrails.
He asked, "When a person who has died a great death comes back to life, what is it like? The Master said, "Give it to him..."
After drinking a cup of tea, [a monk] asked, "I have long heard of the Great Man’s marks of the Master; I beg to join you in this merit. The Master drew in his neck and made a crouching gesture.
The monk was at a loss. [Another monk] asked, "What is the realm of the Way-man? The Master said, "The clay ox sucks dry the waters of the West River;
the wooden horse neighs back the winds of the Northern Pass. [Yet another] asked, "Regarding the direct path to the ultimate principle, I beg for a word from the Master. The Master—

[The student] said, “Such people are rarely encountered. Layman, you have inquired about the profound mysteries of the Buddha-way; I, your disciple, wish to enter therein, yet I do not know if I am capable.
The Master said, “All people can become Yao and Shun. [The student] asked, “How does one achieve entry?

The Master said, “When I desire benevolence (*ren*), then benevolence arrives. [The student] asked, “At all times, how should one practice this? The Master said, “To advance is to overstep; to retreat—”
[The student] said, "That is still not reaching it. He asked, "Is it right to remain neither advancing nor retreating, thereby hitting the middle way?

The Master said, "It is easy to open a mouth for the beginning and the end, but difficult to preserve a heart through the cold of winter. He asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said, "The spring breeze has no face;

flowers and willows fill the imperial capital. He asked, "I do not ask about those who have already attained awakening. But as for those who have not yet awakened, do they have a share in this or not? The Master—
[The monk] said: "Crookedness does not conceal the straight. He asked, "When Bodhidharma came to the Eastern Land, what was it that he transmitted?
The Master said: "Before the pagoda at Mount Xionger, the wind blows; by the cliffs of Shaolin, the moon is dim. He asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said:
"A colorful phoenix flies from within a furnace of blazing flames. He asked, "What is the fundamental principle of the Master? The Master said: "The white heron..."
"A thousand spots of snow on the lower field; a yellow oriole perches upon a branch with a single flower.
Because a Buddha image had been placed at the bottom of a water bucket, the Master saw it and asked the assembly, "Since this is a Buddha, why is he sitting at the bottom of the bucket?
One monk said, "The Buddha-body pervades the entire Dharma-realm. The Master said, "If the Buddha-body pervades the entire Dharma-realm, why is he contained within a small bucket?"
The monk had no reply. The next day, three men requested the Master to speak on their behalf. When they began to recount the previous conversation, the Master urgently pressed them, saying:

"The Buddha is sitting at the bottom of the bucket; let us stop for a moment. But when the bottom of the bucket suddenly falls out, what then? The three men were suddenly enlightened to the essential meaning.

Later, while giving a discourse, the Master cited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* regarding the passage on being "despised by others. The Master said: "The myriad dharmas are fundamentally..."
Emptiness. With a single mind, there is no dwelling; neither grasping nor losing, where could sin or merit reside?
Last night, Śākyamuni the Old Man and Pāpīyān entwined their eyebrows, while Śakra Devendra and King Yama met at the nostrils.
Furthermore, there was a group of men who did not recognize good from evil, intent on separating Buddha and Mara and assigning Heaven and Hell to different places. Yet they were caught by A...

The asura raged; he seized him by his neck and cast him into the ghost-cave of Black Mountain, ensuring that for all kalpas yet to come, he would remain busily preoccupied with karmic consciousness, having no foundation upon which to rely.
Alas! When a person has immediate anxieties, they inevitably lack long-term foresight. Ascending the hall, [he said]:
"Last night there was a great wind, which caused the fallen blossoms to dance upon the steps. Siddhārtha has no handle [to grasp]; for..."
People speak of suffering and emptiness. Addressing the assembly, [the Master] raised the case of Xuansha and Tianlong entering the mountains together and encountering a tiger.
Long said, "The tiger is right before us. Sha said, "It is you. Xuedou said, "If you wish to be a teacher to gods and men, the tiger is truly right before you.
The Master said, "Right here now, there is not even a tiger. What is it that is truly right before you? If you can discern this..."

[He] attained [realization]. "I permit you to be a teacher for humans and devas. Addressing the assembly, he raised the dialogue concerning Qianfeng’s saying, "If you raise one, you must not raise two.
The Master said: "Shide is tipsy with wine; Hanshan has fallen drunk. Supporting one another, they lie together in the mud and grass.
At dawn, they take each other's hands and exit through the pine gate. To this very day, there is nowhere to be found. A monk asked: "What is the meaning of the West?"
[This was] the Master’s meaning. The Master said: "One who has not experienced bitter hardship does not know. When the Master first arrived at Mount Xiong’er, he paid homage at the Patriarch’s stupa.
A temple monk scolded him, saying: "You fool! Why do you bow to an empty stupa? The Master calmly pointed at the stupa and asked:
"Is this an empty stupa? [The monk] replied: "Yes. The Master said: "What about the Patriarch? [The monk] replied: "He took his sandals and departed toward the West long ago."
The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven! A monk, hearing the wind chimes, attained realization.
Leaping for joy, he exclaimed, "Today I have finally seen through this old fellow Guanyin! He immediately entered the room to seek certification.

As soon as he prostrated himself, the Master struck him across the back with a staff and said, "Quickly bring forth the Guanyin you have seen through so that I may look at him. The monk shook his hand.
The Master made the gesture of ringing a bell and produced the sound of a bell with his mouth. He then went straight out from the abbot’s quarters and asked:

"When not a single thought arises and the three periods of time are eternally severed, what is it like? The Master said: "The distant mountains are steep and rugged; the nearby waters resound *ding-dong*. He then asked: "An ancient said..."
"Shatter the mirror to meet me. Once the mirror is shattered, where do you propose to meet? The Master said, "It would put people to shame. Question:
"When a single word expresses everything and there is no further room for speech, what then? The Master said: "The cuckoo cries by the banks of the Wuling Stream;
ten li of peach blossoms are dyed crimson with blood. Question: "All sentient beings will ultimately attain Buddhahood. [The Master said: "Ultimately, they are already Buddhas."
I do not yet understand: what is it like after attaining Buddhahood? The Master replied, "The mountains are naturally high, and the waters naturally flow.

The Master was by nature reticent in speech and moved from place to place without staying long. In the *dingchou* year of the Wanli era, he built a hermitage in the willow lanes of the western city of Beijing. Four years passed.
He passed away in the full lotus posture. His stupa was located at the Small West Gate to the west of the city. His recorded sayings exist in two collections, the Northern and the Southern.
He also compiled a single volume titled *The Model for Śrāmaṇeras* to be handed down to future generations.
One day at dawn, Chan Master Baoyin of Longshu Hermitage on Mount Wutai in Daizhou, a successor of Chan Master Dachu Hong, saw the frost and attained realization. He composed a verse, saying:
"The sun rises from the eastern mountain; The moon sinks behind the western ridge. Yesterday and today— They have never been two different things."
Master Chufeng resided at Bimoya Cliff for over ten years, living in austere simplicity with serene composure.

One day, upon hearing the sound of a firecracker, he attained great enlightenment and spoke this verse: "The eyes protrude from the dead wood; The majestic divine light illuminates the four continents."
The point of contact is clear, yet people do not understand it; how many times has spring passed and autumn returned?
A monk asked Master Yutang, "What is the Way? The Master said, "That which is beneath your feet. The monk asked, "How does one tread upon it?"
The Master said: "Go directly without becoming deluded.

[This concludes the section on] the Dharma heir of Chan Master Kongwei, Chan Master Wuhuan Xingchong of Chexi in Suzhou, a native of the Zhang family of Xiushui. He attended upon Wuqu, who instructed him as follows:
Having attained a realization through the study of the principle of the "Separate Transmission Outside the Teachings," he subsequently shaved his head and donned the dyed robes.

He built a hermitage at Mount Jing and completed the compilation of the *Recorded Sayings* of Wuqu. Upon its completion, he returned for an audience. Wuqu asked him, "Where have you been all this time? The Master replied, "Mount Jing.
Wuqu asked, "What work have you accomplished there? The Master said, "I purchased a plot of land and obtained the original deed."
[The Master] wrote a letter requesting that the Abbot sign it and immediately presented the compiled manuscript. Yunquan hurriedly took it and looked at it, saying, "Is this mine, or yours?
The Master replied, "Abbot, do not encroach upon my trade. Yunquan threw down the manuscript, and the Master hurried out.
Shortly thereafter, he presented a verse. Yunquan said with a smile, "This is neither language nor writing. Did you compose it?"
The Master said, "I am but a fellow who breathes the air of gruel and rice. If you say that I have attained anything, you would be failing the Master by no small measure.

Qiu nodded his head. Later, while instructing the assembly, he said: "On the summit of a solitary peak, one strides across the great thousandfold world; at the crossroads of the city street, those who understand are rarely met.
I do not pay homage to Vimalakīrti, nor do I revere Bodhisattva Fu. After a long silence, he said: 'Lifting my head toward the heavens.'"
Look! Who is this person within? To the assembly: In the Garden of Vairaṇyā he once displayed his ugliness; before the Hall of the Ancient Buddha he again revealed his form.
Were it not for the power of the Moonlight Samādhi, when in years would you ever wash your body clean? Tell me, Great Assembly, speak!
“Śākyamuni the Old Man was born today. I wonder, has he even hit the ground yet? A monk stepped forward and said, “He has already hit the ground.
The Master asked, “Who did you see say that? The monk was speechless. The Master said, “A ladle divining by listening to empty sounds.
He addressed the assembly: “The three realms are mind-only; the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only. He struck the meditation staff and said, “Last night there was a timely rain.”

Drops fall on the empty steps; a single sheet of green moss is soaked through all at once. He addressed the assembly, and after a long silence, said: "The world is this vast and wide—why is it in the hands of this old monk?
Thereupon, he returned to his quarters. He addressed the assembly again: "At this time when smoking is forbidden, Cold Food Festival is observed;
in the desolate graves and wild fields, people weep and wail. Upon the dead skull, living eyes open; it is the tea and rice for ghosts and spirits."
Everything is lost. Mount Shouyang is fit for reclusion. Do not say that spring has no power;
one night the eastern wind stirs at Shaolin, and fallen flowers cover the ground in disarray. Addressing the assembly, he raised his whisk and said:
"If you have not yet understood this very thing, it is all mere false conjecture. Once you have understood this very thing, it is likewise mere false conjecture. A monk stepped forward.
Question: "Before the light of dawn, one makes conjectures; at that time, I have no doubt. But after the light has appeared, why is it also conjecture?
The Master said: "Have you not heard it said: 'Without the spring breeze, the flowers will not bloom; yet once the flowers have bloomed, the breeze blows them down'?"
A monk asked, "What is the mind-seal transmitted secretly from the West? The Master laughed heartily. The monk was at a loss for words. He asked again, "What did he transmit?
The Master struck him, saying, "The fishing flute approaches the gate; the bright moon is upon the azure isles.

A monk asked, "Regarding the principle of pure emptiness, what is it like when one ultimately has no body? The Master said, "A seeker of the Way ought to be thus. The monk asked, "What about that which is above this?"
"Is there anything further? The Master said, "The snow hides the egret; the willows conceal the parrot. Question: "What is it like when the thirtieth day of the twelfth month arrives?
The Master said, "There is no one at home to collect the debt. Question: "After the Master passes away, where will you go?
The Master said, "Bent and curved among a thousand pine trees; leaping and bounding wildly at the tips of the hundred grasses."
While the Master was tending the fire, a monk asked, "What is the self-nature, the original, true Buddha? The Master said, "Bring me a bundle of firewood.
When the monk had brought the wood and asked again, the Master said, "This servant does not even know good from evil," and he struck him.
The monk then asked, "How was it before Bodhidharma had come? The Master said, "Every household has its Avalokiteśvara. He asked, "And after he came? The Master replied, "The same as before."
The Master said, "The Mao-tou star has appeared. A monk asked, "What is the 'taking up' of the One Vehicle? The Master said, "A vine passing through a bamboo mat.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Thirty years from now. The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "From Mount Lu. The Master said, "An ancient said: 'Do not seek the place of descent on Mount Lu; the elephant king’s nostrils reach the heavens in vain.'"
"What is the place where Mount Lu falls? He replied, "To bring it up is not difficult; those who look on from the sidelines are amused. The Master said, "Not so. You should try bringing it up first.
He replied, "Venerable Monk, may you have ten thousand blessings. The Master said, "I still have my doubts about you. He replied, "It is unnecessary. The Master then desisted.
In the winter of the Xinhai year of the Wanli era, suffering from a paralytic ailment, he settled his final affairs and passed away while sitting upright. His *zhai*— [text ends].
Vei respectfully enshrined the sapphire bone stupa at Mount Jing. He passed away on the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month at the age of seventy-two.
He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Xiaoyan Bao of the thirty-second generation under Nan Yue.
Chan Master Hanyou Zhengzhuan of Longchi Yumen in Changzhou was the son of the Lü family of Liyang. At the age of nineteen, he received the tonsure at Xianqin Temple in Jingxi.
He once vowed while burning his crown hair, saying: "If I do not see my nature and clarify my mind, I swear never again to lay this body upon a meditation seat.
One night, hearing the sound of a lamp-flower bursting, he attained an awakening. He then went to visit Xiaoyan and fully recounted [his experience].
For this reason, Yanguan suddenly kicked out a single shoe and said, "Say a word here! The Master was at a loss; he did not sleep all night.

The next morning, he was still standing beneath the eaves when Yanguan saw him and called out his name. The Master looked back, and Yanguan raised one foot, assuming the posture of an asura obstructing the sun and moon.
At that moment, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. One day, Yanguan entered the hall holding a staff and said, "I..."
"Does this staff have some essential purpose for a person? The Head Seat said, "I need it. Yunyan asked, "What do you need it for?

The Head Seat replied, "I need it to cut off the tongues of everyone under heaven. Yunyan rested the staff on his shoulder and said, "Carrying the knotted staff across my shoulders, heedless of others, I go straight into a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks. The Master leaped down from his meditation seat and said, "If..."
"If it is truly so, you may entrust it to such-and-such a person. Go forward to welcome him. Yunyan smiled and said, "You must hold onto this for a long time;
you must surely 'strike the weeds' before you can go. Thereupon, he took his leave.

Yunyan wrote down the *Zhengzong* (Orthodox Lineage) and entrusted it to him, further presenting him with a straw hat, saying, "Cover yourself with this; do not let your sharp edges be exposed. The Master first resided at Longchi.
Next he moved to Bimo on Mount Wutai, then to Puzhao in Beijing, and finally returned to Longchi late in life. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the West?
The Master said, "The deer sleep alone north of the house. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The roosters crow together west of the stream."

The monk asked, "What is the extraordinary matter of the Buddhas and Patriarchs? The Master said, "A shrimp catching a tiger. The monk said, "If that is so, then it is not extraordinary. The Master said, "A cat catching a mouse. As the monk rose to bow, the Master let out a thunderous shout. The monk said, "Why, Master, do you not let me pass? The Master hurriedly called out, "I have business! The monk replied, "What business? The Master said, "Go away! The monk bowed and departed. The Master called after him, "Wait! Wait! The monk turned his head. The Master said, "You have been here for three days; why did you not come forward sooner? The monk said, "I was afraid of being struck by the staff. The Master said, "I am not striking you with the staff; I am striking you with the Dharma. The monk said, "What Dharma? The Master said, "The Dharma of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. The monk said, "What is the Dharma of the Buddhas and Patriarchs? The Master said, "A dog barking at a donkey. The monk said, "How about this: 'The moon shines on the water, the water reflects the moon'? The Master said, "The moon is not in the water; the water is not the moon. The monk said, "How about this: 'The water is not the moon, yet the moon is not elsewhere'? The Master said, "The water is not the moon, and the moon is not elsewhere. The monk said, "How about this: 'The moon is not in the water, yet the moon is not elsewhere'? The Master said, "The moon is not in the water, and the moon is not elsewhere. The monk said, "How about this: 'The moon is not in the water, nor is it elsewhere; it is simply the moon'? The Master said, "The moon is not in the water, nor is it elsewhere; it is simply the moon. The monk said, "How about this: 'The moon is not in the water, nor is it elsewhere; it is neither the moon nor not the moon'? The Master said, "The moon is not in the water, nor is it elsewhere; it is neither the moon nor not the moon. The monk said, "How about this: 'The moon is not in the water, nor is it elsewhere; it is neither the moon nor not the moon, yet it is the moon'? The Master said, "The moon is not in the water, nor is it elsewhere; it is neither the moon nor not the moon, yet it is the moon. Chan Master Miphan Yuanwu of Tiantong, Ningbo Prefecture, was a dharma heir of Chan Master Longchi Chuan of the thirty-third generation under Nanyue. He was the son of the Jiang family of Yixing. From birth, he was solemn and dignified.

Consequently, he was unable to harmonize this with the ancient masters’ teaching that "heaven and earth share the same root" and "all things are one body. He therefore requested instruction from Longchi, who said: [Longchi said: "The ancients spoke of 'the same root' and 'one body' because they were already enlightened; they did not speak of them for those who are still unenlightened. Upon hearing these words, he experienced a great awakening. He then composed a verse: * "The myriad phenomena are originally one; / Where could there be two? * "The ten thousand dharmas are fundamentally empty; / How could there be three? * "If you wish to know the Buddha-nature, / Look directly at your own face. He presented this verse to Longchi, who approved it. From that time on, he never again doubted the teachings of the Buddhas and patriarchs. He remained at Longchi’s monastery for over thirty years, serving as the head of the assembly and presiding over the monastic hall. His reputation spread far and wide, and he became known as the "Elder of the Hall. He passed away at the age of eighty-one. His remains were interred at Mount Xuefeng. His dharma heirs included Master Yinyuan Longqi, Master Zhixu, and others. His posthumous title was Great Master Chongxiao. He was also known as the Elder of the Hall. His collected works comprise ten volumes. He was a man of profound virtue and wisdom, whose influence on the Chan school was immense. His legacy continues to inspire practitioners to this day.

"The water flows cold from the edge of the rocks; the wind comes fragrant from within the flowers. The monk asked, "Apart from this, how is it?
The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows of the staff, Reverend. The monk asked, "Setting aside the blows, how is it?
The Master then gave a shout. The monk asked, "What about after the shout? The Master said, "Do you want me to recite another verse? The monk bowed and withdrew. Subsequently, the head monk...
Jin-su was appointed to the position of West Hall Master. The following year, he followed [his master] to Huangbo. When Tong ascended the seat, he transmitted the lineage robe and whisk to him.
On the day he opened the hall, a monk asked: "In the past you departed from Huangbo; now you come toward Huangbo.
How do you speak of this matter of no coming or going? The Master said: "The head touches the heavens; the feet tread the earth. [The monk asked: "What is the news from Huangbo?"
"What else is there? The Master then shouted, saying, "Though the sand-basin is broken, the family style remains. The Master continued, "This has nothing to do with you, Dharma-heir.
[The student] asked, "You have struck at my old, painful spot from years past; even now I regret that the blow from the staff was too light. I beg for one final blow from the Master.
The Master struck him, saying, "Applying moxa to an old scar. [The student] said, "If that is so, then it has penetrated to the very bone and the very marrow."
[The monk] departs. The Master asks, "What is the meaning of thorough penetration? The monk gives a shout. The Master says, "After the shout, what then?

[The monk] replies, "In these clear times, there is no need to sing songs of peace. The Master says, "You have only cited half of it. [Someone] asks, "What is 'seizing the person but not seizing the environment'?
The Master says, "Strike until the skull is pierced. [The questioner] asks, "What is 'seizing the environment but not seizing the person'? The Master says, "Toss it up!"
He overturned his sitting mat on the ground. [The student] asked, "What is 'both the person and the environment being simultaneously negated'?
The Master said, "I collect both at once. [The student] asked, "What is 'neither the person nor the environment being negated'? The Master said, "I leave you entirely to leap about as you please.
A questioner asked, "An ancient said: 'It is like competing for a swift dragon boat; only when one has won once does one finally rest. But what about when one has not yet won, Master?"

"What kind of assistance do you provide? The Master said, "Cease applying oars and rudders. [The monk] said, "Looking at the old pavilion and the vacant ground, why this despondency and misplaced effort?
The Master said, "Heaven and earth are vast and wide. [The monk] said, "It is precisely the season of the Duanwu Festival."
"Everyone sings the Lotus-Picking Song together. The Master said, "It is not easy to bring it forth. He ascended the hall and said:
"To shoulder the burden with one's whole being and to maintain it with naked body—this must be a man of innate capacity and heroic spirit.
In the ordinary course of daily life, he remains vividly alive and alert, not pasting extraordinary phrases upon his forehead, nor harboring abstruse principles within his depths."

Inwardly, he exclusively employs extraordinary tongs and hammers; alone he brandishes the fangs and claws of the ancestral school. He captures the fierce tiger alive and seizes the savage dragon in hand.

Even if there were one whose words transcend the Buddhas and Patriarchs and whose conduct surpasses Vairocana, upon entering this threshold, they could not avoid being pinned down and squeezed by him.
As for the rest, those who contemplate the mind, form mental conceptions, and focus their thoughts—though dust may settle and light may arise—they possess nothing but a mere semblance of spirit.
O you of exquisite and wondrous wisdom! You must act with your own discernment of what to adopt and what to reject; ultimately, you cannot follow the verbal traces of others.

Only when you possess such decisive and independent mastery can you separately practice the "extra-teaching" (jiaowai), the direct pointing of the single transmission, and wield the staff and shout as the full exercise of the true command.

Yet, even so, you would merely resemble the hooves and horns of those blind donkeys of old. Moreover, at this very moment, when the pivot of the mechanism turns back to its original place—*ekāṃśa*—[one realizes the truth].
[The Master] said: "How do you say it? Originally not obtained by relying on cultivated causes, what need is there to concern oneself with the mind being enlightened or the Dharma being penetrated?
Ascending the hall, he said: "The phrase must be distinct; the meaning must be unerring. When the meaning is unerring and the phrase is distinct, one is free and easy, flowing and expansive.
Everywhere rain falls and clouds rise. This is not like a bald broom falling into a corner of the wall. Therefore, casting the hook into the four seas, one seeks only the fierce [dragon]."
The Dragon. A mysterious mechanism beyond the ordinary; seeking a kindred spirit. Once the fierce dragon has been hooked, it goes without saying that shrimp and earthworms are not even mentioned.

If such a kindred spirit is encountered, then those outsiders standing outside the gate merely labor in vain to grasp at shadows. But tell me: within the assembly of the Golden Grain (Śākyamuni), by what means is a kindred spirit found?
A single drop of water can give rise to waves ten thousand fathoms high; yet even upon arriving, something still remains lacking.
One Ladle. Ascending the hall, he remained silent for a long while and said, "The single phrase prior to sound—I wish everyone to know it. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said, "The heavens are cold and the people are cold; everyone is here. The wind is gentle and the sun is warm; we all move within the realm beyond things."
One must not dwell where a Buddha resides; an iron hammer with a hollow head fears the worms that burrow within.
One must hurry past where no Buddha resides; before the crag of a withered tree, there are many missed paths. If this is so, then do not go. Suddenly turn the body over and seek the original basis.
Plucking the willow flowers—plucking the willow flowers! Who remembers the old master Zhaozhou? Thus, today at Kinsu, the retreat is concluded.
"Is it that which goes? Or is it that which does not go? Seizing both ends, he kicks them both away. In a casual step, the vast sands are cleared.
Entering the hall, he suddenly raised his whisk and said: "This matter, from antiquity to the present, is inherently possessed by every person and fully realized by each individual.
If you understand it, the grasses don the colors of spring; if you do not understand it, the moon pours its clarity in autumn. No need for further effort."
Seeking the Truth and ceasing all views, how could one permit the management of the body while forgetting its form? Throughout the five lakes and four seas, the wind and sun are the same;

village dances and rustic songs celebrate the peace of the age. Entering the hall: The furnace and bellows are opened once more; the tongs and hammers are grasped again. Beyond the standard, we refine and polish;

transcending the ordinary, we forge and smelt. We seize alive those with iron brows and copper heads; we capture living those of extraordinary lineage and unique vision. At this critical moment, it is difficult even to breathe.
Having retreated, how can one explore further? Even if it be as deep as the vast ocean, one must overturn it;
even if it be higher than the blue sky, one must strike it down. Is there, then, any room for people to advance or retreat? Therefore it is said:

"If one proclaims the matters of the School of the Lineage, it shall cause those of the Three Vehicles to tremble with fear and those of the Ten Stages to have their souls startle—even if they were at the stage of Equal Enlightenment."
The Bodhisattva’s seeing of nature is like the crescent moon. As for Śākyamuni, the Old Man—where is he right now? "Bring him here! Fan the brazier and add charcoal!
[He] lets out a shout and says: "Why does it not reach? He plants his staff on the ground and descends from the seat.
Small Assembly Sermon: He cites Xuefeng addressing the assembly, saying: "On South Mountain there is a turtle-nosed snake."
"You all must look very carefully; a snake does not move without its head. Changqing said, "Today, many in this hall will lose their lives," as he opened his mouth like that of a snake.
Yunmen took his staff, thrust it toward him, and made a gesture of fear, revealing the snake's markings.
A monk reported this to Xuansha, who said, "It must have been my elder brother Leng."
[The monk] said, “I have attained it. [The Master] said, “By rubbing yourself against a snake? Even so, I do not act in this way. The monk asked, “How then does the Master act?
The Master said, “What use is Mount Nanshan? To leap out of a snake’s nest! At that time, within Xuefeng’s assembly, there was a whole brood of snakes;

today they have been picked up by this mountain monk upon the tip of his staff. I wish to make them live, and I wish to— (Note: The text appears to be an excerpt from a *gong'an* or Zen dialogue, likely ending mid-thought or with an intentional ellipsis regarding the fate of the snakes.)
One may teach him to die; one may also teach him not to be born; one may also teach him not to die. As it is said: "If you hold him fast, there is no path in the four directions;
if you let him go, he rolls through the thickets. Brothers present here, is there anyone who can give the ancients their due?
If there is, come forward. If you do so, it is like drawing legs for a snake. If there is none, then let a monk come forward.
A swarm of snakes was released, which were about to bite and kill you all. With his staff, he struck them back at once. He ascended the hall and said:
"The intent behind today’s opening of the period at Jingshan is different from the usual custom of other quarters.

Here, the sky is vast and the sea is wide; the mountains are high and the waters are long. It is like the *páng* bird soaring ten thousand miles, its upward rush free and unimpeded. Beneath Chaoyang Peak,"

Auspicious light fills the eyes; one sits in meditation facing the pavilion. Eight sides are transparently clear at the summit of the Almsbowl Peak, where the Fragrant Accumulation (Gandhakuṭī) rises like a mound.
Furthermore, Great Beings provide protection amidst it all. Every point reveals the reality of the place; each instance manifests the true mechanism.

Whatever is known by the mind and eyes, and whatever is reached by hands and feet—none are not the transcendent universe, the ancestral style of the Buddhas of antiquity. Realize this through conditions.
It is attained. When the *udumbara* flowers cover the earth, they settle within their own substance; yet thorns grow crosswise.

Therefore, for those who study the Way, it is valued that the conditions meet the mind and the mind comprehends the objects. Only when mind and object are one and the same is it called liberation. One may then believe the ancients’ saying:
"At the summit of the Peak of Penetrating Mystery, it is not of this human world; outside the mind there is no dharma—every eye meets the green mountains. Suddenly, a shower...
"When it falls, how is it? He struck his staff once and ascended the hall.
He then cited the Patriarch Linji, who said: "If you can attain realization in the first phrase..."
One who can realize this in the first phrase is fit to be a teacher of Buddhas and patriarchs. If one realizes it in the second phrase, one is fit to be a teacher of devas and humans.
If one realizes it in the third phrase, one cannot even save oneself. The Master said: "At Jingshan, it is not like that.
If you realize it in the third phrase, then a stone sprout will grow stalks; if you realize it in the second phrase, then you are planting hemp."
He obtained beans. If one were to seek attainment through the first phrase, then the lacquer bucket would not be satisfactory.

It is laughable to watch Linji forcefully divide the categories, like using a knife to cut water. Standing on the Wangjiang Pavilion with nothing to do, the mountains and rivers are infinitely complete within this.
*Hè!* (A shout). Ascending the hall: Today is the Winter Solstice; all is auspicious and favorable. Within the gate of the patch-robed monks, there is much increase in spirit and vigor.
Each day the sun grows a little longer; the plum blossoms are about to spread their "Sanskrit" script—this is not the calligraphy of the East, nor is it the intent of the West.
Within the ashes of the ritual tube, there is a touch of warmth; the spiritual flame permeates the ground of samādhi. Now tell me: what is this single breath?
"From where does it come? *Chan*. On the third anniversary of the passing of Master Tiantong Wu, he held up incense and said:
"One, two, three; three, two, one. The iron horse neighs in the void, leaving no trace. I remember the time it galloped forth in years past; every time it drinks water, it chokes.
Although this is so, the heart does not betray the person, and the face shows no shame. The Master himself [was from] Huangbo.
From Lianfeng Fatang through Jinsu, Tiantong, Chaoguo, and Fuyan, up to the present Dayuan Wanshou, he forged his disciples with an iron hammer, never flagging in either winter or summer.
Whenever he encountered conduct or speech from various quarters that deviated from the Dharma, he did not avoid enmity or resentment, but instead used his pen to rectify them directly.
He composed twelve volumes of writings titled the "Separate Collection" (Bieji), which are circulated alongside his recorded sayings.
He traveled through the world.
Chan Master Jin-su Shi-che Tong-cheng of Jiaxing Prefecture was the son of the Zhu family of Jinhua. At the age of twenty-six, he took the tonsure under Tian-zhen;
he received full ordination at Yun-men. Upon reading the *Sixth Patriarch’s* kōan regarding "not thinking of good," he attained realization. Not...
Undeterred by the hardships of the journey, he traveled everywhere to consult various spiritual teachers. Later, he visited Tiandong at Jinsu.

Tiandong asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "Yunmen. Tiandong asked, "When did you set out? The Master drew a circle. Tiandong said, "Do not be so disorganized. The Master said, [I am here].
"A thousand *li* share the same wind. Today you have come specifically to receive this painful blow in person. The boy said, "Since a thousand *li* share the same wind, why have you come?
The Master raised his left foot. The boy said, "Not yet. The Master raised his right foot. The boy said, "Wrong.
The Master said, "The wind blows in a different tune. The boy then withdrew. During the next period of entering the room, the boy asked, "When the World-Honored One held up the flower, Kāśyapa..."
The boy smiled. "What do you mean by this? The Master said, "An old woman threading a needle. The boy struck him with his staff and drove him back.

The Master was suddenly enlightened; he offered incense and bowed in thanks. The boy raised his hand again and asked, "How does my hand compare to the Buddha-hand? The Master shook out his sleeves and departed.
He presented a verse, saying: "What is my hand like the Buddha’s hand? With bare feet and disheveled hair, I run straight through to the Mysterious Barrier;
take it for granted that I shall fit the dog's mouth. Dongken approved this and appointed him as the General Supervisor. One day, he led the assembly in manual labor.
The monk said, "I serve as the chief supervisor at Longchi; I am a man who stands out before others. The Master said, "What is the use of such empty fame?
The monk asked, "What is your own true state? The Master struck him a blow across the face. The monk struck back with a series of blows, saying, "I have spent all day chasing after you;
there is great reason for this! The Master shouted, "Better that good things never happen at all! The monk was greatly [impressed].
He scolded them and drove them out. Previously, he appeared in the world at Longqing in Hangzhou; subsequently, he succeeded to the seat at Jinsu. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The Buddhas appear in the world for the sake of the great cause and condition. Bodhidharma came from the West to point people toward seeing their nature and attaining Buddhahood.
I, Jinsu, am not familiar with the 'granny’s Zen'; I simply want everyone to see blood beneath the staff. If you can understand it in this way, you will encounter [the truth]."
"Meeting him everywhere. Not a speck of dust can stand. He extends his hand into the human world, harmonizing with the light to transform beings.
Since he is met at every turn, tell me: who is 'him'? A hair's breadth of difference and heaven and earth are set apart. (He gives a shout. He ascends the hall.
"A thousand words and ten thousand phrases are not as good as saying nothing at all. This morning is the eighth day of the fourth month; why say nothing?
[He] suddenly picked up his staff, struck it once, and said: 'Two rows of tears upon the coral pillow—half are longing for you, half are resentful of you.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "The Way is beyond achievement; to establish achievement is to miss the mark. The profound mystery is unclouded; it is always clearly known. When hungry, eat."
"Rice. When cold, simply add more clothing. Although it is thus, out of ten there are five or six pairs who, upon reaching this point, look over the cliff and retreat.
Little do they realize that this is precisely the realm where all of you fully partake and enjoy. [He strikes the whisk and says: "Do you understand? A hundred flavors are not a rare delicacy;
with one taste of coarse soup, when full, one simply rests. He ascended the hall. [The discourse on] Shaoshi’s True [Dharma].
The pivot: Heaven and humanity are universally nurtured. Pointing directly to the face one had before one’s parents were born—O Great Assembly!
Those with eyes see; those with ears hear. But what is this face before one’s parents were born? After a long silence, he said:
"Outside the wall, the cry of the bird has already shattered; it all lies within the shaking of the head in silence. He let out a shout. Ascending the hall, he said: "Neither cold nor hot."
A matchhead: with a slight flick, it bursts into flame. From this, one undergoes a thorough refining;
moving freely and without obstruction, one may wander at ease. If you can see this, there is no need to draw lines on the ground to build a prison.
If not, how many eyebrows will be burned away? The evening sermon says: "Seizing the heavens and earth, there is not a single thing. Even if you were to attain enlightenment,"

"It is still somewhat fussy and pedantic. Is there anyone who can provide proof? Come forth and meet me. A monk asked, "Master, when the staff and the shout are used together, what is their underlying meaning?
The Master said, "Vividly clear and luminous. He then asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not understand, listen to this verse:
'When the staff and the shout are used together, One realizes the body of the ten directions; It admits no deliberation— Like a spark from flint.'"
Guang struck them apart with his staff. A monk asked, "Before he had even emerged from his mother's womb, he had already finished saving all beings.
Why did the Yellow-Faced Gautama come out again? The Master said, "Striking the grass to startle the snake. [The monk] said, "There is also a guest from Jiangnan in this assembly."
"Do not sing the *zhègū* [partridge] song before others. The Master struck him, saying, "You lacquer bucket, you are not quick-witted!
The monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "Stirring the water does not form a continuous stream. He asked, "What is the Way (*dào*)? The Master said, "It goes straight through to Chang'an.

He asked, "How far apart are Chan and the Way? The Master said, "Their coming and going are no different. He asked, "As for the matter of the supreme vehicle (*zōngchéng*) above, what is it like? The Master—
[The monk] said, “Six times six is thirty-six. I ask: does existence not obtain it? Does non-existence not obtain it? Ultimately, what is this? The Master said, “A worn-out straw sandal.
[The monk] said, “It is not worth half a coin. The Master said, “Who taught you to ask? [The monk] asked, “When the myriad dharmas return to the One, where does the One return?
The Master said, “Scoop up water and the moon is in your hand; play with flowers and their fragrance fills your robe. [The monk] said, “This is still...”
"All phenomena return to the One. Ultimately, where does the One return? The Master struck him. A monk asked, "The three carts are spread outside the gate of the burning house;
I wonder, on what cart is one found atop the Golden Grain Hall? The Master struck him and said, "Realize it right here.
The monk said, "The pure, empty space beyond all things is itself the Tathāgata’s adamantine mind. The Master said, "A flushed face is not as good as a truthful word."
Zhizhu. In the spring of the Wuyin year of the Chongzhen era, he manifested illness. A monk asked, "After this, where shall we meet you, Master?
The Master said, "It is never hidden throughout the entire world. The monk bowed and said, "If that is so, then we shall meet you here.
The Master said, "Do not mistake it. He then passed away peacefully. His worldly age was forty-six. [His remains were] interred...
He remained in his stupa for two years. He was cremated, and his remains were enshrined in a pagoda to the left of his original mountain.
Chan Master Chaozong Tongren of Baohua in Ganzhou was the son of the Chen family of Changzhou.

He left home at the age of twenty and visited Tiandong at Jinsu, yet he felt utterly lost and had no entry point. He traveled extensively to pay respects to various masters throughout the regions but failed to find a karmic connection. Upon returning, Tiandong asked, "Xun..."
"The wind comes from the south; the halls and pavilions feel a subtle coolness. How do you understand this?

The Master replied, "My whole body feels joyful and refreshed; to the very bone I am cool. He presented a verse, saying: "The Hanlin Scholar is soaked through his entire body; The Minister of War is cold to the very bone.
In meeting face-to-face, there is no need for frequent complaints; When one person has cause for celebration, the myriad people are at peace. Tongken approved of him. Thereafter, [he] followed...
The novice went to the invitation of King Aśoka. On a stele at the monastery, there was an inscription of the words spoken by Chan Master Dàqiān:
"The fierce tiger in the mountains takes meat as its life; for what reason does it not eat its own offspring? Pressed by the novice, he sat and lay in restlessness for two days.
Suddenly, the thing choking his chest was removed. He hurried to see the novice and spoke these words: "Only when a person consents of their own accord..."
When he was about to approach, the boy said, "Not yet. The Master laughed and said, "The Abbot can only become a grandson of the Great Thousandfold World," and then he departed.
Shortly thereafter, he heard the boy answer for himself: "Because my meat-eating is not yet exhausted. Only then did the Master realize the meaning of the boy's "not yet."
The following day, Dong ascended the hall. The Master asked, "I do not ask about knowing one's place of return directly; how is it when the Great Function manifests before you?
Dong prepared to take up his staff, but the Master pointed at him and said, "This old fellow! Your tricks will not fool me; you have been caught on a single cast.
Dong shook out his sleeves and left. Later, while presiding over the hall, he said: "To see through is not the true eye; if the eye sees, it is blind. To hear through is not..."
The ears! If the ears hear, they become deaf. The eyes are blinded; the ears are deafened.

Nanquan’s chopping of the cat under his blade, Zhaozhou’s “A cypress tree grows in the courtyard”—if you can truly get a sweat to break out once from these, your chest and breast will overflow [with realization]. This is still not yet equal to Yantou.
How could it be that Xuan Sha’s sealing of a blank sheet of paper was mere proliferation? Great function arises, manifesting the body of absolute reality.
A bottomless bowl has been transmitted by the thousand sages; the radish of Zhenzhou weighs three catties. In the eastern house, the loom weaves without ceasing through the night;
in the western neighbor’s yard, the planting of vegetables never stops all day. Clouds drift across the heavens like white horses passing through a crack; the wind at the treetops—
It is past. Like crows clamoring in the courtyard, the sense bases and objects fall away one by one; the hearing and seeing are majestic and distinct.
Yet, when people reach this point, five out of ten have their ears and eyes changed. Why is it so?
"It is simply because every single thing is already perfectly manifest. He suddenly picked up his staff, struck it once on the ground, and said, "Do you know where this falls?
He struck it again and asked, "What is 'tranquil and unmoving'? The Master replied, "Seven strides forward, eight strides sideways. [The questioner] asked, "What is 'responding and penetrating'?
The Master replied, "Pushing open the door and falling right into the mortar. [The questioner] asked, "As for the fierce tiger in the mountains, it uses meat as..."
Ming asked, "Why do you not eat your own child? The Master said, "That which enters through the gate is not the family treasure.
Ming asked, "How is it that when the Great Matter is already clear, one acts as if mourning for a parent? The Master said, "Simply, there is only me.

Ming asked, "What is the matter beyond the limit of Vipaśyin? The Master said, "It is just this. Ming asked, "How does one apply oneself to the matter above [the ordinary]? The Master then gave him a slap.
The monk hesitated. The Master kicked him and said, "That kick was well-placed. A monk asked, "What is it like when a person is buried in the snow?
The Master said, "Look out beyond the heavens. A monk asked, "What is being born together? The Master said, "Everyone is right here. He asked, "What is dying together?
The Master said, "You head toward the Xiang River; I head toward Qin. The monk said, "Not yet—speak further. The Master said: [He gave a kick.]

"Not one who knows the true sound; in vain do they labor to speak of the year’s end. Question: "When the World-Honored One was first born, he already understood how to point to heaven and point to earth.
Later, upon seeing the morning star, what else did he realize? The Master said: "A poor man thinks of his old debts. Question:
"Regarding the dog having Buddha-nature, why did Zhaozhou say 'no'? The Master said: "Once a single character enters the official gate, even nine oxen cannot pull it out."
He went out. The layman asked, "What is it that the common people use every day without knowing? The Master said, "Shang Daren Qiu Yiji;
Shi Bu Jue. The layman could not help but laugh. The Master then laughed loudly and said, "So, this is just your family’s everyday food and drink!"

The Master remained silent. Again, as the layman was reading a *yulu* (recorded sayings) and reached the passage where [the master] folded his hands and wailed to the blue heavens, he laughed and asked, "Why did he weep at that time? The Master said, "Why do you laugh now?
The layman said, "I cannot understand this one weeping. The Master said, "Can you now understand this one laugh of yours? The layman said, "I laugh at him."
At this cry, the Master said, "He was just crying for you; now look at this smile. The Master asked a monk, "Where are you from? The monk replied, "Suzhou.
The Master kicked over a chair and said, "What is that? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "You do not even recognize Tiger Hill."
He then rebuked him, saying: "Go!
Chan Master Wanyu Tongwei of Longchi in Changzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Jiaxing. He left the household life at Xingshan Temple and later studied under Tiantong.
A monk once asked Tiantong, 'What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Tiantong replied, 'Come closer.'"
The monk approached. As he drew near, the boy struck him. The monk said, "One of superior capacity and great vessel takes this up directly.
But what if one of middling or inferior capacity were to come? The boy replied, "I, an old monk, have never had eyes that see double. The monk was at a loss.

Upon hearing this, the Master attained sudden enlightenment and returned to Jiaxing to dwell in seclusion. Not long after, he went to pay his respects; as soon as he entered the gate, he let out a shout. The boy asked, "Why that shout?"
He shouted wildly. The Master prostrated. The boy struck him, saying, "Shout again and see! The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven! When the tea ceremony was over, he hurried out.
The boy called out, "Wanru, I suspect you of these two shouts from the very bottom of your being. Speak, speak! The Master said:
He paused and said to the Abbot, "I shall go," and then departed. One day, while attending him, the Abbot asked, "The fragrant breeze comes from the south;
the halls and pavilions grow cool. How do you understand this? The Master replied, "The first frost has fallen; it chills to the very bone. The Abbot said, "You are talking nonsense!
The Master shook his sleeves and left, presenting this verse: The fragrant breeze comes from the south; The halls and pavilions grow cool.

His entire body shivered and his hair stood on end; he hid his person within his patched robe. With snoring breath, he awoke from a dream and realized that the state of Yue has always been the southern region.
Having finished reading this, he ceased [his practice]. In the winter of the thirteenth year of the Chongzhen era, he began teaching at Ruru Monastery.
Next he moved to Caoshan, and later took up the post at Longchi. He ascended the hall and said: "Three times three before, three times three after.
Who among you can fathom this message? Wherever the spring breeze blows, flowers form a brocade; where the autumn waters are clear, the moon forms a single bay.
To call this the indestructible Dharma of True Suchness—this person has never yet set foot upon their own threshold. To call it the Dharma of impermanence and birth-and-death—teachings..."
"Accumulated kalpas of remaining retribution—dare I ask the assembly: what, ultimately, is this? [He strikes a circular shape with his whisk and says:
'Before the forms of sentient beings and Buddhas have emerged, the news remains; I do not know how many are willing to take it up.
